    kintu-but; çeña-äkhya-named Çeña; tat-that; äviñöa-entered; pärçada-assembly; viçeñasya-specific;
tat-antaù-pätät-because of insertion; tat-aàçena-as an expansion; eva-certainly; tat-vyävahäraù-His
pastimes; iti- thus; mantavyam-may be considered; tat-therefore; evam-in thes way; eka-rüpatve-in
the status of havint a single form; api- even; präyaù mayä astu me bhartuù na anyä me api vimohiné
iti ädau-Çrimad-Bhägavatam 10.13.37, quoted in full in the privious text; yat-which; tasmin-in
which; tasya-His; bhaktiù-devotion; çrüyate-is heard; tat-that; tu-by; lakñmyä-with opulence; iva-
justas; drañöavyam-may be seen; çré-brahmä-Lord Brahmä; devän-to the Lord.

   Lord Balaräma appears in this world and enjoys pastimes as an associate of Lord Kåñëa. This
statement of Lord Balaräma may be seen as a display of His great devotion for His friend Kåñëa.
This devotion of Lord Balaräma is a display of His spiritual opulence. It does not mean that Lord
Balaräma is not directly a viñëu-tattva expansion of Lord Kåñëa.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.87
records.text:
Text 1


   atha çré-pradyumnasyäpi çiva-netra-dagdhaù smaro jäto 'yam iti yac chrüyate, tad apy eka-deça-
prastava-mätram. tasya çré-gopäla-täpané-çruty-ädau

   atha-now; çré-pradyumnasya-of Çré Pradyumna; api- also; çiva-of Lord Çiva; netra-by the eye;
dagdhaù-burned; smaraù-cupid; jätaù-born; ayam-this; iti-thus; yat-which; çrüyate-is heard; tat-that;
api-al;so; eka-deça-in one place; prastava-reference; mätram-only; tasya-of that; çré-gopäla-täpané-
çruti-ädau-beginning with the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad.


  Now we shall describe Pradyumna, who in His previous life as Cupid was burned to ashes by the
anger of Lord Çiva. This Pradyumna is described in the following verse from the Gopäla-täpané
Upaniñad (2.40):


Text 2


yaträsau saàsthitaù kåñëas
   tribhiù çaktyä samähitaù
rämäniruddha-pradyumn
   rukmiëyä sahito vibhuù

   yatra-where; asau-He; samsthitaù-situated; kåñëa- Kåñëa; tribhiù-by the three; çaktyä-with His
potency; samähitaù-accompanied; räma-by Lord Balaräma; aniruddha- Aniruddha; pradyumnaih-
and Pradyumna; rukmiëyä-and by Çrémati Rukmiëé-devi; sahitaù-accompanied; vibhuù-the all
powerful Supreme Personality of Godhead.


  "Lord Kåñëa, accompanied by His three potencies, and by Balaräma, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, and
Rukmiëé, stays in delightful Mathurä-puré."


Text 3

   ity ädinä nitya-çré-kåñëa-catur-vyühäntaù-patitayä prasiddhes tathä sambhäväbhïät. tasya
smarasyäpi sädharaëa-devatä-viçeña-mätratvena prasiddhatve catur-vyühäntaù-patitäyäm
ayogyatamatvät. tasmäd vakñyamänäbhipräyeëaivaitäd äha

   iti ädnä-by the passage beginning with these words; nitya-eternal; çré-kåñëa-catuù-vyüha-of the
fourfold expansion of Väsudeva. Saìkarçaëa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha; antaù-patitayä-counted
as a part; prasiddhehùj-fame; tathä-in that way; sambhava-of birth; abhavät-because of non-
existence; prasiddhatve-in fame; catuù-vyüha-patitäyäm-in the matter of being part of the four
primary expansions of Lord Kåñëa; ayogyatvät-because of inappropriateness; tasmät- therefore;
vakñyamäana-about to be spoken; abhipräyeëa-with the actual meaning; eva-certainly; etat-this;
äha-he says.


   This Pradyumna, however, cannot be considered to be the same Pradyumna who is one of the
four original expansions of Lord Kåñëa (Väsudeva, Saìkarñaëa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha).
This Pradyumna is simply the demigod Cupid, who is an ordinary living entity, and not the
Personality of Godhead. This is described in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.55.1):


Text 4


kämas tu väsudeväàço
  dagdhaù prag rudra-manyunä
dehopapattaye bhüyas
  tam eva pratyapadyata

   kämaù-cupid; tu-also; väsudeva-of Väsudeva; aàçaù-directly part and parcel; daghaù-burned to
ashes; präk- formerly; redra-of Lord Çiva; manyunä-by the anger; deha-upapattayte-for ataining a
body; bhüyaù-again; tam-that; eva-certainly; pratyapadyata-attained.


   "It is said that Cupid, who is directly part and parcel of Lord Väsudeva, was formerly burned to
ashes by the anger of Lord Çiva. In order to get his body again, he took birth as the son of Kåñëa."*


Text 5


   avedajïasyäpi brähmaëye saty eva brähmaëas tu vedajïa itivat. tu-sabdo 'tra mudhyatäà
sücayati. tataù kämas tu väsudeväàçaù ity asya äsudeväàço yaù kämaù sa eva mukhya ity arthaù. tu-
sabdo 'yam bhinnopakrame vä. tataù väsudeväàças tu kämaù ity anvayo 'pi pürvavad evärthaù. tad
evaà sati yaù prag rudra-manyunä dagdhaù devatä-viçeña indra-bhåtyä ity ekädaça-prasiddhaù
dämaù sa dehopapattaye tat-kopa-dagdhatayä nityam evänaìgataà präptasya tasya svato

dehopapatty-abhäväd deha-präpty-artham. tam eva väsudeväàçaà pradyumnyäkhyaà mukhyaà
kämam eva pratyapadyata praviñöavän. bhüyaù-çabdena pradyumnäd eva pürvam apy udbhüto 'säv
iti bodhyate. yad vä yas tu kämaù prag rudra-manyunä adugdho na dugdhaù; sa bhüyaù
prakaöapléläyäm dehopapattaye sva-mürti-prakäsanärthaà taà çré-väsudevam eva praviñöavän.
adagdhatve hetuù väsudeväàçaù iti.

   aveda-jïasya-of one ignorant of the Vedas; api-even; brahmaëye-brahminical status; sati-may be;
eva-certainly; brähmaëaù-a brähmaëa; tu-but; vedajïaù-one learned in the Vedas; itivat-just as; tu-
çabdaùj-the word "tu(but)"; atra-in this context; mukhyataà-preminence; sücayati- indicates; tataù-
therefore; kämaù tu väsudeva-aàçaù-the phrase "kämas tu väsudeväàçaù (cupid is directly part and
parcel of Lord Väsudeva)" iti-thus; asya-of him; väsudeva-of Lord Väsudeva; aàçaù-as part and
parcel; yaù-which; kämaù-cupid; saù-he; eva-certainly; mukhyaù-prominent; iti-thus; arthaù-the
meaning; tu-çabdaù-the word "tu (but)"; ayam-this; bhinna-of distinction; upakrame-in the
beginning; vä-or; tataù-for this reason; väsudeväàçaù tu kämaù iti anvayaù-the words are given in
the order "väsudevämçaù tu kämaù"; api-even; pürvavat-as before; eva-certainly; arthaù-the
meaning; tat-theefore; evam-in this way; sati-being so; yaù-who; präk rudra-manyuëa daghaù-the
phrase "präg rudra-manyunä daghaù"; devatä- demigod; viçeñaù-as aspecific; indra-of Indra; bhåtyaù-
the servant; iti-thus; ekädasä-among the eleven Rudras; prasiddhaù-famous; kämaù-cupid; saù-he;
deha-upapattaye- for attaining a body; tat-of Çiva; kopa-by the anger; daghatayä-because of being
burned; nityam-continual; eva- certainly; anangatäm-state of being disembodied; präptasya-
attained; tasya-of him; svataù-of His own; deha-upapatti- attainment of a body; abhävät-because of
the lack; deha-of a body; präpti-of attainment; artham-for the purpose;
 tam-him; eva-certainly; väsudeva-of Lord Väsudeva; aàçam-expansion; pradyumna-Pradyumna;
äkhyam-named; mukhyam-original; kämam- cupid; eva-certainly; pratyapadyata-the word
"pratyapadyate"; praviñöavän-means "entered"; bhüyah-çabdena-by the word "bhüyaù (again)";
pradyumnät-from Lord Pradyumna; eva- certainly; pürvam-formerly; api-even; udbhutaù-born; asau-
he; iti-thus; bodhyate-may be known; yat- vä-or else; yaù tu kämaù präk rudra-manyunä-by the
phrase "yas tu käma präg rudra-manyuëa"; adagdhaù-not burned; na-not; dagdhaù- burned; saù-he;
bhüyaù-again; prakaöa-manifested; léläyäm-in pastimes; deha-upapattaye-for attaining a body; sva-
His own; mürti-form; prakäçana-manifesting; artham-for the purpose; tam-Him; çré-väsudeva; eva-
certainly; praviñöavän-entered; adagdhatva-in the status of not being burned by Lord Çiva's anger;
hetuù-the casue; väsudeva- aàçah iti-the statement that cupid is the direct part and parcel of Lord
Väsudeva.


    The word "tu" (but) is very significant in this verse. This word is used to specifically distinguish a
certain person or thing from another or others. For example, if we say "but he is a brähmaëa", a
certain person is distinguished from others, as for example if we say "there may be many who
although born in a brähmaëa family remain ignorant and uneducated, but he is a brähmaëa", the
word "but" distinguishes the learned brähmaëa from others who are less qualified.
    In this verse the phrase "kämas tu väsudeväàçaù" (but that Cupid who is directly part and parcel
of Lord Väsudeva) indicates that there are two Cupids, and one of them is directly part and parcel
of Lord Väsudeva. If it were otherwise, and the intention of the author had been to say "but Cupid
is directly part and parcel of Lord Väsudeva", the order of the words (in Sanskrit) would have been

"väsudeväàças tu kämaù".
   The other Cupid (who is not directly part and parcel of Lord Väsudeva) is described in the
second part of this verse. He is the material Cupid, an ordinary demigod, one of the eleven Rudras,
and a servant of Mahäräja Indra. Burned by Lord Çiva's anger, this material Cupid lost his body and
became disembodied. In order to get his body again he entered the body of Lord Pradyumna, the
original Cupid, who is directly part and parcel of Lord Väsudeva. The material Cupid was then
born again from the body of Lord Pradyumna.
   Interpreted in this way, this verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam may be translated in the following
words:

   "It is said that Cupid was formerly burned to ashes by the anger of Lord Çiva. In order to get his
body again he entered the body of Lord Pradynmna, the original Cupid, who is a direct expansion
of Lord Väsudeva."

  Another explanation of this verse may be given by dividing the first two lines in the following
way:

kämas tu väsudeväàço
  'dagdhaù prag rudra-manyuëa

   By accepting the word "adagdhaù" to replace "dagdhaù", we may translate this verse in this way:

   "The original Cupid, who is directly part and parcel of Lord Väsudeva (and different from the
material Cupid), was not burned to ashes by the anger of Lord Çiva. This original Cupid entered
the body of Lord Väsudeva to appear with Him as He manifested His transcendental pastimes
within the material world."

   In this way we have described the original Cupid, Lord Pradyumna, who, because He is directly
the expansion of Lord Väsudeva, must be different from the material Cupid, who was burned to
ashes by the anger of Lord Çiva.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.88
records.text:
Text 1


pürvoktam eva vyanakti

sa eva jäto vaidarbhyäà
   kåñëa-vérya-samudbhavaù
pradyumna iti vikhyätaù
   sarvato 'navamah pituù

   pürva-former; uktam-statement; eva-certainly; vyanakti- manifests; saù-he; eva-certainly; jätaù-

born; vaidarbhyäm-in the womb of Rukmiëé-devé; kåñëa-samudbhavaù-as the son of Lord Kåñëa;
pradyumhaù iti-by the name Pradyumna; vikhyätaù-famous; sarvataù-in all respects; anavamaù-just
like; pituù-his father.


   This distinction between the material and spiritual Cupids is confirmed by the following verse
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.55.2) which describes the appearance of the material Cupid:
   "Cupid was born as the son of Lord Kåñëa in the womb of Rukmiëé and he became celebrated by
the name Pradyumna. Because he was begotten by Lord Kåñëa directly, his qualities were most
similar to those of Kåñëa."*


Text 2


    yah kåñëa-vérya-samudbhavaù yaç ca pradyumna iti vikhyätaù sa eva prakaöa-lélävasare 'pi
vaidarbhyäà jätaù avirbhütaù, na tv anyaù prakåta-käma eva. tatra hetuù: sarvataù guëa-rüpädiçv
açesesv eva dharmeñu pituù çré-kåñëät anavamaù tulya eveti. anyathä tadåçänavamatvaà na kalpata
iti bhävaù, tasmäd yathä mahäbhärate sarvatra çrémad-arjunasya naratva-prasiddhäv api
païcendropakhyäna indratva-prasiddhir indrasyäpi tatra praveça-vivakñayä ghaöate, tadvad aträpi.
ataù çré näradena ratyai tathopadeças tayä tat-präptis ca na doçäya. pürva-padyasyottarasminn arthe
'pi çré-näradopadeça-balenaiva dagdha-kämasya praveças tatra gamyaù. tataù säkñät pradyumna-
saìgamayogyata tasyäù sparsä-maëivat-tat-samépya-guëäd eva mantavya, çré-pradyumnasya nija-
çaktis tu çrémad-aniruddha-mataiveti jïeyam. atas täpané çruti-labdho 'rtaù samaïjasaù. çré-çukaù.

   yaù-who; kåñëa-samudbhavaù-as the son of Lord Kåñëa; yaù-who; ca-also; pradyumnah iti-by the
name Pradyumna; vikhyätaù-famous; saù-he; eva-certainly; prakaöa-manifest; lélä-pastimes; avasäre-
at the time; api-even; vaidarbhyäm-in the womb of Rukmiëé-devé; jätaù- born; avirbhutaù-
appeared; na-not; tu-but; anyaù-someone else; präkåtam

#####

the Gopala-tapani Upanisad; arthaù-meaning; samanjasaù-correct; çré-sukaù-spoken by Sri
Sukadeva Gosvami.


   This verse describes the viñëu-tattva Lord Pradyumna, the direct expansion of Lord Kåñëa, who
took birth in the womb of Rukmiëé. That this verse describes the viñëu-tattva Pradyumna, and not
the material demigod Cupid may be inferred by the phrase "sarvato 'navamah pituù" (His qualities
were most similar to those of His father Kåñëa).
   The material Cupid, who appeared in Lord Kåñëa's pastimes, is an empowered incarnation of
Lord Pradyumna. Cupid was granted the powers of Lord Pradyumna, just as Arjuna was granted the
powers of Indra by his father, who was Indra himself (this story is related in the Mahäbhärata).
   Because this person was actually the material demigod Cupid, who was granted extraordinary
powers by Lord Pradyumna, Närada informed Rati-devé (Cupid's wife) that her husband had

appeared in Lord Kåñëa's pastimes. For this reason, when Rati-devé was reunited with Pradyumna,
there was no fault on her part, for she simply regained the association of her husband.
   Someone may raise the question how it was possible for Rati-devé, a material demigoddess, to
associate with an empowered incarnation of Lord Pradyumna. The answer to this question is that
by contact with the empowered incarnation of Pradyumna she became purified and qualified to
associate with him, just as ordinary metals become turned to gold by contact with a touchstone.
   The actual viñëu-tattva Lord Pradyumna, however, is not associated with Rati-devé, who is the
potency of the material Cupid. Lord Pradyumna's potency is Lord Aniruddha. This is confirmed in
the verse from Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad quoted in Anuccheda 87, Text 2.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.89
records.text:
Text 1


evam aniruddhasyäpi säkñäc caturvyühatve liìgam äha

apisvid äste bhagavän sukhaà vo
   yaù sätvatäà käma-dugno 'niruddhaù
yam ämananti sma çabda-yonià
   mano-mayaà sattva-turéya-tattvam

   evam-in the same way; aniruddhasya-of Aniruddha; api- also; sakñat-directly; caturvyuhatve-in
the state of being a part of the caturvyuha expansions of Godhead; lingam- characteristic; aha-
describes; api-as also; svit-whether; äste-does He; bhagavän-the Personality of Godhead; sukham- all
happiness; vaù-of you; yaù-one who; sätvatäm-of the devotees; käma-dughaù-source of all desires;
aniruddhaù-the plenary expansion of Aniruddha; yam-whom; ämananti-they accept; sma-from
yore; hi-certainly; çabda-yonim-the cause of the /Rg Veda; manaù-mayam-creator of the mind;
sattva- transcendental; turéya-the fourth expansion; tattvam- principle.


   That Lord Aniruddha is one of the caturvyüha expansions of Godhead is described in the
following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.1.34):

   "May I inquire whether Aniruddha is doing well? He is the fulfiller of all the desires of the pure
devotees and has been considered from yore to be the cause of the Åg Veda, the creator of the mind
and the fourth plenary expansion of Viñëu."*


Text 2


   çabda-yonim niçväsa-vyaïjita-veda-våndam evaà vä are 'sya mahato bhütasya niçväsitam etad
yad åg-vedaù ity ädi çruteù. mano-mayam citte väsudevavan manasy upäsyam. sattvam çuddha-

sattvätmakaù çré-väsudevavädi-rüpo bhagavän yatra turéyan rüpam. ato bäëa-yuddhädau
bandhanänukaraëadikam ätmeccha-mayé lélaiva, çré-rämacandrädivat.

   sabda-yonim-the word "sabda-yonim"; nisvasa-from the breathing; vyanjita-manifested; veda-
vrndam-the Vedas; evam-in this way; vai-certainly; are-O Maitreyi; asya-of Him; mahatah bhutasya-
of the Supreme Lord; nisvasitam-the breathing; etat- this; yat-which; rk-vedaù-the Rg Veda; iti-
thus; adi-in the passage beginning with; sruteù-from the Brhad-aranyaka Upanisad; manah-mayam-
the creator of the mind; citte-in the mind; vasudevavat-like Vasudeva; manasi-in the mind;
upasyam- worshippable; sattvam-the word "sattvam"; suddha-tattva-atmakaù-means "situated in the
transcendental stage of pure godness"; çré-vasudeva-adi-beginning with Vasudeva; rupaù-forms of
the caturvyuha expansions; bhagavan-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; yatra-where; turiyam-
the fourth expansion; rupam-in the form; ataù-therefore; bana-with Banasura; yuddha-in the fight;
adau-in these and other pastimes; bandhana-bondage; anukarana-imitation; adikam-beginning
with; atma-iccha-mayi- according to His own desire; lila-pastime; eva-certainl; çré-ramacandra-adi-
vat-as Lord Ramacandra and other incarnations of the Personality of Godhead.


  The statement "çabda-yonim" (Lord Aniruddha is the cause of the Åg Veda) in this verse is
confirmed in the following statement of Båhad-äraëyaka Upaniñad (2.4.10):

  "O Maitreyé, the Åg Veda is manifested from the breathing of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead."

   The word "mano-mayam" means "the creator of the mind". Each member of the catur-vyüha
expansions is the predominating Deity of one of the subtle elements. Lord Väsudeva is the Deity of
the heart, Lord Saìkarñaëa is the Deity of the false-ego, Lord Pradyumna is the deity of the
intelligence, and Lord Aniruddha is the deity of the mind. Lord Aniruddha is worshiped within the
mind, just as Lord Väsudeva is worshiped within the heart.
   The word "sattvam" means "He who is situated in the transcendental stage of pure godness."
   The word "turéyam" (fourth) means that of the catur-vyüha expansions of the Lord, Lord
Väsudeva is the first expansion, Lord Saìkarñaëa the second, Lord Pradyumna the third, and Lord
Aniruddha the fourth expansion.
   Someone may raise the following objection: If Aniruddha is actually the Personality of Godhead,
then why was He defeated in fighting with Bäëäsura?
   This objection may be answered by saying: By His own wish the Supreme Lord sometimes
pretends to be a limited human being in His pastimes. There are many examples of His acting in
this way in His appearance as Lord Rämacandra and in other incarnations also.


Text 3


  asya pädma-båhat-sahasra-nämni-mähätmya-nämäni caitäni

aniruddho båhad brahma

   pradyumnir viçva-mohanaù
catur-ätmä catur-varëaç
   catur-yuga-vidhäyakaù

catur-bhedaika-viçvätmä
   sarvotkrñöäàça-koöiñuù
äçrayätmä iti.

   asya-of Lord Aniruddha; padma-from the Padma Purana; brhat-sahasra-namni-in the 1000
names; mahatmya-namani- glorification of His holy names; ca-also; etani-these; aniruddhaù-Lord
Aniruddha; brhat-the great; brahma-Brahman; pradyumniù-the son of Pradyumna; visva-the
universe; mohanaù- enchanting; catuh-atma-of the quadruple expansions of Lord Vaudeva,
Sankarsana, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha; catur-varnaù-who appears in four colors; catuh-yuga-the
four yugas; vidhayakaù- who establishes; catuh-bheda-of the four kinds of living entities; eka-visva-
atma-the Supersoul; sarva-utkrsta- superexcellent; amsa-expansions; koti-of millions; suù-parent;
asraya-atma-the supreme shelter.


  Lord Aniruddha is glorified in the following verses from the Båhat-sahasra-näma prayers of the
Padma Puräëa:

   "Lord Aniruddha, the son of Pradyumna, is the Supreme Brahman. He enchants the entire
universe. He is the fourth member of the four catur-vyüha expansions of Godhead. He appears in
four colors (white, red, yellow, and black) in the four yugas (Satya, Tretä, Dväpara, and Kali) to
establish the principles of religion. He is the all-pervading Supersoul who remains in the hearts of
the four kinds (those born from the womb, from eggs, seeds, or perspiration) of conditioned souls.
From Him millions of living entities are manifest, and He is the shelter within whom everything
rests."


Text 4


   ataù çré-kåñëa-vyühatvena mahäniruddhatväd asyaivävirbhäva-viçeçaù pralayärëavädi-dhäma
puruña iti jïeyam. ata eväbhedena jagåhe pauruñaà rüpaà bhagavän ity ädy-uktam. müla-
saìkarñaëädy-aàçair eva. hétara-saìkarñaëädy-avasthä-trayaà puruñaà prakäçayatéti.

   ataù-therefore; çré-kåñëa-vyuhatvena-as one of the catur-vyuha expansions; maha-aniruddhatvat-
as Maha Aniruddha; asya-of Him; avirbhava-incarnation; visesaù-specific; pralaya-of devastation;
arnava-on the ocean; adi-beginning with; dhama- whose abode; puruñaù-Puruña incarnation; iti-
thus; jneyam- should be understood; atah eva-therefore; abhedena-as not-different; jagrhe
pauruñam rupam bhagavan iti adi uktam-Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.3.1; mula- original; sankarsana-of
Lord Sankarsana; amsaiù-by the expansions; eva-certainly; hi-certainly; itara-othe; sankarsana-adi-
beginning with Lord Sankarsana; avastha-trayam- three expansions; puruñam-the puruña-
incarnation; prakasayati- manifests; iti-thus.

   Aniruddha (who appeared as the son of Pradyumna) is therefore the original Mahä-Aniruddha
who remains in the spiritual sky. It is this Lord Aniruddha who stays on the waters of devastation at
the time when the material universe is destroyed. The Lord's expansion as the catur-vyüha puruña-
incarnations within the material world is described in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.3.1):

  "In the beginning of the creation, the Lord first expanded Himself as the universal form of the
puruña-incarnation, and manifested all the ingredients for the material creation."*

  Four catur-vyüha expansions (Väsudeva, Saìkarñaëa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha) are
manifested in the spiritual world, and from these another series of catur-vyüha expansions is
manifested within the material world.


Text 5


  tathaiväbhedena viñëu-dharmottare 'pédam. tatra vajra-praçnaù

kas tv asau bäla-rüpeëa
   kalpänteçu punaù punaù
dåñöo yo na tvayä jïätas
   tatra kautuhalam mama

   tatha-also; eva-certainly; abhedena-as not different; visnu-dharma-uttare-in the Visnu-
dharmottara Purana; api-also; idam-this; tatra-there; vajra-of Vraja; prasnaù-the question; kaù-
who?; tu-indeed; asau-is he; bala-rupena-in the form of a child; kalpa-of the kalpa; antesu-at the
conclusions; punah punaù-again and again; drstaù-is seen; yaù-who; tvaya-by you; jnataù-known;
tatra-in this matter; kautuhalam-curiosity; mama-my.


   That the Mahä-Aniruddha who remains in the spiritual world appears within the material
worlds in Lord Kåñëa's family is confirmed in the following passage from Viñëu-dharma Puräëa,
Uttara-khaëòa, in the question of Vrajanäbha and the answer of Märkaëòeya Muni. Vrajanäbha
asked:

  "At the end of each kalpa a small child always appears. Although I repeatedly see this child I do
not know His identity. Please tell me who this child is, I am very eager to know the answer to this
question."


Text 6


çré-märkaëòeyottaraà ca

bhüyo bhüyas tv asau dåñöo
   mayä devo jagat-patiù
kalpa-kñayeëa viëätaù
   sa mäyä-mohitena vai


kalpa-kñaye vyatéte tu
   taà devaà prapitämahät
aniruddhaà vijäëami
   pitaraà te jagat-patim. iti.

   çré-markandeya-of Markandeya Muni; uttaram-the reply; ca- also; bhuyaù-again; bhuyaù-and
again; tu-indeed; asau-He; drstaù-is seen; maya-by me; devaù-the Supreme Lord; jagat-of the
universe; patiù-the master; kalpa-of the kalpa; ksayena- with the termination; vijnataù-understood;
saù-He; maya-by the illusory potency; mohitena-bewildered; vai-certainly; kalpa-ksaye-at the end of
the kalpa; vyatite-elapsed; tu-indeed; tam-Him; devam-the Supreme Lord; prapitamahat-from your
grandfather, Lord Kåñëa; aniruddham-Aniruddha; vijanami-I know; pitaram-father; te-your; jagat-
of the universe; patim-the master; iti-thus.


   Märkaëòeya Muni replied:

   "Although I myself am not free from the influence of the Lord's illusory potency (mäyä), I have
repeatedly seen the Personality of Godhead appear as a small child at the time of partial cosmic
annihilation (kalpa-kñaya). That same form of the Personality of Godhead appears in Lord Kåñëa's
family as your father, Aniruddha. That your father Aniruddha is the Personality of Godhead is
known to me without any doubt."


Text 7


  bhéçma-parvaëi duryodhanaà prati bhéçma-çikñäyäà çré-kåñëasyävatärärambhe gandha-
madanam ägatasya brahmaëas tad-ävirbhävaà manasi paçyatas tu bälasya tad idaà vacanam.

   bhisma-parvani-in the Bhisma-parva of the Mahabharata; duryodhanam prati-to Duryodhana;
bhisma-of Bhisma; siksayam-in the instrucitons; çré-kåñëasya-of Sri Kåñëa; avatara-of the
incarnation; arambhe-in the beginning; gandha-madanam-to the Gandha-madana mountain;
agatasya-gone; brahmanaù-of Lord Brahma; tat-of the Lord; avirbhavam-incarnation; manasi-in the
mind; pasyataù-seeing; tu-indeed; balasya-of the child; tat- therefore; idam-these; vacanam-words.


   In the Mahäbhärata, Bhéñma-parva, in the instructions of Bhéñma to Duryodhana, Lord Brahmä's
arrival at Gandhamadana mountain at the beginning of Lord Kåñëa's appearance in this material
world is described. While Brahmä was at Gandhamadana mountain he saw the Supreme

Personality of Godhead appear in his heart in the form of a small child. Brahmä spoke the following
words to the Supreme Lord who had thus appeared before him:


Text 8


såñövä saìkarñaëaà devaà
   svayaà ätmänam ätmanä

kåñëatvam ätmanäsrakñéù
   pradyumnaà hy ätma-sambhavam
pradyumnäc cäniruddhaà tu
   yaà vidur viñëum avyayam

aniruddho 'såjan mäà vai
   brahmäëaà loka-dhäriëam
väsudeva-mayaù so 'haà
   tvayaivasmin vinirmitaù. iti.

   srstva-having created; sankarsanam-Lord Sankarsana; devam-the Personality of Godhead;
svayam-personally; atmanam-Your own self; atmana-by Your self; kåñëatvam-the state of being
Kåñëa; atmana-by Your self; asraksiù-you created; pradyumnam- Lord Pradyumna; hi-certainly;
atma-from Your own self; sambhavam-generated; pradyumnat-from Lord Pradyumna; ca-also;
aniruddham-Lord Aniruddha; tu-indeed; yam-whom; viduù-they know; visnum-to be Lord Visnu;
avyayam-the imperishable; aniruddhaù-Lord Aniruddha; asrjat-created; mam-me; vai- certainly;
brahmanam-Brahma; loka-of the planets; dharinam-the maintainer; vasudeva-mayaù-descended
from Lord Vasudeva; saù- that person; aham-I; tvaya-by You; eva-certainly; asmin-in this universe;
vinirmitaù-created; iti-thus.


   "O Lord Väsudeva, You expanded Yourself as Lord Saìkarñaëa and He then expanded Himself
as Lord Pradyumna. Lord Pradyumna expanded Himself as Lord Aniruddha, whom the sages know
to be the eternal Personality of Godhead, Lord Viñëu, and Lord Aniruddha created me, Brahmä,
the maintainer of the universe. O Lord, because I am thus created by You, I am certainly Your part
and parcel."


Text 9


    ata eva ca pürvam api jägåhe ity atra çré-kåñëasyäniruddhävatäräntaù-patitvaà na vyähyättam.
çré-viduraù çrémad-uddhavam.

  atah eva-therefore; ca-also; purvam-previously; api- also; jagrhe iti atra-in the Srimad-
Bhagavatam 1.3.1; çré-kåñëasya-of Sri Kåñëa; aniruddha-of Lord Aniruddha; avatara-incarnation;

antah-patitvam-inclusion within; na-not; vyakhyatam-is explained; çré-viduraù-spoken by Vidura;
çrémat-uddhavam-to Uddhava.


   We may note that in this quotation, and also in the previously quoted verse from Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (1.3.1) "jägåhe pauruñaà rüpam" (in the beginning of creation the Lord first expanded
Himself as the universal form of the puruña-incarnations) it has been clearly described that Lord
Aniruddha is an expansion of Lord Kåñëa. Lord Kåñëa is not described in these verses as an
incarnation of Lord Aniruddha.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.90
records.text:
Text 1


   tad etat tasya catur-vyühätmakasyaiva pürëatvaà vyäkhyätam. çré-gopälottara-täpanyäm api
tathaiväyaà praëavärhatvena darçitaù

   tat-therefore; etat-this; tasya-of Him; catuh-vyuha-atmakasya-the origin of the catur-vyuha
expansions of Godhead; purnatvam-completeness; vyakhyatam-is described; çré-gopala-uttara-
tapanyam-in the Second Chapter of the Gopala-tapani Upanisad; api-also; tatha-in the same way;
eva-certainly; ayam-this; pranava-of the syllable om; arthatvena-in definition; darsitaù-is revealed.


   That Çré Kåñëa is the original Personality of Godhead, the origin from who the catur-vyüha
expansions of Godhead have emanated, is confirmed in the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad's (2.68-69)
definition of the sacred syllable om:


Text 2


rohiëé-tanayo räma
   akäräkñara-sambhavaù
taijasätmakaù pradyumna
   ukäräkñara-sambhavaù

   rohini-of Rohini-devi; tanayaù-the son; ramaù-Balarama; akra-aksara-from the syllable "a";
sambhavaù-manifest; taijasa-atamakaù-the origin of sleep; pradyumna-Pradyumna; ukara-aksara-
from the syllable "u"; sambhavaù-manifest.


   "The sacred syllable om consits of three letters: a,u, and m. Balaräma, the son of Rohiëé, is the
letter a. Splendid Pradyumna is the letter u.

Text 3


prajïätmako 'niruddho vai
   makäräkñara-sambhavaù
ardha-mäträtmakaù kåñëo
   yasmin viçvaà pratiñöhitam. iti.

   prajna-atmakaù-the deity of deep sleep; aniruddhaù- Aniruddha; vai-certainly; makara-aksara-
from the syllble "ma"; sambhavaù-manifest; ardha-matra-atmakaù-kåñëaù- Kåñëa; yasmin-in whom;
visvam-the universe; pratisthitam- rests; iti-thus.


   "Intelligent Aniruddha is the letter m. Lord Kåñëa, in whom the entire universe rests, is the
ardha-mätra letter (à), which complete the syllable oà."


Text 4


   atha çré-kåñëe 'vatarati tat-tad-aàçävatäräëäm api praveça iti yad uddiñöaà tad yathä tatra kåñëas
tu bhagavän svayam ity ädikaà siddham eva, tathä tasya tad-rüpeëaiva çré-våndävanädau
sarvävasthäyitvaà pratipädayiñyämaù.

   atha-now; çré-kåñëe-when Lord Kåñëa; avatarati-appears in the material world; tat-tat-amsa-
avataranam-of His various expansions; api-also; pravesaù-entrance; iti-thus; yat- because; uddistam-
described; tat-that; yatha-just as; tatra- in this matter; kåñëah tu bhagavam svayam iti adikam-the
passage "Sri Kåñëa is the Original Personality of Godhead" (Bhag. 1.3.28); siddham-corroborated;
eva-certainly; tatha-in the same way; tasya-of that; tat-rupena-in that form; eva- certainly; çré-
vrndavana-adau-in Vrndavana and othe sacred places; sarva-avasthayitvam-eternal residence;
pratipadayisyamaù-I shall demostrate.


    By quoting the verse "kåñëas tu bhagavän svayam" (Çré Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of
Godhead) (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.3.28) and many other verses also, it has been clearly demonstrated
that Çré Kåñëa is the Original Personality of Godhead, and when He appears in the material world,
all other forms of Godhead appear within His form.
    Just as this fact has been clearly demostrated, I shall now establish the fact that Çré Kåñëa
eternally resides in the holy abode of Våndävana, and the other places where He enjoyed pastimes.
It is not that He temporarily appears, and then after His appearance in this world He is no longer
manifest. He eternally remains in these spiritual abodes.


Text 5

   atha ca çré-hari-vaàça-mate upendra evävatätareti. jaya-vijaya-çäpa-prastave ca

yasyämi bhavanaà brahman
   etad ante tavänagha" ity atra ca.

pähi vaikuëöha-kiìkarän ity atra ca.

   svämi-vyäkhyänusäreëa vikuëöhasuta eveti, kvacit kñérodakaçäyy eveti. kvacit puruñä eveti.
kvacin näräyaëarçir eveti, båhat-sahasra-nämni lakñmaëasyaiva balaåamatva-kathanena çré-raghava
eveti, kvacin näräyaëa-keça evety ädikam naëävidhatvaà çrüyate. evaà caikaà sandhitsato 'nyat
pracyavate, atra satyaà ca sarva-väkyam. tasmäd vidvadbhir eva vicäryatam: svayaà-bhagavati
tasmin praveçaà vinä kathaà tat sambhaved iti. dåçyate-ca tasmät keçä/cid aàçäëäm ävirbhävah.
yathä pradyumnädénäm.

   atha-now; çré-hari-vamsa-of the Hari-vamsa; mate-in the opinion; upendraù-Vamanadeva; eva-
certainly; avatatara- descended; iti-thus; jaya-vijaya-of Jaya and Vijaya; sapa-of the curse; prastave-
in the explanation; ca-also; yasyami-I shall go; bhavanam-to the abode; brahman-O Brahma; etat-of
this; ante-at the end; tava-your; anagha-O sinless one; iti- thus; atra-in this verse (Bhag. 1.6.27):


idänéà näça äradbha
   kulasya dvija-çäpajah
yasyämi bhavanaà brahman
   etad ante tavänagha

pahi vaikuntha-kinkaran iti atra ca-and also in the verse (Bhag. 11.6.27):


tataù sva-dhäma paramaà
   viçasva yadi manyase
sa-lokän loka-pälän naù
   pähi vaikuëöha-kiìkarän

svami-of Sridhara Svami; vyakhya-the commentary; anusarena-in conformity to; vikuntha-of
Vikuntha-devi; sutaù-the son; eva-certainly; iti-thus; kvacit-in another place; ksirodakasayi-
Ksirodakasayi Visnu; eva-certainly; iti-thus; kvacit-in another place; puruñaù-the puruña
incarnation; eva-certainly; iti-thus; kvacit-in another place; narayana-rsiù-Narayana Rsi; eva-
certainly; iti-thus; brhat-sahasra-namni-in the "Brhat-sahasra-nama" prayers; laksmanasya-of
Laksmana; eva-certainly; balaramatva-the position of Balarama; kathanena-with the description;
çré-raghavaù-Lord Ramacandra; eva-certainly; iti-thus; kvacit-in another place; narayana-of Lord
Narayana; kesaù-a hair; eva-certainly; iti-thus; adikam-beginning; nana-vidhatvam-various
expansions; sruyate-are heard; evam-in this way; ca-also; ekam-one; sandhitsataù-       anyat-
another; pracyavate-falls away; atra-here; satyam-true; ca-also; sarva-all; vakyam-statements; yatha-

just as; sva-mati-of the mind; anubhava-of the experience; anurupat-according to; naa-various;
vakya-statements; eka-one; vakyata-statement; ca-also; tasmat-therefore; vidvadbhiù-by the
learned; eva-certainly; vicaryatam-it may be concluded; svayam-bhagavati-in the Original
Personality of Godhead; tasmin-in Him; pravesam-entrance; vina-without; katham-how is it
possible?; tat-that; smabhavet-may be; iti-thus; drsyate-is observed; ca-also; tasmat-from that;
kesancit-of some; amsanam-of His plenary expansions; punaù-again; avirbhavaù-incarnation; yatha-
just as; pradyumna-
adinam-of Pradyumna and others.


   At this point someone may object, saying that the Hari-vaàça describes Lord Kåñëa as an
incarnation of Lord Upendra (Vämana). This false conception is refuted by the following words
spoken by Lord Kåñëa in the Çrémad-Bhägavatam, which describe Lord Kåñëa's return to His own
eternal abode in the spiritual world (11.6.31), and which are spoken in connection with the story of
the Kumära's cursing of Jaya and Vijaya. Lord Kåñëa said (to Brahmä and the other demigods as He
was about to leave the earth planet to return to the spiritual world):

   "O Brahmä, now that the Yadu dynasty has been destroyed by the curse of the brähmaëas, I shall
visit your planet, known as Brahmaloka, and from there I shall return to My own abode in the
spiritual world."

   "Çrédhara Svämé explains this verse in his commentary:

vaikuëöhaà yäsyan tava bhavanaà yasyämi

   "O Brahmä, I shall visit your abode and then return to the spiritual world of Vaikuëöha."

    That Lord Kåñëa, after leaving the earth planet, returned to His own abode in the spiritual world
is also confirmed in the following statement of Brahmä (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.6.27):

   "O Lord, Your mission in this world is now completed. Please return, if You will, to Your own
abode in the spiritual world. O Lord, please also protect us, the controllers of the planets, along
with all our subjects, for we are all Your sincere servants."

   In some places in the scriptures it may say that Lord Vaikuëöha, the son of Vikuëöhä-devé,
appeared as Lord Kåñëa; in other places it may say that Kñérodakaçäyé Viñëu appeared as Lord
Kåñëa; in other places in the scriptures it may say that the puruña-incarnations appeared as Lord
Kåñëa; in other places in the scriptures it may say that Näräyaëa Åñi appeared as Lord Kåñëa; in the
Båhat-sahasra-näma Prayers in the description of the identity of Lord Balaräma and Lord
Lakñmaëa, it may say that Lord Rämacandra appeared as Lord Kåñëa; in other places in the
scriptures it may say that a hair of Lord Näräyaëa appeared as Lord Kåñëa; and in other places in
the scriptures there may also be other descriptions of how other forms of Godhead have incarnated
as Lord Kåñëa. How are these contradictory statements to be resolved? Actually all these statements
are true, for all forms of the Personality of Godhead are simultaneously present in the form of the
Personality of Godhead, Çré Kåñëa, and when Çré Kåñëa descends o this material world, all other

forms of Godhead also descend with Him.


Text 6


   ata eva vikuëöha-sutasya praveçäbhipräyeëaiva çiçupäla-dantavakrayoù çré-kåñëa-säyujyam eva
tadänéà jätam. punar avatära-lélä-samäptau çré-vikuëöha-sute sva-dhäma-gate prasädatva-präptiù.
yathoktaà çré-näradena

    atah eva-therefore; vikuntha-sutasya-of Lord Kåñëa; pravesa-entrance; abhiprayena-by the
intention; eva-certainly; sisupala-of Sisupala; dantavakrayoù-and Dantavakra; çré-kåñëa-sayujyam-
merging into Kåñëa; eva-certainly; tadanim-then; jatam-came into being; punaù-again; avatara-
descend; lila- pastimes; samaptau-concluded; çré-vikuntha-sute-when Lord Kåñëa; sva-dhama-to His
own abode; gate-went; parsadatva-the status of associates; praptiù-attainment; yatha-just as; uktam-
it is described; çré-naradena-by Narada Muni (in the following verse from Srimad-Bhagavatam).


   When Çiçupäla and Dantavakra were killed by Lord Kåñëa, they attained säyujya-mukti, merging
into the body of the Lord. However, when the Lord's earthly pastimes were concluded, and the Lord
had returned to His own abode in the spiritual world, Çiçupäla and Dantavakra also returned with
Him, and resumed their original posts as personal associates of the Lord. This is described by
Närada Muni in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 7.1.46):


Text 7


vairänubandha-téreëa
   dhyänenäcyuta-sätmatäm
nétau punar hareù pärçvaà
   jagmatur viñëu-pärçadau. iti.

    vaira-anubandha-bond of hatred; tévreëa-consisting of acute; dhyänena-by meditation; acyuta-
sätmatäm-to the effulgence of the infallible Lord; nitau-attained; punaù- again; hareù-of Hari;
pärçvam-the proximity; jagmatuù-they reached; viñëu-pärçadau-the gatekeeper associates of Viñëu;
iti-thus.


   "These two associates of Lord Viñëu-Jaya and Vijaya-maintained a feeling of enmity for a very
long time. Because of always thinking of Kåñëa in this way, they regained the shelter of the Lord,
having returned home, back to Godhead."*


Text 8

   tathä hari vaàçe ca kñérodaçäyino mukuöe daityäpahåte daitya-maraëäya garuòo yävat kåta-
vilambas tävat çré-kåñëo tvatatara. tataç cäsau mukuöam ähåtya tatra cordhva-loke ca kuträpi
bhagavantam adrñövä gomanta-çirasi çré-kåñëayaiva samarpitavän iti prasiddhiù.

   tatha-in the same way; hari-vamse-in the Hari-Vamsa; ca- also; ksirodasayinaù-of Ksirodakasayi
Visnu; mukute-when the crown; daitya-by the demons; apahrte-was stolen; daitya-of the demons;
maranaya-for killing; garudaù-Garuda; yavat-while; krta-vilambaù-spending his time; tavat-then; çré-
kåñëaù-Sri Kåñëa; avatara-incarnated; tataù-then; ca-also; asau-He; mukutam-crown; ahrtya-taking;
tatra-there; ca-also; urdhva-loke-in the spiritual world; ca-and; kutra api-anywhere; bhagavam-the
Personality of Godhead; adrstva-not seeing; gomanta-sirasi-on the peak of Gomanta Mountain; çré-
kåñëaya-to Sri Kåñëa; samarpitavan-offered; iti-thus; prasiddhiù-the famous quotation.


   That Lord Kñérodakaçäyé Viñëu entered the body of Lord Kåñëa when He incarnated on this
earth just as Jaya and Vijaya did when they were killed by the Lord is confirmed in the following
celebrated passage from the Hari-vaàça (Viñëu-parva, Chapter 41):

   "Observing that Lord Kçérodakaçäyé Viñëu's crown had been stolen by the demons, Garuòa
attacked the thieves, killed them, and recovered the Lord's crown. As all this was happening, Lord
Kñérodakaçäyé Viñëu descended to the earth where Lord Kåñëa was performing His pastimes, and
entered Lord Kåñëa's body. In this way Lord Kñérodakaçäyé Viñëu appeared during Lord Kåñëa's
incarnation. Garuòa, trying the return the crown, was unable to find his master in the spiritual
world. He finally found Kñérodakaçäyé Viñëu manifested within the form of Lord Kåñëa (who was
then enjoying pastimes on the peak of Gomanta Mountain). Garuòa then returned his master's
crown."


Text 9


   ato yathä krama-mukti-marge 'rcir-ädi-krama evängé nadé-raçmy-ädi-vividha-kramas tu tad-
aìgatvenaiva prastüyate tadvad ihäpéti. arcir-ädinä tat-pratitheù ity eña nyäyo 'tra
dåñöäntäyitavyaù.

   ataù-therefore; yatha-just as; krama-mukti-marge-on the path of liberation; arciù-the sun's rays;
adi-beginning with; kramaù-path; eva-certainly; angi-the living entity; nadi- subtle passages; rasmi-
beams of light; adi-beginning with; vividha-various; kramaù-paths; tu-also; tat-angatvena-having
these paths; prastuyate-is glorified; tadvat-in this way; iha- here; api-also; iti-thus; arciù-beams of
sunlight; adina- beginning with; tat-prathiteù-the manifestation; iti-thus; esaù-this; nyayaù-the
Vedanta-sutra; atra-in this matter; drstantayitavyaù-may be given as an example.


  How the different forms of Godhead appear in the transcendental body of Lord Kåñëa may be
understood from the following statement of Vedänta-sütra (4.3.1):

arcir-ädinä tat-prathiteù

  "At the time of death, the perfect yogés can travel to any planet using the sun's rays, the subtle
nadé passages extending throughout the universe, the passages of air, or celestial airplanes, as their
means of tranport."

   Just as the yogés may travel in this way to attain liberation or residence in a higher planet, in the
same way the various forms of the Personality of Godhead may easily enter the body of Lord Kåñëa,
and appear with Him as He displays His pastimes on earth.


Text 10


tad etad eväha

tvaà brahma paramaà vyoma
   puruñah prakåteh paraù
avatérëo 'si bhagavan
   svecchopätta-påthag-vapuù

   tat-therefore; etat-this; eva-certainly; aha-he says; tvam-You; brahma-spirit; paramam-supreme;
vyoma-the master of the spiritual world; puruñaù-the Supreme Person; prakrteù-to touch of
material nature; paraù-above; avatirnah asi-You have descended; bhagavan-O Original Personality
of Godhead; sva-iccha-of Your devotees to fulfill the desires; apatta- accepting; prthak-various;
vapuù-forms.


   That all forms Godhead are manifested from the body of Lord Kåñëa is confirmed by the
following statement of Uddhava (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.11.28):

   "O Lord Kåñëa, You are the Original Personality of Godhead, the master of the spiritual world of
Vaikuëöha. You appear in this material world, assuming the forms of Your many incarnations just
to fulfill the desires of Your devotees."


Text 11


   säkñäd bhagavän eva tvam avatérëo 'si. bhagavata eva vaibhavam äha brahma tvam
paramavyomäkhyo vaikuëöhas tvam prakåteù paraù puruñaù api tvam iti. bhagavän api kathaà-
bhütaù sann avatérëaù svecchamayasya ity anusäreëa sveçäà sarveçäm eva bhaktänäà ya icchä
pürayitum upattäni tatas tataù svata akåñöäni pthag-vapüàsi nija-tat-tad-ävirbhäva yena tathä-
bhütaù sann iti.

   saksat-directly; bhagavan-the Original Personality of Godhead; eva-certainly; tvam avatirnah asi-
is meant by the phrase "tvam avatirno 'si"; bhagavataù-of the Personality of Godhead; vaibhavam-
the opulence; aha-he describes; brahma tvam-"You are the Supreme spirit; paramavyoma-akhyaù-
who is known as the master of the spiritual sky; vaikunthaù-the master of Vaikunthaloka; tvam-
You are; prakrteh paraù-beyond the touch of material nature; puruñaù-the Supreme Person; api-
also; tvam- You are; iti-thus; bhagavan-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; api-although; katham-
bhutaù-in what manner?; san-being so; avartirnaù-descended to the material world; sva-iccha-
mayasya- according to His own desire; iti-thus; anusarena-in accordance; svesam-of His own;
sarvesam-of all; eva-certainly; bhaktanam- His devotees; ya-which; iccha-desire; tam-that;
purayitum-to fulfill; upattani-accepted; tatah tataù-in various places; svataù-from Himself; akrstani-
manifested; pthak-various; vapumsi-forms; nija-His own; tat-tat-various;avirbhavaù- appearance;
yena-by that; tatha-bhutaù-in that way; san-being; iti-thus.


   In this verse the phrase "tvam avatérëo 'si" means "O Supreme Personality of Godhead, You have
now descended to this material world." The Supreme Lord's glories and opulences are described in
the following words: "brahma tvam (You are the Supreme Spirit), "vyoma" (You are the master of
the spiritual world of Vaikuëöha), and "prakåteù paraù puruñaù" (You are the Supreme Person,
beyond the touch of material energy).
   Someone may ask: Why does the Supreme Personality of Godhead descend to this material
world?
   The answer is given in the word "svecchopatta-påthag-vapuù" (You appear in many forms in
order to fulfill the desires of Your devotees).
   By describing Lord Kåñëa in this way, Uddhava affirms that Kåñëa is the Original Personality of
Godhead, who assumes many forms to please His devotees.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.91
records.text:
Text 1


tathä

sva-çänta-rüpeñv itaraiù sva-rüpair
   abhyardyamäneñv anukampitätmä
parävareço mahad-aàça-yukto
   hy ajo 'pi jäto bhagavän yathägniù

   tatha-in the same way; sva-çänta-rüpeçu-unto the peaceful devotees of the Lord; itaraiù-othes,
nondevotees; sva-rüpaiù-according to their own modes of nature; abhyardyamäneçu-being harassed
by; anukampita-ätmä-the all-compassionate Lord; para-avara-spiritual and material; éçaù-
controller; mahat-aàça-yuktaù-accompanied by the plenary portion of mahat-tattva; hi-certainly;
ajaù-the unborn; api- although; jätaù-is born; bhagavän-the Personality of Godhead; yathä-as if;

agniù-the fire.


  That Çré Kåñëa is the Original Personality of Godhead from whom all other forms of Godhead
emanate is confirmed in the following statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (3.2.15):

   "Lord Kåñëa, the Original Personality of Godhead, the all-compassionate controller of both the
spiritual and material creations, is unborn, but when there is friction between His peaceful devotees
and persons who are in the material modes of nature, He takes birth just like fire, accompanied by
His plenary expansions."*


Text 2


   tac ca janma nija-tat-tad-aàçäny ädäyaivety äha mahad-aàça-yuktaù mahataù svasyaiväàçair
yuktaù. mahantaà vibhum ätmänam ity ädi çruteù: mahadvac ca iti nyäya-prasiddheç ca, mahanto
ye puruñädayo 'àçäs tair yuktaù iti vä. loka-näthaà mahad bhütam itivad ätmatvävyabhicäraù.
mahadbhir aàçibhir aàçaiç ca yukta iti vä. viduraà çrémad-uddhavaù.

    tat-therefore; ca-also; janma-birth; nija-own; tata-tat-various; amsani-expansions; adaya-
accepting; aha-he says; maùat-amsa-yuktaù-the word "mahad-amsa-yuktah"; mahataù- from the
supremely great Personality of Godhead; svasya-from Yourself; eva-certainly; amsaiù-by the
expansions; yuktaù- accompanied; mahantan-the supremely great; vibhum-all-powerful; atmanan-
Personality of Godhead; iti-thus; adi-in the passage beginning with; sruteù-from the sruti-sastra
(Kaöha Upaniñad 2.22); mahadvat-supremely great; ca-also; iti-thus; nyaya-in the Vedanta-sutra
(1.4.8); prasiddheù-in the celebrated quotation; ca-also; mahantaù-great; puruña-adayaù-the puruña-
avataras and other forms of Godhead; amsaù-expansions; taiù-by them; yuktaù-accompanied; iti-
thus; va-or; loka-of all planetary systems; natham-the master; mahat-bhutam-the supreme living
entity; itivat-in this way; atmatva-form; avyabhicaraù- eternal and unchanging nature; mahadbhiù-
by great; amsibhiù- original expansions; amsaiù-secondary expansions; ca-also; uktaù-accompanied;
iti-thus; va-or; viduram-to Vidura; çrémat-uddhavaù-spoken by Uddhava.


   This verse describes how Lord Kåñëa, accompanied by His expansions, takes birth in the material
world. The word "mahat" in this verse means "the supremely opulent Personality of Godhead", and
the phrase "mahad-aàça-yuktaù" means "accompanied by the expansions of the supremely opulent
Personality of Godhead". This use of the word "mahat" may be seen in the following quotations
from Vedic literature:

mahantaà vibhum ätmänam

   "The Personality of Godhead is full of all powers and opulences."
              -Kaöha Upaniñad 1.2.22

mahad-vac ca

  "The Absolute Truth is the reservoir of all transcendental opulences."
            -Vedänta-sütra 1.4.8

loka-näthaà mahad bhütam

   "The Personality of Godhead is the master of all planetary systems. He is the supreme living
being, full of all powers and opulences."
                 -Viñëu-sahasra-näma-stotra

   Understood in this way, the word "mahat" may refer to the puruña-incarnations of the Lord, or
the Lord's primary or secondary expansions.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.92
records.text:
Text 1


   athaivam athäham aàça-bhägena ity ädäv apy evaà vyäkhyeyam. aàçänäà bhägo bhajanaà
praveço yatra tena paripürëa-rüpeëa bhajanena lakñito vä. präpsyämi iti prakaöa-léläbhipräyeëa
bhaviçyan nirdeçaù. ata eva tad-avatära-samaye yugävatäräç ca sa evety abhipretyäha

   atha-now; evam-in this way; atha aham amsa-bhagena-iti-adau-Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.2.9; api-
also; evam-in this way; vyakhyenam-should be understood; amsanam-of the expansions; bhagaù-the
word "bhagah"; bhajanam-means "part"; pravesaù- entrance; yatra-where; tena-with that; paripurna-
perfect and complete; rupena-form; amsanam-of the expansions; bhajanena- with a part; laksitaù-
characterized; va-or; prapsyami iti-the word "prapsyami"; prakata-manifests; lila-pastimes;
abhiprayena-with the meaning; bhavisyat-future; nirdesaù- instruction; atah eva-therefore; tat-of
the Lord; avatara-of incarnation; samaye-at the time; yuga-avataraù-incarnations of the various
ages; ca-also; saù-He; eva-certainly; iti- thus; abhipretya-intending; aha-said.


   That the various incarnations of Godhead appear within the body of Lord Kåñëa gives us the key
to properly understand the following verse spoken by Lord Kåñëa to Yogamäyä (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.2.9):

athäham aàça-bhägena
   devakyäù putratäà çubhe
präpsyämi tvaà yaçodäyäà
   nanda-patnyäà bhaviñyasi

   "O all-auspicious Yogamäyä, accompanied by My plenary expansions, I shall then appear as the
son of Devaké, and you will appear as the daughter of mother Yaçodä, the queen of Mahäräja
Nanda."

   In this verse the word "aàça-bhägena" means "with some of My plenary expansions". The word
"präpsyämi" (I shall become the son of Devaké) shows us the Lord's plan for performing pastimes in
the material world.
   When Lord Kåñëa appears in the material world, all the yuga-avatäras also appear within His
body. This is confirmed in the following statement of Gargäcärya in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.13):


Text 2


äsan varëäs trayo hy asya
   gåhëato 'nuyugaà tanüù
çuklo raktas tathä péta
   idänéà kåñëatäà gataù

   äsan-were assumed; varëäù trayaù-three colors; hi- indeed; asya-of your son Kåñëa; gåhëataù-
accepting; anuyugam tanüù-transcendental bodies according to the different yugas; çuklaù-
sometimes white; raktaù-sometimes red; tathä-as well as; pétaù-sometimes yellow; idäném kåñëatäm
gataù-at the present moment He has assumed a blackish color.


   "Your son Kåñëa appears as an incarnation in every millennium. In the past, He assumed three
different colors-white, red and yellow-and now He has appeared in a blackish color. [In another
Dväpara-yuga, He appeared (as Lord Rämacandra) in color of çuka, a parrot. All such incarnations
have now assembled in Kåñëa]."*


Text 3


   asya tava putrasya pratiyugam tanuù prakaöayato yadyapi çukla-ädayaù träyaù apy anye varëa
äsan tathäpi idäném asya pradurbhavavaty asmin dväpare tu sa çuklaù yugävatäras tathä raktaù
pétaù apy etad apy upalakñaëam anya-dväpara-yugävatäraù çuka-pakña-varëo 'pi kåñëatam eva gataù
etasmin antarbhüta ity arthaù. tasmät kåñëi-kartåtvät svayaà-kåñëatvät sarväkarñakatväc ca kåñëa
ity ekam asya nämeti prakaraëiko 'py arthaù çreyän tathä ca çré-karabhäjanena
yugävatäropasanäyäm uktam

   asya-the word "asya"; tava-of you; putrasya-of the son; pratiyugam-in each yuga; prakatayataù-
appearing; yadyapi- although; sukla-adayaù-beginning with a white form; trayaù- three; api-also;
varnaù-colors; asan-were assumed; tathapi- nevertheless; idanim-at the present moment; asya-of
Him; pradurvbhavavati-manifested; asmin-during this; dvapare- Dvapara-yuga; tu-but; saù-He;
suklaù-white; yuga-avataraù- incarnation of the age; tatha-in the same way; raktaù-red; pitaù-
yellow; api-also; etat-this; api-also; upalaksanam- characteristic; anya-other; dvapara-yuga-during
Dvapara-yuga; avataraù-incarnation; suka-paksa-varnaù-the color of a parrot's feather; api-
although; kåñëatam-a blackish color; eva- certainly; gataù-assumed; etasmin-in this; antarbhute-

separately considered; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; tasmat- therefore; kåñëi-kartrtvat-because of
appearing with a blackish complexion; svayam-kåñëatvat-because He is originally known as "Kåñëa";
sarva-akarsakatvat-because He is all-atractive; ca- also; kåñah iti-"Kåñëa"; ekam-sole; asya-of Him;
nama-name; iti-thus; prakaranikaù-in this matter; api-also; artha- meaning; sreyan-best; tatha-in
the same way; ca-also; çré-karabhajanena-by Karabhajana Muni; yuga-avatara-of the yuga-avataras;
upasanayam-in the matter of worshipping; uktam-spoken (Bhäg. 11.5.27-29).


   This verse may be paraphrased in the following way: "Your son Kåñëa appears as an incarnation
in every millenium. In the past He assumed three different colors-white, red, and yellow -and now
He has appeared in a blackish color. In another Dväpara-yuga He appeared (as Lord Rämacandra)
in the color of çuka, a parrot. All such incarnations have now assembled in Kåñëa."*

    Because the Original Personality of Godhead has a blackish complexion (kåñëa), and because He
is all-attractive (kåñëa), He is therefore known as "Kåñëa".
    In the course of describing the worship of the yuga-avatäras, Karabhäjana Muni gives the
following description of Lord Kåñëa (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.5.27-29):


Text 4


dväpare bhagavän çyämaù
    péta-väsä nijäyudhaù
çré-vatsädibhir aìkaiç ca
    lakñaëair upalakñitaù

   dväpare-in Dväpara-yuga; bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; çyämaù-blackish; péta-
väsäù- having yellow clothes; nija-own; äyudhaù-having weapons; çré-ädibhiù-such as Çrévatsa;
aìkaiù-by bodily markings; ca-and; lakñaëaiù-by external characteristics such as the Kaustubha
jewel; upalakñtitaù-characterized.


   "In the Dväpara-yuga the Personality of Godhead appears in a blackish hue. He is dressed in
yellow, He holds His own weapons, and He is decorated with the Kaustubha jewel and marks of
Çrévatsa. This is how His symptoms are described.*


Text 5


taà tadä puruñaà martyä
   mahä-räjopalakñaëam
yajanti veda-tanträbhyäà
   paraà jijïäsavo nåpa

   tam-Him; tadä-in that age; puruñam-the supreme enjoyer; martyäù-mortal men; mahä-räja-a
great king; upalalçaëam- playing the role of; yajanti-they worship; veda-tantryäbhyäm- according to
both the original Vedas and ritual tantras; param- the Supreme; jijïäsavaù-those who want to gain
knowledge; nåpa-O king.


   "O king, following the Vedas and Tantras, seekers of the truth worship the Supreme Personality
of Godhead, who then appears as a great king.


Text 6


namas te väsudeväya
   namaù saìkarñaëäya ca
pradyumnäyäniruddhäya
   tubhyaà bhagavate namaù

   namaù-let me offer my respectful obeisances; te-unto You; väsudeväya-Lord Väsudeva; namaù-
respectful obeisances; saìkarñanäya ca-also to Lord Saìkarñaëa; pradyumnäya-to Lord Pradyumna;
aniruddhäya-unto Aniruddha; tubhyam-unto You; bhagavate-unto the Supreme Personality of
Godhead; namaù-my respectful ovbeisances.


   "I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, expanded
asVäsudeva, Saìkarñaëa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha."*


Text 7


   atra çré-kåñëatve liìgam mahäräjopalakçaëam iti väsudeva ity ädi ca çré-harivaàçoka-räja-
räjäbhiçekäd dvärakäyäà catur-vyühatva-prasiddheù. gargaù çré-nandam.

   atra-here; çré-kåñëatve-in the position of Lord Kåñëa; liìgam-the characteristic; mahä-räja-
upalakñaëam iti-the passage beginning "mahäräjopalalakñaëam"; väsudeva iti ädi-the passage
beginning "väsudeva"; ca-also; çré-hari-vaàça-in the Hari-vämça; ukta-described; räja-of Lord Kåñëa;
räja-abhiçekät-because of the coronation; dvarakäyäm-in Dvärkä; catur-vyühatva-as the four catur-
vyuha expansions; prasiddheù-because of fame; gargaù-spoken by Gargäcärya; çré-nandam-to Nanda
Mahäräja.


   In the verses Karabhäana Muni describes (mahäräjopalakñaëam) the appearance in the Dväara-
yuga of Lord Kåñëa, who was crowned king of Dvärakä (Hari-vaàça, Viñëu-parva, Chapter 50), and
who remained in Dvärakä with His catur-vyüha expansions. The verse under discussion (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.8.13, quoted in Text 2) was spoken by Gargäcärya to Nanda Mahäräja.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.93
records.text:
Text 1


   tad evaà çré-kåñëasya svayaà-bhagavatte suñöhu nirdhärite nityam eva tad-rüpatveëasthitir api
svayam eva siddhä. tathäpi tävad-ärädhanaväkyenaiva sa sidhyati. ärädhyasyäbhäva
ärädhanänodanäya vipralipsä-janyatvätteh. tac ca paramäpte çäçtre na sambhavati. sambhave ca
puruñärthäbhävät çästränarthakyam.

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; çré-kåñëasya-of Çré Kåñëa; svayam-bhagavatte-in the position of
the Supreme Personality of Godhead; suñöhu-properly; nidhärite-determined; nityam-eternally; eva-
certainly; tat-His; rüpatvena-manifestation as form; avasthitiù situation; api-also; svayam-
automatically ; eva-certainly; siddha-is established; tathäpi-still; manda-dhiyäm-of those who are
unintelligent; bhranti-mistake; hana- refutation; artham-for the purpose; idam-thus; vivriyate-is
explained; tatra-in this connection; tävat-to that extent; ärädhana of worship; väkyena-by the
description; sa-that; sidhyati is proven; ärädhyasya-of the worshipable; abhäve-in the non-
existence; ärädhana-worship; nodanäyaù-because of encouraging; vipralipsa-cheating; janyatva-
because of being produced from; äpatteù-because of the calamity; tat-that; ca- also; parama-äpte-
which contains the description of the ultimate goal of life; çästre-in the scripture; na-not;
sambhavati-is possible; sambhave-in the arisal; puruña-artha-ofthe ultimate goal of life; abhävät-
because of non-existence; çästra-of the book; anarthakyam-uselessness.


   Although we have clearly proven that Çré Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead and His
form is eternal, doubt may linger in the minds of the less intelligent, to erädicate these doubts we
shall continue this description of Çré Kåñëa. That the form of Kåñëa is eternal is proven by the
Vedic literatures' repeated order that Kåñëa be worshiped. If the form of Kåñëa were only a
temporary manifestation, then what is the use of worshiping Him? If the scriptures advise us to
worship that which is temporary, then the scriptures are defective and are cheating us. In truth the
Vedic literatures teach us the supreme goal of life, and they are free from all defect. If they instruct
us to worship Çré Kåñëa, then the form of Çré Kåñëa is certainly eternal and spiritual. Kåñëa is not a
temporary manifestation of material energy.


Sarva-samvädini Comment


Text 1


   atha dvi-navätétama-väkyänantaraà nityatva-prakaraëe "çästränarthakyam ity asyänantaram
idaà vivecanéyam "nanu bäläturädy-upacchanda-väkyavat taj-jïana-mätreëäpipuruñärtha-siddhir

dåçyate; tato närthäntara-sambhave tat smäraka-väkyaà karaëam ; kintu prathamatas tad-
abhirucite tadäném asaty api vastu-viçeçe tädéya-hita-vastv-antara-cittävatätäräya balädén iva
maträdi-väkyaà saguä-viçeçsädhakäm pravartayati çästram; paçcäd yathä svahite krameëasvayam
eva pravartante balädayas tathä balavac chästrätaraàdåçtvä nirguëe vä nitya-prakaöya-
vaikuëöhanätha-lakñaëasaguëe vä pravartsyante iti.

   atha-now; dvi-navatitama-väkya-the 92nd Anuccheda; anantaram-after; nityatva-of the
eternality; prakarane-in the explanation; çästra-anarthakyam iti-the passage ending with the word
"çästranarthakyam" (Text 1); asya-that; anantaram-after; idam-this; vivecaniyam-may be considerd;
nanu-is it not so?; bala-child; atura-sick; ädi-beginning with; upacchandana-coaxing; väkya-the
statement; vat-like; tat-that; jïänamatrena-by that knowledge; api-also; puruña-artha-of the benefit
of human life; siddhiù-the perfection; drsyate-is seen; tataù-from that; na-not; artha-meaning;
antara-another; sambhave-in the manifestation; tat-that;smaraka-väkyam-as a remainder; karanam-
cause; kintu- however; prathamataù-at first; tat-abhirucite-pleasing;tadanim- then; asati-unreal; api-
although; vastu-substance; visese- specific; tädiya-in relation to him; hita-welfare; vastu- substance;
antara-another; citta-consciousness; avatäraya-for bringing; bala-ädin-to children and others; iva-
just like; matra-ädi-väkyam-statement; sa-gun-with qualities; visese- specific; sadhakam-spiritual
aspirants; pravartayati-teaches; çästram-the knowledge of the Vedic scriptures; pascat- afterwards;
yatha-just as; sva-hite-in that which is beneficial; kramana-gradually; svayam-directly; eva-
certainly; pravartante- are manifest; bala-adayaù-stregnth of the arguments; tatha-in the same way;
balavat-as strong; çästra-the Vedic scriptures; antaram-other; dåñötvä-having seen; nirgune-in the
qualityless Absolute; va-or; nitya-eternal; prakatya- manifes
tation; vaikuntha-natha-of Lord Näräyaëa, the master of Vaikuntha; lakñaëa-characteristics; sa-
gune-with qualities; va-or; pravartsyante-will be manifest; iti-thus.


   After reading the argument of Anuccheda 93, Text 1, someone may raise the following
objection: When a child is stricken with a disease, one may speak many untrue words to coax him
to take a medicine which will cure him. In the same way, the Vedas instruct the conditioned souls
to worship the Personality of Godhead. This is certainly benefical for the conditioned souls who
become purified by that worship and enabled to understand the actual nature of the Absolute,
which is formless and without qualities.


Text 2


   tan na ananta-guëa-rüpädi-vaibhava-nityäspadatvättad-rüpeëävasthitir näsambhaviteti yad
bhütaà bhävac ca bhaviñyac ca iti çruteh, sambhavitayaà tu tasyäm avatära-väkyaà cävatärasya
prapaïca-gata-tadéya-prakäça-mätra-lakñaëatvät. näräyaëädénäà ca tatraivävatäre praveça-mätra-
vivakñato na virudhyate.

   tat-that; na-is not so; ananta-unlimited guna-qualities; rüpa-and forms; ädi-beginning with;
vaibhava-opulence and power; nitya-eternal; aspadatvät-because of being the abode; tat-rupena-
with his form; avasthitiù-situation; na-not; asambhavita- unworthy of being accepted; iti-thus; iti-

thus; yat-what; bhutam- was; bhavat-is; ca-also; bhavisyat-will be; ca-also; iti-thus; çrusteù-from the
Brhad-aranyaka Upaniñad 3.8.3; sambhavitayam- accepted; tu-also; tasyam-when this; avatära-about
the incarnations of the Lord; väkyam-the statement; ca-also; avatärasya-of the Lord's incarnation;
prapanca-to the material universe; gata-travelled; tädiya-His; prakäça-manifestation; matra-only;
lakñaëatvät-because of the charasteristic; näräyaëa-ädinam-of Lord Näräyaëa and the other forms
of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ca-also; tatra-there; eva-certainly; avatäre-in the
incarnation; pravesa-entrance; matra-only; vivakñataù-because of the intention to describe; na-not;
virudhyate-is conträdicted.


   To this objection I reply: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is an eternal reservoir of
unlimited transcendental qualities, opulences and forms. The Supreme Personality of Godhead and
His various incarnations such as Lord Näräyaëa and others, are eternally present in the spiritual
world, although they enter this material world as incarnations for a certain limited period of time.
Because they are present in the spiritual world, the Båhad-äraëyaka Upaniñad explains (3.8.3):
    ,sy 168The Absolute Truth exists eternally. He was in the past. He is in the present. He will be
in the future."

   This describes the eternal form of the Lord.


Text 3

   kià cottara-mémämsäyäà tat-tad-upasana-çästrokta yä yä mürtis tädvatya eva devatäù iti
siddhänta-grahaù.

   kim ca-furthermore; uttara-mimasayam-in the Uttara-mimasa; tat-tat-of various; upasana-
methods of worship; çästra- literature; uktaù-statements; ya ya-whatever; murtiù-form; tadvatyaù-in
that way; eva-certainly; devataù-dieties; iti-thus; siddhanta-graha-acceptance of the conclusion.


   The eternality of the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is also described in the
following statement of the Uttara-mémäàsä: "The Supreme is manifest in many forms".


Text 4


tataç ca

taà péöhagaà ye tu yajanti dhéräs
   teñäà sukhaà çäçvataà netareñäm

ity ädika gopäla-täpany-upaniñad api yenänyäthä manyate tasya tu mahad eva sähasam.

   tataù-then; ca-also; tam-Him; pitha-gam-in His abode; ye-those who; tu-certainly; yajanti-

worship; dhiraù-advanced saintly persons; tesam-of them; sukham-happiness;sasvatam-eternal; na -
not; itaresam-of others; iti-thus; ädika-in the passage beginning; çré-gopäla-täpané-upaniñat-Gopäla-
täpané Upaniñad (1.23); api-also; yena-by which; ayathä-artha-to think otherwise; manyate-is
considered; tasya-of that; tu-but; mahat-great; eva-certainly; sahasam-crime.


   The eternality of the form of the Personality of Godhead is also described in the following
statement of the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad (1.20)

   "They who are intelligent worship Lord Kåñëa. They, and not others, attain eternal
transcendental bliss."

  This verse clearly describes the Lord's form as eternal. They who would interpret it in another
way are committing a great violence to the meaning of the scriptures.


Text 5


   atra ca çäçvata-sukha-phala-präpti-çravaëät tat-péöhasya yajanaà vinäjïänäm sahasamayam
jïänän mokñaù iti småteù. atraiva dhérä iti viçeñaëäd bäläturavad bhävas teñäà düra evotsäritaù.
netareñäm iti nirdharaëena tad-yajanasya paramparä-hetutvam api niñidhyate.

   atra-here; ca-also; sasvata-eternal; sukha-of happiness; phala-of the result; prapti-the attainment;

   In this verse the worshipers of Lord Kåñëa are described as the possesors of eternal happiness.
This means they are liberated from material entanglement, for as long as one remains in the
clutches of matter his position is continuously changing, and he cannot attain eternal happiness.
Because the devotees of Lord Kåñëa are thus liberated, one cannot say that they are ignorant of the
actual nature of things, for knowledge is a prerequisite for liberation. This is confirmed by the
Småti-çästra, which says:

   "When one attains transcendental knowledge he becomes liberated."

   Our opponent says the devotees of the Lord are in a lesser position, and he pushes forward the
example of cajoling the sick child to convince him to take the medicine. This example is not very
appropriate, for the devotees of the Lord are described as "dhéra", advanced saintly persons. They
are not at all like ignorant children. Our opponent would have it that there are different stage of

spiritual advancement, and the devotees are in the lower stage, while the impersonalists are on the
higher stage. This view is rejected by this statement of Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad, which considers
the devotees of the Lord the best of transcendentalists ("Only such devotees of the Lord, and not
others, are able to attain eternal transcendental bliss").

described in this verse is empty and useless. Actually such meditation is not at all useless, for by
continually meditating on the form of the Lord Kåñëa, one may eventually see Him face-to-face.

   deve varñati yajïa-viplava-ruçä vajräçma-varñänalaiù
   sédat-päle-paçu-striyätma-çaraëaà dåñövänukampy utsmayan

     bibhrad goñöham apan mahendra-mada-bhit préyan na indro gaväm";

spañöam-the meaning is clear; çré-sukaù-spoken by Çukadeva Gosvämé.

   That Çré Kåñëa is the eternal Personality of Godhead is also confirmed in the following
statement of the cowherd residents of Våndävana (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.26.25):

   "Let Kåñëa, who is so kind, beautiful and merciful, protect us. When angry Indra sent torrents of
rain, accompanied by showers of ice blocks and high wind, He immediately took compassion upon
us and saved us and our families, cows and valuable possessions by picking up the Govardhana Hill,
just as a child picks up a mushroom. He saved us so wonderfully. May He continue to mercifully
glance over us and our cows. May we live peacefully under the protection of wonderful Kåñëa."*

This verse is spoken by Çukadeva Gosvämé.
