    tértha-çravaù çravaëa-maìgala pähi bhåtyän

spañöam.çré-sütaù.

   tatha-in the same way; çré-kåñëa-O Çré Kåñëa; kåñëa-sakha-O friend of Arjuna; våñëi-of
descendants of Våñëi; rsabha-O chief; avani-the earth; dhruk-rebellious; rajanya-vamsa- dynasties
of the kings; dahana-O annihilator; anapavarga- without deterioration of; virya-prowess; govinda-O
proprietor of Goloka-dhama; gopa-vanita-by the gopés; vraja-of Vrajabhumi;bhrtya-by Your
servants; gita-sung; tritha-sravaù- Your glories; sravana-maìgala-whose glories are auspicious to
hear; pahi-please protect; bhrtyan-Your servants.


   That Çré Kåñëa is eternal is also confirmed by the following verse spoken by Süta Gosvämé
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 12.11.25):
   "O Kåñëa, O friend of Arjuna, O chief among the descendants of Våñëi, You are the destroyer of
those political parties which are disturbing elements on this earth. Your prowess never deteriorates.
You are the proprietor of the transcendental abode. The gopés and Your other servants in
Vrajabhümi continually chant Your transcendental glories, which are auspicious to hear. O Lord
please protect us, who are Your servants."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.96
records.text:
Text 1

api ca svayam eva sva-vigraham eva lakñyé-kåtyäha

tadä väà parituñöo 'ham
   amunä vapuçänaghe
tapasä çraddhayä nityaà
   bhaktyä ca hådi bhävitaù

präduräsaà varada-räd
   yuvayoù käma-ditsayä
vriyatäà vara ity ukte
   mädåço väà våtaù sutaù

   api ca-furthermore; svayam-personally; sva-His own; vigraham-form; eva-certainly; laksyi-kåta-
revealing; aha- said; tadä-then (after the expiry of twelve thousand celestial years); väm-with both
of you; parituçtaù aham-I was very much satisfied; amunä-by this; vapusä-in this form as Kåñëa;
anaghe-O My dear sinless mother; tapasä-by austerity; çraddhayä-by faith; nityam-constantly
(engaged); bhaktyä-by devotional service; ca-as well as; hådi-within the core of the heart; bhävitaù-
fixed (in determination); präduräsam-appeared before you (in the same way); vara-da-rät-the best
of all who can bestow benedictions; yuvayoù-of both of you; käma-ditsayä-wishing to fulfill the
desire; vriyatäm-asked you to open your minds; varaù-for a benediction; iti ukte-when you were
requested in this way; mädåçaù-exactly like Me; väm-of both of you; våtaù-was asked;sutaù-as Your
son (you wanted a son exactly like Me).


  This also confirmed in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.37-38) spoken by Lord
Kåñëa when He revealed His Original form to Vasudeva and Devaké within Kaàsa's prison:

   "O sinless mother Devaké, after the expiry of twelve thousand celestial years, in which you
constantly comtemplated Me within the core of your heart with great faith, devotion and austerity,
I was very much satisfied with you. Since I am the best of all bestowers of benediction, I appeared
in this same form as Kåñëa to ask you to take from Me the benediction you desired. You then
expressed your desire to have a son exactly like Me."*


Text 2


ity upakramya

adåçtvänyatamaà loke
   çélaudärya-guëaiù samam
ahaà suto väm abhavaà
   påçnigarbha iti çrutaù

   iti-thus; upakramya-adåçtvä-not finding; anyatamam- anyone else; loke-in this world; çéla-

audärya-guëaiù-with the transcendental qualities of good character and magnamimity; samam-
equal to you; aham-I; sutaù-the son; väm-of both of you; abhavam-became; påçni-garbhaù-
celebrated born as Påçni; iti-thus; çrutaù-I am known.


   The Lord further explained (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.41-43):

   "Since I found no one else as highly elevated as you in simplicity and other qualities of good
character, I appeared in this world as Påçnigarbha, or one who is celebrated as having taken birth
from Påçni."*


Text 3


tayor väà punar eväham
   ädityäm äsa kaçyapät
upendra iti vikhyäto
   vämanatväc ca vämanaù

   tayoù-of you two, husband and wife; väm-in both of you; punaù eva-even again; aham-I Myself;
ädityäm-in the womb of Aditi; äsa-appeared; kaçyapät-by the semen of Kaçyapa Muni; upendraù-by
the name Upendra; iti-thus; vikhyätaù- celebrated; vämanatvät ca-and because of being dwarf;
vämanaù-I was known as Vämana.


  "In the next millennium, I again appeared from the two of you, who appeared as My mother,
Aditi, and My father, Kaçyapa. I was known as Upendra, and because of being a dwarf, I was also
known as Vämana."*


Text 4


tåtéye 'smin bhave 'ham vai
    tenaiva vapuçätha eväm
jäto bhüyas tayor eva
    satyaà me vyähåtaà sati iti.

   tåtéye-for the third time; asmin bhave-in this appearance (as Kåñëa); aham-I Myself; vai-indeed;
tena- with the same personality ; eva-in this way; vapuçä-by the form; atha-as; väm-of both of you;
jätaù-born; bhüyaù- again; tayoù-of both of you; eva-indeed; satyam-take as truth; me-My;
vyähåtam-words; sati-O supremely chaste; iti- thus.


   "O supremely chaste mother, I, the same personality, have now appeared of you both as your son

for the third time. Take My words as the truth."*


Text 5


    amunä çré-kåñëasya mama prädurbhava-samaye 'tra prakäçamähenaitena çré-kåñëakhyenaiva.
tritéye iti tenaiva pürvaà varärthaà prädurbhavitenaiva.

   amuna-by this form; çré-kåñëasya-of Çré Kåñëa; mama-My; pradurbhava-of appearance; samaye-at
the time; atra-here; prakäçamanena-appearing; etena-with this; çré-kåñëa-akhyena- named Çré-
Kåñëa; trtiye-in the third appearance; iti-thus; tena-with the same personality; eva-in the same way;
pürvam- formerly; vara-benediction; artham-for the purpose of fulfilling; pradurbhavitena-
manifested; eva-certainly.


   In this last verse the Supreme Personality of Godhead explains that He has now appeared in His
original form as Lord Kåñëa before Vasudeva and Devaké in order to fulfill the benediction formerly
granted to them. This is the third time He had appeared as their son.


Text 6


   ata eva påçnigarbhäditvenaiva vapuñä ity uktatvät, na tu tadäném adhunaiva svayam eva
babhüva, kintv aàçenaiveti gamyate.

   atah eva-therefore; påñëigarbha-äditvena-as the origin of Lord Påñëigarbha and other expansions
of Godhead; eva-certainly; vapusa-by using the word "vapusa"; iti-thus; nuktatvät-because of
speaking; na-not; tu-but; tadanim-then; adhuna-now; eva- certainly; svayam-personally; eva-
certainly; babhuva-has appeared; kintu-but; amsena-as an expansion; eva-certainly; iti-thus;
gamyate-is intended.


   In these verses the word "vapuñä" (personally) is used by the Lord to describe His appearance as
Kåñëa, and it is not used to describe His appearance as Lord Vämana or Lord Påçnigarbha. From this
we may conclude that Lord Vämana and Lord Påçnigarbha are immediate expansions of the
Original Godhead, and Lord Kåñëa is the Original Form of the Personality of Godhead, the origin
of Lord Påçnigarbha, Vämana, and all other incarnations of Godhead.


Text 7


   påçnigarbhas tu te buddhim ätmmänam bhagavän paraù ity aträpy etad eva gir-devyä sücitam
asti.

   påñëigarbhaù-Lord Påñëigarbha; tu-indeed; te-your; buddhim-intelligence; atmanam-your soul;
bhagavan-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; paraù-transcendental; iti-thus; atra- in these
words; api-also; etat-this; eva-certainly; gih-devya-by Sarasvati, the goddess of learning; sucitam-
indicated; asti-is.


    That Lord Påçnigarbha is an expansion of Godhead, and not the Original Form of the Godhead
is described in the following eloquent prayer, which clearly distinguishes Lord Påçnigarbha from
the original Personality of Godhead (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.6.25):

   "May Lord Påçnigarbha protect your intelligence, and may the Supreme Personality of Godhead
protect your soul."*


Text 8


   ata eva tåtéye eva bhäve tat-sädåça-präpti lakñaëa-varasya parama-pürëatväpekñayä 'taträiva
satyaà me vyähåtam ity uktaà catur-bhujatvaà cedaà rüpaà çré-kåñëa eva kåñëavatärotsava-ity-
ädibhis tasyätyanta-prasiddheù. çré-bhagavän çré-devaké-devém.

   atah eva-therefore; trtiye-for the third time; eva- certainly; bhave-in the appearance; tat-sadrsa-
like Himself; suta-son; prapti-attainment; lakñaëa-characterized; varasya- of the benediction;
parama-pürëatva-supreme perfection and completeness; apekñaya-in relation to; tatra-there; eva-
certainly; satyam-take as truth; me-My; vyahrtam-words; iti- thus; uktam-spoken; catuh-bhujatvam-
status as the four-handed Lord Viñëu; ca-also; idam-this; rüpam-form; çré-kåñëaù-Çré Kåñëa; eva-
certainly; kåñëa-avatära-utsava-iti-ädibhiù-by Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.11


sa vismayotphulla-vilocano harià
   sutaà vilokyänakadundubhis tadä
kåñëavatärotsava-sambhramo 'spåçan
   mudä dvijebhyo 'yutam äpluto gaväm

tasya-of Him; atyanta-great; prasiddheù-because of fame; çré-bhagavan-spoken by the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; çré-devaki-devim-to Devaki-devi.


   When the Supreme Lord appeared for the third time as the son of Vasudeva and Devaké, He
appeared in His complete original form, and thus fulfilled His promise that He would appear as the
son of Devaké and Vasudeva. Because the Lord's promise was thus fulfilled, He said "satyaà me
vyähåtam" (take My words as truth).
   At this point someone may doubt that the two-handed form of Kåñëa is the Original Perssonality
of Godhead. After all, in these verses Kåñëa is speaking to Vasudeva and Devaké in His four-armed
Viñëu-form. The Lord first appeared to Vasudeva and Devaké in this four-armed form. Is not the

four-armed form of Viñëu the original Godhead, and Çré Kåñëa only a later and temporary
expansion?
   Actually the four-armed form of the Personality of Godhead who appeared as the son of
Vasudeva and Devaké was not Lord Viñëu, but a four-handed manifestation of Lord Kåñëa. This is
especifically described in the following verses from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.3.11):

    "When Vasudeva saw his extraordianary son, four-handed Lord Kåñëa (kåñëävatära), his eyes
were struck with wonder. In transcendental jubilation, he mentally collected ten thousand cows
and distributed them among the brähmaëas as a transcendental festival."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.97
records.text:
evaà ca deväkyäà deva-rüpiëyäm ity ädi. spañöam. çré-çukaù.

  evam-in the same way; ca-also; deväkyam deva-rupinam iti ädi-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.8:


niçithe tama-udbhüte
   jäyamäne janärdane
deväkyäà deva-rüpiëyäà
   viñëu sarva-guhä-çayaù
äviräséd yathä präcyäà
   diçéndur iva puçkalaù";

spañöam-the meaning is clear; çré-sukaù-spoken by Sukadeva Gosvami.


   The same son of Devaké described as Kåñëa (kåñëävatära) in this verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.3.11) is described as Viñëu in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.8):

   "Then the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viñëu, who is situated in the core of everyone's
heart, appeared from the heart of Devaké in the dense darkness of night, like the full moon rising
on the eastern horizon, because Devaké was of the same category as Çré Kåñëa."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.98
records.text:
Text 1


  nanu satyaà tasya catur-bhujäkära-rüpasya tädåçatvam, kintu

rüpaà cedaà pauruñaà dhyäna-dhiñëyaà
   ma pratyakñaà mäàsa-dåçäà kåçéñöhäù

   nanu-is it not; satyam-truth; tasya-His; catuh-bhuja-akara-rüpasya-of the four handed-form;
tadrsatvam-in this way; kintu-but; rüpam-in Your Viñëu form; ca-also; idam-this; pauruñam-as the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; dhyäna-dhiñëyam-who is appreciated by meditation; mä-not;
pratyakñam-directly visible; mäàsa-dåçäm-to those who see with their material eyes; kåçéñöhäù-
please be.


    Someone may raise the following objection:
Is not this four-handed form of Viñëu the original, eternal form of the Personality of Godhead, and
the two-handed form of Çré Kåñëa only a temporary expansion from that four-handed form? This is
certainly confirmed by these words spoken by Devaké after the Lord appeared as her son in His four-
armed Viñëu-form (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.28):

   "My Lord, because You dispel all the fear of Your devotees, I request You to save us and give us
protection from the terrible fear of Kaàsa. Your form as Viñëu, the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, is appreciated by yogés in meditation. Please make this form invisible to those who see
with material eyes."*


Text 2


mätr-vijïäpaëanuçareëa

etad väà darçitaà rüpaà
   präg-janma-smaraëäya me
nänyathä mad-bhavaà jïänaà
   martya-liìgena jäyate

    etat-this form of Viñëu; väm-unto both of you; darçitam-has been shown; rüpam-My form as the
Supreme Personality of Godhead with four hands; präk-janma-of My previous appearances;
smaranäya-just to remind You; me-My; na-not; anyathä-otherwise; mat-bhavam-Viñëu's
appearance; jïänam-this transcendental knowledge; martya-liìgena-by taking birth like a human
child; jäyate-does arise; matå- mother; vijïäpana-anusärena-by the instruction.


   That Lord Viñëu is the original Personality of Godhead is also confirmed in the following words
spoken by the Lord to mother Devaké (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.44):

   "I have shown you this form of Viñëu just to remind you of My previous births. Otherwise, if I
appeared like an ordinary human child, you would not believe that the Personality of Godhead,
Viñëu, has indeed appeared."*


Text 3

iti pratyuttaryya

ity uktväçid dharis tüñëéà
   bhagavän ätma-mäyayä
pitroù sampaçyatoù sadyo
   babhüva präkåtaù çiçuù. ity ukta-diçä.

   iti-thus; pratyuttaryya-responding; iti-uktvä-after instructing in this way; äsét-remained; hariù-
the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tüñëém-silent; bhagavän-Lord Viñëu, the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; ätma-mäyayä-by acting in His own spiritual energy; pitroù sampaçyatoù-
while His father and mother were factually seeing Him; sadyaù- immediately; babhüva-He became;
präkåtaù-like an ordinary human being; çiçuù-a child; iti-thus; ukta-spoken; diça- by the direction.


   By the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.46) we may also see that Lord Viñëu is the
original Personality of Godhead, and Lord Kåñëa is expanded from Him:

    "After thus instructing His father and mother, the Supreme Personality of Godhead remained
silent. In their presence, by His internal energy, He then transformed Himself into a small human
child."*


Text 4


   yan-manuñäkära-rüpaà své-kåtavän,tatra sandigdham iva bhäti. atra ca bhavatu vä harir api
tatyaja äkåtià tryadhéçaù iti, tyakñyan deham iti ca tantra-bhägavatänusäreëäntardhäpanärthatväd
asahayam.

   yat-which; manusa-human; akara-rüpam-form; svi-kåtavan- accepted; tatra-there; sandigdham-
materially influenced; iva- appearing as if; bhati-manifested; atra-in this matter; ca- also; bhavatu-
may be; va-or; hariù-the Personality of Godhead; api-also; tatyaje-abandoned; akåtim-the form of
Kåñëa; tryadhisaù-the Lord of the three worlds; iti-thus; tyaksyan- giving up; deham-His form; iti-
thus; ca-also; tantra-bhagavata-of the passage from Tantra-bhagavata; anusarena-in accordance;
antardhapana-dissappearance; arthatvät-because of the significance; asahayam-alone.


   From these verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam it appears that transcendental Lord Viñëu accepted the
form of Kåñëa, a temporary and material (präkåtaù çiçuù) form. The argument that the form of
Kåñëa is temporary and material is supported by the following statements from Çrémad-Bhägavatam:

harir api tatyaja äkåtià tryadhéçaù

   "After His pastimes on earth were completed, the Lord gave up the form of Kåñëa and assumed

His original form."
                      -3.4.28

tyakñyan deham

   "The Supreme Lord then gave up the form of Kåñëa."
                  -3.4.29


Text 5


yayäharad bhuvo bhäraà
   täà tanuà vijahäv ajaù
kaëöakaà kaëöakeneva
   dvayaà cäpéçituù saman

   yayä-that by which; aharat-took away; bhuvaù-of the world; bhäram-burden; täm-that; tanum-
body; vijahau- relinquished; ajaù-the unborn; kaëöakam-thorn; kaëöakena- by the thorn; iva-like
that; dvayam-both; ca-also; api- although; éçituù-controlling; samam-equal.


   That the Original Personality of Godhead is Lord Viñëu, who assumess the temporary material
form of Kåñëa, is substantiated in the following verses of Çrémad Bhägavatam (1.15.34-35)

   "The supreme unborn Lord caused the members of the Yadu dynasty to relinquish their bodies,
and thus He relieved the burden of the world. This action was like picking out a thorn with a
thorn, though both are the same to the controller.*


Text 6


yathä matsyädi-rüpäëi
   dhatte jahyäd naöaù
bhü-bhäraù kñapito yena
   jahau tac ca kalevaram"

iti tu paripoñakam.

   yathä-as much as; matsya-ädi-incarnation as a fish, etc.; rüpäëi-forms; dhatte-eternally accepts;
jahyät- apparently relinquishes; yathä-exactly like; naöaù-magician; bhü-bhäraù-burden of the
world; kñapitaù-relieved; yena- by which; jahau-let go; tat-that; ca-also; kalevaram-body; iti-thus; tu-
indeed; paripoñakam-substantiating.

   "The Supreme Lord relinquised the body which He manifested to diminish the burden of the
earth. Just like a magician, He relinquishes one body to accept different ones, like the fish
incarnation and others."*


Text 7


etad eva çré-vasudeva-vacane 'pi labhyate

süté-gåhe nanu jagäda bhavän ajo nau
   saïjajïa ity anuyugaà nija-dharma-guptyai
nänä-tanür gagana-vad vidadhaj jahäsi
   ko veda bhumna urugäya vibhüti-mäyäm ity atra

   etat-this; eva-certainly; çré-vasudeva-of Maharaja Vasudeva; vacane-in the statement; labhyate-is
attained; suti-grhe-in the maternity room; nanu-is it not?; jagada-spoke; bhavan-Your Lordship;
ajaù-unborn; nau-to us; sanjajne-take birth; iti-thus; anuyugam-in every yuga; nija-Your own;
dharma-principles of religion; guptyai-in order to protect; nana-various; tanuù-with forms;
gaganavat-like the sky; vidadhat-accepting; jahasi-you give up; kaù-who? veda-knows; bhumna-
Lord; urugaya-glorified by devotees; vibhuti-mayam- glories and opulence; iti-thus; atra-here.


   That the Supreme Personality of Godhead accepts the temporary and material form of Kåñëa
may also be substantiated by quoting the following prayer spoken to Kåñëa by Mahäräja Vasudeva
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.85.20):

   "My dear Lord, at the very moment when You first appeared in Kaàsa's prison house, I was
informed that You were the Supreme Personality of Godhead and that You descended for the
protection of the principles of religion as well as the destruction of the unfaithful. Although
unborn, You descend in every millenium to execute Your mission. My dear Lord, as in the sky there
are many forms appearing and disappearing, so You also appear and disappear in many forms. Who,
therefore, can understand Your pastimess or the mystery of Your appearance and dissappearance?
Our only business should be to glorify Your supreme greatness."*


Text 8


   atrocyate tat-tad-vacanam anyärthatvena dåçyam iti. ekasminn eva tasmin çré-vigrahe kadäcic
catur-bhujatvasya kad acid dvi-bhujatvasya ca prakäça-çravaëenaviçeñäpätäd bhü-bhara-kñapaëe
dvayor api sämanyät. süté-gåhe ity-ädi-väksyasya catur-bhuja-viñayatväc ca. kià ca yair vidvad-
anubhava-sevita-çabda-siddhair nityatvädibhir dharmaiù çré-vigrahasya parama-tattväkäratvaà
sädhitam. te präyaço naräkäram adhikåtyaiva hy udähriyante sma dvitéya-sandarbhe. tathätraiva
copäsakeçu säkñät-kärädi liìgena siddha-nirdeçena ca tad-äkärasyäpi nitya-siddhatvaà dåòhé-kåtam.
udahäriñyate ca nityam eva mäà keçavo gadayä prätar avyäd govinda äsaìgatvam atta-veëuù iti.

sampraty anyad api tatrodähriyate.

   atra-in this matter; ucyate-it is said; tat-tat-various; vacanam-statements; anyarthatvena-with a
different interpretation; drsyam-may be seen; iti-thus; ekasmin-ekasmin- in one; eva-certainly;
tasmin-in this; çré-vigrahe-in the form of the Lord; kadacit-sometimes; catur-bhujatvasya-of the
nature of being four-handed; kadacit-sometimes; dvi-bhujatvasya-of the nature of being two-
handed; ca-also; prakäça- manifestation; sravanena-by hearing; avisesapatat-because of non-
difference; bhu-of the earth; bhara-the burden; kñapane-in the matter of removing; dvayoù-of the
two; api-also; samanyat- because of equality; suti-grhe-iti-ädi-väkyasya-of this verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.85.20) beginning with the words "suti-grhe"; catur-bhuja-the four-armed form;
visyatvät-because of being in relation; ca-also; kim ca-furthermore; yaiù-by which; vidvat- of the
learned devotees; anubhava-sevita-directly experienced; sabda-by sound; siddhaiù-conclusively
proven; nityatva-ädibhiù-beginning with eternity; dharmaiù-with attriutes; çré-vigrahasya-of the
form of the Personality of Godhead; parama-tattva-supreme truth; akaratvam-the state of having
form; sadhitam-is demonstrated; te-they; prayasaù-generally; nara-akaram-the human-like form;
adhikåtya-with reference to; eva- certainly; hi-indeed; udahriyante-sma-were described; dvitiya-
sandarbhe-in the Second-(bhagavat-) sandarbha; tatha-in the same way; atra-here; eva-certainly; ca-
also; upasakesu-among the worshipers; sakñat-kara-ädi-beginning with direct manifestation; lingena-
characterized by; siddha-nirdesena-by perfect instruction; ca-also; tat-His;
 akarasya-of the form; api-also; nitya-siddhatvam-eternal manifestation; drdhi-kåtam- established;
udaharisyate-is described; ca-also; nityam- eternal; eva-certainly; mam-me; kesavaù-Lord Kesava;
gadaya- by His club; prataù-in the morning hours avyat-may He protect; govindaù-Lord Govinda;
asaìgatvam-during the second part of the day; atta-venuù-holding His flute; iti-thus; samprati-at
present; anyat-otherwise; api-even; tatra-there; udahriyate- is described.


   Although these verses seem to support the view that the Supreme Godhead assumes various
forms, and all these forms (including the form of Kåñëa) are temporary, when properly understood
these verses do not at all support such a view. The actual fact is that the Supreme Personality of
Godhead has a form which may sometimes manifest four-hands, and then again appear as two-
handed. When the Lord apppear on this earth, both of these four-handed and two-handed features
appeared equally powerful in the matter of killing the demons and removing the burden of the
earth. If one accepts this verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.85.20, quoted in the previous text) to mean
that the form of Kåñëa is a temporary manifestation, then one must accept that the four-handed
form of Lord Viñëu is also a temporary manifestation, for both two-handed and four-handed forms
are clearly described to be equally powerful. This is not an acceptable conclusion, for the four-
handed form of Lord Viñëu is described as eternal throughout all the Veic literatures.
   The revelation of the Vedic literatures is the most reliable source of knowledge, and throughout
the Vedic literatures the forms of the Lord, and especifically the form of Çré Kåñëa, are described as
eternal. This scriptural evidence has been elaborately presented in the second (Bhagavat)
sandarbha, and therefore we will not repeat the evidence previously presented, evidence that
described the direct appearance of Lord Kåñëa before His devotees and proved the eternality of the
form of Çré Kåñëa.
   For example, the following verse, spoken by Viçvarüpa to Mahäräja Indra long before Lord Kåñëa

appeared in the material world, and clearly describing the form of Lord Kåñëa, may be taken as
conclusive scriptural evidence for the eternality of the form of Kåñëa:

  "May Lord Keçava protect me with His club in the first portion of the day, and may Lord
Govinda, who is always engaged in playing His flute, protect me in the second portion of the day."*


Text 9


kaàso batädyäkåta me' ty-anugrahaà
   dräkñye 'ìghri-padmaà prahito 'munä hareù
kåtävatärasya duratyayaà tamaù
   pürve 'taran yan-nakha-maëòala-tviñä

   kamsaù-Kamsa; bata-certainly; akåta-has performed; me-to me; ati-a great; anugraham-mercy;
draksye-I shall see; aìghri-padmam-the lotus feet; prahitaù-sent; amuna-by him; hareù-of Lord
Hari; kåta-avatärasya-incarnated; duratyayam-difficult to overcome; tamaù-darkness of material
existence; pürve-formerly; ataran-transcendental; yat-of whom; nakha-maëòala-of the nails; tviñä-
by the effulgence.


   The following verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.38.7-8), which describe the worship of Lord Kåñëa
in ancient times, are further evidence for the eternality of the form of Çré Kåñëa:

   "Akrüra reflected: I am very much favored by Kaàsa, who is sending me to bring Kåñëa and
Balaräma, and thus enabling me to see the Lord. Formerly great sages and saintly persons became
liberated from the material world simply by seeing the shining nails of the lotus feet of Kåñëa.*


Text 10


yad arcitaà brahma-bhavädibhiù suraiù
   çriyä ca devyä munibhiù sa-sätvätaiù
go-cäraëäyänucaraiç carad vane
   yad gopikänäà kuca-kuìkumäìkitam

   yat-which; arcitam-are worshiped; brahma-by Brahma; bhava-Siva; ädibhiù-beginning with;
suraiù-by the demogods; sriya-by Laksmi; ca-and; devya-the goddess; munibhiù-by the sages; sa-
satvätaiù-with the devotees; go-the cows; caranaya- for herding; anucaraiù-with His associates;
carat-wandering; vane-in the forest; yat-which; gopikanam-of the gopés; kuca- of the breasts;
kunkuma-by the kunkuma podwer; aìkitam-marked.


  "I shall soon see Lord Kåñëa's lotus feet, which are worshiped by great demigods like Brahmä,

Närada, and Lord Çiva, which traverse the ground of Våndävana while herding the cows with the
gopas, and which touch the breasts of the gopés, covered with tinges of kuìkuma."*


Text 12


   atra pürve-ity-ädi-dyotitam go-cäraëäya-ity-ädi labdhasya sphuöaà çré-naräkäsyaiva
nityävasthäyitvaà labhayate, çrémad-akrüraù.

   atra-in these verses; pürve-iti-ädi-dyotitam-demonstrated by the word "pürve(formerly)"; go-
caranaya-iti-ädi-labdhasya- described as "go-caranaya(herding the cows); sphutam-clearly; çré-nara-
akarasya-with a human-like form; eva-certainly; nitya-avasthayitvam-eternally; labhyate-is
demonstrated; srimad-akrurah-spoken by Akrura.


    In these verses the words "pürve" (formerly great sages and saintly persons became liberated from
the material world simply by seeing the shinning nails of the lotus feet of Kåñëa), and "go-caraëäya"
(I shall soon see Lord Kåñëa's lotus feet, which are worshiped by great demigods like Brahmä,
Närada, and Lord Çiva, and which traverse the ground of Våndävana while herding the cows with
the gopas) clearly indicate the eternality of the form of Lord Kåñëa.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.99
records.text:
Text 1


yathä

yä vai çriyärcitam ajädibhir äpta-kämair
   yogeçvarair api sadätmani räsa-goñöhyäm
kåñëasya tad bhagavataç caraëäravindaà
   nyastaà staneçu vijahuù parirabhya täpam

   yatha-just as; yaù-who; vai-certainly; sriya-by the goddess of fortune; arcitam-worshiped; aja-by
Brahma; ädibhiù-and others; apta-kamaiù-whose desires are fulfilled; yoga-isvaraiù-by the masters
of yoga; api-also; sadä-continuously; atmani-in the heart; rasa-gosthyam-in the arena of the rasa
dance; kåñëasya-of Lord Kåñëa; tat-that; bhagavataù-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead;
carana-feet; aravindam-lotus; nyastam-placed; stanesu-on the breasts; vijahuù-gave up; parirabhya-
embracing; tapam-distress.


   The eternality of the form of Çré Kåñëa is described in the same way in the following verse
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47,62):

   "The gopés relieved themselves of all kinds of material contamination by placing on their high,
beautiful breasts the lotus feet of Kåñëa, which are not only eternally worshiped by the goddess of
fortune, but by such exalted demigods as Brahmä and Lord Çiva, and which are eternally meditated
upon by great yogés within their hearts."*


Text 2


    sadä bhüta-vartamäna-bhaviçyat-käleçu çry-ädénäà sarvadävasthäyitvena prasiddheù, sadä-ity-
asya tathaiva hy artha-pratétiù, saìkoca-våttau kañöatäpatteù, çré-bhagavati tädrçatva-bhaväbhäväc
ca.

   sada-the word "sada(continuously)"; bhuta-past; vartamana-present; bhavisyat-kalesu-and in the
future; çré-ädinam-of Laksmi-devi and the other demigods; sarvada-eternal; avasthayitvena-by
existence; prasiddheù-because of fame; sada-iti-asya-of the word "sada"; tatha-in that way; hi-
certainly; artha-pratitiù-the meaning; saìkoca-vrttau-in a more limited interpretation; kastata-
apatteù-because of accepting an indefensible interpretation; çré-bhagavati-in the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; tvadrsatva-in the state of being in this way; bhava-existence; abhavat-
because of the non-existence; ca-also.


   In this verse the word "sadä" (continuously) means that Lakñmé and others worship Kåñëa
eternally in all phases of time: past, present, and future. In other words: because the demigods
eternally worship Lord Kåñëa, therefore Lord Kåñëa must be eternal.
   Someone may say that the form of Kåñëa is temporarily manifested, and during the time of His
manifestation the demigods continuously worship Him. This argument is simply jugglery of words
to create a different meaning out of the clear statement of this verse. We do not take it very
seriously, for it contradicts the Vedic description of the eternal nature of the Personality of
Godhead.


Text 3


  tathä ca çrutau tam ekaà govindaà sac-cid-änanda-vigrahaà païca-padaà våndävana-süra-
bhüruha-taläsénaà satataà samarud-gaëe 'haà paramayä stutyä toñayämi. çrémad-uddhavaù.

   tatha-in the same way; ca-also; çrutau-in the Gopala tapani Upaniñad (1.37); tam-Him; ekam-
alone; govindam-Lord Govinda; sat-eternal; cit-full of knowledge; ananda-and bliss; vigraham-
whose form; panca-padam-this mantra consisting of five words; våndävana-in Våndävana; sura-
bhuruha-tala-under a desire tree; asinam-seated; satatam-continually; sa-accompanied by; marut-
ganaù-the demigods; aham-I; paramasya-with eloquent; stutya-prayers; tosayami-I please; srimat-
uddhavaù-spoken by Uddhava.

   The eternality of the form of Çré Kåñëa is described in many Vedic literatures. For example, in
the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad Lord Brahmä (1.38) explains:

  "With eloquent prayers I and the Maruts please Lord Govinda, whose form is eternal and full of
knowledge and bliss, who stays in Våndävana, and who is this five-word mantra."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.100
records.text:
evaà ca

yat-päda-päàsur bahu-janma-kåcchato
   dhåtätmabhir yogibhir apy alabhyaù
sa eva yad-dåg-viçayaù svayaà sthitaù
   kià varëyate diñöam ato vrajaukasäm.

   atra svayam ity anena bädham evänyathä-pratétir durdhiyaà nirastä. çré-çukaù.

   evam-in the same way; ca-also; yat-whose; päda-päàsuù-dust of the lotus feet; bahu-janma-in
many births kåcchrataù-from undergoing severe austerities and penances as a way of practicing
yoga, meditation, etc.; dhåta-ätmabhiù-by persons able to control the mind; yogibhiù-by such yogés
(jïäna-yogés, räja-yogés, dhyäna-yogés, etc.); api- indeed; alabhyaù-cannot be achieved; saù-the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; eva-indeed; yat-dåk-viçayaù-has become the object of direct
vision, face to face; svayam- personally; sthitaù-present in front of them; kim-what; varëyate-can be
described; diñöam-about the fortune; ataù- therefore; vraja-okasäm-of the inhabitants of
Vrajabhümi, Vådävana; atra-in this verse; svayam iti-anena-by the word "svayam (personally)";
badham-affirmed; eva-certainly; anyatha-the other; pratitiù-explanation; durdhiyam-of the faulty
logicians; nirasta-is rejected; çré-sukaù-spoken by Sukadeva Gosvami.


   The eternality of the form of Çré Kåñëa is also confirmed by Çukadeva Gosvämé in the following
verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.12):

   "Yogés may undergo severe austerities and penances for many births by practicing yama, niyama,
äsana and präëäyäma, none of which are easily performed. Yet in due course of time, when these
yogés attain the perfection of controlling the mind, they will still be unable to taste even a particle
of dust from the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. What then can we describe
about the great fortune of the innhabitants of Vrajabhümi, Våndävana, with whom the Supreme
Personality of Godhead personally lived and who saw the Lord face to face?"*

   In this verse the word "svayam" (personally) indicates that Çré Kåñëa is the Original Personality
of Godhead. For this reason it should be accepted that His form is eternal, and not simply
manifested for a short time to serve a particular purpose.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.101
records.text:
TYext 1


   ata eva svabhäva-siddhatvaà pürëaiçvaryädy-äçrayatvaà ca

gopyas tapaù kim acaram yad amuñya rüpaà
   lävaëya-säram asamordhvam ananya-siddham
dågbhiù pibanty anusaväbhinavaà duräpam
   ekänta-dhäma yaçasaù çriya aiçvarasya

   ananya-siddham anyena tat siddham iti na, kintu svabhävikam evety-arthaù. anyaträsiddham iti
tu vyäkhyä. piñöa-peñaëam. asamordhvam iti by uktam eva. mathurä-pura-striyaù parasparam.

   atah eva-therefore; svabhava-by nature; siddhatvam- perfection; pürëa-of complete; aisvarya-
power and opulence; ädi-beginning with; asrayatvam-as the abode; ca-also; gopyaù-the gopés; tapaù-
austerities; kim-what; acaram-performed; yat-from which; amuçya-of such a one (Lord Kåñëa); r-
upam- the form; lävaëya-säram-the essence of loveliness; asama-ürdhvam-not paralleled or
surpassed; ananya-siddham-not perfected by any other ornament (self-perfect); dågbhiù-by the eyes;
pibanti-they drink; anusava-abhinavam-constantly new; duräpam-difficult to obtain; ekänta-dhäma-
the only abode; yaçasaù-of fame; çriyaù-of beauty; aiçvarasya-opulence; ananya-siddham-the word
"ananya-siddham (self-perfect)"; anyena-by another; tat-therefore; siddham-perfected; iti-thus; na-
not; kintu-but; svabhavikam-naturally; eva-certainly; iti- thus; arthaù-the meaning; anyatra-
asiddham-with imperfections; iti-thus; tu-but; vyakhya-interpretation; pista-pesanam-a waste of
words; asama-urdhvam-by the word "asamordhvam (not paralleled or srpassed)"; iti-thus; hi-
certainly; uktam-spoken; eva- certainly; mathura-pura-striyaù-spoken by the women of Mathura;
parasparam-among themselves.


  That Çré Kåñëa is the Original Personality of Godhead, self-perfect, and full of all opulences is
confirmed in the following words spoken by the women of Mathurä among themselves (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.44,14):

   "What austerities must the gopés have performed? With their eyes they always drink the nectar
of the face of Lord Kåñëa, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed.
That loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and
extremely rare."*

   The word "ananya-siddham" (self-perfect) in this verse indicates the Çré Kåñëa is perfect by
nature. He does not require anyone else to award Him perfection. If someone wants to divide this
word "an-anyasiddham" (without other perfections), his interpretation is useless, for it is
contradicted in this very verse by the word "asamordhvam" (not equalled or surpassed).

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.102
records.text:
Text 1


  atha vibhutvam na cantar na bahir yasya-ity ädau. präkåta-vastv-atitiriktatvam tväk-smäçru-keça-
nakha-roma-pinaddham-ity-ädau spañöam.

  atha-now; vibhutvam-all-pervasiveness; na ca antah na bahih yasya iti adau-in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.9.13:


na cäntar na bahir yasya
   na pürvaà näpi cäparam
pürväparaà bahiç cäntar
   jagato yo jagac yaù

taà matvätmajam avyaktaà
   martya-liìgam adhokñajam
gopikolükhale dämnä
   babandha präkåtam yathä

prakåta-vastu-matter; atiriktatvam-superiority; tvak-smaçru-kesa-nakha-roma-pinaddham iti-adau-
in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.45):


tväk-smäçru-roma-nakha-keça-pinnadham antar
   mäàsästhi-rakta-kåmi-viö-kapha-vitta-vätam
jévac-chavaà bhajati känta-matir vimüòhä
   yä te padäbja-makarandam ajighrati çré

spañöam-the meaning is clear.


   That Çré Kåñëa is all-pervading is confirmed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.13):

   "Lord Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, has no beginning and no end, no exterior
and no interior, no front and no rear. In other words, He is all-pervading. Because He is not under
the influence of the element of time, for Him there is no difference between past, present and
future; He exists in His own transcedental form at all times. Being absolute, beyond relativity, He is
free from distinctions between cause and effect, although He is the cause and effect of everything.
That unmanifested person, who is beyond the perception of the senses, had now appeared as a
human child, and mother Yaçodä, considering Him her own ordinary child, bound Him to the

wooden mortar with a rope."*

  That the form of Çré Kåñëa is not material is confirmed in the following words spoken by
Rukmiëé-devé to Lord Kåñëa (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.45):

   "A man within this material is just a dead body. In fact, superficially, the living entity is covered
by this body, which is nothing but a bag of skin decorated with beards and moustaches, hairs on the
body, nails on the fingers and hairs on the head. Within this decorated bag there are bunches of
muscles, bundles of bones, and pools of blood, always mixed up with stool, urine, mucus, bile, and
polluted air, and enjoyed by different kinds of insects and germs. A foolish woman accepts such a
dead body as her husband and, in sheer misunderstanding, loves him as her dear companion. This
only possible because such a woman has never tasted the ever-blissful flavor of Your lotus feet."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear.


Text 2


   sva-prakäça-lakñaëatvam

asyäpi deva vapuço mad-anugrahasya
   svecchämayasya na tu bhütamayasya ko 'pi
neçe mahi tv avasituà manasäntareëa
   säkñät tavaiva kim utätma-sukhänubhüteù

   sva-prakäça-form; lakñaëatvam-the characteristic; asya-of this; api-indeed; deva-O my Lord;
vapuçaù-this form which appears just like a small child; mat-anugrahasya-merciful to me; sva-
icchämayasya-which appears to fulfill the desires of the devotees; na-not; tu-but; bhütamayasya-
composed of material elements; kaù-Brahma; api-although I am; na-not; içe-I am able; mahi-the
transcendental potencies; tu-indeed; avasitum- to ascertain; manasä-by my mind; antarena-within;
säkñat- directly; tava-Your; eva-certainly; kim uta-and what to speak of; ätma-sukha-anubhüteù-the
happiness You experience in Your transcendental pastimes.


   That Kåñëa's form is spiritual and not composed of material elements is confirmed in the
following prayer spoken by Lord Brahmä (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.2):

   "My dear Lord Kåñëa, people may say that I am the master of all Vedic knowledge, and I am
supposed to be the creator of this universe, but it has been proved now that I cannot understand
Your personality, even though You are present before me just like a child. You are playing with
Your boyfriends, calves and cows, which might imply that You do not even have sufficient
education. You are appearing just like a village boy, carrying Your food in Your hand and searching
for Your calves. And yet there is so much difference between Your body and mine that I cannot
estimate the potency of Your body. Your body is not material."*

Text 3


   asya nauméòya te ity-ädinä varëita-lakñaëasya çréman-naräkärasya tava samprati bälaka-
vatsädyämçair därçiteçv ekam api deva-rüpaà catur-bhujäkäraà yad vapus tasyäpi. evam ca sati
säkñäd etad-rüpasyäàçinas tava kim uta vapuñaù viçeçaëam mad-anugrahasya ity ädi, mamänugraho
yasmät tasya tad-darçanenaiva bhavan-mahima-jïänät. kathaà-bhütasya tava ätma-
sukhänubhüteù. ätmanä svenaiva na tv anyena sukhasyänubhütir anubhävo yasya tasyänanya-
vedyänandasyety arthaù. brahmä çré-bhagavantam.

  asya-of this; naumi idya te iti ädina-in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.1:


nauméòya te 'bhra-vapuçe taòid-ambaräya
   guïjävataàsa-paripiccha-lasan-mukhäya
vanya-sraje kavala-vetra-viçäëa-veëu-
  lakñma-çriye mådu-pade paçupäìgajäya

   varnita-described; lakñaëasya-characteristics; srimat-nara-akarasya-of the Personality of
Godhead, appearing in a human-like form; tava-of You; samprati-at the present time; balaka-boys;
vatsa-calves; ädi-beginning with; amsaih- expansions; darsitesu-revealed; ekam-one; api-even; deva-
of the Personality of Godhead; rüpam-form; catuh-bhuja-with four arms; akaram-form; yat-which;
vapuh-form; tasya-of Him; api- also; evam-in the same way; ca-also; sati-being so; sakñat- directly;
etat-rüpasya-of this form; amsinah-the origin of the expansions; tava-of You; kim uta-what to
speak?; vapusah- of the form; visesanam-attribute; mat-to me; anugrahasya- merciful; iti-ädi-thus
beginning; mama-to me; anugrahah- merciful; yasmat-from whom; tasya-of Him; tat-of that
darsanena-by the sight; eva-certainly; bhavat-of Your Lordship; mahima-glories; jïänat-because of
knowing; katham-bhutasya-what is He like?; tava-of You; sukha-of transcendental happiness;
anubhuteh-experiencing; atmana-by His self; svena-own; na-not; tu-bu; anyena-by any other
source; sukhasya-of happiness; anubhutih-experience; anubhavah- experience; yasya-of whom; tasya-
of Him; ananya-not by another; vedya-knowable; anandasya-bliss; iti-thus; arthah- the meaning;
brahma-spoken by Lord Brahma; bhagavantam-to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.


  The form of Çré Kåñëa is described in the following prayer spoken by Lord Brahmä (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.14.1):

   "My dear Lord, You are the only worshipful Supreme Lord, Personality of Godhead; therefore I
am offering my humble obeisances and prayers just to please You. Your bodily features are of the
color of clouds filled with water. You are glittering with a silver electric aura emanating from Your
yellow garments.
   "Let me offer my respectful repeated obeisances unto the son of Mahäräja Nanda who is standing
before me with conchshell, earrings, and peacock feather on His head. His face is beautiful; He is

wearing a helmet, garlanded by forest flowers, and He stands with a morsel of food in His hand. He
is decorated with cane and bugle, and He carries a buffalo horn and flute. He stands before me with
small lotus feet."*

   Shortly before speaking this verse, Brahmä had directly seen that all the cowherd boys and
calves were expansions of Kåñëa, and they all had manifested four-handed forms of Lord Näräyaëa.
In this way Kåñëa revealed that He is the original source of all viñëu-tattva expansions. Brahmä
states that he is able to directly see Kåñëa and know something of His glories because of Kåñëa's
mercy upon him (mad-anugrahasya). Brahmä also says that no one is able to understand the full
extent of the transcendental happiness experienced by Kåñëa. (kim utätma-sukhänubhüteù).

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.103
records.text:
kaimutyena svayaà-rüpatva-nirdeçaç ca

sakåd yad-aìga-pratimäntar-ähitä
   manomayé bhägavatéà dadau gatim
sa eva nityätma-sukhänubhüty-abhi-
   vyudasta-mäyo 'ntar-gato hi kià punaù

spañöam. çré-çukaù.

   kaimutyena-by the same argument of "what to speak of"; +svayam-original; rüpatva-form;
nirdesah-description; ca-also; sakåt-once only; yat-whose; aìga-pratimä-the form of the Supreme
Lord (there are many forms, but Kåñëa is the original form); antaù-ähitä-placing within the core of
the heart, somehow or other; manaù-mayé-thinking of Him even by force; bhägavatém-which
competent to offer devotional service to the Lord; dadau-Kåñëa gave; gatim-the best destination;
saù-He (the Supreme Personality of Godhead); eva-indeed; nitya-always; ätma-of all living entities;
sukha-anubhüti-anyone thinking of Him immediately enjoys transcendental pleasure; abhivyudasta-
mäyaù-because all illusion is completely removed by Him; antaù-gataù-He is always present within
the core of the heart; hi-indeed; kim punaù-what to speak; spañöam-the meaning is clear; çré-sukah-
spoken by Sukadeva Gosvami.


   The argument ("If even the demons attain salvation by the mercy of Kåñëa, then what is to be
said of the devotess") presented by Çukadeva Gosvämé in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.12.39) also indicates that the form of Kåñëa is the original aspect of the Personality of Godhead:

   "If even only once or even by force one brings the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead
into one's mind, one can attain the supreme salvation by the mercy of Kåñëa, as did Aghäsura.
What then is to be said of those whose hearts the Supreme Personality of Godhead enters when He
appears as an incarnation, or those who always think of the lotus feet of the Lord, who is the source
of transcendental bliss for all living entities and by whom all illusion is completely removed?"*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.104
records.text:
Text 1


  ata eva säkñät para-brahmatvam eva darçitam adyaiva tvad-åte 'sya ity ädau.

   atah eva-therefore; sakñat-directly; para-brahmatvam-the status of the Supreme Godhead; eva-
certainly; darsitam-is revealed; adya eva tvät-rte asya-iti-adau-in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.18:


adyaiva tvad-åte 'sya kià mama na te mayatvam adarçitam
   me 'ko 'si prathamaà tato vraja-suhåd-vatsaù samastä api
tävanto 'si catur-bhujas tad-akhilaiù säkaà mayopäsitäs
   tävanty eva jaganty abhüs tad amitaà brahmädvayaà çiñyate.


   The revelation that Çré Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead is found in the following
verses from Çrémad-Bhägavatam and other Vedic literatures:

   "My dear Lord Kåñëa, leaving aside all other things and just considering today's happenings-what
I have seen-are they not all due to Your inconceivable energies? First of all I saw You alone;
thereafter You expanded Yourself as Your friends, the calves and all the existence of Våndävana;
then I saw You and all the boys as four-handed Viñëus, and They were being worshiped by all
elements and all demigods, including myself. Again They were all wound up, and You remained
alone as You were before me. Does this not mean that You are the Supreme Lord Näräyaëa, the
origin of everything, and from You everything emanates, and again everything enters unto You,
and You remain the same as before?"*
                   -Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.18


Text 2


  aho bhägyam aho bhägyam ity-ädau ca.

   aho bhagyam aho bhagyam iti-adau ca and also in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.32:


aho bhägyam aho bhägyaà
   nanda-gopa-vrajaukasäm
yan-mitraà paramänandaà
   pürëaà brahma sanätanam

   "How greatly fortunate are Nanda Mahäräja, the cowherd men and all the innhabitants of
Vrajabhümi! There is no limit to their fortune because the Absolute Truth, the source of
transcendental bliss, the eternal Supreme Brahman, has become their friend."*
                       -Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.32


Text 3


  ata evoktam güòhaà paraà brahma manuçya-liìgam iti.

   ata eva-therefore; uktam-it is described; güòham-very confidential; param-transcendental;
brahma-the Parabrahman, Kåñëa; manuçya-liìgam-as if an ordinary human being; iti- thus.


  "The Supreme Godhead is Çré Kåñëa, whose form resembles that of a human being, and who is
very difficult to understand."
                       -Çrémad-Bhägavatam 7.15.75


Text 4


vaiñëave ca:

yador vaàçaà naraù çrütvä
   sarva-päpaiù pramucyate
yaträvatérëaà kåñëäkhyaà
   paraà brahma naräkåtiù iti.

   vaisnave-in the Viñëu Purana (4.11.2); ca-also; yadoh vamsam-the Yadu dynasty; narah-a person;
çrutva-having heard about; sarva-from all; papaih-sins; pramucyate-becomes delivered; yatra-where;
avatirnam-descended; kåñëa-Kåñëa; akhyam-named; param-the supreme; brahma-Godhead; nara-of
a humna being; akåtih-in the form; iti-thus.


   "The Supreme Godhead, who has a humamlike form, and whose name is Çré Kåñëa, descended to
this material world, appearing in the dynasty of Mahäräja Yadu. For this reason, simply by hearing
about the activities of the great souls who appeared in Mahäräja Yadu's family, one can become
delivered from all sinful reactions."
                    -Viñëu Puräëa 4.11.2


Text 5

  naräkåti paraà brahma iti båhat-sahasra-näma-stotre ca.

  nara-of a human being; akåti-form; param brahma-the Supreme Godhead; iti-thus; brhat-sahasra-
nama-stotre-in the Brhat-sahasra-nama prayers; ca-also.


  "The form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead resembles that of a human being."
                 -Båhat-sahasrama-näma-stotra


Text 6


   etena çré-kåñëasya naräkåtitvam eveti. dvibhujatva eva çré-kåñëatvaà naräkåti-kaivalyän
mukhyam. caturbhujatve tu çré-kåñëatvaà naräkåti-bhüyiñöhatvät tad-anantaram eva. ata eva
caturbhujatve 'pi manuçya-rüpatvaà
tenaiva rüpena catur-bhujena
   sahasra-bäho bhava viçva-mürte ity uktvä;

dåñövedaà mänuçaà rüpaà
   tava saumyaà janärdana
idäném asmi saàvåttaù. iti uktatvät.

evaà-jätéyakäni bahüni väkyäni santi, täni ca dräñöavyäni.

   etena-by this description; çré-kåñëasya-of Çré Kåñëa; nara-akåtitvam-the nature of having a
humanlike form; eva- certainly; iti-thus; dvibhujatve-in the state of having two hands; eva-
certainly; çré-kåñëatvam-the nature of Çré Kåñëa; nara-akåti-kaivalyat-because of being most like a
human form; mukhyam-principal; caturbhujatve-in the state of having four hands; tu-but; sri-
kåñëatvam-the nature of Çré Kåñëa; nara-akåti-of the human like form; bhuyistavat-because of being
most prominent; tat-anantaram-afterwards; eva-certainly; atah eva- therefore; caturbhujatve-in the
state of having four hands; api-even; manusya-rüpatvam-the state of having a humanlike form;
varnitam-is described; srimat-arjunena-by Arjuna; tena eva-by that; rüpeëa-with form; catur-
bhujena-four-handed; sahasra-bäho-O thousand-handed one; bhava-just become; viçva-mürte- O
universal form; iti-thus; uktva-having spoken; dåñövä- seeing idam-this; mänuçam-human being;
rüpam-form; tava- Your; saumyam-very beautiful; janärdana-O chastiser of te enemies; idäném-just
now; asmi-I am; saàvåttaù-settled; iti-uktatvät-from these words; eva-jatiyakani-similar; bahuni-
many; väkyani-statements; santi-are; teni-they; ca-also; drastavyani-should be seen.


    These verses confirm that the primary feature of Çré Kåñëa is His two-handed humanlike form,
although He may also manifest His humanlike form in an only-slightly-changed four-armed feature.
This four-armed feature of the humanlike form of Kåñëa is described by Arjuna, who desired to see
it and who spoke the following request (Bhagavad-gétä 11.46):

  "O universal Lord, I wish to see You in Your four-armed form, with helmeted head and with

club, wheel, conch and lotus flower in Your hands. I long to see You in that form."*

   Arjuna was very pleased to see Lord Kåñëa's original, humanlike form. He said (Bhagavad-gétä
11.51):

  "Seeing this humanlike form, so very beautiful, my mind is now pacified, and I am restored to
my original nature."*

   Let us now examine some of the many scriptural passages that describe the humanlike form of
the Supreme Personality of Godhead.


Text 7


  ata eva sa naräkära-mürtir eva parama-käraëaà vastu-tattvam ity äha näräyaëe käraëa-martya-
mürtau iti.

   atah eva-therefore; sah-He; hara-akara-murtih-with a human like form; eva-certainly; parama-
karanam-the ultimate cause of everything; vastu-tattvam-the Absolute Truth; iti-thus; aha-he
describes; näräyaëe karana-martya-murtau iti-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.33


tasmin bhavantäv akhilätma-hetau
   näräyaëe käraëa-martya-mürtau
bhävaà vidhattaà nitaraà mahätman
   kià vävaçiñöaà yuvayoù sukåtyam


       Speaking to Mahäräja Nanda and Mother Yaçodä, Uddhava said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.33):

   "My dear Yaçodä and Nanda Mahäräja, you are always absorbed in ecstatic thought of Kåñëa and
Balaräma, who, although their transcendental forms resemble those of ordinary human beings, are
actually Lord Näräyaëa, the Personality of Godhead who is the cause of all causes. Because you are
always absorbed in ecstatic love for Them, what activity remains to be performed by you?"*


Text 8


       sarva-käraëaà yat tattvaà tad eva martyäkära mürtir yasya. tad uktam tattvaà paraà yoginäm
iti,

   sarva-karanam-the cause of everything; yat-which; tattvam-Absolute Truth; tat-that; eva-
certainly; martya-akara- humanlike; murtih-form; yasya-of whom; tat-that; uktam- described;
tattvam param yoginam iti-in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10, 43.17):

mallänäm açanér nåëäà nara-varaù stréëäà smaro mürtimän
  gopänäà svajano 'satäà kñiti-bhujäà çañöä sva-pitroù çéçüù
måtyur bhoja-pater iväda-viduçäà tattvaà paraà yoginäm
  våñëéëäà paravateti viditor aìgäìgataù sägrajaù".


  The humanlike form of Çré Kåñëa is the ultimate cause of all rasas, or relationships. This is
confirmed in the following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.43.17):

   "When Kåñëa entered the wrestling arena with Balaräma and Their friends, He appeared
differently to different people according to their different relationships (rasas) with Him. Kåñëa is
the reservoir of all pleasure and all kinds of rasas, both favorable and unfavorable. He appeared to
the wrestlers exactly like a thunderbolt. To the people in general He appeared as the most beautiful
personality. To the females He appeared to be the most attractive male, Cupid personified, and thus
increased their lust. The cowherd men who were present there looked upon Kåñëa as their own
kinsman, coming from the same village of Våndävana. The kñatriya kings who were present saw
Him as the strongest ruler. To the parents of Kåñëa, Nanda and Yaçodä, He appeared to be the most
loving child. To Kaàsa, the king of the Bhoja dynasty, He appeared to be death personified. To the
unintelligent, He appeared to be an incapable personality. To the yogés present, He appeared to be
the Supersoul. To the members of the Våñëi dynastyHe appeared to be the most celebrated
descendant. Thus appreciated differently by different kinds of men present, Kåñëa entered the
wrestling arena with Balaräma and His cowherd boy friends."*


Text 9


dåñöväti-håñöo hy abhavaà
   sarva-bhüçaëa-bhüçaëam
gopälam abalä-saìga-
   muditaà veëu-vädinam

tato mäm äha bhagavän
   vådävana-caraù smayan
yad idam me tvayä dåñöaà
   rüpaà divyaà sanätanam

niçkalaà niçkriyaà çäntaà
   sac-cid-änanda-vigraham
pürëaà padma-paläçäkñaà
   nätaù parataraà mama

idam eva vadanty ete

   vedäù käraëa-käraëam ity ädi

uddhavaù. çré-vrajeçvaram.

   tatha-in the same way; ca-also; padma-of the Padma Purana; nirmana-khande-in the Nirmana-
khanda; çré-veda-vyasa-of Vedavyasa; väkyam-the statement; dåñötvä-seeing; ati-very; håñöah-
jubilant; hi-certainly; abhavam-I became; sarva-bhusana-of all ornaments; bhusanam-the ornament;
gopalam-the cowherd boy, Çré Kåñëa; abala-of the gopés; saìga-by the associattion; muditam-
delighted; venu-His flute; vädinam- playing; tatah-then; mam-to me; aha-spoke; bhagavan-the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; våndävana-in Våndävana; carah- wandering; smayan-smiling; yat-
which; idam-this; me-of Me; tvaya-by You; dåñöam-seen; rüpam-form; divyam- transcendental;
sanatana-eternal; niskalam-complete; niskriyam-without any material activities; santamj-peaceful;
sat- eternity; cit-knowledge; ananda-bliss; vigraham-form; pürëam- perfect; padma-lotus; palasa-
petals; akñam-with eyes; na-not; atah-that this; parataram-superior; mama-My; idam-this; eva-
certainly ; vadanti-describe; ete-they; vedah-the Personified Vedas; karana-karanam-te original
cause of all causes; iti- thus; ädi-in the passage beginning; uddhavah-spoken by Uddhava; çré-vraja-
isvaram-to Nanda Maharaja, the king of Vraja.


   That the humanlike form of Çré Kåñëa is the original cause of all causes is also confirmed in the
following statement of Vedavyäsa (in the Nirmäna-khaëòa of the Padma Puräëa):

   "Lord Kåñëa was playing His flute, and enjoying the company of the gopés. He was very
handsome, and He was like a splendid ornament that beautified the ornaments He wore. When I
saw Him I became very happy. As we walked together in the forest of Våndävana, the Lord smiled
and said to me: You are now seeing my eternal transcendental form, which is perfect and complete,
eternal, full of knowledge and bliss, and free from all material activities. There is nothing superior
to this lotus-eyed form of Mine, which you are now seeing, and which all the Vedas declare to be
the Original Personality of Godhead, the ultimate cause of all causes."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.105
records.text:
Text 1


   ata eva bahüàs catur-bhujän dåçåvän api narakarasyaiva viçeçataù stuty-arthaà pratijänéte
naumiòya te 'bhra-vapuñe taòid-ambaräya ity ädi. idam eva tava paramaà tattvam ity ajätvä pürvam
ahaà bhrantavän, adhunä te adyaiva tvad-åte 'sya ity ädi-darçitäya bhavataù kåpayä jïaöavän ity
atra tatra tad-äkäram evaa tväà labdhuà stauméti tätparyam. brahmä çré-bhagavantam.

   atah eva-therefore; bahun-many; catur-bhujan-four-handed forms; dåñöavan-seen; api-although;
nara-akarasya-of the humanlike form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; eva- certainly;
visesatah-specifically; stuti-prayer; artham-for the purpose; pratijanite-affirms; naumi idya te abhra-

vapuse tädit-ambaraya-iti-ädi-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.1):


nauméòya te 'bhra-vapuçe taòid-ambaräya
  guïjätaàsa-paripiccha-lasam-mukhäya
vanya-sraje kavala-vetra-viçäëa-veëu-
  lakñma-çriye mådu-pade paçupäìgajäya

idam-this; eva-certainly; tava-Your; paramam-supreme; tattvam-position; iti-thus; ajïätva-not
understanding; pürvam-before; aham-I; bhrantavan-was bewildered; adhuna-now; te-of You; adya
eva tvät-rte asya iti ädi-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.2

asyäpi deva vapuño mad-anugrahasya
   svecchämayasya na tu bhütamayasya ko 'pi
neçe mahi tv avasituà manasäntareëa
   säkñät tavaiva kim utätma-sukhänubhüteù


    Although Lord Brahmä has many times seen the four-armed form of Lord Viñëu, he specifically
glorifies the two-armed form of Lord Kåñëa (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.1):
    "My dear Lord, You are the only worshipful Supreme Lord, Personality of Godhead; therefore I
am offering my humble obeisances and prayers just to please You. Your bodily features are of the
color of clouds filled with water. You are glittering with a silver electric aura emanating from Your
yellow garments.*
    "Let me offer my respectful repeated obeisances unto the son of Mahäräja Nanda who is standing
before me with conchshell, earrings and peacock feather on His Head. His face is beautiful; He is
wearing a helmet, garlanded by forest flowers, and He stands with a morsel of food in His hand. He
is decorated with cane and bugle, and He carries a buffalo horn and flute. He stand before me with
small lotus feet."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.106
records.text:
Text 1


   tad evaà sädhüktaà tat-tad-vacanam anyarthatvena dåçyam iti. tathä hi pürva-rétyä
caturbhujatva-dvibhujatvayor dvayor api dhyäna-dhiñëyatve sati yat pürvasya jananya niguhana-
prärthanaà tat tu tasya prasiddhatayä sarva eva jïasyatéti janma te mayy asau päpo me vidyän
madhusüdana-ity-ädy-ukta-lakñaëayä kaàsa-bhiyä, viçvaà yad etat sva-tanau niçänte-ity-ädy-ukta-
lakñaëayä maàsa-dåk-çabdokta-bhagavat-svarüpa-çakti-viläsa-taj-janmädi-lélä-tattvänabhijïa-
präkåta-dågbhyo lajjayä ca, na punar aparasya güòhaà paraà brahma manuñya-liìgam-ity-ädau
güòhatvena kathitasya dhyäna-dhiñëyatvabhäva-vivakñayä.

  tat-therefore; evam-in this way; sadhu-well; uktam- described; tat-tat-various; vacanam-

statements; anya-arthatvena-with a different subject; drsyam-may be seen; iti- thus; tatha hi-for
example; pürva-previous; ritya-be exposition; caturbhujatva-the fourhanded; dvibhujatvayoh-and of
the two-handed form of Krssna; dvayoh-of the two; api-also; dhyana-dhisnyatve-sati-meditated; yat-
which; pürvasya- previous; jananya-by Mother Devaki; niguhana-concealment; prarthanam-prayer;
tat-therefore; tu-certainly; tasya-of Him; prasiddhataya-with fame; sarve-everything; eva-certainly;
jïäsyati-you will understand; iti-thus; janma ta mayi asau papah na vidyat madhusudana-iti-ädi-
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.29:


janma te mayy asau päpo
   mä vidyän madhusüdana
samudvije bhavad-dhetoù
   kaàsäd aham adhéra-dhéù

uktya-by the statement; lakñaëaya-characterized; kamsa-of Kamsa; bhiya-by fear; visvam yat etat sva-
tanau nisante-iti-ädi-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.31


viçvaà yad etat sva-tanau niçänte
   yathävakäçaà puruñaù paro bhavän
bibharti so 'yaà mama garbhago 'bhüd
   aho nå-lokasya viòambanaà hi tat

ukta-the statement; lakñaëaya-characterized; mamsa-material; drk-eyes; sabda-word; ukta-described;
bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; svarüpa-of the original form; sakti-potency;
vilasa-pastimes; tat-His; janma-birth; ädi-beginning with; lila-of the pastimes; tattva-the truth;
anabhijïä-ignorant; prakåta-material; drgbhyah-for the eyes; lajjaya-with embarressment; ca-also;
na-not; punah-again; aparasya-of the inferior; gudham-hidden; iti-thus; adau-in the passage
beginning; gudhatvena-by the position of being concealed; kathitasya-described; dhyana-dhisnyatva-
the position of being the proper object of meditation; abhava-state of not-being; vivakñaya-with a
desire to describe.


   We have now clearly proved the eternality of the form of Çré Kåñëa and answered all doubts and
objections. We shall now proceed to another topic: the transcendental opulences of Çré Kåñëa.
   Let us consider now the two forms of Çré Kåñëa: the two-handed and four-handed forms. Lord
Kåñëa first appeared before mother Devaké in His four-handed form. Fearing what Kaàsa might do
to her son, Devaké requested that Kåñëa conceal His four-handed form. She said (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.3.29):

   "O Madhusüdana, because of Your appearance, I am becoming more and more anxious in fear of
Kaàsa. Therefore, please arrange for that sinful Kaàsa to be unable to understand that You have
taken birth from my womb."*

  Fearing the ridicule of ordinary persons who are unaware of the transcendental nature of the

appearance, pastimes, and potencies of the Personality of Godhead, and who see Him with
materially contaminaded eyes, Devaké gave another reason for Lord Kåñëa to conceal His four-
handed form (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.31):

   "At the time of devastation, the entire cosmos, containing all created moving and nonmoving
entities, enters Your transcendental body and is held there without difficulty. But now this
transcendental form has taken birth from my womb. People will not be able to believe this, and I
shall become an object of ridicule."*

  Actuallly the two-handed form of Lord Kåñëa is a very confidential form of the Personality of
Godhead, and it is very difficult to understand it. This is confirmed in the following explanation of
Närada Muni (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 7.15.75):

   "The two-handed form of Çré Kåñëa, who appears like an human being, is the Supreme aspect of
the Personality of Godhead. This feature of the Lord is very confidential and difficult to
understand."*


Texts 2-4


   çré-gopalä-täpané-çrutäv apy ubhayor api dhyäna-dhiñëytvaà çrüyate

mathuräyäà viçeñeëa
   mäà dhyayan mokñam açnute
añöa-patraà vikasitaà
   håt-padmaà tatra saàsthitam

   ity-ädiñu madhye. caturbhujaà saìkha-cakra-ity-ädikam uktvä. sarvänte såìga-veëu-dharaà tu
vä ity-äpy uktam.

    çré-gopäla-täpané-çrutau-in the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad (2.61-62); api-even; ubhayoh-of both; api-
also; dhyana-dhisnayatvam-proper object of meditation; çruyate-is heard; mathurayam-in Mathura;
visesena-specifically; mam-upon Me; dhyayan-meditating; mokñam-liberation; asnute-attains; asta-
with eight; patram-petals; vikasitam-blossoming; hrt-of the heart; padman-lotus flower; tatra-there;
samsthitam-situated; iti ädisu madhye-in this passage; caturbhujam saìkha-cakra-iti-ädikam-uktva-
having spoken these words; sarva-of everything; ante-at the conclusion; srnga-venu-dharam tu va
iti api uktam-in these words.



    That the devotees should meditate on Çré Kåñëa in both His two-handed and four-handed forms
is described by Lord Kåñëa Himself (Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad 2.74-78):

  "He who meditates on Me as I appear in Mathurä attains liberation. In his mind one should
meditate on Me standing on the blossomed eight-petaled lotus of the heart, My teo feet marked

with conchshell, flag and umbrella, My chest marked with Çrévatsa and splendid with the
Kaustubha gem, My four arms holding the conch, cakra, mace, and çärìga bow, My arms decorated
with armlets, My neck splendid with a flower-garland, My head circled by a splendid crown, My
ears decorated with glistening shark-shaped earrings, and My form splendid and handsome, holding
a flute and buffalo-horn bugle, and granting fearlnessness to the devotees."


Text 5


   evam ägame 'pi dvibhuja-dhyänaà çrüyate. tasàan nigüòhatva-vivakñaiva samécéna. tathaiva tad-
vivakñayä nänyathä mad-bhävaà jïanaà martya-liìgena jäyate iti çré-bhägavatoktam.

accepted and rejected various mental stages or conceptions. The samemeaning of the words "tanu",
"rüpa", and "kalevara" applies in this verse in relation to the Personality of Godhead. This verse
does not, therefore, describe the Lord's abandonment of His form, but His rejecting a certain
condition of mind. Lord Krñëa descended to relieve the burden of the earth and protect the
demigods and devotees. When these purposes were accomplised, the Lord gave up the desire to
relieve the earth and protect the pious. It is these desires that are intended by the words "tanu",
"rüpa", and "kalevara" in this verse.

relation to the example of the thorn being used to remove the thorn. These two thorns (the
devotees and the demons) are closely related to the "tanu" (the two desires) given up by the Lord.

(Anucchedas 85-87), and we refer the reader to that passage for more information.

The phrase therefore means that the Personality of Godhead accepts and rejects the desire to
protect the devotees and kill the demons as the need arises. In other words, when the devotees
require protection, the Lord thinks about their protection, and when the demons cause a
disturbance, at that time the Lord thinks about their destruction.

shows that the Personality of Godhead accepts and rejects various material forms, just as an actor
plays a role on the stage. The actual intention of the example of the actor is that the actor accepts
the different sentiments and emotions of the hero or heroine, and then rejects those emotions also
in the course of the drama. In the same way the Supreme Personality of Godhead accepts different
emotions to protect the devotees and vanquish the demons, and the Lord also rejects those same
emotions at another time in order to fulfill the same purpose. That is the actual meaning of the
example of the actor, and it is confirmed by the following definition of the word "actor" found in
Srédhära Svämé's commentary on Srémad-Bhägavatam 1.11.21:

usage of this word, but actually this interpretation is very appropriate. We see many examples of the
usage of obscure meanings of words. For example in the Sahasra-näma-bhäñya we find the
explanation:

   "In this verse the statement `He does the saintly devotees' actually means `He protects the saintly
devotees' for in this context the verb `to do' (kr) means `to protect'".

   Another example of an obscure usage of a word is the phrase "käñthäni kuru". Although the verb
"kr" generally means "to do", in this phrase it means "to bring", and therefore "käñthäni kuru" means
"please bring some wood".

  In these verses from Brahma-saàhitä the abode of Sré Krñëa is described as a great thousand-
petaled lotus flower made of transcendental cintämaëi jewels. The phrase "mahat padam" may be
interpreted to mean either "the greatest abode" or "the abode of the supremely great Personality of
Godhead".
  Because this transcendental abode of Sré Krñëa is divided into three parts (Gokula, Mathurä, and
Dvärakä), the author of Brahma-saàhitä specifies the abode of Gokula as the object of his
description. The word "gokula" is generally understood to mean "an abode of cowherd men and
cows" and this meaning should be accepted in spite of any number of other fanciful interpretations,
based on etymology, that may be offered. The rejection of other interpretations of this word is
supported by the following statement of nyäya-çästra:

  "The generally understood meaning of a word is its primary meaning, and etymology-based
meanings are secondary to that generally understood meaning."

 In this way the Gokula described in these verses should be understood as the abode of Sré Krñëa,
Nanda, Yaçodä, and all their friends and relatives.

   Although the eighteen-syllable Krñëa mantra (kléà krñëäya govindäya gopéjanavallabhäya svähä)
is written in many places, the most important place it is written is described in the Brahma-saàhitä
verse quoted in Text 52. In this verse this mantra is described as written in a hexagonal figure in
the form of a mystic diagram. Within that hexagonal mystic diagram is situated the form of Sré
Krñëa, who is luminous as a diamond. The six words of the mantra are written on the six sides of
the hexagon. In that abode reside the predominated (prakrti) and predominating (puruña) aspects
of the Absolute. Both the predominated and predominating aspects are described as "pramänanda-
mahänanda-rasaëa avasthitam" (immersed in the bliss of countless varieties of exchanges of
spiritual love).
    The käma-béja syllable (klém) is described in these verses as situated within the eighteen-syllable
krñëä-mantra.
   After the description of the internal abode of Sré Krñëa, which is the whorl of the lotus-flower
known as Goloka, there is a description of the petals situated about that abode. Those petals are the
abodes of the cowherd residents of Goloka, who are all the relatives and friends of Sré Krñëa. That
the cowherds of Vrndävana are the relatives of Krñëa is described by Sukadeva Gosvämé in the
following verse (Srémad-Bhägavatam 10.36.15):

or Satyaloka. He may further say that that word "soma-gatiù" clearly means "the abode of the moon-

another planet within the material plane.

Brahmaloka) is not acceptable because the moon, sun, and other planets are all situated beneath
Maharloka and Dhruvaloka. Your interpretation of the word "sadhya" to refer to a class of minor
demigods is also unacceptable, for the minor Sadhya demigods are not at all qualified to protect the
abode of Lord Brahmä. We may also note that the Goloka planet is described as all-pervading (sarva-
gatiù) in Text 73 (hardly a word to describe an ordinary place). We are simply astonished that you
are offering such a contradictory interpretation.
