Vaikunthaoka; upari-above; api-although; sthitiù- situation; mähätmya-glorification; avalambena-in
reference to; bhajatäm-of the devotees; sphurati-manifest; iti-thus; jïeyam-may be known; ayam-
this; eva-certianly; mathurä-of Mathurä ; dvärakä-dvärakä; gokula-and Gokula; prakäça-
manifestation; atmakaù-consisting of; çré-kåñëalokaù- Çré Kåñëaloka; tat-with Lord Kåñëa; vihäriëä-
intimate devotee who directly performed pastimes; çrémat-uddhavena-by Uddhava; api-also;
samädhäu-in samadhi; anubhütaù-experienced; iti-thus; aha-Sukadeva Gosvami has described in
the Çrémad-Bhägavatam ( (3.2.6).


   These words of glorification spoken by the devotees prove that the earthly Våndävana is not
different from the limitless Goloka realm in the spiritual world. The Våndävana on this earth is
situated above all the Vaikuëöhalokas in the spiritual world. This has been established by the
previous statements of the Vedic literatures, where Våndävana-dhäma is glorified by the devotees.
This supreme spiritual planet, which is divided into three realms: Mathurä, Dvärakä, and Gokula,
was seen in trance by Uddhava, who personally enjoyed pastimes with Lord Kåñëa. Uddhava's
return to the material world after his vision of the Kåñëaloka planet is described in the following
statement of Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.2.6):


Text 166


çanakair bhagaval-lokän
   nålokaà punar ägataù

vimåjya netre viduraà
   prétyähoddhava utsmayan

spañöam. çré-çukaù.

   çanakaiù-gradually; bhagavat-the Lord; lokät-from the abode; nålokam-the planet of the human
beings; punaù ägataù-coming again; vimåjya-wiping; netre-eyes; viduram-unto Vidura; prétyä-in
affection; äha-said; uddhavaù-Uddhavaa; utsmayan-by all those remembrances; spañöam-the
meaning is clear; çré-sukaù-spoken by Sukadeva Gosvami


  "The great devotee Uddhava soon came back from the abode of the Lord to the human plane,
and wiping his eyes, he awakened his reminiscence of the past and spoke to Vidura in a pleasing
mood."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.107
records.text:
Text 1


imam eva lokaà dyu-çabdenäpy äha

viñëor bhagavato bhänuù
   kåñëäkhyo 'sau divaà gataù
tadäviçat kalir lokaà
   päpe yad ramate janaù

   imam-this; eva-certianly; lokam-planet; dyu-çabdena-by the word "divam"; api-also; äha-he said;
viñëoù-of Lord Visnu; bhagavataù-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; bhänuù- the sun; kåñëa-as
Kåñëa; akhyaù-named; asau-He; divam- to the spiritual world; gataù-gone; tat-that; aviçat- entered;
kaliù-Kali; lokam-the world; päpaù-in sins; yat-in which; ramate-engaging; janaù-the people.


   Lord Kåñëa's departure from this world and return to His own abode in the spiritual sky is
described in the following verses from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (12.2.29-30), where the word "divam"
refers to the Kåñëaloka planet:

   "Çré Kåñëa is like the sun, and Lord Viñëu is like a ray of light expanded from the original sun of
Lord Kåñëa. When Lord Kåñëa returned to His own abode in the spiritual world, Kali-yuga entered
this earth. Because of the entrance of kali-yuga, the people of the earth became addicted to sinful
activities.


Text 2

yävat sa pada-padmäbhyäà
   spåçann äste ramä-patiù
tävat kalir vai påthivéà
   paräkräntum na cäçakat

   yavat-as long as; saù-Lord Kåñëa; pada-padmabhyam-with His two lotus feet; sprsan-touching;
aste-remained; rama-of the goddess of fortune; patiù-the husband; tavat-fro that time; kaliù-Kali;
vai-certainly; prthivim-the earth; parakrantum-to overpower; na-not; ca-and; asakat-was able.


   "As long as Çré Kåñëa remained in this world, touching it with His two lotus feet, Kali-yuga
remained unable to overpower the residents of this earth."


Text 3


   yadä guëävatärasya bhagavato viñëoù tad-aàçatväd raçmi-sthänéyasya kåñëäkhyo bhänuù: süry-
maëòala-sthänéyo divam präpaïcika-lokägocaraà mathurädénäm eva prakäça-viçeña-rüpaà
vaikuëöhalokaà gataù, tadä kalir lokam äviçat.

   yadä-when; guëa-avatärasya-of the guëa-avatära; bhagavataù-of the supreme Lord; viñëoù-of
Lord Viñëu; tat-of Lord Kåçna; aàçatvät-as a plenary part; raçmi-sthänéyasya-as a ray of light; kåñëa-
as Kåñëa; akhyaù- named; bhänuù-the sun; sürya-maëòala-sthänéyaù-as the sun; divam-the word
"diva"m; präpaïcika-loka of the material world; agocaram-beyond the perception; mathura-adénäm-
of Mathurä , Dvarka and Gokula; eva-certainly; prakäça- manifestation; viçeña-specific; rüpam-
consisting; vaikuëöhalokam-Vaikuëöhaloka; gataù-gone; tadä-then; kaliù-Kali; lokam-this world;
äviçat-entered.


   Now (in Texts 3 and 4) we will explain the meaning of these verses. The phrase "viñëor
bhagavato bhänuù kåñëäkhyaù" means "Çré Kåñëa is like the sun, and Lord Viñëu is like a ray of
light expanded from the original sun of Lord Kåñëa." The word "divam" means the Kåñëaloka
planet, which consists of the realms of Mathurä, Dvärakä, and Gokula, and which is situated in the
topmost part of the non-material Vaikuëöha planetary system." When Lord Kåñëa returned to that
spiritual planet, then Kali was able to enter the earth.


Text 4


   eñäà sa ca prakäçaù påthivé-stho 'py antardhäna-çaktyä tam aspåçann eva viräjate. atas tayä na
spåçyate påthivyädi-bhütamayair asmäbhir värähokta-mahä-kadambädir iva. yas tu präpaïcika-loka-
gocaro mathurädi-prakääù, so 'yaà kåpayä påthivéà spåçan evävatérëaù. atas tayä ca spåçyate

tadåçair asmäbhir dåçyamäna-kadambädir iva. asmiàs ca prakäçe yad avatérëo bhagaväàs tadä tat-
sparçenäpi tat-sparçät taà spåçann eväste sma. tad etad abhpretyäha yävat: iti. paräkrantum ity
anena tat-pürvam api kiïcit kälaà präpya praviñöo 'säv iti jïäpitam. çré-çukaù.

   eñäm-of them; saù-that; ca-also; prakäçaù- manifestation; påthivé-sthaù-situated on the earth; api-
even; santardhäna-of disappearance; çaktyä-with the potency; tam- the earth; aspåçan-not touching;
eva-certainly; viräjate-is manifest ataù-from this tayä-by the earth; na-not; spåçyate-touched;
påthivi-adi-beginning with earth; bhütamayaiù-consisting of the various material elements;
asmäbhiù-by us; väräha-in the passage from the Väraha Purana; ukta-described; mahä-great;
kädamba-kädamba tree; adiù-beginning with ; iva-just like; yaù-which; tu-but; präpaïcika-loka-of
the material world; gocaraù-within the range of perceptionl mathura-Mathurä ; adi-beginning with;
prakäçaù-manifestation; sah ayam-that place; kåpayä- mercifully påthivém-the earth; spåçan-
touching; eva- certainly; avatérëaù-descended to; ataù-from this; tayä-by the earth; ca-also; spåçyate-
touched; tadåçaiù-like that; asmäbhiù-by us; dåçyamäna-seen kadamba-kadamba tree; adiù-
beginning with; iva-just like; asmin-in this; ca-also; prakäçe-manifstation; yat-because; avatérëaù-
descended; bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tadä-then; tat- His; sparçena-by the
touch; api-also; tat-His; sparçät- from the touch; tam-the earth; spåçan-touching; eva- certainly;
astesma-remained; tat etat-this; abhipretya- intending; aha-he said; yävat iti-the phrase beginning
with the word "yävat"; paräkrantum-to overpower; iti-thus; anena- by this; tat-purvam-previous; api-
even; kiïcit-a little; kälam-time;.fn
 2 präpya-attaining; praviñöaù-entered; asau-he; iti-thus; jïäpitam-instructed; çré-çukaù-spoken by
Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé.


   The Lord stayed on the earth for some time and then, by the agency of His antardhäna-çakti, left
and no longer touched the earth. As long as the earth was not touched by this antardhäna-çakti,
the great kadamba tree described in the Varäha Puräëa and other great wonders were manifest
before conditioned souls such as us. In this way Mathurä and the Lord's other abodes were manifest
before the senses of the people of the material world when the Lord, by His mercy touched the
earth (påthivém spåçan). When people like us are touched by His mercy in this way we are able to
see this kadamba tree and the other wonders of the Lord's abode. As long as the Lord's abode was
manifest, the Lord touched the earth (spåçan eva äste). This is the meaning intended when the
speaker of this verse said the word "yävat" (as long as).
   The phrase beginning with the word "paräkräntum" (Kali was unable to overpower the earth as
long as Lord Kåñëa touched it with His lotus feet) shows that Kali entered the earth planet shortly
before Lord Kåñëa's disappearance.
   These verses (quoted in Texts 1 and 2) were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.108
records.text:
Text 1

   tena dhérä api yaëti brahma-vida upakramya svargalokam ito vimuktäù iti çruty-anusäreëa
svarga-çabdenäpy äha

yatudhäny api sä svargam
   aväpa janané-gatim. iti.

    tena-by this; dhéräù-sober persons; api-also; yänti- go; brahma-vidaù-aware of the true nature of
the Supreme Personality of Godhead; apakramya-surpassing; svargalokam-the spiritual world; itaù-
then; vimuktäù-liberated; iti-thus; çruti-the description in the Brhad-aranyaka Upanisad (4.4.8);
anusäreëa-according to; svarga-çabdena-by the word "svarga"; api-also; äha-he said; yatudhäni api-
although she was a witch (whose only business was to kill small children and who had tried to
killKåñëa also); sä-she; svargam-the transcendental abode; aväpa-acheived; janané-gatim-the
position of a mother; iti-thus.


   The transferral of the devotees to the spiritual abode of Lord Kåñëa is described in the following
verses, where the word "svarga" means "the planet of Lord Kåñëa in the spiritual world":

  "The saintly devotees become liberated from the clutches of matter and enter the abode of Lord
Kåñëa
                -Båhad-äraëyaka Upaniñad 4.4.8

   "Although Pütanä was a great witch, she attained the position of Kåñëa's mother in the
transcendental world and thus acheived the highest perfection".*
                -Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.6.38


Text 2


   atra jänané-gatim iti viçeçeëa lokäntaraà nirastam. tat-prakaraëa eva tad-ädénäà bahuço gaty-
antara-niçedhät"sad-vesä iva pütanäpi sakulä tväm eva devä pitä ity atra säkñät tat-präpti
nirdharaëäc ca.

   atra-in this verse; jänané-gatim-the word "jänané-gatim iti-thus; viçeçena-as an adjective; loka-
antaram- another planet; nirastam-is refuted; tat-prakaraëe-in that chapter; eva-certainly; tat-
ädénäm-of other passages beginning with this one; bahuçaù-many; gati-destination; antara-another;
niçedhät-because of refutation; sat-vesätiva-appearing as a devotee; pütana-Pütana; api-even; sa-
kulä-with her brother Aghasura; tväm-You; eva-certainly; deva- the Supreme Personality of
Godhead; apita-attained; tat- Him; präpti-of attainment; nirdharaëat-because of conclusive
demonstation; ca-also.


   Because this verse states that Pütanä attained the post of Lord Kåñëa's mother in the svarga
planet, the svarga planet must be Lord Kåñëa's planet, Goloka Våndävana. The word svarga here
cannot mean the planet of Indra. That Pütanä became Lord Kåñëa's mother in the transcendental

world is also confirmed by the following statement of Lord Brahmä in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.14.35):

   "O My dear Lord, even Pütanä, who came to cheat You by dressing herself as a very affectionate
mother, was awarded liberation and the actual post of a mother. And other demons belonging to
the same family, such as Aghäsura and Bakäsura, were also favored with liberation."*


Text 3


   tathä ca kenopaniñadi dåçyate keneçitaà manaù patati, präëasya präëam uta cakñusaù cakñur
atimucya dhéräù pretyäsmäl lokäd amåtä bhavanti ity upakramya tad eva brahma tvaà viddhi: iti
madhye procya amåtatvaà hi vindate, satyam äyatanam, yo va etam upaniñadaà vedäpahatya
papmänäm anante svarge loke pratiñöhati ity upasaàhåtam.

   tathä-in the same way; ca-also; kena-upaniñadi-in the Kena Upanisad; dåçyate-is seen; kena-by
whom?; içitam- controlled; manaù-the mind; patati-falls; präëasya-of the breath; präëam-the
breath; uta-indeed; cakñusaù-of the eye; cakñuù-the organ of vision; atimucya-becoming liberated;
dhéräù-the saintly devotees; pretya-after death; asmät- from this lokät-material wrld; amåtäù-
immortal; bhavanti- become; iti-thus; upakramya-continuing; tat-that; egva- certainly; brahma-the
Supreme; tvam-You; viddhi-should know; iti-thus; madhye-in the middle; procya-having said;
amåtatvam-immortality; hi-certainly; vindate-he attains; satyam-the eternal; äyatanam-abode; yaù-
one who; vai- certainly; etam-this; upaniñadam-Upanisad; veda-understnads; apahatya-having
destroyed; papamänam-all sinful reactions; anante-in the unlimited; svargeloke-spiritual world;
pratiñöhati-becomes established; iti-thus; upasaàhåtam- summarized.


   The devotees' attainment of the spiritual world is also described in the following statements of
the Kaöha Upaniñad, where the word "svarga" is also used to meant the spiritual world (and not the
planet of Indra):

   "Lord Çiva asked: Who si the controller of the mind and the other senses?
   "Brahmä replied: the ability to see, the functions of all the senses, and indeed life itself, are all
given to the living entities by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The saintly devotees who
understand this true position of the Supreme Lord become free from the cycle of birth and death,
After leaving this body, they return tothe spiritual world, never again to take birth or die."
                  -1.1-2

   "Please try to understand the truth of tthe Supreme Personality of Godhead. One who
understands the Supreme Lord returns to the spiritual world and becomes free from birth and
death."
                   -1.4, 2.4

   "The transcendental abode of the Supreme Lord is eternal."

                  -4.8

  "One who understands the teaching of this Upaniñad becomes free from all past sinful reactions.
He becomes liberated and enters the unlimited spiritual world (svarga)."
                 -4.9


Text 4


   tataù ko vä svargaù kià tad brahma. ity apekñäyäm puruño ha vai näräyaëaù: ity upakramya
punaç cäbhyäsena nityo deva eko näräyaëaù ity uktvä näräyanopäsakasya ca stutià kåtvä tad
brahma näräyaëa eva iti vyajya svargaà pratipädayitum vaikuëöhavana-lokaà gamiñyati, tad idaà
puram idaà puëòarékaà vijïäna-ghanaà tasmät tad ivä vabhäsam. iti vana-lokäkärasya
vaikuëöhasyänandätmakatvaà pratipädya sa ca tad-adhiñöhätä näräyaëaù kåñëa evety upasaàharati
brahmaëyo devaké-putraù iti. çré-çukaù.

   tataù-according to these statements; kaù-what is intended?; vä-or; svargaù-by the use of the
word"svarga"; kim-what is meant?; tat brahma-by the use of the word "brahma"; iti apekñäyäm-in
reference to this question; puruñaù-the Supreme Person; ha-certainly; vai-indeed; näräyaëaù-is
known as Narayana; iti-thus; upakramya-continuing; punaù- again; ca-also; abhyäsena-by
continued study; nityaù-the eternal; deva-Supreme Lord; ekaù-is only; näräyaëaù- Näräyaëa; iti-
thus; uktvä-speaking; näräyaëa-of Lord Näräyaëa; upäsakasya-of the devotee; ca-also; stutim-
prayer; kåtvä-having spoken; tat-that; brahma-Absolute Truth; näräyaëaù-is Lod Näräyaëa; eva-
certainly; iti-thus; vyajya-indicating; svargam-the word "svarga"; pratipädayitum-to establish the
definition; vaikuëöhavana-lokam-the Vaikuntha planetary system; gamiñyati-he will go; tat idam-
that very; puram-city; idam-this; puëòarékam-lotus flower; vijïäna-ghanam-full of transcendental
knowledge; tasmät-therefore; tat-that; iva-just like avabhäsam-is manifested;iti-thus; vana-loka-
akärasya-of the transcendental forest; vaikuëöashy-of Vaikuëöha; ananda-atmakatvam-the
blissfulness; pratipädya-establishing; saù-He; ca-also; tat- of that; adhiñöhätä-the creator; näräyaëaù-
Näräyaëa; kåñëaù-Kåñëa; eva-certainly; iti-thus; upasaàharati- concludes; brahmaëyaù-the
Original Personality of Godhead; devaki-of Devaké; putraù-the son; iti-thus; çré-çukaù- spoken by
Çré Çukadeva Gosvami.


   Someone may question our interpretation of the words "svarga" and "brahma" in these passages.
In order to allay their doubts we give the following evidence from Vedic literatures to confirm our
understanding that the word "svarga" means "the planet of Çré Kåñëa" and the word "brahma means
"the Personality of Godhead, Çré Kåñëa, who is known as Näräyaëa".

   "Lord Näräyaëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead".
                -Näräyaëa Upaniñad

   "Lord Näräyaëa is the eternal Supreme Lord".
                -Näräyaëa Upaniñad

   "Lord Näräyaëa is the Supreme Brahman."
                -Prayers of the devotees
                of Lord Näräyaëa

   That the word "svarga" means "the abode of Çré Kåñëa" is described in the Vedic literatures:

   "Saintly devotee will attain the highest Vaikuëöha planet, which is a forest in the form of a great
lotus flower full of transcendental knowledge."

   In this way the blissful nature of Vaikuëöhaloka's forest (Kåñëaloka) is described. The ruler of
that forest is Lord Kåñëa, who is known as Näräyaëa. This is confirmed in the Atharva Veda:

   "The son of Devaké is the Original Personality of Godhead."

   The Çrémad-Bhägavatam verse quoted in Text 1 was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.109
records.text:
kañöhä-çabdenäpi tam evoddiçati

brühi yogeçvare kåñëe
   brahmanye dharma-varmaëi
sväà käñöhäm adhunopete
   dharmaù kaà çaraëaà gataù

   sväà kañöhäà diçam. yatra svayaà nityaà tiñöhati, tatraiva präpaïcika-loka-sambandhaà
tyaktvä gate satéty arthaù. çré-çaunakaù.

   kaçthä-çabdena-by the word "kastha"; api-also; tam- that; eva-certainly; uddiçati-he indicates;
brühi-please tell; yoga-éçvare-the Lord of all mystic powers; kåñëe- Lord Kåñëa; brahmaëye-the
Absolute Truth; dharma-religion; varmaëi-protector; sväm-own; käñöhäm-abode; adhunä-
nowadays; upete-having gone away; dharmaù-religion; kam-unto whom; çaraëam-shelter; gataù-
gone. sväm kañöhäm-the words "svam kastham"; diçam-mean "own direction"; yatra-where; svayam-
personally; nityam-eternally; tiñöhati-He remains; tatra-there; eva-certainly; präpaïcika-loka-the
material world; sambandham-contact; tyaktvä-having abandoned; gate sati-having gone; iti-thus;
arthaù-the meaning; çré-çaunakaù-spoken by Çré Saunaka Rsi.


   The word "kañöhä"is also used to mean the abode of Lord Kåñëa. This is confirmed by the
following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.1.23):

   "Since Çré Kåñëa, the Absolute Truth, the master of all mystic powers, has departed for His own
abode (kañöhä), please tell us to whom the religious principles have now gone for shelter."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.110
records.text:
Text 1


tad evam abhipretya dvärakäyäs tävan nitya-çré-kåñëa-dhämatvam äha

satyaà bhayäd iva guëebhya urukramäntaù
   çete samudra upalambhana-mätra ätmä
nityaà kad-indriya-gaëaiù kåta-vigrahas tvaà
   tvat-sevakair nåpa-padaà vidhütaà tamo-'ndham

   tat-this; evam-in this way; abpretya-intending; dvarakayaù-of Dväraka; tävat-in that way; nitya-
eternal; çré-krçëa-of Çré Kåñëa; dhämatvam-status as the abode; äha-she describes; satyam-in truth;
bhayät-because of fear; iva-as if; guëebhyaù-from the qualities of material nature; urukrama-O
Supremely powerful Lord; antaù-within the heart; çete-You remain; samudre-in the ocean;
upalambhana-mätraù-the form of transcendental knowledge; ätmä-the Supersoul; nityam-eternally;
kat-indriya-gaëaiù-with the senses; kåta-vrgrahaù-at war; tvam-You; tvat-Your; sevakaiù- by the
servants; nåpa-of king padam-the position; vidhütam- abandoned; tamah andham-darkness of
ignorance.


  That Dvärakä is the eternal abode of Çré Kåñëa is described by Queen Rukmiëé in the following
words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.35):

   "My dear husband, You have rightly said also that being afraid of the kings, You have taken
shelter in the water of the sea. But who is the king of this material world? I do not think that the so-
called royal families are kings of the material world. The kings of the material world are the three
modes of material nature. They are actually the controllers of this material world. You are situated
in the core of everyone's heart where you remain completely aloof from the touch of the three
modes of material nature, and there is no doubt about it.
   "You say You always maintain enmity with the worldly kings. But who are the worldly kings? I
think the worldly kings are the senses. They are most formidable, and they control everyone.
Certainly You maintain enmity with these material senses. You are never under the control of the
senses; rather, You are the controller of the senses, Håñékeça. My dear Lord, You have said that You
are bereft of all royal power, and that is also correct. Not only are You bereft of material world
supremacy, but even Your servants, those who have some attachment to Your lotus feet, also give
the material world supremacy because they consider the material position to be the darkest region,
which checks the progress of spiritual enlightenment. Your servants do not like material supremacy,
so what to speak of you?"*


Text 2

ayam arthaù-pürvaà çré-kåñëadevena çré-rukmiëé-devyai

räjabhyo bibhyataù subhru
   samudraà çaraëaà gatän
balavadbhiù kåta-dveñän
   präyas tyakta-nåpäsanän

   ayam-this; artha-meaning; pürvam-previously; çré- kåñëadevena-by Çré Kåñëadeva; çré-rukmiëé-
devyai-to Queen Rukmini; räjabhyaù-of the kings; bibhyataù-afraid; subhru-O Queen Rukmini,
whose eyebrows are very beautiful; samudram-in the ocean; çaraëam-shelter; gatän-gone to;
balavadbhiù-powerful; kåta-dveñän-enimical; präyaù-for the most part; tyakta-abandoned; nåpa-of a
king; asanän- position.


   This statement of Queen Rukmiëé was her reply to these teasing words previously spoken to her
by Lord Kåñëa (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.12):

   "My dear beautiful Queen Rukmiëé, you may know that I was so much afraid of Jaräsandha that I
could not dare to live on the land, and thus I have constructed this house within the water of the
sea. It is not My business to disclose this secret to others, but you must know that I am not very
heroic; I am a coward and am afraid of them. Still I am not safe, because all the great kings of the
land are inimical to Me. I have personally created this inimical feeling by fighting with them in
many ways. Another fault is that although I am on the throne of Dvärakä I have no immediate
claim. Although I got a kingdom by killing My maternal uncle Kaàsa, the kingdom was to go to My
grandfather; so actually I have no possession of a kingdom."*


Text 3


   kasmän no vavåñe iti parihasitam. tatrottaram äha satyam iti. atra ätmä tvam ity etayoù padayor
yugapat çete iti kriyänvayayogä viçeñaëa-viçeñya-bhävaù pratihanyate. väkya-bhede tu
kañöhatäpatet. tataç copmänopameya-bhävenaiva te upatiñöhitaù. iyaà ca luptopamä. tathä ca ätmä
säkñé yathä guëebhyaù sattvädi-vikärebhyas tad-asparçäl liìgät bhayädiva samudre tadvad agädhe
viçayäkärair aparicchinne upalambhana-mätre jïäna-mätra-sva-çakty-äkäre antaù hådaye nityaà
çete akñubdhatayä prakäçate. he urukrama tathä tvam api tebhyaù samprati tad-vikäramayebhyo
räjabhyaù bhayäd iva upalambhana-mätre vaikuëöhäntaravad cid-eka-viläse antaù samudre
dvärakäkhye dhämni nityam eva çeçe, svarüpänanda-viläsair güòhaà viharasi. artha-vaçäd vibhakti-
vipariëämaù prasiddha eva.

   ksamät-for what reason; na-me; va/våçe-you chose; iti-thus; parihasitam-joking; tatra-to this
statement; uttaram- reply; äha-she speaks; satyam-it is true; iti-thus; atra-in this statement; ätma-
the word "atma" ; tvam-You; iti-thus etayoù-of both; padayoù-statements; yuga-at-at the same time;

çete iti-the word "sete"; kriya-anvaya-ayogät-because of being not connected to the verb; viçeñaëa-of
the modifier; viçeçya-of tne noun so modified; bhävaù-nature; pratihanyate-is destroyed; väkya-
bhede-in the contradictory statement; tu-but; kañöhata-a difficult construction; apatet-may occur;
tataù-therefore; ca-also; upamäna-upameya-bhävena-in the nature of a comparison; eva-certianly;
te-the tow words; upañöhitaù-are situated; iyam-this; ca-also; lupta-upamä-an elliptical simile; tathä-
in the same way; ca- also; ätmä-the word "atma"; säkñé-the witness; yathä- just as; guëebhyaù-the
word "gunebhyah"; satva-adi-vikärebhyaù-the three modes of material nature-goodness, passion,
and ignorance; tat-asparçät-from non-cntact; liìgät-with the form; bhayät-from fear; iva-as if;
samudre-in the ocean; tadvat-in that way; agädhe-deep; viçaya-akäraiù-with the objdects of the
senses; aparicchinne- unlimited; upalambhana-mätre-the word "upalambhana-matre"; jïana-mätra-
sva-çakti-äkäre-means "the form of transcendental knowledge"; antaù-the word "antaù"; hådaye-
means "within the heart"; nityam-eternally; çete-remains akñubdhatayä-without disturbance;
prakäçate-is manifest; he urukrama-O All-powerful Lord; tathä-in the same way; tvam- YUou; api-
also;.fn
2 tebhyaù-of them; samprati-at the present moment; tat-vikäramayebhyaù-consisting of the modes
of material nature; räjabhyaù-of the kings; bhayät-from fear; iva-as if; upalambhana-mätre -in the
form of transcendental knowledge; vaikuëöha-antara-vat-as if in Vaikunthaloka; cit-eka-viläse- in
the transcendental abode; antaù samudre-within the ocean; dväraka-akhye-named Dvaraka;
dhämni-in the abode; nityam-eternally; eva-certainly; çeçe-You remain; sva-rüpa-of Your
transcendental form; ananda-bliss; viläsaiù-with pastimes; güòham-confidentially; viharasi-You
perform pastimes; artha-vaçät-because of the meaning of words; vibhakti-of the cases; vipariëämaù-
change; prasiddhaù-accomplised; eva-certainly.


   Kåñëa's teasing jokes to Rukmiëé consisted of a joking description of His own bad qualities.
Kåñëa proposed to Rukmiëé that she divorce Him and accept a more suitable husband. "Why did
you accept Me, who am so unqualified, as your husband?" Lord Kåñëa jokingly said. Rukmiëé-devé
replied to Lord Kåñëa's joking words by saying: "What you have spoken is the truth," and then
explaining how each point of Lord Kåñëa's self-criticism, is actually a glorification of His exalted
transcendental qualities. These two verses are an example of Lord Kåñëa's and Queen Rukmiëé's
replies.

   We may note that in this verse (Text 1) that the word "ätmä" is in the nominative case, the word
"tvam" is a first-person pronoun, and the verb "çete" is a verb in the third-person singular. These
words do not agree with each other (to agree with "tvam" the word "ätmä" would have to be in the
vocative and not the nominative case). In addition, the verb "çete" is in the third-person and also
cannot agree with the pronoun "tvam". Actually, however, the words "tvam", "ätmä", and "sete" are
intended to refer to each other. Their non-concordance is a use of the literary embellishment
"luptopama" (an elliptical simile)". The word "ätmä" in this verse is intended to also mean "the
Paramätmä (Supersoul) who is the witness observing the activites of all living entities.
   The word "guëebhyaù" means "the three modes of material nature: goodness, passion, and
ignorance". Afraid of these modes, Lord Kåñëa has taken shelter of "upalambhana-mätra" (His own
transcendental knowledge). The phrase "antaù nityaà çete" means "without any external
disturbance, Lord Kåñëa eternally resides in the hearts of all living beings." The phrase "urukrama

bhayäd iva upalambhana-mätre antaù samudre" means "All-powerful Lord, afraid of the kings who
are the material senses, sense-objects, and modes of material nature, You have taken shelter of Your
own transcendental abode which is known as Dvärakä-dhäma. You remain there and eternally
enjoy blissful confidential pastimes there." We may note in this verse that the meaning of the
sentence as a whole establishes the grammatical concordance of certain words which would
otherwise not be in grammatical agreement.


Text 4


udähariñyate ca nitya-sthäyitvam

nityaà sannihitas tatra
   bhagavän madhusüdanaù iti.

   udähariñyate-will be described; ca-also; nitya-sthäyitvam-eternal residence in Dvaraka; nityam-
eternally; sannihitaù-remaining; tatra-there; bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead;
madhuçudanaù-Lord Madhusudana; iti- thus.


  Lord Kåñëa's eternal residence in Dvärakä will also be described in a further chapter of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (11.31.24) in the following words:

  "Lord Madhusüdana eternally stays in Dvärakä".


Text 5


   ato vastutas tasya tad-äçrayakasya jéva-caitanyasya yadi tebhyuo bhayaà nästi, kintübhayaträpi
sva-dhämaikya-viläsitvät tatraudasinyam eva bhayatvenotprekñata iti bhävaù. evaà tasya tava ca
samaïjasatä. teñäà tu daurätmyam evety äha tathäpy ätmä kutsitänäm indriyäëäà gaëais tadéya
nänavåtti-rüpaiù kåto vigraho yatra tathä-vidhaù. tvam api kutsita indriya-gaëo yeñäà tathä-bhütai
räjabhiù kåta-vigrahaù. atra vigraha ubhayaträpy ävaraëa-dhärñöyam. yady evaà-bhütas tvam, tarhi
ka tava nåpäsana-parityäge häniù. tat tu tvat-sevakaiù prathamika-tvad-bhajanonmukhair eva
vidhütam tyaktam. tac coktaà tayaiva yad-vaïchayä nåpa-çikhamänayaù ity ädinä. yataù andhaà
tamaù eva tat, präkåta-sukhamayatvät, ataù çré-dvärakäyä nityatvam api dhvänitam. çré-rukmiëé çré-
bhagavantam.

   ataù-from this; vastutaù-in actuality; tasya-of him; tat-äçrayakasya-taken shelter of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; jéva-caitanyasya-of the individual living entity; yadi-if; tebhyaù-from
them; bhayam-fear; na-not; asti-is; kintu-however; ubhayatra-in reference to both the supreme Lord
and the individual living entity; api-also; sva-dhäma-in the Lord's transcendental abode; aikya-
viläsitvät-because of performing pastimes; tatra-there; audasinyam-indifference; eva-certainly;
bhayatvena-by fear; utprekñataù-from indifference; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning; evam-in the same

way; tasya- of Him; tava-of You; ca-also; samaïjasatä-properness; teñäm-of them; tu-but;
daurätmyam-wickedness; eva- certainly; iti-thus;äha-she describes; tatha api- nevertheless; ätmä-
self; kutisitänäm-wicked; indriyäëäm-of the senses; gaëaiù-with the multitudes; tadéya-of them;
nana-with various/ ävåtti-rüpaiù-repetitions; kåtaù- waged; vigrahaù-war; yatra-where; tathä-
vidhaù-in that way; tvam-You; api-even; kutsita-inimical; indiya-gaëaù- multitude of the senses;
yeñäm-of whom; tathä-bhütaiù-in that way; räjabhiù-with the kings; kåta-vigrahaù-the word "kåt-
vigrahah"; atra-in this; vigrahe-war; ubhayatra-in both places; api-even; ävaraëa-for protection;
dhärñöyam- courage; yadi-if evam-bhütaù-in this way; tvam-You are; tarhi-then; ka-what? tava-
Your; nåpa-of the king; asana- position; parityäge-in abandonment; häniù-loss; tat- therefore; tu-
but; tvat-sevakaiù-by Your servants; prathamika-for
emost; tvat-of You; bhajana-the worship; unmukhaiù-eager to perform; eva-certainly; vidhütam-the
word 'vidhutam"; tyaktam-means "abandoned"; tat-therefore; ca- also; uktam-spoken; taya-by Queen
Rukmini; eva-certainly; yat-vaïchayä-with a desire to engage in Your pure devotional service; nåpa-
çikhämayaù-the greates kings; iti-thus; ädinä-in the passage beginning; yataù-from which; andham-
blind; tamaù-darkness; eva-certainly; tat-therefore; präkåta-material; sukhamayatvät-from
happiness; ataù- therefore; çré-dvarakaù-of dväraka-dhama; nityatvam-eternal residence; api-even;
dha/vnitam-is described; çré-rukmiëé- spoken by Çré Rukmiëé-devi; çré-bhagavantam-to the Supreme
Personality of Godhead.


   Both the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the individual living entity are by nature aloof
from the material senses and sense-objects. Therefore, both the Lord and individual living entities
who take shelter of the Lord remain always unafraid of the material senses. In the second part of
this verse the enimical senses are described, and Lord Kåñëa is described as always at war with these
enimical senses, which are metaphorically described as kings. Lord Kåñëa is always very courageous
in the matter of defending Himself from the attacks of the senses.
   As far as Lord Kåñëa's abandonment of the post of king, Queen Rukmiëé replies:

  "What loss is there for You if You reject the royal post? This kingly post is rejected both by You
and by the great devotees who become Your servants."

   Queen Rukmiëé said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.41):

   "From the history of the world we can see that princes like Aìga, Påthu, Bharata, Yayäti and
Gaya were all great emperors of the world, and there were no competitors to their exalted positions.
But in order to achieve the favor of Your lotus feet, they renounced their exalted positions and
enterd into the forest to practice penances and austerities."*

   In the last part of this verse,the position of a king is described as "tamaù andham" (darkness of
ignorance) because a king has great facility for material enjoyment, which leads one into ignorance.
   In thise verse we may especially note the description of Lord Kåñëa's eternal residence in
Dvärakä (çete nityam). He stays there eternally.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.111
records.text:
atha çré-mathuräyäù

mathurä bhagavän yatra
  nityaà sannihito hariù iti.

arthät tätratämym. çré-çukaù.

   atha-now; çré-mathuräyäù-os Çré Mathura-dhama; mathurä-the place known as Mathurä ;
bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; yatra-wherein; nityam-eternally; sannihitaù-
intimately conncected, living eternally; hariù-the Lord, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
arthät-because of the meaning; tätratämyam-there; çré-sukaù-spoken by Çré Sukadeva Gosvami.


  That Çré Kåñëa eternally remains at Mathurä is confirmed by the following verse from Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.1.28) spoken by Çukadeva Gosvämé:

   "The city and district Mathurä are very intimately connected with Kåñëa, for Lord Kåñëa lives
there eternally."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.112
records.text:
tat täta gaccha bhadraà te
   yamunäyäs taöaà çuci
puëyaà madhuvanaà yatra
   sännidhyaà nityadä hareù

spañöam. çré-närado dhruvam.

   tat-that; täta-my dear son; gaccha-go; bhadram-good fortune; te-for you; yamunäyaù-of the
Yamunä; taöam-bank; çuci-being purified; puëyam-the holy; madhuvanam-fo the name Madhuvana;
yatra-where; sännidhyam-being nearer; nityadä- always; hareù-of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead. spañöam-the meaning is clear; çré-näradaù-spoken by Çré Närada; dhruvam-to Dhruva
Maharaja.


  Lord Kåñëa's eternal residence in Mathurä is also described in the following verse of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (4.8.42) spoken by Närada Muni to Dhruva Mahäräja:

   "My dear boy, therefore I wish all good fortune for you. You should go to the bank of the
Yamunä, where there is a virtuous forest named Madhuvana, and there be purified. Just by going
there, one draws nearer to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who always lives there."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.113
records.text:
Text 1


tasya hareù çré-kåñëatvam eva vyanakti

ity uktas taà parikramya
   praëamya ca nåpärbhakaù
yayau madhuvanaà punyaà
   hareç caraëa-carcitam

   tasya-of Him; hareù-Lord Hari; çré-kåñëatvam-the position of being Lord Kåñëa; eva-certainly;
vyanakti- reveals; iti-thus; uktaù-being spoken; tam-him (Närada Muni_; parikramya-by
circumambulating; praëamya-by offering obeisances; ca-also- nåpa-arbhakaù-the boy of the King;
yayau-went to; madhuvanam-aforest in Våndävana known as Madhuvana; puëyam-which is
auspicious and pious; hareù-of the Lord; caraëa-carcitam-imprinted by the lotus feet of Lord Kåñëa.


  That the word "Hari" is another name of Lord Kåñëa is confirmed by the following verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 4.8.62):

   "When Dhruva Mahäräja, the son of the King, ws thus advised by the great sage Närada Muni,
he circumambulated Närada, his spiritual master, and offered him respectful obeisances. Then he
started for Madhuvana, which is always imprinted with the lotus footprints of Lord Kåñëa (Hari)
and which is therefore especially auspicious."*


Text 2


   pratikalpam ävirbhävät tasyaiva nitya-sannidhyatvaà gamyate. ata eva dvädaçäkñara-vidyä-
daivatasya çré-dhruvärädhyasyatv anyata eva taträgamanam abhihitam. çré-maitreyaù.

   pratikalpam-in every kalpa; ävirbhävät-because of appearance; tasya-of Him; eva-certainly; nitya-
sannidhyatvam- eternal residence; gamyate-is attained; ataù-eva-therefore; dvädaça-akñara-vidyä-
daivatasya-the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is worshipped by chanting the 12 syllable
mantra "om namo bhagavate vasudevaya"; çré-dhruva-arädhyasya-and who was thus worshipped by
Dhruva Maharaja; tu-also; anyataù-otherwise; eva-certainly; tatra-there; agamanam-arrival;
abhihitam- described; çré-maitreyaù-spoken by Çré Maitreya Muni.


  This verse explains that Lord Kåñëa eternally remains in Mathurä. If it were not so that Lord
Kåñëa eternally remains in Mathurä, His presence would have been explained by describing His

arrival in Mathurä from another place. There is no such description, so we must therefore conclude
that Lord Kåñëa eternally stays in Mathurä. In Mathurä, Dhruva Mahäräja diligently worshiped
Lord Kåñëa by chanting the 12 syllable mantra glorifying Him (om namo bhagavate väsudeväya).
This verse (Text 1) was spoken by Maitreya Muni.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.114
records.text:
Text 1


atha çré-våndävanasya

puëyä bata vraja-bhuvo yad ayaà nå-liìga-
   güòhaù puräëa-puruño vana-citra-mälyaù
gäù pälayan saha-balaù kvaëayaàç ca veëuà
   vikréòayäïcati giritra-ramärcitäìghriù

   puëyäù-pious; bata-indeed; vraja-bhuvaù-the land of Vrajabhumi; yat-where; ayam-He; nå-liìga-
güòhaù- appearing as an ordinary human being; puräëa-puruñaù-the oldest, the Supreme Person;
vana-citra-mälyaù-decorated with garlands of colorful forest flowers; gäù-the surabhi cows; pälayan-
protecting; saha-accompanied by; balaù-Balarama; kvaëayan-playing; ca-also; veëum-the flute;
vikrédaya-with transcendental pastimes; aïcati-going; giritra-by Lord Siva; rama-and Laksmi-devi;
arcita-worshiped; aìghriù-lotus feet.


  That Çré Kåñëa eternally remains in Våndävana is described in the following statement of the
women of Mathurä in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.44.12):

    "Dear friends, just imagine how fortuante the land of Våndävana is where the Supreme
Personality of Godhead Himself is present, always decorated with flower garlands and engaged in
tending cows along with His brother, Lord Balaräma. He is always accompanied by His cowherd boy
friends, and He plays His transcendental flute. The residents of Våndävana are fortunate to be able
to constantly see the lotus feet of Kåñëa and Balaräma, which are worshiped by great demigods like
Lord Çiva and Brahmä and the goddess of fortune."*


Text 2


   atra pürvädahåta-çruty-ädy-avastambhena tiñöhanti pürvadä itivad aïcati sadaiva viharatéti
mathurä-stréëäà çré-bhagavat-prasädajä yathävad bhäraté nihåtir iyam iti vyäkhyeyam. pura-striyaù
parasparam.

  atra-in this verse; pürväda-previously; ahåta- described; çruti-ädi-in the Vedas; avastambhena-by

scriptural evidence; tiñöhanti-remains; pürvadä-as begore; itivat-in the same way; aïcati-goes; sada-
eternally; eva-certainly; viharati-performs pastimes; iti-thus; mathura-of Mathurä -puri; stréëäm-of
the women; çré-bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; prasäda-from the mercy; ja-born;
yathävat-in the same way; bhäraté-Sarasvati; niùsåtiù- manifest; yiyam-she; iti-thus; vyäkhyeyam-
may be explained; pura-of the city of Mathurä ; striyaù-the women; parasparam- among themselves.


   Although Lord Kåñëa wsa present before them in Mathurä, the ladies of Mathurä in this verse
describe His presence in Våndävana. By the Lord's mercy the ladies of Mathurä were able to
understand and properly describe the transcendental situation: that even though the Supreme Lord
may appear in Mathurä or so many other places, He always remains in Våndävana and enjoys
transcendental pastimes there. this is also confirmed in many verses from Vedic literature.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.115
records.text:
Text 1


jayati jana-niväso devaké-janma-vädo
   yadu-vara-pariçat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam
sthira-cara-våjina-ghnaù susmita-çré-mukhena
   vraja-pura-vanitänäà vardhayan käma-devam

   jatati-eternally lives gloriously; jana-niväsaù-He who lives among human beings like the
members of the Yadu dynasty and is the ultimate resort of all living entities; devaké-janma-vädaù-
known as the son of Devaké(No one can actally became the father or mother of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead. Therefore devaki-janma-väda means that He known as the son of Devaké.
Similarly, He is also known as the son of yaçodä, Vasudeva or Nanda Mahäräja) yadu-vara-parisat-
served by the members of the Yadu dynasty of the cowherd men of Våndävana (all of whom are
constant associates of the Supreme Lord and are the Lord's eternal servants); svaiù dorbhiù-by His
own arms, or by His devotees like Arjuna who are just like His own arms; asyan-killing; adharmam-
demons or the impious; sthira-cara-våjina-ghnaù-the destroyer of all the ill forutne of all living
entities, moving and not moving; su-smita-always smiling; çré-mikhena-by His beautiful face; vraja-
pura-vanitänäm-fo the damsels of Våndävana; vardhayan-increasing; käa-devam- the lusty desires.


  Çré Kåñëa's eternal residence in Våndävana is also described in the following verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.90.48)

   "Lord Çré Kåñëa is He who is known as jana-niväsa, the ultimate resort of all living entities, and
who is also known as Devaké-nandana or Yaçodä-nandana, the son of Devaké and Yaçodä. He is the
guide of the Yadu dynasty, and with His mighty arms He kills everything inauspicious as well as
every man who is impious. By His presence He destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities,

moving and inert. His blissful smiling face always increases the lusty desires of the gopés of
Våndävana. May He be all glorious and happy!"*


Text 2


   yadu-vara-pariñat sabhyä-rüpa yasya saù, devaké-manma-vädaù taj-janmatvenn labdha-khyätiù.
devakyäà janmeti vädas tattva-bubhütsu-kathä yasya sa iti vä çré-kåñëaù jayati paramotkarçeëa
sadaiva viräjate. lohitoçëéçaù pracarantétivad yadu-vara-sabhyä-viçiñöatayaiva jayäbhidhänam. atra
yadu-vara-çabdena çré-vrajeçvara-tad-bhrätaro 'pi gåhyante, teñäm api yadu-vaàçotpannatvena
prasiddhatvät.

   yadu-vara-pariçat-this phrase; sabhyä-of the assembly; rüpa-consisting; yasya-of whom; saù-He;

proven that Çré Kåñëa eternally enjoys transcendental pastimes in the three abodes Våndävana,
Mathurä, and Dvärakä.

Text 1


    atha yad uktaà çré-våndävanasyaiva prakäça-viçeñe golokatvam, tatra prapaïcika-lokäprakaöa-
lélävakäçatvenävabhäsamäna-prakäço goloka iti samärthanéyam. prakaöa-léläyäà tasiàs tac-chabda-
prayoga-darçanä bhedäàça-çravaëäc ca. prakaöäprakaöa ayä lélä-bhedaç cägre darçayitavyaù. tad
evaà våndävana eva tasya golokähya-prakäçasya darçanenäbhivyanakti

   atha-now; yat-which; uktam-described; çré-våndävanasya-of Çré Våndävana-dhama; eva-certainly;

prapaïcika-composed of the five material elements; loka-in the material world; aprakaö-not

golokaù-Goloka; iti-thus; samärthanéyam-should be established; prakaöa-léläyäm-in the manifest
pastimes; tasmin-in that; tat-that; sabda-of words; prayoga-darçanät-because of the use; bheda-aàça-
a part of a part; çravaëät-from hearing; ca-also; prakaöa-manifest aprakaöatayä-and unmanifest; lélä-
of pastimes; bhedaù-distinctions; ca-also; agre-in the beginning; darçayitavyaù-should be revealed;
tat-therefore; evam-in thsi way; våndävane in Våndävana; eva- certainly; tasya-of that; goloka-as

Goloka; akhya-named; prakäçasya-of that which is manifest; darçanena-by the sight; abhivyanakti-is
manifest.


  When Lord Kåñëa's transcendental abode is manifest in the spiritual world it is known as
Goloka. In that Goloka planet the Lord enjoys aprakaöa pastimes, which He does not display in the
material world. These pastimes are different from the prakaöa pastimes He reveals in the material
world. We shall now discuss the difference between these prakaöa and aprakaöa pstimes, and also
we shall discuss the nature of the Lord's abode in the spiritual world, known as Goloka Våndävana.
These topics are described in the following passage, which describes the vision of Goloka
Våndävana revealed to the cowherd residents of Våndävana in the material world (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.28.10-17):


Text 2


nandas tv atindriyaà dåñövä
   loka-päla-mahodayam
kåñëe ca sannatià teñäà
   jïätibhyo vismito 'bravét

   nandaù-Nanda Maharaja; tu-but; atindriyuam-unprecedented; dåñövä-having seen; loka-päla-of
the demigod Varuna; maha-udayam-great opulence; kåñëe-to Kåçna; ca-also; sannatim-respectful
obesances; teñäm-of them; jïätibhyaù- to his relatives; vismitaù-astonished; abravét-spoke.


   "Nanada Mahäräja was surprised that, although the demigod Varuëa was so oplent, he offered
such respect to Kåñëa. This was very astonishing to Nanda, and he began to describe the incident to
his friends and relatives with great wonder.*


Text 3


te cautsukya-dhiyo räjan
   matvä gopas tam éçvaram
api naù sva gatià sükñmäm
   upadhäsyad adhéçvaraù

   te-they; ca-also; autsukya-with eager; dhiyaù-minds; räjan-O king; matvä-having considered;
gopaù-the cowherd men; tam-Him; éçvaram-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; api-perhaps; naù-
of us; sva-gatim-His own abode; sükñmäm- transcendental; upadhäsyat-may transfer us to;
adhéçvaraù- the Supreme Controller.

   "The friends of Nanda Mahäräja, all the cowherd men, became eager to know if Kåñëa were
actually the Supreme Personality and if He were going to give them all salvation.*


Text 4


iti svänäà sa bhagavän
    vijïäyäkhika-dåk svayam
saìkalpa-siddhaye teñäà
    kåpayaitad acintyat

   it-thus; svänäm-of His own relatives and friends; saù- He; bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of
Godhead; vijïäya- having understood; akhila-dåk-who sees everything; svayam- personally;
saìkalpa-of their desires; siddhaye-for the fulfillment; teñäm-fo them; kåpaya-with mercy; etat-this;
acintyat-thought.


  "When they were all thus consulting among themselves, omniscient Kåñëa understood their
minds. Being merciful to them, Lord Kåñëa reflected in the following way:*


Text 5


jano vai loka etasminn
   avidyä-käma-karmabhiù
uccävacäsu gatiñu
   na veda sväà gatià bhraman

   janaù-my own people, the residents of Våndävana; vai- certainly; loke etasmin-in this world;
avidyä-from ignorance; käma-karmabhiù-with actions for material sense-gratification; ucca-
avac/esu-in thigher and lower; gatiçu-species of life; na-not; veda-know; sväm-their own; gatim-
destination; bhraman-wandering.


   "Generally ordinary persons are engaged in simply working hard in the material world. Engaged
in ignorant materialistic activities, the conditioned souls rotate through various higher and lower
species of life. They have no information that there is an eternal spiritual world.*


Text 6


iti saïcintya bhagavän
    mahä-käruëiko hariù

darçayäm äsa lokaà svaà
   gopänäm tamasaù param

   iti-thus; säncintya-considering; bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; mahä-käruëika-
very merciful; hariù- Lord Hari; darçayäm äsa-revealed; lokam-planet; svam-His own; gopänäm-to
the cowherd men; tamasaù-the darkness of material existance; param-above.


   "Reflecting in this way, merciful Lord Hari revealed to the cowherd men His own transcendental
abode, which is above the darkness of the material world.*


Text 7


satyaà jïänam anantaà yad
   brahma jyotiù sanöanam
yad dhi paçyanti munayo
   guëäpaye samähitaù

   satyam-real; jïänam-full of knowledge; anantam- unlimited; yat-which; brahma-spiritual worldk;
jhotiù-self-illumined; sanätanam-eternal; yat-which; hi-certainly; paçyanti-see; munayaù-great
sages; guëa-apaye-in the transcendental position, above the three modes of material nature;
samähitaù-situated,


   "Thus Kåñëa showed them the eternal, ever-existing spiritual sky, which is unlimited, full of
knowledge, and self-illuminating. Information of the spiritual sky can be had only from great sages
and saintly persons who have already surpassed the influence of the three modes of material nature.
Unless one is constantly situated on that transcendental platform, it is not possible to understand
the spiritual nature.*


Text 8


te tu brahma-hradaà nétä
   magnäù kåñëena coddhåtäù
dadåçur brahmaëo lokaà
   yaträkrüro 'dhyagat purä

   te-they; tu-certainly; brahma-hradam-the lake of Brahma; nétäù-brought; magnäù-immersed;
kåñëa-with Kåñëa; ca-also; uddhåtäù-risen; dadåçuù-saw; brahmaëaù-lokam- the spiritual planets;
yatra-where; akruraù-Akrura; adhayagat-had gone; purä-before.

   "Thus Kåñëa led all the cowherd men, headed by Nanada Mahäräja, to the lake where Akrüra
was later to be shown the Vaikuëöha planetary system. They took their bath immediately and saw
the real nature of the Vaikuëöhalokas.*


Text 9


nandädayas tu taà dåñövä
   paramänanda-nirvåtäù
kåñëaà ca tatra chando bhiù
   stüyamänaà suvismitäù

   nanda-Nanda; adyaù-and the other cowherd men; tu- certainly tam-Lord Kåñëa; dåñövä-having
seen; parama- ananda-nirvåtäù-full of transcendental bliss; kåñëam- Kåñëa; ca-also; tatra-there;
chandobhiù-by the Vedic hymns; stüyamänam-being glorified; suvismitäù-greatly astonished.


   "After seeing the spiritual sky and the Vaikuëöhalokas, all the men, headed by Nanda Mahäräja,
felt wonderfully blissful, and coming out of the river, they saw Kåñëa, who was being worshiped
with excellent prayers."*


Text 10


  aténdriyam adåñöa-pürvam, loka-pälaù varuëaù, sva-gatim sva-dhäma, sükñmäm durjïeyäm,
upadhäsyat ity arthaù.

   atindriyam-the word "atindriyam"; adåñöa-pürvam-means "never before seen" loka-pälaù-the word
"loka-pälaù" varuëaù-refers to Varuna; sva-gatim-the word "sva-gatim"; sva-dhäma-means "His own
transcendental abode; sükñmäm-the word "sükñmäm" durjïeyäm-means "difficult to be understood;
upadhäsyat-the word "upadhäsyat"; upadhasyati-means "will give"; naù-the word "nah"; asmän-
means "us"; prati-to; prapäyiñyati-will cause to attain; iti-thus; saìkalpitavantaù-considering;iti-thus;
arthaù-the meaning;


   In these verses the word "aténdriyam" means "never seen before", the word "loka-pälaù" refers to
the demigod Varuëa, the word "sva-gatim" means "His own transcendental abode", "sükñmäm"
means "very difficult to understand", "upadhäsyat" means "will give", and "naù" means "us". The
cowherd men thought that Kåñëa would enable them to enter the spiritual world.


Text 11

   jana iti. jana asau vraja-väsé mama svajanaù. etasmin prapaïcika-loke avidyäbibhiù kåtä ya
uccävacä gatayo deva-tiryag-ädayaù. täsu sväà gatià bhraman tabhyo nirviçeñatayä janän tam eva
sväà gatim. na vedety arthaù. tato 'yaà bhramo yadyapi tat-tal-lélä-poçayaiva madéya-lélä-çaktyä

tam äpaneçyäméti bhävaù. vailakñaëyaà cägre vyaïjanéyam.

   janah iti-the passage beginning with the word "janah"; janaù-the word "janah"; asau-this; vraja-
väsé-the residents of Vraja; mama-My; svajanaù-relatives; etasmin-in this; prapaïcika-loke-material
world; avidya-by ignorance; adibhiù-and other material imperfections; kåtäù-created; yaù-which;
ucca-higher; avacäù-and lower; gatayaù-statuses of life; deva-demigods; tiryag-animals; ädayaù-
beginning with; täsu-among them; sväm-their own; gatim-abode; bhraman-wandering; tabhyaù-
from these states of existance; nirviçeñatayä- without distinction; janän-perceiving; täm-that; eva-
certainly; sväm-their own; gatim-abode; na-do not; veda- understand; iti-thus arthaù-the meaning;
tataù-therefore; ayam-this; bhramaù-bewidlerment; yadyapi-although; tat-tat-various; lélä-pastimes;
poçaya-for increasing; eva- certainly; madéya-by My; lélä-for pastimes; çaktyä- potency; kalpitaù-
considered; tathäpi-nevertheless; tat- iccha-their desire; anusärena-in accordance with; kñaëa-
katipayam-for a moment; tadéyam-their; sarva-vilañaëam- extraordinary; sväm-own; gatim-
destination; darçayan- revealing; äpaneçyämi-I shall take away; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning;
vailakñyam-extraordinariness; ca-also; agre-in the beginning; vyaïjanéyam-is intended to be
experienced.


    In these verses the word "janaù" means the "residents of Vraja, who are all Kåñëa's relatives and
friends". Kåñëa considered that the cowherd men of Vraja had wandered through various species of
life in this material world, impelled by ignorance and other material faults, and therefore they were
unaware of Lord Kåñëa's own transcendental abode. In order to expand His own transcendental
pastimes the Lord manifested His own lélä-çakti (pastime potency) and revealed Hs extraordinary
abode to the residents of Vraja.


Text 12


   gopänäà svaà lokaà çré-golokam. yaù khalu cintämaëi-prakara-sadma ity-ädibhir bahu-varëita-
vyakta-baibhaväti-kranta-prapaïca-loka-mahodayas tam. tamasaù prakåteù param
prapaïcanäbhivyaktatvena tadéyenäpy asaìkaram. sta eva sac-cid-änanda-rüpa eväsau loka ity äha
satyam iti. satyädi-rüpaà yad brahma yac ca guëätyate paçyanti tad eva sva-rüpa-çakti-våtti-viçeña-
prakatyena satyädi-rüpävyabhicäriëaà golokaà santam darçayäm äseti pürveëänvayaù.
yathänyaträpi vaikuëöhe bhagavat-sandarbhodähåtaà padmädi-vacanaà brahmäbhinnatä-
väcitvena darçitaù tadvat.

   gopänäm-of the cowherd men svam-own lokam-planet; çré-golokam-Goloka; yaù-which; khalu-
certainly; cintämaëi-prakara-sadma-iti-ädibhiù-in the Brahma-samhita (2.29):

cintämaëi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-våkña-
   lakñävåteñu surabhér abhipälayantam
lakñmé-sahasra-çata-sambhrama-sevyamänaà
   govindam ädi-puruñaà tam ahaà bhajämi

bahu-in many places; varëita-described; vyakta-manifest; vaibhava-opulence; ati-kranta-surpassing;
prapaïca-loka-material world "tamasaù" prakåteù-means "the material nature"; param-above;
prapaïca-anabhivyaktatvena-as not material; tadéyena-His; api-certainly; asaìkaram-not toucheed;
atah eva-therefore; sat-eternal; cit-full of knowledge; änanda-and bliss; rüpaù-with a form; eva-
certainly; asau-this; lokaù-planet; iti-thus; äha-he describes; satyam iti-with the word "satyam"; satya-
adi-rüpam-wtih such a spiritual form; yat-which; brahma-spiritual realm; yat-which; ca-also; guëa-
atyaye-in the postion above the three modes of material nature; paçyanti-they see; tat-that; eva-
certainly; sva-rüpa-own form; çakti-potency; våtti-action; vieçeña-specific; prakatyena-by the
manifestation satya-adi-rüpa-avyabhicäriëam-eternal and spiritual ; golokam-Goloka santam-
spiritual reality; darçayäm äsa- revealed; iti-thus; pürveëa anvyayaù-the meaning of these words;
yatha-just as; anyatra api-in another place; vaikuëöhe-in aikunthaloka; bhagavat-sandarbha-in the
Bhagavat sandarbha; udahåtam-described; padma-adi-vacanam-in the statement of the Padma
Purana and other Vedic literatures; brahma-abhinnatä-väcitvena-described as purely spiritual;
daåsitaù-revealed; tadvat-in that way.


  The Goloka Våndävana planet, the ultimate destination of the cowherd residents of
Vrajabhümi, is described in Brahma-saàhitä (5.29):

   "I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, the first progenitor, who is tending the cows, yielding all
desires, in abodes built with spiritual gems and surrounded by millions of purpose trees. He is always
served with great reverence and affection by hundreds and thousands of goddesses of fortune."*

   The Goloka planet is completely spiritual and it is full of eternity, knowledge, and bliss. It is
above the darkness of the material world (tamasaù param). They who are above the three modes of
material nature, and are in the transcendental position, are able to properly understand the Goloka
planet. By manifesting His own transcendental potency, Lord Kåñëa revealed the Goloka planet to
the residents of Vrajabhümi. In the Bhagavat-sandarbha we have already quoted from the Padma
Puräëa and many other Vedic literatures many verses describing the Goloka planet as the highest
of all the Vaikuëöhalokas.


Text 13


    atha çré-våndävane ca tädåça-darçanaà katama-deça-sthitänäà teñäà jätam ity apekñäyäm äha
brahma-hradam akrüra-tértham kåñëena nétäù punaç ca tad-äjïayaiva magnaù punaç ca tasmät
térthät çri-kåñëenaiva uddhåtäù santo naräkåti-para-brahmaëaù äré-kåñëäsya lokam golokäkhyaà
dadåçuù. yatra ca brahma-hrade adhyaga açtü adhigatavän iti vä.

   atha-now; çré-våndävane- in Çré Våndävana-dhama; ca-also; tädåça-darçanam-appearing in that
way; katama-deça-sthitänäm-of many places; teñäm-of them; jätam- born; iti-thus; apekñäyäm-in
reference to that; äha-he said; brahma-hradam-the "brahma-hradam"; akrüra-tértham-the place
known as Akrüra-tértha; kåñëena-By Kåñëa; nétäù-brought; punaù-again; ca-also; tat-ajïaya-by His
order; magnaù-immersed; punaù-again; ca-also; tasmät-from that; térthät-holy place; çré-kåñëena-by
Çré Kåñëa; eva- certainly; uddhåtäù-risen; santaù-being; nara-akåti-in the form of a human being;
para-of the wupreme; bramaëaù-Godhead; çré-kåñëasya-of Çré Kåñëa; lokam-planet; goloka-akhyam-
named Goloka; dadåçuù-saw; yatra-where; ca-also; brahma-hrade-at Brahma-hrada; adhyagat-the
word "adhyagat"; añöaut-offered prayers; adhigatavän-learned the truth; iti- thus; vä-or.


    The cowhered men, coming from all different parts of Våndävana, were brought to Akrüra-
tértha by Kåñëa. By Kåñëa's order they took bath in the lake there and also came out of the lake.
The word "brahmaëaù" means " of Çré Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose
transcendental form appears like that of a human being", "loka" means "Goloka", "yatra" means "at
Brahma-hrada", and "adhyagat" may mean "offered prayers" or "understood the truth about Kåñëa".


Text 14


    sarvatraiva çré-våndävane yadyapi tat-prakäçeço 'sau goloko darçayituà çakyaù syät tathäpi tat-
tértha-mähätmya-jïäpanärtham eva vä vinodärtham eva vä tasmin majjanam iti jïeyam.

   sarvatra-everywhere; eva-certainly; çré-våndävane- in Çré Våndävana-dhama; yadyapi-although;
tat-of that; prakäça-manifestation; visesaù-specific; asau-that; golokaù-Goloka; daåsayitum-to be
revealed; çakyaù-is able; syät- may be; tathäpi-nevertheless; tat-that; tértha-holy place; mähätmya-
glories; jïäpana-teaching; artham-for the purpose; eva-certainly; vä-or; vinoda-pastimes; artham-for
the purpose; eva-certainly; vä-or; tasmin-in that lake; majjanam-immersion; iti-thus; jïeyam-may be
understood.


   Çré Kåñëa could have revealed Goloka Våndävana to the cowherd men from any place within
Våndävana-dhäma. Goloka was revealed at Brahma-tértha in order to glorify that specific place, or
also it may be said that Goloka was revealed at that place because the Lord wished to perform that
specific pastime there.


Text 15


   atra sväà gatim iti tadéyatä-nirdeço gopänäà svaà lokam iti çañöhé-sva-çabdayor nirdeçaù
kåñëam iti säkñät tan-nirdeçaç ca vaikuëöhäntaraà vyavacchidya çré-golokam eva pratipädayati. ata
eva teñäà tad-darçanät paramänanda-nirvåtatvaà suvismitatvam api yuktam uktam. tasyaiva
putratvät. tathaiva puträdi-rüpeëaivodayäc ca.

   atra-in these verse; sväm gatim iti-the word 'svam gatim"; tadéyatä-nirdeçaù-description;
gopänäm-of cowherd men; svam-own; lokam-planet; iti-thus; çañöhé-in the genetive case; sva-
çabdayoh-the two times the word "sva" is used; nirdeçaù-indication; kåñëam-Kåñëa; iti-thus; säkñät-
directly; tat-nirdeçaù-indication of that; ca-also; vaikuëöhä-Vaikuëöhäloka; antaram-within;
vyavacchidya- specifying; sri-golokam-Çré Goloka; eva-certainly; pratipädayati-establishes; atah-eva-
therefore; teñäm-of them; tat-darçanät-because of seeing Goloka; parama-ananda-nirvåtatvam-
transcendental bliss; suvismitatvam-great astonishment; api-also; yuktam-engaged; uktam-it is
described; tasya-of Him; eva-putratvät-because of the sonship; tatha-in the same way; eva-certainly;
putra-of son; adi-rüpeëa-and other relationships; eva-certainly; udayät-because of the arisal; ca-also.


   In the words "sväà gatim" and "svaà lokam", the word "svam" is understood to function as if in
the genitive case. In both places the word "svam" means "of the cowherd men". The spiritual abode
described in these verses is Goloka Våndävana, which is situated in the highest part of the
Vaikuëöhalokas, and which is the specific abode of Çré Kåñëa. By seeing the Goloka planet, the
cowherd men became astonished and filled with transcendental bliss. When they saw child Kåñëa,
whom they regarded with feelings of parental affection, glorified by the Personified Vedas on the
Goloka planet, they became struck with wonder.


Text 16


   tathä tatra kåñëaà yathä dadåçus tathä tat-parikaraëam anyeñäà darçanänuktes tä eka eva tatra
parikara ity abhivyajyate. tataç ca lélä-dvaye kåñëavat teñäm eva prakäça-bhedaù. yadä ca prakäça-

   tathä-in the same way; tatra-there; kåñëam-Kåñëa; yathä-just s; dadåsuù-they saw; tathä-in the
same way; tat-of Çré Kåñëa; parikaraëam-of the associates; anyeñäm-other; darçana-sight; anukteù-
because of the lack of description; t/e-they; ekaù-one; eva-certainly; tatra- there; parikaraù-
associate; iti-thus; abhivyajyate-is manifest; tataù-because of this; ca-also; lélä-dvaye-in both
pastimes; kåñëavat-just s Kåñëa; teñam-of them; prakäça-of manifestation; bhedaù-difference; yadä-
when; ca-also; prakäça-of manifestation; bhedaù-distinction; bhavati-is; tadä-then; tat-tat-lélä-rasa-
of the Lord's various transcendental pastimes; poçäya-for increasing; teñu-among them; tat-tat-
various; lélä-of pastimes; çaktiù- potency; eva-certainly; abhimäna-bhedam-distinction; parasparam-
mutually; an-anusandhänam-without inquiry; ca- also; präyaù-for the most part; sampädayati-
effects; iti- thus; gamyate-is attained; udähariñyate-will be described; ca-also; agre-at the beginning;
atah eva-therefore; uktam-is said; na-not; vda-know; sväm-their own; gatim-destination; bhraman-
being bewildered; iti-thus; tathä-in the same way; ca-also; sati-being so; idäném-at present; çré-vraja-
väsinäm-of the residents of Vraja; kathaïcit-somewhat; jétayä-produced; tadåça-like this; icchayä-

with a desire; tebhyaù-from them; teñäm-of them; eva-certainly; tädåçam-like this; prakäça-
manifestation; viçeña-specific; adikam-beginning with; darçitam-revealed; iti
-thus; gamyate-is attained; na-not; ca-also; prakäça-manifestation; antaram- another;
asambhävanéyam-not possible; parama-içvaratvena-as the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tat-of
Çré Kåñëa; çré-vigraha-of the transcendental form; parikara-associates; dhäma-abode; léla-pastimes;
adénäm-of those things beginning with these; yugapat-simultaneously; ekatra-in one place; api-
even; ananta-unlimited; vidha-manifestations; vaibhava-of opulences; prakäça-manifestation;
çélavat- because of possessing the nature; tat-therefore; evam-in this way; uktaù-spoken; arthaù-
meaning; samaïjasaù-properly; eva-certainly; çré-çukaù-spoken by Sri Sukadeva Gosvami.


   We may note in this description of Çrémad-Bhägavatam that there is no mention of Çré Kåñëa's
revealing the Lord's associates on the Goloka planet. The reason for this is that the residents of
Gokula Våndävana on this earth are the same personages who accompany the Lord in the Goloka
planet in the spiritual world. Because the residents of Gokula were unaware of their actual identity
and abode in the spiritual world (na veda sväà gatià bhraman) the Lord revealed to them their
actual home in the spiritual world. The Lord's transcendental form, associates, abode, pastimes, and
everything else in relation to the Lord possess unlimited opulence. They have the power to be
manifest in many places simultaneously. Therefore it is not impossible that the residents of earthly
Våndävana were the same liberated souls who associate with the Lord in Goloka Våndävana.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.117
records.text:
Text 1


   evaà dvärakädénäà tasya nitya-dhämatvaà siddham. atha tatra ke tävad asya parikaraù. ucyate.
puryor yädavädayo vane çré-gopädayaç ceti. devärakädi-nitya-dhämatvena teñäà svataù siddham.
tad-rüpative parikaräntaränäm ayuktatväd açravaëäc ca. tat-parikaratvenaiväradhanädi-väkyäni
darçitäni darçayitavyäni ca. ata evoktaà padme kärttika-mähätmye çré-kåñëa-satyabhämä-saàväde

    evam-in this way; dväraka-adénam-of Dvaraka and the other abodes of the Lord; tasya-of Him;
nitya-dhämatvam-the status s eternal abodes; siddham-is proven; atha-now; tatra- there; ke-who?
tävat-to that extent; asya-of that; parikaraù-associates; ucyate-it is said; puryoù-of the two cities
(Mathurä and Dvaraka); yädava-adayaù-the associates beginning with the members of the Yadu
dynasty; vane-in Våndävana; çré-gopa-adayaù-the gopas, gopis and others; ca- and; iti-thus; dväraka-
Dväraka; adi-beginning with; nitya-dhämatvena-as the eternal abode; teñäm-of them; svataù
siddham-axiomatic; tat-rüpatve-in that form; parikara-antaram-other associates; ayuktatvät-because
of impropriety; açravaëät-because of not being described in the Vedic literatures; ca-also; tat-
parikaratvena-as the Lord's associate; eva-certainly; aradhana-worship; adi-beginning with; väkyäni-
statements; darçitäni-revealed; daarçayitavyäni-should be revealed; ca-also; atah eva- therefore;
uktam-spoken; padme-in the Padma Purana; kärttika-mähätye-in the glorification of Karttika; çré-
kåñëa-of Çré Kåñëa; satyabhämä-and Satyabhämä; saàväde-in the conversation.

   Having decisively proven that Våndävana, Mathurä and Dvärakä are the eternal abodes of Lord
Kåñëa, we shall now begin our discussion of the Lord's liberated associates. Who are the Lord's
associates in these three abodes? In the two cities of Mathurä and Dvärakä, the Lord's associates are
headed by the members of the Yadu dynasty, and in Våndävana the gopas, gopés, and others are the
associates of the Lord. There is no description in the Vedic literatures of any other asociates of the
Lord. The exalted status of the Lord's associates is described by Lord Kåñëa in the following verse
from the Kärttika-mähätmya of the Padma Puräëa:


Text 2


ete hi yädaväù sarve
   mad-gaëä eva bhämini
sarvadä mat-priyä devi
   mat-tulya-guëa-sälinaù iti

eva-kärän na devädayaù.

   ete-these; hi-certainly; yädaväù-members of Yadu dynasty; sarve-all of them; mat-ganäù-My
associates; eva- certainly; bhämini-My dear Satyabhama; sarvadä-in all respects; mat-priyäù-dear to
Me; devi-O queen; mat-with Me; tulya-equality; guëa-qualitites; çälinaù-possessing; iti- thus; eva-
kärät-because of the word "eva"; na-not; deva-the demigods; adayaù-and others.


  "My dear Queen Satyabhämä, the members of the Yadu dynasty are very dear to Me. They are all
My intimate associates, and their transcendental qualities are equal to My own."

   We may note that by using the "eva" (certainly) it is is emphasized that this description applies
only to the Yädavas and not to the demigods or anyone else.


Text 3


çré-hari-vaàçe 'py aniruddhänveçaëa tädåçatvam evoktam akrüreëa

devänäà ca hitärthäya
   vayaà yäta manuçyatäm iti.

   çré-hari-vaàçe-in the Hari-vamsa; api-also; aniruddha-fro Aniruddha; anveçaëe-in the
description of the search; tädåçatvam-this same point; eva-certainly; uktam-is spoken akrüreëa-by
Akrüra; devänäm-of the demigods; ca-also; hita-arthäya-for the welfare; vayam-we; yätaù-have
attained; mauçyatäm-the status of human beings; iti-thus.

  That the members of the Yadu dynasty are more exalted than the demigods is confirmed by
Akrüra in the Aniruddhänveñaëa chapter of the Hari-vaàça:

  "In order to beneifit the demigods, we members of the Yadu dynasty are present on this earth,
appearing as ordinary mortals."


Text 4


   çré-mathuräyäà tv avatärävasare näbhivyakta api nigüòhatayä kecit tasyäm eva vartamänaù
çrüyante. yathä çré-gopälottara-täpanyäm

yaträsau saàsthitaù kåñëas
   tribhiù çaktyä samähitaù
rämäniruddha-pradyumnai
   rukmiëyä sahito vibhuù

    çré-mathuräyäm-at Mathurä -puri; tu-certainly; avatära-of the appearance; avasare-at the time;
na-not; abhivyakte- manifested; api-even; nigüòhatayä-with secrecy; kecit-some; tasyäm-at Mathurä
; eva-certainly; vartamänaù-at ptesent; çrüyante-are heard; yathä-just as; çré-gopäla-uttara-
täpanyäm-in the Gopala-tapani Upanisad 2.40; yatra-where; asau-He; saàsthitaù-situated; kåñëaù-
Kåñëa; tribhiù- by the three; çaktyä-with His potency; samähitaù- accompanied; räma-by Lord
Balarama; aniruddha-Aniruddha; pradyumanaiù-and Pradyumna; rukminya-and by Srémati
Rukmiëé-devi; sahitaù-accompanied; vibhuù-the all powerful Supreme Personality of Godhead.


   The same pastimes the Lord enjoyed at Mathurä during His manifest presence are secretly
enjoyed by Him there even today. This is described in Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad (2.40):

  "Lord Kåñëa, accompanied by His three potencies, and by Balaräma, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, and
Rukmiëé, eternally stays in delightful Mathurä-puré."


Text 5


   çré-våndävane taiù sadä vihäraç ca. yathä padma-pätäla-khaëòe çré-yamunäm uddiçya

aho abhägyaà lokasya
   na pétaà yamunä-jalam
go-gopa-gopikä-saìge
   yatra kréòati kaàsahä iti.

   çré-våndävane-in Çré Våndävana; taiù sadä-with them; vihäraù-pastimes; ca-also; yathä-just as;
padma-pätäla-khaëòe-in the Pätäla-khaëòa of the Padma Purana; çré-yamunäm-the yamunä river;
uddiçya-in relation to; aho-Oh; abhägyam-misfortune; lokasya-of those living entities; na-not; pétam-
drunk; yamunä-of the Yamuna; jalam-the water; go-the surabhi cows; gopa-the cowherd men and
boys; gopikä- and the gopis; saìge-in the company; yatra-where; kréòati- performs pastimes; kaàsa-
hä-Çré Kåñëa, the killer of Kamsa; iti-thus.


   That Çré Kåñëa eternally enjoys pastimes in Våndävana accompanied by His associates is
confirmed by the following statement of Padma Puräëa, Pätäla-khaëòa, where the Yamunä's glories
are described:

   "How unfortunate are they who have never drunk the waters of the Yamunä where,
accompanied by the cows, gopas, and gopés, Çré Kåñëa enjoys pastimes eternally!"


Text 6


skande tu

vatsair vatsa-taribhiç ca
   sadä kréòati mädhavaù
våndävanäntara-gataù
   sa-rämo balakair våtaù iti.

   skande-in the Skanda Purana; tu-also; vatsaiù-with the calves; vatsa-taribhiù-with the cowherd
boys; ca-also; sadä- eternally; kréòati-performs pastimes; mädhavaù-Çré Kåñëa; våndävana-
Våndävana; antara-gataù-entered within; sa-along with; rämaù-Balarama; balakaiù-with the boys;
våtaù-accompanied; iti-thus.


   This is also confirmed by the following statement of the Skanda Puräëa:

   "Accompanied by Balaräma, the cowherd boys, and the calves, Çré Kåñëa enjoys pastimes in the
forest of Våndävana eternally."


Text 7


   na tu prakaöa-lélä-gatebhya ete bhinnaù. ete hi yädaväù sarve ity anusärät. tathä hi padma-
nirmäna-khaëòe ca çré-bhagavad-väkyam

nityaà me mathuräà viddhi
   vanaà våndävanaà tathä

yamunäà gopa-kanyäç ca
  tathä gopäla-bälakän
mamävatäro nityo 'yam
  atra mä saàçayaà kåthäù iti.

   na-not; tu-but; prakaöa-manifest; lélä-pastimes; gatebhyaù-from those who participated; ete-they;
bhinnaù- different; ete-these; hi-certainly; yädaväù-Yädaväs; savre-all; iti-thus; anusärät-according
to these words; tathä hi-furthermore; padma-nirmäna-khaëòe-in the Niramana-khanda; of the
Padma Purana; ca-also; çré-bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; väkyam-the
statement; nityam- eternal; me-My; mathuräm-Mathurä ; viddhi-please know; vanam-the forest;
våndävanam-of Våndävana; tathä-in the same way; yamunäm-the Yamuna river; gopa kanyäù-the
gopis; ca- also; tathä-in the same way; gopäla-bälakän-the cowherd boys; mama-My; avataräù-
incarnation; nityaù-eternal; ayam- this; atra-in this connection; mä-don't; saàçayam-doubt; kåthäù-
entertain; iti-thus.


    The Lord's associates in His manifest pastimes are not different from His eternal associates. This
is described in the Lord's words to Satyabhämä:

   "All the members of the Yadu dynasty are My eternal associates".

   This is also described in the Padma Puräëa, Nirmäna-khaëòa, where Lord Kåñëa says:

   "Know that My Mathurä is eternal. So also is Våndävana. So also are the Yamunä, to gopés, and
the gopa boys. This incrnation of Mine is eternal. Do not doubt."


Text 8


atas tan evoddiçya çrutau ca, tatra åkñu

taà väà vastuny uñmasi gamädhye yatra gävo bhüri-çåìgä ayäsaù.
tad urugäyasya våñëaù paramaà padam avabhäti bhüri. iti.

   ataù-therefore; tan-to them; uddiçya-in relation; çrutau-in the smriti ca-also; tatra-there; åkñu-in
the Rg Veda; ca-and; tam-that; väm-of Kåñëa and Balaräma; vastuni-the transcendental abodes;
uñmasi-we desire; gamädhye-to attain; yatra-where; gävaù-surabhi cows; bhüri-with excellent;
çåìgäù-horns; ayäsaù-move about; atra- in the same scripture; aha-the seer describes; tat-that;
urugäyasya-of Lord Kåñëa, who is glorified by the liberated souls; vrsnaù-and who fulfills all the
desires of the devotees; paramam-transcendental; padam-abode; avabhäti-is splendidly manifest;
bhüri-unlimitedly; iti-thus.


    The Lord's aprakaöa (unmanifested) pastimes in the spiritual world are described in the Åg Veda
(1.154.6):

   "O Kåñëa and Balaräma, we desire to attain Your transcendental abode full of splendid surabhi
cows with beautiful horns. This spiritual realm is the abode of Lord Kåñëa, who is glorified by
liberated souls and whose lotus feet fulfill all the devotees' desires."


Text 9


   vyäkhyätà ca tam täni väm yuvayoù kåñëa-rämayoù vastüni lélä-sthänäni ga-madhye gantuà
präptum uñmasi kämayämahe.

   vyäkhyätam-explanation; ca-also; tam-the word "tam"; täni-means "them"; väm-the word "vam";
yuvayoù-means "of You two"; kåñëa-rämayoù-and refers to Lord Kåñëa and Lord Balarama; vastüni-
the word "vastüni"; lélä-sthänäni- means "places of pastimes; ga-madhye-the "ga-madhye" gantum-
means " to go to"; präptum-or "to attain"; uçmasi-the word "usmasi"; kämayämahe-means "we desire";


  An explanation of this verse follows: In this verse the word "tam" means "them, "väm" means "of
You two" and refers to Lord Kåñëa and Lord Balaräma, "vastüni" means "places of pastimes", "ga-
madhye" means "to go to" or "to attain", and "uñmasi" means "we desire".


Text 10


   täni kià viçiñöäni. yatra yeñu bhüri-çåìgäù mahä-çåìgyaù gävaù vasanti. yathopaniñadi bhüma-
vakye dharmi-pareëa bhüma çabdena mahiñöham evocyate, na tu bahutaram iti. yütha-dåñöyaiva
vara bhüri-çåìgäù bahu-çåìgyo bahu-çubha-lakñaëaiti va. ayäsaù çubhaù. atra bhümau tal-loka-veda-
prasiddhaà çré-golokäkhyam urugäyasya svayaà-bhagavataù våñëaù sarva-käma-dugha-
caranäravindasya paramam prapaïcätétam padam sthänam bhüri bahudhä avabhäti ity äha veda iti.

   täni-they; kim-what?; viçiñöäni-distinguishing characteristics; yara-the word "yatra"; yeñu-means
"among them"; bhüri-çåìgäù-the word "bhuri-srngah"; mahä-çåìgyäù-means "with large horns";
gävaù-cows; vasanti- reside; yatha-just as; upaniñadi-in the Upanisads; bhüma-vakye-the word
"bhuman"; dharmai-pareëa-by the saintly devotee; bhüma-çabdena-by the word "bhuman";
nahiñöham- greatness; eva-certainly; ucyate-is described; na-not; tu- but; bahutaram-plurality; iti-
thus; yütha-of the herd of surabhi cows; dåñöya-by the sight; varaù-excellent; bhüri-çåìgäù-intended
by the word "bhüri-çåìgäù"; bahu-çåìgyäù-"bahu-çåìgayäù"; bahu-the word "bahu"; çubha-means
"beautiful"; lakñaëaù-indirect meaning; iti- thus; va-or; ayäsaù-the word "ayasah" çubhaù-means
"splendid"; atra-the word "atra"; bhümau-means "on this earth"; tat-that; loka-among the people
veda-in the vedas; prasiddham-celebrated; çré-goloka-akhyam-named Goloka; urugäyasya-the word
"urugayasya"; svayam-bhagavataù-means "of the Original Personality of Godead"; vrsnaù-the
"våñëaù" sarva-käma-dugha-caraëa-aravindasya-means "of Him whose lotus feet fulfill all desires";
paramam-the "paramam"- the word "paramam"; prapaïca-atétam-means "beyond the material
energy"; padam-the word "padam"; sthänam-means "abode"; bhüri-the word "bhuri"; bahudhä-means

"in many ways; avabhäti-manifested; iti-thus; äha-he says; vede-in the åg Veda; iti-thus.


   How is this transcendental abode described? The description is found in the phrase that follows
the word "yatra". Synonyms for difficult words follow: "yatra" means "upon the surabhi cows"; "bhüri-
çåìgäù" means "there are beautiful horns" ("bhüri" means "beautiful" as well as "many". We see a
similar secondary usage of the word "bhüman" which is used in the Upaniñads not to express
plurality, but to mean "great"). "ayäsaù" means "splendid", "atra" means "in the earthly Goloka
Våndävana, which is famous both in the world and in the Vedas", "urugäyasya" means "of the
original Personality of Godhead", "våñëaù" means "of Him whose lotus feet fulfill all desires",
"paramam" means "beyond the reach of material energy", "padam" means "abode", "bhüri" means "in
many ways"; and "avabhäti" means "manifested". This description of Goloka Våndävana is found in
the Åg Veda.


Text 11


  yajuùsu madhyandinéyas tu ya te dhämany uñmasi ity ädau viñëoh paramaà padam avabhäti
bhüri it paöhanti.

   yajaùsu-in the Yajur Veda; madhyandinéyaù-the Madhyandina-sruti; tu-also; yaù-which; te-they;
dhämani-the transcendental abode; uçmasi-we desire; iti-thus; ädau-in the passage beginning;
viñëoù-of Lord Viñëu; paramam padam- the transcendental abode; avabhäti-manifests; bhüri-in
many ways; iti-thus; paöhanti-they read.


  The transcendental abodes of the Lord are also described in the Madhyandina-çruti of the Yajur
Veda in the following words:

   "We desire to attain the many transcendental abodes of Lord Viñëu".


Text 12


    padmottara-khäëde tu yat tv iyaà çrutiù paravyoma-prastava udähåtä, tat paramavyoma-
golokayor ekatäpatty-apekñayeti mantavyam. go-çabdaysa çaçnädimaty eva pracüra-prayogena
jhaöhity-artha-pratéteù, çré-golokasya brahma-saàhitä-hari-vaàça-mokña-dharmädiñu prasiddhatväc
ca.

   padma-uttara-khäëòe-in the Uttara-khanda of the Padma Purana; tu-certainly; yat-which; tu-
certainly; iyam-this; çrutiù-Vedic assertion; paramavyoma-of the Vaikuëöhä planetary system;
prastave-at the beginning; udähåtä- described; tat-therefore; paravyoma-of Vaikuëöhä; golokayoù-
and of Goloka; ekata-apatti-identy; apekñaya-in consideration of; iti-thus; mantavyam-should be
considered; go-çabdasya-of the word "go"; çaçnädimati-with the bulls; eva-certainly; pracüra-

prayogena-in the plural; jhaöhiti-at once; artha-meaning; prtéteù-becasue of conviction; çré-
golokasya-of Çré Goloka; brahma-saàhitä-in the brahma-saàhitä; hari-vaàça-Hari-vaàça; mokña-
dharma-Mokña- dharma; adiçu-and other Vedic literatures; prasiddhatvät- because of fame; ca-also.


   In the Uttara-khaëòa of the Padma Puräëa, Goloka Våndävana is described as one of the
spiritual Vaikuëöhä planets. Goloka Våndävana, the abode of many surabhi cows, is also glorified in
the Brahma-saàhitä, Hari-vaàça, Mokña-dharma, and other Vedic literatures.


Text 13


atharvni ca çré-gopäla-täpanyäm

   "janma-jaräbhyäm bhinnaù sthänur ayam acchedyo 'yaà yo 'sau saurye tiñöhati yo goçu tiñöhati
yo 'sa gäù pälayati yo 'sau gopeñu tiñöhati ity ädi.

    artharvani-in the Artharva Veda; ca-also; çré-gopala- tapanyam-in the Gopäla-täpani Upanisad
(2.23); janma-from birth; jaräbhyäm-and old age; bhinnaù-different; sthänuù- unchanging; ayam-
He; acchedyaù-who cannot be cut; ayam-He; yaù-who; asau-He; saurye-on the shore of the Yamuna;
tiñöhati-remaining; yaù-who; asau-He; goçu-among the cows; tisthati-remaining; yaù-who; asau-He
gäù-the cows; pälayati-protects; yaù-who; asau-He; gopeñu-among the cowherd men and boys of
Vraja; tiñöhati-stays; iti ädi-in the passage thus beginning.


  It is described in the Atharva Veda (Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad 2.27) in these words:

   "Kåñëa, who is free from birth and death, who is unchanging, who cannot be cut, who stays by
the Yamunä, who stays among the surabhi cows, and who protects the surabhi cows, stays among
the cowherd boys."


Text 14


    tad evam ubhayeñäm api nitya-parçadatve siddhe yat tu çasträghata-kñata-viça-päna-mürchä-
tattva-bubhütsa-saàsära-nistäropadeçäspadatvädikaà çrüyate, tad bhagavata iva nara-
lélaupayikatayä prapaïcitam it mantavyam.

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; ubhayeñäm-among them; api-also; nitya-parçadatve-in the state
of being eternal associates; siddhe-perfected; yat-which; tu-but; çastra-from weapons; aghata-by
blows; kñata-wounded; viça-of poison; päna-from drinking; mürchä-fainting; tattva-the truth;
bubhütsa-desire to know; saàsära-material existence in the cycle of birth and death; nistära-
overcoming; upadeça- instruction; aspadatva-as the abode; adikam-beginning with; çrüyate-is heard;
tat-that; bhagavataù-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; iva-just like; nara-léla-aupayikatayä-
