possessing pastimes just like an ordinary human being; prapaïcitam-material; iti-thus; mantavyam-
may be considered by the unintelligent.


   Although we have proved that the cowherd residents of Gokula and the members of the Yadu
dynasty are the eternal associates of Çré Kåñëa, some unintelligent people may think that these
great devotees are simply ordinary human beings like themsleves. They may quote the following
pastimes to prove the ordinariness of these great devotees: 1. The Päëòavas and Yädavas were
wounded by weapons in their fighting pastimes as kñatriyas; 2. the cowherd boys fell unconscious
after drinking the Yamunä's water that had been poisoned by Käliya; and 3. Mahäräja Vasudeva's
asked about the nature of the Absolute Truth and the way to become free from the cycle of birth
and death (Vasudeva asked these questions of Närada Muni at the time of the eclipse at
Kurukñetra). These pastimes of the devotees appear like the activities of ordinary persons, just as
the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself displays pastimes that appear like the activities of an
ordinary living entity.


Text 15


tathä taveyaà viçäma buddhiù ity ädikam, säkñät çré-rukmiëéà prati çré-baladeva-väkye.

   tathä-in the same way; tava iyam viçäma buddhiù-iti ädikam- Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.54.42) the
entire verse is:


taveyaà viñamä buddhiù
   sarva-bhüteñu durhådam
yan manyase sadäbhadraà
   suhådaà bhadram ajïavat

säkñät-directly; çré-rukmiëém prati-to Çré Rukmini-devi; çré-baladeva-of Lord Balarama; väke-in the
statement


   Another example of an eternal associate of Çré Kåñëa acting like an ordinary conditioned soul is
Çré Rukmiëé-devé. who lamented for the distressess suffered by her unworthy brother, Rukmé. Lord
Balaräma rebuked her in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.54.42):

   "My dear Rukmiëé, your affection for your brother Rukmé, who has created enmity with so many
persons is a perverse consideration befitting an ordinary materialistic person. Your brother's
character is not at all adorable, considering his treatment toward other friends, and yet, as an
ordinary woman, you are so affectionate to him. He is not fit to be your brother, and still you are
lenient to him."*

Text 16


yac ca çrémad-uddhavam uddiçya

sa kathaà sevayä tasya
   kälena jarasam gataù

ity uktam, tad api cira-käla-sevä-tätparyakam eva.

   yat-which; ca-also; çrémad-uddhavam-uddhava; uddiçya-in reference to; saù-Uddhava; kastham-
how; sevayä-by such service; tasya-his; kälena-in course of time; jarasam- invalidity; gataù-
undergone; iti-thus; uktam-said; tat-that; api-even; cira-käla-for a long time; sevä-devotional
service; tätparyakam-meaning; eva-certainly.


   Another example of the so-called ordinariness of the Lord's eternal associates is Uddhava, who
appeared to grow old, just as an ordinary conditioned soul. This is described in the following verse
from the Çrémad-Bhägavatam (3.2.3):

   "Uddhava thus served the Lord continually from childhood, and in his old age that attitude of
service never slackened. As soon as he was asked about the message of the Lord, he at once
remembered all about Him."*


Text 17


tatra pravayaso 'py asan
   yuväno 'ti-balaujasaù

iti virodhät.

   tatra-there; pravayasaù-the old men; api-even; asan- became; yuvänaù-youthful; ati-with great;
bala-ojasaù- strength; iti-thus; virofhat-from the contradiction.


   Another example of the so-called ordinary nature of the devotees is the description that the
residents of Mathurä were subject to the afflicton of old-age, just as any ordinary conditioned souls.
This is described in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.45.19):

   "Even the old-men of Mathurä became fully invigorated with youthful energy and strength by
regularly seeing Lord Kåñëa."*


Text 18

   kvacic ca prakaöa-léläyäù prapaïcika-loka-miçratväd yathärtham eva tad-ädikam. yathä
çatadhanva-vadhädau.

   kvacit-sometimes; ca-also; prakaöa-léläyäù-of the manifest pastimes; prapaïcika-loka-with the
material world; miçratvät-because of mixture; yathä-artham-proper; eva- certainly; tat-ädikam-these
examples; yathä-just as; çatadhanva-of Çatadhanva; vadha-of the death; adau-in the beginning.


   Because the manifest pastimes of the Lord and His devotees are displayed within the material
world, it is sometimes proper for these pastimes to appear like those of ordinary persons. An
example of this is Kåñëa's seemingly cruel and vengeful killing os Çatadhanvä, the murderer of the
Lord's father-in-law.


Text 19


  antaräìgänäà bhagavat-sadharaëyaà tu yädavän uddiçyoktam mat-tulya-guëa-çälinaù iti. gopän
uddiçya ca gopaiù samäna-guëa-çéla-vayo-viläsa-veçaiç ca iti; padma-nirmäna-khaëòe ca gopäla
munayaù sarve vaikuëöhänanda-mürtayaù iti.

   antaräìgänäm-of the confidential associates; bhagavat- with the Supreme Personality of
Godhead; sadharaëyam-equality; tu-certainly; yädavän-the members of the Yadu dynasty; uddiçya-
in relation to; uktam-said; mat-to Me; tulya-equal; guëa-sälinaù-in transcendental qualities; iti-thus;
gopän- the cowherd boys; uddiçya-in relation to; ca-also gapaiù- with the cowherd boys; samäna-
equal; guëa-qualities; çéla- character; vbayaù-age; viläsa-pastimes; veçaiù-and appearance; ca-also; iti-
thus; padma-nirmäna-khaëòe-in the Nirmäna-khaëòa of the Padma Purana; ca-also; gopälaù-the
cowherd boys; munayaù-great devotees; sarve-all; vaikuëöha- of the Personality of Godhead; ananda-
bliss; mürtayaù-forms; iti-thus.


   That the confidential associates of the Lord are almost equal to the Lord Himself is confirmed in
the following statements from Vedic literature:

   "Although I am the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the members of the Yadu dynasty possess
transcendental qualities equal to My own."

  "The cowherd boys are equal to Lord Kåñëa Himself in their qualities, character, age, pastimes,
and appearance".

   "All the cowherd boys are great devotees, and they possess transcendental blissful forms, equal to
the spiritual form of Lord Kåñëa Himself."
           -Padma Puräëa, Nirmäna-khaëòa

Text 20


    yato yo vaikuëöhaù çré-bhagavän, sa ivänanda-mürtayas te tatas tat-parama-bhaktatväd eva
muayaù ity ucyate. na tu muny-avatäratväd it jïeyam. naite sureça åçayo na caite ity ädikam çré-
baladeva-väkyaà ca bhagavad-ävirbhäva-lakñaëa-gopädénäm keyaà vä kuta äyätä daivé vä nary
utäsuré ity ädi präptam anyatvam eva niñedhati, na tu pürveñäà ca tad vidadhäti, kalpana-gauraväd
iti jïeyam.

   yataù-from which; yaù-who; vaikuëöhaù-the word "vaikuëöha"; çré-bhagavän-is a name of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; saù-He; iva-just like; ananda-of transcendental bliss; mürtayaù-
forms; te-they; tataù- therefore; tat-parama-bhaktatvät-because of being great devotees of the Lord;
eva-certainly; munayaù-the word "munayaù"; iti-thus; ucyate-is said; na-not; tu-but; muni- of sages;
avatäratvät-as incarnations; iti-thus; jïeyam-it should be undrstood; na-not; ete-these boys; sura-
içaù-the best of the demigods; åçayaù-great sages; na-not; ca-and; ete-these calves; iti-thus; ädikam-
in the passsage beginning; çré-baladeva-of Lord Balarama; väkyam-the statement; ca- also; bhagavat-
of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ävirbhäva-appearance; lakñaëa-characteristic; gopa-adénäm-
of the cowherd boys and calves; ka-who? iyam-this; vä-or; kutaù-from where; äyätä-has come; daivé-
whether demigod; vä-or; nari-woman; uta-or; asuré-demoness; iti- thus; ädi-in the passage beginning;
präptam-attained; anyatvam-another ature; eva-certainly; niçedhati-prohibits; na-not; tu-but;
pürveñäm-of the previous boys and calves; ca-also; tat-that; vidadhäti-places; kalpana-of conception;
gauravät-because of gravity; iti-thus; jïeyam-may be understood.


   In this last quote the word "vaikuëöha" is a name of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and
the compound word "vaikuëöhänanda-mürtayaù" means that the cowherd boys had transcendental
blissful forms, just like the form of Lord Vaikuëöha Himself. The word "munayaù" used in this last
quote means that the cowherd boys are great devotees. It should not be taken to mean that the
cowherd boys are incarnations of various great sages. This is confirmed by the followng statement
of Lord Balaräma (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.13.39):

   "O Supreme Controller! These boys are not great demigods, as I previously thought. Nor are
these calves great sages like Närada. Now I can see that You alone are manifesting Yourself in all
varieties of difference. Although one, You are existing in the different forms of the calves and
boys."*

  When Brahmä had stolen the cowherd bys and calves, Kåñëa manifested Himself as so many boys
and calves to replace His friends who were stolen by Brahmä. Bewildered by this manifestation of
Kåñëa's potency, Balaräma exclaimed:

  "Who is this mystic power, and where has she come from? Is she a demigod or a demoness? She
must be the illusory potency of My master Lord Kåñëa, for who else can bewilder Me?"*

  Someone may say that the cowherd boys, who had been stolen by Brahmä and were sleeping
under the spell of his mystic potency, were great sages and demigods, and it is only the viñëu-tattva

expansions of Kåñëa whom Lord Balaräma is declaring are not sages or demigods. Even though some
may speak in that way, it should be understood that as intimate associates of Lord Kåñëa, the
demigods should be understood to be much more than demigods or sages.


Text 21


yuktaà caiçaà tat-sädåçyam

tasyätma-tantrasya harer adhéçituù
   parasya mäyädhipater mahätmanaù
präyeëa dütä iha vai manoharäç
   caranti tad-rüpa-guëa-svabhäväù

iti çré-yama-väkyädy-anugatatvät.

   tasya-of Him; ätma-tantrasya-being self sufficient, not dependent on any other person; hareù-
the Supreme Personality of Godhead;adhéçituù-who is the master of everything; parasya- the
Transcendence; mäyä-adhipateù-the master of the illusory energy; mahä-ätmanaù-of the Supreme
Soul; präyeëa-almost; dütäù-the order carriers; iha-in this world; vai-indeed; manoharäù-pleasing in
their dealings and bodily features; caranti-they move; tat-of Him; rüpa-possessing the bodily
features; guëa-the transcendental qualitites; sva-bhäväù- and nature; iti-thus; çré-yama-of Yamaraja;
väkya-adi-anugatavät- according to the statement.


  The exalted posititon of the liberated devotees, who have the same qualities and powers as the
Lord Himself is described by Yamaräja (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 6.3.17):

   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead is self-sufficient and fully independent. He is the master
of everyone and everything, including the illusory energy. He has His form, qualities and features;
and similarly His order carriers, the Vaiñëavas, who are very beautiful, possess bodily features,
transcendental qualities and a transcendental nature almost like His. They always wander within
this world with full independence."*


Text 22


dåñöaà ca yathä prathame praviçat puram ity äräbhya

madhu-bhoja-daçärhärha-
   kukurändhaka-våñëibhih
ätma-tulya-balair guptäà ity ädau

dåñöam-observed; ca-also; yathä-in the following way; prathame-in the First Canto of Çrémad-

Bhägavatam; praviçat puram iti äräbhya-in the passage beginning with the words "pravisat puram"
(1.11.11-12); madhu-Madhu; bhoja-Bhoja; daçärha-Daçärha; arha-Arha; kukura-Kukura; andhaka-
Andhaka; våñëibhiù-by the descendants of Våñëi; ätma-tulya-as good as Himself; balaiù-by strength;
guptäm-protected; iti-ädau-in the passage beginning.


   That the associates of the Lord are almost His equals is also described in the following verse of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.11.12):

   "As Bhogavaté, the capital of Nägaloka, is protected by Nägas, so was Dvärakä protected by the
descendants of Våñëi-Bhoja, Madhu, Daçärha, Arha, Kukura, Andhaka, etc.-who were as strong as
Lord Kåñëa,"*


Text 23


ata eva

gopa-jäti-praticchannä
   devä gopäla-rüpiëém
iòére kåñëaà rämaà ca
   naöä iva naöaà nåpa

ity atra sämänyam eva sücitam.

   atah eva-therefore; gopa-of cowherd boys; jäti-in the family; praticchannäù-disguised; deväù-the
demigods; gopäla-rüpiëém-cowherd boys; iòére-glorified with prayers; kåñëam-Lord Kåñëa; rämam-
Lord Balarama; ca-and; natäù-one artist; iva-just like; natam-to another artist; nåpa-O king; iti-
thus; atra-in this verse; sämänyam-equality; eva- certainly; sücitam-is indicated.


   The equality of Lord Kåñëa and His intimate associates is also described in the following verse
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.18.11):

   "The cowherd boys, who were almost equal to Kåñëa, were encouraging Kåñëa in His dancing,
just as one artist encourages another with praise."*


Text 24


   arthaç ca deväù çré-kåñëävaraëe mad-bhakta-püjäbhyadhikä iti nyäyena tadvad evopäsya api
çrédämädayo gopa-jätyä paricchannäù anya-gopa-sämänya-bhävena präyas tädåçatayä lakñayitum
açakyaù. tatra kåñëaà rämaà ca gopäla-rüpiëam iti dåñöäntam. yathä tädåçäv api tau tad-rüpiëau
tathä te 'péty arthaù. atra 'devaù ity anena mahattva sämyam. gopäla-rüpiëam ity anena prakåti-

veça-lélä-sämyam, natä iva naöam ity anena guna-sämyaà cäbhipretam iti.

   arthaù-the meaning; ca-also; deväù-the word "devah"; çré-kåñëa-avaraëe-in the concealment of
Kåñëa; mat-My bhakta-fo the devotees; püja-worship; abhyadhikä-is more important; iti-thus;
nyäyena-by the example; tadvat-in that way; eva-certainly; upäsyaù-worshippable; api-also; çrédäma-
adyaù-Çrédama and the other cowherd boys; gopa- jätyä paricchannäù-the phrase "gopa-jäti-
paricchannäù"; anya-gopa-with the other cowherd boys; sämänya-bhävena-with equality; präyaù-for
the most part; tädåçatayä-like that; lakñayitum-to be characterized; açakyaù-not able; tatra-in that
connection; kåñëam rämam ca gopäla-rüpiëam-the phrase "kåñëam ramam ca gopäla-rüpinam"; iti-
thus; dåñöäntam-is an example; yathä-just as; tädåçäu-like that; api-also; tau-Kåñëa and Balarama; tat-
rüpiëau-with the forms of cowherd boys; tathä-in the same way; te-the many cowherd boys; api-
also; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; atra- in this connection; devaù iti anena-by the word "deva";
mahattva-sämyam-is intended "with the same glory"; gopäla-rupiëm iti anena-by the word "gopäla-
rüpiëam"; prakåti- veça-lélä-sämyam-is meant "with the same nature, appearance, and pastimes";
naöah iva natäm it anena-by the phrase "nata iva natam"; guna-of qualities; sämyam-sameness; ca-
also; abhipretam-is intended; iti-thus.


    In this verse the word "deväù does not mean that Çrédämä and the other cowherd boys were
incarnations of demigods, but rather that they were on the same level as Çré Kåñëa, the Supreme
Lord (deva), and therefore they are also called "deva". That the cowherd boys are as worshipable as
Lord Kåñëa Himself is confirmed by the Lord in the following statement (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
11.19.21):

   "More important than the worship of Me is the worship of My pure devotee."

   Kåñëa and Balaräma were equal to the other cowherd boys, and therefore Kåñëa and Balaräma
were described as "gopäla-rüpiëam". If Kåñëa and Balaräma could be described as cowherd boys
because of Their equality with Their companions, by the same token the cowherd boys may also be
described as "deva" because they are as great as their great friend.Because the cowherd boys are
equal to Kåñëa in nature, qualities, and appearance, they were able to praise Kåñëa's singing and
dancing (naöä iva naöam).


Text 25


tatra yädavädénäà tat-pärñadatvaà yojayati

ahaà yüyam asäv äryä
   ime ca dvärakaukasaù
sarve 'py evaà yadu-çreñöha
   vimågyäù sacaräcaram

   tatra-in this connection; yädava-adénäm-of the Yadavas and other associates of Çré Kåñëa; tat-

pärçadatvam-the state of being His associates; yojayati-He reveals; aham-I; yüyam-you; asäu-
Balarama; äryäù-worshippable; ime-these; ca-also; dväraka-okasaù-residents of Dväraka; sarve-all;
api-even; evam-in this way; yadu-çreñöha-O best of the yadus; vimågyäù-inquired; sa-along with;
cara-moving; acaram-and non-moving entities.


  Lord Kåñëa personally tells Mahäräja Vasudeva that the members of the Yadu dynasty are His
confidential associates in the following verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.85.23):

  "My dear father, everyone, including Myself and My worshipable brother Balaräma, as well as the
inhabitants of the city of Dvärakä, and the whole cosmic manifestation, is exactly as you have
explained. Balaräma and I are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and everything that exists is
the manifestation of Our spiritual and material potencies. You and the members of the Yadu
dynasty are our confidential associates."*


Text 26


  yüyam çrémad-ananakadundubhy ädayaù. vimågyäù paramärtha-rüpatväd anveñaëéyaù. tathänyad
api dvärakoko jäìgama-sthävara-sahitaà yat kiïcit tad anveñyam. aham çré-kåñëaù iti
dåñöäntatvenopanyastam. tataç ca naräkära-brahmaëi sväminn iva tan nitya-parikare sarvatraiva
parama-puruñärthatvam iti bhävaù. tasmäd yathä pürvam sattvaà rajas tamaù ity ädinä sattvädi-
guëänäà tad-våtténäà ca brahmaëi traikälika-sparçäsambhavän mäyayaiva tad-adhyäso bhavatä
varëitas tathä dåñöir atra tu na käryeti tätparyam.

   yüyam-the word "yuyam (you)"; çrémat-anankadundubhi-ädayaù-refers to Mahäräja Vasudeva and
the other members of the Yadu dynasty; vimågyäù-the word "vimågyäù"; parama-artha-rüpatvät
anveñaëéyaù-search for the ultimate goal of life; tatha-in the same way; anyat-another; api-also;
dväraka-okaù-the residents of Dvaraka; jäìgama-sthävara-sahitam-including the moving and non-
moving entities; yat-whatever; kiëcit-there may be; tat-that; anveñyam-may be considered; aham-
the word "aham (I)"; çré-kåñëaù-refers to Çré Kåñëa; iti-thus; dåñöäntatvena-as an example;
upanyastam-spoken; tataù-therefore; ca-also; nara-of a human being; akära-in the form; brahmaëi-
in the Supreme Godhead; svämin-the Lord; iva-just like; tat-nitya-parikare-with His eternal
associates; sarvatra-everywhere; eva-certainly; parama-puruña-arthatvam-the supreme goal of life;
iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning; tasmät-therefore; yathä-just as; pürvam-previously (Bhäg. 10.85.13);
sattvam rajah tamah iti ädinä-by this verse:


sattvaà rajas tama iti
  guëäs tad-våttayaç ca yäù
tvayy addhä brahmaëi pare
  kalpitä yogamäyayä

sattva-adi-beginning with the mode of goodness; guëänäm-of the modes of material nature; tat-

våtténäm-and their activities; ca-also; brahmaëi-in the Supreme Godhead; traikälika-in past present
and future; sparça-contact; asambhavät-because of non-existence; mäyaya-by the illusory potency;
eva-certainly; tat-adhyäsah-controlling that; bhavatä-by You; varëitaù-described; tathä-in that way;
dåñöiù-sight; atra-here; tu-but; na-not; kärya-action; iti-thus; tätparyam-the explanation.

   In this verse the word "yuyam vimågyaù" means "My dear Mahäräja Vasudeva and all members of
the Yadu dynasty. You have all searched for the supreme goal of life with great diligence." Mahäräja
Vasudeva, and all the inhabitants of Dvärakä. (dvärakaukasaù) including all moving and non-
moving living entities (sacaräcaram) have accepted as the supreme goal of life and the dearmost
associate: Lord Kåñëa, the Original Personality of Godhead, whose form is like that of a human
being." Çré Kåñëa was previously described by Mahäräja Vasudeva as the Supreme Lord in the
following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.85.13):

  "My dear Kåñëa, You are the supreme cause of all causes, the eternal principle. Everything is, in
fact, a manifestation of Your one energy. The three qualities of material nature-sattva, rajas and
tamas-and the result of their interaction, are linked up with You by Your agency of yogamäyä. They
are supposed to be independent, but actually the total material energy is resting upon You, the
Supersoul. Since You are the supreme cause of everything, the interactions of material
manifestation-birth, existence, growth, transformation, deterioration and annihilation-are all
absent in Yourself."*

 Because Çré Kåñëa is always (in past, present and future) free from the influence of the three
modes of material nature, His devotees are also free in the same way.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.118
records.text:
Text 1


laukikädhyätma-goñöhé tv evam evety äha dvayena. yathä

ätmä hy ekaù svayaà-jyotir
  nityo 'nyo nirguëo guëaiù
ätma-såñöais tat-kåteñu
  bhüteñu bahudheyate

   laukika-in the material world; adhyätma-the Supersoul; goñöhé-multitude; tu-but; evam-in this
way; iti-thus; äha-he says; dvayena-in two verses; yathä-just as; ätmä-the Supersoul; hi-certainly;
ekaù-is one; svayam-jyotiù-self-effulgence; nityaù-eternal; anyaù-non-material; nirguëaù-beyond
the three modes of material nature; guëaiù-by the three modes of material nature; ätma-by Himself;
såñtaiù-created; tat-by that; kåteñu-created; bhüteñu-in the bodies of the conditioned living entities;
bahudha-in many places simultaneously; iyate-manifest.

  In the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.85.24), Çré Kåñëa describes His expansion as the
Supersoul, present in every atom of the material creation:

   "The Supersoul is one and undivided. He is self-effulgent, eternal, non-material, and beyond the
jurisdiction of the three modes of material nature. He is indeed the original creator of these modes
of nature, from which the material bodies of the conditioned living entities are fashioned.
Appearing simultaneously in many forms, He is manifested in the hearts of these conditioned
souls."*


Text 2


   atränugatärthäntaraà ca dåçyate dvärakäyäm iti prakaraëena labhyate hi yasmät eka evätmä
bhagavattvam ätma-såñöaiù svarüpäd evollasitaiù guëaiù svarüpa-çakti-våtti-viçeñaiù kartåbhiù tat-
kåteñu tasmin svarüpa eva pradurbhäviteñu bhüteñu paramärtha-satyeñu dvärakäntar-vartti-vastuñu
bahudhä tat-tad-rüpeëa éyate prakäçate. sahasra-näma-bhäçye lokanäthaà mahad bhütam ity atra
ca bhütam paramärtha-satyam iti vyäkhyätam. tathä tathä ca prakäçaù svarüpa-
guëaparityägenaivety äha svayaà-jyotiù sva-prakäça eva san, nityaù eva san, anyaù prapaïce
'bhivyakto 'pi tad-vilakñaëa eva san, nirguëaù präkåta-guëa-rahita eva sann iti.

   atra-in this verse; anugata-artha-from the obvious meaning; antaram-another meaning; ca-also;
dåçyate-may be seen; dvärakäyäm iti-prakaraëena-in the passage beginning with the word
"dvärakäyäm"; labhyate-is obtained; hi-certainly; yasmät-from which; ekaù-one; eva-certainly; atmä-
soul; bhagavattvam-the state of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ätma-såñöaiù-created by the
self; svarüpät-means "from His own transcendental form; eva-certainly; ullasitaiù-splendid; guëaiù-
with qualities; svarüpa-of His transcendental form; çakti-of the potencies; våtti-with the activities;
viçeñaiù-specific; kartåbhiù-by the doers; tat-kåteñu-the word "tat-kåteñu"; tasmin-in that; svrüpe-
transcendental form; eva-certainly; pardurbhäviteñu-manifested; bhüteñu-the word "bhüteñu";
parama-artha-the supreme goal of life; satyeñu-the supreme truth; dväraka-Dväraka; antaù-within;
vartti-remaining; vastuñu-substance; bahudhä-the word "bahudha"; tat-tat-rüpeëa-mean "in these
various forms"; éyate-the word "iyate"; prakäçate-means "mnifested"; sahasra-näma-bhä/xye-in the
commentary on the Viñëu-sahasra-nama-stotra; loka-natham-the Lord of the Universe; mahat
bhütam-"the Absolute Truth"; iti atra-in the passage; ca-also; bhütam-the word "bhutam"; parama-
artha-the supreme goal of life; satyam-the supreme truth; iti-thus; vyäkhyätam-explained; tathä
tathä-in various ways; ca-also; prakäçaù-manifestation; svarüpa-of His transcendental form; guëa-
the qualities; aparityägena-without abandoning; eva-certainly; iti-thus; äha-He says; svayam-jyotiù-
the word "svayam-jyotiù";.fn
 2 sva-prakäçaù-which means "appearing by His own will"; eva-certainly; san-being so; nityaù-
eternal; eva-certainly; san-being; anyaù-the word "anyaù"; prapaïce-in the five elements of material
nature; abivyaktaù-manifested; api-although; tat-bilakñaëaù-not material; eva-certainly; san-being;
nirguëaù-the word "nirguëa"; präkåta-material; guëa-qualities; rahitah-without; eva-certainly; san-
being; iti-thus.

  On the surface this verse appears to be a description of Lord Kåñëa's expansion as the all-

pervading Supersoul. However, another interpretation of this verse may also be given: describing
the Lord's appearance in many forms within the city of Dvärakä. According to this second
interpretation, this verse may be translated in the following way:

   "Lord Çré Kåñëa is the eternal Supreme Personality of Godhead, spiritual and beyond the
influence of the three modes of material nature. Displaying His own splendid transcendental
qualities, by His own wish He has simultaneously appeared in many different forms in many
different places within the city of Dvärakä".

   The following synonyms may be given for this verse: "ätma-såñöaiù" means "of His own
transcendental forms"; "guëaiù" means "the splendid qualities reproduced from the potencies of His
transcendental forms"; "tat-kåteñu" means "in those transcendental forms"; "bhüteñu" means "those
forms of the Absolute Truth, who is the Supreme Goal of life and who is manifested in Dvärakä"
(we may note that the commentator on the Viñëu-sahasra-näma-stotra has explained the word
"bhüta" as "the Absolute Truth who is the Supreme Goal of life"); "bahudhä" means "in many forms";
"iyate" means "is manifested"; "svayaà-jyotiù" means "who appears by His own wish," (this word does
not mean that the Lord is without qualities, He retains all the splendid qualities of His own
transcendental form); "nityaù" means "eternal"; "anyaù" means that "although He appears within
this material world, He Himself is purely spiritual, and not a product of material energy"; and
"nirguëaù" means "free from the influence of the three modes of materal nature" or, it may also
mean "without any material qualities."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.119
records.text:
Text 1


   ata cärthäntaraà yathä tarhi kathaà bhavatra atyantikaà samam evätra sarvam ity äçaìkya
tathäpi mayy asti vaiçiñöhyam ity äha

khaà väyur jyotir äpo bhüs
  tat-kåteñu yathäçayam
avistéro 'lpa-bhüry eko
  nänätvaà yäty asäv api

  atra-in this connection; ca-also; artha-meaning; antaram-different; yathä-just as; tatha-then;
katham-how is it; bhavataù-of Your Lordship; atyantikam-great; samam-oneness; eva-certainly; atra-
here; sarvam-all; iti-thus; äçaìkya-doubting; tatha api-nevertheless; mayi-in Me; asti-there is;
vaiçiñöhyam-variety; iti-thus; äha-He said; kham-ether; väyuù-air; jyotiù-fire; äpaù-water; bhüh-
earth; tat-kåteñu-in things constructed of these five elements; yatha-açayam-just as the forms are
manifested; aviù-manifestation; téraù-dissappearance; alpa-smallness; bhüri-plurality; ekaù-one;
nänätvam-the stte of being many; yäti-attains; asäu-He; api-also.

   At this point someone may object: If this unusual interpretation of the verse is to be accepted,
then how should we interpret the next verse, which clearly describes Lord Kåñëa's oneness and
difference from the material elements, and thus supports the first interpretation of the verse. In
this next verse (10.85.23), Çré Kåñëa says:

  "Just as the five material elements, ether, air, fire, water, and earth are manifested in the great
and small material manifestations, and just as these elements are manifested to appear as
homogenous units or complicated varieties, and just as these elements are sometimes visible, and
sometimes their presence is unnoticed, in the same way the all-pervading Supersoul is present in all
the variety of this material world. Sometimes He may be seen, and sometimes He remains invisible."


Text 2


   satkärya-vädäbhyupagamät tasya käraëänanyatväbhyupagamäc ca. yathä khädéni bhütäni tat-
kåteñu tat-svarüpeëaiva vikäçitesu väyv-ädi-ghaöänteñu yathäçayam väyv-ädy-ävirbhävädy-
anurüpam evävirbhävädikaà yänti, na tu teñv adhikam. atra yävän väyur gåhyate, tävän eva
taträkäça-dharmaù çabdo 'péty adikaà jïeyam. tathä svarüpeëaiva vikäçiteñu dvärakä-vastuñu asau
bhagavad-äkhyä ätmäpi. tasmäd ahaà tu tat-tat-sarvamayaù sarvasmät påthak paripürëas cety asti
vaiçiñöyam iti bhävaù. anena dåñöäntena matta evollasita mad-dharma eva te bhavitum arhanti na
tv äkäçe dhuraratvädivän mayi kevala-madhyastha iti ca jïäpitam. atra yathä tatheti vyäkhyänam
api-çabdena dyotyate. çré-bhagavän çré-vasudevam.

   satkärya-väda-proper statement; abhyupagamät-because of accepting; tasya-of Him; käraëa-cause;
ananyatva-without another; abhyupagamät-because of accepting; ca-also; yathä-just as; kha-ether;
adéni-and the other; bhütäni-elements; tat-kåteñu-constructed by Him; tat-svarüpeëa-by His form;
eva-certainly; vikäçitesu-manifest; väyu-air; adi-beginning with; ghaöänteñu-manifesting; yatha-
açayam-just as the forms are manifest; väyu-adi-of air and the other elements; ävirbhäva-
manifestation; adi-beginning with; anurüpam-according to; eva-certainly; avirbhäva-appearance;
adikam-beginning with; yänti-attain; na-not; tu-but; teñu-among them; adhikam-more; atra-here;
yävän-to which extent; väyuh-air; gåhyate-is accepted; tävän-to that extent; eva-certainly; tatra-
there; äkaça-of the ether; dharmaù-nature; çabdaù-sound; api-also; gåhyate-is taken; yävät-to which
extent; jyotih-light; tävät-to that extent; eva-certainly; väyu-of the air; dharmaù-nature; sparçaù-
touch; api-also; iti-thus; adikam-beginning with; jïeyam-sould be understood; tathä-in the same
way; svarüpeëa-by His original form; eva-certainly; vikäñiteçu-manifested; dvärakä-of Dvärakä;
vastuñu-among the contents; asau-He; bhagavat-as the Supreme Personality of Godhead; äkhyäh-
named; ätma-self; api-also; tasmät-therefore; aham-I; tu-but; tat-tat-sarvamayaù-containing
everything; sarvasmät-from everything; påthak-different; paripürëah-perfect and complete; ca-also;
iti-thus; asti-is;.
fn 2 vaiçiñöhyam-difference; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning; anena-by this; dåñöäntena-example;
mattah-from Me; eva-certainly; ullasita-manifest; mat-My; dharmah-nature; eva-certainly; te-they;'
bhavitum-to be; arhanti-are worthy; na-not; tu-but; äkäçe-in the ether; dhusaratva-adivän-as grey;
mayi-in Me; kevala-madhya-sthah-situated in the center; iti-thus; ca-also; jïäpitam-is instructed;

atra-here; yathä-just as; tatha-in the same way; iti-thus; vyäkhyänam-explanation; api-çabdena-by
the word "api"; dyotyate-is manifest; çré-bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; çré
vasudevam-to Mahäräja Vasudeva.

   This verse should be interpreted in the following way: "The elements are manifested one from
another. For example, at first ether is manifested, and from ether, air is manifested. From air fire is
manifested, and so forth. By nature, ether carries sound, and therefore air and all the other
elements can also carry sound, for they are manifested from ether. In the same way the nature of
fire is to contain the sensation of touch. All the elements manifested from fire (water and earth)
can carry the sensation of touch. In the same way, whatever is present within the city of Dvärakä is
manifested from the Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, and therefore He is present everywhere in that
city, just as sound is naturally present in all the elements manifested from ether, or touch is present
in the elements manifested from fire."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.120
records.text:
Text 1


ata eväha

tad-darçana-sparçanänupatha-prajalpa-
  çayyäsanäçana-çayauna-sapiëòa-bandhaù
yeñäà gåhe niraya-vartmani vartataà vaù
  svargäpavarga-viramaù svayam äsa viñëuù

   atah eva-therefore; aha-He says; tat-of Lord Kåñëa; darçana-sight; sparçana-touch; anupatha-
travelling on the same path; prajalpa-talking; çayya-on the bed; asana-on the sitting place; açana-
taking meals; çayauna-by matrimonial relationship; sapiëòa-and by blood relationship; bandhaù-
relation; yeñäm-of whom; gåhe-in the home; niraya-to hell; vartmani-on the road; vaù-you; svarga-
elevation to the upper planetary system; apavarga-and liberation; viramaù-stopping; svayam-
personally; äsa-is; viñëuù-Lord Viñëu.

  The exalted position of the members of the Yadu dynasty, who associated with Lord Kåñëa as
equals, is described in the following statement spoken by an assembly of Kings to Mahäräja
Ugrasena (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.30):

   "Your majesty, King of the Bhojas, you are related with the Yadu dynasty by matrimonial
relationship and by blood relationship also. As a result You are constantly in touch with Lord
Kåñëa, and You have no difficulty in seeing Him at any time. Lord Kåñëa moves with You, talks
with you, sits with you, rests with you, and dines with you. The Yadus appear to be always engaged
in wordly affairs, which are considered to lead to the royal road to hell, but due to the presence of
Lord Kåñëa, the Original Personality of Godhead in the Viñëu category, who is omniscient,

omnipresent, and omnipotent, all of You are factually relieved from all material contamination,
and are situated in the transcendental position of liberation and Brahman existence."*


Text 2


   yeñäà väù yuñmäkaà våñëénäm gåhe viñëuù çré-kåñëäkhyo bhagavän svayam ätmanä svabhävatä
eva äsa niväsaà cakre, na tv anyena hetunety arthaù. kathaà-bhüte aniraya-vartmani nirayaù
saàsäras tad-vartma prapaïcaù, tato 'nyasmin prapaïcätéta ity arthaù.

   yeñäm väù-the words "yesam vah"; yuñmäkam-mean "of you"; våñëénäm-members of the Våñëi
dynasty; gåhe-in the home; viñëuù-Lord Viñëu; çré-kåñëa-Çré Kåñëa; akhyah-with the name;
bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; svayam-the word "svayam"; ätmanä-means
"personally"; svabhävatäh-by His own nature; eva-certain; äsa-the word "asa"; niväsam cakre-means
"resided"; na-not; tu-but; anyena-otherwise; hetuna-by another cause; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning;
katham-bhüte-what is your home like?; aniraya-vartmani-it is described by the word "aniraya-
vartmani"; nirayaù-the word "niraya"; saàsärah-means "material existence"; tat-vartma-that path;
prapaïcaù-is the material world; tatah-from that; anyasmin-in another place; prapaïca-material
existence; atétah-beyond; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.

   In this verse the words "yeñäà vaù" mean "of you members of the Våñëi dynasty"; "viñëuù" means
"the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kåñëa"; "svayam" means "personally"; "äsa" means
"resides". The homes of the members of the Yadu dynasty are described by the word "aniraya-
vartmani" which means "beyond the sphere of material existence."


Text 3


  kédåçénäm. väù tasminn eva vartamänänäà svayaà kathaà-bhütaù. svargäpavarga-viramaù
svargasyäpavargasya ca viramo yena. yo nija-bhaktebhyas tad-bahirmukhatä-karaù svargaà na
dadäti, tad-bhakty-udäsénaà kevalaà mokñaà ca na dadäti, kintu tän sva-caraëäravinda-tula eva
rakñatéty arthaù.

   kédåçénäm-what were they like?; väù-you; tasmin-in that; eva-certainly; vartamänänäm-at
present; svayam-personally; katham-bhütaù-what is He like?; svarga-apavarga-viramaù-He is
described by the word "svargäpavarga-viramaù"; svargasya-of elevation to the upper material
planetary system; apavargasya-of impersonal liberation; ca-also; viramah-the cause of cessation;
yena-by whom; yah-who; nija-bhaktebhyah-to His own devotees; tat-bahirmukhatä-karaà-which
makes one averse to devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; svargam-elevation
to the upper material planets; na-does not; dadäti-give; tat-His; bhakti-devotional service; udäsénam-
without reference; kevalam-monistic; mokñam-liberation; ca-also; not; does not; dadäti-give; kintu-
but; tän-them; sva-caraëa-aravinda-tale-under His lotus feet; eva-certainly; rakñati-gives protection;
iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.

  How is Lord Kåñëa described in this verse? He is described by the word "svargäpavarga-virama",
which means that He does not give to His devotees either elevation to the higher material planets,
or impersonal liberation. Residence in the higher material planets makes one uninterested in
spiritual life, or Kåñëa consciousness, and impersonal liberation removes one from the sphere of
loving devotional service to Lord Kåñëa. For this reason these inferior benedictions are not given
by the Lord. Instead He gives to His devotees shelter under the protection of His own lotus feet.


Text 4


   yeñäm yuñmäkaà tu gåhe sa evaà-bhüta eva äsa ity aha tad-darçana iti. tasya yuñmat-kaåtrkaà
darçanaà ca anupathaù anugatiç ca, prajalpaù goñöhé ca, tathä yuñmat-samvalita çayyä çayanaà ca
äçanam ca äçanam bhojanaà ca tair viñiñöaiç cäsau çäyäuna-sapinda-bandhaù ceti çaka-pärthivädi-
van madhya-pada-lopé karmädhärayaù. tatra våñëébhiù saha yauna-bandho viväha-sambandhaù,
sapinda-bandho daihika-sambandhas täbhyäà saha vartamäne 'säv iti bahuvréhi-garbhatä. räjänaù
çrémad-ugrasenam.

   yeñäm-the word "yeñäm; yuñmäkam-means "of you; tu-certainly; gåhe-in the home; sah-He; evam-
bhüte-described in this way; eva-certainly; äsa-resides; iti-thus; aha-he says; tat-darçanaù iti-the
phrase beginning with the word "tad-darsana"; tasya-of Him; yuñmat-of You; kaåtåtvam-the doer;
darçanam-the sight; ca-also; anupathaù-the word "anupathah"; anugatih-means "following the
patha"; ca-also; prajalpaù-the word "prajalpah"; goñöhé-means "conversation; ca-also; tathä-in that
way; yuñmat-with You; samvalita-associated; çayyä-the word "çayyä"; çayanam-means "bed"; äçanam-
seat; ca-also; äçanam-the word "äçanam"; bhojanam-means "meals"; ca-also; taih-with them; viçiñöaih-
specifically; ca-also; asau-He; çäyäuna-sapinda-bandhaù-this word; ca-also; iti-thus; çaka-pärthivädi-
vat-consisting of royalty; madhya-pada-lopé-where the middle word is omitted; karmädhärayaù-
Karmädhäraya-samasa; tatra-there; våñëibhiù saha-with the members of the Våñëi dynasty; yauna-
bandhah-the word "yauna-bandha"; viväha-sambandhaù-means marriage ties"; sapinda-bandhah-the
word "sapinda-bandha"; daihika-sambandhah-means "blood relationship"; täbhyäm-both of them;
saha-along with; vartamänah-at present; asau-He; iti-thus; bahuvréhi-garbhatä-Bahuvréhi-samasa;
räjänaù-the kings; çrémat-ugrasenam-to Maharaja Ugrasena.

   Lord Kåñëa resides in the same house with the members of the Yadu dynasty. They have no
difficulty in seeing Him (tad-darçanam). They move with Him (anupatha) talk with Him (prajalpa),
rest with Him (çayyä), sit with Him (äsana), and dine with Him (açana). They are related with Him
by matrimonial relationship (sayauna), and by blood relationship (sapiëòa-bandhaù). In this
sentence we may note the use of madhya-pada-lopé-samäsa, and bahuvréhi-samäsa.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.121
records.text:
kià ca

saìkhyähäà yädavänäà kaù
  kariñyati mahätmanäm
yaträyutänäm ayuta-
  lakñeëäste sa ähukaù

  ähukaù ugrasenaù. yaträste iti vartamäna-prayogena taträpi sadä iti nityatä-väcakavyäyena teñäà
nitya-pärñadatvaà su-vyaktam. çré-çukaù.

   kim ca-furthermore; saìkhyänäm-enumeration; yädavänäm-of the members of the Yadu dynasty;
kaù-who?; kariñyati-will be able to do; maha-atmanäm-of the great devotees; yatra-where; ayutänäm
ayuta-lakñaëa-with millions of millions of personal attendants and bodyguards; aste-remains; sah-
he; ahukah-Maharaja Ugrasena; ähukaù-the word "ähukaù"; ugrasenaù-means "Maharaja
Ugrasena"; yatra-where; aste-he remains; iti-thus; vartamäna-prayogena-by the use of the present-
tense; tatra-there; api-also; sadä-eternally; iti-thus; nityatä-eternality; väcaka-by the word; avyäyena-
without fail; teñäm-of them; nitya-pärñadatvam-the status of eternal associates; su-vyaktam-is
clearly manifested; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çré Çukadeva Gosvami.

   That the members of the Yadu dynasty are eternal associates of Lord Kåñëa is confirmed in the
following statement of Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.42) where the use of the
present tense ("äste") indicates "eternally".

  "Who will be able to count the great souls who are members of the Yadu dynasty. There numbers
are certainly beyond counting. Eternally remaining among them, King Ugrasena alone has ten
quadrillion soldiers as personal bodyguards."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.122
records.text:
atas teñäà çré-bhagavat-pärñadatve yogyatäm avyabhicaritvam api dåñöäntena spañöayati

tatropaviñöaù paramäsane vibhur
  babhau sva-bhäsä kakubho 'vabhäsayan
våto nå-siàhair yadubhir yadüttamo
  yathoòu-räjo divi tärakä-gaëaiù

  spañöam. evam eva duryodhanaà prati svayaà viçva-rüpaà darçayatä çré-bhagavatä teñäà
yädavädénäà nijävaraëa-rüpatvaà darçitam ity udyama-parvaëi prasiddhiù. çré-çukaù.

  atah-from this; teñäm-of them; çré-bhagavat-pärñadatve-as eternal associates of the Supreme Lord;
yogyatäm-appropriateness; avyabhicaritvam-eternality; api-also; dåñöäntena-by an example;
spañöayati-is clearly described; tatra-in the Sudharam assembly house; upaviñöaù-entered; parama-
asane-on the royal throne; vibhuh-the omnipotent Lord; babhau-shone; sva-bhäsä-by His own
splendor; kakubhah-all directions; avabhäsayan-illuminating; våtah-surrounded; nå-siàhaih-by the

great heros; yadubhih-the members of the Yadu dynasty; yadu-üttamah-the best of the Yadu
dynasty; yatha-just like; uòu-räjah-the moon; divi-in the sky; tärakä-gaëaiù-with the stars; spañöam-
the meaning is clear; evam-in the same way; eva-certainly; duryodhanam prati-to Duryodhana;
svayam-own; viçva-rüpam-Universal Form; darçayatä-revealing; çré-bhagavatä-by the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; teñäm-of them; yädava-adénäm-the Yadavas and the other associates of the
Lord; nija-own; avaraëa-covering; rüpatvam-consisting of; darçitam-revealed; it-thus; udyama-
parvaëi-in the Udyama-parva; prasiddhiù-fame; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çré Sukadeva Gosvami.

  That the members of the Yadu dynasty are eternal associates of Lord Kåñëa is also described in
the following simile spoken by Çukadeva Gosvämé in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.70.18):

  "After entering the Sudharmä assembly house, Lord Kåñëa used to sit on the exalted royal throne
and would be seen to emenate glaring rays of transcendental effulgence. In the midst of all the great
heros of the Yadu dynasty, Kåñëa resembled the full moon in the sky, surrounded by multi-
luminaries."*

  The eternal relationship between Lord Kåñëa and the Yädavas may also be seen by
(Mahäbhärata, Udyama-parva) Lord Kåñëa's revelation of His Universal Form to Duryodhana in
order to protect the Yädavas and Päëòavas.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.123
records.text:
Text 1


  yaiç caiñam ekädaça-skandhänte tad-anyathä-bhävaù çrüyate, sa tu çrémad-arjuna-paräjaya-
vimoha-paryanto mäyika eva. tathä-vacanaà ca brahma-çäpänivarttya-täthyäpanayaiva go-
brähmaëa-hitävataréëa bhagavatä vihitam iti jïeyam. dåçyate ca båhad-agni-puräëädau rävaëa-
kåtäyäù sétäyä mäyikatvaà yathä tädvat. tathä hi tadäném eväha

  yaiù-by whom; ca-also; eñam-of them; ekädaça-skandha-ante-at the end of the Eleventh Canto of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam; tat-anyathä-bhävaù-a different condition of life; çrüyate-is heard; sah-He; tu-
but; çrémat-arjuna-of Arjuna; paräjaya-defeat; vimoha-the bewilderment; paryantah-up until;
mäyikah-illusory; eva-certainly; tathä-in that way; vacanam-statement; ca-also; brahma-by the
Brähmaëas; çapa-cursing; anivarttya-unavoidable; täthyäpanaya-for the appropriateness; eva-
certainly; go-of the cows; brähmaëa-and the Brähmaëas; hita-for the welfare; avatariëa-descended;
bhagavatä-by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; vihitam-accomplished; iti-thus; jïeyam-it may
be understood; dåçyate-may be seen; ca-also; båhat-agni-puräëa-adau-in the Agni Puraëa and other
Vedic literatures; rävaëa-for Ravana; kåtäyäù-fashioned; sétäyäh-of Séta; mäyikatvam-illusory
nature; yathä-just as; tädvat-in the same way; tathä-in the same way; hi-certainly; tadäném-at that
time; eva-certainly; aha-He said.

  Someone may object, saying that according to the description in the Eleventh Canto of Çrémad-

Bhägavatam Arjuna was defeated by a band of infidel cowherdsmen, and the Yadu dynasty became
cursed by a brähmaëa and in an intoxicated condition killed themselves in a fratricidal war. Our
objector will protest that these are not actions befitting eternal associates of the Lord.
  To this objection I reply that Lord Kåñëa, who descended to this world for the benefit of the cows
and brähmaëas was unwilling to let the brähmaëa's curse go in vain, and therefore the Yadus were
destroyed in a fratricidal war. Actually, even more important than that is the nature of the Lord's
pastimes, where illusory things are sometimes acted out by the Lord's internal potency. This magical
jugglery of the Lord may be seen in many pastimes. For example: when Rävaëa attempted to steal
Sétä-devé, Lord Rämacandra created a false-Sétä-devé by His mystic potency. The illusory Sétä was
captured by Rävaëa, while the actual Sétä was never taken by the demon. The defeat of Arjuna and
the annihilation of the Yadu dynasty are similar magical feats performed by the Lord. This is
specifically described by Lord Kåñëa Himself in the following statement spoken by Him to His
chariot-driver Daruka (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.30.49):


Text 2


tvaà tu mad-dharmam ästhäya
  jïäya-niñöhä upekñakaù
man-mäyä-racitam etaà
  vijïäyopaçamaà vraja

  tvam-you; tu-certainly; mat-My; dharmam-pure devotional service; ästhäya-asking shelter of;
jïäna-niñöhäù-absorbed in transcendental knowledge; upekñakaù-patient; mat-My; mäyä-illusory
potency; recitam-fabricated; etam-these calamities; vijïäya-understanding this; upaçamam-
peacefulness; vraja-please attain.

   "My dear Daruka, do not be unhappy because of the destruction of the Yadu dynasty or the
dissapearance of Lord Balaräma. Become patient and fixed in actual knowledge. These calamities
are simply an illusory show fabricated by My internal potency. There is no need to become agitated
because of these so-called catastrophies."


Text 3


  tvaà tu darukaù jïäna-niñöhaù madéya-lélä-tattva-jïaù. mad-dharmam mama sva-bhakta-
pratipälayitåtva-rüpaà svatulya-parikara-saìgitva-rüpaà ca sva-bhävam ästhäya viçrabhya etam
adhunä prakäçitaà sarvam eva mauñalädi-léläà mama indrajälavad racitam vijïäya upekñakaù bahir-
dåñöyä jätaà çokam upekñamänaù upaçamam citta-kñobhäh nivåttim vraja präpnuhi. tu-çabdenänye
tävan muhyantu, tava tu tathä moho na yukte eveti dhvanitam. atra çré-darukasya svayaà
vaikuëöhävatérëatvena siddhatvät etam ity aträtisannihitärtha-läbhäc cänyathä-vyäkhyänam eva
prathama-pratétya-viñaya iti vivektavyam. çré-bhagavän darukam.

   tvam tu-the words "tvam tu; darukaù-refer to Daruka; jïäna-niñöhaù-the word "jïäna-niñöhaù;
madéya-lélä-tattva-jïäù-means "understanding the truth about My transcendental pastimes"; mat-
dharmam-the word "mad-dharmam"; sva-bhakta-partipalayitåtva-rüpam-means "My natural
tendency to protect My devotees; svatulya-parikara-saìgitva-rüpam-"like you"; ca-also; sva-bhävam-
My nature; ästhäya-the word "asthaya"; viçrabhya-means "have faith"; etam-this; adhunä-at this
time; prakäçitam-is manifested; sarvam-everything; eva-certainly; mauñala-adi-léläm-destruction of
the Yadu dynasty and other catastrophies; mama-My; indrajälavat-like a magical performance;
racitam-fabricated; vijïäya-understanding this; upekñakaù-become aloof; bahih-by superficial;
dåñöyä-understanding; jätam-is produced; çokam-grief; upekñamänaù-be aloof; upaçamam-the word
"upasamam"; citta-of the mind; kñobhät-from agitation; nirvåttim-cessation; vraja-the word "vraja";
präpnuhi-means "you should attain"; tu-çabdena-by the word "tu"; anye-others; ävat-in that way;
muhyantu-may become bewildered; tava-of you; tu-but; tathä-in that way; mohah-illusion; na-not;
yuktah-is appropriate; eva-certainly; iti-thus; dhvenitam-it is spoken; atra-here; çré-darukasya-of
Daruka; svayam-personally; vaikuntha-from Vaikuntha; avatirnatvena-the state of having
descended; siddhatvat-because of perfection; etam-this; iti-thus; atra-here; ati-sannihita-fixed; artha-
meaning; läbhät-because of attainment; ca-also; anyathä-other; vyäkhyänam-explanation; eva-
certainly; prathama-first;
 pratétya-viñaya-in the area of what should be accepted; vivektavyam-should be considered; çré-
bhagavän-spoken by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; darukam-to Daruka.

  In this verse the words "tvaà tu" refer to Daruka; "jïäna-niñöhaù" means "understanding the
truth about My transcendental pastimes"; "mad-dharmam" means "My natural inclination to protect
My devotees, such as yourself"; and "ästhäya" means "having faith". Kåñëa tells Daruka that the
present calamities, such as the destruction of the Yadu dynasty are like magical tricks performed by
Him. Daruka should understand all this (vijïäya) and become free (upaçamaà vraja) from grief and
agitation of the mind, which is produced by superficial understanding. By the word "tu" (but), Çré
Kåñëa tells Daruka:

   "Others may become bewildered by these pastimes of Mine, but you should not."

  Daruka, a perfectly liberated devotee who had descended with the Lord from Vaikuëöha
understood this statement of the Lord. This is the proper explanation of the Lord's final pastimes
and the destruction of the Yadu dynasty.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.124
records.text:
Text 1


tathä ca padya-trayam

räjan parasya tanu-bhåj-jananäpyayehä
   mäyä-viòambanam avehi yathä naöasya

såñövätmanedam anuviçya vihåtya cänte
   saàhåtya cätma-mahimoparataù sa äste

   tatha-in the same way; ca-also; pada-trayam-three verses; räjan-O king; parasya-of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; tanu-bhåt-with the Yadavas and His other associates; janana-appearance;
apyaya-dissapearance; ihäh-activities; mäyä-viòambanam-an illusory show; avehi-please understand;
yathä-just as; naöasya-of an actor; såñöva-having created; atmana-by His own potency; idam-this
world; anuviçya-having entered it; vihåtya-performing pastimes; ca-also; ante-at the time of
dissolution; saàhåtya-destroying it; ca-also; atma-mahima-by His own glory; uparataù-peaceful and
aloof; sah-He; äste-remains.

   The transcendental nature of the appearance and dissapearance of Lord Çré Kåñëa and His
confidential associates is described in three verses from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.31.11-13). In the
first of these verses (11), Çukadeva Gosvämé says to Mahäräja Parékñit:

   "O king, please try to understand that the appearance of Çré Kåñëa and His confidential
associates (who have spiritual forms just like that of the Lord), their pastimes, and their
dissappearance from this earth are like a dramatic play enacted by Lord Kåñëa's internal potency.
Çré Kåñëa is not an ordinary living entity, but in truth He is the Supreme Person who has created
this entire material world, who entered into every atom of that creation as the all-pervading
Supersoul, and who will destroy the entire universe at the time of annihilation. He is the Supreme
Lord, who sometimes comes to this material world to display His pastimes here, although He always
remains free from the influence of the material energy, and situated in His own transcendental
glory."***


Text 2


   parasya çré-kåñëasya ye tanu-bhåtaù prayujyamäne mayi täà çuddhäà bhägavatéà tanum iti çré-
näradokty-anusäreëa tadéyäà tanum eva dhärayantas tat-pärñadä yädavädayas teñäm jananäpyaya-
rüpa éhä ceñöäù kevalaà parasyaiva mäyayä viòambanam anukaraëam avehi. yathendrajäla vettä
nataù kaçcij jévata eva märayitveva dagdhveva punaç ca tad dehaà janayitveva darçayati tasyeva.
viçva-sargädi-hetv-acintya-çaktas tasya tädåça-çaktitvaà na ca citram ity äha viçva iti.

   parasya-the word "parasya"; çré-kåñëasya-means "of Çré Kåñëa"; ye-which; tanu-bhåtaù-with forms;
prayujyamäne-engaged; mayi-Me; täm-this; çuddhäm-pure; bhagavatém-of the Lord; tanum-form; iti-
thus; çré-närada-of Närada Muni (Bhägavatam 1.6.29); ukti-statement; anusäreëa-in accordance
with; tadéyäm-his; tanum-body; eva-certainly; dhärayantah-manifesting; tat-pärñadäh-the associates
of the Lord; yädava-adayah-the Yädavas and others; teñäm-of them; janana-birth; apyaya-
dissappearance; rüpah-consisting of; éhäh-the word "éhäh"; ceñöäù-means "activities"; kevalam-
exclusively; parasya-of the Supreme Lord; eva-certainly; mäyayä-by the illusory potency;
viòambanam-the word "viòambanam"; anukaraëam-imitation; avehi-please understand; yatha-just
as; indrajälavattäh-expert in magical tricks; nataù-actors; kaçcit-some; jévate-live; eva-certainly;
märayitva-after killing; iva-just as; dagdhva-having burned; iva-just as; punah-again; ca-also; tat-

that; deham-body; janayativa-having re-created; iva-just as; darsayati-reeal; tasya-his; iva-just as;
ivçva-of the material universe; sarga-creation; adi-beginning with; hetu-cause; acintya-
inconveivable; çakteh-of the potency; tasya-His; tädåsa-of the same nature; çaktitvam-potency; na-
not; ca-and; citram-astonishing; iti-thus; äha-He says; srstva iti-the passage beginning with the word
"srstva".

  In this verse the word "parasya" (of the Supreme) refers to Çré Kåñëa. The word "tanu-bhåt" means
"with spiritual forms". Both the Lord and His liberated devotees have spiritual forms. This is
confirmed by Närada Muni (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.6.29) in the following words:

  "Having been awarded a transcendental body befitting an associate of the Personality of
Godhead, I quit the body made of five material elements, and thus all acquired fruitive results of
work [karma] stopped."*

    For this reason the words "janana" (appearance) "apyaya" (dissappearance), and "éhä" (activities)
refer not only to the Lord but also to the Yädavas and other devotees who were the Lord's intimate
associates. Çukadeva Gosvämé says in this verse "mäyä-viòambanam avehi" (Please understand that
the activities, dissappearance, and appearance of both the Lord and His intimate associates appear
superficially to be under the jurisdiction of the illusory potency mäyä, although actually they are
not so). Just as a magician may make a show of burning Himself in a fire, and then re-appear again,
alive and unburned before His audience, in the same way Lord Kåñëa makes a magical show of His
own dissappearance and the dissappearance of His associates.
   That the Lord has such inconceivable potency to do wonderful things is confirmed in the second
part of this verse where it is said that Çré Kåñëa creates and annihilates the entire material universe.
If by His potency the Lord can create and destroy the universe, then it is not at all astonishing that
He can make a magical show of His devotees' and His own dissappearance.


Text 3


   evaà sati saìkarñaëädau mugdhänäm anyathäbhän ahetudäharaëäbhäsaù sutaräm eva mäyika-
lélä-varëane praveçito bhavati. skande çré-lakñmaëasyäpy anyadåçatvaà na sampratépannam.
näräyaëa-varmaëi ca çeñäd vilakñaëa-çaktitvena nityam evopäsaka-pälakatvena tathaivänumatam
iti darçitam.

   evam-in the same way; sati-being so; sahkarsana-adau-Lord Sankarsana and His expansions;
mugdhanam-of the bewildered conditioned souls; anyatha-abhan-appearing otherwise; ahetu-
without cause; udaharana-narration; abhasah-appearance; sutaram-greatly; eva-certainly; mayika-in
the realm of the material energy; lélä-pastimes; varnane-in the description; pravesitah-entered;
bhavati-is; skande-in the Skanda Purana; sri-laksmanasya-of Laksmana; api-also; anyadrsatvam-
another nature; na-not; sampratipannam-considered; narayana-varmani-in the Narayana-varma; ca-
also; sesat-from Ananta Sesa; vilaksana-extraordinary; saktitvana-with potencies; nityam-eternally;
eva-certainly; upasaka-of the devotees; palakatvena-as the protector; tatha-in the same way; eva-
certainly; anumatam-considered; iti-thus; darsitam-demonstrated.

   In the eyes of the foolish conditioned souls, the appearance, activities, and disappearance of Lord
Balaräma may appear to be material, just as those of a conditioned soul, although of course, His
activities and disappearance are transcendental, just as those of Çré Kåñëa. In the Skanda Puräëa we
find the description of the extraordinary disappearance of Lord Balaräma's expansion, Lakñmaëa.
Lord Balaräma's disappearance is similar to that of Lakñmaëa. The eternal position of Lord
Balaräma's expansion Ananta Çeña, His extraordinary potencies and His natural inclination to
protect His devotees are all described in the scripture known as the Näräyaëa-varma.


Text 4


   ata eva jaräsandha-väkye tava räma yadi çraddhä ity atra çré-svämibhir apétthaà västavärtho
vyaïcjitaù acchedyo deho 'säv iti svayam eva matvä aparitoñät pakñäntaram äha yad vä 'mäà jahi'
iti.

  atah eva-therefore; jaräsandha-of Jaräsandha; väkye-in the statement; tavat räma yadi çraddhä-
Bhägavatam 10.50.18:


tava räma yadi çraddhä
  yuddhasva sthairyam udvaha
hitvä vä mac-charaiç chinnaà
  deham svär yähi mäà jahi

iti-thus; atra-in this verse; çré-svämibhih-by Çrédhara Svami; api-also; ittham-in this way; västava-
actual; arthah-meaning; vyaïjitaù-is revealed; acchedyah-not able to be cut; dehah-body; asau-this;
iti-thus; svayam-directly; eva-certainly; matvä-having considered; aparitoñät-because of displeasure;
pakña-antaram-the alternative; äha-he said; yadvä-or else; mäm-me; jahi-defeat; iti-thus.

  Even when the demon Jaräsandha attempted to defame Lord Balaräma with many insults, all his
insults may be interpreted as praises. For example, Jaräsandha said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.50.18):

  "You Balaräma! If you like You can fight along with Kåñëa, and if You have patience, then You
can wait to be killed by my arrows. Thus you can be promoted to heaven. Come! Fight with me, and
defeat me if You can."*

   Çrédhara Svämé, in his commentary on this verse has explained the actual import of this
statement of Jaräsandha:

  "Lord Balaräma's body is spiritual, and thus cannot be cut by Jaräsandha's arrows or any other
weapon. Therefore the only possible outcome of Jaräsandha's fight with Lord Balaräma is explained
by the words "mäà jahi" (Balaräma will defeat Jaräsandha).

Text 5


  tad evaà cänena vyäkhyänena lokäbhirämam ity ädi padyeñu yogi-jana-çakti-vilakñaëa-bhagavac-
chakti-vyaïjakaà çré-svämi-caraëänäm adagdhvä ity ädi pada-cchedädi-mäyä-vyäkhya-sauñöhavaà
kaimutyätiçayena suñöhv eva sthäpitam. yata eva dåçyate cädyapy upaçäkänäm ity ädikam ca tad
uktaà susaìgataà bhavati; tat-tat-parikareëaiva särdhaà teñäà tat säkñät-kära iti.

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; ca-also; anena-by this; vyäkhy/ena-explanation; loka-abhiramam
iti ädi padyeñu-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.31.5:


lokäbhirämaà sva-tanuà
  dharaëä-dhyäna-maìgalam
yoga-dharaëayägneyyä
  dagdhvä dhämäviçat svakam

yogi-jana-of the mystic yogis; çakti-potency; vilakñaëa-extraordinary; bhagavat-of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; sakti-potency; vyaïjakam-manifesting; çré-svämi-caraëänäm-of Çrédhara
Svami; adagdhvä iti ädi-the word "adagdhvä"; pada-of the word; cheda-dicision; adi-beginning with;
mäyä-consisting of; sauñöhavam-superiority; kaimutya-atiçayena-with great superiority; suñöha-
properly; eva-certainly; sthäpitam-is established; yatah-because; eva-certainly; dåçyate-is observed;
ca-also; adya-now; api-even; upaçäkänäm-of the devotees; iti-thus; ädikam-beginning; ca-also; tat-
that; uktam-said; susaìgatam-in agreement; bhavati-is; tat-tat-parikareëa-various associates; eva-
certainly; särdham-with; teñäm-of them; tat-therefore; säkñät-kärah-appearance; iti-thus.

   In his comment on Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.31.5 Çrédhara Svämé explains that the phrase
"adagdhvä dhämäviçat" means that Lord Kåñëa left the material world and entered the spiritual
world in His same transcendental body. In other words, He did not change His body. The same is
also true for the Lord's associates. They accompany Çré Kåñëa to the material world and eventually
they return to the spiritual world without changing their bodies. In other words, the associates of
the Lord never had material bodies, but they appeared in this world in their eternal spiritual forms,
just as Çré Kåñëa Himself does.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.125
records.text:
Text 1


  apräkåta-dehänäà teñäà tän na sambhavatéty astam, çré-kåñëa-pälyatvenaiva na sambhavatéty
äha

martyena yo guru-sutaà yamaloka-nétaà
 tvaà cänayac charaëadaù paramästra-dagdham

jigye 'ntakäntakam apéçam asäv anéçaù
   kià svavane svar anayaë mågayuà sadeham

  apräkåta-not material; dehänäm-of forms; teñäm-of them; tät-therefore; na-not; sambhavati-is
possible; astam-may be; çré-kåñëa-by Çré Kåñëa; pälyatvena-because of being protected; eva-certainly;
na-not; sambhavati-is possible; äha-he says; martyena-in the same body; yah-who; guru-of His
teacher, Sandipani Muni; sutam-the son; yama-lokam-to the planet of Yamaraja; nétam-brought;
tam-You (Maharaja Parikñit); ca-also; anayat-protected; saraëadaù-the protector of the surrendered
souls; parama-astra-by the Brahmastra weapon; dagdham-burned; jigye-conquered; antaka-antakam-
the conqueror of death; api-even; içam-Lord Çiva; açau-He; anéçaù-completely independent; kim-
how is it? sva-avane-in the protection of His devotees; sväh-to the spiritual world; anayat-brought;
mågayum-the hunter; sa-deham-in the same body.

   The bodies of Lord Kåñëa's associates are not material. Because such great devotees are always
protected by Çré Kåñëa, they do not die in the same way conditioned souls die, but rather they
return to the spiritual world in their spiritual forms, for they had never accepted material bodies in
the first place. That the Lord's associates return to the spiritual world without having to change
bodies is confirmed by the following statement of Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
11.31.12):

  "My dear Mahäräja Parékñit, please know that Çré Kåñëa is always the protector of the surrendered
souls. He protected you, when as an unborn child you were burned by the brahmästra weapon, and
He delivered the son of His teacher from the planet of Yamaräja. His teacher's son did not even
change his body, but the Lord brought him before his parents in the very same body in which he
had first appeared before them. Lord Kåñëa defeated Çiva, who is victorious even over death
himself, and He brought to Vaikuëöha the hunter who shot Him in the heel with an arrow. This
hunter also did not change his body, but entered Vaikuëöha in the very same body. How is it
possible for this omnipotent Lord Kåñëa to be weak and unable to protect Himself? It is not at all
possible."***


Text 2


   yaù çré-kåñëaù yama-lokam gatam api guru-sutam guror jätena païcanjana-bhakñitena tena
martyena dehanaiva anayat, na ca brahma-tejaso balavattvaà mantavyam. tvaà ca brahmästra-
dagdhaà yas tasmäd brahmästräd anayad rakñitavän ity arthaù. kim anyad vaktavyam, yaç
cäntakänäm antakam éçam rudram api bäëa-saìgrame jitavän, aho yaç ca taà jaräkhyam mågayum
api svaù vaikuëöha-viçeñaà sa-çaréram eva präpitavän, sa katham svänäm yadünäm avane éço na
bhavati? tasmät teñv anyathä-darçanaà na tattvika-lélänugatam. sa-çaréraà tu teñäà sva-loka-gatam
atéva yuktam ity arthaù.

  yaù-who; çré-kåñëaù-Çré Kåñëa; yama-lokam-to Yamaloka; gatam-gone; api-even; suru-sutam-the
word "guru-sutam; guroh jätena-means "the son of the guru; païcajana-by the demon Païcajana;
bhakñitena-swallowed; tena-with that; martyena-the word "martyena"; dehena-means "in the same

body"; eva-certainly; anayat-delivered; na-not; ca-also; brahma-tejasah-ordinary brahminical
prowess; balavattvam-strength; mantavyam-should be considered; tvam-you; ca-also; brahmästra-by
the Brahmästra weapon; dagdham-burned; yaù-who; tasmät-from that; brahmästrät-Brahmästra
weapon; anayat-the word "anayat"; raksitavän-means "protected"; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; kim
anyat-what further; vaktavyam-need be said; yah-who; antakänäm-of destroyers; antakam-the
destruction; éçam-the word "isam"; rudram-means "Lord Siva"; api-even; bäëa-saìgrame-in the battle
begun by Banasura; jitavän-defeated; aho-Oh; yah-who; ca-and; tam-him; jara-akhyam-named Jara;
mågayum-hunter; api-even; svaù-the word "svaù"; vaikuëöha-viçeñam-means a specifi Vaikuëöha
planet; sa-çatéram-in the same body; eva-certainly; präpitavän-caused to attain; sah-Lord Kåñëa;
katham-how is it possible?; svänäm-of His own; yadünäm-of the members of the Yadu dynasty;
avane-in the matter of protection; éçah-competent; na bhavati-is not; tasmät-therefore; teñu-on
these points; anyathä-darçanam-another opinion; na-not; tattvika-lélä-anugatam-a factual
description of Çré Kåñëa's pastimes; sa-çarétam-in the same body; tu-even; teñäm-of the members of
the Yadu
 dynasty; sva-loka-to their own abode in the spiritual world; gatam-gone; atéva-very; yuktam-proper;
iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.

   In this verse the word "yaù" (who) refers to Çré Kåñëa; the word "guru-sutam" means "the guru's
son (who had been swallowed by the demon Païcajana, and eventually taken to Yamaräja)"; and
the word "martyena" means "in the same body". We may note in this connectgion that by rescuing
His guru's son, Çré Kåñëa displayed His great transcendental prowess. In other words, it was not
merely ordinary brahminical power that was used by Çré Kåñëa to accomplish this extraordinary
task. In this verse Çukadeva Gosvämé also mentions Mahäräja Parékñit (tvam) who was first burned
by a brahmästra weapon and then rescued by Çré Kåñëa. In this connection the word "anayat" means
"rescued". In the battle fought with Bäëäsura, Çré Kåñëa also defeated Lord Çiva (éçam), who is
victorious even over death himself (antakäntakam). Kåñëa also delivered a hunter (mågayum)
named Jarä, and enabled him to enter the spiritual world (svaù) without having to change his body
(sa-çaréram). If Çré Kåñëa is this powerful, why should we think Heis not able to protect (avane) His
own confidential associates (sva), the members of the Yadu dynasty? Certainly any conception that
Çré Kåñëa did not protect the members of the Yadu dynasty and enable them to enter the spiritual
world is not a factual understanding of Çré Kåñëa's pastimes. The members of the Yadu dynasty
certainly returned to their own abode in the spiritual world, without having to change bodies. This
is the proper understanding.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.126
records.text:
Text 1


   nanu gacchantu te sa-çarérä eva svaà dhäma, taträpi svayaà bhagavän viräjata eveti na teñäà tad-
viraha-duùkham api. çré-bhagaväàs tu tathäsamarthyaç cet tarhi katha anyäàs tädåçän ävirbhävya
taiù saha martya-lokänugrahärtham aparam api kiyantaà kälaà martya-loke 'pi prakaöo näsét. ity
atra siddhantayan teñäà çré-bhagaväàç ca sauharda-bhareëäpi parasparam avyabhicäritvam äha

   nanu-is it not so?; gacchantu-may go; te-they; sa-çaréräh-in the same body; eva-certainly; svam
dhäma-to their own abode in the spiritual world; tatra-there; api-even; svayam bhagavän-the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; viräjate-is manifested; eva-certainly; iti-thus; na-not; teñäm-of
them; tat-from Him; viraha-of separation; duùkham-unhappiness; api-even; çré-bhagavän-the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; tu-but; tatha-in that way; asamarthyah-unable; cet-if; tarhi-then;
katham-how is it?; anyän-others; tädåçän-like them; ävirbhävya-having manifested; taiù saha-with
them; martya-loka-to the residents of the material world; anugraha-mercy; artham-for the purpose
of; aparam-api kiyantam kälam-for a short time; martya-loka-in the material world; api-even;
prakaöaù-manifest; na-not; asét-was; iti-thus; atra-in this connection; siddhantayan-establishing the
final conclusion; teñäm-of them; çré-bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ca-also;
sauharda-love; bhareëa-with great; api-also; parasparam-between temselves; avyabhicäritvam-
unbreakable relationship; äha-he describes.

   Someone may raise the question: If the members of the Yadu dynasty had gone back to their own
abode in the spiritual world, and if Çré Kåñëa, being self-sufficient, were not unhappy because of
separation from them, then why did the Lord not stay within the material world for a time longer,
and perform pastimes with His other associates in order to show mercy to the conditioned souls of
this world?
   The conclusive answer to this question is found in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
11.31.13), which reveals the unbreakable bond of intimate friendship between Lord Kåñëa and the
members of the Yadu dynasty:


Text 2


tathäpy açeña-sthiti-sambhaväpyayeñv
  ananya-hetur yad açeña-çakti-dhåk
naicchat praëetuà vapur atra çeñitaà
  martyena kià svästha-gatià pradarçayan

  tathäpi-even so; açeña-of everything; sthiti-maintenance; sambhava-creation; apyayeñu-and
destruction; ananya-hetuh-sole cause; yat-because; açeña-çakti-dhåk-He is the master of all
potencies; na-not; aicchat-desired; praëetum-to leave; vapuh-His transcendental form; atra-here in
the material world; çeñitam-remaining; martyena-kim-what is the use of remaining for the
conditioned souls?; svästha-of the pure devotees; gatim-the destination in the spiritual world;
pradarçayan-revealing.

   "Çré Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the master of all transcendental potencies,
and the sole creator, maintainer, and destroyer of unlimited material universes. After the departure
of the Yadu dynasty, He no longer desired to remain in the material world. He considered: `I have
delivered My devotees to the spiritual world, why should I stay in the material world surrounded by
non-devotees?'"***

Text 3


  yadyapy ukta-prakäreëa açeña-sthiti-sambhaväpyayeñv ananya-hetuù, yad yasmät tad ürdhvam
apy ananta-tädåça-çakti-dhåk, tathäpi yädavän antardhäpya nijam vapur atra çeñitaà praëetum
kiïcit kälaà sthäpayitum naicchat, kintu svam eva lokam anayat. tatra hetuù tan vinä martyena
kim mama prayojanam iti svashtänäm tad-dhäma-gatänäà teñäm gatim eva svasyäbhimatatvena
prakåñöam darçayan iti. çré-çukaù.

   yadyapi-although; ukta-prakäreëa-by this statement; açeña-of everything; sthiti-maintenance;
sambhava-creation; apyayeñu-and destruction; ananya-hetuù-sole cause; yat-the word "yat"; yasmät-
means "because"; tat-ürdhvam-beyond that; api-even; ananta-unlimited; tädåça-like that; çakti-
potencies; dhåk-possessing; tathäpi-nevertheless; yädavän-the members of the Yadu dynasty;
antardhäpya-having caused to dissappear; nijam-His own; vapuh-transcendental form; atra-here in
the material world; çeñitam-remaining; praëtum-to leave; kiïcit kälam-for a certain time;
sthäpayitum-to manifest; na-did not; aicchat-desire; kintu-but; svam-to His own; eva-certainly;
lokam-abode; anayat-brought; tatra-here; hetuù-is the reason; tan-the members of the Yadu
dynasty; vinä-without; martyena kim-what is the use of remaining for the conditioned souls; mama-
of Me; prayojanam-what is the necessity?; iti-thus; svasthänäm-the word "svastha"; tat-dhäma-
gatänäm-means "of those who had gone to the abode of Çré Kåñëa"; gatim-the destinaton in the
spiritual world; eva-certainly; svasya-of His own; abhimatatvena-because of affection; prakåñöam-
greatly; darçayan-revealed; iti-thus; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé.

   In this verse we may note Çré Kåñëa is described as the sole cause of the creation, maintenance,
and destruction of unlimited material universes (açeña-sthiti-sambhaväpyayeñv ananya-hetuù).
Even more significant than that, He is the master of all unlimited potencies (açeña-çakti-dhåk).
   Even though Çré Kåñëa is the omnipotent Godhead, after the departure of the Yadu dynasty, He
did not desire (naicchat) to remain in His transcendental form within this material world (vapur
atra çeñitaà praëetum). He decided to return to His own abode in the spiritual world. What is the
reason for the Lord to decide in this way? The reason is that He considered: what is the use of this
material world (martyena kim), for I have already brought My pure devotees to the spiritual world
(svastha-gatià pradarçayan). This verse shows the great affection felt by the Lord for the members
of the Yadu dynasty.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.127
records.text:
Text 1


  atas teñäà çré-bhagavadvad antardhänam eva, na tv anyad astéti çré-bhagavad-abhipräya-
kathanenäpy äha

mitho yadaiñäà bhavitä vivädo
  madhv-ämadätämra-vilocanänäm
naiñäà vadhopäya iyän ato 'nyo
  mayy udyate 'ntardadhate svayaà sma

  atah-from this; tesäm-of them; çré-bhagavat-vat-just like the Supreme Personality of Godhead;
antardhänam-dissappearance; eva-certainly; na-not; tu-but; anyat-otherwise; asti-it is; iti-thus; çré-
bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; abhipräya-of the intention; kathanena-by the
description; api-even; äha-he said; mithaù-one another; yadä-when; eñäm-of them; bhavitä-will take
place; vivädaù-quarrel; madhu-ämada-intoxication by drinking; ätämra-vilocanänäm-of their eyes
being copper-red; na-not; eñäm-of them; vadha-upäyaù-means of disappearance; iyän-like this; ataù-
besides this; anyaù-alternative; mayi-on My; udyate-disappearance; antaù-dadhate-will disappear;
svayam-themselves; sma-certainly.

   The members of the Yadu dynasty left this material world in much the same way as Lord Kåñëa
Himself left (by the agency of the Lord's transcendental potency). The Lord's plan for causing the
disappearance of the Yadu dynasty is described in the following statement of Çré Kåñëa related by
Uddhava to Vidura (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.3.15):

  "When they quarrel among themselves, influenced by intoxication, with their eyes red like
copper because of drinking [madhu], then only will they disappear; otherwise, it will not be possible.
On My [Kåñëa's] disappearance, this incident will take place."*


Text 2


  eñäm yadünäà yadä mithaù vivädaù tadäpi eñäm påthivé-parityäjane vadha-rüpaù upäyaù na
vidyate, kim utänyena viväde sa na syäd iti. tarhi teñäà mayäbhiläñite påthivé-parityäjane katama
upäyo bhavet. tatra punaù parämåçati ataù vadhät anyaù eva iyän etavän eva upäyo vartate. ko 'sau
mayy udyate mamecchayaite svayam antardadhate iti yaù. sma iti niçcyate. yadvä, vadhasyopäyo na
vidyate ity eva vyäkhyayä, ataù vadhopäyät anyaù iyän vadhopäya-tulya upäyo vidyata iti
vyäkhyeyam. anyat samänam. çrémad-uddhavo viduram.

   eñäm-of them; yadünäm-of the members of the Yadu dynasty; yadä-when; mithaù-one another;
vivädaù-quarrel; tada-then; api-even; eñäm-of them; prthivé-from the earth; parityäjane-in the
departure; vadha-killing; rüpaù-in the form of; upayaù-means; na-not; vidyate-exists; kim uta-how
much more; anyena-with another; viväde-in a quarrel; sah-that; na-not; syät-may be; iti-thus; tarhi-
then; teñäm-of them; maya-by Me; abhiläñite-desired; påthivé-from the earth; parityäjane-in the
departure; katamah-what; upäyah-method; bhavet-may be; tatra-in this matter; punaù-again;
parämåçati-He reflects; ataù-besides this; vadhät-killing; anyaù-alternative; eva-certainly; iyän-like
this; etavän-like this; eva-certainly; upäyah-method; vartate-exists; kah-who?; asau-he; mayi-on My;
udyate-disappearance; mama-by My; icchaya-desire; ete-they; svayam-themselves; antardadhate-will
disappear; iti-thus; yaù-who; sma-certainly; iti-thus; niçcaye-in the matter of certainty; yadvä-or;
vadhasya-of killing; upäyah-method; na-does not; vdyate-exist; iti-thus; eva-certainly; vyäkhyayä-

having explained; ataù-besides this; vadha-upäyat-method of causing the disappearance; anyaù-
alternative; iyän-like this; vadha-upäya-tulyah upäyah-method for causing the disappearance;
vidyate-exists; iti-thus; vyäkhyeyam-may be explained; anyat-others; samänam-equal; çrémat-
uddhavah-spoken by Uddhava; viduram-to Vidura.

  In this verse Lord Kåñëa is considering: Anyone who fights with the members of the Yadu
dynasty will be unable to kill them, and even if the Yädavas fight among themselves, they will still
be unable to kill each other. In this way it will not be possible to effect the disappearance of the
Yadu dynasty from this earth. What method of causing the Yadus to dissappear exists: except for
My own wish?" The Lord further thought: "Only if I wish it, will the Yadus leave this earth planet".
This decision of the Lord is confirmed by the use of the word "sma", which means "certainly".
  Another interpretation of this verse is that in truth there is no method that will succeed in the
"vadha" (killing) of the Yadu dynasty, for their disappearance from this earth is not at all like the
death of the conditioned souls. The Yädavas returned to the spiritual world without changing their
bodies, and therefore they did not at all die (vadha).

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.128
records.text:
Text 1


  ata eväntarhite çré-bhagavati çrémad-uddhavasya viduù iti vartamäna-pratyaya-nirdeça-väkyena
tadäném antarhitasyäpi tad-vargasya çré-bhagavataiva saha saàväso vyajyate. yathä

durbhago bata loko 'yaà
  yadavo nitaräm api
ye saàvasanto na vidur
  harià ménä ivoòupam

  atah eva-therefore; antarhite-disappeared; çré-bhagavati-when the Supreme Personality of
Godhead; çrémat-uddhavasya-of Uddhava; viduù iti-the phrase beginning with the word "viduh";
vartamäna-pratyaya-the present tense; nirdeça-indicating; dissappeared; tat-vargasya-of His
associates; çré-bhagavata-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; eva-certainly; saha-along with;
saàväsah-mutual residence; vyajyate-is manifested; yathä-just as; durbhagaù-unfortunate; bata-
certainly; lokaù-universe; ayam-this; yadavaù-the Yadu dynasty; nitaräm-more specifically; api-also;
ye-those; saàvasantaù-living together; na-do not; viduù-understand; harim-the Personality of
Godhead; ménäù-the fishes; iva uòupam-like the moon.

  After the departure of Çré Kåñëa and the Yadu dynasty, Uddhava spoke the following verse
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.2.8), using the word "viduù" (present-tense) to indicate that even after their
departure from this earth planet, the Yädavas still remained intimate associates of Çré Kåñëa,
residing in the same place with Him. Uddhava said:

  "This universe with all its planets is most unfortunate. And even more unfortunate are the
members of the Yadu dynasty because they cannot identify Lord Hari as the Personality of
Godhead, any more than the fish could identify the moon."*


Text 2


  ayam mama hådaye sphuran dvärakä-väsé lokaù. ye samvasantaù saha-vasanto 'pi na viduù
jänanti. ahaà tu saàväsa-bhägya-héno na jänäméti näçcaryam iti bhävaù. atra tadänéà yadi
saàväso näbhaviñyat, tadä navediñur ity evävakñyad iti jïeyam.

   ayam-this; mama-my; hådaye-in the heart; sphuran-manifest; dvaraka-of Dvärakä; väsi-resident;
lokaù-universe; ye samvasantaù-the words "ye samvasantah; saha-vasantah-mean "those who are
living together"; api-even; na-do not; viduù-understand; jänanti-understand; aham-I; tu-but;
saàväsa-of living together; bhägya-the good fortune; hénah-bereft of; na-do not; jänämi-I
understand; iti-thus; na-not; açcaryam-astonishing; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning; atra-in this verse;
tadäném-then; yadi-if; saàväsah-residing together; na-not; abhaviñyat-would have been; tadä-then;
na-not; avediñuh-would have known; iti-thus; eva-certainly; avakñyat-would have said; iti-thus;
jïeyam-may be understood.

  In this verse the words "ayaà lokaù" mean "the residents of Dvärakä, who are now remembered
in my thoughts"; "ye saàvasantaù" means "even though living together"; "na viduù" means "do not
understand". Although not explicitly stated, Uddhava intends to lament for Himself also in this
verse. It is as if he had said: "I have been cheated by Lord Kåñëa and by the Yädavas, for I am now
bereft of the good-fortune of their association. I am also unfortunate for I also am unable to
understand Lord Kåñëa. All these things are not at all surprising for I am certainly unworthy to
attain the Lord's association or qualified to understand Him. Still, somehow or other, in the past I
did have Lord Kåñëa's association, and if it were not for that, I would not know enough to speak in
this way."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.129
records.text:
Text 1


  nanv adhunäpi na jänantéti kathaà janaséty açaìkya hetuà präcéna-nijänubhävam äha

iìgita-jïäù puru-prauòhä
  ekärämäç ca sätvatäù
sätvatäm åñabhaà sarve
  bhütäväsam amaàsata

  nanu-is it not so?; adhuna-at this moment; api-even; na-do not; jänanti-understand; iti-thus;

katham-how is it possible?; janasi-that you understand; iti-thus; açaìkya-doubting; hetum-the
reason; präcéna-previous; nija-own; anubhävam-experience; äha-he describes; iìgita-jïäù-expert in
psychic study; puru-prauòhäù-highly experienced; eka-one; ärämäù-relaxation; ca-also; sätvatäù-
devotees, or own men; sätvatäm åñabham-head of the family; sarve-all; bhüta-äväsam-all-pervading;
amaàsata-could think.
