  At this point in their conversation, Vidura may object: "If the Yadavas do not understand Lord
Kåñëa, even now, then how is it that you understand this much?"
   In order to remove Vidura's doubt, Uddhava spoke the following verse, explaining that the
Yädavas are able to understand Kåñëa to a certain extent. They know that He is the all-pervading
Supersoul, but they are not aware that He is the Original Personality of Godhead, the origin of all
expansion of Godhead. Uddhava said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.2.9):

  "The Yadus were all experienced devotees, learned and expert in psychic study. Over and above
this, they were always with the Lord in all kinds of relaxations, and still they were only able to
know Him as the one Supreme who dwells everywhere."*


Text 2


  sätvatäm sveñäm eva åñabham nitya-kula-patitvena vartamänaà svayaà bhagavantam api bhüta-
väsam tad-aàça-rüpaà bhutäntaryäminäm eva amäàsata iti. sarva-bhütädhiväsaù ity antaryämi-
çruteù. uktaà ca våñëénäà para-devatä iti. çrémad-uddhavaù çré-viduram.

   sätvatäm-the word "satvatam"; sveñäm-means "of the family"; eva-certainly; åñabham-the word
"åñabham"; nitya-kula-patitvena-means "the eternal leader of the family"; vartamänam-remaining;
svayam-bhagavantam-the Original Personality of Godhead; api-also; bhüta-väsam-all-pervading; tat-
aàça-rüpam-by His expansion as Kñirodakasayi Viñëu; bhutaantaryäminäm-the Supersoul; eva-
certainly; amäàsata-could think; iti-thus; sarva-of all; bhüta-living entities; adhiväsaù-residing in
the hearts; iti-thus; antaryämi-description of the Supersoul; çrutaù-from the Çruti-sastra; uktam-
said; ca-also; våñëénäm-of the members of the Våñëi family; para-devatä-the supreme diety; iti-thus;
çrémat-uddhavaù-spoken by Uddhava; çré-viduram-to Vidura.

   In this verse the words "sätvatäm åñabham" mean "the eternal leader of the family". Even though
Çré Kåñëa is the Original Personality of Godhead, the source of all incarnations, the Yädavas
thought of Him (amäàsata) as the all-pervading Supersoul (bhüta-väsam), who is one of the
expansions (Kñérodakaçäyé Viñëu) of Lord Kåñëa. The Supersoul is described in the following
statement of Çruti-çästra:

   "The Supersoul resides in the hearts of all living entities."

   That Çré Kåñëa is the leader of the Yadu dynasty is also described in the following statement of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.43.17):

   "Çré Kåñëa is the supreme Deity worshiped by the members of the Våñëi dynasty."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.130
records.text:
Text 1


yam eva saàväsaà pürvam api prärthayäm äsa

nähaà taväìghri-kamalam
  kñaëärdham api keçava
tyaktuà samutsahe nätha
  svadhäma naya mäm api

  yam-which; eva-certainly; samvasam-associates; purvam-former; api-also; prarthayam asa-
requested; na-not; aham-I; tava-Your; anghri-kamalam-lotus feet; ksana-ardham-for half a second;
api-even; kesava-O Kesava; tyaktum-to abandon; samutsahe-desire; natha-O Lord; sva-dhama-to
Your transcendental abode; naya-please bring; mam-me; api-also.

   After the departure of Lord Kåñëa and the Yädavas from the earth, Uddhava offered the
following prayer, begging the Lord to enable him to regain their former association. Uddhava said
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.6.43):

 "O Lord Keçava, I am not willing to abandon Your lotus feet for even half a second. Please bring
me to Your transcendental abode."***


Text 2


  svadhäma dvärakäyä eva prapaïcikäprakaöa-prakäça-viçeñam apéti. yathä yädavän anyän nayasi,
yathä mäm api naya ity arthaù. arthäntare tv api-çabda-vaiyärthyaà syät. çrémad-uddhavaù.

   sva-dhäma-the word "svadhäma; dvärakäyäh-of Dväraka; eva-certainly; prapaïcika-in the
material world; aprakaöa-unmanifested; prakäça-manifestation; viçeñam-specific; api-even; iti-thus;
yathä-just as; yädavän-members of the Yädu dynasty; anyän-others; nayasi-You bring; tathä-in the
same way; mäm-me; api-also; naya-bring; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; artha-antara-another
meaning; tu-also; api-çabda-of the word "api"; vaiyärthyam-in the sense of ueslessness; syät-may be;
çrémat-uddhavaù-spoken by Uddhava.

  In this verse the word "sva-dhäma" refers to the abode of Dvärakä in the spiritual world, beyond
the view of the material world. Uddhava says in this verse: "O Lord, You have brought the other
members of the Yadu dynasty to Your abode, You should also bring me." Another meaning of the
word "api" is "even". Interpreted in this way, Uddhava says "Please bring even me to Your abode". In

this way Uddhava humbly describes his own uselessness and lack of good qualities.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.131
records.text:
Text 1


padmottara-khaëòe yädavänäm tädåçam

yathä saumitré-bharatau
  yathä saìkarñaëädayaù
tathä tenaiva jäyante
  nija-lokad yadåcchayä

punas tenaiva gacchanti
  tat-padaà çäçvataà param
na karma-bandhanaà janma
  vaiñëavänäà ca vidyate iti.

   padma-uttara-khaëòe-in the Uttara-khaëòa of the Padma Purana; yädavänäm-of the members of
the Yädu dynasty; tädåçam-like that; yathä-just as; saumitré-Laksmana; bharatau-and Bharata; yathä-
just as; saìkarñaëa-Balarama; adayaù-and others; tathä-in the same way; tena-with Çré Kåñëa; eva-
certainly; jäyante-they take birth; nija-lokat-from their respective abodes in the spiritual sky;
yadåcchayä-by their own wish; punah-again; tena-with the Lord; eva-certainly; gacchanti-they go;
tat-padam-to their abodes in the spiritual world; çäçvatam-eternal; param-transcendental; na-not;
karma-of fruitive actions; bandhanam-bondage; janma-of birth; vaiñëavänäm-of the pure devotees
of the Lord; ca-and; vidyate-exists; iti-thus.

   The appearance and activities of the Yädavas are transcendental, just as those of Çré Kåñëa. This
is confirmed in the following statement of Padma Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa:

  "Just as Lakñmaëa and Bharata descend into the material world to accompany Lord Rämacandra,
and just as Lord Balaräma and others also descend to accompany Lord Kåñëa, in the same way the
members of the Yadu dynasty descend from their own abodes in the spiritual sky, and take birth in
the material world to accompany Çré Kåñëa. When Lord Kåñëa again returns to the spiritual world,
the members of the Yadu dynasty again accompany Him. They thus return to their original eternal
abodes in the spiritual sky. The Yädavas and other great devotees, therefore, never take birth in the
material world, as the conditioned souls do. Neither are they bound by the reactions of fruitive
activities, as are the conditioned souls."


Text 2

 atra nija-lokät iti tat-padam iti ca räma-kåñëädi-vaikuëöhaà padmottara-khaëòa-matam
matsyädy-avatäräëäà påthak påthak vaikuëöhävasthitas tatra säkñäd uktatvät.

   atra-in this verse; nija-lokat-from their own abode; iti-thus; tat-padam-that abode; iti-thus; ca-
also; räma-of Lord Rämacandra; kåñëa-of Lord Kåñëa; adi-beginning with; vaikuïtham-Vaikuëöha
realm; padma-uttara-khaëòa-of the Padma Purana, Uttara-khaëòa; matam-opinion; matsya-of Lord
Matsya; adi-and other avatäräëäm-incarnations of Godhead; påthak påthak-variously; vaikuëöha-in
Vaikuëöhaloka; avasthiteh-because of residents; tatra-there; säkñät-directly; uktatvät-because of the
statement.

  In these verses the words "nija-lokät" and "tat-padam" refer to the planets of Lord Kåñëa and Lord
Rämacandra in the spiritual world. According to this statement of Padma Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa,
the incarnations of the Lord, (such as Lord Matsya and others), each have Their own planet in the
Vaikuëöhalokas.


Text 3


  tädåçänäà bhagavat iva bhagavad-icchayaiva janmädi-käraëaà coktaà çré-vidureëa

ajasya janmotpatha-näçanäya
   karmäëy akartur grahaëäya puàsäm
nanv anyathä ko 'rhati deha-yogaà
   paro guëänäm uta karma-tantram

   tädåçänäm-of those like Him; bhagavatah-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; iva-just like;
bhagavat-of the Supreme Lord; icchaya-by the desire; eva-certainly; janma-adi-of their appearance,
activities, and disappearance; käraëam-cause; ca-also; uktam-described; çré-vidurena-by Çré Vidura;
ajasya-of the unborn; janma-appearance; utpatha-näçanäya-for the sake of annihilating the
upstarts; karmäëi-works; akartuù-of one who has nothing to do; grahaëäya-to take up; puàsäm-of
all persons; nanu anyathä-otherwise; kaù-who; arhati-may deserve; deha-yogam-contact of the
body; paraù-transcendental; guëänäm-of the three modes of nature; uta-what to speak of; karma-
tantram-the law of action and reaction.

  The reason for the voluntary appearance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and His
associates in this material world is described by Vidura in the following verse from Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (3.1.44):

   "The appearance of the Lord is manifested for the annihilation of the upstarts. His activities are
transcendental and are enacted for the understanding of all persons. Otherwise, since the Lord is
transcendental to all material modes, what purpose could He serve by coming to earth?"*


Text 4

   ko vänyo 'pi iti öékä ca. tad evaà teñäà çré-kåñëa-nitya-parikäratve siddhe sädhite çré-
vasudevädénäà präg janmani sädhakatvädi-kathanaà ca bhagavata iva bhagavad-icchayaiva loka-
saìgrahädyärtham aàçenaivävatärät kvacij jéväntaräveçät sambhavati. punaç ca svayam avatäratsu
teñu tad-aàça-praveçaù kathä-rétyä tv ekatvena kathanam iti jïeyam, yathä pradyumnasya
vyäkhyätam.

   kah-who?; va-or; anyah-another; api-even; iti-thus; öékä-the commentary of Çrédhara Svami; ca-
also; tat-therefore; evam-in this way; teñäm-of them; çré-kåñëa with Çré Kåñëa; nitya-parikäratve-in
the position of being eternal associates; siddhe-perfect; sädhite-proved; çré-vasudeva-adénäm-of
Maharaja Vasudeva and the other confidential associates of Lord Kåñëa; präk-before; janmani-in
the birth; sädhakatva-the state of becoming eligible to become the Lord's associate; adi-beginning
with; kathanam-description; ca-also; bhagavatah-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; iva-just
like; bhagavat-of the Supreme Lord; icchaya-according to the desire; eva-certainly; loka-the word;
saìgraha-protection; adi-beginning with; artham-for the purpose; aàçena-by a partial expansion;
eva-certainly; avatärät-from incarnation; kvacit-somewhere; jéva-a living entity; antara-with; aveçät-
because of entrance; sambhavati-is possible; punah-again; ca-also; svayam-personally; avatäratsu-
descending; teñu-among them; tat-of Him; aàç-part; praveçaù-entrance; kathä-rétyä-by the
statement; tu-but; ekatvena-as one; kathanam-account; iti-thus; jëeyam-may be understood; yathä-
just as; pradumnasya-of Pradyumna; vyäkhyätam-explained.

  The word "kaù" in this verse is explained by Çrédhara Svämé:

  "In this verse the word 'kaù' means 'otherwise'".

   Now that we have proven that Mahäräja Vasudeva and the other confidential associates of Lord
Kåñëa are all the Lord's eternal associates in the spiritual world, someone may protest, saying that
there are many places in the Vedic literatures where it is described that the Lord's associates were
demigods or great devotees in their previous lives, and because of their great devotion they became
eligible to become the Lord's associates.
   To this objection I reply that in such cases it should be understood that such great devotees are
empowered expansions of particular associates of the Lord. In other words, at the time of the Lord's
appearance in this world, some of the Lord's eternal associates may empower certain great devotees
to assume their roles in the Lord's pastimes within the material world. Such empowerment is like
the empowerment of Pradyumna, who was the demigod Cupid empowered by (viñëu-tattva) Lord
Pradyumna of the catur-vyüha.


Text 5


  evam tåtéye vedäham ity ädi bhagavad-väkya uddhavaà prati vasv-aàçatväpekñäyaiva vaso iti
sambodhanam. tädåçäàça-paryävasanäspadäàçi-rüpatvena carama-janmatoktiç ca jïeyä.

  evam-in this way; tåtéye-in the Third Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (3.4.11): veda aham iti ädi
bhagavat-väkye-in the followingn statement of the Supreme Personality of Godhead


vedäham antar manasépsitaà te
  dadämi yat tad duraväpam anyaiù
satre purä viçva-såjäà vasünäà
  mat-siddhi-kämena vaso tvayeñöaù

uddhavam-Uddhava; prati-to; vasu-of Vasu; aàçatva-partial incarnation; apekñaya-in relation to;
eva-certainly; vaso-the word "vaso"; iti-thus; sambodhanam-in the vocative case; tädåça-like that;
aàça-partial incarnation; paryävasana-conclusion; aspada-abode; aàçi-origin of the incarnation;
rüpatvena-in the form of; carama-final; janmata-birth; uktih-statement; ca-also; jïeyä-may be
understood.

  An example of one of the Lord's associates who did not descend from the spiritual world to
accompany the Lord in His pastimes is Uddhava. This is described by Çré Kåñëa to Uddhava, where
the Lord described Uddhava's previous birth as Vasu. Çré Kåñëa said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.4.11):

    "O Vasu, I know from within your mind what you desired in the days of yore when the Vasus
and other demigods responsible for expanding the universal affairs performed sacrifices. You
particularly desired to achieve My association. This is very difficult to obtain for others, but I award
it unto you."*

  In this verse Lord Kåñëa addressed Uddhava as "vaso" (in the vocative case) because in his
previous birth he was the demigod Vasu. He was a partial expansion of the Lord's associate
Uddhava. Uddhava's previous birth as Vasu should be understood in this way.


Text 6


ata eväha

tvam eva pürva-sarge 'bhüù
  påçniù sväyambhuve sati
tadäyaà sutapä näma
  prajäpatir akalmañaù

tvaà çré-devaké-devy eva påçnir abhüù, na tu påçnis tvam abhüd iti. evam tadéyam apéti. çré-
bhagavän.

  atah eva-therefore; aha-He says; tvam-you; eva-indeed; pürva-sarge-in a previous millenium;
abhüù-became; påñnéh-by the name Påçni; sväyambhuve-the millennium of Sväyambhuva Manu;
sati-O supremely chaste; tadä-at that time; ayam-Vasudeva; sutapä-Sutapä; näma-by the name;
prajäpatiù-a Prajäpati; akalmañaù-a spotlessly pious person; tvam-the word "tvam (you)"; çré-devaké-

devi-refers to Devaké-devi; eva-certainly; påçniù-by thename Påñni; abhüù-became; na-not; tu-but;
påçniù-Påçni; tvam-you; abhüt-became; iti-thus; evam-in the same way; tada-at that time; ayam-
Vasudeva; api-also; iti-thus; çré-bhagavän-spoken by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

  Devaké and Mahäräja Vasudeva are described in the same way. Lord Kåñëa says to Devaké
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.32):

   "My dear mother, best of the chaste, in your previous birth, in the Sväyambhuva millennium,
you were known as Påçni, and Vasudeva, who was the most pious Prajäpati, was named Sutapä."*

  The Lord here says thatg Devaké became Påçni. He does not say that Påçni became Devaké.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.132
records.text:
evam eväha

vasudevam hareù sthänaà
  vadanty anakadundubhim iti

sattvaà viçuddhaà vasudeva-çabditaà
  yad éyate tatra pumän apävåtaù

ity ädau prasiddhaà vasudeväkhyam hareù sthänam atra anakadundubhià vadanti munaya iti. çré-
çukaù.

   evam-in this way; eva-certainly; aha-he says; vasudevam-unto Vasudeva; hareù-of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; sthänam-that place; vadanti-they call; änaka-dundubhim-
/Anakadundubhi; sattvam-consciousness; viçuddham-pure; vasudeva-Vasudeva; çabdi-tam-known
as; yat-because; éyate-is revealed; tatra-there; pumän-the Supreme Person; apävåtaù-without any
covering; iti-thus; ädau-in the passage beginning; prasiddham-celebrated; vasudeva-Vasudeva;
akhyam-named; hareù-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; sthänam-the place; atra-there;
anakadundubhim-Anakadundubhi; vadanti-they call; munayah-the sages; iti-thus; çré-çukaù-spoken
by Çré Çukadeva Gosvami.

  That Mahäräja Vasudeva is described in Çrémad-Bhägavatam:

  "The stage of pure goodness, where one is able to realize the Supreme Lord, is known as `vasudeva-
sattva'"*

  "Because Anakadundubhi was situated in the platform of pure goodness (vasudeva-sattva), he
became the place where the Supreme Personality of Godhead made His appearance within this
world. This is described by the great sages."*

  This means that the sages say that Anakadundubhi became famous as Vasudeva, the place of the

Lord's appearance. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.133
records.text:
tathäträpy evaà vyäkhyeyam

  devakyäà deva-rüpiëyäm iti.

   devo väsudevas tad-rüpiëyäm çuddha-sattva-våtti-rüpäyäm eveti. ata eva viñëu-puräëe täà prati
deva-stutau tvaà parä prakåtiù sükñmä iti bahutaram. çré-çukaù.

   tatha-in the same way; atra-here; api-also; evam-in this way; vyäkhyeyam-may be explained;
devakyäm-Devaki; deva-rupiëyäm-whose form was spiritual; iti-thus; devah-the word "deva";
väsudevah-means the transcendental state of väsudeva-sattva; tat-rupiëyäm-with such a
transcendental form; çuddha-sattva-våtti-rüpäyäm-with a form of pure goodness; eva-certainly; iti-
thus; atah- ; eva-therefore; viñëu-puräëe-in the Visnu Purana; tämprati-to her; deva-of the
demigods; statue-in the prayers; tvam-you are; parä-superior; prakåtiù-nature; sükñmä-subtle; iti-
thus; behutaram-greatly; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çré Çukadeva Gosvami.

 It is further explained (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.8):

  "Devaké appeared in a spiritual form."

  The word "deva" here means "of Lord Väsudeva" and "deva-rüpiëyäm" means "a spiritual form of
pure goodness."
   The spiritual form of Devaké-devé is also described in the Viñëu Puräëa, where the demigods,
offer the following offering prayers to her:

  "O Devaké, your form is transcendental."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.134
records.text:
ata eväham iva nityam eva mat-pitå-rüpeëäprakaöa-léläyäà vartamänau yuvam adhunä prakaöa-
léläm anugatau punar aprakaöa-lélä-praveçaà yadåcchayäpy athety äha

yuväà mäà putra-bhävena
  brahma-bhävena cäsakåt
cintayantau kåta-snehau
  yäsyethe mad-gatià paräm

  brahma-bhävena naräkåti-para-brahma-buddhyä param prakaöa-léläto 'nyam mad-gatim léläm.

   atah eva-therefore; aham-I; iva-as if; nityam-eternally; eva-certainly; mat-my; pitå-father; rüpeëa-
in the form; aprakaöa-léläyäm-in the unmanifested pastimes; vartamänau-being; yuvam-you two;
adhunä-at present; prakaöa-léläm-manifest pastimes; anugatau-attained; punah-again; aprakaöa-lélä-
praveçam-attainment of the unmanifest pastimes; yadåcchaya-automatically; atha-then; iti-thus;
äha-He said; yuväm-both of you (husband and wife); mäm-unto Me; putra-bhävena-as your son;
brahma-bhävena-knowing that I am the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ca-and; asakåt-
constantly; cintayantau-thinking like that; kåta-snehau-dealing with love and affection; yäsyethe-
shall both obtain; mat-gatim-My supreme abode; paräm-which is transcendental, beyond this
material world; brahma-bhävena-the words "brahma-bhävena"; nara-human; akåti-form; para-
brahma-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; buddhyä-with the understanding; param-the word
"param"; prakaöa-lélätah-than the manifest pastimes; anyam-other; mat-My supreme abode;
lélämpastimes.

  Before Çré Kåñëa appeared in this material world, Vasudeva and Devaké were His parents in the
aprakaöa-lélä (unmanifest pastimes) of the spiritual world. These two parents entered this material
world along with the Lord, and performed the manifest pastimes (prakaöa-lélä) there. When Kåñëa
would return to the spiritual world, Vasudeva and Devaké would automatically follow Him there,
and again assume their parental roles there. It is with this understanding that Çré Kåñëa said to
them (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.45):

  "Both of you, husband and wife, constantly think of Me as your son, but always know that I am
the Supreme Personality of Godhead. By thus thinking of Me constantly with love and affection,
you will achieve the highest perfection; returning home, back to Godhead."*

   In this verse we may note that the word "brahma-bhävena" means "with the understanding that
the Supreme Personality of Godhead has appeared in a humanlike form" and the words "mad-gatià
paräm" means "the unmanifest pastimes of the spiritual world, different from the manifest pastimes
of the material world."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.135
records.text:
Text 1


   yuvayoù präg-aàçenävirbhütayor api mad-eka-niñöhäséd ity äha

ajuñöa-grämya-viñayäv
  anapatyau ca dam-paté
na vavräthe 'pavargaà me
  mohitau deva-mäyayä

 yuvayoù-of the two of you; präk-formerly; aàçena-by a partial incarnation; avirbhütayoh-
manifest; api-also; mad-eka-niñöha-firm faith and devotion to Me; iti-thus; äha-He describes; ajuñöa-

grämya-viñayau-for sex life and to beget a child like Me; anapatyau-because of possessing no son; ca-
also; dam-paté-both husband and wife; na-never; vavräthe-asked for (any other benediction);
apavargam-liberation from this world; me-from Me; mohitau-being so muchy attracted; deva-
mäyayä-by transcendental love for Me (desiring Me as your beloved son).

  Çré Kåñëa describes the great devotion and faith felt by Vasudeva and Devaké in their partial
incarnation as Sutapä and Påçni in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3.39):

  "Being husband and wife but always sonless, you were attracted by sexual desires, for by the
influence of devamäyä, transcendental love, you wanted to have Me as your son. Therefore you
never desired to be liberated from this material world."*


Text 2


  mama mäyayä mad-viñeyaka-sneha-mäyyä çaktyety arthaù.

vaiñëavéà vyatanon mäyäà
  putra-snehamayéà vibhuù

iti vraja-räjïéà prati ca darçanät. tädåça-sneha-janikäyä mama kåpayeti vä mäyä dambhe kåpäyäà
ca iti viçva-prakäçät. tat-premëaiva hy apavargasya tiraskäraù sarvatra çrüyate, yadyapi mokña-
varaëe hetur astéty äha ajuñöa iti. viñayäveçäbhäväd vairägyät patter iti bhävaù. çré-bhagavän
pitarau.

   mama mäyayä-the words "mama mäyayä; mat-viñayaka-sneha-mayya-mean "with transcendental
love for Me"; çaktya-by that potency; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; vaiñëavém-viñëumäyä, or
yogamäyä; vyatanot-expanded; mäyäm-yogamäyä; putra-sneha-mayém-very much attached because
of maternal affection for her son; vibhuù-the Supreme Lord; iti-thus; vraja-of Vrajabhumi; räjïém
prati-to the queen (Mother Yaçoda); ca-also; darçanät-because of seeing; tädåça-like that; sneha-
love; janikäyä-produced from; mama-My; kåpäyä-by the mercy; iti-thus; va-or; maya-the word
"maya"; dambhe-in the sense of deceit; krpayam-or mercy; ca-and; iti-thus; viçva-prakäçät-from the
Visva-prakasa dictionary; tat-premëa-by that pure love for Kåñëa; eva-certainly; hi-indeed;
apavargasya-of liberation; tiraskäraù-eclipse; sarvatra-everywhere; çrüyate-is heard; yadyapi-
although; mokña-of liberation; varane-in the selection; hetuh-the reason; asti-is; iti-thus; äha-He
said; ajuñöa iti-the verse beginning with the word "ajusta"; viñaya-aveça-abhävä-because of not
engaging in material sense-gratification; vairägyät patteh-because of renunciation; iti-thus; bhävaù-
the meaning; çré-bhagävän-spoken by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; pitarau-to His parents.

  In this verse the word "mäyayä" means "by the Lord's potency which inspires transcendental love
for Him". The word "mäyä" is also used in this sense in the following quote from Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.8.43), where Mother Yaçodä's love for Kåñëa is described in the following words:

  "Mother Yaçodä, by the grace of the Lord, could understand the real truth. But then again, the

supreme master, by the influence of the internal potency, yogamäyä, inspired her to become
absorbed in intense maternal affection for her son."*

   The word "mäyä" may also mean "My mercy, which is the cause of intense love for Me." This
interpretation is supported by the Viçva-prakäça dictionary, which defines the word "mäyä" in the
following way:

   "The word `mäyä' means either `deceit', or `mercy'".

   Although pure love of Kåñëa is the natural cause of liberation from material entanglement, it also
eclipses that benediction of liberation and makes it seem very insignificant. For this reason,
Vasudeva and Devaké were not very eager to attain liberation. We may also note that the phrase
"ajuñöa-grämya-viñayau" does not mean that Vasudeva and Devaké were intent on material sense
gratification as the conditioned souls are. Actually Vasudeva and Devaké were supremely
renounced and free from all material desires.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.136
records.text:
atha çré-gopädénäm api tan-nitya-parikaratvam jayati jana-niväsaù ity ädäv eva vyaktam. ata
eväha

tasmän mac-charaëaà goñöhaà
  man-näthaà mat-parigraham
gopaye svätma-yogena
  so 'yaà me vrata ähitaù

spañöam. çré-bhagavän.

  atha-now; çré-gopa-adinäm-of the cowherd residents of Våndävana; api-also; tat-nitya-
parikaratvam-status as the eternal associates of Çré Kåñëa; jayati jana-niväsaù-(Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.90.48):

jayati jana-niväso devaké-janma-vädo
  yadu-vara-pariñat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam sthira-cara-våjina-ghnaù susmita-çré-mukhena
  vraja-pura-vanitänäà vardhayan käma-devam

iti ädäu-in that passage; eva-certainly; vyaktam-is revealed; atah eva-therefore; aha-Çré Kåñëa said;
tasmät-therefore; mat-saraëam-taking shelter of Me; goñöham-the residents of Våndävana; mat-
nätham-taking Me as their lord; mat-parigraham-My associates; gopaye-I shall protect; sva-atma-
yogena-by My own transcendental potency; sah-ayam-that; me-My; vratah-vow; ähitaù-accepted;
spañöam-the meaning is clear; çré-bhagavän-spoken by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

  That the residents of Gokula Våndävana are also eternal associates of Çré Kåñëa is confirmed in
the following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.90.48):

   "Lord Çré Kåñëa is He who is known as jana-niväsa, the resort of all living entities, and who is
also known as Devaké-nandana or Yaçodä-nandana, the son of Devaké and Yaçodä. He is the guide
of the Yadu dynasty, and with His mighty arms He kills everything inauspicious as well as every
man who is impious. By His presence He destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities,
moving and inert. His blissful smiling face always increases the lusty desires of the gopés of
Våndävana. May He be all glorious and happy."*

   Çré Kåñëa also affirmed that the residents of Våndävana are His eternal associates in the
following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.25.18):

  "The residents of Våndävana have completely taken shelter of Me. They consider Me their
supreme master, and they are all My eternal associates. By expanding My own transcendental
potency, I shall therefore protect them from Indra's wrath, for I have vowed that I shall always
protect My devotees."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.137
records.text:
Text 1


tathä

tata ärabhya nandasya
  vrajaù sarva-samåddhimän
harer niväsätma-guëai
  ramäkréòam abhün nåpa

   tathä-in the same way; tataù ärabhya-beginning from that time; nandasya-of Mahäräja Nanda;
vrajaù-Vrajabhümi, the land for protecting and breeding cows; sarva-samåddhimän-became opulent
with all kinds of riches; hareù niväsa-of the residence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ätma-
guëaiù-by the transcendental qualities; ramä-äkréòam-the place of pastimes for the goddess of
fortune; abhüt-became; nåpa-O King (Mahäräja Parékñit).

   That the gopés of Våndävana are goddesses of fortune in the spiritual world is confirmed by the
following statement of Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.5.18):

  "O Mahäräja Parékñit, the home of Nanda Mahäräja is eternally the abode of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead and His transcendental qualities and is therefore always naturally endowed
with the opulence of all wealth. Yet beginning from Lord Kåñëa's appearance there, it became the
place for the pastimes of the goddess of fortune."*


Text 2

  harer niväsa-bhüto yaù ätmä tasya ye guëäs tair eva sarva-samåddhimän. nitya-yoge
matvärthéyena nityam eva sarva-samåddhi-yuktaù çré-nandasya vrajaù. tatas taà çré-kåñëa-
prädurbhävam ärabhya tu ramä-kréòäm

cintämaëi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-våkña-
  lakñävåteñu surabhér abhipälayantam
lakñmé-sahasra-çata-sambhrama-sevyamänaà
  govindam ädi-puruñaà tam ahaà bhajämi

ity atra prasiddhyä ramäëäà mahä-lakñméëäà çré-vraja-devénäm api säkñäd vihäräspadaà babhüva.
hari-niväsätmani tatra çré-kåñëo yävan nigüòhatayä viharati sma, tävat tä api tathaiva viharanti
sma. vyaktatayä tu ta api vyaktatayety arthaù. çré-çukaù.

   hareh-of Lord Hari; niväsa-residence; bhütaù-become; yaù-who; ätmä-self; tasya-of whom; guëaiù-
by the qualities; taiù-by them; eva-certainly; sarva-samåddhimän-opulent with all kinds of riches;
nitya-yoge-eternally; matva-having considered; arthéyena-with opulence; nityam-eternally; eva-
certainly; sarva-samåddhi-yuktaù-opulent with all kinds of riches; çré-nandasya-of Maharaja Nanda;
vrajaù-Vrajabhumi; tatah-therefore; tam-that; çré-kåñëa-of Çré Kåñëa; prädurbhävam-appearance;
ärabhya-beginning from that time; tu-also; ramä-kréòäm-the place of pastimes for the goddess of
fortune; cintämaëi-touchstone; prakara-groups made of; sadmasu-in abodes; kalpa-våkña-of desire
trees; lakña-by millions; ävåteñu-surrounded; surabhéù-surabhi cows; abhipälayantam-tending; lakñmé-
of goddesses of fortune; sahasra-of thousands; çata-by hundreds; sambhrama-with great respect;
sevyamänam-being served; govindam-Govinda; ädi-puruñam-the original person; tam-Him; aham-I;
bhajämi-worship; iti-thus; atra-here; prasiddhyä-with grea fame; ramäëäm mahä-lakñméëäm-of the
most exalted goddess of fortune; çré-vraja-devénäm-of the gopés of Vrajabhumi; api-even; säkñat-
directly; vihära-of transcendental pastimes; aspadam-abode; babhüva-became; hari-niväsa-atmani-
in that abode of Çré Kåñëa; tatra-there; çré-kåñëaù-Çré Kåñëa; yävat-as long as; nigüòhatayä-with
confidential pastimes; viharati sma-sported; tävat-for that length of time; täh-they; api-also; tatha-
in the same way; eva-certainly; viharanti sma-performe
d pastimes; vyaktatayä-with the manifestation; tu-also; tah-the gopés; api-also; vyaktataya-with the
manifestation; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvami.

   In this verse Våndävana-dhäma, the home of Nanda Mahäräja (nandasya vrajaù) is described as
eternally endowed with the opulence of all wealth (sarva-samåddhimän). When Çré Kåñëa appeared
in Våndävana with all His transcendental qualities (atma-guëaiù), and enjoyed confidential
pastimes there, the most exalted goddesses of fortune in the spiritual world came with Him to enjoy
pastimes with the Lord. As long as the Lord stayed in the material world, these goddesses of fortune
also stayed. In this way Våndävana-dhäma became the place of Çré Kåñëa's pastimes, and also the
residence of the greatest goddesses of fortune. That Våndävana-dhäma is the abode of pastimes for
the goddesses of fortune (ramä-kréòäm) is confirmed by the following verse from Brahma-saàhitä
(5.29):

  "I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, the first progenitor, who is tending the cows, yielding all

desires, in abodes built with spiritual gems and surrounded by millions of purpose trees. He is always
served with great reverence and affection by hundreds and thousands of goddesses of fortune."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.138
records.text:
Text 1


etad eva prapaïcayati ñaòbhiù

aho bhägyam aho bhägyaà
  nanda-gopa-vrajaukasäm
yan-mitraà paramänandaà
  pürëaà brahma sanätanam

   etat-this; eva-certainly; prapaïcayati-is manifested; ñaòbhiù-by six verses (Bhägavatam 10.14.32-
37); aho-what great; bhägyam-fortune; aho-what great; bhägyam-fortune; nanda-of Mahäräja
Nanda; gopa-of other cowherd men; vraja-okasäm-of the inahabitants of Vrajabhümi; yat-of whom;
mitram-friend; parama-änandam-the supreme bliss; pürëam-complete; brahma-the Absolute Truth;
sanätanam-eternal.

  That the residents of Gokula Våndävana are the eternal associates of Çré Kåñëa is confirmed by
Lord Brahmä in six verses from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.32-37), which I shall now discuss (in
Anucchedas 138-143).
  In the first of these verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.32), Brahmä glorified the residents of
Våndävana, saying:

   "How greatly fortunate are Nanda Mahäräja, the cowherd men and all the inhabitants of
Vrajabhümi! There is no limit to their fortune because the Absolute Truth, the source of
transcendental bliss, the eternal Supreme Brahman, has become their friend."*


Text 2


   bhägyam anirvacéyä käpi çré-kåñëasya kåpä, tasya punar ukty-òäreëa sarvathaiväparicchedyatvam
uktam. pürëa-paramänanda-brahmatvenaiva sanätanatve siddhe yat punas tad-upädänäà tan-mitra-
padasyaiva viçeñaëatvena läbhyam. athavä vidheyasya viçeña-pratipatty-artham anudyaà viçiñyate.
yathä manoramaà suvarëam idaà kuëòalaà jätam iti kuëòalasyaiva manoramatvaà sädhyam,
tasmäd aträpy anudyasya çré-kåñëakhyasya para-brahmaëaù paramänanda-pürëatva-lakñaëam
viçeñaëa-dvayaà vidheyäyä mitratäyä eva tat-tad-bhävaà sädhayatéti tad-ekärtha-pravåttaà
sanätanatvaà tasyäs tad-bhävaà sädhayet. kià cätra mitram iti käla-viçeña-yoga-nirdeçäbhävät käla-
sämänyam eva bhajate. tataç ca tasya mitratä-lakñaëasya vidheyasya käla-trayävasthayitvam eva
spañöam. käläntaräsaïjanaà tu kañöam. atra cottarayor arthayoù çré-kåñëasya sanätanatve çabda-

labdhe sati tadéya-maitré-mataà parikaraëam api sanätanatvaà näsambhavam api. çré-rukmiëé-
prabhåténäà tathä darçanät.

   bhägyam-good fortune; anirvacanéyä-indescribeable; käpi-something; çré-kåñëasya-of Çré Kåñëa;
kåpä-mercy; tasya-of His; punaù-again; ukti-to the statement; ädäreëa-by careful attention;
sarvatha-completely; eva-certainly; aparicchedyatvam-limitlessness; uktam-is described; pürëa-
perfect and complete; parama-ananda-full of transcendental bliss; brahmatvena-by the sttus as the
Supreme Godhead; eva-certainly; sanätanatve-in eternality; siddhe-perfect and complete; yat-
because; punah-again; tat-upädänäm-an additional meaning; tat-mitra-padasya-of the word "mitra";
viçeñaëatvena-as modifying; läbhyam-may be obtained; athavä-or; vidheyasya-of the predicate;
viçeña-pratipatti-artham-modification of the meaning; anudyam-the subject; viçiñyate-is
distinguished; yathä-just as; manoramam-beautiful; suvarëam-golden; idam-this; kuëòalam-earring;
jätam-produced; iti-thus; kuëòalasya-of the earring; eva-certainly; manoramaivam-beauty; sädhyam-
may be established; tasmät-therefore; atra-here; api-also; anudyasya-of the suject; çré-kåñëa-akhyasya-
of Çré Kåñëa; para-brahmaëaù-the Supreme Godhead; parama-ananda-transcendental bliss; pürëava-
full of; lakñaëam-characteristic; viçeñaëa-dvayam-two modifiers; vidheyäyäh-of the predicate;
mitratäyäh-of the friendship; eva-certainly; tat-tat-bhävam-various status; sädhayati-substantiates;
iti-thus; tat-of that; eka-one; artha-meaning; pravåttam-established; sanätanatvam-eternality;
tasyäh-of that friendship; tat-bhävam-that condition; sädhayet-may establish; kim ca-
furthermore; atra-here; mitram iti-the word "mitram"; käla-time; viçeña-specific; yoga-contact;
nirdeça-indication; abhävät-because of the lack; käla-time; sämänyam-in general; eva-certainly;
bhajate-is meant; tatah-therefore; ca-also; tasya-of that; mitratä-by friendship; lakñaëasya-
characterized; vidheyasya-of the predicate; käla-traya-in all three phases of time (past, present, and
future); avasthayitvam-condition; spañöam-is clearly established; käla-antara-asaïjanam-limited to a
specific period of time; tu-but; kañöam-a meaning difficult to accept; atra-here; ca-also; uttarayoh-
arthayoù-of the two meanings; çré-kåñëasya-of Çré Kåñëa; sanätanatve-when there is eternality;
çabda-labdhe-expressed in this statement; sati-there is (indication of a locative abslute); tadéya-
matré-matam-of those who have attained friendship with Him; parikaraëam-of the associates; api-
also; sanätanatvam-eternality; na-not; asambhavam-unlikely; api-also; çré-rukmiëé-prabhåténäm-of
the great devotees beginning with Queen Rukmini;tathä-in the same way; darçanät-because it may
be seen.

   In this verse the word "bhägyam" (good fortune) does not refer to the ordinary auspicious
situation created by ordinary pious activities. The transcendental good fortune described in this
verse was obtained by receiving the indescribable causeless mercy of Çré Kåñëa. We may also note
that the word "bhägyam" is repeated twice to indicate the limitless extent of that good-fortune.
   In the second part of the verse, the subject "brahma" refers to Çré Kåñëa. The subject is modified
by the words "pürëam" (complete), "paramänandam" (the supreme bliss), and "sanätanam" (eternal).
The predicate is "mitram" (friend). The adjective "sanätana" (eternal) may be understood to modify
either "brahma" (the Absolute Truth), or "mitram" (friend). In this way the construction may be
interpreted: "The eternal Absolute Truth is the friend of the inhabitants of Vrajabhümi" or it may
also be interpreted: "The Absolute Truth is the eternal friend of the inhabitants of Vrajabhümi."
An example of this may be seen in the sentence "manoramaà suvarëam idaà kuëòalaà jätam",
where the adjective "manoramam" (beautiful) may be understood to modify either "suvarëam"

(gold), or "kundalam" (earring). Interpreted in the first way, the sentence may be translated: "This
earring is fashioned from beautiful gold", and interpreted in the second way the sentence may be
translated: "This golden earring is beautiful". Both inerpretations are possible.
   In this verse both interpretations may be accepted simultaneously, and "sanätanam" may modify
both "brahma" (the Absolute Truth) and "mitram" (friend) at the same time. Therefore we may say
that "Çré Kåñëa is the eternal Absolute Truth", and we may also say that Çré Kåñëa, the Absolute
Truth is the eternal friend of the inhabitants of Vrajabhümi". If we wish to completely reject the
second interpretation, and say that Çré Kåñëa is the eternal Absolute Truth, and He is only
temporarily the friend of the inhabitants of Vrajabhümi", we will create an interpretation that is
hard for a reasonable person to accept. For this reason we may understand that this verse (by using
the phrase "mitaà sanätanam") affirms that the inhabitants of Vrajabhümi are the eternal
associates of Çré Kåñëa just as Rukmiëé and the other intimate associates of the Lord are. Their
relationship continuously exists in all three phases of time (past, present, and future).

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.139
records.text:
Text 1


  aho astu tävad eñäà nityam eva çré-kåñëa-maitré-paramänandam anubhävatäm bhägyam,
sampraty asmäkam api tat kim api jätam ity äha

eñäà tu bhägya-mahimäcyuta tävad astam
  ekädaçaiva hi vayaà bata bhüri-bhägäù
etad-dhåñéka-casakair asakåt pibämaù
  sarvädayo 'ìghry-udaja-madhv-amåtäsavaà te

  aho-Oh!; astu-there may be; tävat-in that way; eñäm-of them; nityam-eternal; eva-certainly; çré-
kåñëa-of Çré Kåñëa; maitré-of the friendship; parama-anandam-transcendental bliss; anubhävatäm-
experiencing; bhägyam-good fortune; samprati-at the present moment; asmäkam-of us; api-also; tat-
that; kim-api-somewhat; jätam-produced; iti-thus; äha-he says; eñäm-of these residents of
Våndävana; tu-indeed; bhägya-mahima-the glories of their good fortune; acyuta-O infallible Lord;
tavad-as much as; astam-it may be; ekadasa-the presiding deities of the senses such as Candra, etc.;
eva-certainly; hi-indeed; vayam-myself, Lord Brahma; bata-oh; bhuri-bhagah-greatly fortunate; etat-
hrsika-casakaih-through the vessels of the senses; asakrt-always; pibamah-we drink; sarva-adayah-
the deities headed by Sarva (Siva), etc.; anghri-udaja-of the lotus feet; madhu-sweet; amrta-asavam-
the nectar; te-Your.

   After describing the good fortune of the residents of Vrajabhümi, who are able to experience the
transcendental bliss of eternal friendship with Çré Kåñëa, Brahmä describes the auspicious
condition that is attained even by him and the other demigods, Brahmä says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.14.33):

  "O infallible Lord, although the good-fortune of these inhabitants of Vrajabhümi is beyond
compare, even the demigods, such as Çiva, Candra, and myself have become greatly fortunate, for
we always drink through our senses the honey-like nectar of Your lotus feet."*


Text 2


   eka akhaëòita nityeti yävat, sa bhägya-mahimä bhägya-mähätmyam eñäà tävad astam samprati
sarvädayaù daça-dikpäla-devatä eva vayaà bhüri-bhägäù. parama-bhaktatvät tesu mukhyatväc ca
sarvädayaù ity uktam. bhüri-bhägatvam eva darçayati håñéka-cäsakaiù cakñur-ädi-lakñaëa-päna-
patraiù kåtvä vayam apy etat säkñäd eva yathä syät tathä te tava aìghry-udaja-madhv-amåtäsavam
asakåt punaù punar ihägatya pibämaù iti. caraëa-saundaryädikam eväti-manohäratvän madhv-
äditayä tridhäpi rüpitaà samähära-dvandvena. etat iti cäsyaiva va viçeñaëam. atra tuñyatu-nyäyena
çré-vraja-väsinäà präkåta-dehitva mato 'pi teñäà käraëair devatä-kaåtåka-bhogo na yujyate, asya ca
nityatvät ity atra çré-çaìkaräcäryeëa ca käraëa-pakñasyaiva hi devatä, na bhoktå-pakñasya ity
ätmana eva bhoktåtva-nirdharaëät.

   eka-the word "eka"; akhaëòita-unbroken; nitya-eternal; iti-thus; yävat-to that extent; saù-that;
bhägya-of the good fortune; mahimä-glory; bhägya-of the good fortune; mähätmyam-glorification;
eñäm-of them; tävat-as much as; astam-it may be; sampriti-at the present moment; sarva-adayaù-the
dieties headed by Çiva; daça-ten; dik-päla-protecting the directions; devatäh-demigods; eva-
certainly; vayam-we; bhüri-bhägäù-greatly fortunate; parama-bhaktatvät-because of great devotion;
tesu-among them; mukhyatvät-primarily; ca-also; sarvä-dayaù-the word "sarvädayaù"; iti-thus;
uktam-is said; bhüri-bhägatvam-great good fortune; eva-certainly; darçayati-he reveals; håñéka-
cäsakaiù-through the vessels of the senses; cakñuh-the eyes; ädi-beginning with; lakñaëa-
characterized by; päna-patraiù-with the drinking vessels; kåtvä-having done; vayam-we; api-also;
etat-this; säkñät-directly; eva-certainly; yathä-just as; syät-may be; tathä-in the same way; te-the
word "te"; tava-means "Your"; aìghri-udaja-of the lotus feet; madu-sweet; amåta-asavam-nectar;
asakåt-always; punaù-again; punaù-and again; iha-here; agatya-having arrived; pibämaù-we drink;
iti-thus; caraëa-of the lotus feet; saundarya-beauty; adikam-great; eva-certainly; ati-manohäratvät-
because of great beauty; madhu-äditayä-with sweetness and other good qualities; trdha-in three
ways; api-also; rüpitam-described; samähära-dvandvena-by a samahara-dvandva-samasa; eteat-the
word "etat"; iti-thus; ca-also; asya-of that; e
va-certainly; va-or; viçeñaëam-modifying; atra-here; tuñyatu-nyäyena-the example of "may he be
pleased"; çré-vraja-väsinäm-of the inhabitants of Vrajabhumi; präkåta-dehatva-matah-the opinion of
possessing material forms; api-even; teñäm-of them; käraëaih-with the senses; devatä-kaåtåka-of the
demigods; bhogah-enjoyment; na-not; yujyate-is engaged; asya-of Him; ca-also; nityatvät-because of
eternality; iti-thus; atra-here; çré-çaìkara-acäryeëa-by Çrépada Çankaracarya; ca-also; käraëa-
pakñasya-of the senses; eva-certainly; hi-indeed; devatä-the demigods; na-not; bhoktå-pakñasya-of
the enjoyers; iti-thus; ätmanah-of the self; eva-certainly; bhoktåtva-the condition of being the
enjoyer; nirdharaëät-because of demonstration.

  In this verse the word "eka" means "unbroken" or "eternal", and the word "bhägya-mahimä" means

"the glorification of their good-fortune". "Sarvädayaù" means "the demigods (headed by Çiva) in
charge of the ten directions". We may note that Lord Çiva is put at the head of all demigods because
he is the greatest devotee of Lord Kåñëa. The word "bhüri-bhägyäù" indicates the good-fortune
experienced by these demigods. The word "håñéka-casakaiù" means "with the drinking vessels of the
eyes and the other senses" and the word "te" means "Your". In the last part of the verse, Brahmä
says: "We always drink the nectar of Your lotus feet". By using the three words "madu", "amåta" and
"asavam" which all mean "nectar", the swetness and beauty of the Lord's lotus feet is described.
These three words form a samähära-samäsa in order to indicate the limitless variety and amount of
nectar present in the Lord's lotus feet. We may also note that the demonstrative pronoun "etat"
(this) refers to the nectar of Lord Kåñëa's lotu feet.
   Someone may argue that because the demigods are the administrators of the affairs of the
material senses of the living entities within the material world, we may conclude that they
perceived the Lord through the senses of the residents of Vrajabhümi, and this is what is meant by
the phrase "håñéka-casakaiù pibämaù". This cannot be the case, for the inhabitants of Vrajabhümi
all have eternal spiritual forms, not under the jurisdiction of the material demigods. But even if we
accept that the inhabitants of Vrajabhümi had material senses, still, the demigods do not enjoy the
activities of the senses of conditioned souls, or directly experience through those senses. This is
confirmed by Çrépäda Çaìkaräcärya in his commentary on Vedänta-sütra (2.4.17) in the following
words:

   "The demigods are administrators of the the conditioned souls' senses. Only the individual living
entities directly experience through their senses. The administrative demigods do not experience
through the living entities senses."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.140
records.text:
ataù pürvam api tad astu me nätha sa bhüri-bhägäù ity ädinä yat prärthitam, tad etad evety äha
tad bhüri-bhägyam iha janma kim apy aöavyäà
  yad gokule 'pi katamäìghri-rajo-'bhiñekam yaj-jévitam tu nikhilaà bhagavän mukundas
  tv adyäpi yat-pada-rajaù çruti-mågyam eva

  anena çré-gokula-jaàa-läbhäd eva tava päda-niñeva-lakñaëo yäcito bhüri-bhägäù sadaiva setsyatéti
sücitam. tasmät teñäà bhäga-dheyaà kià varëanéyam.

  ataù pürvam-before this; api-also; tat astu me nätha sa bhüri-bhägäù iti ädinä-in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.14.30:
tad astu me nätha sa bhüri-bhägo
  bhave 'tra vänyatra tu vä tiraçcäm yenäham eko 'pi bhavaj-janänäà
  bhütvä néseve tava päda-pallavam

yat-what; prärthitam-is prayed for; tat etat-that; eva-certainly; iti-thus; äha-he says; tat-therefore;
bhuri-bhagyam-greatly fortunate; iha-here; janma-birth; kim api-moreover; atavyam-in the forest of
Våndävana; yat-which; gokule-in Gokula; api-even; katama-which of many; anghri-raja-by the dust

of the feet; abhisekam-smeared; yat-whose; jivitam-life; tu-indeed; nikhilam-whole; bhagavan-the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; mukundah-Mukunda; tu-indeed; adya api-even til now; yat-
whose; pada-rajah-dust of the feet; sruti-mrgyam-sought by the Vedas; eva-certainly; anena-by this;
çré-gokula-in Gokula; janma-birth; läbhät-from the attainment; eva-certainly; tava-Your; päda-lotus
feet; ñeva-the service; lakñaëah-characterized by; yäcitah-requested; bhüri-bhägäù-great good
fortune; sada-always; eva-certainly; setsyati-may be; sücitam-clearly; tasmät-therefore; teñäm-of
them; bhäga-of good fortune; dheyam-gift; kim-what; varëanéyam-is able to be described.

  The exalted position of the inhabitants of Gokula is confirmed in the following appeal spoken by
Lord Brahmä to Çré Kåñëa (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.30-34):

    "Therefore, my Lord, either in this life or wherever I may take my birth, even as an animal or a
bird, I pray that I may be so fortunate that I may be counted as one of Your devotees. Wherever I
may be, I pray that I may be engaged in the devotional service of Your lotus feet."*
   "My dear Lord, I am therefore not interested in either material opulences or liberation. I am most
humbly praying at Your lotus feet for You to please give me any sort of birth within this Våndävana
forest so that I may be able to be favored by the dust of the feet of some of the devotees of
Våndävana. Even if I am given the chance to grow just as the humble grass in this land, that will be
a glorious birth for me. But if I am not so fortunate to take birth within the forest of Våndävana, I
beg to be allowed to take birth outside the immediate area of Våndävana so that when the devotees
go out they will walk over me. Even that would be a great fortune for me. I am just aspiring for a
birth in which I will be smeared by the dust of the devotees' feet.*
   "I can see that everyone here is simply full of Kåñëa consciousness; they do not know anything
but Mukunda. All the Vedas are indeed searching after the lotus feet of Kåñëa."*

   In these verses Brahmä requests a birth within the area of Våndävana, because in that way he
may attain the good fortune of eternal devotional service to the lotus feet of Çré Kåñëa. In these
verses it is as if Brahmä had asked: "What can compare to the good-fortune of taking birth within
the area of Våndävana?" By glorifying the land and residents of Våndävana in this way, Brahmä
affirms that the residents of Våndävana are the eternal associates of Çré Kåñëa.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.141
records.text:
Text 1


  aho yeñäà bhaktyä bhavän api nityam åëitäm äpanno yeñu ruddha iväste ity äha

eñäà ghoña-niväsinäm uta bhavän kim deva räteti naç
  ceto viçva-phalät phalaà tvad-aparaà kuträpy ayam muhyati
sad-veñäd iva pütanäpi sa-kulä tväm eva deväpitä
  yad-dhämärtha-suhåt-priyätma-tanaya-pränäçayäs tvat-kåte

   aho-Oh; yeñäm-of whom; bhaktyä-with devotion; bhavän-Your Lordship; api-also; nityam-
eternally; åëitäm-the condition of a debtor; äpannah-have attained; yeñu-among whom; ruddhah-
obstructed; iva-as it were; aste-remain; iti-thus; äha-He says; eñäm-to these; ghoña-niväsinäm-
residents of Våndävana; uta-indeed; bhavän-Your Lordship; kim-what; deva-O Lord; räta-will give;
iti-considering thus; naù-my; cetaù-mind; viçva-phalät-from the supreme source of all benedictions;
phalam-reward; tvat-aparam-other than You; kutra-where; api-indeed; ayam-this; muhyati-
bewilders; sat-veñät-by dressing as Your devotee; iva-indeed; pütanä-Pütanä; api-even; sa-kulä-along
with other members of her family such s Aghäsura; tvam-You; eva-certainly; deva-O Lord; apitä-
obtained; yat-whose; dhäma-homes; artha-wealth; suhåt-friends; priya-dear ones; ätmä-bodies;
tanaya-children; präëä-lives; äçayaù-thoughts; tvat-kåte-dedicated to You.

  In the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.35), Brahmä explains that Çré Kåñëa is greatly
indebted to the residents of Våndävana for their pure devotional service. Because of this unpayable
debt, Çré Kåñëa thinks He must eternally remain among the residents of Våndävana and accept
their devotional service. Brahmä says:

   "My Lord, sometimes I am puzzled as to how Your Lordship will be able to repay, in gratitude, the
devotional service of these residents of Våndävana. Although I know that You are the supreme
source of all benediction, I am puzzled to know how You will be able to repay all the service that
You are receiving from these residents of Våndävana. I think of how You are so kind, so
magnanimous, that even Pütänä, who came to cheat You by dressing herself as a very affectionate
mother, was awarded liberation and the actual post of a mother. And other demons belonging to
the same family, such as Aghäsura and Bakäsura, were also favored with liberation. Under the
circumstances, I am puzzled. These residents of Våndävana have given You everything: their homes,
wealth, friends, dear ones, bodies, children, lives and minds. Everything is being utilized for Your
purpose. So how will You be able to repay their debt? You have already given Yourself to Pütanä! I
surmise that You shall ever remain a debtor to the residents f Våndävana, being unable to repay
their loving service."*


Text 2


  satäm çuddha-cittänäà dhatry-ädi-janänäm iva veñät. tasmät anädi-kalpa-paramparägatatväd
avatärata evaivaà präptatvena tair ekair eva bhakti-ruddhatvät sanätanaà mitram ity evam
sädhüktam. tataç ca tad-bhüri-bhägyam ity ädikam api sädhv eva prärthitam iti bhävaù.

   satäm-the word "satäm"; çuddha-cittänäm-with pure hearts; dhatri-of the mother; ädi-beginning
with; janänäm-of the residents of Våndävana; iva-indeed; veñät-by external appearance; tasmät-
from that; anädi-without beginning; kalpa-of kalpas; parampara-series; agatatvät-because of the
passing; avatäratah-from the incarnations; eva-certainly; evam-in this way; präptatvena-by
attainment; taih-by them; ekaih-one by one; eva-certainly; bhakti-of devotional service; ruddhatvät-
because of being filled; sanätanam-eternal; mitram-friend; iti-thus; evam-in this way; sädhu-
properly; uktam-said; tatah-therefore; ca-also; tat-bhüri-bhägyam iti ädikam-Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.14.34; api-also; çadhu-properly; eva-certainly; prärthitam-requested; iti-thus; bhävaù-the

meaning.

  In this verse the word "sad-veñät" means "appearing like Mother Yaçodä and the other pure-
hearted devotees of Våndävana". Because each of the residents of Våndävana loves Çré Kåñëa with
great intensity, therefore they have attained His association from time immemorial. Çré Kåñëa is
their eternal friend (sanätanaà mitram) and therefore they are extremely fortunate (tad-bhüri-
bhägyam). By praying for a birth in the land of Våndävana, Brahmä has spoken properly. This is a
very good request.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.142
records.text:
Text 1


  nanv eñäà manuñyäntaravad rägädikaà dåçyate, kathaà tarhi svayaà bhagavato nitya-
parikaratvam? tatra kaimutyenäha

tävad rägädayaù stenäs
  tävat kärä-gåhaà gåham
tävan moho 'ìghri-nigaòo
  yävat kåñëa na te janäù

  nanu-is it not so?; eñäm-of them; manuñya-antara-vat-just like ordinary conditioned souls; räga-
adikam-material attachments; dåçyate-are observed; katham-how is it possible; tarhi-then; svayam
bhagavatah-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; nitya-parikaratvam-the condition of being
eternal associates; tatra-in this connection; kaimutyena-how much more so; aha-he says; tävat-so
long; räga-ädayaù-material attachments and so on; stenäù-thieves; tävat-so long; kärä-gåham-a
prison house; gåham-one's home; tävat-so long; mohaù-illusion; aìghri-nigaòaù-a fetter on the legs;
yävat-as long as; kåñëa-O my dear Lord Kåñëa; na-are not; te-Your; janäù-devotees.

   Someone may object, saying that the residents of Våndävana are ordinary householders and
conditioned souls, for they manifest all the ordinary material attachments to family and home that
are manifested by ordinary creatures. They are not great sages or renounced sannyäsés. How is it
possible, therefore, that they are eternal assocites of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
   In order to answer this objection, Brahmä replies that because the residents of Våndävana are
immersed in love for Kåñëa, they cannot be at all encumbered by material desires or attachments as
the conditioned souls are. Brahmä explains this in the next verse, where he contrasts the condition
of the materially contaminated living entities with that of the pure devotees of Våndävana. Brahmä
says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.36):

   "My Lord, I can understand that the superexcellent service of the residents of Våndävana is due
to their engaging all natural instincts in Your service. It is said that attachments for material
objects are like thieves which steal away the valuable time of the living entity. The material

illusions of such attached persons are like shackles which bind him by the legs to his house and
paraphernalia which become no more than a prisonhouse for him. But this is only the case for
persons who are not in Kåñëa consciousness. In the case of the residents of Våndävana, such
obstructions as attachment for hearth and home are non-existent. Because their attachment has
been converted to You, and their home has been converted into a temple because You are always
there, and because they have forgotten everything for Your sake, there is no impediment. For a
Kåñëa conscious person, there is no such thing as impediments in hearth and home. Nor is there
illusion."*


Text 2


  stenaù puruña-sära-häraù. anyeñäà präkåta-janänäm api tävat eva rägädayaù caurädayo bhavanti,
yävat te janäs te tava na bhavanti, sarvato-bhävena tvayy ätmänaà na samarpayanti, samarpite
cätmani teñäà rägädayo 'pi tvan-niñöhä eveti rägädénäà präkåtatväbhävän na cauräditvam, praty
uta paramänandarüpatvam evety arthaù.

   stenaù-the word "stenah; puruña-sära-häraù-means "stealing that which is of value to the living
entities; anyeñäm-of others; präkåta-materialistic; janänäm-persons; api-also; tävat-to that extent;
eva-certainly; räga-adayaù-material attachments; caura-adayah-thieves; bhavanti-are; yävat-as long;
te-they; janäh-devotees; sarvatah-bhävena-in all respects; tvayi-to You; ätmänam-themselves; na-do
not; samarpayanti-offer; samarpite-offered; ca-and; atmani-when the self; teñäm-of them; räga-
adayah-material attachments; präkrtatva-abhavät-because of being non-material; na-not; caura-adi-
tvam-the condition of being thieves; prati uta-on the contrary; parama-transcendental; ananda-
bliss; rüpatvam-consisting of; eva-certainly; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.

   In this verse Brahmä explains that as long as one does not completely surrender himself at the
lotus feet of Lord Kåñëa, or in other words, as long as one remains a non-devotee materialist, his
material attachments will act as thieves (stenaù), stealing away the valuable opportunity offered in
the human form of life. On the other hand, if one becomes devoted to Lord Kåñëa, and offers
himself with love at the Lord's lotus feet, then his so-called material attachments to home and
hearth do not remain material in nature, but become spiritualized because of being engaged in the
Lord's service in Kåñëa consciousness. Such so-called material attachments do not act as thieves,
but on the contrary, they are a source of transcendental happiness for the devotees.


Text 3


tathaiva prärthitaà çré-prahlädena

yä prétir avivekänäà
  viñayeñv anapäyiné
tvam anusmarataù sä me

  hådayän mäpasarpatu iti.

  tatha-in the same way; prärthitam-prayed; çré-prahladena-by Prahläda Mahäräja; yä-which; prétih-
attachment; avivekänäm-of the foolish conditioned souls; viñayeñu-in the objects of the senses;
anapäyiné-constant; tvam-You; anusmarataù-remembering; sä-that; me-myu; hådayät-from the
heart; ma-may not; apasarpatu-appear; iti-thus.

  This is described by Prahläda Mahäräja in the following prayer (Viñëu Puräëa 1.20.19):

  "The foolish materialists take great delight in the contact of the senses with the sense-objects. O
Lord, I pray that that same attachment may be manifested towards You. That I may always
remember You and perceive You with my senses. May the attachment to You never leave my
heart."*


Text 4


  ato yadi sädhakänäm eva värtä, tadä kià vaktavyam, nityam eva tädåça-priyatvena satäà çré-
gokula-väsinäm eveti. ittham evoktam

iti nandädayo gopäù
   kåñëa-räma-kathäà mudä
kurvanto ramamämëäç ca
   nävindan bhava-vedanäm

  atah-therefore; yadi-if; sädhakänäm-of the great devotees who have completely surrendered to
Lord Kåñëa; eva-certainly; värtä-description; tadä-then; kim-what?; vaktavyam-more need be said;
nityam-eternally; eva-certainly; tädåça-priyatvena-dear to Lord Kåñëa; satäm-of the saintly
devotees; çré-gokula-väsinäm-of the residents of Gokula; eva-certainly; iti-thus; ittham-in this way;
eva-certainly; uktam-it is said; iti-in this way; nanda-ädayaù-all the cowherd men, headed by Nanda
Mahäräja; gopäù-cowherd men; kåñëa-räma-kathäm-narration of incidents in connection with
Bhagavän Kåñëa and Räma; mudä-in great transcendental pleasure; kurvantaù-doing that;
ramamäëaù ca-enjoyed life and increased their affection for Kåñëa; na-not; avindan-perceived;
bhava-vedanäm-the tribulations of material existence.

   If Prahläda Mahäräja and other great devotees who have completely surrendered to the Supreme
Lord may remain in family life, apparently attached to family and home, then why should anyone
think that simply because the residents of Våndävana are householders, and not renounced
sannyäsés, therefore they cannot be eternal associates of the Lord? The residents of Våndävana are
eternally dear to Lord Kåñëa, and they are perfectly situated in the highest platform of spiritual
happiness free from all contact of the material energy. This is described in the following statement
of Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.11.58):

  "In this way all the cowherd men, headed by Nanda Mahäräja, enjoyed topics about the pastimes

of Kåñëa and Balaräma with great transcendental pleasure, and they could not even perceive
material tribulations."*


Text 5


   bhavanty asminn iti bhävaù prapaïcaù. yadyapi prapaïca-janeñv abhivyaktas te tathäpi tat-
sambandhiné yä vedana viñaya-duùkhädi-jïänaà tam nävindan ity arthaù. vedana jïäna-péòayoù
iti koça-jïaù.

  bhavanti-there are; asmin-in this; iti-thus; bhävaù-the word "bhavah"; prapaïcaù-means
"material existence"; yadyapi-although; prapaïca-janeñu-among the conditioned souls; abhivyaktah-
manifested; te-they; tathäpi-nevertheless; tat-sambandhiné-in relation to that; yä-which; vedana-
the word "vedana"; viñaya-from the material sense-objects; duùkha-adi-happiness and distress;
jïänam-awareness; tam-that; na-did not; avindan-find; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; vedana-the
word "vedana"; jïäna-means "knowledge; péòayoù-or "suffering"; iti-thus; koça-jïaù-according to the
dictionary definition.

  In this verse the word "bhava" means "material existence", and "vedana" means "awareness of
material happiness and distress". We may note in this regard that the dictionary definition of
"vedana" is:

   "The word 'vedana' means 1. knowledge, or 2. suffering".

   Although apparently situated in the material world as ordinary conditioned souls, the residents
of Våndävana were completely free from the bondage of material existence. They did not suffer any
of the distresses of material life.


Sarva-samvädiné Comment (Anucchedas 139-142)


Text 1


tad etam api paripätim paçcäd vidhäyäha

eñäà tu bhägya-mahimacyuta tävad astam
  ekädaçaiva hi vayaà bata bhüri-bhägäù
etad-dhåñéka-cañakair asakåt pibämaù
  çarvädayo 'ìghry-udaja-madhv-amåtäsavaà te

  tat-therefore; etat-this; api-also; paripätim-arrangement; paçcät-afterwards; vidhäya-giving; äha-
he said; eñäm-of these residents of Våndävana; tu-indeed; bhägya-mahima-the glories of their good
fortune; acyuta-O infallible Lord; tävad-as much as; astam-it may be; ekädaça-the presiding deities

of the senses such as Candra, etc.; eva-certainly; hi-indeed; vayam-myself, Lord Brahmä; bata-oh;
bhüri-bhägäù-greatly fortunate; etat-håçika-casakaiù-through the vessels of the senses; asakåt-
always; pibämaù-we drink; çarva-ädayaù-the deities headed by Çarva (Çiva), etc.; aìghri-udaja-of
the lotus feet; madhu-sweet; amåta-asavam-the nectar; te-Your.

  Brahmä explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.33-36):

   "My dear Lord, no one can actually appreciate the good fortune of these residents of Våndävana.
We are all demigods, controlling deities of the various senses of the living entities, and we are proud
of enjoying such privileges, but actually there is no comparison between our position and the
position of these fortunate residents of Våndävana becasue they are actually relishing Your
presence and enjoying Your association by dint of their activities. We may be proud of being
controllers of the senses, but here the residents of Våndävana are so transcendental that they are
not under our control. Actually they are enjoying the senses through service to You. I shall
therefore consider myself fortunate to be given a chance to take birth in this land of Våndävana in
any of my future lives."*


Text 2


tad bhüri-bhägyam iha janma kim apy aöavyäà
  yad gokule 'pi katamäìghri-rajobhiñekam
yaj-jévitam tu nikhilaà bhagavan mukundas
  tv adyäpi yat-pada-rajaù çruti-mågyam eva

  tat-therefore; bhüri-bhägyam-greatly fortunate; iha-here; janma-birth; kim api-moreover;
aöavyäm-in the forest of Våndävana; yat-which; gokule-in Gokula; api-even; katama-which of
many; aìghri-rajaù-bythe dust of the feet; abhiñekam-smeared; yat-whose; jévitam-life; tu-indeed;
nikhilam-whole; bhagavan-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; mukundaù-Mukunda; tu-indeed;
adya api-even til now; yat-whose; pada-rajaù-dust of the feet; çruti-mågyam-sought by the Vedas;
eva-certainly.

   My dear Lord, I am therefore not interested in either material opulences or liberation. I am most
humbly praying at Your lotus feet for You to please give mem any sort of birth within this
Våndävana forest so that I may be able to be favored by the dust of the feet of some of the devotees
of Våndävana. Even if I am given the chance to grow just as the humble grass in this land, that will
be a glorious birth for me. But if I am not so fortunate to take birth within the forest of Våndävana,
I beg to be allowed to take birth outside the immediate area of Våndävana so that when the
devotees go out they will walk over me. Even that would be a great fortune for me. I am just aspiring
for a birth in which I will be smeared by the dust of the devotees' feet.*
   "I can see that everyone here is simply full of Kåñëa consciousness; they do not know anything
but Mukunda. All the Vedas are indeed searching after the lotus feet of Kåñëa."*

Text 3


   ity atra yatravätérëäh çré-bhagavän tatra iha çré-mathurä-maëòale, tatra apy aöavyäm çré-
våndävane, taträpi çré-gokule. katham-bhütaà janma? atra öékä ca gokula-väsinäà madhye 'pi
'katamasya' yasya kasyäpy 'aìghri-rajasäbhiñekäù' yasmims tat ity eñä.

   iti-thus; atra-here; yatra-where; avatérëaù-descended; çré-bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of
Godhead; tatra-there; iha-here; çré-mathurä-maëòale-in the district of Mathurä; tatra-there; api-
also; aöavyäm-in the forest; çré-våndävane-in Våndävana; tatra-there; api-also; çré-gokule-in Gokula;
katham-bhütam-what kind?; janma-of birth; atra-here; öékä-the commentary of Çrédhara Svämé; ca-
also; gokula-väsinäm-of the residents of Gokula; madhye-in the midst; api-also; katamasya-of
someone; yasya-of whom; kasya-of a certain; api-even; aìghri-of the lotus feet; rajasä-by the dust;
abhiñekaù-sprinkling; yasmin-in which; tat-that; iti-thus; eñä-the commentary.

  In this verse the word "iha" (here) means "in the district of Mathurä, where the Supreme
Personality of Godhead descended. "Apy aöavyäà çré-gokule" means "in the forest of Våndävana".
What kind of birth does Brahmä pray to get? Çrédhara Svämé explains in his commentary:

   "Brahmä prays for any kind of birth in Våndävana where he may be able to become sprinkled by
the dust of the lotus feet of the residents of Våndävana."


Text 4


eñäà ghoña-niväsinäm uta bhavän kim deva räteti naç
  ceto viçva-phalät phalaà tvad-aparaà kuträpy ayam muhyati
sad-veñäd iva pütanäpi sa-kulä tväm eva deväpitä
  yad-dhämärtha-suhåt-priyätma-tanaya-pränäçayäs tvat-kåte

ity atra rätä dätä; tvat tvattaù äyat itas tato gacchat.

   eñäm-to these; ghoña-niväsinäm-residents of Våndävana; uta-indeed; bhavän-Your Lordship; kim-
what; deva-O Lord; räta-will give; iti-considering thus; naù-my; cetaù-mind; viçva-phalät-from the
supreme source of all benedictions; phalam-reward; tvat-aparam-other than You; kutra-where; api-
indeed; ayam-this; muhyati-bewilders; sat-veñät-by dressing as Your devotee; iva-indeed; pütanä-
Pütanä; api-even; sa-kulä-along with other members of her family such as Aghäsura; tvam-You; eva-
certainly; deva-O Lord; apitä-obtained; yat-whose; dhäma-homes; artha-wealth; suhåt-friends; priya-
dear ones; ätmä-bodies; tanaya-children; präëä-lives; äçayaù-thoughts; tvat-kåte-dedicated to You;
iti-thus; atra-here; rätä-the word "rätä"; dätä-means "giver; tvat-the word "tvat"; tvattaù-means
"from you"; äyat-the word "äyat"; itaù-from there; tataù-from there; gacchat-going.

  My Lord, sometimes I am puzzled as to how Your Lorship will be able to repay, in gratitude, the
devotional service of these residents of Våndävana. Although I know that You are the supreme

source of all benediction, I am puzzled to know how You will be able to repay all the service that
You are receiving from these residents of Våndävana. I think of how You are so kind, so
magnanimous, that even Pütanä, who came to cheat You by dressing herself as a very affectionate
mother, was awarded liberation and the actual post of a mother. And other demons belonging to
the same family, such as Aghäsura and Bakäsura, were also favored with liberation. Under the
circumstances, I am puzzled. These residents of Våndävana have given You everything: their bodies,
their minds, their love, their homes. Everything is being utilized for Your purpose. So how will You
be able to repay their debt? You have already given Yourself to Pütanä! I surmise that You shall
ever remain a debtor to the residents of Våndävana, being unableto repay their loving service."*

  In this verse "ratä" means "giver" and "tvat" means "from You".


Text 5


tävad rägädayaù stenäs
  tävat kärä-gåhaà gåham
tävan moho 'ìghri-nigaòo
  yävat kåñëa na te janäù

  tävat-so long; räga-ädayaù-material attachments and so on; stenäù-thieves; tävat-so long; kärä-
gåham-a prison house; gåham-one's home; tävat-so long; mohaù-illusion; aìghri-nigaòaù-a fetter on
the legs; yävat-as long as; kåñëa-O my dear Lord Kåñëa; na-are not; te-Your; janäù-devotees.

   My Lord, I can understand that the superexcellent service of the residents of Våndävana is due to
their spontaneously engaging all natural instincts in Your service. It is said that attachment for
material objects and home is due to illusion, which makes a living entity conditioned in the
material world. But this is only the case for persons who are not in Kåñëa consciousness. In the case
of the residents of Våndävana, such obstructions, as attachment to hearth and home, are
nonexistent. Because their attachment has been converted unto You, and their home has been
converted into a temple because You are always there, and because they have forgotten everything
for Your sake, there is no impediment. For a Kåñëa conscious person, there is no such thing as
impediments in hearth and home. Nor is there illusion.*


Text 6


antar-gåha-gatäù käçcid
  gopyo 'labdha-vinirgamäù
kåñëaà tad-bhavanä-yuktä
  dadhyur milita-locanäù

  antaù-within; gåha-the house; gatäù-gone; käçcit-some; gopyaù-gopés; alabdha-without attaining;

vinirgamäù-exit; kåñëam-Kåñëa; tat-bhavanä-yuktäù-meditating on; dadhyuh-milita-locanäù-closed
their eyes.

  This is also described in the following verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.9-16):

  "Some of the gopés were factually detained from going to Kåñëa by their husbands and were
locked up by force within their rooms. Being unable to go to Kåñëa, they began to meditate upon
His transcendental form by closing their eyes. They already had the form of Kåñëa within their
minds.*


Text 7


duùsaha-preñöha-viraha-
  tévra-täpa-dhutäçubhaù
dhyäna-praptäcyutäçleña-
  nirvåtyä kñéëa-maìgaläù

  duùsaha-difficult to bear; preñöha-from the beloved; viraha-separation; tévra-sever; täpa-by pain;
dhuta-cleansed; açubhaù-all inauspicious things; dhyäna-meditation; prapta-attained; acyuta-of the
infallible Personality of Godhead; açleña-of the embrace; nirvåtyä-by the happiness; kñéëa-
diminished; maìgaläù-auspicious reactions of material pious activities.

  "If they had been bound by fruitive action, they were fully freed from the reaction of karma by
constant meditation on Kåñëa. Their severe painful yearnings caused by their not being able to see
Kåñëa freed them from all sinful reactions, and their ecstacy of transcendental love for Kåñëa in His
absence was transcendental to all their reactions of material pious activities.*


Text 8


tam eva paramätmänaà
  jära-buddhyäpi saìgataù
juhur guëamayaà dehaà
  sadyaù prakñéëa-bandhanäù

   tam-Him; eva-certainly; parama-atmänam-the Supreme Soul; jära-of a paramour; buddhya-with
the conception; api-even; saìgataù-by the contact; juhuh-they abandoned; guëamayam-consisting
of the three modes of nature; deham-body; sadyaù-immediately; prakñéëa-bandhanäù-free from
bondage.

  "All the gopés who concentrated their minds on Kåñëa in the spirit of paramour love became fully
uncontaminated from all the fruitive reactions of material nature, and some of them immediately
gave up their material bodies developed under the three modes of material nature.*

Text 9


çré-parékñid uväca

kåñëaà viduù paraà käntaà
  na tu brahmatayä mune
guëa-pravähoparämäs
  täsäà guëa-ghiyäà katham

  çré-parékñit uväca-Mahäräja Parékñit said; kåñëam-Kåñëa; viduù-they understood; param-supreme;
käntam-lover; na-not; tu-but; brahmatayä-as the Supreme Personality of Godhead; mune-O sage;
guëa-praväha-uparämäh-free from the influence of the modes of material nature; täsäm-of them;
guëa-dhiyäm-with material conceptions; katham-how is it possible?

   "Mahäräja Parékñit heard Çukadeva Gosvämé explain the situation of the gopés who assembled
with Kåñëa in the räsa dance. When he heard that some of the gopés, simply by concentrating on
Kåñëa as their paramour, became fred from all contamination of material birth and death, he said:
The gopés did not know that Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. They accepted Him as a
beautiful boy and considered Him to be their paramour. So how was it possible for them to get freed
from the material condition just by thinking of a paramour?'*


Text 10


çré-çuka uväca

uktaà purästad etaà te
  caidyaù siddhià yathä gatäù
dviñann api håñékeçam
  kim utädhokñaja-priyaù

   çré-çukah uväca-Çré Çukadeva Gosvami said; uktam-explained; purästat-before; etam-this; te-to
you; caidyaù-Çiçupäla; siddhim-perfection; yathä-just as; gatäù-attained; dviñan-hating; api-
although; håñikeçam-Lord Kåñëa; kim uta-what to speak?; adhokñaja-of the Supreme Lord; priyaù-
the dear devotees.

  "On hearing this question of Mahäräja Parékñit, Çukadeva Gosvämé replied: My dear King, your
question is already answered, even before this incident.*
  "Çiçupäla was always envious of Kåñëa, and because of his envy Kåñëa killed him. Since Kåñëa is
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Çiçupäla gained salvation simply by seeing Him. If an envious
person can get salvation simply by concentrating his mind on Kåñëa, then what to speak of the
gopés who are so dear to Kåñëa and always thinking of Him in love? There must be some difference

between the enemies and the friends. If Kåñëa's enemies could get freed from material
contamination and become one with the Supreme, then certainly His dear friends like the gopés are
freed and with Him.*


Text 11


nåëäà niùçreyasärthäya
  vyaktir bhagavato nåpa
avyayasyäprameyasya
  nirguëasya gunätmanaù

  nåëäm-of the conditioned souls; niùçreyasa-arthäya-for the benefit; vyaktih-manifestation;
bhagavatah-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; nåpa-O king; avyayasya-imperishable;
aprameyasya-unlimited; nirguëasya-free from the modes of material nature; guna-atmanaù-the
origin of all qualities.

  "Kåñëa is not an ordinary person. He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, full of all spiritual
qualities. He appears in this material world out of His causeless mercy, in order to benedict the
conditioned souls, and whenever He appears, He appears as He is without change.*


Text 12


kämaà krodhaà bhayaà sneham
  aikyaà sauhådam eva ca
nityaà haräu vidadhato
  yänti tan-mäyatäm hi te

  kämam-lust; krodham-anger; bhayam-fear; sneham-love; aikyam-oneness; sauhådam-friendship;
eva-certainly; ca-also; nityam-eternally; haräu-in relation to Lord Kåñëa; vidadhatah-those who
place; yänti-attain; tat-mäyatäm-the same nature as His; hi-certainly; te-they.

  "If one somehow or other becomes attached to Kåñëa or attracted to Him, either because of His
beauty, quality, opulence, fame, strength, renunciation or knowledge, or even through lust, anger or
fear, or affection or friendship, then one's salvation and freedom from material contamination is
assured.*


Text 13


na caiva vismayaù käryo
  bhavatä bhagavaty aje

yogeçvareçvare kåñëe
  yata etad vimucyate.

   na-not; ca-also; eva-certainly; vismayaù-astonishment; käryah-result; bhavatä-by you; bhagavati-
in relation to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; aje-unborn; yoga-içvara-of the masters of the
yoga system; içvare-the controller; kåñëe-Lord Kåñëa; yatah-from which; etat-therefore; vimucyate-
liberated.

   "Rest assured that one attracted by Kåñëa attains liberation from material bondage because Kåñëa
is the transcendental master of all mystic power. There is nothiong surprising about this."*


   Note: The main text of the Sandarbha is resumed at this point.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.143
records.text:
Text 1


  tarhi kathaà gokule prapaïcavd bhänaà lokänäà bhavati taträha

prapaïcaà niñprapaïco 'pi
  viòambayasi bhü-tale
prapanna-janatänanda-
  sandohaà prathituà prabho

   tarhi-then; katham-how iis it; gokule-in Gokula; prapaïcavat-like the material world; bhänam-
appearance; lokänäm-of the residents; bhavatri-is; tatra-in this connection; aha-he says; prapaïcam-
material activities; niñprapaïcaù-not material; api-although; viòambayasi-You imitate; bhü-tale-on
the surface of the earth; prapanna-surrendered; janatä-of Your devotees; änanda-of the
transcendental bliss; sandoham-the volume; prathitum-to increase; prabho-O my Lord.

  Someone may say that if the residents of Våndävana are free from the bondage of material
existence, then why
do they seem like ordinary inhabitants of the material world. In order to answer this objection,
Brahmä explains that the appearance and activities of both Çré Kåñëa and the residents of
Våndävana are spiritual, only superficially do they appear to be material. Brahmä said (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.14.37):

   "My dear Lord Kåñëa, I can also understand that Your appearance as a small cowherd boy, a child
of the cowherd men, is not at all a material activity. You are so much obliged by their affection that
You are here to enthuse them with more loving service by Your transcendental presence. In
Våndävana there is no distinction between material and spiritual because everything is dedicated to
Your loving service. My dear Lord, Your Våndävana pastimes are simply to enthuse Your devotees.

If someone takes Your Våndävana pastimes to be material, he will be misled."*


Text 2


  prapaïcätéto 'pi tvam bhü-tale sthitam prapaïcaà viòambayasi svayam anena prastutena gokulea-
rüpeëänukaroñi. vastutas tu çré-gokula-rüpam idaà tava svarüpaà prapaïcavad eva bhäti. na tu
prapaïca-rüpam eveti tätparyam. tadvac ca bhänaà kim artham? taträha prapanna iti. tädåça-
laukikäkära-lélayaiva hi prapanna-jana-våndasya pramänando bhavatéty etad artham. tasmät
sädhüktam aho bhägyam.

  prapaïca-the mateiral world; atitah-beyond; api-although; tvam-You; bhu-tale-on the earth;
sthitam-situated; prapaïcam-the activities of ordinary creatures; vidambayasi-You imitate; svayam-
personally; anena-by this; prastutena-glorified; gokula-rupena-by the form of a cowherd boy in
Gokula; anukarosi-You imitate; vastuteh-in truth; tu-but; sri-gokula-rupam-form of a cowherd boy
in Gokula; idam-this; tava-Your; svarupam-original form; prapancavat-superficially appearing like
an ordinary person; eva-certainly; bhati-is manifest; na-not; tu-but; prapanca-comnposed of the five
material elements; rupam-form; eva-certainly; iti-thus; tatparyam-the meaning; tadvat-in that way;
ca-also; bhanam-appearance; kim artham-what is the reason?; tatra-in this matter; aha-he says;
prapanna iti-the phrase beginningn with the word "prapanna"; tadrsa-like that; laukika-material;
akara-form; lilaya-and pastimes; eva-certainly; hi-indeed; prapanna-jana-vrndasya-of the
surrendered devotees; parama-anandah-transcendental bliss; bavati-is; iti-thus; etat artham-this is
the meaning; tasmat-therefore; sadhu-properly; uktam-it is said; aho-Oh; bhagyam-good fortune; iti-
adi-in the verse beginning; brahma-spoken by Brahma; sri-bhagavantam-to the Supreme
Personality of Godhead.

   In this verse Brahmä explains that Çré Kåñëa is beyond the touch of the material energy, and He
imitates the form and activities of the ordinary living entitles in the material world, appearing as a
small cowherd boy in Gokula. Even though this is true, still the form of Çré Kåñëa, the small
cowherd boy in Gokula, is not a temporary manifestation of the Supreme Lord for a particular
purpose, but rather it is the original feature of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In other words,
