the form of Çré Kåñëa is the original form of God, and is not made of the five material elements, but
is completely spiritual.
    Someone may ask: Why does the Supreme Lord appear in this way as a small child? To this
question the following answer may be given: Lord Kåñëa seems like an ordinary child, and performs
activities that seem like those of an ordinary child, in order to grant transcendental bliss to the
devotees who become His associates. In other words, they become charmed and pleased by the
Lord's apparently ordinary activities. Because these devotees are so intimately associated with the
Lord in this way, Brahmä praised them in the verse beginning with the words "aho bhägyam"
(quoted in Anuccheda 138, Text 1).

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.144
records.text:
Text 1


ata eväha

täsäm avirataà kåñëe
  kurvaténäà sutekñaëam
na punaù kalpate räjan
  saàsäro 'jïäna-sambhavaù

   atah eva-therefore; aha-he said; täsäm-of all of them (of all the gopés); aviratam-constantly; kåñëe-
unto Lord Kåñëa; kurvaténäm-making; suta-ékñaëam-as a mother looks upon her child; na-never;
punaù-again; kalpate-can be imagined; räjan-O King Parékñit; saàsäraù-the material bondage of
birth and death; ajïäna-sambhavaù-which is to be accepted by foolish persons ignorantly trying to
become happy.

  Although superficially appearing as ordinary householders, the residents of Våndävana remained
always free from all material contamination. This is confirmed in the following statement of Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.6.40):

  "For that Personality of Godhead, the gopés always felt maternal love, and Kåñëa sucked their
breasts with full satisfaction. Therefore, because of their relationship as mother and son, although
the gopés were engaged in various family activities, one should never think that they returned to
this material world after leaving their bodies."*


Text 2


  täsäm çré-gopa-pura-stréëäm saàsäraù saàsäritvaà prapaïcikatvam na punaù kalpate, na tu
ghaöate, kintv aprapaïcikatvam eva ghaöata ity arthaù; yato 'sau ajïäna-sambhavaù. täsäà tu
kathaà-bhütänäm? ajïäna-tamaù-süryasya jïänasyopari-viräjamäno yaù premä tasyäpy upari
viräjamänaà yat sutekñaëam putra-bhävo vätsalyäbhidhaù premä tadeva, taträpi aviratam nityam
anädita eva çré-kåñëe kurvaténäm iti. çré-çukaù.

   täsäm-the word "täsäm (of them)"; çré-gopa-pura-stréëäm-refers to the gopés of Vrajabhümi;
saàsäräh-the word "saàsäraù"; samsaritvam prapaïcikatvam-means "material existence"; na-never;
punaù-again; kalpate-can be imagined; na-never; tu-certainly; ghaöate-may occur; kintu-however;
aprapaïcikatvam-freedom from material entanglement; eva-certainly; ghaöate-occurs; iti-thus;
arthaù-the meaning; yataù-because; asau-this; ajïäna-sambhavaù-which is to be accepted by foolish
persons ignorantly trying to become happy; täsäm-of them; katham-bhütänäm-how may they be
described?; ajïäna-of ignorance; tamaù-the darkness; süryasya-of the sun for illuminating; jïänasya-
of knowledge; upari-above; viräjamänah-manifested; yaù-which; premä-love of God; tasya-that; api-
even; upari-above; viräjamänam-manifest; yat-which; suta-ikñaëam-glance of a mother upon her

child; putra-of the child; bhävaù-conception; vätsalya-vätsalya-rasa; abhidhaù-named; premä-love
of God; tat-that; eva-certainly; taträpi-nevertheless; aviratam-the wod "aviratam"; nityam-means
"constantly"; anäditah-without beginning; eva-certainly; çré-kåñëe-unto Lord Kåñëa; kurvaténäm-
making; iti-thus; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé.

   In this verse the word "täsäm" (of them) refers to the gopés of Vrajabhümi, and the word
"saàsäraù" means "material existence". The phrase "na punaù kalpate" means "one should never
think that the gopés returned to this material world, for they were always situated in the
transcendental position,aloof from the contact of the material energy". Material existence is a
condition imposed upon those who are ignorant (ajïäna-sambhavaù), but because the gopés were
always enlightened by pure Kåñëa consciousness, they remained always free from the darkness of
material existence. Although the brilliant sun of transcendental knowledge destroys the darkness of
material existence, the exalted state of love of Godhead is situated on a platform above the
condition of transcendental knowledge. The intimate love of the gopés for Kåñëa in the mood of
parental love (vätsalya-rasa) is a very exalted condition, superior to ordinary love of God. The gopés
are eternally situated in in that condition of intense love of Kåñëa (avrataà çré-kåñëe kurvaténäm).
Because in this verse Çukadeva Gosvämé has used the word "aviratam" (eternally), we should
understand that the relationship of the gopés with Kåñëa is eternal and beginningless. The gopés are
also, therefore, eternal associates of Çré Kåñëa.

records.text:
yasmäd eva çré-gopädénaà tadéya-nitya-parikaratvaà tadmäd etat prakaraëaà tv asiddha-
dehänäà sädhaka-cäà käsäïcid apekñayä. yadvaitad-abhipräyam, tac ca, antar-grùa-gatäù, ity
ädikam na caiva vismayaù käryaù ity ädy-antam.

   yasmat-because; eva-certainly; çré-gopä-adénäà-of the cowherd men, gopés, and other
innhabitants of Vådävana; tadiyä-of Lord Kåñëa; nitya-eternal; parikaratvaà-the status of
associates; tasmät-therefore; etat-in this; prakaraëaà-account; tu-but; asiddha-dehänäà-with
material bodies; sädhaka-cärinäà-perfect devotees who became eligible to become Çré Kåñëa's

meaning; tat-that; ca-also; antah-gåha-gatäù iti ädikam na ca eva vismayaù käryaù iti ädi-antam-
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.9-16 (the original verses follow)


antar-gåha-gatäù käçcid

kåñëaà tad-bhavaëa-yuktä
   daddhyur milita-locanäù

duùsaha-presöùa-viraha-

dhyäna-praptäcyutäçleña-

guëa-pravähoparämäs

dviçann api håçékeçam
   kim utädhokñaja-priyaù

nåëäà niùçreyasärthäya
   vyaktir bhagavato nåpa
avyayasyäprameyasya
   nirguëasya gunätmanaù

käma' krodhaà bhayaà sneham
   aikyaà sauhådam eva ca
nityaà haräu vidadhato

na caiva vismayaù käryo
   bhavatä bhagavaty aje
yogeçvareçvare kåñëe
   yata etad vimucyate.


   Someone may argue that because the Çrémad-Bhägavatam says "na punaù kalpate saàsäraù" (the
gopés never returned to the material world), therefore we must conclude that at a certain time the
gopés were conditioned souls, or else how would it be possible for them to not return to the material
world (if they had never been in it in the first place).
   The answer to this question is that the gopés of Vrajabhümi may divided into two classes: 1.
eternal associates of Çré Kåñëa, and 2. those who are being promoted to that status from the
material world.
   The description "na punaù kalpate saàsäraù refers to this second class of gopés, who are

becoming eligible to be eternal associates of Çré Kåñëa. It is this second class of gopés who are
described by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.9-16):

   "Some of the gopés were factually detained from going to Kåñëa by their husbands and were
locked up by force within their rooms. Being unable to go to Kåñëa, they began to meditate upon
His transcendental form by closing their eyes. They already had the form of Kåñëa within their
minds. *
   "If they had been bound by fruitive action, they were fully freed from the reaction of karma by
constant meditation on Kåñëa. Their severe painful yearnings caused by their not being able to see
Kåñëa freed them from all sinful reactions, and their ecstacy of transcendental love for Kåñëa in His
absence was transcendental to all their reactions of material pious activities.*
   "All the gopés who concentrated their minds on Kåñëa in the spirit of paramour love became
fully uncontaminated from all the fruitive reactions of material nature, and some of them
immediately gave up their material bodies developed under the three modes of material nature.*
   "Mahäräja Parékñit heard Sukadeva Gosvämé explain the situation of the gopés who assembled
with Kåñëa in the räsa dance. When he heard that some of the gopés simply by concentrating on
Kåñëa as their paramour, became freed from all contamination from material birth and death, he
said: The gopés did not know that Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. They accepted
Him as a beautiful boy and considered Him to be their paramour. So how was it possible for them to
get freed from the material condition just by thinking of a paramour?*
   "On hearing this question of Mahäräja Parékñit , Çukadeva Gosvämé replied, "'My dear King, your
quesition is already answered, even before this incident.*
   "Çiçupäla was always envious of Kåñëa, and because of this envy Kåñëa killed him. Since Kåñëa is
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Çiçupäla gained salvation simply by seeing Him. If an envious
person can get salvation simply by concentrating his mind on Kåñëa, then what to speak of the
gopés who are so dear to Kåñëa and always thinking of Him in love? There must be some difference
between the enemies and the friends. If Kåñëa's enemies could get freed from material
contamination and become one with the Supreme, then certainly His dear friends like the gopés are
freed and with Him. *
   "Kåñëa is not an ordinary person. He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, full of all spiritual
qualities. He appears in this material world out of His causeless mercy in order to benedict the
conditioned souls, and whenever He appears, He appears as He is without change.*
   "If one somehow or other becomes attached to Kåñëa or attracted to Him, either because of His
beauty, quality, opulence, fame, strength, renunciation or knowledge, or even through lust, anger or
fear, or affection or friendship, then one's salvation and freedom from material contamination is
assured.*
   "Rest assured that one attracted by Kåñëa attains liberation from material bondage because
Kåñëa is the transcendental master of all mystic power. There is nothing surprising about this."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.146
records.text:
Text 1

  atra antaù iti sphuöam eva. açubham çré-kåçna-präptäv antaräya-rüpaà guru-bhayädikam.
maìgalam çré-kåñëa-präptau sädhanaà sakhyädi-sahayyä-cintanam.

na karma-bandhanaà janma
   vaiñëavänäà ca vidyate ity uktam eva.

   atra-here; antaù iti-the verse beginning with the word "antaù" (10.29.9); sphuöam-the meaning is
clear; eva- certainly; äsubham-inauspicious things; çré-kåñëa-präptau-when Çré Kåñëa was attained;
antaräya-rüpa- consisting of impediments; guru-of superiors; bhayä-fear; ädikam-beginnig with;
maìgalam-auspiciousness; çré-kåñëa-präptau-when Çré Kåñëa wa attained; sädhanaà- practice;
sakhyä-ädi-beginnign with friendship; sahayyä- assistance; cintanam-meditation; na-not;karma-of
fruitive actions; bandhanaà-bondage; janma-no birth; vaiñëaväëaà- of the pure devotees of the
Lord; ca-also; visyate-exists; iti-thus; uktam-it is said; eva-certainly.


   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.10 (the second verse quoted in Anuccheda 145), the word "açubha"
means "the gopés' fear of their superiors, and other inauspicious impediments, which obstructed
their going to meet Kåñëa", and the word "maìgalam" means "the auspicious process of thinking of
Kåñëa as their dearmost friend, which enables the gopés to very quickly attain Him."
   By intently meditating on Çré Kåñëa, these gopés became purified of all material defects and
returned back to the spiritual world. That such an auspicious result is obtained by the devotees is
confirmed in the following verse from Vedic literature:

   "Pure devotees of Lord Kåñëa are always free from the bondage of fruitive actions (karma). Such
devotees do not again take birth in the material world, for they return to the eternal spiritual
world."


Text 2


  dåçyate cänyaträpi tad-asambhava-sthale tac-chabda-prayogaù

association.

     nåëäm iti sämäyato jévänäm eva niùçreyasäya vyaktau satyaà bhaktänäm tu sutaräm evety
äyätam. anyathä tasya vyaktir eva na sambhaved ity äha avyayasya iti. nirguëasya präkåta-guëa-
rahitasya guëätmanaù. tatra ye caiçvaryädayo guëäs ta ätmanaù svarüpäëy eva yasya tasya. tarhy
etädåça-léläyä kathaà nåëäà niùçreyasäm bhavati? ucyate etad-bodhanena bhavatéty äha kämam
iti.

   nåëäm iti-the verse beginning with the word "nåëäm" (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.14), quoted on
pps 1060 and 1061; sämänyataù-in general; jévänäm-of living entities in the material world; eva-
certainly; niùçreyasäya-for the well-being; vyaktau-manifested; satyaà-when; bhaktänäm-of the
devotees; tu-certainly; sutaräm-greatly; eva-certainly; iti-thus; äyätam-attains; anyathä-otherwise;
tasya-His; vyaktiù- personal presence; eva-certainly; na-not; sambhavet-would not be possible; iti-
thus; äha-he says; avyayasya iti-of the phrase beginning with the word "avyayasya"; nirguëasya-the
word "nirguëasya"; präkåta-material; guëa-qualities; rahitasya- devoid of; guëa-ätmanaù-the word
"guëätmanaù"; tatra- there; ye-which; ca-also; aiçvarya-ädayag-various powers and opulences; guëaù-
qualities; te-they; ätmanaù-of the self; svarüpäë-own forms; eva-certainly; yasya-of whom; tasya-of
Him; tarhi-then; etädåça-léläyä-with these pastimes; kathaà-how is it?; nåëäà-of the human beings;
niùçreyasäm-auspiciousness; bhavati-is; ucyte-it is said; etat-bodhanena-by this understanding;
bhavaté-is; iti-thus; äha-he says; käman iti-the next verse (10.29.15), which begins with the word
"käman".


    In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.14. (quoted in Anuccheda 145), Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé said that
Lord Kåñëa appears in this material world in order to benefit the conditioned souls. Otherwise He
has no reason to appear in this world. This is explained in the second part of the verse, where the
word "avyayasya" means that Lord Kåñëa never falls down. In other words, He is never forced to
descend to this material world, but only comes out of His own wish.
    In this vere the word "nirguëasya" indicates that Çré Kåñëa has no material qualities, for He has
all spiritual qualities, powers and opulences (guëätmanaù).
    The question may be asked: Why are that Lord Kåñëa's pastimes in this material world beneficial
for the conditioned souls? The answer to this question is given in the next verse (10.29.15), where it
is said:

   "If one somehow or other becomes attached to Kåñëa or attracted to Him, either because of His
beauty, qualities, opulence, fame, strength, renunciation or knowledge, or even through lust, anger,
or fear, or affection or friendship, then one's salvation and freedom from material contamination
are assured."*

  In other words, by appearing in this world and manifesting His transcendental pastimes, Lord
Kåñëa gives the conditioned souls an opportunity to hear about Him and thus become attracted to
Him. Attraction to Kåñëa is the beginning of all-auspiciousness for the conditioned souls.


Text 16


   atra tan-mayatä-çabdena-pracüratocyate. tatra käma-snehädisu tad-uparaktätmateti
paryavasanam. stré-mayo jalma itivat krodha-bhayaikyeñu tu präyas tat-pralinäteti. dugdhamayaà
jalam itivat.

   atra-in this verse; tat-mayatä-çabdena-by the word "tanmayata"; tat-pracürata-is meant "His
greatness"; ucyate- it is said; tatra-there; käma-lust; snehao-affection; ädisu-beginning with; tat-to
Him; uparaktä-attached; ätmata-mind; iti-thus; paryavasanam-the conclusion; stréh-mayaù-lusty;
jalmaù-degraded man; itivat-just as; krodha-anger; bhaya- fear; aikyeçu-in oneness; tu-certainly;
präyaù-mainly; tat-pralénata-entering; iti-thus; dugha-mayaà-with milk; jalam- water; itivat-like.


   In this verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10 29.15, quoted in Anuccheda 145), the word "tan-mayatäm"
means "the greatness of Çré Kåñëa". In the case of the devotees, who always remember Kåñëa with
love and affection, this means that they become attracted to Çré Kåñëa. In the case of the demons,
however, this means that by meditating on Kåñëa in a mood of fear and anger, they get the
opportunity to merge into the effulgence of Kåñëa, just as a drop of water merges into a container of
milk. In this way there are two separate destinations for the devotees and the demons, although
both kinds of liberation are designated by the single word "tan-mayatäm" in this verse.


Text 17


   ekasya çabdasya viçeñaëa-väçäd artha-bhedaç ca yujyate. syäc caikasya brahma-çabdavat iti
nyäyena krodha-bhayayor atra paöhanam anyesu kaimutyopapadanäyaiva, na tu tad-upadeça-
vivakñayä.

   ekasya-of one; çabdasya-word;viçeñaëa-väçät-according to characteristics; artha-bhedaù-different
meanings; ca-also; yujyate-are engaged; syät-there may be; ca-also; ekasya-of one; brahma-çabda-the
word "brahma"; vat-like; iti-thus; nyäyena-according to the Vedanta-sutra (2.3.4); krodha-of anger;
bhayayoù-and fear; atra-here; paöhanam-reading; anyeçu-among others; kaimutya-upapadanäya-
what to speak of?; eva-certainly; na-not; tu-but; tat-of that; upadeça- instruction; vivakñayä-with a
desire to speak.


   In this context the word "tan-mayatäm" has these two meanings. The phrase "dugdhamayaà
jalam" is an example of an ambiguous statement that can be interpreted in different ways. The fact
that a single word may have many meanings is described in the following statement of Vedänta-

sütra (2.3.4):

syäc caikasya brahma-çabdavat

   If the demons attained liberation simply by meditating on Çré Kåñëa in the mood of fear and
anger, then the devotees, by meditating on Kåñëa with love, certainly attained a much greater
result. Therefore the destination attained by the gopés was certainly much greater than the
liberation attained by Jaya and Vijaya.


Text 18


   na ca gopikädénäà ye kämädayo bhäväs tad-anusaraëenänye kåtärthä bhavantéti citram ity äha
na ca iti. kià vaktavyam ekeñäà vimuktir jagato 'pi sambhavatéty äha yataù iti. çré-çukaù.

   na-not; ca-also; gopikä-ädénäà-of the gopis and other residents of Vrndavana; ye-which; kämä-
lust; ädayaù- beginning with; bhävän-sentiments; tat-anusaraëena-in accordance with; änye-others;
kåtä-ärthäù-results; bhavanté-come into being; éti-thus; citram-astonishment; iti-thus; äha-he said;
na ca iti-the phrase beginning with the words na ca" (10.29.16); kià-what more; vaktavyam-need
said; ekeñäà-of each one; vimuktiù-liberation; jagataù-from material existence; api-also; sambhavaté-
came into existence; iti-thus; äha-he said; yataù iti-the phrase beginning with the word "yatah"
(10.29.16);çré-çukaù-spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvami.


   The gopés attained liberation from material existence (yata etad vimucyate) simply by
meditating on Kåñëa in what was apparently lust, and the other residents of Våndävana also became
liberated by meditating on Kåñëa as their child or friend. One might be surprised to hear that the
residents of Våndävana became liberated by lust and other seemingly material emotions. One would
have certainly expected a different result to be obtained from lust and other emotions. However,
because these emotions were directed towards Kåñëa, Çukadeva Gosvämé informs Mahäräja Parékñit
that this auspicious result obtained by the residents of Våndävana is not at all surprising (na caiva
vismayaù käryaù).

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.147
records.text:
Text 1


   atra pürvavad ihäpi çré-vrajeçvarädénäà präcéna-janmädikaà vyakhyeyam. tathä hi

trayyä copaniñadbhiç ca
   säìkhya-yogaiç ca sätvataiù
upagéyamäna-mähätmayaà

  harià sämanyatätmajam ity etat.

   atha-now; pürvavat-as before; ihä-here; äpi-also; çré-vrajeçvarä-ädénäà-of Maharaja Nanda and
the other residents of Vrndavana; präcéna-former; janmä-birth; ädikaà-beginning with; vyahyeyam-
may be explained; tatha hi- furthermore; trayyä-by studying the three Vedas (Säma, Yajur and
Atharva); ca-also; upaniñadbhiù ca-and by studying the Vedic knowledge of the Upaniñads; säìkhya-
yogaiù-by reading the literature of säë khya-yoga; ca-and; sätvataiù-by the great sages and devotees,
or by reading Vaiñëava-tantra, Pancarätras; upagéyamäna-mähätmyam-whose glories are worshiped
(by all these Vedic literatures); harim-unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; sä-she; amanyata-
considered (ordinary); ätmajam-as her own son; iti-thus; etat-this.


   The previous births of the king of Vraja and other associates of the Lord will now be discussed.
The glorious position of Mother Yasoda is described in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.8.45):

  "The glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are studied through the three Vedas, the
Upaniñads, the literature of säìkhya-yoga, and other Vaiñëava literature, yet mother Yaçodä
considered that Supreme Person her ordinary child."*


Text 2


  nemaà viriïco na bhavaù

  na imaà viriïcah na bhavaù-the following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.20):


nemaà viriïco na bhavo
   na çrér apy aìga-saàçrayä
prasädaà lebhire gopé
   yat tat präpa vimuktidät.


   Mother Yaçodä's good fortune is also described in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.9.20):

   "Neither Lord Brahmä, nor Lord Çiva, nor even the goddess of fortune, who is always the better
half of the Supreme Lord, can obtain from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the deliverer from
this material world, such mercy as received by Mother Yaçodä."*


Text 3

  iti vakñyamänänusäri-mahä-mähätmyaà çrutvä vismita-manäù çré-räjoväca

nandaù kim akarod brahman
   çreya evaà mahodayam
yaçodä ca mahä-bhägä
   papau yasyäh stanaà hariù

   iti-thus; vakñyamänäm-about to be spoken; anusäri-the following; mahä-great; mähätmyaà-
glorification;çrutvä- hearing; vismita-manäù-astonished; çré-räjä uväca- Mahäräja Parékñit; further
inquired (from Çukadeva Gosvämé; nandaù-Mahäräja Nanda; kim-what; akarot- performed;
brahman-O learned brähmana; çreyaù-auspicious activities, like performing penances and
austerities; evam-as exhibited by him; mahä udayam-from which they achieved the greatest
perfection; yaçodä-mother Yaçodä; ca-also; mahä-bhägä-most fortunate; papau-drank; yasyäù-of
whom; stanam the breast milk; hariù-the Supreme Personality of Godhead.


   Having heard of the great fortune of Mother Yaçodä, Parékñit Mahäräja became astonished and
inquired form Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.46):

   "O learned brähamaëa, mother Yaçodä's breast milk was sucked by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead. What past auspicious activites did she and Nanda Mahäräja perform to achieve such
perfection in ecstatic love?"*


Text 4


pitarau nänvanindetäà
   kåñëodärärbhakehitam
gäyanty adyäpi kavayo
   yal loka-çamaläpaham

yayoh prasanno 'vatérëas tau pitarau api.

   pitarau-the actual father and mother of Kåñëa; na-not; anva-vindetäm-enjoyed; kåñëa-of Kåñëa;
udära- magnamimous; arbhaka-éhitam-the childhood pastimes He performed; gäyanti-are glorifying;
adya api-even today; kavayaù-great, great sages and saintly persons; yat-which is; loka-çamala-
apaham-by hearing of which the contamination of the whole material world is vanquished; yayoù-
with whom; prasannah-pleased; avatérëaù-descended; tau-the two; pitarau-the actual father and
mother of Kåñëa; api-even.


   Parékñit Mahäräja also described the great fortune of Nanda Mahäräja and Yaçodä-devé in the
following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.47):

  "Although Kåñëa was so pleased with Vasudeva and Devaké that He descended as their son, they

could not enjoy Kåñëa's magnanimous childhood pastimes, which are so great that simply chanting
about them vanquishes the contamination of the material world. Nanda Mahäräja and Yaçodä,
however, enjoyed these pastimes fully, and therefore their position is always better than that of
Vasudeva and Devaké."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.148
records.text:
tad evaà praçnam avadhärya çré-çuka uväca

droëo vasünäà pravaro
   dharayä bhäryayä saha
kariçyamäëa ädeçän
   brahmaëas tam uväca ha

ädeçän gopälanädi-lakñaëam.

   tat-then; evam-in this way; praçnam-the question of Pariksit Maharaja; avadhärya-hearing; çré-
çukaù-Çré Çukadeva Gosvami; uvaca-said; droëaù-by the name Drona; vasünäm-of the eight Vasus
(a type of demigod); pravaraù-who was the best; dharayä-with Dharä; bhäryayä-His wife; saha- with;
kariçyamäëaù-just to execute; ädçän-the orders; brahmaëaù-of Lord Brahmä; tam-unto him; uväca-
said; ha-in the past; ädeçän-the orders; gopälanä-ädi-lakñaëam- birth in a family of cowherds.


  Considering Mahäräja Parékñit's question about the previous birth of Nanda and Yaçodä,
Çukadeva Gosvämé replied (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.48):

   "To follow the orders of Lord Brahmä, Droëa, the best of the Vasus, along with his wife, Dharä,
spoke to Lord Brahmä in this way."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.149
records.text:
kim uväca. tad äha

jätayor nau mahädeve
   bhuvi viçveçvare harau
bhaktiù syät paramä loke
   yayäïjo durgatià taret

   kim-what?; uväca-did he say; tat-this; äha-he said; jätayoù-after we two have taken birth; nau-
both husband and wife, Droëa and Dharä; mahädeve-in the Supreme Person, the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; bhuvi-on the earth; viçva-içvare-in the master of all planetary systems;
harau-in the Supreme Lord; bhaktiù-devotional service; syät-will be spread; paramä-the ultimate

goal of life; loke-in the world; yayä-by which; aïjaù-very easily; durgatim-miserable life; taret-one
can avoid and be delivered.


   What did they say? They said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.49):

    "Droëa and Dharä said: Please permit us to be born on the planet earth so that after our
appearance, the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, the supreme controller and master of
all planets, will also appear and spread devotional service, the ultimate goal of life, so that those
born in this material world may very easily be delivered from the miserable condition of
materialistic life by accepting this devotional service."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.150
records.text:
Text 1


tataç ca

astv ity uktaù sa bhagavän
   vraje droëo mahä-yaçaù
jajïe nanda iti khyäto
   yaçodä sä dharäbhavat

   tataù-then; ca-also; astu-when Brahmä agreed, "Yes, it is all right"; iti uktaù- thus being ordered
by him; saù-he (Droëa); bhagavän- eternally the father of Kåñëa (Bhagavän's father is also
Bhagavän); vraje-in Vrajabhümi, Våndävana; droëaù-Droëa, the most powerful Vasu; mahä-yaççù-
the very famous transcendentalist; jajïe-appeared; nandaù-as Nanda Mahäräja; iti-thus; khyätaù-is
celebrated; yaçodä-as mother Yaçodä; sä-she; dharä-the same Dharä;abhavat- appeared.


   Lord Brahmä agreed to the request of Droëa and Dharä (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.50):

  "When Brahmä said, `Yes,let it be so,' the most fortunate Droëa, who was equal to Bhagavän,
appeared in Vrajapura, Våndävana, as the most famous Nanda Mahäräja, and his wife, Dharä,
appeared as Mother Yaçodä."*


Text 2


tato bhaktir bhagavati
   putré-bhüte janärdane
dampatyor nitaräm äsid

  gopa-gopéñu bhärata

   tataù-thereafter; bhaktiù bhagavati-the cult of bhakti, devotional service unto the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; putré-bhüte-in the Lord, who had appeared as the son of mother
Yaçodä;janärdane-in Lord Kåñëa; dam-patyoù-of both husband and wife; nitaräm-continously; äsét-
there was; gopa-gopéçu-all the inhabitants of Våndävana, the gopas and the gopés, associatting with
Nanda Mahäräja and Yaçodä and following in their footsteps; bhärata-O Mahäräja Parékñit.


  Çukadeva Gosvämé continued the narration (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.51):

   "Therefore, O Mahäräja Parékñit, best ofthe Bhäratas, when the Supreme Personality of Godhead
became the son of Nanda Mahäräja and Yaçodä, they maintained continuous, unswerving
devotional love in parental affection. And in their association, all the other inhabitants of
Våndävana, the gopas and gopés, developed the culture of kåñëa-bhakti."


Text 3


  anyeñäm yaù putro näsét, tasmiàs tu tayoù putratäà präpta iti cvi-pratyayärthaù bhakti-viçeço-
mätreëaivodaya-viçeña-niyamät.

   anyeñäà-of others; yaù-who; putraù-the son; nä-not; äsét-was; tasmië-in this connection; tu-but;
tayoù-of Nanda and Yasoda; putratäm-the condition of being the son;präptaù-attained; iti-thus; cvi-
pratyaya-ärtha-the meaning of the cvi-affix; bhakti-viçeña-mätreëa-simply by pure devotional
service; eva-certainly; udaya-viçeña-niyamät-appearing according to.


  Kåñëa became the son of Nanda and Yaçodä. He was not the son of anyone else. This is the
meaning of the use of cvi-pratyaya in this verse. He became their son because of their deep love for
Him.


Text 4


   vätsalyäbhidha-prema-viçeçeëaiva çré-kåñëaù putratayodeti, na tu sva-dehäd ävirbhävena
hiraëyakaçipu-sabhä-sambhe çré-nåsiàhasya, brahmaëi çré-varähasya ca pitåtvaprayogät, na ca
garbha-praveçena parékñid-rakñaëärtham tat-praviñöasyäpi tasyottara-mätåtvaçravaëät.

   vätsalyä-äbhida-named vätsalyä-räsa; prema- love; viçeçeëa-by the specific; eva-certainly;çré-
kåñëaù-Çré Kåñëa; putrataya-as a son; udeti-appears; na-not; tu-but; sva-dehät-from one's own body;
ävirbhävena-by appearance; hiraëyakaçipu-of Hiraëyakaçipu; sabhä-in the assembly hall; stambhe-
in the pillar; çré-nåsiàhasya-of Lord Nåsiàha; brahmaëi-in Lord Brahma;çré-varähasya-of Lord
Varäha; ca-also; pitåtva-fatherhood; aprayogät- because of unsuitability; na-not; ca-also; garbha-

within the womb; praveçena-by entrance; parékñit-of Maharaja Parékñit; rakñaëä-protection;ärtham-
for the purpose; tat-that; praviñöasyä-entered;äpi-even; tasya-of Lord Kåñëa; uttara-of Uttara-devi;
mätåtva-motherhood; açravaëät-because of not being described in the Vedic literatures.


   Çré Kåñëa appears as the son of a certain devotee when that devotee is immersed in parental love
for the Lord. It is this parental love for Kåñëa that makes the Lord one's son, and not simply the
Lord's appearance from the body of a certain living entity. For example, Lord Nåsiàha appeared
from the pillar in Hiraëyakaçipu's assembly hall, and Lord Varäha appeared from the nostril of Lord
Brahmä, but no one will say that the pillar is the father of Lord Nåsiàha, or that Brahmä is the
father of Lord Varäha. In the same way, Lord Viñëu entered the womb of Uttarä-devé in order to
protect Mahäräja Parékñit, but no one will say that Uttarä was the mother of Lord Viñëu, even
though He entered her womb. Therefore it is not the superficial appearance of being born as the
"natural" son of a certain devotee that establishes the devotee's parental relationship with the Lord,
but rather it is the increase of parental love that is the sole cause of that relationship.


Text 5


   tädåça-prema tu çuddhaù samudriktaç ca çré-vrajeçvarayor eva. ata eva garbha-praveçädikaà
vinäpi tayoù putratayä tasya prasiddhiù. yathä nandas tv ätmaja utpanne ity ädau. tathopäsanä ca
yathä sakala-loka-maìgalo nandagopa-tanayaù ity ädau, na tv evaà stambhädeù.

   tädåça-like this; prema-love; tu-certainly; çuddhaù-pure; samudriktaù-intense; ca-also; çré-vraja-
içvarayoù-of the king and Queen of Vraja; eva-certainly; atah eva-therefore; garbha-within the
womb; praveçä-entrance; ädikaà-beginning with; vinä-without; äpi-even; tayoù-of Nanda and
Yaçodä; putratayä-sonship; tasya-of Lord Kåñëa; prasiddhiù-fame; yathä-just as; nandah tu atmaje
utpanne iti ädau-Çrémad Bhägavatam 10.5.1-- the entire verse is:


nanda tv ätmaja utpanne
  jätählädo mahä-manäù
ähüya viprän veda-jïän
  snätaù çucir alaìkåtaù

tathä-in the same way; upäsanä-worship; ca-also; yathä- just as; sakala-all; loka-of planets and living
entities; maìgalaù-auspiciousnesss; nanda-gopa-of Nanda Maharaja; tanayaù-the son; iti-thus; ädau-
in the passage beginning; na-not; tu-but; evaà-in the same way; stambhä-ädeù-from the pillar or
other places from which Lord appears.


   Even though Çré Kåñëa was not born from the womb of Yaçodä-devé, because of Nanda and
Yaçodä's intense pure love for Kåñëa in the mood of parental love, they are famous as the parents of
Çré Kåñëa. The parenthood of Nanda and Yaçodä is confirmed in the following verses from the

Vedic literatures:
   "Çukadeva Gosvämé said: Nanda Mahäräja was naturally very magnanimous, and when Lord Çré
Kåñëa appeared as his son, he was overwhelmed by jubilation. Therefore, after bathing and
purifying himself and dressing himself properly, he invited brähmaëas who knew how to recite
Vedic mantras. After having these qualified brähmaëas recite auspicious Vedic hymns, he arranged
to have the Vedic birth ceremony celebrated for his newborn child according to the rules and
regulations, and he also arranged for worship of the demigods and forefathers."
               -Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.5.1

   "Nanda Mahäräja's son is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who brings auspiciousness to all
planetary systems and all living entities".
               -Vaiñëava Literature


Text 6


   kià ca çrémad-anakadundubhi-prabhåtiñv ävirbhävo 'pi na präkåtavat tadéya-carama-dhätv-ädau
praveçaù, kintu sac-cid-änanda-vigrahasya tasya tanomanasy äveça eva. tad uktam

   kià ca-furthermore; çrémat-anakadundubhi-Maharaja Vasudeva; prahåtiçu-and in the Lord's
other fathers; ävirbhävaù-appearance; api-also; na-not; präkåtavat-like that of an ordinary child;
tadéya-his; carama-dhätu-ädau-in the semen; praveçaù-entrance; kintu-however; sat-eternal; cit-full
of knowledge; änanda-and bliss; vigrahasya-of the form; tasya-of Lord Kåñëa; tat-of Maharaja
Vasudeva; manasi- within the mind; äveçaù-entrance; eva-certainly; tat-this; uktam-is described.


   Even the Lord's so-called natural parents did not beget Him as ordinary parents beget a child by
seminal injection in the womb of the mother. Lord Kåñëa appeared, in His eternal, all-cognizant
and blissful spiritual form within the mind of Mahäräja Vasudeva, and from there He was
transfered to the heart of Devaké. This is described in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.2.18):


Text 7


tato jagan-maìgalam acyutäàçaà
   samähitaà çüra-sutena devé
dadhära sarvätmakam ätma-bhütaà
   käñöhä yathänanda-karaà manastaù

   tattaù-thereafter;jagat-maìgalam-auspiciouness for all living entitiesl in all the universes of the
creation; acyuta-aàçam-the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is never bereft of the six
opulences, all of which are present in all His plenary expansions; samähitam-fully transfered; çüra-
sutena-by Vasudeva, the son of Çürasena; devé-Devaké-devé; ätma-bhütam-the cause of all causes;

käñöhä-the east; yathä- just as; änanda-karam-the blissful (moon); manastaù-being placed within the
mind.


   "Thereafter, accompanied by plenary expansions, the fully opulent Supreme Personality of
Godhead, who is all-auspicious for the entire universe, was transferred from the mind of Vasudeva
to the mind of Devaké. Devaké, having thus been initiated by Vasudeva, became beautiful by
carrying Lord Kåñëa, the original consciousness for everyone, the cause of all causes, within the
core of her heart, just as the east becomes beautiful by carrying the rising moon."*


Text 8


   tataù-çré-närada-prahläda-dhruvädiñu darçanät sarva-sammatatvät tädåça-prema-viçayatvena
säkñäc ca çré-bhagavad-ävirbhäväyavahita-pürva-pracura-kalaà vyäpya santatas tad-äveçaù çré-
vrajeçvarayor apy avaçyaà eva kalpyate. brahma-vara-prärthanayäpi tad eva labhyata iti samänä
eva granthäù.

   tataù-therefore; çré-närada-among Närada; prahläda- Prahläda; dhruva-Dhruva; ädisu-and
others; darçanät- because of sight; sarva-sammatatvät-because of agreement; tädåça-prema-
viçayatvena-because of this kind of love; säkñät-directly; ca-also; çré-bhagavat-of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; ävirbhävä-appearance; ävyavahita- immediate; purva-previous; pracura-
long; kalaà-time; vyäpya-having pervaded; santataù-continually; tat-äveçaù-the entrance of Çré
Kåñëa; çré-vraja-içvarayoù-in the King and Queen of Vrajabhumi; api-even; avaçyam-certainly; eva-
indeed; kalpyate-is accomplished; brahma-of Lord Brahma; vara- benediction; prärthanayä-by the
request; äpi-also; tat- that; eva-certainly; labhyate-is attained; iti-thus; samänäù-agreed; eva-
certainly; granthäù-scriptures.


   Çré Kåñëa is actually already always present in the material world in His all-pervading feature.
He is present in everyone's heart, and great devotees such as Närada, Prahläda, and Dhruva are able
to see Him because they are filled with love for Him. Just as Lord Kåñëa is always visible to Närada
and other great devotees because of their love for Him, in the same way, the Lord appeared before
the king and queen of Vrajabhümi as their son because of their pure love for Him, and also because
of the benediction granted to them by Brahmä in their previous life. This description is confirmed
by all Vedic literatures, and this is the actual meaning of the word "tataù" in this verse (Text 7).


Text 9


  vätsalyaà tv aträdhikam, yena vinä tasya putra-bhävo na sambhavatéty atraiva putratäà
manyamäëa iti puribhüta ity asya bhävaù.

  vätsalyaà-parental love; tu-certainly; aträ-ädhikam- increased; yena-by which; vinä-without;

tasya-of Çré Kåñëa; putra-of son; bhävaù-state; na-not; sambhavaté-is possible; éti-thus; atra-here; eva-
certainly; putratäà- sonship; manyämähe-we consider; iti-thus; putra-son; bhütaù-become; iti-thus;
asya-of this verse; bhävaù-the meaning.


   In this verse (10.8.51, quoted in Text 7) the word "putra-bhütaù" indicates that because of the
intense parental love felt by Vasudeva, Devaké, Nanda, and Yaçodä for Lord Kåñëa, the Lord
became their son. Without intense parental love for Him it is not possible for one to get the Lord as
a son.


Text 10


   idaà prakaöäyäà léläyaà samahitam aprakaöäyäà tu. tayor nitya-siddhatva eva pürato
'vadhärayiçyamäne-viñëor anädita ädi-rasa-siddha-dam-patyavat çré-vrajeçvarayos tasya cänädito
vatsala-rasa-siddha-pitå-putra-bhävo vidyata eva. atah putra-bhüta iti ca kvacit paöhaù.

   idaà-this; prakatäyäà-manifest; léläyäà-in the pastimes; samahitam-arranged; aprakaöäyäà-in
the unmanifest pastimes; tu-but; tayoù-of the Lord's parents; nitya-siddhatve-in the eternal
perfection; eva-certainly; pürataù- formerly; avadhärayiçyamäne-will be determined; lakñmé-
viñëvoù-of Lakñmé and Viñëu; anäditaù-without beginning; ädi-original; rasa-mellow; siddha-
perfected; dam-patyavat-as husband and wife; çré-vraja-içvarayoù-of the king and queen of Vraja;
tasya-of that; cä-also; änäditaù-beginningless; vatsala-rasa-in parental love; siddha-perfected; pitå-of
father; putra-and son; bhävaù-condition; vidyate-is; eva- certainly; ataù-from this; putra-bhütaù-
the word "putra bhütah"; iti-thus; ca-also; kvacit-in some manuscripts; paöhaù-alternate reading.


   In the Lord's pastimes within the material world (prakaöa-lélä), the relationship of parent and
child exchanged by the Lord and His devotees in the parental mellow (vätsalya-rasa) begins at a
certain point in time, and appears to be existing within the limitations of material time. The same
parental mellow is experienced by the Lord's parents in the unmanifested pastimes (aprakaöa-lélä)
in the spiritual world also. The parental mellow actually has no beginning in time.
   In some manuscripts of Çrémad-Bhägavatam we find the reading "putra-bhütaù" (who is the son)
instead of "putré-bhütaù" (who became the son). The reading "putra-bhütaù" refers to the
beginningless mellow of parental love for the Lord tasted by the devotees in the spiritual world.


Text 11


   ata eva na hy asyästi priyaù kaçcit ity ädi prakaraëe

yuvayor eva naiväyam
   ätmajo bhagavän hariù
sarveñäm ätmajo hy ätmä

   pitä mätä sa éçvaraù

ity etat çré-vrajeçvarau prati çrémad-uddhava-väkyam.

   atah eva-therefore; na hi asyä ästi priyaù kaçcit iti ädi prakaraëe-in the passage beginning with
these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.37); yuvayoù-of the two of youl; eva- certainly; na-not; eva-
certainly; äyam-He; ätmajaù-the son; bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; hariù-Hari;
sarvesäm-of everyone; ätmajaù-the son; hi-certainly; ätmä-the Supersoul; pitä-father; mätä-mother;
saù-He; éçvaraù-the supreme controller; iti-thus; etat-this; çré-vraja-içvarau prati-to the king and
queen of Vraja; çrémat-uddhava-of Uddhava; väkyam-the statement.


  We may note here the following verse spoken by Uddhava to the king and queen of Våndävana,
which seems to deny the parental relationship between Lord Kåñëa and the king and queen of
Vraja. Uddhava said to them (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.42):

   "My dear Nanda and Yaçodä, Kåñëa is not your son, but the Personality of Godhead. He is one's
son. He is actuallly everyone's father, mother, and supreme controller."*


Text 12


   tadaudasénya-prakaöanenäpata-santväna-mätra-tatparyaka-bahyärtham api vastavam artham tv
evaà vahati pürvokta-prakereëayaà priyäpriyädi-mata-piträdi-rahito 'pi bhagavän harir yaù saù
ayaà kåñëa-rüpatvena viçeñakäraù san yuvayor evätmajo naiva sarveñäm. sa eveçvara-rüpatvena
sämähyakäratas tu sarvesäà ätmajädi-sarva-rüpah syät. kintu paratra mäyä-mayatvan näsmäkan
ädärah. pürvatra tu mumukñu-mukta-bhakta-çläghya-premamayatväd atyädära iti bhävaù.

   tat-aduasénya-aloof from everything; prakaöanena-by the manifestation; äpata-at that moment;
santväna-for consoling; mätra-only; tätparyaka-meaning; bahyä-external; ärtham- meaning; api-
although; vastavam-actual; artham-meaning; tu- but; evaà-in this way; vahati-is; pürva-previously;
uktam- spoken; prakareëa-by the method; ayaà-this; priyä-dear; apriya-not dear; adi-beginning
with; mata-mother; pitå- father; ädi-beginning with; rahitaù-devoid of; api-although; bhagavän-the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; hariù-Hari; yaù-who; saù-He; ayaà-He; kåñëa-rüpatvena-in the
form of Çré Kåñëa; viçeña-specific; akäraù-form; san-being; yuvayoù-of the two of you; evä-certainly;
atmajaù-the son; na-not; eva-certainly; sarveñäm-of everyone; saù-He; eva- certainly; içvara-
rüpatvena-as the Supreme Controller; sämänya-akärataù-as the all-pervading Supersoul; tu-also;
sarveñäm-of everyone; ätmajä-son; ädi-beginning with; sarva-all; rüpaù-form; syät-may be; kintu-
however; paratra-in others; mäyä-mayatvat-because of being a poduction of the illusory energy; nä-
not; äsmäkan-of us; ädaraù-faith; pürvatra-previously; tu-but; mumukñu- desiring liberation; mukta-
and liberated; bhakta-by the devotees; çläghya-praiseworthy; premamayatvät-because of pure love;
ati-great; ädäraù-faith; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning.

    The basic meaning of this verse is that, in order to pacify Nanda and Yaçodä, Uddhava tells
them that their son, Kåñëa, is actually the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is aloof from the
entire cosmic manifestation and impartial to all living entities. There is, however, another, a deeper
meaning of this verse. This verse actually means: Although Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of
Godhead (bhagavän harir yaù saù), and although He is aloof to all living entities, impartial to
friends and enemies, and without father, mother, or other relations, still He has become the son of
Nanda and Yaçodä (yuvayor evätmajah), even though He is never the son of anyone (naiva
sarveñäm). One may say also interpret this phrase as "ätmaja eva sarveñäm (He is the son of
everyone), in which case it is understood that Lord Kåñëa expands as the Supersoul in the hearts of
all conditioned souls, and in this way He becomes their son. This interpretation is a product of the
illusory potency, mäyä. This second interpretation is nt very sound, and we do not accept it. The
great devotees who are liberated or aspiring to become liberated praise the other interpretation
(yuvayor evatämajah) which describes the great parental love of Nanda and Yaçodä for Kåñëa. We
also endore this interpretation, which emphasizes the parenthood of Nanda and Yaçodä.


Text 13


tathoktaà präg eva

tayor itthaà bhagavati
   kåñëe nanda-yaçodäyoù
vékñyänurägaà paramaà
   nandam ahoddhavo mudä

yuyaà çläghyatamau nünaà
   dehinäm iha mänada
näräyaëe 'khila-gurau
   yat kåtä matir édåçé iti.

   tatha-in the same way; uktaà-described; präk-before; eva-certainly; tayiù-of the two of them;
itthaà-in this way; bhagavati-for the Supreme Personality of Godhead; kåñëe- Kåñëa; nanda-of
Nanda Maharaja; yaçodäyoù-and Yaçodä-devé; viksyä-seeing; änurägaà-love; paramaà-
transcendental; nandam-to Nanda; aha-spoke; uddhavaù-Uddhava; mudä-with happiness; yüyaà-
you two; çläghyatamau-most praiseworthy; nünaà-indeed; dehinäm-of living entities; iha-in this
world; mänada-O glorious one; näräyaëe-for Lord Näräyaëa; akhila-of everyone; gurau-the Lord;
yat-because; kåtä-attained; matiù-conception; édåsé-like this. iti-thus.


   The parental love of Nanda and Yaçodä for their son Kåñëa is glorified in the following verses
from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.19-30):

   "When Uddhava saw Mahäräja Nanda and Yaçodä so extraordinarily overwhelmed with thoughs
of Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and when he experienced their extraordinary

affection for Him, he also became overwhelmed and began to speak as follows, `My dear mother
Yaçodä and Nanda Mahäräja, you are most respectable among human beings because no one but
you can meditate in such transcendental ecstasy'".*


Text 14


tathä

sa pitä sä janané
   yau puñëétaà svaputravat
çiçün bandhubhir utsåñtän
   akalpaiù poña-rakñaëe

   iti çré-vrajeçvaraà prati çré-kåñëa-rämäbhyäà santvänäà ca çré-rämasyaiva para-putratvam
apekñyeti jïeyam.

   tathä-in the same way; saù-he; pitä-the father; sä- she; ca-also; janané-the mother; yau-who;
puñëétaà- nourished; sva-putra-vat-as their own son; çiçün-the children; bandhubhiù-by his
relatives; utsåñtän-abandoned; ekalpaiù-unable to protect; poça-in nourishment; rakñaëe- and
protection; iti-thus; çré-vraja-içvaram-prati-to the king of Vrajabhumi; çré-kåñëa-rämäbhyäà-by
Lord Kåñëa and Balarama; santvänäà-conslotion; ca-also; çré-rämasya-of Lord Balarama; eva-
certainly; para-transcendental; putratvam-sonship; apekñya-in reference to; iti-thus; jïaeyam-may
be understood.


   In the following verse Kåñëa and Balaräma console Nanda Mahäräja and glorify Nanda and
Yaçodä's exalted parental relationship with them. Kåñëa and Balaräma said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.45.22):

   "My dear father and mother, although I was born of Vasudeva and Devaké, you have been Our
real father and mother, because from Our very birth and childhood, you raised Us with great
affection and love. Your affectionate love for Us was more than anyone can offer one's own
children. You are actually Our father and mother, because you raised Us as your own children at a
time when We were just like orphans. For certain reasons We were rejected by Our father and
mother, and you protected Us."*


Text 15


yathoktaà tatraiva tena

yathä yüyaà vrajaà täta
   vayaà ca sneha-duhkhitän

jïätén vo drañöum eñyämo
   vidhäya suhådäà sukham iti.

   yatha-just as; uktaà-said; tatra-in that passage; eva- certainly; tena-by Lord Kåñëa; yatha-you
should go; yüyaà- you; vrajaà-to Vraja; täta-O father; vayaà-we; ca-also; sneha-by love; duùkhitän-
distressed; jïatén-relatives; vaù-you; drañöum-to see; eñyämaù-we shall go; vidhäya- having given;
suhådäà-to our friends; sukham-happiness; iti-thus.


   "My dear father and mother, I know you will be feeling separation by returning to Våndävana
and leaving us here, but please rest assured that I shall be coming back to Våndävana just after
giving some satisfaction to My real father and mother, Vasudeva and Devaké, My grandfather, and
other relatives and family members."*


Text 16


   drañtüm eñyämaù paçyante eva sthäsyäma ity arthaù. tasmäd anayor eva mukhyaà putratvam çré-
kåñëe viräjata iti siddham. präkåtam anusarämaù.

    drañöum-to see; eçyämaù-we shall go; paçyantaù- seeing; eva-certainly; sthäsyämaù-shall cause to
stay; iti- thus; arthaù-the meaning; tasmät-therefore; anayoù-of Nanda and Yaçodä; eva-certainly;
mukhyaà-primary; putratvam- sonship; çré-kåñëe-in relationship to Çré Kåñëa; viräjate-manifested;
iti-thus; siddham-demonstrated; präkåtam-natural; anusarämaù-in accordance with.


   In this verse Kåñëa promises to return to Vraja to see Nanda and Yaçodä. This means that He
intends to remain in Vraja for some time. In this verse we may see that Nanda and Yaçodä, and not
Vasudeva and Devaké are the real parents of Çré Kåñëa.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.151
records.text:
Text 1


  gopa-gopénäm api tasmin premäséd eva dam-patyoù tayos tu täsv api nitaräm äsét iti.

  gopa-of the cowherd men; gopénäm-and gopés; api-also; tasmin-in relation to Lord Kåñëa; prema-
pure love; äsét-was; eva-certainly; dam-patyoù-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.51


dam-patyor nitaräm äséd
  gopa-gopéñu bhärata;

tayoù-of Nanda and Yaçodä; täsu-among the gopés; api-also; nitaräm-greatly; äsét-was; iti-thus.


  The elderly cowherd men and gopas of Våndävana also felt intense parental love for Lord Kåñëa.
This is confirmed in the following verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.51):

   "Therefore, O Mahäräja Parékñit, best of the Bhäratas, when the Supreme Personality of
Godhead became the son of Nanda Mahäräja and Yaçodä, they maintained continuous, unswerving
devotional service in parental affection. And in their association, all other inhabitants of
Våndävana, the gopas and gopés, developed the culture of kåñëa-bhakti."*


Text 2


upasaàharati

kåñëo brahmaëa ädeçaà
   satyam kartuà vraje vibhuù
saha-rämo vasaàç cakre
   teñäà prétià sva-lélayä

   upasaàharati concludes; kåñëaù-the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa; brahmaëaù-of
Lord Brahmä; ädeçam-the order; satyam-truthful; kartum-to make; vraje-in Vrajabhümi,
Våndävana; vibhuù-the supreme powerful; saha-rämaù-along with Balaräma; vasan-residing; cakre-
increased; teñäm-of all inhabitants of Våndävana; prétim-the pleasure; sva-lélayä-by His
transcendental pastimes.


   In the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.52) Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé concludes his
description of the parenthood of Nanda and Yaçodä:

   "Thus the Supreme Personality, Kåñëa, along with Balaräma, lived in Vrajabhümi, Våndävana
just to substantiate the benediction of Brahmä. By exhibiting different pastimes in His childhood,
He increased the transcendental pleasure of Nanda and the other inhabitants of Våndävana."*


Text 3


   sveñu bhakta-jana-viçeñeñu ya lélä tad-bhakti-viçeña-väsa-lélä-viçeñas tayaiva teñäm sarveñäm api
prétià cakre. dväv api tau prati tena vara-dänäd iti bhävaù. yadyapy evam, tathäpi brahmaëa
ädeçaà satyaà kartum mahad-äçér anyathä na syad iti darçayitum apéty arthaù. yadvä, sva-léläyä
teñäà prétià kartuà vraje väsän brahmaëä ädeçaà satyam cakre. tad-anuçaìgataù svayam ädåtya
sarvaträvyabhicärinäà cakäreti. çré-çukaù.

   sveñu-among His own; bhakta-jana-devotees; viççeçu- specific; ya-which; lélä-pastime; tat-bhakti-
viçeña-by devotional service; väsa-controlled; lélä- pastimes;viçeñaù-specific; taya-by that; eva-
certainly; teñäm-of them; sarveñäm-of all the inhabitants of Vrndavana; api-also; prétià-pleasure;
cakre-increased; dväv api tau-to Nanda and Yaçodä; tena-by that; vara-dänät-because of granting
the benediction; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning; yadyapi-although; evam-in this way; tathäpi-
nevertheless; brahmaëaù-of Lord Brahma; ädeçaà- the order; satyaà-truthful; kartum-to make;
mahat-äçéù- great benediction; anyathä-otherwise; na-not; syät-may be; iti-thus; darçayitum-to
reveal; apé-also; éti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; yadvä-or; sva-lélayä-by His transcendental pastimes;
teñäà-of them; prétià-the pleasure; kartuà-to make; vraje-in Vrajabhumi; väsän-
residing;brahmaëaù-of Lord Brahma; ädeçaà-the order; satyaà-truthful; cakre-made; tat-
anusaìgataù-by placing the words in this sequence; svayam-personally; ädåtya-respecing; sarvaträ-
everywhere; avyabhicärinäà-without break; cakära-did; iti-thus; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çréla
Sukadeva Gosvami.


   Çré Kåñëa becomes controlled by the pure love of His devotees, and He increased the pleasure of
the residents of Vrajabhümi in transcendental reciprocation for their pure love for Him. Even so,
Lord Kåñëa arranged that the residents of Vraja obtained His association as a result of the
benediction of Brahmä. The Lord did this in order to demonstrate that the association of Lord
Kåñëa is not ordinary. It is a great benediction bestowed upon the living entities. It is also posssible
to interpret this verse to mean: "Çré Kåñëa lived in Våndävana just to increase the pleasure of His
devotees there. Incidentally, He did this by fulfilling the benediction offered by Brahmä".

records.text:
Text 1


   tad etat käraëaà tad-äbhäsam eva manyamänac tayor brahmädibhyo 'pi saubhägyätiçayasya
khyäpanärtham anantaram eva ekadä gåha-däséñu ity ädy ädhyäyam ärabdhavän. tatraiva ca säkñac

brahmaëäpi çiva-lakñmébhyäs api durlabhaà bhagavat-prasäda bhäram äha

   tat-therefore; etat-of this; käraëaà-the cause; tat-äbhäsam-in appearance; eva-certainly;
manyamänaù- considering; tayoù-of Nanda and Yasoda; brahmä-ädibhyaù-than what is obtained by
Brahma, or other demigods; api-even; saubhägyä-good fortune; ätiçayena-be greatness; khyäpana-
praising; ärtham-for the purpose; anantaram-afterwards; eva- certainly; ekadä gåha-däsésu iti ädi
ädhyäyam-the Ninth Chapter of the Tenth Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam, which begins with the
words "ekada gåha-däsésu"; ärabdhavän-began; tatra-there; eva-certainly; ca-also; säkñät-directly; çré-
bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; bandhana- binding; rüpa-consisting of; mahä-

   Nanda and Yaçodä did not become Lord Kåñëa's parents by achieving the blessing of Brahmä.
Actually, Nanda and Yaçodä are more fortunate and exalted than the demigod Brahmä. This is
confirmed in the Ninth Chapter of the Tenth Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam, where we find the
description of the glories of mother Yaçodä's maternal love for Kåñëa, how Lord Kåñëa is completely
under the control of Mother Yaçodä, and how she bound Him with ropes. Mother Yaçodä obtained
greater mercy form Lord Kåñëa then even Brahmä, Çiva or Lakñmé could ever attain. This is
described in the following verse, (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.9.20):

this material world, such mercy as received by mother Yaçodä."*

confirmed in the following statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (2.9.5):

   "Lord Brahmä is the first spiritual master."

   Çiva is still more exalted. This is described in the following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(12.13.16):

   "Çiva is the best among all the devotees of Lord Kåñëa".

   Because Lakñmé is considered the teacher of devotional service to Brahmä and Çiva, she is more
exalted then even Brahmä and Çiva. The glories of Lakñmé are so great that they cannot be
described by even Brahmä and Çiva. Lakñmé's good fortune extends beyond the realm of ordinary
devotional service, for she is an intimate friend of the Personality of Godhead. This is confirmed in
this verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.9.20) by the word "aìga-saàçrayä" (Lakñmé-devé is the better half
of the Supreme Lord).

greater than liberation. This is described in the following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (5.6.18):

  "Those engaged in getting the Lord's favor attain liberation from the Lord very easily, but He
does not very easily give the opportunity to render direct service unto Him."*

   Yaçodä-devé, the queen of the gopés (gopé) obtained an indescribable (yat tat) benediction
(prasädam) from Lord Kåñëa, which could not be obtained (na lebhire) by even Brahmä, Çiva, or
Lakñmé. The phrase "na lebhire" (not attained) should be understood to be repeated three times to
refer to Brahmä, Çiva, and Lakñmé. In this way the rarity of the mercy obtained by Yaçodä is
emphasized.

   Someone may say that Droëa and Dharä are ordinary material demigods, and therefore they
could not possibly have become Kåñëa's parents without receiving a benediction form Brahmä. That
Droëa and Dharä become Kåñëa's parents because of Brahmä's blessings is not an acceptable
proposition, however, for Çrémad-Bhägavatam clearly says that Brahmä himself is not able to attain
the good fortune obtained by Droëa and Dharä (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.9.20, quoted in Text 2).
How can Brahmä give as a gift what other great devotees and he himself are unable to attain?
Brahmä himself says this in the following prayer (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.14.34):

   "My dear Lord, I am therefore not interested in either material opulences or liberation. I am mot
humbly praying at Your lotus feet for You to please give me any sort of birth within this Våndävana
forest so that I may be able to be favoured by the dust of the feet of some devotees of Våndävana.
Even if I am given the chance to grow just as the humble grass in this land, that will be a glorious
birth for me. But if I am not so fortunate to take birth within the forest of Våndävana, I beg to be
allowed to take birth outside the immediate area of Våndävana so that when the devotees go out
they will walk over me. Even that would be a great fortune for me. I am just aspiring for a birth in
which I will be smeared by the dust of the devotees' feet."*

  Also, no Vedic literature says that Droëa and Dharä performed great devotional service to the
Lord to make themselves eligible to become his parents.
  The truth is that Droëa and Dharä are partial expansions (aàça-avatära) of Nanda and Yaçodä,
Kåñëa's eternal parents in the spiritual world. They descended to this material world, just as the
Lord Himself did in order to display His pastimes on earth.

brahmä-adibhiù-by Brahma and other great devotees of the Lord; tatra-there; yat-because; kiïcit-

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam is the best of scriptures because it describes pure love for the Supreme
Personality of Godhead as the ultimate goal of life. That pure love of Godhead is perfectly
manifested in the holy abode of Gokula, and Nanda and Yaçodä, the king and Queen of Gokula, are
perfect examples of that pure love for Kåñëa. For this reason, Brahmä prays to attain any sort of
birth in that holy land of Gokula.

Text 1

bodily concept of life, especially the karmés; gopikä-sutaù-Kåñëa, the son of mother Yaçodä (Kåñëa
as the son of Vasudeva is called Väsudeva, and as the son of mother Yaçodä He is known as Kåñëa);

self-sufficient yogés; yathä-as; bhakti-matäm-of the devotees; iha-in this world.


   Nanda and Yaçodä are actually the eternal parents of Çré Kåñëa in the spiritual world. Now that
we have clearly demonstrated this fact, we shall explain that such an intimate realtionship with Çré
Kåñëa can only be obtained by those engaged in devotional service to the Lord. It cannot be
obtained by anyone else. That Lord Kåñëa may be attained only by devotional service is described
in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.9.21):

   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, the son of mother Yaçodä, is accessible to
devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental
speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austetities and penances, or to those who
consider the body the same as the self."*

easily attained; kintu-but; pürveëa-former; eva-certainly; karaëena-by the cause; jäta-produced; tat-

become manifested; tat-that; evä- certainly; äyam-this; iti-thus; cintyayadbhiù-meditating; taiù-by
them; kath
ancit-somehow; evä-certainly; äsau-He; labhyate-is attained; tat-therefore; ca-also; dvayoù-of the
two; api-also; tayoù-of them; sädhanayoù-engaged in spiritual practices; hénatvat-without; tat-
läbhaù-attainment of Çré Kåñëa; ca-also; na-not; säkñät-directly; kintu-however; kencit-by a certain;
amçena-partial expansion; eva- certainly; iti-thus; vyanjitam-manifested.


    This verse explains that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, the son of Mother Yaçodä,
is not easily accesible to the materialists, who consider the body the same as the self, even if they
perform austerities and other similar practices to attain Him. Such persons may become somewhat
purified at heart by prolonged austerities, and after a long time they may receive the merciful
glance of a pure devotee of the Lord. By the mercy of such a devotee, the materialist may learn how
to offer his performance of austerities and other spiritual practices as service to the Lord, and in
that way Lord Kåñëa may become accesible to him. In the same way, Lord Kåñëa is also not easily
accesible to the mental speculators who are from the bodily conception of life and who meditate on
the impersonal Brahman. Only by the mercy of a devotee of the Lord can such speculators actuallly
perceive the real nature of the Absolute Truth, and direct their meditation to Lord Kåñëa. These
two processes (austerity and mental speclation) do not enable us to directly perceive the original
feature of the Absolute Truth, but give us only a glimpse of His nature.

   This is confirmed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself (Bhagavad-gétä 12.4-5):

   "But those who fully worship the unmanifested, that which lies beyong the perception of the

senses, the all-pervading, inconceivable, fixed, and immovable-the impersonal conception of the
Absolute Truth-by controlling the various senses and being equally diposed to everyone, such
persons, engaged in the welfare of all, at last achieve Me.*
   "For those whose minds are attached to the unmanifested, impersonal feature of the Supreme,
advancement is very troublesome. To make progress in that discipline is always difficult for those
who are embodied."*

Personality of Godhead. That philosophy which does not satisfy the transcendental senses of the
Lord is considered worthless."*

   One may ask: Who, then, is able to attain Çré Kåñëa? This question is answered by the word
"bhaktimatäm" (by the devotees) in this verse. The Supreme Personality of Godhead (bhagavän),
who is known as the son of Yaçodä-devé (gopikä-sutaù) is attainable by Mother Yaçodä, and the
other devotees. What more need be said in this regard? The word "sukhäpaù" may also be
interpreted to mean "the object of happiness". This mean that Çré Kåñëa appeared to be an ordinary
child, the son of Yaçodä-devé. Thinking of Kåñëa as her own son, Yaçodä attained transcendental
bliss by observing Çré Kåñëa's charming childhood pastimes. The mental speculators are always
absorbed in meditation on the all-pervading impersonal feature of the Lord, and are thus unable to
understand the transcendental happiness obtained by seeing the astonishing and beautiful
transcendental form and pastimes of the Supreme Person.

   The word "sukhäpaù" may also be interpreted to mean "easily understood". When Çré Kåñëa
performs extraordinary feats (such as the lifting of Govardhana Hill), the mental speculators and
materialistics immersed in the bodily concept of life become able to understand that Çré Kåñëa is
the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The intimate devotees and associates of the Lord, however,
continue to consider the Lord to be their friend or son, and thus, in one sense, it is difficult for
them to understand the true position of the Lord, because of their intimate friendship with Him.

   The devotees of the Lord are thus perfectly enlightedned about the real purpose of life, and they
are plunged in transcendental bliss (sukhäpa) because of their awareness of the Lord's

transcenmdental handsome form and charming pastimes. This is described in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(12.12.69):

   "Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé was simply attracted by the charming pastimes of Lord Kåñëa, and
therefore his mind was always filled with transcendental bliss. He had givenm up all attraction for
everything else."

   Three points may be noted in this verse. First, the word "iha" (here) may be understood to mean
specifically the devotees attached to the form of Çré Kåñëa. In this way the devotees attached to the
Lord in His other forms, such as Näräyaëa, the master of Vaikuëöha, are also considered to be
unable to understand the Lord in His original form as Çré Kåñëa. The second and third points are
that the conceptions that Çré Kåñëa is only the adopted son of Yaçodä, and that instead He is the
actual son of Devaké, are both refuted by the use of the word "gopikä-sutaù". That Nanda and
Yaçodä, the king and queen of Vrajabhümi, are the eternal parents of Çré Kåñëa is the true meaning
of this word (gopikä-sutaù). This point is also supported by the great self-realized devotees who
understand the true nature of Çré Kåñëa.

the previous statement; asat-vyäpadeçat-as false; na-not; iti-thus; cet-if; na-not; dharmä-meaning;

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.9.1-20 we find an explanation of Nanda and Yaçodä's eternal
parenthood of Çré Kåñëa, and in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.49, we find the explanation of Nanda and
Yaçodä's previous birth as Droëa and Dharä. The seeming contradiction of these two statements
may be resolved by accepting the explanation that Droëa and Dharä are partial incarnations of
Nanda and Yaçodä, the Lord's eternal parents in the spiritual world. We may also note that the
description of the eternal parenthood of Nanda and Yaçodä is given after the description of their
previous birth as Droëa and Dharä. If there are two contradictory statements in the scriptures, the
second statement should be accepted, and the previous statement should be interpreted so that it
does not contradict the later statement. This rule of interpretation is expressed in the Vedänta-
sütra in the following words (2.1.17):

asad-vyäpadeçän neti cen na dharmäntareëa väkya-çeñät.

Text 1


   tad evaà çruti-puräëädi-nigamokty-anusärean çré-kåñëasya nityäbhivyaktitvaà dvärakädiñu
nitya-vihäritvaà nitya-yädavädi-parikaratvaà ca darçitam. itthaà ca kåñëas tu bhagavän svayam iti
su-siddham.

   tat-therefore; evaà-in this way; çruti-of the Vedas; puräëä-and Puräëäs; ädi-beginning with;

thus; ca-also; kåñëah tu bhagavän svayam-the statement of Bhägavatam 1.3.28 ("Çré Kåñëa is the
Supreme Personality of Godhead"); iti-thus; su-siddham- clearly proved.


   We have thus quoted many statements from the Vedas and Puräëas to clearly prove: 1. the form
of Çré Kåñëa is eternal, 2. Çré Kåñëa eternally enjoys pastimes in Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Våndävana,
and 3. Çré Kåñëa eternally associates with the Yadu dynasty and the inhabitants of Våndävana. By
proving these points we have strengthened the argument of the Bhägavatam's paribhäñä-sütra
(kåñëas tu bhagavän svayam: Çré Kåñëa is the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, 1.3.28).


Text 2

bhagavantaà parityajya te tasmai nivedayituà gataù? kathaà vä janmädi-léläyä krameëa mathuräà
gokulaà punar mathuräà dvärakäà ca tyaktvä vaikuëöham ärüòhavän? iti.

this way; çré-kåñëa akhyaù-Çré Kåñëa; svayam bhagavan-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tatra
tatra-in various places; nija-parikaraiù-His associates; säàdhaà-accompanied by; viharati-performs
pastimes tarhi-then; kathaà-how is it?; brahmä-of Brahma; ädi-and the other demigods;
prärthanäya- by the appeal; çré-narayanaù-Çré Näräyana; eva-certainly; ävatatära-incarnated; iti-
thus; çruyate-it is heard in the Bhägavatam and other Vedic literatures; tasya-of Him; yadi-if; çré-
kåñëaù-Çré Kåñëa; praveçaù-entrance; tarhi- then; ca-also; kathaà-how is it possible?; nityam-
eternally; eva-certainly; dväraka-ädisu-in Dvaraka, Mathura, and Våndävana; virajamanaà-
manifested; svayaà-bhagavantaà-the Original Supreme Personality of Godhead; parityajya-
abandoning; te-they; tasmai-to Lord Näräyana; nivedayituà-to appeal; gataù-went; kathaà-how is
it?; vä-or; janmä-ädi- beginning with His birth; léläyä-pastimes; krameëa-in accrdance with;
mathuräà-Mathura; gokulaà-Gokula; punaù- again; mathuräà-Mathura; dvärakaäà-Dvaraka; ca-
also; tyaktvä-abandoning; vaikuëöham-to Vaikuëöha-loka; ärüdhavän-ascended; iti-thus.


    Now someone may doubt:
    1. If Çri Kåñëa is the Original Supreme Personality of Godhead, who eternally enjoys pastimes
with His liberated associates, as you say, then why is it that the Bhägavatam and other Vedic
literatures say that Brahmä and the other demigods presented an appeal to Lord Näräyäëa, who
then descended to the earth in the form of Çré Kåñëa?

    2.If Çré Kåñëa eternally remains in Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Våndävana, then why did the
demigods not approach Lord Kåñëa personally with their request? Why did they approach Lord
Näräyaëa instead?
    3.If Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Våndävana are the eternal abodes of Çré Kåñëa, then why did Kåñëa
first appear in Mathurä, then travel to Gokula, then again return to Mathurä, then travel to
Dvärakä, and finally leave Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Gokula, in order to go to Vaikuëöhaloka?


Text 3

brahmäëòädhikäriëo brahmädayo 'pi brahmäëòa-käryaà tasmä eva nivedayitum arhanti. tatas
tadäpi tasmä eva påthivé-bhärävatäräya niveditavantaù.

Mathura, and Gokula; nityaà-eternally; viharati-performs pastimes; çré-kåñëa-äkhyaù-Çré Kåñëa;
svayaà bhagavän-the Original Supreme Personality of Godhead; parät paraù-supreme; brahmä-

yaù-who; tu-certainly; kñérodä-ädi-lélä-dhäma-who performs pastimes in the ocean of milk and other
pla?; näräyaëä-ädi-näma-known by the name Näräyana, and by other names also; puruñaù-the
puruña incarnation; sah eva-that Supreme Person; viñëu-rüpaù-in the form of Lord Viñëu; säkñät-

was appropriate for them; tataù-therefore; tadä-then; äpi-certainly; tasmäi-to Narayana; eva-

   To the first two questions we reply: The Original Personality of Godhead, Lord Kåñëa, who
eternally enjoys pastimes in Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Våndävana, does not generally appear before
Brahmä and the other demigods. They cannot approach Him, although they may approach Lord
Kåñëa's expansion as Kñérodakaçäyé Viñëu, who is known to them as the maintainer and creator of
the universe. For this reason they appealed to Lord Kñérodakaçäyé Viñëu to relieve the burden of the
earth.

   After hearing the demigods' appeal, the Personality of Godhead indicated the He desired to
personally appear on the earth. The description of this may be found in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.1.22,
and also in the description of the incarnation of a hair found in some scriptures. When the time
came for Lord Kåñëa to end His manifest pastimes on the earth, He ascended to Vaikuëöha in the
form of one of His expansions aàça-avatära, although in His original form He actually remained in
Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Gokula, and secretly enjoyed pastimes there, invisible to the eyes of
ordinary human beings. This description is confirmed by the account found in the Tantra-
bhägavata, Varäha Puräëa, and other Vedic literatures. That Çré Kåñëa eternally remains in
Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Gokula is also confirmed by the folllowing verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(11.31.24):

   "Çré Kåñëa eternally remains in the abode of Dvärakä."

   We may also note that this mystery of the appearance and pastimes of the Original Personality
of Godhead is difficult to understand, and not everyone was able to perceive these secret activities
of the Lord.

   Great sages say the appearance and disappearance of Lord Kåñëa from this material world is like
the rising and setting of the sun (The sun remains unchanged, although it appears and dissappears

from the view of certian living entities). This is described in the following statement of the Çruti-
çästra:

   "The Personality of Godhead appears and disappears from this material world just as the sun
seems to rise in the morning and then seems to enter the ocean again at sunset."

   This comparison of Lord Kåñëa's appearance and disappearance to the rising and setting of the
sun gives us only a partial understanding of the Lord's appearance in this world. Lord Kåñëa's
pastimes may be divided into two types: 1. prakaöa (manifested) pastimes, and 2. aprakaöa
(unmanifested) pastimes. Lord Kåñëa eternally remains in Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Gokula (which
are simultaneously manifest in both the spiritual and material worlds and, invisible to the eyes of
ordinary conditioned souls, enjoys aprakaöa pastimes. When the proper time for the Lord's prakaöa
(manifest) pastimes arrives, Lord Näräyaëa and the other viñëu-tattva expansions of the Lord enter
the transcendental body of Lord Kåñëa and appear along with Him in His prakaöa pastimes, which
may be seen by the living entities in the material world. When the time for the Lord's prakaöa
pastimes is ended, Lord Näräyaëa and the other forms of the Lord leave the earth planet and return
to the Vaikaëöhalokas. The original form of Çré Kåñëa remains however, and, invisible to the eyes
of ordinary living entities, enjoys aprakaöa pastimes in Dvärakä, Mathurä, and Gokula. We have
already described the Lord's manifest and unmanifest pastimes, quoting many statements from
Vedic literatures. We may note the following verse from Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad (2.48), where the

   Lord Kåñëa's manifest (prakaöa) pastimes in Våndävana are described in Brahma-saàhitä (5.29):

   "I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, the first progenitor, who is tending the cows, yielding all
desires, in abodes built with spiritual gems and surrounded by millions of purpose trees. He is always
served with great reverence and affection by hundred and thousands of goddesses of fortune."*

    The Lord's unmanifested (prakaöa) pastimes are completely distinct from the material world and
its influence, and are also completely free from the limitations of material time. In this way, Lord
Kåñëa eternally enjoys pastimes, day after day entering the assembly hall of Dvärakä as the king of
the Yadu dynasty, and day after day taking care of the surabhi cows as the young prince of
Vrajabhümi. Although Lord Kåñëa's pastimes are always aloof from the influence of matter, in His
manifested (prakaöa) pastimes, by His own wish, and by the workings of His internal potency, His
pastimes appear to be material, and appear to be under the jurisdiction of time: with a beginning,
growth, dwindling, and end.

   To worship the Lord's unmanifested (aprakaöa) pastimes, two processes may be adopted: 1.
mantropäsanamayé, and 2. svärasiké. The first process (mantropäsanamayé) entails remaining
permenantly in a place where the Lord enjoyed pastimes, and worshiping the Lord by chanting
various mantras describing His pastimes. This process of mantropäsana is described in the Båhad-
dhyäna-ratnäbhiñeka chapter of the Krama-dépikä, and in other passages in the Vedic literatures.
The Gautaméya Tantra also describes this process of mantra-meditation in the passage which begins
with the following verse:

   "I shall now the describe the process of meditating upon Lord Kåñëa, whose eyes are like lotus-
flowers, and who is dressed in yellow garments. Meditating on Lord Kåñëa in this way, one becomes
free from the reactions to all past sins."
