   tam ekaà govindaà sac-cid-änanda-vigrahaà païca-padaà våndävana-süra-bhüruha-taläsinaà
satataà samarud-gaëe 'haà paramayä stutyä toçayämi.


  The following mantra from the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad (1.38) describes the process of
mantropäsanä:

   "With eloquent prayers I and the Maruts please Lord Govinda, whose form is eternal and full of
knowledge and bliss, who stays under a desire-tree in Våndävana, and who is the five-word mantra
(kléà kåñëäya govindäya gopéjanavallabhäya svähä)."


Text 17


  ya tu tat-tat-kämänatmaka-prayogamayé pütanä-vadhädi-rüpä,

yad-yad-dhiyä ta urugäya vibhävayanti
   tat-tad-vapuù praëayase sad-anugrahäya

ity uktänusäreëädyäpi sädhaka-hådi kadäcit sampratéva sphurati, sa khalu mantropäsanamayétve 'pi
särasikyäm eva paryavasyati, atétatvena sarvatra nirdiñöatvät.

   ya-which; tu-certainly; tat tat-various; kämäno-atmaka-according to His desires; prayogamayé-
application; pütanä- of Putana; vadhä-killing; ädi-beginning with; rüpä- consisting of; yat-yat-
whichever; dhiyä-by meditating; te- Your; urugäya-O multiglorious; vibhävayanti-they specifically
think of; tat-tat-the very same; vapuù-transcendental form; praëayase-do You manifest; sat-
anugrahäya-to show Your causeless mercy; iti-thus; ukti-the statement; änusäreëä- according to;
ädyä-today; äpi-even; sädhaka-of the elegible devotees; hådi-in the heart; kadäcit-sometimes;
sampraté-today; éva-as it were; sphurati-manifest; sa-that; khalu-certainly; mantra-mantra; upäsana-
worship; mayétve- consisting of; api-even; särasikyäm-in rasikopasane; eva- certainly; paryavasyati-
becomes completed; atétatvena-greatly; sarvatra-everywhere; nirdiñöatvät-because of being
indicated.


   When the process of mantropäsanä (worship of the Lord by chanting mantras) becomes
complete, the eligible devotee attains the stage known as särasiké (direct perception), where Lord
Kåñëa personally appears in the heart of the devotee and manifests His transcendental pastimes
there. Even today, some devotees have attained this exalted stage of devotional service. This
svärasiké stage of meditation on Lord Kåñëa is described in the following verse of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (3.9.11):

   "O my Lord, Your devotees can see You through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing, and
thus their hearts become cleansed, and You take Your seat there. You are so merciful to Your
devotees that You manifest Yourself in the particular eternal form of transcendence in which they
always think of You."*


Text 18


atha svärasiké ca yathodähåtam eva

vatsair vatsa-tarébhiç ca
   sadä kréòati mädhavaù
våndävanäntara-gataù
   sa-rämo balakair våtaù

   atha-now; svärasiké-the stage of svarsikopasana; ca- also; yathä-just as; udahåtam-described; eva-
certainly; vatsaiù-with the calves; vatsa-tarébhiù-the young cows; ca- and; sadä-eternally; kréòati-
performs pastimes; mädhavaù- Lord Kåñëa; våndävanä-äntara-gataù-within the forest of Vådävana;
sa-rämaù-with Balarama; balakaiù-and the boys; våtaù-accompanied.


   The following verse from the Vedic literatures describes the pastimes of the Lord seen by a
devotee in the svärasiké stage of meditation:

   "Lord Kåñëa eternally enjoys pastimes with Balaräma, the cowherd boys, the calves, and the
surabhi cows in the forest of Våndävana."


Text 19


   atra ca-kärät çré-gopendrädayo 'pi gåhyante. räma-çabdena rohiëy api tathä tenaiva kréòati ity
ädinä vrajägamana-sayanädi-léläpi. kréòä-çabdasya vihärärthatväd vihärasya nänä-sthänänusäraëa-
rüpatväd eka-sthäna-niñöhayä mantro-äsenä-mayya bhidyate. yathävasara-vividha-svecchamayé
svärasiké.

   atra-in this verse; ca-kärät-from the word "ca (and)"; çré-gopa-indrä-Nanda Maharäja, the king of
the cowherd men; ädayaù-and the other residents of Vraja; api-also; gåhyante- may be understood;
räma-çabdena-by the word "räma"; rohiëi- Rohiëi-devi; api-also; tathä-in the same way; tena-by this;
eva-certainly; kréòati iti ädinä-by the phrase beginning with the word "kréòati"; vrajä-in Vrajä;
ägamana-arrival; sayanä-resting; ädi-beginning with; lélä-pastime; api- also; krédä-çabdasya-of the
word "krédä"; vihärä-arthavät-from the meaning "pastime"; vihärasya-of the pastime; nänä-various;
sthänä-places; anusäraëa-rüpatvät-because of the feature; eka-one; sthäna-place; niñöhayäù-because
of firmly staying; mantra-upäsanä- worship by chanting mantras; mayya-by that wich consist of;
bhidyate-manifested; yathä-as; ävasara-occasion; vividha- various; sva-iccha-mayé-according to His

own wish; svärasiké-directly perceived pastimes.


   In this verse the word "ca" (also) is used to describe the presence of Nanda Mahäräja and the
other residents of Vraja, and the word "räma" is used to indicate the presence of Lord Balaräma's
mother Rohiëé-devé. The phrase beginning with the word "kréòati" describes Lord Kåñëa's pastimes:
entering the pasture land of Vraja, taking a nap in the afternoon, and many other pastimes
performed in various places of Våndävana-dhäma. The svärasiké pastimes are performed by the Lord
according to His own wish and according to various circumstances. By remaining in a holy place,
without traveling to other places, one may perform this process of mantropäsanä worship, and
become eligible to directly percieve Lord Kåñëa's pastimes in the svärasiké way.


Text 20


evaà brahma-saàhitäyäm

cintämaëi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-våkña-
   lakñävåteñu surabhér abhipälayantam
lakñmé-sahasra-çata-sambhrama-sevyamänaà
   govindam ädi-puruñaà tam ahaà bhajämi

   evam-in the same way; brahma-saàhitäyäm-in the Brahma-saàhitä (5.40); cintämaëi-
touchstone; prakara-groups made of; sadmasu-in abodes; kalpa-våkña-of desire trees; lakña- by
millions; ävåteçu-surrounded; surabhéù-surabhi cows; abhipäkayantam-tending; lakñmé-of goddesses
of fortune; sahasra-of thousands; çata-by hundreds; sambhrama-with great respect; sevyamänam-
being served; govindam-Govinda; ädi-puruñam-the original person; tam-Him; aham-I; bhajämi-
worship.


   Lord Brahmä, for example, directly saw Lord Kåñëa's pastimes in the svärasiké way and described
them in the following verse (Brahma-saàhitä 5.40):

   "I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, the first progenitor, who is tending the cows, yielding all
desires, in abodes built with spiritual gems and surrounded by millions of purpose trees. He is always
served with great reverence and affection by hundreds and thousands of goddesses of fortune."*


Text 21


   atra kathaà gänaà naöyaà gamanam api ity aträpy anusandheyam.

   atra-in this connection; kathaà gänaà naöyaà gamanam api iti-in the following verse (Brahma-
saàhitä 5.67):

çriyaù käntäù parama-puruñah kalpa-taravo
   drumä bhümiç cintämaëi-gaëa-mayé toyam amåtam
kathä gänaà näöyaà gamanam api vaàsi priya-sakhé
   cid-änandaà jyotiù param api tad äsvädyam api ca

   atra-her; api-also; anusandheyam-confirmed.


   Lord Brahmä also described his own svärasiké realization in the following verse (Brahma-saàhitä
5.56):

    "The damsels of Våndävana, the gopés, are super goddesses of fortune. The enjoyer in Våndävana
is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Kåñëa. The trees there are all-fulfilling trees, and the land is
made of transcendental touchstone. The water is all nectar, the talking is singing, the walking is
dancing, and the constant companion of Kåñëa is His flute. The effulgence of transcendental bliss is
experienced everywhere. Therefore Våndävana-dhäma is the only relishable abode."*


Text 22


   tatra nänä-lélä-praväha-rüpatayä svärasaiké gaìgeva. ekaika-lélätmakatayä mantropäsanamayé tu
labdha-tat-sambhava-hräda-çreëéva jïeyä. kià ca mantropäsanä-mayyäm api vraja-räjädi-
sambandhaù çruyate, kim uta svärasikyäm iti na kuträpi tad-rahitatä kalpanéyä. tad etat sarvaà
müla-pramaëe 'pi dåçyate. tatra prakaöa-rüpä vispañöaiva. athäprakaöäyäà mantropäsanämayém äha

   tatra-there; nänä-various; lélä-pastimes; praväha- river; rüpatayä-in the form; svärasiké-svärasiki-
realization of the Lord's pastimes; gaìga-the Gaìges river; iva-like; eka-eka-one after another; lélä-
atmakatayä- consisting of pastimes; mantra-upäsana-mayé-mantropasana realization; tu-but; labdha-
tat-sambhava-in relation to the svärasiké river; hräda-of lakes; çreëé-series; éva- like; jïeyä-may be
known; kià ca-furthermore; mantra-upäsanä-mayyäm-in the stage of matropasana worship; api-
also; vraja-räjä-the king of Vraja; ädi-beginning with; sambandhaù-in relation to; çruyate-is heard;
kim uta-what to speak; svärasikyäm-in the state of svärasiké realization; iti-thus; na-not; kuträpi-
anywhere; tat-rahitatä- confidential nature; kalpanéyä-conceivable; tat-therefore; etat-this; sarvaà-
everything; müla-pramäëe-in the origin of all evidence; api-even; dåçyate-is seen; tatra-there;
prakaöa-rüpä-the Lord's manifest pastimes; vispañöa-very clearly seen; eva-certainly; athä-now;
aprakaöäyäà-in the unmanifeste pastimes; mantra-upäsanä-mayém-in the form of mantropasana;
äha-he says.


   In the stage of svärasiké realization, the various pastimes of Lord Kåñëa appear before the devotee
like a constantly flowing Ganges river. Some of those svärasiké pastimes become recorded in various
mantras, and thus the mantropäsanä stage of realization may be compared to a series of lakes within
the Ganges river of svärasiké realization. In the mantropäsanä stage one hears about Lord Kåñëa,

Nanda Mahäräja, and the residents of Vrajabhümi, whereas in the svärasiké stage one is able to
directly see Lord Kåñëa and His associates. From this we may understand that the svärasiké stage is
very elevated and difficult to achieve. The most confidential matters are understandable in that
svärasiké stage of realization. The svärasiké stage is described in Çrémad-Bhägavatam, the most
authoritative source of spiritual knowledge, and many svärasiké pastimes are described in its verses.
The following verse, (6.8.20), describes Lord's Kåñëa's unmanifest (aprakaöa) pastimes, as seen in
the svärasiké stage. The pastimesare presented in the form of mantras to be chanted by devotees in
the mantropäsanä stage.


Text 23


mäà keçavo gadayä prätar avyäd
  govinda äsaìgavam ätta-veëuù

   mäm-me; keçavaù-Lord Keçavaù; gadayä-by His club; prätaù-in the morning hours; avyät-may
He protect; govindaù-Lord Govinda; äsaìgavam-during the second part of the day; ätta-veëuù-
holding His flute.


  "May Lord Keçava protect me with His club in the first portion of the day, and may Govinda,
who is always engaged in playing His flute, protect me in the second portion of the day."*


Text 24


   ätta-veëuh iti viçeñaëena govindaù çré-våndävana-deva eva tat-saha-paöhät keçavaù api çré-
mathurä-nätha eva, tau hi våndävana-mathurä-prasiddha-mahä-yoga-péöhayos tan-nämnaiva
sahitau prasiddhau. tauca tatra präpaïcika-loka-dåñtyäà çrémat-pratimäkäreëäbhätaù, svajana-
dåñöyäà säkñäd-rüpeëa ca. tatrottara-rüpaà brahma-saàhitä-govinda-stavädau prasiddham. ata
eväträpi säkñäd-rüpa-våndävana-prakaraëa eva tau paöhitau tataç ca näräyaëa-
varmäkhyaàantropäsya-devatätvena çré-gopäla-täpany-ädi-prasiddha-svatantra-manträntaropäsya-
devatätvena ca mantropäsanä-mayyäm idam udähåtam. viçvarüpa indram.

   ätt-veëuù iti-the word "atta-venuh; viçeñaëena- describing; govindaù-Govinda; çré-våndävana-
devaù-the master of Våndävana; eva-certainly; tat-therefore; saha- along with; paöhät-the words;
keçavaù-Keçava; api-also; çré-mathurä-näthaù-the lord of Mathurä; eva-certainly; tau-they; hi-
certainly; våndävana-in Våndävana; mathurä- and Mathurä; prasiddha-famous; mahä-great; yoga-
péöhayoù- holy places; tat-nämna-by these names; eva-certainly; sahitau-with; prasiddhau-famous;
tau-they; ca-also; tatra-there; präpraïcika-loka-of the conditioned souls in the material world;
dåñtyäà-in the sight; çrémat-pratimä-äkareëa-in the form of the deity; äbhätaù-manifested; svajana-
of His intimate devotees; dåñtyäà-in the sight; säkñät-in His direct form; ca-also; tatra-there; uttara-
rüpaà-the latter form; brahma-saàhitä-in the Brahma-samhita; govinda-to Lord Govinda; stavä-of

the prayers; ädau-in the beginning;prasiddham-famous; atah evä-therefore; äträ-here; äpi-also;
säkñät-in His direct; rüpa-form; våndävana- of Våndävana;prakaraëe-in the chapter; eva-certainly;
tau- they; paöhitau-read; tataù-therefore; ca-also; näräyaëa-varmä-äkhya-of the scripture known as
the Näräyana-varmät; mantra-by the mantras; upäsya-worshipable; devatätvena-as the supreme
master; çré-gopäla-täpané-ädi-in the Gopäla-täpané Upanisad and other Vedic literatures; prasiddha-
famous; sva atra-independent; manträ-mantras; antara-by other; upäsya-worshippable; devatätvena-
as the supreme master; ca- also; mantra-up
äsanä-mayyäm-in the stage of mantropasena; idam-this; udähåtam-described; viçvarüpaù-the
brahamana Viçvarüpa; indram-to Maharaja Indra.


   In this verse the word "govinda" refers to the form of Lord Kåñëa as the master of Våndävana,
and the name "keçava" refers to Lord Kåñëa as the Lord of Mathurä. The Lord appears in these two
forms as the Deity visible to the people in general, and He also appears directly before His intimate
devotees. The second manifestation of the Lord's form before the devotee is described in the
prayers to Lord Govinda in the Brahma-saàhitä and in other Vedic literatures as well. Realization
of the Lord in the stage of mantropäsanä is described in the verses of Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad and
the scripture known as the Näräyaëa-varma.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.155
records.text:
Text 1


   vakñyamäna-bhagavad-abhipräyänusäreëäspañöärthatvena ca vastutaù svärasikém äha

mä khidyatäà mahä-bhägau
   dräkñyathaù kåñëam antike
antar hådi sa bhütänäm
   äste jyotir ivaidhasé

   vakñyamäna-which will be described; bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead;
abhipräyä-intention; änusäreëa-in conformity with; aspasöä-unclear; ärthatvena-with a meaning; ca-
also; vastutaù-in truth; svärasikém-the svärasiké stage of realization; äha-he describes; mä-don't;
khiyatäà-be unhappy; mahä-bhägau-O greatly fortunate Nanda and Yaçodä; dräkñyathaù-you will
see; kåñëam-Kåñëa; antike-nearby; antaù-within; hådi- the heart; saù-He; bhütänäm-of the living
entities; äste- remains; jyotiù-light; iva-like; edasi-in fuel.


   Following Lord Kåñëa's instructions, Uddhava spoke the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.46.36) to Nanda and Yaçodä. Although seeming ambiguous, these words actually describe the
svärasiké stage of spiritual realization. Uddhava said:

   "My dear Mother Yaçodä and Nanda Mahäräja, Kåñëa promised that He would come back to

Våndävana after finishing His business in Mathurä. This promise He will surely fulfill. I therefore
request you both, who are the best among all fortunates, to be not aggrieved on account of Kåñëa's
absence.*
   "You are already perceiving His presence twenty-four hours a day, and yet He will come and see
you very soon. Actually He is present everywhere and in everyone's heart, just as fire is present in
wood."*


Text 2


   he mahä-bhägau çré-vrajeçvarau, mä khidyatäm yataù çré-kåñëaà dräkñyatéhaù. katham? yataù
saù antike eva äste; tasyäntika-sthiter avyäbhicäre dåñöäntaù bhütänäm antar hådi paramätma-
lakñaëam jyotir iva edhasi cägni-lakñaëam jyotir iva iti. atra nirantara-tat-sphurtir eva bhavatäà
präùinäm iti bhävaù. arthäntare tüttarärdhasya hetutväspañöatvam. paramätma-rüpeëäntar hådi
sthitaçyäpi darçanänéyamät. uddhavaù çré-vrajeçvarau.

   he-O; mahä-bhägau-greatly fortunate; çré-vraja-éçvarau-O king and Queen of Vrajabhumi; mä
khidyatäm-don't lament; yataù-because; çré-kåñëam-Çré Kåñëa; dräkñyathaù-you will see; katham-
how is this possible?; yataù-because; saù-he; antike-nearby; äste-stays; tasyä- of Him; äntika-sthiteù-
staying nearby; avyäbhicära-in non-separation; dåñöäntaù-an example; bhütänam-of the living
entities; anöaù-within; hådi-the heart; paramä-lakñaëam- as the Supersoul; jyotiù-light; iva-like;
edhasi-in fuel; cä-and; ägni-of fire; lakñaëam-characteristics; jyotiù-light; iva-like; iti-thus; atra-
here; nirantara-continual; tat-His; sphurtiù-manifestation; eva-certainly; bhavatäà-of them;
präëinäm-living entities; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning; arthä-äntare-another interpretation; tü-
but; üttarä-of the second; ärdhasya-half of the verse; hetutvä-of the cause; äspañöatvam-ambiguity;
paramä-ätma-as the Supersoul; rüpä-form; äntaù-within; hådi-the heart; sthitisyä- staying; äpi-also;
darçanä-of the sight; änéyamäte- because of the oubt; uddhavaù-spoken by Uddhava; çré-vraja-
éçvarau-to Nanda and Yaçodä.


   In this verse the word mahä-bhägau" (greatly fortunate) refers to Nanda and Yaçodä, the king
and queen of Vrajabhümi. Uddhava says to them: "Do not be unhappy, you will see Kåñëa." Why
does Uddhava say that? "Because Kåñëa is already staying nearby" is the answer Uddhava gives.
Then he speaks the following example: "Just as fire and light are present within firewood, in the
same way, Kåñëa, in His form as the all-pervading Supersoul is present in the hearts of all living
entities." The second half of this verse may also be interpreted to mean: "It is as if (iva) Kåñëa is the
Supersoul present in the hearts of all living entities." In this way there is some doubt as towhether
Kåñëa will become visible as the Supersoul, or in some othe way. In this way it may be understood
that Kåñëa will become visible to Nanda and Yaçodä by the process of svärasiké realization. In this
way Nanda and Yaçodä will not see the form of the Supersoul but the original form of Kåñëa, who
was enjoying His pastimes.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.156
records.text:
Text 1


evaà çré-bhagavän uväca

bhavaténäà viyogo me
  na hi sarvätmanä kvacit

   me mayä saha bhavaténäm so 'yam viyogaù; saù sarvätmaëa sarveëäpi prakäçena na vidyate. kià
tarhy ekena prakaöa-léläyäà viräjamänena prakäçena viyogaù; aprakaöa-léläyäà tv anyena samyoga
evety arthaù.

   evam-in this way; çré-bhagavaë-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; uväca-said; bhavaténäm-of
you; viyogaù- separation; me-with; na-not; hi-certainly; sarva-atmanä-in all respects; kvacit-at any
time; me-the word "me"; mayä seha-with me; bhavaténäm-of you; sah ayam-that; viyogaù-
separation; saù-that; sarva-atmanä-the word; "sarvatmanä"; sarveëa-by all; api-even; prakäçena-
manifestation; na-not; vidyate-is; kim-how? tarhi-then; ekena-by one; prakaöa-léläyäm-in the
manifest pastimes; viräjamänena-manifested; prakäçena-manifestation; viyogaù-separation;
aprakaöa-léläyäm-in the unmanifest pastimes; tu-but; anyena-with another; samyogaù-meeting; eva-
certainly; iti-thus;


   The svärasiké stage of realization is also described by Lord Kåñëa Himself in His message to the
gopés
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.29):

  "My dear gopés, you should understand that it is not possible for you to be separated from Me at
any time."*

   Although the gopés seemed to be separated from Kåñëa,
as He appeared in His prakaöa-lélä (manifested pastimes), they were always thinking of Him, and
thus perceiving His presence directly in His aprakaöa-lélä (unmanifested pastimes). Being situated
in the stage of svärasiké realization, the gopés thus constantly saw Çré Kåñëa. In this way, although
they were separated from His prakaöa form, they associated with Him in another way (in His
aprakaöa pastimes). In this way Çré Kåñëa's statement that it is not possible to be separated from
Him may be understood.


Text 2


  atraitad uktaà bhavati na cäntar na bahir yasya ity ädi dämodara-lélä-praghaööaka-dåñöyä måd-
bhakñaëa-lélädau çré-vrajeçvary-ädénäà tathänubhütyä ca çré-vigrahasya madhyamatva eva

vibhütvaà dåçyate. tac ca paraspara-virodhi-dharma-dvayam ekaträcintya-çaktimati tasmin
näsambhavam, çrutes tu çabda-mül tvät ity etan nyäyena, ity evaà bhagavat-sandarbhe
praghaööakena vivåtam asti.

   atra-here; etat-this ; uktäm-statement; bhavati-is; na cäntar na bahir yasya iti adi Srimad
Bhägavatam 10.9.13; dämodara-of Lord Dämodara; lélä-pastimes; praghaööaka- the precept; dåñöyä-by
the sight; måt-clay; bhakñaëa- eating; léla-adau-beginning with the pastimes; çré-vraja-içvari-of the
queen of Vrajabhumi; ädénäm-and the other residents of Vrajabhumi; tatha-in that way; anubhütyä-
by perceiving; ca-also; çré-vigrahasya-of the transcendental form of Çré Kåñëa; madhyamatve-in the

separately create many new forms, but He simply manifests His own original form in many places at
once, as He wishes, by the agency of His inconceivable potencies. He manifests His own form in
many places just as single form may be reflected in many places by the use of mirrors. A person who
causes his form to be reflected in many mirrors cannot perform the functions of His senses through
the reflected forms: for example he cannot see, hear, touch, etc. through his reflected forms. This
may be true for an ordinary person, but for Lord Kåñëa He can see, hear, touch, and perform all
sensory activities through these "reflected" forms. This is the specific potency of Lord Kåñëa's
expanded or "reflected" forms.

sometimes they would be separated from Him. This meeting and separation of the Lord and His
devotees is a very wonderful activity effected by the Lord's yogamäyä potency.

   When Lord Kåñëa is not directly pesent before His devotees He remains present in His aprakaöa
(unmanifested) form. In this way, even when He had gone to Mathurä and Dvärakä, He remained
present before the gopés and other inhabitants of Våndävana. By either His prakaöa (manifest) or

aprakaöa (unmanifest) presence He always remains in Våndävana, Mathurä, and Dvaåakä.
Although superficially a description of His all-pervading feature as the Supersoul, Lord Kåñëa's
instruction to the gopés that "It is not possible for you to be separated from Me" (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.47.29), is actually a description of His eternal aprakaöa presence in Våndävana, and
the gopés constant perception of Him in the särasiké form of meditation. In this way, while
apparently speaking about the Supersoul, Kåñëa actually described His eternal prescence in
Våndävana and His eternal association with the residents of Våndävana. Such a method of
indirectly expressing one thing while appearing to say another may be seen in many places inVedic
literature. For example, such a device was used by Vidura to warn the Päëòavas travelling to the
house of lac, and a similar method of expression was also used by Närada Muni in his allegorical
explanations to the Haryaçvas and Savaläçvas, the sons of Mahäräja Dakña (as described in the
Sixth Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam).

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.157
records.text:
Text 1


yad evaà punar api tathaivopadiçati

yathä bhütäni bhüteçu
   khaà väyv-agnir jalaà mahé
tathähaà ca manaù-präëa-
   bhütendriya-guëäçrayaù

   yat-because; evam-in this way; punah again; api-also; tatha-in that way; eva-certainly; upadiçti-
instructs; yathä-just as; bhütäni-the material elements; bhüteçu-in the varieties of material
manifestation and in the moving and non-moving living entities; kham-ether; väyu-air; agniù-fire;
jalam-water; mahé-earth; tatha-in the same way; aham-I; ca- also; manaù-the mind; präëa-the life-
breath; bhüta- elements of the body;indriya-senses; guëa-and qualitities; açrayaù-the shelter.


   Superficially describing the all-pervading Supersoul, Lord Kåñëa actually described the gopés'
constant meditation on Him and their uninterrupted svärasiké perception of Him through strong
feelings of separation in the following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.29):

   "My dear gopés, just as the five material elements of earth, water, fire, air, and ether are all-
pervading within this material world, and present in the bodies of all living entities, in the same
way, I am always present within you. I reside in your minds, senses, and Your life-breath, for I have
taken shelter in all these places."*


Text 2

    yathä khädéni käraëa-rüpäëi bhütäni väyv-ädiñu sva-sva-kérya-rüpeñu bhüteñu avasthitäni.
taträkäçasya sthitir väyau vayor agnäv ity ädi, tathä bhavatéçv ahaà bahir anupalabhyamäno 'pi
nityaà tiñöhämety evärthaù. kathaà-bhüto 'ham? bhavaténäà mad-eka-jévätünäà mana-ädy-
äçrayaù anyathä nimeñam api mad-viyogena täny api na tiñöheyur iti bhävaù. yad vä kià-rüpas
tiñöhaséty äkäìkñäyäm äha bhavaténäm mana-ädy-äçraya-bhüto yo dvibhuja-çyämasundara-veëu-
vinodi-rüpas tad-rüpa eveti.

   yathä-the word "yathä"; ka-adéné-ether, and the other material elements; käraëa-rüpäëi-causes;
bhütäni- elements; väyu-ädisu-in air and other elements; sva-sva-own; kärya-rüpeçu-in the effects;
bhüteçu-in the elements; avasthitäni-situated; tatra-there; akäçasya-of ether; sthitiù-resting place;
väyau-in air; väyoù-of air; agnäu- in fire; iti-ädi-and the other elements in the same way; tathä-in
the same way; bhavatéçu-in you; aham-I; bahiù-outside; anupalabhyamänaù-not attainable; api-
although; nityam- eternally; tiñöhäma-I am situated; iti-thus; eva-certainly; arthaù-the meaning;
katham-bhütaù-like what?; aham-I am; bhavaténäm-of you; mat-eka-jévätünäm-for whom I am the
very life anbd soul; mahah-ädi-in the mind and other senses; äçrayaù-taken shelter; anyathä-
otherwise; nimeñam-for a second; api-even; mat-viyogena-by separation from Me; täni- they; api-
even; na-not; tiñöheyuhj-could be situated; iti- thus; bhävaù-the meaning; yat vä-or; kim-rüpaù-in
what for?; tiñöhasi-are you situated; iti-thus; äkäìkñyäm- in the desire; äha-he says; bhavaténäm-of
you; mahah-ädi- of the mind and other senses; äçrayah-bhütaù-taken shelter; yaù-who; dvi-bhuja-
with two hands; çyämasundara-whose form is black and beautiful; veëu-the flute; vinodi-playing;
rüpaù-with the form; tat-rüpaù-with that form; eva- certainly; iti-thus;


   This statement of Çré Kåñëa may be interpreted in the following way: "The material elements are
causes of each other. For example, ether is the cause of air, air of fire, fire of water, and water of
earth. Each elemental cause is situated within its effect. For example, ether is situated within air,
air within fire, fire within water, and water within earth. Because4 I am the cause of everything, I
am situated within everything in the same way, because as a general rule a cause is always situated
within its effect. Even though we have been externally separated, I am still remaining always within
you in this way. Especially for you, O gopés of Vraja, who have dedicated your life and soul to Me,
separation between us is not possible at any time, for I always reside within your minds and senses.
How do I reside there? In what form? I remain always there in My original form, playing the flute
with two hands and handsome with a dark complexion."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.158
records.text:
Text 1


   nanv itthaà prakäça-vaicitré kathaà syät, yayä viraha-saàyogayor yugapad eva sthitir ity

äsaìkyähya

ätmany evätmanätmänaà
   såje hanmy anupälaye
ätma-mäyänubhävena
   bhütendriya-guëätmaëa

    nanu-is it not so?; ittham-in this way; prakäça-of manifestation; vaicitré-wonder; katham-how is
it possible; syät-that it may be; yayä-by which; viraha-of separation; saàyogayoù-and association;
yugapat-simultaneously; eva- certainly; sthitiù-situation; iti-thus; äçaìkya-having doubted; aha-He
says; ätmani-in the atma; eva-certainly; atmäna-by the atma; atmänam-the atma; såje-I create;
hanmi-I destroy; anupälaye-I protect; ätma-mäya-anbhävena-by My own potency; bhüta-of the
elements; indriya-and senses; guëa-and qualities; atmanä-by the atma.


  Someone may object: How is it possible for the gopés to be simultaneously associated with Çré
Kåñëa, and then again separated from Him? This is very astonishing. In order to allay this doubt, Çré
Kåñëa spoke the following words in His message to the gopés (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.30):

   "My dear gopés, you should understand this appearance of Mine in My aprakaöa form in your
meditation on Me. By My inconceivable internal potency I appear in this aprakaöa form with all My
transcendental attributes and thus I relieve the distresses born from My absence."


Text 2


   ätmani ananta-prakäça-maye çré-vigraha-lakñaëe svasmin ätmanä svayam ätmänam prakäça-
viçeñam såje abhivyaïjayämi. kena? nimitta-bhütena ätma-mäyänubhävena acintyäyäù svarüpa-
çakteù prabhävena; svarüpa-bhütäyä nitya-çaktyä mäyäkhyäyä yutaù iti madhva-bhäçya-dhåta-catur-
veda-çikhätaù.

   ätmani-the word; "atmani"; ananta-unlimited; prakäça- manifestations; maye-consisting of; çré-
vigraha-lakñnëe-the form of Çré Kåñëa; svasmin-in His own; atmana-the word "atmana"; svayam-
means "personally;" ätmänam-the word "atmanam"; prakäça-viçeñam-means "specific manifestation;
såje-the word "såje"; abhivyaïjayämi-means "I manifest"' kena-how?; nimitta-bhütena-by His
instrument; ätma-mäya-anubhävena-by His potency; acintyäyäù-inconceivable; svarüpa-of His
transcendental form; çakteù-of the potency; mäya-akhyäyä-named maya; yutaù-endowed with; iti-
thus; madhva-of Madhvacarya; bhäçya-in the commentary; dhåta- quoted; catuh-veda-çikhätaù-
from the Catur-veda-sikha;


  In this verse the word "ätmanä" may be understood to mean "the form of Çré Kåñëa, which is
manifested in unlimited kinds of expansion". The word "svayam" may mean "personally", and the
word "ätmänam" may mean "this specific form"' The word "såje" may mean "I manifest". Understood

in this way, the verse may be interpreted to mean "Out of all my unlimited forms, I personally
appear in this specific form (the aprakaöa form perceived in svärasiké meditation)."
    One may ask: By what method does Lord Kåñëa appear in this way? The answer to this question
is that the Lord appears in this way by the agency of His personal inconceivable potency (ätma-
mäyänubhävena). This potency of the Lord is described in the following statement from the Catur-
veda-çikhä quoted in Madhväcärya's commentary explaining this verse:

   "The Supreme Lord possesses His own eternal potency, which is manifested from His own
transcendental form, and which is known as mäyä."


Text 3


   kédåçena? bhütendriya-guëätmanä bhütäni paramärtha-satyäni yäni mamendriyäëi, ye ca guëa-
rüpa-rasädayas teñäm ätmanä prakäçakenety arthaù. buddhéndriya iti paöhe ätmanä iti asya
viçeñaëam. buddhayo ntaùkaraëäni, indriyäëi bahiù-karaëäni, guëa-rüpädayas täni sarväëy api
ätmä svarüpaà yatra teneti.

   kidresena-what is the nature?; bhuta-indria-guna-atmana- the word "bhutendriya-gunatamana"
bhutani-the word "bhuta"; prama-artha-satyani-means "transcendental"; yani-which; mama- My;
indriyani-senses; ye-which; va-also; guna-qualities; rupa-rasa-adyaù-beginning with the beauty of
His transcendental form; tesam-of them; atmana-by the self; iti-prakasakena- manifesting; iti-thus;
arthaù-the meaning; buddhindriya-the word "bhuddhinriya; iti-thus; pathe-in the text; atmana-iti-
the worde "atmana" asya-of that word; visesanam-modifier; buddhayaù-the word "buddhi"; antah-
karanani-means the mind and intelligence; indriyani-the word "indriya; bahiù-karanani- means
"the external senses"; gunaù-qualifies; rupa-adyaù- beginning with beauty; tani-them; sarvani-all;
api-also; atma-self; svarupam-own form; yatra-where; tena-by that; iti- thus;


   One may ask: How is this aprakaöa form manifested? To this question the answer may be given:
Kåñëa appears with His own transcendental qualities and senses: "bhüendriya-guëätmanä". In this
word "bhüta" means "transcendental", "guëa" means the handsomeness of Lord Kåñëa's form and His
other transcendental attributes", and "ätmanä" means "manifesting". In some texts of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam we find the word "buddhéndriya" instead of "bhütendriya". According to this reading,
the Lord appears with His own transcendental mind and intelligence.


Text 4


   tad evam ävirbhüya anu paçcät kadäpi hanmi, tato 'nyatra gacchämi; han hiàsä-gatyoù. kadäpi
anu paçcät punaù pälaye, svayam ägatya palayämi, nija-viraha-dunän iti çeñaù. etat-käraëaà tu yat
tv aham bhavaténäà vai ity ädau vakñyate.

  tat-therefore; evam-in this way; ävirbhüya-having become manifested; anu-the word "anu";

paçcät-means "afterwards"; kadäpi-at a certain time; hanmi-I destroy; tataù-of this; anyatra-
otherwise; gacchämi-I go; han-the verbal root "han"; hiàça-gatyoù-in the sense of killing; kadäpi-at
a certain time; anu-the word "anu"; paçcät-means "afterwareds"; punaù-again; pälaye-I protect;
svayam- personally; ägatya-having arrived; palayämi-I maintain; nija-own; viraha-separation; dunän-
afflicted; iti-thus; señaù- the remainder; etat-of that; käraëam-the cause; tu-also; yat tv aham
bhavaténäm vai iti adau-in the Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.34; vakñyate-about to be described;


   In this verse (quoted in Text 1) the word "anu" means "after appearing in this way" and "hanmi"
means "I go". The verb "han" may mean either "to kill" or "to go". The word "pälaye" means "after
coming, I protect from the sufferings created by separation from Me". This will be described in
Çrémad-Bhäagavatam 10.47.34.


Text 5


   hanter arthäntare trayäëäm eka-karmakatve 'pi tam ätmänaà prakäçaà kadäcit tirodhäpayämi.
tasmät taà prakäçam äkåçya prakäça-vaividhyäm eké-karométy arthäh.

   hanteù-of the verb "han"; artha-antare-in the alternate meaning; trayänäm-of the three; eka-
karmakatve-in the single actor; api-also; tam-Him; ätmäna-own; prakäçam-form; kadäcit-at a
certain time; tirodhapayämi-disappears; tasmät-from that; tam-that; prakäçam-form; äkåçya-pulling;
prakäça-of form; vividhyäm-plurality; eké-karomi-I become one; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.


   If the alternate meaning of the verb "han" (to kill) is accepted, it may be interpreted to mean
that the Lord sometimes makes His form invisible. One example of this is when the thousands of
expansions (of Lord Kåñëa at Dvärakä meet together at a certain time and) become a single Kåñëa
(who enters the Sudharmä assembly house).


Text 6


   evam eva daçama-saptitamädhyäye svämibhir api vyäkhyätam evaà sarva-gåhebhyaù påthak
påthaì nirgatyänantaram eka eva sudharmaà präviçat iti.

   evam-in this way; eva-certainly; daçama-of the Tenth Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam; saptitama-
adhyäye-in the 70th Chapter; svämibhiù-by ÇRédhara Svami; api-certainly; vyäkhyätam-is
explained; evam-in this way; sarva-gåhebhyaù-from all the palaces in Dvaraka; påthak påthak-in
various forms; nirgatya-after having left; anantaram-afterwards; ekaù- one; eva-certainly; ;
sudharmam-the sudharama assembly house präviçat-entered; iti-thus;


  This is described in the following words by Çrédhara Svämé (in his commentary on Çrémad-

Bhägavatam 10.70.17):

   "The many expansions of Çré Kåñëa, having each left His own respective palace in Dvärakä,
become a single Kåñëa who then entered the Sudharmä assembly house."


Text 7


tathä ca madhva-bhäñya-dhåtaà padma-vacanam

sa devo bahudhä bhütvä
   nirguëaù puruñottamaù
eké-bhüya punaù çete
   nirdoño harir ädi-kåt iti.

   tathä-in the same way; ca-also; madhva-of Madhvacarya; bhäçya-in the commentary; dhåtam-
quoted; padma-of the Padma Purana; vacanam-the statement; saù-He; devaù-the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; bahudhä-many; bhütvä-having becoem; nirguëaù-above the three modes
of material nature; puruça- uttamaù-the Supreme Person; eké-bhüya-having become one; puhaù-
again; çete-lies down; nirdoçaù-free from al fault; hariù-Hari; ädi-kåt-the original creator of
everything; iti- thus;


   This is also confirmed by Çrépäda Madväcärya who, in his commentary on this verse quotes the
following statement from the Padma Puräëa:"

   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Hari, is the original creator of everything. He is
always free from any fault or defect, and He is always transcendental to the influences of the three
modes of material nature. He sometimes expands Himself into many forms, and then again all His
expansions enter Him, and He becomes one."


Text 8


   çrutiç ca çaìkara-bhäçya-dhåta sa ekadhä bhavati
tridhä bhavati ity ädyä.

  çrutiù-the Çruti-sastra; ca-also; çaìkara-of Çaìkaräcärya; bhäçya-in the commentary; dhåta-
quoted; saù-he; ekadhä-in one form; bhavati-is manifested; tridhä- in many forms; bhavati-is
manifested; tridhä-in many forms; bhavati-is manifested; iti-thus; ädyä-in the passage beginning.


   The manyfold expansions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are also described in the
following verse from the Çruti-çästra, (quoted in the commentary of Çankaräcärya):

  "The Supreme Personality of Godhead is sometimes manifested as one, and then again,
sometimes He expands Himself into many forms."


Text 9


   tad-anantaraà punar api tam ätmänaà pälaye punar abhivyajya nija-preñöha-janaiù saha
kréòayä sambhütänandaà karométy arthaù. evaà hanmy açlélo 'pi sva-viyogi-jana-viñaya-käruëya-
kåta-bhäväntareëa svayam eva prayukta iti na doña äçaìkyaù; chindyäà sva-bähum api vaù
pratiküla-çélam itivat.

    tat-anantaram-afterwards punaù-again; api-also; tam- that; ätmänam-atma; pälaye-I maintain;
punaù-again; abhivyaja-I manifest; nija-with my own; preñöha-janaih-dear devotees; saha-along
with; kréòayä-with pastimes; sambhüta-anandam-bliss; karomi-I experience; iti-thus; arthaù-the
meaning; evam-in this way; hanmi-I destroy; açlélaù-not a very pleasant word; api-although; sva-
viyogi-separated from Me; jana-personss; viçaya-field of experience; käruëya-merciful kåta-being;
bhäva-antareëa-because of love; svayam- personally; eva-certainly; prayuktaù-appeared; iti-thus; na-
not; dosaù-fault; äçaìkyaù-worthy of being suspected; chindyäm-sva bähum api vaù pratiküla-sétam
itivat-as Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.16.6


   In this verse the phrase "ätmänaà pälaye" means "I appear before My devotees and enjoy
transcendental bliss by performing pastimes in their association". One should not take it that the
use of the word "hanmi" is a literary fault in theis verse. A similar phrase is spoken by the Lord in
the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.16.6): "chindyäà sva-bähum api vaù pratiküla-çélam."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.159
records.text:
Text 1


   nanu prakaöam eva mathuräyäà vikréòaséty aträsmäkaà sambhävanä kathaà jäyatäm ity
äçaìkya täsäm evänubhävaà pramäëayati

ätmä jïänamayaù çuddho
   vyatirikto 'guëänvayaù
suçupti-svapna-jägradbhir
   mano-våttibhir éyate

   nanu-is it not so; prakaöam-manifested; eva-certainly; mathuräyäm-in Matura; vikréòasi-You
perform pastimes; iti- thus; atra-here; asmäkam-of us; sambhävanä-possibilty; katham-how is it

possible; jäyatäm-may become produced; iti- thus; äçaìkya-having doubted; täsäm-of the gopés; eva-
certainly; anubhävan-the direct experience; pramäëayati- demnstrates; ätmä-the self; jïäna-mayaù-
full of transcendental knowledge; çuddhaù-pure; vyatiriktaù-aloof from material entanglement;
aguëa-anvayaù-free from the three modes of material nature; suçupti in deep sleep; svapna-
dreaming sleep; jägradbiù-and the wakeful condition; manah-våttibhiù- with the activities of the
mind; éyate-goes.


   After hearing Lord Kåñëa's explanation of His aprakaöa presence in Våndävana, even after He
had gone to Mathurä, the gopés might protest: "My dear Kåñëa, at present You
are enjoying pastimes in Mathurä, how is it possible for You to be still present with us in the village
of Våndävana?" In order to answer the gopés' doubt, as well as to explain their svärasiké perception
of Him, Lord Kåñëa spoke the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.31):

   "This Personality of Godhead is free from all phases of material entanglement and from the grip
of the three modes of nature. He is pure and full of all transcendental knowledge. He appears in the
thoughts of His devotees whether they are awake, dreaming, or deeply asleep."*


Text 2


   yadvä, astäà tävad aprakaöa-léläyäà mad-viyogäbhäva-värtä prakaöa-léläyäm api
tathänusandhéyatäm ity äha ätmä jïänamayaù ity ädi.

léläyäm-in the manifested pastimes; api-also; tatha-in the same way; anusandéyatäm-may be
investigated; iti-thus;


   In this verse Çré Kåñëa says that just as He is present before His devotees in His manifested
(prakaöa) pastimes, He is also not separated from them in His aprakaöa (unmanifested) pastimes.
Although appearing to be absent from them, He is always manifested within their thoughts.


Text 3

bhavaténäà suçupty-ädi-lakñaëäbhiù mano våttibhir éyate anubhüyate eva.

   arthaù-the meaning; ca-also; ayam-this; ätmä-çabdaù- the word "atma"; asmin-in this context;
asmat-sabda-paraù- menas "I"; tataù-therefore; ca-also; ätmä-the word "ätmä"; aham-I; çré-kåñëa-
lakñaëaù-Çré Kåñëa; bhavaténäm-of the gopés; suçupti-ädi-lakñaëäbhiù-in wakefulness, dreaming,
and deep sleep; manah-våttibhiù-by the activities of the mind; éyate-is perceived; anubhüyate-is

   In this verse the word "ätmä" means "I, Çré Kåñëa", and the phrase "mano-våttibhir éyate" means "
I am perceived in meditation by the gopés when they are awake, dreaming, and even deeply

viçeçeëätirikta iti vä vyatiriktaù sarvottamaù. guëänvayaù sarva-guëa-çälé; ata eva sa ca sphürti-

käraëaà jïeyam.

   kédåsaù-what is His nature? jïänamayaù-jïänamaya"; nänä-in various; vidyä-departments of
knowledge; vidagdhaù-expert; çuddhaù-pure; doça-fault; rahitaù-withot; vigataù-separated;
atiriktaù-best; yasmät- from which; iti-thus; vä-or; viçeçeëa-specifically; atiriktaù-best; iti-thus; vä-
or; viçeçeëa-specifically; atiriktaù-best; iti-thus; vä-or; vyatiriktaù-the word "vyatiriktaù"; sarva-
uttamaù-means "the best of all"; guëa- anvayaù-the word " guëänvayaù" sarva-guëa'çälé-means "full
of all auspicious attributes"' atah eva-therefore; saù-He; ca-also; sphürti-is manifest; rüpaù-whose
form; ayam-this; anubhavaù-direct perception; kadäcit-at certain times; säkñät-käratvaya-for direct
appearance; api-also; kalpyate-is suitable; iti-thus; cira-käla-for a long time; virahe-in separation; ai-
even; täsäm-of the gopés ; sadhukñaëa-of intensifying the love; käraëam-the cause; jïeyam-may be
known.


   How is this Supreme "ätmä" described? He is expert in all kinds of knowledge (j"änamayaù), pure
and free from any fault (çuddhah), superior to all living entities (vyatiriktaù), and full of all
auspicious attributes (sarva-guëa-çälé). The perception of Lord Kåñëa's aprakaöa form in the gopés'
meditation enlivened them, increased their love for Him, and made it possible for them to bear the
long period of their spearation from Him.


Text 5


   atra suñupte 'pi tat-spürti-nirdeñaù sarvadaiva sphuräméti-mäträ-tätparyakaù. yadvä tatra täsäà
svapna-jägrator ananya-våttitvaà siddham eva. våtty-antaräsambhavät tu çré-kåñëa-samädhi-
lakñaëe suçupte 'pi tasminn eva svapna-jägrad-gatänäà våtti-vaicitréëäà tad-anubhävita-
mäträveçatayä praveço bhavati. tad uttara-käle präkåtaiù sukham aham asvapsam itivat täbhiù sa
evänusandhéyata iti tathoktam.

   atra-here; susupte-in deep sleep; api-even; tat-of Çré Kåñëa; sphürti-nirdeçaù-appearance; sarvada-
at every moment; eva-certainly; sphurämi-I am manifest; iti-thus; mäträ-only; tätparyakaù-meaning;

yad vä-or; tatra-there; täsäm-of the gopés; svapna-in dream; jägratoù-or awake; ananya-without any
other; våttitvam-activity; siddham- perfection; eva-certainly; ; våtti-activity; antara-other;
asämbhavät-because of the absence; tu-but; çré-kåñëa-samädhi-lakñaëe-in ecstatic meditation on Çré
Kåñëa; suçupte-in deep sleep; api-even; tasmin-in that; eva- certainly; svapna-jägrat-gatänäm-of the
gopés who were either awake or asleep; våtti-vaicitréëäm-who activities were wonderful; tat-
anubhävita-by that perception of Çré Kåñëa in constant meditation; mätra-only; aveçatayä-by the
entrance; praveçaù-appearance; bhavati-is; tat-therefore; uttara-käle-after that; präkåtaiù-by
ordinary conditioned souls; sukham-happily; aham-I; asvapsam-slept; itivat-like; täbhiù-by the gopés;
saù-He; anusandhéyate-was seen in meditatin; iti-thus; tatha-in that way; uktam-said.


   Lord Kåñëa appeared before them even in their sleep. That is the meaning of His statement: "I
am always manifest before you." This proves that whether awake or asleep they did not do anything
but meditate on Him. Whether awake, asleep, or in deep sleep, the gopés were always wonderfully
able to see Lord Kåñëa in meditation. In this way Lord Kåñëa entered them and appeared before
them. The gopés constantly saw Lord Kåñëa, even in the condition of dreamless deep sleep (the kind
of sleep which, when experienced by ordinary conditioned souls, is described by them with the
words "I slept well".).


Text 6


tathä hi garuòe

jägarat-svapna-suñupteñu
   yoga-sthasya ca yoginaù
yä käcin manaso våttiù
   sa bhavaty acyutäçrayä iti

   tatha hi-furthermore; garuòe-in the Garuda Purana; jägrat-either waking; svapna-dreaming;
suçupteçu-or in deep sleep; yoga-sthasya-situated in yoga; ca-also; yoginaù-the aspiring
transcendentalist; yä-which; käcit-some; manasaù-fo the mind; våttiù-activity; sa-that; bhavati-is;
acyuta-to the infalliable Supreme Personality of Godhead; açrayä-in relation with; iti-thus;


  Constant meditation on Lord Kåñëa is also described in the following verse from the Garuòa
Puräëa:

   "Whether awake, dreaming, or in deep sleep, transcendentalists continuously meditate on the
infallible Supreme Personality of Godhead (Lord Acyuta)."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.160
records.text:
Text 1


   nanu tathäpy asmäkam viraha eva sarvopamärdakaù sphurati, kià karma ity äçaìkya, hanta yadi
mad-viyogitäbhimäni-mano-våttià katham api roddhuà çaknutha, tadä svata eva nitya-
saàyogitvam udeçyatéty evam upadeçena vaktuà yoga-çästra-prakriyäm äha dväbhyäm

   nanu-is it not so?; tatha-api-nevertheless; asmäkam-our; virahaù-seperation; eva-certainly; sarva-
completely; upämardakaù-devestating; sphurati-is manifest; kim-what is this?; karma-activity; iti-
thus; äçaìkya-doubting; hanta- indeed; yadi-if; mat-from Me; viyogita-seperation; abhimäni-
considering; manaù-of the mind; våttim-activity; katham api- somehow; roddhum-to obstruct;
çaknutha-you may be able; tadä-then; svataù-personally; eva-certainly; nitya- eternal;saàyogitvam-
association; udeçyati-will become manifested; evam-in this way; upadeçena-by the instruction;
vaktum-to speak; yoga-çästra-of the yoga-scriptures; prikriyaà-activities; äha-He spoke; dväbhyäm-
in the next two verses.


    At this point the gopés might reply: "We now feel the devastating effect of seperation from You,
O Kåñëa." How is it that You now tell us we are not separated from You?" Considering that the
gopés might raise this objection, Çré Kåñëa decided to instruct them with the following words: "My
dear friends, if you become able to free Yourselves from the illusion of thinking that You are
separated from Me, you will find that will have My association at every moment." Intending to give
this instruction to the gopés, Lord Kåñëa spoke the next two verses from Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.47.32-33) in which He describes the process of meditation prescribed in the yoga-çästras. The
first of these verses (10.47.32) follows:


Text 2


yenendriyärthän dhyäyeta
   måçä svapnavad utthitaù
tan-niruddhyäd indriyäëi
   vinidraù pratyapadyate

   yena-by whom; indriya-arthän-the objects of the senses; dhyäyeta-may meditate; måçä-false;
svapnavat-like a dream; uttitaù-awakened; tat-that; niruddhyät-by supressing; indriyäëi-the senses;
vinidraù-awakened from sleep; pratyapadyata-becomes.


    "The living entity in his sleeping or dreaming condition sees his dream body, senses, and sense-
objects as real, and in his awake condition sees the same things as unreal. In the same way one who
is awake to spiritual knowledge sees that the external material body, senses, and sense-objects are
temporary. He should check the activities of the material senses, therefore, in order to actually
understand the eternal Absolute Truth."*

Text 3


   utthitaù pumän yathä mithyä-bhütam eva svapnaà dhyäyati, evaà badhitän api indriyärthan
çabdädén yena manasä dhyäyeta cintayet, dhyäyaàç ca yenendriyäëi pratyapadyata präpa, tan-
manaù vinidrah analasaù sana niruddhyät niyacched iti.

   utthitaù-risen from sleep; pumän-person; yathä-just as; mithya bhütam-false; eva-certainly;
svapnam-dream; dhyäyati-considers; evam-in the same way; badhitän-checked; api-although;
nidriya-of the senses; arthän-the objects; çabda-adin-beginning with sound; yena-by which; manasä-
by the mind; dhyäyaeta-cintayet-may consider; dhäyayan-thinking in this way; ca-and; yena-with
the mind; indriyäëi-the senses; pratyapadyata präpa-attains; tat-mahaù-his mind; vindiraù analasaù-
awake; san-being; niruddhyät-niyacchet- controls; iti-thus;


   This verse explains that just as a person who is awakened (utthitaù) from a dream sees all the
activities of the dream as unreal. In the same way a transcendentalist who is awake (vinidraù) to
spiritual knowledge should consider (dhyäyeta) that the sense-objects (indriyärthän), such as
sound, sight, smell, taste, and touch, when manifested in matter are similarly unreal because they
are temporary. Such a wise person should restrict (niruddhyät) the activities of the material senses
in order to attain a higher spiritual goal.


Text 4


   yadyapi svapnädivat tad-vihäras täsu näjïänädhyastaù, prakaöa-léläyäà tasyäpräptes täsäm
evänubhäva-siddhatvät, tathäpy aprakaöa-léläyäà nitya-saàyogam anusandhäpayituà tasya
tädåçatvenaivopadeço bhagavatä yogya iti tathoktam. ekäàçe 'pi saàyogo viyogo nästy eveti va
tathoktam.

   yadyapi-although; svapna-adivat-like a dream or other kind of illusion; tat-from Kåñëa; viharaù-
the separation; täsu- among the gopés; na-not; ajïäna-ignorance; adhyastaù-may be attributed;
prakaöa-léläyäm-in the Lord's manifested pastimes; tasya-of Lord Kåñëa; apräpteù-from not
attaining; täsäm-of the gopés; eva-certainly; anubhäva-of direct perception; siddhatvät-because of
perfection; tathapi- nevertheless; aprakaöa-léläyäm-in the unmanifested pastimes; nitya-eternal;
saàyogam-contact; sanusandhäpayitum-to reveal; tasya-of that; tädåçatvena-like this; upadeçaù-
instruction; bhagavatä-by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; yogyaù-appropriate; iti-thus; tatha-
in that way; uktam- described; eka-aàçe-in one expansion; api-although; saàyogaù-contact;
viyogaù-separation; na-not; asti-is; eva- certainly; iti-thus; va-or; tatha-in that way; uktam-
explained


   In the verse Çré Kåñëa hinted to the gopés that their conception of being separated from Him was

an illusion, like the illusions one sees in a dream. He wanted to explain to them that if they were
associating with Him in His aprakaöa feature, by constantly meditatting on Him, they were
certainly not separated from Him, but were continuously associating with Him.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.161
records.text:
Text 1


mano-nirodham eva stauti

etad-antaù samämnayo
   yogaù sänkhyaà manésinäm
tyägas tapo damaù satyaà
   samudränta iväpagäù

   manaù-of the mind; inrodham-control; eva-certainly; stauti-He glorifies; etat-having Him; antaù-
as their goal; samämnayaù-study of the Vedic literature; yogaù-yogah sänkhyam-empiric
philosophy; manéçinäm-of the philosophers; tyägaù-renunciation; tapaù-austerity; damaù-control of
the mind; satyam-truthfulness; samudra-antaù-entering the ocean; iva-just like; apagäù-rivers.


   In the next verse (10.47.33), Lord Kåñëa continued His explanation, hinting to the gopés that
because they were always thinking of Him, they were therefore not actually separated from Him.
Lord Kåñëa said:

   "My dear gopés, all kinds of spiritual paths are intended to bring the follower closer to Me in
Kåñëa consciousness. Different processes of spiritual realization such as Vedic study, yoga, study of
saìkhya philosophy (as followed by great thinkers), renunciation, austerity, self-control,
truthfulness, and other auspicious activities, are intended to bring the followers closer to Me. All
these different ways of determining the goal of life are compared to rivers. I am like the ocean, and
as rivers flow down towards the ocean, all attempts for knowledge flow towards Me."*


Text 2


   eña mano-nirodho 'ntaù samäptiù phalaà yasya saù. samämnäyaù vedaù, sa tatra paryavasyatéty
arthaù. märga-bhede 'py ekatra paryavasäne dåñöäntaù samaudräntäh äpagaù nadyaù iva iti. yasmät
sarvair eva vedädividbhiù praçasyate mano-nirodhas tasmäd yüyam api mad-viyogäbhimäni-mano-
våttim niyacchateti padya-dvayena dhvanitam.

   eñaù-this; manaù-of the mind; nirodhaù-control; antaù- end; samäptiù-conclusion; phalam-

result; yasya-of whom; saù-he; samämnäyaù-the word "samämnäya"; vedaù-means the Vedas; saù-
that; tatra-here; paryavasyati-attain completion; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; märge-of spiritual
paths; bhede-in the distinction; api-although; ekatra-in one place; prayavasäne-in the conclusion;
dåçtäntaù-an example; samudra-in the ocean; antaù-the word "äpagaù"; nadyaù-mens "rivers"; iva-
just like; iti-thus; yasmät- because; sarvaiù-by all; veda-adi-vidbhiù-the knowers of Vedic literatures;
praçasyate-is pacified; manaù-of the mind; nirodhaù-control; tasmät-therefore; yüyam-you; api-also;
mat-viyoga-abhimäni-considering youselves sepaerated from Me; manaù-of the mind; våttim-
activity; niyacchata-you should control; iti-thus; padya-dvayena-by these two verses; dhvanitam-
spoken in this way.


   In this verse Çré Kåñëa gives the example of the rivers and the ocean. Just as many rivers flow to
the ocean, in the same way, study of the Vedic literatures, and other spiritual practices all find their
ultimate conclusion in Kåñëa consciousness. Çré Kåñëa also explains to the gopés that they who
understand the meaning of the Vedas carefully control the activities of the mind. Therefore Lord
Kåñëa advises the gopés to control their minds and become free from the misconception of thinking
that they are separated from Him.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.162
records.text:
Text 1


   nanu, aho yadi tvad-virahena vayam ati-duùkitä ity ataù kåpälu-cittas tvam asmabhyaà nija-
präpti-sädhanam upadiçasi, tarhi svayaà kim u prakaöam eva nayasi, tasmät kaitavam evedäm tava
kåpälutvam ity äçaìkyäha

   nanu-is it not so?; aho-Oh; yadi-if; tvat-from You; virahena-by separation; vayam-we; ati-
duùkhitäù-greatly distresses; iti-thus; ataù-therefore; kåpalu-with a merciful; cittaù-heart; tvam-
You; asmabhyam-to us; nija-präpti-for attaining You; sädhanam-method; upadiçasi-You are
teaching; tarhi-then; svayam-personally; kim u-why is it?; prakatam-appearance; eva-certainly; na-
not; ayasi-you are manifesting; tasmät-for this reason; kaitavam-cheating; eva- certainly; idam-this;
tava-Your; kåpälutvam-mercy; iti- thus; äçaìkya-considering that the gopés might think in this way;
aha-Lord Kåñëa said.


   At this point Çré Kåñëa considered that the gopés response to His instructions might take the
form of the following thoughts:

   "My dear Kåñëa, we are certainly distressed by Your long absence. You advertise Yourself as very
merciful by giving this philosophical instruction to us. However, if you are actually merciful to us,
then why do You not return to Våndävana and appear before us as associate with us as before. We
think that Your clever words and Your so-called mercy to us are simply meant for cleverly cheating

us."

   Considering that the gopis might be thinking in this way, Lord Kåñëa spoke the following words
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.34):


Text 2


yat tv ahaà bhavaténäm vai
   düre varte priyo dåçäm
manasaù sannikarsärthaà
   mad-anudhyana-kämayä

   yat-because; tu-certainly; aham-I; bhavaténäm-of you; vai-certainly; düre-far away; varte-I
remain; priayù-dear; dåçäm-to the eyes; manasaù-of the mind; sannikarsa-of attracting; artham-for
the purpose; mat-upon Me; anudhyana- meditation; kämyayä-with great desire.


   "My dear gopés, although you were accostumed to love Me from the very beginning of your lives,
in order to increase your superexcellent love for Me, I have purposely separated Myself from you. I
have done this so that you may be in constant meditation on Me."*


Text 3


   bhavaténäà dåçäà priyaù apy aham yad düre varte, tad-bhavaténäà mad-anudhyänecchayä yaù
manasaù sannikarñaù tad artham mama bhavan-nikaöe sthitau mad-arthaà bhavaténäà
dåçyeväveçaù syäd düre tu manasy eveti tatra mama sannikarñam syäd ity etad arthaù.

   bhavaténäm-of you; dåsäm-of the eyes; priyaù-dear; api-although; aham-I am; yat-because; düre-
far away; varte- I remain; tat-therefore; bhavaténäm-of you; mat-upon Me; anudhyäna-meditation;
icchayä-with a desire; yaù-who; manasaù-of the mind; sannikarçaù-attraction; tat-artham-for this
purpose; mama-My; bhavan-you; nikaöe-near; sthitau- situation; mat-artham-for My sake;
bhavaténäm-of you; dåçya- by the sight; iva-like; aveçaù-entrance; syät-may be; düre-from a distance;
tu-but; manasi-in the mind; eva- certainly; iti-thus; utatra-there mama-My; sannikarçam-
attraction; syät-may be; iti-thus; etat-this; arthaù-the meaning.


   In this verse Çré Kåñëa says to the gopés:

   "Although you are all full of love for Me and very eager to always see Me (bhavaténäà dåçäm
priyaù), I have now separated Myself from your company (yad düre varte) In order that you may
constandly meditate upon Me (manasaù sannikarñärtham). In this way you may always see Me
within your minds, just as formerly you always saw Me with your eyes."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.163
records.text:
tad eva nidarçayati

yathä düra-care preñöhe
    mana äviñya vartate
stréëäà ca na tathä cetaù
    sannikåñöe 'kñi-gocare

ca kärät stréñu preñöhasya ca.

   tat-therefore; eva-certainly; nidarçayati-Lord Kåñëa reveals; yathä-just as; düra-care-faraway;
preñöhe- beloved; manah-the mind; äviñya-having entered; vartate- remains; stréëäm-of women; ca-
and; na-not tathä-in the same way; cetaù-the mind sannikåçte-attracted; akñi-gocare-in the sense of
sight; ca-kärät-from the word "ca (and)"; stréçu-among women; preñöhasya-of the beloved; ca-also;


   Lord Kåñëa continued His explanation in the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.35):

   "When a woman's beloved is away, she thinks of Him meditatively, and he is present before her.
In fact she is more conscious of him than when he was actually present. In the same way you have
become more conscious of Me in this condition of separation then when I was directly present
before you."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.164
records.text:
manaù-sannikarñe kià syät taträha

mayy äveçya manaù kåñëe
  vimuktäçeña-våtti yat
anusmarantyo mäà nityaà
  acirän mäà upeñyatha

   vimuktaù açeñaù viraha-tat-käraëa-bhävanä-rüpaù våttayaù yena tan-manaù mayi kåñëa-rüpa
eva äveçya mäà kåñëa-rüpam eva acirät eva samépa eva eçyatha, ananya-vedyatayä präpsyatha.

   manaù-of the mind; sannikarçe-in the attraction; kim- that result; syät-may occur; tatra-in this
connection; aha- Çré Kåñëa says; mayi-in Me; äveçya-having entered; manaù-the mind; kåñëe-Kåñëa;
vimukta-açeña-våtti- free from thinking of anything else; yat-which; anusmarantyaù- meditating;
maà-on Me; nityam-constantly; acirät-quickly; mäm-Me; upeçyatha-you will attain; vimuktaù-
freed; açeñaù-complete; viraha-separation; tat-käraëa-that cause; bhävanä-of meditation; rüpaù-in

the form; våttayaù-activities; yena-by which; tat-manaù-the mind; mayi-in Me; kåñëa-rüpe-in the
form of Kåñëa; eva- certainly; äveçya-having entered; mäm-Me; kåñëa-rüpam- in the form of Kåñëa;
eva-certainly; aciräte-quickly; eva- certainly; samépe-near; eva-certainly; eçyatha-you will go;
ananya-vedyatayä-without being aware of anyone else; präpsyatha-you will attain.


   In the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.36), Lord Kåñëa describes the result obtained by the
gopés' constant meditation on Him:

   "My dear gopés, because you constantly think of Me without thinking of anything else, or ever
forgetting Me, You will quickly attain Me."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.165
records.text:
Text 1


tarhi kathaà prakaöaà mägacchase? taträha

yä mayä kréòatä rätryäà
   vane 'smin vraja ästhitaù
alabdha-rasaù kälyäëyo
   mäpur mad-vérya-cintayä

   tarhi-then; katham-why is it?; prakaöam ma agacchasi-you are not present before us; tatra-to this
question; aha-Lord Kåñëa replies; yä-which; mayä-with Me; kréòatä- performing pastimes; rätryäm-
at night; vane asmin-in this forest of Våndävana; vraje-in Vraja; ästhitaù-situated; älabdha-not
attained; rasaù-dance; kälyäëyaù-fortunate gopés; ma-Me; apuù-attained; mat-vérya-of My
transcendental glories; cintayä-by meditation.


  The gopés might reply to this statement by saying:

  "If by thinking of You one quickly attains Your association, then why have You not already
appeared before us?"

  To answer this question, Çré Kåñëa spoke the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.37):

   "My dear gopés, when I performed the räsa dance with you in the evening of the çarat season in
this forest of Våndävana, some fortunate gopés were forcibly prevented from going to see Me. These
gopés immediately left their bodies and quickly attained My eternal association by constantly
thinking of My transcendental glories. In this way they quickly attained Me by thinking of Me."*

Text 2


   tädvad bahir-vighna-väncanärthaà ity arthaù. tä hi tad-rätri-prakaöa-rasa-mätram alabdhavatyo
'py asmin våndävana eva sarva-vighëaspastaprakaöa-vicitra-kréòa-nidhänaà mäm apur eveti. tathä
ca väsana-bhäñya-dhåtam markandeya-väcanam:

tadäném eva taù präptaù
   çrémantaà bhakta-vatsalam
dhyänataù paramänandaà
   kåñëaà gokula-näyikaù iti.

   tadvat-in that way; bahiù-external; vighna-impediments; väncanä-artham-for removing; iti-thus;
arthaù-the meaning; täù-the gopés; hi-certainly; tat-rätri-on that night; prakaöa-manifest; rasa-
mätram-the rasa dance; alabdhavatyah-not attaining; api-although; asmin-in this; våndävane- forest
of Våndävana; eva-certainly; sarva-all; vighëa- impediments; aspasta-not manifest; aprakaöa-
aprakaöa, unmanifest presence; vicitra-wonderful; kréòa-pastimes; nidhänam-abode; mäm-Me; apuù-
attained; eva-certainly; iti- thus; tathä-in the same way; ca-also; väsana-bhäçya-in the commentary
Väsana-bhäçya; dhåtam-quoted; markandeya-of the Markandeya Purana; väcanam-the statement;
tadäném-then; eva-certainly; taù-the gopés; präptaù-attained; çrémantam- full of the transcendental
beauty and opulence; bhakta-to the devotees; vatsalam-affectionate; dhyänataù-by meditation;
parama-anandam-full of transcendental bliss; kåñëam-Çré Kåñëa; gokula-of Gokula; näyikaù-the
ladies; iti-thus.


   In this verse Çré Kåñëa says that when certain gopés were prevented from entering the arena of
the räsa dance He personally appeared before them in His aprakaöa form, and those gopés gave up
their bodies mediatating on Kåñëa and directly seeing Him in His aprakaöa feature, and in this way
they attained the direct association of Çré Kåñëa, who eternally enjoys wonderful pastimes with His
devotees. The same incident is also described in the following verse from the Märkaëòeya Puräëa,
quoted in the Väsana-bhäñya:

   "When some of the gopés were prevented from entering the arena of the räsa-dance, they gave up
their bodies meditating on Lord Kåñëa, who is full of transcendental bliss, handsomeness, and
opulence, and who is full of love for His devotees. By meditating on Him in that way, those gopés
attained His eternal association."


Text 3


   taträpi kälyäëyaù sarva-vighëa-rahitaù. arthäntare sa-çarira eva ca. täsäm çarira-parityägädikaà
tu mayikam eveti bhävaù. tasmät täsäm vraje prakaöyenänupälämbhät tathä mayi bhaktir hi
bhütänäm ity adi vakñyamänänusärena markaëòeya-vacanänusärena ca tadiyäbhipsita-rüpa-rüpa-

viläsasyaiva mama präpteù siddhätväc ca vidyata eva prakaöayä asya lilayaù påthak tasminn anya
léla, tasyäm ca mäm eva yusmäkam api sthitir adhyävasiyatam.

   taträpi-nevertheless; kälyäëyaù-the word "kälyänyaù"; sarva-from all; vighëa-impediments;
rahitaù- free; artha-antare-in a second meaning; sa-çarira-with the body; eva-certainly; ca-also;
täsäm-of these gopés; çarira-the body; parityäga-abandonment; adikam-beginning with; tu-but;
mayikam-material; eva-certainly; iti-thus; bhavaù-the meaning; tasmät-therefore; täsäm-of the
gopés; vraje-in Vrajajbhumi; prakaöyena-y the manifestation; anupälämbhät-because of not being
perceived; tathä-in that way; mayi bhaktih hi bhütänäm iti adi-in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.44:


mayi bhaktir hi bhütänäm
   amåtatväya kalpate
diñöyä yad äsén mat-sneho
   bhavaténäà mad-äpanaù

vakñyamäna-to be spoken; anusärena-in accordance with; markaëòeya-of the Markaëòeya Purana;
vacana-the statement; anusarena-in accordance with; ca-also; tadiya-His; abhipsita- desired; rüpa-
form; viläsyasya-and pastimes; eva-certainly; prakaöayäù-manifested; asyaù-of this; lilayaù-pastimes;
påthak-variously; tasmin-in this; anya-another; léla- pastime; tasyaà-in that pastime; ca-also; ma-

   In this verse the word "kälyäëyaù" may be interpreted to mean either "free from all impediments"
or "along with the body". If the second interpretation is accepted, it is to be understood that these
gopés left behind material bodies in order to convince their husbands that they had not gone to
Kåñëa, although in their original spiritual forms they attained the association of Lord Kåñëa in His
aprakaöa pastimes.
   These gopés entered the etenal spiritual world to associate with Lord Kåñëa and enjoy pastimes
with Him in the specific way they desired. This is described in the previous statement quoted from
Märkaëòeya Puräëa and also in the following verse spoken by Lord Kåñëa in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.82.44):

   "Lord Kåñëa told the gopés: The means of attaining My favor is loving service unto Me, and
fortunately you are all thus engaged. Those living beings who render service unto Me are eligible to
be transferred to the spiritual world and attain eternal life with knowledge and bliss."*


Text 4


  yam eva léläà madiyä-vrajägamanasakåt-pratijïänusarena çéghram eva yadu-puryaù sakäçäd
bhavat-prema-yantritayä samagatyähaà sarvebhya eva vraja-väsibhyaù santatam darçayiñyaméti

asakåt-many times; pratijïa-promis; anusrena-in accordance with; çéghram- quickly; eva-certainly;
yadu-puryaù sakäçät-from Dvaraka; bhagavat-prema-by love of God; yantritaya-by the controlling
power; samagatya-having met; aham-I; sarvebhyaù-to all; eva- certainly; vraja-väsibhyaù-the
residents of Vrahabhumi; santatam-continually; darçayiñyami-I will reveal; iti-thus; bhavaù-the
meaning; asmin-in this; iti-thus; nirdeçät-by specifically mentioning; tädäném-then; api-also; svasya-
of Himself; våndävanästhatvam-residence in Våndävana; sucayati-He indicates; prakärene-passage;
asmin-in this; idam-this; uktam-said; bhavati-is;


   In these verses it is as if Kåñëa had said to the gopés:

   "I am completely submissive to the pure love of My devotees, and therefore every day I leave the
city of the Yadus and come to Vrajabhümi, revealing My prakaöa form to the residents there. This is
just according My repeated promise to return to Våndävana."

   We may also note that the use of the word "asmin" (in this Våndävana) (in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.4737, quoted in Text 1) indicates Çré Kåñëa remaining in Våndävana, even after it was
understood by the people in general that He was living in the city of the Yadus.


Text 5


na hy atra täsäm adhyätama-vidyä çreyas-käré bhavati

tasmän mad-bhakti-yuktasya
   yogino vai mad-ätmanaù
na jïänaà na ca vairägyaà
   prayaù çreyo bhaved iha iti bhägavate.

   na-not; hi-cerainly; atra-in this connection; täsäm-of the gopis; adhyätama-transcendental; vidyä-
knowledge; çreyah-käré-better; bhavati-is; tasmät-therefore; maj-bhakti-yuktasya-of one who has
devotion for Me; yoginaù- engaged in bhakti-yoga; vai-certainly; mat-ätmanaù-who has become
completely dedicated to Me; na-not; jïänam- transcendental knowlegde; na-not; ca-and; vairägyam-
renunciation; prayaù-generally; çreyaù-better; bhavet-may be; iha-here. iti-thus; bhägavata-spoken
by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.


   The gopés were able to attract Çré Kåñëa to continuously stay among them in His aprakaöa form
because they were situated in the platform of pure devotional service, a position more exalted than
the attainment of transcendental knowledge or the performance of severe austerities. That
devotional service to Çré Kåñëa is superior to the cultivation of knowledge or austerity is confirmed
by Lord Kåñëa Himself in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.20.31):

   " A pure devotee who is completely dedicated to My service is already situated in the topmost

perfection of life. His position will not be improved by adopting the inferior activities of cultivation
of transcendental knowledge or performance of severe austerities."*


Text 6


  jïäne prayäsam udapäsya namanta eva jévanti iti brahmaëä ca sädharaëa-bhaktänäm apy
anupadeyatvenoktatvät. na ca tac-chravaëena täsäm viraha-jvala samyati.

   The cultivation of impersonalism will not extinguish the burning fire of the gopés' separation
from Kåñëa. Even for ordinary devotees, the cultivation of impersonal spiritual knowledge is never
recommended. This is described in the following verse spoken by Lord Brahmä to Lord Kåñëa in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.3):

   "My dear Lord, those devotees who have thrown away the impersonal conception of the
Absolute Truth and have therefore abandoned discussing empiric philosophical thruths should hear
from self-realized devotees about Your holy name, form, pastimes and qualitities. They should
completely follow the principles of devotional service and remain free from illicit sex, gambling,
intoxication and animal slaughter. Surrendering themselves fully with body, words and mind, they
can live in any äçrama or social status. Indeed, You are conquered by such persons, although You
are always unconquerable."*



Text 7


taà syämaà manoharaà vinä sädharana-bhaktänäm api

   svargäpavarga-na rakeçv
      api tulyärtha-darsinaù ity ukta-diça

   tam-Him; syämam-the blackish form of Çré Kåñëa; manah-haram-enchanting to the mind; vinä-
without; sädharana-ordinary; bhaktänäm-of devotees; api-even; svarga-apavarga-narakaesu api

näräyaëa-paräù sarve
   na kutaçcana bibhyati
svargäpavarga-narakeçv
   api tulyärtha-darçinaù


  Even ordinary devotees reject the knowledge and liberation offered by the impersonalists.
Ordinary devotees reject these things because they prevent one from seeing and understanding the
handsome dark form of Çré Kåñëa. That the devotees reject the liberation offered by the
impersonalists is described in the following verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (6.10.28):

   "Devotees solely engaged in the devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead,
Näräyaëa, never fear any condition of life. For them the heavenly planets, liberation and the
hellish planets are all the same, for such devotees are interested only in the service of the Lord."*


Text 8


   nätyantikaà vigaëayasy api te prasädam ity ady ukta-diça vä heya-rupatvenänubhävät.

   That the devotees reject the impersonalists illusory liberation is also confirmed in the words of
the Four Kumäras to the Supreme Personality of Godhead (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 3.15.48):

   "Persons who are very expert and most intelligent in understanding things as they are engage in
hearing narrations of the auspicious activities and pastimes of the Lord, which are worth chanting
and worth hearing. Such persons do not care even for the highest material benediction, namely
liberation, to say nothing of other less important benedictions like the material happiness of the

heavenly kingdom."*


Text 9


täsäm tu sva-rasasya parama-virodhy eva tat. purvaà ca

çruyataà priya-sandeço
   bhavaténäà sukhävahaù ity evoktam

   täsäm-of the gopés; tu-also; sva-rasasya-of their own mellows of devotional service to Çré Kåñëa;
parama-supreme; virodhi-obstruction; eva-certainly; tat-that impersonalist conception of spiritual
knowledge; purvam-formerly; ca-also; çruyatam-let it be heard; priay-of your beloved Kåñëa;
sandeçaù-the message; bhavaténäm-of You; sukha-happiness; avahaù-bringing; iti-thus; eva-

  The impersonalist theory is the greatest possible impediment to the gopés' ecstatic love of Kåñëa,
which is described by Uddhava in these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.28):

   "My dear gopés, please hear this message from Lord Kåñëa, the Supreme Lord whom You love
very dearly. Hearing this message from Kåñëa will greatly delight you."*

gamya iti. çré-bhagavän vraja-deviù.

   ataù-from this; uktam-spoken; täsäm-of the gopés; eva-certainly; abhipraya-of the intention;
kathane-in the statement; çré-svämibhiù-by ÇRédhara Svami; api-also; nänu-is it not so?; kim-what?;
anyan-others; iva-just like; asmän-to us; ätma-vidyaya-with the false theories of the impersonlists;
lobhayasi-You are cheating; vayam-we; tu-but; sarva-with all; sundara-beautiful; sarva-with all;
alankarena ornaments; tvayä-with you; viraham-separation; na-not; eva- certainly; sahämahe-we

iyam-this; iti-thus; ukte-said; eva- certainly; arthaù-the meaning; bhavati-is; antah-angaù-hidden
and confidential; saù-he; ca-also; çré-yudhiñöhirasya-of Maharaja yuddhiçthira; iva-just like; täsaà-of
gopés; eva- certainly; gamyaù-approachable; iti-thus; çré-bhagavän- spoken by the Supreme

   In his commentary on Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.34, Çrédhara Svämé gives following glimpse into

the gopés' thoughts when they heard Çré Kåñëa's message, The gopés thought:

    "O Kåñëa, why are you trying to cheat us by speaking these theories of the impersonalists to us as
if we were outsiders? You may speak in this way to others, but not to us. O Lord, we think that You
are the ultimate in all handsomeness, and we are completely unable to tolerate being seperated from
You."

   When traveling to the house of lac where Duryodhana had planned to kill the Päëòavas, Vidura
spoke a riddle to the five Päëòavas hinting the nature of Duryodhana's plan, and Yudhiñöhira was
able to undertand the information concealed in Vidura's words. In the same way Çré Kåñëa
informed the gopés of His eternal presence among them in His aprakaöa form and the gopés were
able to understand the meaning of this riddle He spoke to them.

  The gopés were able to understand the description of Çré Kåñëa's aprakaöa presence among them
and they became pleased and satisfied to understand that they were not actually separated from
Him. Their satisfaction is described by Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.38):

   "After hearing the message written by their dearmost Kåñëa, the gopés became pleased and
satisfied. Remembering that message, they spoke the following words to Uddhava."*

   tat-sandeçenagatä smrtir nitya-saàyogänusandhana-rüpa yäsäà tädåsyaù. ata eva prétaù. itaù

   Remembering Lord Kåñëa's instructions, the gopés were able to directly see Lord Kåñëa's aprakaöa

very much pleased and satisfied (prétäù).

am; vayuù-air; jyotiù-light; aìganaù-O gopés; evam-in the same way; hi-certainly; etäni-these;

   "My dear gopés, just as the material elements are present within all material objects (which have
the material elements as their origin), in the same way, because I am the origin (and also the cause
of dissolution) of everything, I am present everywhere, within and without everything. You saw Me
in My prakaöa form in the forest of Våndävana. Now please see Me in My aprakaöa form, eternally
manifested before you in meditation."*

evaà idamtahämtaspadaà yat ubhayaà tac ca punaù pare prakaöam atra dåsyamäne 'pi täsyäm
våndätavyaà virahämane akñare nityaà eva yuçmat-sanginé mayy äçraya-rüpe abhatam
virajamänaà paçyata iti. tasmät prakäsä-bhedäd eva tat-tad-vastv-adid-bheda-vyapadeça-viraha-
saàyoga-vyavästha cetidam aträpi vyaktam.

   yathä-just as; aham-I; ahaìkäraù-conception of ego; bhüta-of living entities; adiù-origin;
sarveñäm-of all; bhütänäm-material elelments; kha-adinäm-ether, air, fire, water and earth; adi-
beginning; anta-end; adi-orginal; rüpaù-form; ahaìkära-false-ego; antah-gatani-within; eva-
certainly; khä-adini-the material elements; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; yathä-just as; kha-adini-
beginning with ether; bhütäni-the material elelments; bhautikänam-of what is constructed from the
materila elements; sarava-a shallow dish; saindhava-salt; adinam-beginning with; adi-beginning;
anta- end; rupäëi-forms; kha-adinam-of ether and the other elements; antah-gatäni-within; eva-

the manifest pastimes; anubhüyamänäni-being perceived; yuçmäkam-of you; mamata- ego; aspadäni-
