ego; aspadam-abode; ätma-the word "atma"; ca-and; aprakaöa-léla-abhimäni-manifested in the
prakaöa pastimes; ahänta-ego; aspadam-abode; ätma-the word "atma"; ca-and; aprakaöa- léla-
abhimäni-in the aprakaöa pastimes; ahanta-of ego; aspadena-by the abode; atmana-by the "ätmanä";
tataù-the word "tataù"; vyäptaù-means "pervaded"; eam-in this way; idanta-the state of being like
this; ahanta-ego; aspadam- abode; yat-which; ubhayam-both; tat-that; ca-also; puhaù- again; pare-in
the Supreme; prakaöam-manifested; atra-here; drçyamäne-being observed; api-although; täsyäm-in
that; vånda-atavyam-forest of Våndävana; virahämane-separated; akñare-imperishable; nityam-
eternally; eva-certainly; yuçmat-with you; sanginé-associated; mayi-in Me; äçraya-rüpe-the ultimate
shelter; abhatam-the word "abhatam"; virajamänam-means "is manifested; paçyata-please see; iti-
thus; tasmät-therefore; prakäça-of manifestation; bhedät- from distinction; eva-certainly; tat-tat-
various; vastu- substances; adi-beginning with; bheda-distinction; vyapadeça- by name; viraha-
separation; saàyoga-and meeting; vyavästha- condition; ca-and; iti-thus; idam-this; atra-here; api-
also; vyaktam-manifested


    In these verses Kåñëa says: "Just as (yathä) the material elements are present within all material
objects (which have the material elements as their origin), in the same way, because I am the origin
of everything, I am also present within everything." Lord Kåñëa explains that He is present in both
His manifest prakaöa (ätmä) and all-pervading aprakaöa (ätmanä) forms. He said: "In My prakaöa
form (pare) you saw Me in the forest of Våndävana. Now please see Me in My aprakaöa form
(akñare) eternally manifested before you. I am the Supreme Lord and the ultimate shelter of all
living entities, and there is no real difference between My prakaöa and aprakaöa forms."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.170
records.text:
Text 1


çré-bhagavac-chikñänurüpam eva çré-åñir uväca

adhyätma-çikñayä gopyä
   evaà kåñëena çikñitaù
tad-anusmaraëa-dhvasta-
   jéva-koças tam ädhyagan

   çré-bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; çikñä-the instructions; anurüpam-
following; eva-certainly; çré-åçiù-Çréla Çukadeva Gosvami; uväca-said; adhyätma-spiritual ; çikñayä-

with instruction; gopyäù-the gopés; evam-in this way; kåñëena-by Çré Kåñëa; çikñitaù- taught; tat-
that; anusmarana-by rememberance; dhvasta- destroyed; jéva-koçaù-material illusion; tam-on Him;
ädùyagan-meditated;


   After describing Lord Kåñëa instructions to the gopés, Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämi described the
gopés' response (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.47):

   "By hearing and remembering Lord Kåñëa's instruction about His presence among them in His
aprakaöa form, the gopés became free from all illusion. They constantly meditated on Kåñëa, and
thus always associated with Him in His aprakaöa form."


Text 2


   ädhyätma-sikñaya tad-upadeçenätmänaà çré-kåñëam adhikåtya yä çikñä tayä vä; tathä-vidhaà yad
upädiçtam tad-anusmaraëena nitya-siddhäprakaöa-lélayaù punar anusandhanena dhvastaù tyakta-
präyaù jéva-koçaù prapaïcas tatra prakaöyäbhiniveço
yäbhis taù. taà svayam upadiñöam nitya-saàyukta-rüpaà çré-kåñëam ädhyagan pranihitavatyah.
taträpi purva-darçita-çruti-puraëädi-gata-nityata-väkyaà mayi bhaktir hi iti phala-bheda-väkyaà
ca na jïänaà na ca vairägyam ity ady ayuktata vyaïji-väkyam cänusandhäya parokña-vädärtha-
prayuktam arthäntaraà na prameyam.

   ädhyätm-about Himself; sikñaya-by instruction; tat- upadeçena-by that instruction; atmänam-
the Supreme Person; çré-kåñëa-Çré Kåñëa; adhikåtya-in relation to; yä- which; sikñä-instruction; tayä-
with that; vä-or; tathä- vidham-in that way; yat-which; upädiçtam-instructed; tat- anusmaränena-by
remembering that; nitya-siddha-etrnally perfect; aprakaöa-unmanifested; lélayaù-of pastimes; punaù-
again; anusandhanena-by meditative understanding; dhvastaù-the word "dhvasta"; tyakta-prayaù-
means "given up"; jéva-kosaù- the word "jéva-kosa"; prapaïcaù-material conception; tatra- there;
prakaöya-to the manifest pastimes; abhiniveçaù- attachment; yäbhiù-by them; taù-they; tam-Him;
svayam- personally; upadiçtam-instructed; nitya-saàykta-eternally associated; rüpam-form; çré-
kåñëam-Çré Kåñëa; ädhyagan-the word "ädhyagan"; pranihitavatyaù-means "meditated on"; taträ-
nevertheless; purva-peviously; darçita-shown; çruti-in the Çruti; puraëa-Puraëas; adi-and other
Vedic literatures; gata-within; nityate-eternality; vakyam-statements describing; mayi bhaktih hi iti-
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.44; phala-of results; bheda-dinstinction; vakyam- description; ca-also; na
jïänam na ca vairägyam- iti adi-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.20.31; aykta-unsuitablilty; vyaïji-
manifesting; vakyam-statement; ca-also; anusandhaya-having examined; parokña-väda-artha-
prayuktam-a hidden meaning; artha-antaram-another meaning; na not; prameyam-ascertainable.


   By remembering (tad-anusmaraëa) Lord Kåñëa's instructions about His aprakaöa presence
(ädhyätma-çikñayä) among them, the gopés gave up their illusion of being attached to Çré Kåñëa's
prakaöa form, and not being aware of His eternal presence in their midst in His aprakaöa form.
Understanding Lord Kåñëa instructions, the gopés constantly meditated on His form and pastimes,

and in that way continuously associated with Him. Çré Kåñëa's eternal presence among the gopés in
His aprakaöa form is described in the following verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam:

  "Devotional service rendered to Me by the living beings revives their eternal life. O My dear
damsels of Vraja, your affection for Me is your good fortune, for it is the only means by which you
have obtained My favor."*
                     -10.82.44

   "A pure devotee who is completely dedicated to My service is already situated in the topmost
perfection of life. His position will not be improved by adopting the inferior activities of the
cultivation of transcendental knowledge or performance of severe austerities."
                      -11.20.31

   If one analyzes these verses and tries to discover another hidden meaning here, he will not find
any suitable alternate meaning. What we have just explained is the only appropriate
interpretation.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.171
records.text:
Text 1


   atha jïäna-rüpaà prakaöärtham asvi-kurvanä nitya-lélä-rüpaà rahasyärthaà svi-kurvanä api
purvavät punaç ca prakaöa-léläbhiniveçena viraha-bhétaù parama-dainyottaram evam prärthayam
äsur ity äha

   atha-now; jïäna-rüpam-of knowledge; prakata- manifested; artham-meaning; asvi-kurvanäù-not
accepting; nitya-eternal; lélä-of pastimes; rüpam-form; rahasya- confidential; artham-meaning; svi-
kurvahäù-accepting; api- also; purvavät-as before; punaù-again; ca-also; prakaöa-léla-to Lord Kåñëa's
prakata pastimes; abhiniveçena-with great attachment; viraha-os separation; bhétaù-afraid; parama-
of great; dainya-humbleness; uttaram-reply; evam-in this way; prärthayam äsuù-prayed; iti-thus; äha-
said.


   In this way it may be understood that by accepting Çré Kåñëa's instructions as true, the gopés did
not accept the monistic conception of the all-pervasiveness of the Absolute, but rather understood
Kåñëa's confidential explanation of His eternal presence among them in His aprakaöa form. Even
though the gopés were able to understand that Lord Kåñëa was always present before them in His
aprakaöa form, they became afraid of being again separated from His prakaöa form, and with great
humbleness offered the following prayer (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.48):


Text 2

ähuç ca te nalina-näbha padäravindaà
   yogeçvarair hådi vicintyam agädha-bodhaiù
saàsära-küpa-patitottaraëävalambaà
   gehaà juñäm api manasy udiyät sadä naù

   ähuù-the gopés said; ca-and; te-Your; nalina-näbha-O Lord, whose navel is just like a lotus
flower; pada-aravindam- lotus feet; yoga-éçvaraiù-by great mystic yogés; hådi- within the heart;
vicintyam-to be meditated upon; agädha-bodhaiù-who are highly learned philosophers; saàsära-
küpa- in the dark well of material existence; patita-of those fallen; uttaraëa-for deliverance;
avalambam-the only shelter; geham- in family affairs; juçäm-of those engaged; api-although; manasi-
in the minds; udiyät-let be awakened; sadä-always; naù-our.


   "The gopés spoke thus: Dear Lord, whose navel is just like a lotus flower, Your lotus feet are the
only shelter for those who have fallen into the deep well of material existence. Your feet are
worshiped and meditated upon by great mystic yogés and highly learned philosophers. We wish that
these lotus feet may also be awakened within our hearts, although we are only ordinary persons
engaged in household affairs."*


Text 3


   ästaà täväd durvidhihatanam asmäkaà tad-darçana-gandha-vartäpi he nälina-näbha tava
padäravindaà tvad-upadeçänusärenäsmäkaà manasy apy udiyat. nänu kim iväträsambhavyaà?
taträhuù yogeçvaraiù. eva hådi vicintyaà na tv asmäbhis tat-smaranärambha eva mürccha-
gaminibhiù. tad uktam uddhavaà prati svayaà-bhägavata

    ästam-let there be; tävät-in that way; durvidhiù-by misfortune; hatanam-struck; asmäkam-of us;
tat-of that; darçana-of the sight; gandha-slight; varta-news; api-even; he-O; nälina-näbha-O Lord
whose navel is just like a lotus flower; tava-Your; pada-aravindam-lotus feet; tvat-upadeça- Your
instructions; anusarena-according to; asmäkam-of us; manasi-in the minds; api-although; udiyaet-let
it be awakened; nan-is it not so?; kim iva-is it?; atra-in this case; asambhavyam-impossible; tatra-in
this connection; ahuù-they say; yoge-içvaraiù-by great mystic yogis; eva-certainly; hådi-within the
heart; vicintyam-to be meditated upon; na- not; tu-but; amsäbhiù-by us; tat-smarana-of
remembering Your lotus feet; arambhe-in the activity; eva-certainly; mürccha-gamibhiù-
bewildered.


   In this verse the gopés say: "O Lord, please permit us, who are very unfortunate, to have an
occasional glimpse of Your lotus feet. O Lord whose navel is like a lotus flower, we wish that Your
lotus feet may be awakenend within our hearts." If Kåñëa were to ask the gopés: "What is the
difficulty? Why is it impossible or so difficult for you to remain content by meditating on My lotus

feet?" then the gopés might reply: "O Lord, Your feet are worshiped and meditated upon by great
mystic yogés and highly learned philosophers. We are only ordinary persons engaged in household
afairs. How is it possible, then, for us to meditate on Your lotus feet, which are the proper object of
meditation for great souls.


Text 4


tad uktam uddhavaà prati svayaà-bhagavatä

mayi taù preyäsaà preñöha
  düra-sthe gokula-striyaù
smarantyo 'nga vimuhyanti
  virahotkaëöha-vihvalaù iti.

   ta-that; uktam-said; uddhavam prati-to Uddhava; svayam-bhägavata-by the Supreme Personality
of Godhead; mayi-Me; taù-they; preyäsam-preñöhe-the most dear; düra sthe-far away; gokula-of
Gokula; striyaù-the women; smarantyaù- meditating; anga-O friend; vimuhyanti-are overwhelmed;
viraha- of separation; utkaëöha-with anxiety; vihvalaù-agitated; iti-thus.


  Always eager to directly associate with Çré Kåñëa, the gopés continuously meditated upon Him.
This is described in the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.5) spoken by Lord Kåñëa to
Uddhava:

   "My dear Uddhava, the gopés are always absorbed in thoughts of Me, who am most dear to them.
Since I have gone away to Mathurä, they are alwyas thinking of Me in such a way that they remain
overwhelmed and almost dead in anxiety due to separation from Me."*


Text 5


   tad evopapadayanti agadha-bodhaiù säkñäd-darçane 'py akñubhita-buddhibhiù, na tv asmäbhir
iva tad-darçanecchayä kñubhita-buddhibhiù. caranasyäravindata-rüpakaà ca, tat-sparçenaiva daha-
çantir bhavati, na tu smaraneneti jïäpayanti.

   tat-therefore; eva-certainly; upapadayanti-they explain; agadha-bodhaiù-who are highly learned
philosophers; säksät- darçane-in directly seeing; api-even; akñubhita-with unagitated; buddhibhiù-
intelligence; na-not; tu-but; asmäbhiù-by us; iva-as it were; tat-Your lotus feet; darçana-to see;
icchayä-with the desire; kñubhita-with agitated; buddhibhiù-intelligence; caranasya-of the feet;
aravindata-of a lotus flower; rüpakam-metaphor; ca-also; tat-of them; sparçena-by the touch; eva-
certainly; daha-of the fire; çantiù-extinguishing; bhavati-comes into existence; na- not; tu-but;
smaranena-by remembering; iti-thus; jïäpayati- they presented their appeal.

   In this verse the gopés protest to Kåñëa that they cannot remain satisfied simply by remembering
His lotus feet, but they insist that they must have His direct association. In this verse they intended
to say: "O Lord, the highly learned philosophers are able to meditate upon You because their minds
are tranquil and free from all desires, including the desire to directly attain Your lotus feet. This
peaceful condition of the mind is certainly a prerequisite in the matter of meditation. We are not
able to meditate on Your lotus feet because our minds are agitated with the desire to directly see
You, and therfore, in that unpeaceful condition, we cannot fix our minds in meditation. The
metaphor comparing Your feet to a lotus flower is very appropriate, for a lotus flower is very cooling
to the touch, although simply thinking of a lotus flower is not at all cooling. Therefore, in the same
way, our burning desire to associate with You can be relieved only by the direct contact of Your
lotus feet. Our desires ill not be satisfied simply by meditating on You.


Text 6


   nanu tathä nididhyäsanam eva yogeçvaränäà saàsära-duhkham iva bhavaténäà viraha-
duùkhaà düri-kåtya tad-udäyaà kariñyatéty asaìkyähuù saàsära-küpa-patitänäà eva
uttaranavälambaà, na tv asmäkaà viraha-sindhu-nimägnänäà tac-cintänarambhe duùkha-
våddher evänubhuyämänätväd iti bhavaù.

   nanu-is it not so?; tathä-in that way; nididhyäsanam- meditation; eva-certainly; yoga-içvaränäm-
of the yogis; saàsära-of material existence; duùkham-suffering; iva-as it were; bhavaténäm-of you;
viraha-of separation; duhkham- suffering; düri-kåtya-casting far away; tat-udäyam-the arisal of that;
kariñyati-will do; iti-thus; asaìkya- considering; ahuù-they said; saàsära-küpa-in the dark well of
material existence; patitänäm-of those fallen; eva- certainly; uttarana-for deliverance; avälamba-the
only shelter; na-not; tu-but; asmäkam-of us; viraha-of separation; sindhu-in the ocean; nimägnänäm-
drowning; tat-cintäna-arambhe-in the activity of remembering Your lotus feet; duùkha-of suffering;
våddheù-of the increase; eva-certainly; anubhuyämänätvät-because of experiencing; iti-thus;
bhavaù-the meaning.


   The gopés thought that Kåñëa might say to them: "The great mystic yogés meditate on My lotus
feet and thus become relieved from the sufferings of material existence. Please, therefore, take up
this process of meditating on My lotus feet and you will become free from the suffering of
separation from Me just as the yogés become free from suffering in the same way".
   By distingusihing themsleves from the yogés in this verse, the gopés intended to say to Kåñëa:
"They who have fallen into the dark well of material existence may become delivered by meditating
on Your lotus feet, but such meditation is not helpful for us, who are drowning in the ocean of
separation from You. When we remember Your lotus feet we do not at all experience relief, but
rather the intense suffering of our separation only increases."


Text 7

   nanv adhunaiväträgatya muhur mäà säkñäd evänubhavata, taträhuù gehaà juçam iti tava
saìgatis ca tvat-pürva-saìgama-viläsa-dhämni tat-tade-asmät-käma-dughe svabhävikäsmät-préti-
nilaye nija-gåhe gokula eva bhavatu, na tu dvärakädav iti sva-manoratha-viçeñena tasminn eva
prétimaténäm ity arthaù. yaù kaumära-haraù sa eva hi varaù ity adivat. tasmäd asmäkaà manasi tac-
caraëa-cintanäbhavat svayam-aga manasyäsamarthyad-anäbhi-rucer vä säksäd eva çré-våndävana
eva yady agacchasi, tadaiva nistara iti bhavaù.

   nanu-is it not so?; adhuna-at present; eva-certainly; atra-here; agatya-having arrived; muhuù-
constantly; mäm-Me; säkñät-directly; eva-certainly; anubhavata-you may see; tatra-in this
connection; ahuù-they said; geham-in family affairs; juçam-of those engaged; para-of others;
gåhénénäm-of the waves; asvädhinänäm-not independant; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; yad vä-or;
geham juçam-the words "geham juçam"; iti-thus; tava-Your; saìgatiù- association; ca-also; tvat-Your;
pürva-previous; saìgama-in the association; dhämni-in the abode; tat-tat-various; asmät-of us; käma-
desires; dughe-fulfilling; svabhävik-by nature; asmät-of us; préti-nilaye-the object of love; nija-in
Your; gåhe-home; gokule-in Gokula; eva-certainly; bhavatu-should be; na-not; tu-but; dväraka-adau-
in Dväraka or other places; iti-thus; sva-manoratha-viçeçena-with a specific desire; tasmin-in that
place; eva-certainly; prétimaténäm-with attachment; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; yaù kumära-
haraù sa eva hi varaù iti adi vat-as in the followingverse (Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya lila 13.122):


yaù kaumära-haraù sa eva hi varas tä eva caitra-kñapäs
   te conmélita-mälaté-saurabhayaù prauòhäù kadambäniläù
sä caiväsmi tathäpi tatra surata-vyäpära-lélä-vidhau
   revä-rodhasi vetasé-taru-tale cetaù samutkaëöhate

tasmät-therefore; asmäkam-of us; manasi-in the mind; tat-caraëa-of Kåñëa's lotus feet; cintana-
meditation; abhavat- because of inability; anäbhiruceù-because of lack of desire; vä-of; säksät-
directly; eva-certainly; çré-våndävane- in Våndävana; eva-certainly; yadi-if; agacchasi-You come;
tada-then; eva-certainly; néstaraù-felief; iti-thus; bhavaù-the meaning;


   The gopés also thought that Kåñëa might suggest that they return with Him to Dvärakä, where
they may associate with Him without interruption. For this reason the gopés said the words "gehaà
juñäm" (we are only ordinary persons engaged in household affairs). In this way they reminded
Kåñëa that they were the wives of others, and not independent of their husbands. It was not
possible for them to leave their husbands and go with Him to Dvärakä. One may also interpret the
words "gehaà juñäm" to mean "My dear Kåñëa it is not at all suitable for us to associate with You in
Dvärakä or any other place except for this land of Våndävana. We are very attached to this land of
Våndävana, which seems to us to fulfill all our desires, and which is the place where we formerly
enjoyed pastimes in Your company. This desire of the gopés to remain in Våndävana and enjoy
Kåñëa's association there is described in the following verse (Caitanya-caritämåta Madhya-lélä
13.122):

   "That very personality who stole away my heart during my youth is now again my master. These
are the same moonlit nights of the mont of Caitra. The same frgrance of mälaté flowers is there, and
the same sweet breezes are blowing from the kadamba forest. In our intimate relationship, I am also
the same lover, yet still my mind is not happy here. I am eager to go back to that place on the bank
of the Revä under the Vetasé tree. That is my desire."*

   By these words (gehaà juñäm) the gopés said to Kåñëa: "We cannot become relieved of our
distress by meditating on Your lotus feet, and we are not able to return to Dvärakä with You, nor
would we desire to do so if we could. Therefore the only solution to our plight is if You personally
return with us to Våndävana and grant us Your association there."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.172
records.text:
Text 1


   tad evaà svarasiky aprakaöa-lélä darçitä. athäprakaöa-prakaöa-léle dve 'py artha-viçeñeëäha

gopénäà tat-paténäà ca
   sarveñäm api dehinäm
yo 'ntaç carati so 'dhyakña
   eña kréòana-deha-bhäk

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; svarasiki-in the svarasiki state of self-realization; aprakaöa-
unmanifested; lélä pastimes; darçitä-are revealed; atha-now; aprakaöa- unmanifested; prakaöa-and
manifested; léle-pastimes; dve- both; api-also; artha-viçeçeëa-with the specific description; gopénäm-
of the gopés; tat-paténäm-and of their husbands; ca-also; sarvesäm-of everyone; api-also; dehinäm-
situated within a body; yah-who; antaù-within; carati-moves; saù-He; adhyakñaù-the witness; eñaù-
He; kréòana- for pastimes; deha-bhäk-with a form.


   Çré Kåñëa's prakaöa form, and also His aprakaöa form which appeared in the hearts of the of the
devotees in the stage of svärsiké meditation, are both described in the following verse from Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.33.35):

   "The same Çré Kåñëa who appeared in Våndävana in His prakaöa form and enjoyed pastimes in
the company of the cowherd men of Våndävana, also appeared in His aprakaöa form within the
hearts of all of the Vraja-gopés and the cowherd men who were their husbands."


Text 2

   antaù antaù-sthitam aprakaöaà yathä syät tahä gopénäm ta-paténäm ca tat-patià-manyänäà
kréòana-deha-bhäk san teñäm eva gokula-yuva-räjataya adhyakñaù ca san yaç carati kréòati, sa eñaù
prakaöa-lélä-gato 'pi bhütvä sarveñäm viçva-vartinäm dehinäm api kréòana-deha-bhäk san, teñäà
pälakatvenädhyakño 'pi san carati tasmäd anädita eva täbhiù kréòä-çälitvena siddhatvät tac-chakti-
rüpäëäà täsäà saìgame vastuta eva para-däratä-doço 'pi nästi.

   antaù-the word "antaù; antaù-sthitam-meanis "situated within"; aprakaöam-unmanifested; yathä-
just as; syät-may be; tathä-in the same way; gopénäm-of the gopés; tat-paténäm-of their husbands; ca-
also; tat-patim-their husband; manyänäm-considered; kréòana-for pastimes; deha-the form;
manifesting; san-being so; teñäm-of them; eva-certainly; gokula-of Gokula; yuva-räjatayä-as the
prince; adhyakñaù-the monarch; ca-also; san-being so; yaù-who; carati-the word ïcarati"; kréòati-
means "performs pastimes;" sah eñaù-He; prakaöa-lélä-gataù-in His manifest pastimes; api-also;
bhütvä-having become; sarveñäm-of everyone; viçva-vartinäm-in the universe; dehinäm-embodied
beings; api-even; kréòana-for pastimes; deha-form; bhäk-manifesting; san- being so; teñäm-of them;
pälakatvena-as the protector; adhyakñaù-the monarch; api-even; san-being; carati-performs
pastimes; tasmät-therefore; anäditaù-without beginning; eva- certainly; täbhiù-witht he gopis; kréòä-
çälitvena- performing pastimes; siddhatvät-because of the perfecton; tat-sakti-of His potency;
rüpäëäm-as the forms; täsäm-of them; saìgame-in the association; vastutaù-in fact; eva- certainly;
para-of another; däraöä-with the wife; doçaù- fault; api-even; na-not; asti-is.


   In His aprakaöa form Çré Kåñëa was manifested within (antaù) the thoughts of the gopés (tat-
paténäm). Çré Kåñëa is known as "adhyakña" (the monarch) both because He is the playful (yaç
carati) prince of Gokula, and because He is the supreme monarch and protector of all living entities
(sarveñäà dehinäm). Lord Kåñëa is the real husband of the gopés and He has been enjoying pastimes
with them from time immemorial. Because the relationship of Çré Kåñëa and the gopés is actually
eternal, Çré Kåñëa cannot be criticized for "immorality" or "adultery".


Text 3


   tatas teñäà tat-patitvaà ca näsuyan khalu kåñëäya ity adi vakñyamäna-diçä teñäà täsäà ca
pratétika-mätram, na tu daihikam. tädåça-prätéti-sampadänäà ca täsäm utkaëöha-poñärtham iti tat-
prakaraëa-siddhäntasya pärakasthä darçitä. çré-çukaù.

   tataù-therefore; teñäm-of them; tat-patitvam-the position of husband; ca-also; na asuyan khalu
kåñëäya iti adi-in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.33.37:


näsuyan khalu kåñëäya
   mohitäs tasya mäyayä
manyamänäù sva-parçvasthän
   svän svän därän varjaukasaù

vakñyamäna-about to be spoken; diçä-by this statement; teñäm-of the husbands; täsäm-of the gopés;
ca-also; pratétika-existing in the imagination; mätram-only; na-not; tu-but; daihikam-in an actual
form; tädåça-in that way; pratéti-sampadänäm-conviction; ca-also; täsäm-of the gopés; utkaëöha-
longing; poça-increasing; artham-for the purpose of; iti tat-prakaraëa-of that description;
siddhäntasya-of the conclusion; pära-akasthä-without doubt; darçitä-demonstrated; çré-çukaù-
spoken by Çré Çukadeva Gosvami.


   Çré Kåñëa is the real husband of the gopés. The cowherd men who played the role of being the
gopés' husbands were actually not their husbands. The husband and wife relationship between the
various cowherd men and the gopés was existing only in their imagination and only for enhancing
Kåñëa's pärakéya relationship with the gopés. This is confirmed in the following statement of Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.33.37):

   "The gopés' husbands thought that their wives were sleeping by their sides. Enamoured by the
influence of the external energy of Kåñëa, they thought that the gopés were their wives. They could
not understand that the had gone to dance with Kåñëa."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.173
records.text:
Text 1


   evaà tat-tal-lélä-bhedenaikasyäpi tat-sthänasya prakäça-bhedaù çré-vigrahavät. tad uktam våñëaù
paramaà padam avabhäti bhüriù iti çrutyä.

   evam-in the same way; tat-tat-in various; lélä- pastimes; bhedena-by distinctions; ekasya-of the
single Supreme Lord; api-even; tat-sthänasya-in the transcendental abode; prakäça-of
manifestation; bhedaù-distinctions; çré-vigrahavät-just as there are many different forms of the
Supreme Lord; tat-therefore; uktam-it is said; våñëaù-the Supreme Personality of Godhead who
fulfills all desires; paramam padam-in the transcendental abode; avabhäti-is manifested; bhüriù-in
many different forms; iti-thus; çrutyä-the Statement of the Åg Veda (      ).


   Just as the Supreme Personality of Godhead has many different forms in order to enjoy many
different pastimes, in the same way, the transcendental abode of the Lord, although one, is
manifested in many different forms. This is described in the following verse from the Åg Veda:

  "The transcendental abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who fulfills all desires, is
manifested in many different ways."


Text 2

    tatra tv itara-léläntaù-patibbhiù präyaça itara-lélävakäça-viçeço nopalabhyate; dåçyate ca prakaöa-
léläyäm api asaìkäri-bhävenaiva viciträvakäçatvam. yathä dvädaça-yojana-mätra-pramitäyäà
dvärakäntaù-puryäà kroça-dvaya-pramita-gåha-koöi-prabhåti-vastuni, yathä sv-alpe govardhana-
garte tad-asaìkhya-gokula-praveñaù yathä brähmaëä dåñöyä våndävanasya sva-våkña-tåëa-
pakñädyavakäçatä brahmäëòädy-ananta-vastv-avakäçatä ca, yathä ca çré-närada-dåñöa-yogamäyä-
vaibhave samakalam eva dvärakäyäà patastya-madhyähnika-çayäntana-lélä ity ädi, tad evaà
våndävanasya tävat prakäça-bhedä udähriyante.

    tatra-in this connection; tu-also; itara-léla-antaù-patibhiù-with other pastimes; avakäça-
opportunity; viçeñaù-specific; na-not; upalabhyate-is attained; dåçyate-is observed; ca-also; prakaöa-
léläyäm-in the manifest pastimes; eva-certainly; vicitra-avakäçatvam- astonishing characteristics;
yathä-just as; dvädaça-yojana- of 12 yojanas (96 miles); mätra-only; pramitäyäm- measurement;
dväraka-of Dväraka; antaù-puryäm-inner part of the city; kroça-dvaya-of 2 krosas (4 miles); pramita-
the measurement; gåha-palaces; koöi-millions; prabhåti- beginning with; vastuni-substances; yathä-
just as; su-alpe- very small; govardhana-of Govardhana Hill; garta-in the valley; tat-asaìkhya-
immeasurable; gokula-Gokula; praveçaù- entrance; yathä-just as; brähmanä-by Lord Brahma; dåñöyä-
by his glance; våndävanasya-of Våndävana; sva- own; våkña-trees; tåëa-blades of grass; pakña-birds;
adi-beginning with; avakäçatä-entrance; brahmäëòa-universes; adi-beginning with; ananta-
unlimited; vastu-substances; avakäçatä-entrance; ca-also;yathä-just as; ca-also; çré-närada-by Närada;
dåñöa-seen; yogamäyä-of Yogamaya; vaibhave-in the potency; sama-kalam-simultaneously; eva-
certainly; dvärakäyäm-at Dvärakä; pratastya-of morning; madhyähnika-of midday; çayäntana-of
evening; léläù-pastimes; iti-thus; ädi-beginning with; tat- therefore; våndävanasya-of Våndävana;
tävat-in that way;prakäça-bhedäù-varying manifestations; udähriyante-are described.


   Each different abode of the Lord has its own specific feature, and specific pastimes are enjoyed
in each abode. There is no overlapping of pastimes, where the pastimes of one abode are performed
in another. However, even in the Lord's manifest pastimes within the material world, the Lord's
abode manifests very wonderful features. For example, although the inner part of Dvärakä city is
only 12 yojanas (96 miles) in diameter, within that relatively small place there are millions of
palaces 2 kroças (4 miles) across, as well as many gardens, lakes, and so on, all very large. Another
example is the valley Govardhana Hill, which although very small in size, contains the infinitely
large spiritual realm of Gokula. Another example is the small animals and plants in the forest of
Våndävana, which were seen by Lord Brahmä is be larger than innumerable universes. Another
example may be seen in Dvärakä City, where Närada Muni observed the Lord's morning, midday,
and evening pastimes occuring simultaneously (in othe words, Närada saw that in Dvärakä it was
morning, midday, and evening all at the same time).
   In this way the Lord's abode of Goloka Våndävana is manifested in many different parts, each
part being the place of specific pastimes.


Text 3

taträprakaöa-lélänugato yathä yämale rudra-gauré-samväde

véthyäà véthyäà niväso 'dhara-madhu-suvacas tatra santanakänäm
   eke rakendu-koöy-atäpa-viçäda-käras teñu caike kamante
rame rätrer virame samudita-tapana-dyoti-sindhüpameyä
   ratnäìganaà suvarëacita-mukura-rucas tebhya eke drumendraù

yat kusumaà yadä àrgyaà
   yat phalaà ca varänane
tat tadaiva prasüyante
   våndävana-suradrumäù

   tatra-in this connection; aprakaöa-léla-anugataù-in the unmanifested pastimes; yathä-just as;
yämale-in the Yämala-tantra rudra-of Lord siva; gauré-and Parvati; saàväde-in the conversation;
vithyäm-vithyäm-on every path; niväsaù- residence; adhara-madhu-suvacaù-O Parvati, whose
speeches are very sweet and pleasing; tatra-there; santanakänäm-of the desire-trees; eke-some; raka-
indu-full moon, atäpa-viçäda-käraù-with the clear shining; teçu-among them; ca-also; eke-some;
kamante-appear very beautiful; rame-O Parvati; rätreù- of night; virame-in the end; samudita-
arisen; tapana-shining; dyoti-splendor; sindhu-ocean; upameyäù-compared to; ratna-of jewels;
aìganam-branches; suvarëa-acita-golden; mukura-of the buds; rucaù-splendor; tebhyaù-from them;
eke-some; druma-indraù-desire-trees; yat-what; kusumam-flower; yadä-when; mågyam-sought; yat-
what; phalam-fruit; ca-also; vara-anane-O beautiful-aced Parvati; tat-that; tada-then; eva-certainly;
prasüyante-blossoms forth; våndävana-of Våndävana; sura- drumäù-the dsire trees.


   Another wonderful feature of the Lord's abode is the presence of desire trees there. The desire
trees in the aprakaöa spiritual Goloka Våndävana are described in the following passage from the
Yamala Tantra, where Lord Çiva says to Pärvaté:

    "My dear sweetly speaking Pärvaté, on each and every path in Goloka Våndävana are many
different kinds of desire trees. Some are splendid as the pristine full moon, and some are like the
newly rising sun, or like an expansive ocean of brilliant light. Some have jeweled branches, and
some have buds splendid as gold. Whatever flower or fruit one wishes to pick from these desire trees
is at once manifest on their branches."


Text 4


   arthaç ca he adhara-madhu-suvacaù adhara-madhu-tulyäni suvacäàsi yasyäs tathä-bhüte, he
gauri. tatra çré-våndävane ratnäìgänäà santakänäm madhye eke drumendra rakendu-koöy-atäpa-
viçada-karaù. he rame teñu ca santakeñu eke rätrer virame samudita-täpana-dyoti-sindhüpameyaù
kamante viräjante, tebhyaù tan apy atikramya eke kamante. kathaà-bhütaù? suvarëacita-mükura-
rucaù iti. atra ca yadä yat kusumaà mågyam bhavati, yadä ca yat phalam mågyaà bhavati, tadaiva

tad-våndävana-suradrumaù prasüyante iti.

   arthaù-the meaning; ca-also; he-O; adhara-madhu-suvacaù- this word "adhara-madhu-suvacaù";
adhara-lips; madhu-honey; tulyäni-equal; suvacäàsi-eloquent words; yasyäù-of whom; tathä-bhüte-
in that way; he gauri-O Gauri; tatra-there; çré-våndävane-in Våndävana; ratna-aìgänäm-with
jewelled branches; santakänäm-of the desire trees; madhye-in the midst; eke-some; druma-indraù-
desire trees; raka-indu-the full moon; koöi-millions; atäpa-shining; viçada-clear; karaù-effulgence;
he-rame-O goddess; teçu-among them; ca- also; santakeçu-desire trees; eke-some; rätreù-of night;
virame-at the end; samudita-arisen; täpana-shining dyuti- splendor; sindhu-ocean; upameyaù-
compared to; kamante-the word "kamante"; viräjate-means "shine beautifully"; tebhyaù- from them;
api-even; atikramya-passing beyond; eke-some; kamante-shine beautifully; katham-bhutaù-what are
their characteristics?; suvarëa-with gold; acita-studded; mükura- buds; rucaù-splendor; iti-thus; atra-
here; ca-also; yadä- when; yat-that; kusumam-flower; mågyam-issought; bhavati- is; yadä-when; ca-
also; yat-what; phalam-fruit; mågyam- sought; bhavati-is; tada-then; eva-certainly; tat-våndävana-of
Våndävana; suradrumaù-the desire trees; prasüyante- cause it to blossom; iti-thus;


   In these verses the word "adhara-madu-suvacaù" means "O Pärvaté, whose words are as sweet as
honey", and the word "ratnäìganam" and "santakänäm" mean "among the desire trees, whose
branches are studded with jewels". The sentence "eke kamante" means "although some desire trees
are as splendid as the moon, and others as splendid as the sun, some (eke) desire trees shine with a
specific splendor, surpassing that of the others. The second verse means that whatever flower or
fruit one may wish to take from the desire trees, they will immediately produce.


Text 5


evaà brahma-saàhitäyäm apy ädi-puruña-govinda-stotra eva

çriyaù käntäù käntaù parama-puruñaù kalpa-taravo
   drumä bhümiç cintämaëi-gaëa-mayé toyam amåtam
kathä gänaà näöyaà gamanam api vaàçé priya-sakhé
   cid-änandaà jyotiù param api tad äsvädyam api ca

sa yatra kñéräbdhiù sravati surabhihyaç ca sumahän
   nimeñärdhäkhyo vä vrajati na hi yaträpi samayaù bhaje
çvetadvépaà tam aham iha golokam iti yaà
   vidantas te santaù kñiti-virala-cärä katipaye

   evam-in the same way; brahma-saàhitäyäm-in the Brahma-samhita; api-also; ädi-puruça-the
Original Person; govinda- to Lord Govinda; stotre-in the prayers; eva-certainly; ; çriyaù-the goddess
of fortune; käntäù-the damsels; käntaù-the enjoyer; paarama-puruçaù-the Supreme Personality of
Godhead; kalpa-taravaù-desire trees; drumaäù-all the trees; bhümiù-the land; cintämaëi-gaëa-mayé-
made of the transcendental touchstone jewel; toyam-the water; amåtam- nectar; kathä-talking;

gänam-song; näöyam-dancing; gamanam-walking; api-also; vaàçé-the flute; priya-sakhé- constant
companion; cit-änandam-transcendental bliss; jyotiù- effulgence; param-the supreme; api-also; tat-
that; äsvädyam-everywhere perceived; api ca-also; saù-that; yatra-where; kñéra-of milk; abdhiù-
ocean; sravati-flows; surabhibhyaù-from the surabhi cows; ca-also; sumahän-great; nimeña-ardha-
akhyaù-the space of half a moment; vä-or; vrajati-passes; na-not; hi-certainly; yatra- where; api-also;
samayaù-occasion; bhaje-worship; çvetadvépam-Çvetadvépa; tm-that; aham-I; iha-here; golokam-
Goloka Våndävana; iti-thus; yam-which vidantaù- know; te-they;santaù-self-realized souls; kñiti-
virala-cäräù-in this world; katipaye-a very few.


   The wonders of the spiritual Goloka Våndävana planet are also described in the following verses
from Brahma-saàhitä (5.56-57):

   I worship Lord Kåñëa's transcendental abode, known as Çvetadvépa, or Goloka Våndävana. The
damsels of Våndävana, the gopés, are super goddess of fortune. The enjoyer in Våndävana is the
Supreme Personality of Godhead Kåñëa. The trees there are all wish-fulfilling trees, and the land is
made of transcendental touchstone. The water is all nectar, the talking is singing, the walking is
dancing, and the constant companion of Kåñëa is His flute. The effulgence of transcendental bliss is
experienced everywhere. Therefore Våndävana-dhäma is the only relishable abode.*
   "In that Våndävana numberless milk-cows always emit transcendental oceans of milk, and in
that Våndävana there is eternal existence of transcendental time, who is ever present and without
past or future and hence is not subject to the quality of passing away even for the space of half a
moment. That realm is known as Goloka only to a very few self-realised souls in this world."**


Text 6


   jyotiù laukika-lélä-mädhuryayä mahä-pralaye 'py anasvaraà süryädi-rüpaà yat tatra vartate,

   jyotiù-effulgence; laukika-earthly; lélä-pastimes; mädhuryayä-for the sweetness; mahä-pralaye-at

spiritual; eva-certainly; gautaméye tantra-in the Gautamiya Tantra; kathitä-is described; samäna-
equal; udita-arisen; candra-moon; arkam-and sun; iti-thus; hi-certainly; våndävana-of Våndävana;
viçeñaëam- description; samänatvam-equality; ca-also; rätrau rätrau- night after night; räka-

candramayatvät-because of the full moon; iti-thus; api ca-also; iti-thus; api ca-also; iti- thus; parena
anvayaù-as previously stated; rasa-of the blissful spiritual relationships between Lord Kåñëa and His
liberated associates; aveçena-because of the entranc; tat-ajïänät-because of ignorance of time; eva-
certainly; samayaù-time; na-does not; vrajati-exist; iti-thus; uktam- said; anyathä-otherwise; paurva-
before; apärya-and after; abhäve-non-existence; sati-being so; ceñöa-atmikäyäù- consiting of
activities; léläyäù-of pastimes; svarüpa-the form; haniù-destruction; syät-would be; çvetam-the word
"çvetam"; çubhram-means "white" or "pure"; doça-of all fault; rahitam-free; iti-thus; arthaù-the
meaning; dvépam- island;
 tat-that; iva-like; anya-with others; saìga-contact; çünyam-devoid of; sarvataù-everything; param-
above; iti- thus; arthaù-the meaning;


   In these verses the word "jyotiù" (effulgence) indicates that in the spiritual realm of Goloka
Våndävana there are a spiritual and eternal sun and moon, which are not destroyed at the time of
cosmic annihilation. That delightful sun and moon are eternal, and full of knowledge and bliss.
They are not material and are different from the material sun and moon in many ways. For
example, the material moon waxes and wanes, appearing as a full moon on only one day a month. In
Goloka Våndävana, however, on each night the moon is full, and it never wanes. This is described
in the Gautaméya Tantra in the following words:

   "In Goloka Våndävana there are a spiritual sun and moon. There a full moon rises on each night,
for the moon never wanes."

   We may also note in these verses the word "bhaje" (I worship). This word shows that the abode
of Çré Kåñëa is worshipable as the Lord Himself. The word "bhaje" is used here just as some verses
previously Lord Brahmä used the same word to worship Lord Kåñëa (govindam ädi-puruñaà tam
ahaà bhajämi).
   The phrase "samayo na vrajati" indicates that the residents of Goloka Våndävana are so
immersed in love of Kåñëa and and enthralled by their pastimes with Him that they forget about
time. This phrase should not be interpreted to mean that there is no sequence of events in the
spiritual world, for if this were so it would be impossible for the Lord to enjoy pastimes there with
His devotees.
   The word "çvetam" (white) means "pure and free from all fault". The word "dvépam" (island)
means that Goloka Våndävana is situated far above the material worlds. It is free from any touch of
matter, just as a lotus flower remains always untouched by water. This is described in the following
statement of the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad (2.30):

   "As a lotus remains always untouched by water, so the spiritual world of Goloka Våndävana
remains always untouched by matter."


Text 7


   kiïca brahma-saàhitäyäm eva tat-stavädau-cintämaëi-prakara-sadmasu kalpavåkña-lakñävåteñu

iti.

   kiïca-furthermore; brahma-saàhitäyäm-in the Brahma-samhita (5.29); eva-certainly; tat-stava-
of Brahma's prayers; adau-in the beginning; cintämaëi prakara-sadmasu kalpa-våkña-lakñävrteñu iti-

   The spiritual world of Goloka Våndävana is also described by Lord Brahmä in the following
verse from the Brahma-saàhitä (5.29):

   "I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, the first progenitor, who is tending the cows, yielding all
desires, in abodes built with spiritual gems and surrounded by millions of purpose trees. He is always
served with great reverence and affection by hundreds and thousands of goddesses of fortune."*

       The spiritual world of Goloka Våndävana is also described in Närada-païcarätra:

  "The spiritual world of Çvetadvépa is a great white island surrounded by a nectar ocean of milk.
Gaurds stand in all ten directions to protect this spiritual realm.

gorves of desire trees.

   "The splendor of the jewels on these roofs is the origin of the Brahman effulgence. In this way
the abode of Goloka Våndävana is the summit of all beauty. Who is able to describe the beauty of
Våndävana?"

into mantropäsanä and svärasiké) are manifest is known as Goloka Våndävana. This abode of
Goloka Våndävana has been described in this book in many verses and it is also eloquently
described in the First Chapter of Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad.

  The Lord's abode of Våndävana is also described in the Skanda Puräëa, where Närada Muni says:

   "In that spiritual world is Lord Govinda's pure and splendid Våndävana, which is filled with
devotees of the Lord. I also stay there.

   tasmin våndävane nåpa

bhrtyaù-the Lord's servants; santi-are; govinda -for Lord Govinda; lalasaù-full of love.


   "That spiritual abode of Lord Govinda is also manifested on this earth planet, O king, and it is
known as Våndävana-dhäma. Tulasé-devé, myself, and many other great devotees of Lord Govinda
stay there."

   The on this earth where the Lord enjoyed His manifest pastimes are glorified in the Viñëu
Puräëa, Hari-vaàça, and other Vedic literatures. At the time of the Lord's manifest presence on
this planet, certain very fortunate residents of this world had the opportunity to personally see the
Lord and His abode, and even today we may see the transcendental places on this earth where the
Lord, appearing like an ordinary human being, enjoyed pastimes. Even when manifested in this
world, the abodes of the Lord are always transcendental and above the influence of the material
energy. This is confirmed by the Çruti and Småti literatures.


Text 17

   The glories of the Lord's abode and its residents are described in the Ädi-Varäha Puräëa:

   "They who are situated in transcendental knowledge can see that the residents of Mathurä have
four-armed spiritual forms like the form of Lord Viñëu. This fact is not visible to ordinary persons,
unaware of the transcendental nature of the Lord's abode."

Text 18


  tad etan-müla-pramäëe 'py aprakaöa-lélänugataù prakäçaù çré-våndävanasya

te cautsukya-dhiyo räjan

ity ädau darçitam eva.

   tat etat-this; müla-pramäëe-in evidence; api-also; aprakaöa-léla-anugataù-unmanifested pastimes;

eager to know; rajan-O king; matvä-having considered; gopaù-the cowherd men; tam-Him; içvaram-
the Supreme Personality of Godhead; iti-thus; adau-in the passage beginning; darsitam-revealed;
eva-certainly;


  That the Lord revealed His unmanifest pastimes in Våndävana is described in the Çrémad-
Bhägavatam passage (10.28.11) where the Lord showed the vrajaväsés the spiritual world.

tatpuruño vä. çré-bhagavän çré-baladevam.

   prakrtä-léla-anugataù-manifest pastimes; yathä-just as; aho-Oh; amé-these; deva-vara-amara-by
the best of the demigods; arcitam-worshiped; pada-ambujam-lotus feet; te-your; sumanaù-of
Sumahaù flowers; phala-and fruits; arhanam- offerings; namanti-offer obeisances; upädäya-having
offered; çikhäbhiù-with their branches; ätmanaù-of themselves; tamaù-of the darkness of
ignorance; upahatyai-for removal taru-as trees; janma-birth; yat-by whom; kåtam-accepted; iti-thus;
adi-in the passage beginning; atmanaù-from themselves; sumanaù-sumanah flowers; phala-and
fruits; rupam-consisting of; arhanam-offering; upadaya-placing; atmanaù-from themselves; eva-
certainly; sikhabhiù-with their branches; namanti-offer obeisances; yat-the word; "yat"; yaiù-means
"by whom"; srnvatam-of the hearers; pasyatam-of the hearers; ca-also; samsarinam-of the residents

of the material world; tamaù-of the ignorance; upahatyai-for the removal; taru-as trees; janma-
birth; etat-this krtam-accepted; iti-thus; yat-krtam-the word "yat-krtam";iti-thus; trtiya-tatpurusaù-
as an instrumental tatpurusa compound; va-or; sri-bhagavan-spoken by Lord Kåñëa; sri-baladevam-
to Lord Baladeva.


   The extraordinary nature of the Lord's abode in this world during His manifest pastimes is also
described in the following verse spoken by Lord Kåñëa to Lord Baladeva (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.15.5):

   "My dear brother You are superior to all of us, and Your lotus feet are worshiped by the
demigods. Just see how these trees, their branches full with fruits and sumanaù flowers, have bent
down to worship Your lotus feet. It appears that they are trying to get out of the darkness of being
obliged to accept the form of trees. It futher appears that they have accepted the forms of trees in
order to offer everything to You, so that those who see them or hear of their exemplary devotional
service may become purified of the darkness of material life."*

yathä ca

miträëéväjitäväsa-

   samänäm ätmärämänäm api, samasya sahacarasya çré-bhagavato 'pi vä, ä sarvato-bhävena
sarväàçenaiva priyam iti taträtad-aàçatvaà niñidhya sarvato 'py änandätiçaya-pradatvaà
pradarçitam. çré-çukaù.

   yathä-just; ca-also; apadi-immediately; eva-indeed; abhitaù-on all sides; paçyan-looking; diçaù-in
the directions; apaçyat-Lord Brahmä saw; puraù-sthitam-situated in front of him; våndävanam-
Våndävana; jana-äjévya-druma-äkérëam-dense with trees, which were the means of living for the
inhabitants; samä-priyam-and which was equally pleasing in all seasons; yatra-where; naisarga-by
nature; durvairäù-living in enmity; saha äsan-live together; nå-human beings; måga-ädayaù-and
animals; miträëi-friends; iva-like; ajita-of Lord Çré Kåñëa; äväsa-residence; druta-gone away; ruö-
anger; tarçaka-ädikam-thirst and so on. samänäm-equally disposed to everyone; ätma-arämänäm-of
the transcendentalists who take pleasure in the Srlf; api-also; samasya-the word "sama"; sahacarasya-

companions; çré-bhagavataù-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; api-also; vä-or; ä-the letter "a";
sarvatah-bhävena-in all respects; sarva-aàçena-in all details; eva-certainly; priyam-dear; iti-thus;
tatra-there; atat-aàçatvam-the conditon of beng material; niçidhya-having rejected; sarvataù-
completely; api- also; änanda-of bliss; atiçaya-great; pradatvam-granting; pradarçitam-os revealed; çré-
çukaù-spoken by ÇRéla Çukadeva Gosvami.


   Çré Våndävana-dhäma is the Lord's transcendental place, beyond the reach of the illusory
energy. It is full of unlimited transcendental bliss, and it is pleasing to everyone, and especially to
the self-satisfied, saintly devotees, who are equal to everyone, and inimical to no one. This
confirmed by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.13.59-60):

   "Then, looking in all directions, Lord Brahmä immediately saw Våndävana before him, filled
with trees, which were the means of livelihood for the inhabitants and which were equally pleasing
in all seasons.*
   "Våndävana is the transcendental abode of the Lord, where there is no hunger, anger or thirst.
Through naturally inimical, both human beings and fierce animals live there together in
transcendental friendship."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.175
records.text:
Text 1


   tad evaà çré-kåñëasya nitya-léläspadatvena täny eva sthänäni darçitäni. tac cävadhäräëäà çré-
kåñëasya vibhutve sati vyabhicäri syät. tatra samädhéyate teñäà sthänänäà nitya-tal-léläspadatvena
çrüyamänatvät tadädhära-çakti-lakña-svarüpa-vibhutvam avagamyate. sa bhagavaù kasmin
pratiñöhati it sve mahmni iti çruteù. säkñäd brahma gopäla-puré ity ädeç ca.

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; çré-kåñëasya-of Çré Kåñëa; nitya-eternal; léla-of pastimes;
aspadatvena- as the abode; täni-they; eva-certainly; sthänäni-places; darçitäni-reealed; tat-that;
avadhäräëäm-conclusion; çré-kåñëasya-about Çré Kåñëa; vibhutve sati-in the all-pervasiveness;
vyabhicäri-error; syät-may be; tatra-in this matter; samädhéyate-the doubt is resoved; teñäm-of
them; sthänänäm-of the places; nitya-eternal; tat-of Him; léla-of pastimes; aspadatvena-as the
abode; çrüyamänatvät-because it is heard in the Vedic literatures; tat-of Him; adhära-for
maintenance; çakti-potency; lakñaëa- characterized; svarüpa-form; vibhutvam-all-pervasiveness;
avagamyate-may be understood; saù-He; bhagavaù-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; kasmin-
where?; pratiñöhati-is situated; iti-thus; sve-in His own; mahimni-glory; iti-thus; çruteù-from the
Çruti-sastra (Chandogya Upansiad 7.24.1); säkñät-directly; brahma-the Supreme spirit; gopäla-of
Lord Gopala; puré-the town (Våndävana); iti-thus; ädeù-in the passage eginning (Gopala-tapani
Upanisad 2.29) ca-also;

   We have thus explained that Våndävana, Mathurä, and Dvärakä are the transcendental abodes
where Çré Kåñëa eternally enjoys pastimes. At this point someone may object, saying that because
Lord Kåñëa is all-pervading, it is improper to limit Him to these three places. He is present
everwhere. To this objection we may reply that the Vedic literatures describe Våndävana, Mathurä
and Dvärakä as the places where Lord Kåñëa eternally enjoys pastimes, and the Vedic literatures
also explain that Lord Kåñëa is all-pervading by His potencies. His potencies, which He uses to
maintain the material creation, are all-pervading, and in that sense He is peresent in every corner
of the universe. He does not, however, eternally enjoy pastimes in every corner of the material
universe. His presence in His original form as Çré Kåñëa, and His eternal pastimes, are specifically
manifest in Våndävana, Mathurä, and Dvärakä, and not in other places. This is confirmed in the
following statements of Sruti-çästra:

   "Where does the Supreme Personality of Godhead reside? He resides in His own glorious abode
in the spiritual world.."
                      -Chändogya Upaniñad 7.24.1

   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead in His original form eternally resides in His own spiritual
abode known as Gopäla-puré (Våndävana)."
                  -Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad 2.29


Text 2

shäraëä-çaktis tu nataram. yatra kvacid va prakaöa-léläyäà tad-gamanädikaà çrüyate. tad api teñäm
ädhära-çakti-rüpäëäà sthanänäm äveçäd eva mantavyam. vaikuëöhäntarasya tv aprakåtatve 'pi çré-

enjoy many sweet pastimes there. When the Lord had completed all these pastimes in the company
of His associates, He left the material world and returned to the spiritual world. At that time the
Lord's prakaöa (manifest) pastimes were no longer visible to the residents of the material world, and
only the aprakaöa (unmanifest) pastimes of the spiritual world (where Lord Kåñëa delighted His
associates without any impediment) remained. At that tme there was no longer any distinction
between prakaöa and aprakaöa pastimes, for the Lord's pastimes could no longer be directly seen by

   The separation felt by the residents of Våndävana after Lord Kåñëa's departure to Mathurä are
specifically described in various Vedic literatures. In Kåñëa's absence, the Våndävana residents were
greatly afflicted with feelings of separation, and in that state they considered a momentary glimpse
of Lord Kåñëa to be more valuable to them than the value of their entire lives multiplied by millions
of times. Uddhava visited them in order to console them, and after Uddhava's departure, when the
distress of the devotees in Våndävana became again very great, Lord Balaräma Himself returned to
Våndävana in order to pacify them.

   The hearts of the residents of Våndävana were filled with unlimited intense longings to again
see Lord Kåñëa, and on the pretext of going on pilgramage during the time of a solar eclips, they
went to the holy place of Kurukñetra to see Kåñëa. At Kurukñetra the residents of Våndävana were
just like cataka birds (who do not accept water to drink from any source other than rainwater,
drunk by them as it falls through the sky), who have regained their almost lost lives by seeing the
dark cloud of Lord Kåñëa's form and hearing the grave thunder of His words. Then again, the
residents of Våndävana also seemed like poverty-stricken men on the brink of starvation who have
jsut gotten the urgently needed meal that was the personal association of Lord Kåñëa. In this way,
Lord Kåñëa, after satisfying the residents of Våndävana with His own association, after enjoying
some pastimes in their company, and after speaking (as He had also previously done) many words
reassuring them that He would soon return to Våndävana e with them again, Lord Kåñëa again sent
them all back to their delightful abode of Çré Våndävana-dhäma.

   The sequence of events may be given as follows: First, the residents of Våndävana traveled to
Kurukñetra at the time of the solar eclips, then (2) there was the Räjusüya sacrifice of Mahäräja
Yudhiñöhira, during which (3) Çiçupäla was killed. Then (4) there was the gambling match between
the Kurus and Päëòavas, and then (5) the killing of Çälva, the celebrated description of which is
found in the Vana-prarva of the Mahäbhärata. After that (6) Dantavakra was killed, and after that
(7) the Päëòavas were exiled to the forest. After that (8) Lord Balaräma went on His tour of all the
holy places, and after that (9) the Kurukñetra war was fought, and Duryodhana was killed. From

this sequence of events we may conclude that the journey of the residents of Våndävana to
Kurukñetra at the time of the solar eclips happened not a very long time after the killing of Kaàsa.

   In this connection someone may raise the objection that Lord Kåñëa's grandson Aniruddha was
already full grown when the residents of Våndävana met Lord Kåñëa at Kurukñetra and therefore
that event must have been many years after the killing of Kaàsa. That Aniruddha was already an
adult by that time is proven by the following statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.6):

   "When the residents of Våndävana and the members of the Yadu dynasty went to Kurukñetra at
the time of the solar eclips, some important personalities like Aniruddha, the son of Pradyumna,
and Kåtavarma, the commander-in-chief of the Yadu dynasty, along with Sucandra, Çuka, and
Çaraëa, remained in Dvärakä to protect the city."*

   This objection is answered by the fact that both Pradyumna and Aniruddha grew very quickly. It
did not take many years for them to change from new-born infants to fully grown adults. And
therefore, there need not have been an period of many years between the killing of Kaàsa and the

adulthood of Pradyumna and Aniruddha. The rapid growth to adulthood by Pradyumna and
Aniruddha is described in the following statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.55.9):

   "Pradyumna, the son of Lord Kåñëa grew very swiftly, and before long he was fully grown."

   Another explanation may also be given: Another person, one of the direct sons of Lord Kåñëa
was also named Aniruddha. This Aniruddha was one of the 18 mahäratha sons of Lord Kåñëa and
he is mentioned at the end of the Tenth Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam. It may be that the
Aniruddha who remained in Dvärakä at the time of the pilgrimage to Kurukñetra was this
Aniruddha. At any rate, there was not a very long interval of time between the killing of Kaàsa
and the meeting of Lord Kåñëa with the inhabitants of Våndävana at Kurukñetra.

yamunäm-the Yamuna river; uttirya- having corssed; nanda-vrajam-the cowherd land of Nanda
Maharaja; gatvä-having gone; sa-utkanthau-full of longing; pitarau- parents; abhivädya-greeting;
asväsya-and comforting; täbhyam-by them; ça-asru-covered with tears; kaëöham- necks; äliìgitaù-
embraced; sakala-to all; gopa-våndän-the cowhered men; pranämya-offering obeisances; asväsya-and
comforting; bahu-many; vastra-garments; abharaëa-ornaments; adibhiù-and with other gifts; tatra-
sthän-staying there; sarvän-all; samarpayäm äça-gave.


   "Hearing that Çiçupäla had been killed by Kåñëa, Dantavakra arrived at Mathurä to fight with
the Lord, and when Lord Kåñëa heard about this, He mounted a chariot and went to Mathurä to
fight with the demon. Kåñëa and Dantavakra remained at the entrance of Mathurä and fought day
and night for a long time. In the midst of this battle Lord Kåñëa struck Dantavakra so heavily with
His club that the demon immediately fell down dead to the ground, all his limbs crushed by the
force of Lord Kåñëa's blow. He seemed like a great mountain smashed to pieces by a powerful bolt of
lightning. Because he was killed by Lord Kåñëa, the demon Dantavakra attained a spiritual form
like the Lord's and entered the eternal and blissful spiritual world, which is only approached by the

perfect yogés. Dantavakra and Çiçupäla had actually been the gatekeepers of Vaikuëöha, and their
names were Jaya and Vijaya. On the pretext of being cursed by the four Kumäras, they had
descended to the material world for three lifetimes in order t facilitate the pastimes of the
Personality of Godhead. Now that the three lifetimes were completed, they were killed by the Lord,
and they attained liberation, returning to their original posts in the spiritual world.
   "After killing this demon, Lord Kåñëa crossed the Yamunä river, and entered Vrajabhümi, the
kingdom of Nanda Mahäräja. His foster parents, Nanda and Yaçodä had been greatly aggrieved
because of separation from the Him, and He greeted them and consoled them. Tears running down
their necks, Lord Kåñëa's parents embraced their dear son. Lord Kåñëa also offered respectful
obeisances to all the cowherd residents of Vraja, consoling them with many words, and offering
them many gifts of costly garments, ornaments and other things.

pastimes; keçavaù-Lord Keçavah.


   "Having returned to Våndävana, Lord Kåñëa continuously enjoyed pastimes, day and night, with
the gopés on the charming Yamunä shore, which had many groves of transcendental desire-trees.

there; mäsa-dvayam-for two monts; aväsa-uvasa-resided; ha-certianly.


   "The Lord remained in Våndävana for two months. Garbed as a cowherd boy, He enjoyed many
delightful pastimes with the residents of Vraja, and reciprocated their expressions of love in many
ways."

saìgamaù. yat sthänam adyäpi dvärakä-dig-gataà tad iheti prasiddhaà vartate. sarvam etat çré-
näradasya çré-bhagavad-rathasy ca mano-mayatvät sambhavati. ataù çré-bhagavatenäpi virodho
nästéty alaà kalpa-bheda-kalpanäya. yata eva jhaöiti tasya çälva-vadha-çravaëam api tatroktaà
sampadyate. tathä çré-kåñëasya gokulägamanaà ca çré-bhägavata-sammatam eva

   atra-in this connection; idam-this; jïeyam-may be understood; dantavakrasya-of Dantavakra;
mathuräyäm- at Mathurä; ägamanam-arrival; räjasüya-the Räjasüya sacrifice; anantaram-after;

ickly; tasya-of him; çälva-of Çalva; vadha-of the death; çravaëam-hearing; api-also; tatra- there;
uktam-said; sampadyate-was; tathä-in the same way; çré-kåñëasya-of Çré Kåñëa; gokula-at Gokula

certainly.


   It may seem to some readers that this account of the killing of Dantavakra and Lord Kåñëa's
return to Våndävana contradicts the description found in Çrémad-Bhägavatam. Actually there is no
contradiction here, and the accounts of the Padma Puräëa and Çrémad-Bhägavatam are in perfect
agreement. This may be understood in the following way: Dantavakra considered that, upon
Uddhava's advice, Lord Kåñëa had asked Bhéma to kill Jaräsandha in a club duel, because Lord
Kåñëa Himself was not very expert at fighting with clubs. Proud of His own skill in club-fighting,
Dantavakra planned to challenge Lord Kåñëa to a private club duel, and then kill Him. Dantvakra
wanted to fight with Lord Kåñëa alone in order to protect himself from any possible revenge Lord
Kåñëa's friends might try to take on him after he had killed the Lord. Thinking in this way,

Dantavakra specifically did not want to fight Lord Kåñëa in Dvärakä, but in some place far away
from the Lord's capitol city. Thinking that Lord Kåñëa had remained in Inraprastha after the
Räjasüya sacrifice had ended, Dantavakra sent a message challenging the Lord to come to Mathurä
and fight with him. The message came to Indraprastha, and Närada Muni, travelling on Lord
Kåñëa's personal chariot, which moves as swiftly as the mind, instantly carried it to Dvärakä, where
Lord Kåñëa had just finished killing Çälva. Lord Kåñëa and Närada Muni immediately travelled to
Mathurä on the Lord's transcendental chariot, (the place in Mathurä where they arived is still
known, even today, as the "Dvärakä Gate"), and the Lord answered Dantavakra's challenge, and
killed him. Because Våndävana is so close to Mathurä, Lord Kåñëa took the opportunity to visit the
gopas and gopés there.
    The Padma Puräëa's description of Lord Kåñëa's return to Våndävana is in perfect harmony with
the account of the Lord's pastimes found in Çrémad-Bhägavatam. This may be seen in the following
quotation from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.39.35):


Text 27


tas tathä tapyatir vékñya

santvayäm äsa sa-premair

  taù-the gopis; tathä-in that way; tapyatiù-suffering; vékñya-having seen; sva-prasthäne-on the

   "Kåñëa was very much affected upon seeing the plight of the gopés, and He therefore consoled
them. He told them they should not be aggreived; He was coming back very soon after finishing His
business."*

having given; suhådäm-to our friends and well-wishers; sukham-happiness; iti-thus.

  Lord Kåñëa's promise to return to Våndävana is also recorded in the following verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.45.23) spoken by the Lord to Nanda and Yaçodä, shortly after the Lord had killed
Kaàsa:

   "My dear father and mother, I know you will be feeling separation by returning to Våndävana
and leaving Us here, but please rest assured that I shall be coming back to Våndävana just after
giving some satisfaction to my real father and mother, Vasudeva and Devaké, My grandfather, and
other relatives and family members."*

pratépam-the enemy; sarva-of all; sätvatäm-the members of the Yadu dynasty; yat- which; aha-said;
vaù-to us; samägtya-assembled; kåñëaù- Lord Kåñëa; satyam-truth; karoti-will do; tat-that;
ägamiçyati-will arrive; adérgena-in a short; kälena-time; vrajam-to Vraja; acyutaù-the infallible

  The following verses (spoken by Uddhava to Nanda Mahäraja and Yaçodä-devé) also record Lord
Kåñëa's promise to return to Våndävana (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.35 and 34):

   "I have brought a message from Kåñëa to the effect that He will soon come back to Våndävana
and satisfy you both by His personal presence. Now that Kåñëa has killed King Kaàsa, the Yädava's
enemy, in the wrestling arena, Kåñëa has promised that He will come back to Våndävana after
finishing His business in Mathurä. This promise He will surely fulfill."*


Text 30


    tasya çré-mukhena bhakta-mukhena ca bahuçaù kalpänäm anyathänupapatteù satya-saìkalpaù

    tasya-of Lord Kåñëa; çré-mukhena-from the mouth; bhakta-of the devotees; mukhena-by the
mouth; ca-also; bahuçaù-many times; kalpänäm-of these expressions; anyatha-otherwise;
anupapatteù-no reason; satya-saìkalpaù-truthful; iti-thus; çruteù-from the çruti-sastra; éçvaränäm-
of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; vacaù-the words; satyam- truth; iti-thus; svayam-directly;
çré-bhägavatam-in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.31); ca-also.


   Many different times Lord Kåñëa promised that He would return to Våndävana, and His
devotees also repeated that promise. It is not reasonable to assume that Lord Kåñëa would not keep
such a promise repeated so many times. Lord Kåñëa always speaks truthfully and does not break His
promise. This is confirmed by the çruti-çästra, which says:

  "The Supreme Personality of Godhead is always truthful."

  Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.31) also says:

  "The Supreme Personality of Godhead always speaks the truth."


Text 31


na kevalam etävad eva känaëam, tasya vrajägamanam api sphuöam evety ähuù

yarhy ambujäkñäpasasära bho bhavän
   kurün madhün vätha suhåd-didåkñayä

describe; yarhi-whenever; ambuja-akña-O lotus-eyed one; apasasära-You go away; bho-oh; bhavän-
Yourself; kurün-the descendants of King Kuru; madhün-the inhabitants of Mathurä Vrajabhümi);
vä-either; atha-therefore; suhåt-didåkñayä-for meeting them; evam-in this way; madhün-the word
"madhün"; mathuräm- means Mathurä; va-or; iti-thus; vyäkhäya-having explained; tadäném-then;
tat-maëdale-in that area; suhådaù-the word "suhådaù (friends)"; vrajasthäù-means "the residents of
Vraja"; eva-certainly; prakaöäù-manifested; iti-thus; taiù- by them; api-also; abhimatam-considered.


   These are not the only quotes where Lord Kåñëa's return to Våndävana is promised or described.
For example, Lord Kåñëa's return to Våndävana is described in the following statement of the
inhabitants of Dvärakä (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.11.9), where (according to Çrédhara Svämé) the word
"madhün" refers to the residents of Våndävana (which is situated within the district of Mathurä):

  "O lotus-eyed Lord, whenever You go away to Mathurä, Våndävana or Hastinäpura to meet

Your friends and relatives,
every moment of Your absence seems like a million years. O infallible one, at that time our eyes
become useless, as if bereft of sun."*


Text 32


tatra yoga-prabhävena
   nétvä sarva-janaà hariù

ity atra sarva-çabdät. dvärakä-väsinäù çré-bhagavantam.

    tatra-there; yoga-prabhävena-by His mystic potency; nétvä-having carried; sarva-janam-all His
friends and relatives; hariù-Lord Hari; iti-thus; atra-in this connectio9n; sarva-çabdät-from the
word sarva (all)". dvärakä-väsinaù-the residents of Dvärakä; çré-bhagavatam-to the Supreme
Personality of Godhead.


   The Lord also arranged for the residents of Våndävana to visit Him at Dvärakä. This is described
in the following verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.50.57):

  "By His mystic potency Lord Kåñëa brought all the residents of Våndävana to Dvärakä."

   The word "sarva" (all) here must include the residents of Våndävana. This verse is spoken by the
residents of Dvärakä about the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

because; jïätén-relatives; vaù- you; drañöum-to see; eçyämaù-we shall return; vidhäya- having given;

   That Çré Kåñëa visited Våndävana after the killing of Dantavakra is confirmed by these verses of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam, and also by the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.45.23), where Lord
Kåñëa (just after killing King Kaàsa) says to Nanda Mahäräja and Yaçodä-devé:

   "My dear father and mother, I know you will be feeling separation by returning to Våndävana
and leaving us here, but please rest assured that I will be coming back to Våndävana just after
giving some satisfaction to my real father and mother, Vasudeva and Devaké, My grandfather, and
other relatives and family members."*

upekñitam-neglected; äsét-was.


   That meeting of Lord Kåñëa with the residents of Våndävana at the holy place of Kurukñetra
occured before His visit to Våndävana and also before the killing of Dantavakara is confirmed by
the following words spoken by Lord Kåñëa to the gopés during their meeting at Kurukñetra (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.82.41):

   "My dear friends, you know that Lord Balaräma and Myself left Våndävana just to please our
relatives and family members. Thus we were long engaged in fighting with our enemies, and were
obliged to forget you, who were so much attached to Me in love and affection. I can understand
that by this action I have been ungrateful to you, but still I know you are faithful to Me. May I
inquire if you have been thinking of Us although We had to leave you behind? My dear gopis do
you now dislike remembering Me, considering Me to have become unfaithful to you? Do you take
My misbehavior with you very seriously?"*

   Lord Kåñëa did not want to return to Våndävana until after most of the important demons had
been killed. After Dantavakra was killed, however, He considered that most of the demons had

already been dispatched, and He could then return to Våndävana for a visit.

punar evaà mä bhüd iti bhü-bhära-häraëädi-prayojana-rüpeëa nija-priya-jana-sahgamäntaräyena

rüpaà çré-våndävanasyaiva prakäça-viçeñaà tebhyaù kåñëaà ca tatra chandobhiù stüyamänam ity

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; mäsa-dvayam-for two months; prakaöam-manifested; kréòitvä-
performing pastimes; çré-kåñëaù-Lord Kåñëa; api-also; taë-to them; ätma- their hearts; viraha-of
separation; arti-by distress; bhaya-by fear; péòitän-tormented; avadhäya-having heard; punaù- again;
evam-in this way; mä-doët; bhüt-be; iti-thus; bhü-of the earth; bhära-the burden; häraëa-removal;

pastime; eké-kåtya-joining; pürva-previously; ukta-described; apraköa- unmanifest; lélä-for pastimes;
avakaça-opportunity; rüpam- consisting of; çré-våndävanasya-of Çré Våndävana-dhama; eva-
certianly; prakäça-viçeñam-specific manifestation; tebhyaù-from them; kåñëam-Lord Kåñëa; ca-also;
tatra- there; chandobhiù-by the vedic hymns; stüyamänam-being glorified; iti ädi-beginning with
these words; ukta-diçä-by the statement; svena-own; näthena-by the Lord; sa-nätham- having a
ruler; çré goloka-akhyam-named Goloka; padam-abode;

also; jagäma- went.


   Lord Kåñëa then returned to Våndävana and enjoyed manifest pastimes with the devotees there
for two months. When Lord Kåñëa became aware that the inhabitants of Våndävana were very
anxious about the possibility of being again seperated from, He reassured them, telling them that
He would never be separated from them. He remained in Våndävana with them in His aprakaöa
form, invisible to the eyes of ordinary conditioned souls, and He fulfilled their earnest desire to
have His association constantly. At the same time in His prakaöa form He left Våndävana and
returned again to Dvärakä. Lord Kåñëa's eternal aprakaöa presence in Våndävana in the spiritual
world (Goloka) is described in the following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.28.18):

  "All the cowherd men saw Kåñëa, who was being worshiped with excellent prayers on the Goloka
Våndävana planet."

Text 4

   After Lord Kåñëa's two month visit to Våndävana He brought all the residents of Våndävana
back with to Goloka Våndävana in the spiritual world. This is confirmed in the following prose
passage from the Padma Puåaëa, Uttara-khaëòa (which immediately follows the passage quoted in
Anuccheda 175, Texts 23-24):

    "Then, by Lord Kåñëa's mercy, Nanda Mahäräja, and all the cowherd men of Vraja, along with
all their wives, children, cows and other domestic animals, as well as all the deer and other wild
animals in the Våndävana forest, and every living entity in Våndävana, all manifested eternal
spiritual forms and, boarding transcendental airplanes, traveled to Goloka Våndävana, the highest
planet in the spiritual sky. Lord Kåñëa thus gave to His friends eternal residence in His own abode,
which is free from all imperfection. After this, Lord Kåñëa, who was being glorified by the demigods
in the upper material planets, entered Dvärakä and continued His manifest pastimes within the
material world."

became unaware tha Kåñëa had ever gone to Mathurä, or that they had ever been separated from
Him.

   tataù-then; ca-also; vimäna-of airplanes; çironàaëinä-by the crest-jewel; svena-by His own; eva-

find; kim artham-why?; parvatam-to a mountain; vrajet-would one go; iti-thus; nyäyät-from the
adage; samépa-of "nearby"; arthe-with the meaning; avyayam- always; arke-çabdaù-the word "arke";

na-did not; veda- understand; sväm-their own; gatim-destination; bhraman- bewildered; iti-thus;
vadatä-speaking; çré-bhagavatä-by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tesäm-of them; gatitvena-
about the destination; vibhävitaù-manifested; asau-this; tasmät-therefore; vndävane-in Våndävana;
nigüòha- concealed; praveçe-entrance; eva-certainly; samaïjasaù- correctly; atra-here; våndävana-
in Våndävana; nity- eternal; lélä-pastimes; väkya-descriptions; våndam-many; ca-also; adhikam-
abundance; api-also; asti-there is; pramäëam-evidence.


   Someone may raise the objection: If previously (Çrémad-Bhägavatam Canto 10 Chapter 28) Lord
Kåñëa had shown the highest planet in the spiritual world (goloka) to the cowhered men in
Våndävana, and thus revealed that the Våndävana of this earth planet is in truth non-different
from the Goloka Våndävana in the spiritual world, then why did He take them to the Goloka
Våndävana in the spiritual world, if the earthly Våndävana and the Goloka Våndävana planet are
actually identical? There is an adage "Why should one go to a mountain in search of honey, if
honey is easily available nearby?" According to this understanding, therefore, there is no reason for
Lord Kåñëa to transfer the residents of Våndävana to the Goloka planet, because they are actually
already living there.
   The answer to this objection follows: In the Tenth Canto, 28th Chapter of Çrémad-Bhägavatam,
Lord Kåñëa reveals His aprakaöa (invisible to the eyes of ordianry conditioned souls) presence in
Våndävana. In the spiritual world (goloka), Lord Kåñëa, His associates, and His pastimes are all
aprakaöa (invisible to the conditined souls), whereas in the Lord's pastimes in the earthly
Våndävana, these are all prakraöa (visible to the conditioned souls). Therefore when this passage
says that the Lord traveled to Goloka Våndävana with His associates, the primary understanding is
that the Lord remained with them in His aprakaöa (invisible to the conditioned souls) form. These
aprakaöa pastimes are known as the pasitmes of Goloka Våndävana, the highest planet in the
spiritual world. Many scriptural passages confirm this explanation of the Lord's eternal pastimes in
the Goloka Våndävana planet.

    The words "dväravatéà viveça" (and then the Lord entered Dvärakä) at the end of the prose
passage from the Padma Puräëa, Uttara-khanda (quoted in Anuccheda 176, Text 4) may be
explained in the following way:
    Lord Kåñëa and the members of the Yadu dynasty left Dvärakä to kill Çälva. After Çälva was
killed, the Yädavas waited for Lord Kåñëa to return without Him. Therefore, after the killing of
Çälva, Lord Kåñëa entered Dvärakä, along with all the members of the Yadu dynasty. This
description follows the account given in Çrémad-Bhägavatam. Although the Yädavas waited for two
months for Lord Kåñëa to return from Våndävana, that two months seemed to them to be only a
few moments. A similar contraction of time was experienced by the Våndävana cowherd boys
stolen by Lord Brahmä. This is described in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.43):

   "Although they had been absent for an entire year, the cowherd boys thought that year to be as
long as half a moment."

abhipräyeëa-with the meaning; eva-certianly; çré-våndävana-of Våndävana; nätha-for the Lord;
upäsanä-worship; mantre-in the mantra; nihata-kamsatvena-as the killer of Kaàsa; tat-of Him;
viçeñaëam-description; dattam-is given; yathä-just as; baudhäyana-of the Baudhäyana; ukte-in the

   That Lord Kåñëa returned to Våndävana after killing Kaàsa, Çälva, and Dantvakra is alluded to
in many verses that describe the worship of Lord Kåñëa as the master of Våndävana, and the killer
of Kaàsa. That both descriptions are found in the same verses confirms the explanation that Lord
Kåñëa returned to Våndävana after killing Kaàsa. Examples of this may be found in the following
statements of the Baudhäyana-çästra:

   "O Lord Govinda, O Supreme Personality of Godhead who is worshiped by Lord Indra, the king
of the demigods, O Lord who killed Kaàsa, and who is very dear to the gopés."

   "O Lord Govinda, O Supreme Controller, O killer of Kaàsa, O Lord who is very dear to the
gopés."


Text 12

anusmarantyo mäà nityam
  acirän mäm upaisyatha iti;

diñöyä yadäsén mat-sneho
   bhavaténäà mad-äpanaù iti;

   ittham-thus; eva-certainly; punaùa-again; präpti- attainment; abhipräyeëa-by the intention;
uktam-is spoken; anusmarantyaù-remembering; mäm-Me; nityam-constantly; acirät-quickly; mäm-
Me; aupisyatha-you will attain; diñöyä-by good fortune; yada-when; asét-there was; mat- for Me;
sneha-love; bhavaténäm-of you; mat-for Me; äpanaù-attainment; iti-thus.


   When Lord Kåñëa explained to the gopés that they would again mmet Him, this should be taken
as a prediction of His return to Våndävana. The following verses may be taken as examples of this
prediction:

   "My dear gopés, by constantly remembering Me, you will quickly attain My association."*
              -Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.36

   "O My dear damsels of Vraja, your affection for Me is your good fortune, for it is the only means
by which you have attained My favor."*
              -Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.44


Text 13


gopénäà sä gurur satiù iti ca.

   gopénäm sah guruù gatiù it ca-also in the following verse from Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10 83.1)


athäungåhya bhavavän
   gopénäà sa gurur gatiù

yudhiñöhiram athäpåcchat
  sarväàs ca suhådo 'vyayaù.


   That the gopés were again to attain Lord Kåñëa's association is also confirmed by the following
statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10 83.1):

   "Lord Kåñëa is the spiritual master and ultimate destination which was to be attained by the
gopés."*


Text 14


   tathaiva kevalena hi bhävena ity ädi padya-dvaya-kåtena sädhaka-cäréëäà gopénäà prathama-

   gopyo gävo nagä mågäù

sädhaka-cärénäm-elevated devotees; gopénäm-of the gopis; prathama-first; tat-of Lord Kåñëa; präpti-
attainment; prastavena-from the beginning nitya-eternally; preyasénäm- very dear; api-although; tat-
from Lord Kåñëa; mahä-great; viyoga-separation; anantara-after; präptim-attainment; tasya-of this;

dväbhyäm-by the following two verses ( Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.12.10-11).


   Although the greatly elevated gopés were extremely dear to Lord Kåñëa from the very first time
they met Him, they still were separated from Him for a certain time. Their reunion with Him and
the end of their separation from Him is alluded to in the following verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(11.12.8, 11.12.10, and 11.12.11):

   "All the inhabitants of Våndävana, including the gopés, cows, unmoving creatures, the twin
arjuna trees, animals, living entities with stunted consciousness, bushes and thickets and snakes like
Käliya all achieved the perfection of life by unalloyed love for Me and thus very easily achieved
Me."***


Text 15

rämeëa särdhaà mathuräà praëéte
   çväphalkinä mayy anurakta-cittäù
vigäòha-bhävena na me viyoga-
   tévrädhayo 'nyaà dadåçuù sukhäya

   rämeëa-with Balaräma; särdham-with; mathuräm-to Mathurä City; praëéte-when brought;
çväphalkinä-by Akrüra; mayi-Myself; anurakta-constantly attached; cittäù- those whose
consciousness was; vigäòha-extremely deep; bhävena-by love; na-not; me-than Me; viyoga-
separation; tévra-intense; ädhayaù-mental distress, ansiety; anyam- other; dadåçuù-they say; sukhäya-
that could make them ahppy.


   "The residents of Våndävana headed by the gopés were always completely attached to Me with
deepest love. Thus when I, along with My brother Balaräma, was brought to Mathurä City by My
uncle Akrüra, the residents of Våndävana suffered extreme mental distress due to separation from
Me, and could not find any other source of happiness in their lives."***


Text 16


täs täù kñapäù preñöhatamena nétä
   mayaiva våndävana-gocareëa
kñaëärdhavat täù punar aìga täsäà
   hénä mayä kalpa-samä babhüvuù

   täù täù-all those; kñapäù-nights; preñöhatamena- with the most dearly beloved; néäù-spent; mayi-
with Me; eva-indeed; våndavana-in Våndävana; gocareëa-who can be known in; kñaëa-a moment;
ärdhavat-like half; täù-those very nights; punar-again; aìga-dear Uddhava; täsäm-for the gopés;

   "Dear Uddhava, all of those nights which the gopés spent with Me, their most dearly beloved, in
the land of Våndävana, seemed to them to pass in less than a moment. Bereft of My association,
however, those same nights appeared to the gopés to drag on forever, as if each night were equal to a
day of Brahmä."***


Text 17


  atra vigäòha-bhävena viyoga-tévrädhayaù satyo mattaù anyam nija-sakhyädikam api na sukhäya
