satyaù kalpa-samä babhüvuù. adhunä tu tädåçyo na bhavantéti nästy eva viyoga ity arthaù.

    atra-in this verse; vigäòha-extremely deep; bhävena-by love; viyoga-separation; tévra-intense;
adhayaù-mental distress; datyaù-truth; mattaù-than Me; anyam-other; nija- own; sakhya-
friendship; adikam-beginning with; api-even; na- not; sukhäya-that could make the happy; dadåçuù-
they saw; tataù-therefore; ca-also; adhunä-at present; tu-but; sukhäya-for happiness; paçyanti-they
see; iti-thus; viyogaù-separation; na-not; asti-is; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; evam-in this way; taù-
täù-all those; kñapäù-nights; mayä-of Me; hénäù-bereft; satyaù-in truth; kalpa-a day of Brahma;
samäù-equal to; babhüvuù-became; adhunä-at present; tu-but; tädåçyaù-like that; na-not; bhavanti-
are; iti-thus; na-not; asti-is; eva-certainly; viyogaù- separation; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.


   We may note that in these verses the verbs "dadåçuù" (saw) and "babhüvuù" (became) are in the
past tense. Using the past-tense, these verses describe the gopés' unhappiness because of separation
from Kåñëa and their experiencing a single night to be as long as a day of Brahmä because of Lord
Kåñëa's absence. Because these activities are described in the past, we may conclude that they are
no longer happening at the time Lord Kåñëa spoke these verses to Uddhava. At that time the gopés'
separation from Lord Kåñëa had ended, and they were continually enjoying pastimes with Him in
His aprakaöa form.

   tataù-therefore; ca-also; prakaöa-manifest; aprakaöayoù-and of unmanifest pastimes; påthaktva-
distinction; apratipattya-by non-acceptance; eva-certainly; aprakaöa-unmanifested; bhävam-nature;
äpadya-attaining; sva-of His own; näma-holy name; rüpayoù-and form; eva- certainly; täù-the gopis;
sthitäù-situated; iti-thus; äha-He says; täù-they (the gopés); na-not; avidan-were aware of; mayi-in
Me; anuçanga-by intimate contact; baddha-bound up; dhiyaù-their consciousness; svam-their own;
ätmänam-body or self; adaù-something remote; tathä-considering like that; idam-this which is most
near; yathä-just as; samädhau-in yoga samädhi; munayaù-great sages; abdhi-of the ocean; toye- in
the water; nadyaù-the rivers; praviñöäù-have entered; iva-like; näma-names; rüpe-and forms.


   The Lord's presence in His prakaöa (visible to the conditioned souls) and aprakaöa (invisible to

the conditioned souls) forms is ultimately one. There is no real distinction between prakaöa and
aprakaöa. Always engaged in ecstatic meitation on Lord Kåñëa and perceiving Him in His aprakaöa
form, the gopés forgot even about their own names and forms. This is described in the following
verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.12.12) where Lord Kåñëa says:

   "My dear Uddhava, just as the great sages in yoga trance merge into self-realization like rivers
merging into the ocean, and are thus not aware of material names and forms, similarly the gopés of
Våndävana were so completely attached to Me within their minds that they could not think of
their bodies, nor of this world, nor of their future lives. Their entire consciousness was simply
bound up in Me."***


Text 2


    täs tathä-bhütä virahautkaëöhyätiçayenäbhivyakta-durdhara-mahä-bhävaù satyaù, atha kadäcit
täsäà darçanärthaà gate mayi labdhno yaù anuçaìgaù mahä-modana'bhäväbhivyakti-käré punaù-
saàyogas tena baddho dhér yäsäà tathä-bhütaù satyaù svaà mamatäspadam ätmänam
ahaìkäräspadaà ca adaù aprakaöa-lélänugatatvenäbhimataà vä tathedam prakaöa
lélänugatatvenäbhimataà vä yathä syät tathä nävidan kintu dvayor aikyenaivävidur ity arthaù.

   täù-the gopis; tathä-bhütäù-in that way; viraha-of separation; autkaëöhya-with anxiety;
atiçayena-great; abhivyakta-manifested; durdhara-difficult to acheive; mahä-bhävaù-ecstatic love;
satyaù-truth; atha-now; kadäcit-at certain times; täsäm-of them; darçana-seeing; artham-for the
purpose; gate-gone; mayi-in Me; labdhaù-attained; yaù-which; anuçaìgaù-contact; mahä-great;
modana-bliss; bhäva- state; abhivyakti-käré-manifesting; punaù-again; saàyogaù-meeting; tena-by
that; baddhaù-bound; bhéù-mind; yäsäm-of whom; tathä-bhütaù-in that way; satyaù-uthfully; svam-
own; mama-aspadam-concept of pssesiveness; ätmänam-self; ahaìkära-aspadam-concept of self; ca-
also; adaù-from this; aprakaöa-unmanifest; léla-pastimes; anugatatvena-following; abhimatam-
considered; vä-or; tatha-in that way; idam-this prakaöa-manifested; léla-pastimes; anugatatvena-
following; abhimatam-considered; vä-or; yathä-just as; syät-may be; tathä-in the smae way; na-not;
avidan-understood; kintu- however; dvayoù-of the two; aikyena-as one; ev-certainly; aviduù-
understood; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.


   In this verse Lord Kåñëa describes the gopés' ecstatic love for Him in the mood of separation.
Having gotten the blissful opportunity to again see Lord Kåñëa and associate with Him, the gopés
became absorbed in continuously thinking of Him. This continuous thought of Lord Kåñëa
absorbed all their attention, and eventually they could no longer think of who they were or what
their possesions or status was. They could not understand if they were only remembering Lord
Kåñëa (aprakaöa) or whether Lord Kåñëa was actually present before them (prakaöa), they were so
intently meditating upon Him.


Text 3

   prakaöäprakaöatayä bhinnaà prakäça-dvayam abhimäna-dvayaà lélä-dvayaà cäbhed
enaiväjänann iti vivakñitam. tataç ca näma ca rüpaà ca tasmin tat-tan-näma-rüpätmany aprakaöa-
prakäça-viçeçe praviñöa iva" na tu praviñöaù, vastu-bhedäd ity arthaù. näma-rüpa iti samähäraù.

   prakaöa-as manifested; aprakaöatayä-and as unmanifested; bhinnam-different; prakäça-
manifestations; dvayam-two; abhimäna-conceptions; dvayam-two; lélä- pastimes; dvayam-two; ca-
also; abhedena-with no difference; ajänan-not understanding; iti-thus; vivakñitam-intended to be
said; tataù-therefore; ca-also; nama-name ca-and; rüpan- form; ca-also; tasmin-in that; tat-tat-
various näma-names; rüpa-atmani-and forms; aprakaöa-unmanifested; prakäça- appearance; viçeçe-
specific; praviñöaù-entered; iva-just as if; na-not; tu-but; praviñöaù-entered; vastu-of substance;
bhedät-because of difference; iti-thus; arthaù- the meaning; näma-rüpaù-the word "näma-rüpah"; iti-
thus; samaähäraù-a dvandva-samahara-samasa.


    The gopés were unable to make any distinction between the names and forms (näma-rüpe) in the
Lord's prakaöa and aprakaöa pastimes. In both prakaöa and aprakaöa pastimes the Lord manifests the
same form and His associates are also the same, He and His associates have the same names and
forms, and the pastimes are also the same. Actually prakaöa and aprakaöa are the same, except that
when the Lord and His pastimes are visible to the conditioned souls they are called prakaöa, and
when they are not seen by the conditioned souls, they are called aprakaöa. We may also note in this
connection that the phrase "praviñöa iva" (as if they had entered) indicates that the prakaöa and
aprakaöa pastimes of the Lord did not merge together and become one series of pastimes. The
prakaöa and aprakaöa pastimes were always identical, even from the very beginning, and therefore it
is not possible for them to join together, for they never had been separate. for this reason, Lord
Kåñëa said "as if they had become one". We may aso note that the word "näma-rüpe" is a samähära-
dvandva-samäsa (names and forms).


Text 4


   tatra prakaöäprakaöa-lélä-gatayor-näma-rüpayor abhede dåñöäntaù yathä samädhau munayaù iti.
samädhir atra çuddha-jivasyeti gamyam. tayor lélayor bhedävedane dåñöäntaù yathäbdhi-toye
nadyaù iti. yathä nadyaù påthivé-gatam abedhi-toya-gataà ca sva-sthitià bhedena na vindanti,
kintübhaytasyäm api sthitau samudra-toyänugatäv eväviçanti, tathä mad-anuñaìge sati prakaöam
aprakaöaà ca ca lélä-sthitià täç ca bhedena na viduù, kintu mayy eväviviçur ity arthaù. dåñöäntas tv
ayaà lélä-bhedävedanäàça eva, na tu sarvävedanäàçe; lokavat tu lélä-kaivalyam itivat. tad evaà
prakaöäprakaöa-lélayor dvayor api täsäà sva-präptau bhäva eva käränaà darçitam.

   tatra-in this verse; prakaöa-of manifest; aprakaöa- and unmanifest; lélä-pastimes; gatayoù-gone;
näma-names; rüpayoù-and of forms; abhede-in nondistinction; dåñöäntaù-example; yathä-just as;
samädau-in trance; munayaù-sages; iti-thus; samädhiù-trance; atra-here; çuddha-purified; jivasya-by
the soul; iti-thus; gamyam- approachable; tayoù-of the two; lélayoù-pastimes; bheda- difference;

avedane-in the description; dåñöäntaù-example; yatha-just as; abdhi-of the ocean; toye-in the
waters; nadyaù-the rivers; iti-thus; yathä-just as; nadyaù-the rivers; påthivé-gatam-gone to the earth;
abdhi-toya-the water of the ocean; gatam-gone; ca-also; sva-sthitim-own position; bhedena-with
difference; na-do not; vindanti-find; kintu-however; ubhayasyäm-in goth; api-also; sthitau- situated;
samudra-toya-anugatäu-in the water of the ocean; eva-certainly; aviçanti-enter; tathä-in the same
way; mat-anuçaìge-in My association; sati-when manifested; prakaöam- manifest; aprakaöa-
unmanifest; ca-also; lélä-of pastimes; sthitim-sitation; täù-the gopis; bhedena-as different; na- did
not; viduù-understand; kintu-however; mayi-in Me; eva- certainly; aviviçuù-entered; iti-thus;
arthaù-the meaning; dåñöäntaù-example; tu-but; ayam-this; lélä-of pastimes; bheda-difference;
avedana-description; aàçe-part; eva- certainly; na-not; tu-but; sarva-everything avedana- describing
aàçe-part; lokavat-just like ordinary living entities; tu-but; lélä-pastimes;.fn
2 kaivalyam-transcendental; itivat-just like; tat-therefore; evam-in this way; prakata-of manifested;
aprakaöa-and unmanifested; lélayoù-pastimes; dvayoù-of the two; api-also; täsäm-of the gopis; sva-
präptau-in the attainment; bhävaù-state; eva-certainly; käraëam-cause; darçitam-is revealed.


   In order to explain that the names and forms of the Lord and His devotees are the same in both
prakaöa and aprakraöa pastimes, Lord Kåñëa gives the following example: "yathä samädhau
munayaù" (just as great sages in the yoga trance of nirvikalpa-samädhi merge into self-realization).
In other words, the Lord explains that the names and forms of the prakaöa and aprakraöa pastimes
are not different, just as the minds of the yogés are not different from the object of their
meditation.
   Lord Kåñëa then gives another example to explain that the prakaöa and aprakraöa pastimes are
actually identical. The Lord says: "yathäbdhi-toye nadyaù" (just as rivers merge into the ocean).
This example may be taken to describe the prakaöa and aprakraöa pastimes. In other words, just as
the water flowing in different places of a river is not different from the water at the river's mouth
about to enter the ocean, in the same way the Lord's prakaöa and aprakraöa pastimes are non-
different. In other words, because the gopés were immersed in constant meditation upon Lord
Kåñëa, they perceived His presence directly, and for them there was no distinction of prakaöa and
aprakraöa.
   These examples of the yogés' meditation and the rivers' entering the ocean should be taken as
explaining the non-difference of the Lord's prakaöa and aprakraöa pastimes. They should not be
taken to explain that all variety is meaningless, as the impersonalists would have it.
   The Lord's pastimes are described in the following way in the Vedänta-sütra (2.1.33):

  "Tthe activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead may appear like those of an ordinary
human being, but they are not so in actual fact. They are all transcendental pastimes, and not in
any way like the fruitive actions of the conditioned souls."

   In this way we have described the Lord's prakaöa and aprakraöa pastimes, and the gopés' direct
association with Lord Kåñëa by continuously meditating upon Him in ecstatic love.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.178
records.text:
Text 1


tataç cäprakaöa-léläyäà praviñöa api yädåçaà tasya svarüpaà präptas tad darçayann anyad apy
anuvadati

mat-kämä ramaëaà järam
   asvarüpa-vido 'baläù
brahma mäà paramaà präpuù
   saìgäc chata-sahasraçaù

   tataù-therefore; ca-also; aprakaöa-unmanifested; léläyäm-in pastimes; praviçtaù-entered; api-
although; yädåçam-like which; tasya-His; svarüpam-original form; präptaù-attained; tat-that;
darçayan-revealing anyat- another; api-even; anuvadati-repeats; mat-Me; kämäù-those who desired;
ramaëam-a charming lover; järam-the lover of another's wife; asvarüpa-vidaù-not knowing My
actual situation; abaläù-women; brahma-the Absolute; mäm-Me; paramam-supreme; präpuù-they
achieved; saìgät-by association; çata-sahasraçaù-by hundreds of thousands.


  That the gopés attained the direct association of Lord Kåñëa in His original form by always
meditating upon Him is confirmed in the following explanation spoken by Lord Kåñëa (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 11.12.13):

   "All those hundreds of thousands of gopés were unaware of My actual position, understanding
Me to be their most charming lover and ardently desiring Me in that way. Thus, intimately
associating wih Me, the gopés attained Me, the Supreme Absolute Truth."***


Text 2


   evaà pürvokta-rétyä ta abalä brahma präpus tac ca paramaà bhagavad-rüpaà präpuù. brahmaëo
hi pratiñöhäham ity ädeù.

   evam-in this way; pürva-precious; ukta-rétyä-by the statement; taù-they; abaläù-the gopis;
brahma-the Absolute Brahman; präpuù-attained; tat-that; ca-also; paramam- supreme; bhagavat of
the Personality of godhead; rüpan-the form; präpuù-they attained; brahmaëaù-of the Brahman; hi-
certainly; pratiñöha-the basis; aham-I am; iti ädeù-from this passage (Çrémad-Bhagavad-gita 14.27).


   We may note in this verse that the word "brahma" means "the Supreme Absolute Truth", which
should be understood to mean the transcendental form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. If
one argues that the owrd "brahma" means the impersonal Brahman effulgence, still the word
"brahma" means Lord Kåñëa, for the Brahman efulgence is the emanation of the bodily rays of Lord

Kåñëa. This is confirmed in the following verse of Bhagavad-gétä (14.27), where Lord Kåñëa says:

  "I am the basis of the impersonal Brahman."

  Therefore the phrase "brahma präpuù" indicates that the gopés attained the association of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kåñëa.


Text 3


   tad evaà sthite täsäà mad-aàça-bhütänäà nitya-priyänäà saìgäd anya api tadénäm eva gokula-
bhäjaù çata-sahasraçaù präpuù. saìgasya tat-präpakatvaà ca jhaöiti samäna-bhäva-janakatvät.
yathoktam etat pürvam eva kevalena hi bhävena gopyo gävaù ity ädi. evaà gävädiñv api dvi-
vidhatvaà gamyam.

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; sthite-situated; täsäm-of them; mat-aàça-bhütänäm-manifested
from My transcendental potency; nitya-eternally; priyänäm-dear associates; saìgät-from
association; anyaù-others; api-also; tadäném-then; evga-certainly; gokulabhäjaù-residents of Gokula;
çata-in hundreds; sahasraçaù-and thousands; präpuù-attained; saìgasya-of association; tat-
präpakatvam- the cause of attainment; ca-also; jhaöiti-at once; samäna- equal; bhäva-condition;
janakatvät-because of being the origin; yatha-just as; uktam-described; etat-this; pürvam-
previously; eva-certainly; kevalena-exclusively; hi-certainly; bhävena-by love and devotion; gopyaù-
the gopés; gaväù-and surabhi cows; iti-ädi-in the passage beginning (Çrémad-Bhagavatam ); evam-
in this way; gäva-adiñu-among the surabhi cows and other residents of Gokula; api-also; dvi-
vidhatvam-two divisions; gamyam-may be understood.


   Some of the gopés were intimate eternal associates of Lord Kåñëa and manifestations of His
internal potency, whereas many hundreds and thousands of other gopés and residents of Gokula
were pure devotees who were being elevated to that position from the status of conditioned souls.
This second group is described in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.12.8):

   "It is only by pure love and devotion for Lord Kåñëa that the gopés, surabhi cows, and other
residents of Vraja were able to attain His association."***

  In this way we may understand that the residents of Gokula were divided into these two groups.


Text 4


   kim äkhyaà präpus taträha mäà kåñëäkhyam eva, naräkåti paraà brahma iti puräëa-vacanät, yo
'vatäräëäà madhye çreñöho 'vatäraù ko bhavitä katham asyävatärasya brahmatä bhavatéti
täpanébhyaç ca.

   kim-what?; äkhyam-name; präpuù-attained; tatra-in this connection; aha-He says; mäm-Me;
kåñëa-akhyam-named Kåñëa; eva-certainly; nara-human; akåti-from; praram-the supreme; brahma-
Absolute Truth; iti-thus; puräëa-of the Çrémad-Bhägavatam (7. ); vacanät-from the statement;
yaù-who; avatäräëäm-of the incarnations of Godhead; madhye-in the midst; çreñöhaù-the best;
avatäraù-incarnation; kaù-who?; bhavitä-will be; katham-how is it?; asy-of this; avatärasya-
incarnation; brahmatä-greatness; bhavati-is; iti-thus; täpanébhyaù-from the Gopala-tapani
Upaniñad; ca-also.


    Someone may ask what is the name of this "brahma" attained by the gopés. The Lord answers the
question when He says " mäà kåñëäkhyam eva" (I am the Supreme Brahman, and My name is
Kåñëa).
    Lord Kåñëa is the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is confirmed by
all Vedic literatures. For example the Çrémad-Bhägavatam says:

  "The Absolute Truth has a humanlike form."

  In the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad the question is asked:

   "Of all the features and forms of the Absolute Truth, what is His ultimate feature and original
form?"

  To this question the following answer is given:

  "Lord Kåñëa is the ultimate feature and the original form of the Absolute."

   Therefore, when it is described that the gopés attained the Brahman, it does not mean that they
attained something impersonal. Rather, it means that they attained the association of the Supreme
Person, Lord Kåñëa.


Text 5


   kédåsa-sambandhaà tväà präpus taträha ramaëaà järam iti. ramaëaù patir nandana çabdavad
yaugikatva-badhät. yathä miträ-putro miträ-nandana evocyate, na tu miträ-patiù. miträ-patir api
miträ-ramaëa evocyate, na tu miträ-putra iti. tataç cäyam arthaù.

   kédåça-what kind; sambandham-of relationship; tväm- with You; präpuù-they attained; tatra-in
this connection; aha-He says; ramaëam-charming lover; järam-the lover of another's wife; iti thus;
ramaëaù-the word "ramana"; patiù- means "husband" or "lover"; nandana-çabdavat-like the word
"nandana (son)" yaugika-badhät-because of improper usage; yathä-just as; mitra-of Mitra; putraù-
the son; mitra-nandanaù-"mitra-nandana"; eva-certainly; ucyate-is said; na- not; tu-but; mitra-patiù-
"mitra-pati"; mitra-of Mitra; patiù-the husband or lover; api-although; mitra-ramaëaù-"mitra-
ramana"; eva-certainly; ucyate-is said; na-not; tu-but; mitra-putraù-"mitra-putra"; tatah-from this;
ayam-this; arthaù-is the meaning.

   One may ask: What relationship did the gopés have with Lord Kåñëa?
   The answer to this question is found in the words "ramaëaà järam" (Lord Kåñëa was the gopés'
lover). We may carefully note the distinction between the words "ramaëa" (lover) and "nandana"
(son). For example, when we say "miträ-ramaëa", we mean " Miträ's lover or husband", and when we
say "miträ-nandana" we mean "Miträ's son".


Text 6


   yathä bhésmam udära-darçaëéyaà kataà karotéty atra kriyä khalu viçeñasya kåtià pratyayayanti
viçeñaëänäm api pratyayayti, kataà karoti taà ca bhéçmam ity ädi rétyä, tathäträpi präptaà brahma
präpus tac ca paramaà bhagavad-rüpaà tac ca mäà çré-kåñëäkhyam svayaà bhagavad-rüpam ity
ädi rétyä.

   yathä-just as; bhéçmam-fearful; udära-expanded; darçaëéyam-visible; katam-the adjective "kata";
karoti-does iti-thus; atra-here; kriyä-activity; khalu-certainly; viçeñasya-of the specific word; kåtim-
action; pratyayayanti-explain; viçeñaëänäm-of the adjectives; api-also; pratyayayati-explains;
katham-how is it; karoti-he does; tam- that; ca-also; bhéçmam iti ädi-beginning with the word
"bhéçma"; rétyä-according to the context; tatha-in that way; atra-here; api-also; praptam-attained;
brahma-the Supreme; präpuù-they attained; tat-that; ca-also; parama- transcendental; bhagavat-of
the Personality of Godhead; rüpam- form; tat-that; ca-also; mäm-Me; çré-kåñëa-akhyam-named Çré
Kåñëa; svayam-personally; bhagavat-of the Personality of Godhead; rüpam-the form- iti-thus; ädi-
beginning with; rétyä according to the context.


   We may understand that the word "brahma" in this verse refers to the personal form of Çré
Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by studying the context of the word. In this context to
interpret the word "brahma" to mean the impersonal Brahman effulgence would be inappropriate.
The word must mean Lord Kåñëa here. The appropriate meaning of a word may be seen by the
context in which it is used. For example, the word "kata" may mean "fearful," "expanded", "visible",
or "beautiful". The only way to determine the proper meaning in a particular sentence is obviously
to study the context in which the word is used. In the context of this verse the word "brahma"
clearly refers to Lord Kåñëa.


Text 7


   kintu järam ity ukter eva ramaëa-viçeñatve labdhe ramaëa-padam adhikam syäd ity
akñarädhikyenärthädhikyam iti nyäyäd adhikärtham eva bodhayati. tatra cädhika-padasyaivärthaù
paryavasyatéti prayatne nopadanäj järatvaà ca pratétika-mätram.

   kintu-however; järam iti-the word "jara"; ukteù-vrom the word; eva-certainly; ramaëa-of

"ramana"; viçeñatve-as a figure of speech; labdhe-attained; ramaëa-padam-the word "ramaëa";
adhikam-specific; syät-is; iti-thus; akñara-of the letters; adhikyena-more than; artha-the ordinary
meaning; adhikyam-exceeding; iti-thus; nyäyät-from the nyaya-sastra; adhika-expanded; artham-
meaning; eva-certainly; bodhayati- teaches; tatra-there; ca-also; adhika-expanded; padasya-of the
word; eva-certainly; arthaù-meaning; prayavasyati-is determined; iti-thus; prayatne-with great
endeavor; na-not; upadanät-as a figure of speech; järatvam-as a paramour; ca- also; pratétika-an
imagination; mätram-only.


   In this verse the word "jära" (paramour) should be understood to mean "husband". The word
"jära" here is a playful figure of speech (as described in the nyäya-çästra), and does not exactly
convey the simple face-value of the word. Actually Lord Kåñëa was the eternal husband of the
gopés, and they had no other lover or husband other than Lord Kåñëa. The idea that the gopis had
other husbands and that Lord Kåñëa was their paramour was an illusion existing only in the gopés'
imagination. They considered Lord Kåñëa their paramour, although in fact He ws their husband.


Text 8


   gopénäà tat-paténäm ca ity ädeh kintu sädharaëéñv api para-brahmaëaù sarväàçitvät sarva-
pätåtväc ca patitvam eva.

   gopénäm-of the gopis; iti ädeù-in the passage beginning with these words; kintu-however;

confirmed by all siddhänta-çästras and rasa-çästras, and by all philosophers and poets, ancient and
contemporary, engaged in describing the Supreme Lord's pastimes, which are sometimes like the

activities of an ordinary human being, and sometimes are extraordinary and superhuman. These
conclusions are also confirmed in the Lalita-Mädhava-näöaka by Çréla Rüpa Gosvämé, whose lotus
feet are my life and soul, and they are also confirmed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead
Himself in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.34-37):

   "My dear gopés, although you were accostumed to love Me from the very beginning of your lives,
in order to increase your superexcellent love for Me, I have pruposely separated Myself from you. I
have done this so that you may be in constant meditation on Me.*
   "When a women's beloved is away, she thinks of him meditatively, and he is present before her.
In fact, she is more conscious of him than when he was actually present. In the same way you have
become more conscious of Me in this condition of separation than when I was directly present
before you.*
   "My dear gopés, because you constantly think of Me without thinking of anything else, or ever
forgetting Me, You will quickly attain Me.*
   "My dear gopés, when I performed the räsa dance with you in the evening of the çarat season in
this forest of Våndävana, some fortunate gopés were forcibly prevented from going to see Me. These
gopés immediately left their bodies and quickly attained My eternal association by constantly
thinking of My transcendental glories. In this way they quickly attained Me by thinking of Me."*

frought with danger and calamity. Such a conclusion is not correct and it is not supported by the
evidence of Vedic literature.

insane. In this condition they tried for some time to conceal their ecstatic love for Lord Kåñëa, and

service carefully studied the entire situation in Våndävana, they came to this conclusion. They
were perfectly convinced that the dealings of Lord Kåñëa with the gopés did not in any way violate
the principles of morality.
