This is confirmed by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.33.25):

   "While strolling on the bank of the Yamunä, Kåñëa recited various kinds of poetry. He thus
enjoyed the company of the gopés in the soothing moonlight of autumn."*


Text 39


   para-putratva-pratipädanäyaiva hi päyayantya çiçün payaù ity evoktam. na tu sutän stanam iti.

   para-of others; putratva-children; pratipädanäya-for extablishing; hi-certainly; päyayantya-
feeding; çiçün-the children; payaù-milk; iti-thus; eva-certainly; uktam-said; na-not; tu-but; sutän-
own children; stanam-breast-milk; iti-thus.


   That the children mentioned in this connection were not the gopés' own children, but the
children of others, is also confirmed in the following statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam: "The gopés

were feeding the children milk." We may note that this passage does not specify "their own"
children, and does not say that the gopés were feeding the children milk from their breasts. From
this we may conclude that these were not the gopés' own children.


Text 40


ata eva

mätaraù pitaraù puträù
  bhrataraù patayaç ca vai

iti parihäsatvenaiva çré-bhagavad-väkyaà rasäya sampadyate, vastavatvena tu vairäsyäyaiva syät,
täsäm aìgé-kariñyamänatvät.

   atah eva-therefore; mätaraù-mothers; pitaraù-husbands; putraù-sons; bhrataraù-brothers;
patayaù-husbands; ca-also; vai-certainly; iti-thus; parihäsatvena-with joking; çré-bhagavat-of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; väkyam- statement; rasäya-for transcendental mellows;
sampadyate-is produced; vastavatvena-in actuality; tu-but; vairäsyäya-for a perverted expression of
mellows; syät-may be; täsäm-of them; aìgé-kariçyamänatvät-about to accept.


  When Lord Kåñëa was about to perform the räsa-dance, He joked with the gopés, saying (Çrémad-
Bhävagatam 10.29.19):

   "My dear friends, I can understand that you have left your homes without permission of your
gaurdians; therefore I think your mothers, your fathers, your elderly brothers or even your sons, and
what to speak of your husbands, must be very anxious to find you."*

   This description of the gopés' husbands and sons should be taken as a joking fabrication invented
by Kåñëa. This view may be easily accepted by studying the nature of these joking words spoken by
the Lord. Accepted as joking words, this statement is perfectly compatible with the mellows of
devotional service. If these words, however, are taken to be literally true, they are a vulgar
expression of that which is incompatible with the mellows of devotional service. Therefore, in this
instance the literal interpretation should be abandoned.


Text 41


   kvacit täbhir eva teñu yat pati-çabdaù prayuktas tad bahir loka-vyavaharata eva näntar-dåñöitaù,
yat paty-apaty-suhådam ity ädinä tad-aìgé-kärät.

   kvacit-in some places; täbhiù-by the gopés; eva- certainly; tesu-among them; yat-which; pati-
çabdhaù-the word "pati (husband)"; prayuktaù-used; tat-that; bahih-loka-vyavaharataù-according to

the conventions of the external material world; eva-certainly; na-not; antah-dåñöitaù- according to
internal perception; yat pati-apatya-suhådam iti ädinä-according to the Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.29.29):


yat paty-apatya-suhådäm anuvåttir aìga
   stréëäà sva-dharma iti dharma-vidä tvayoktam
astv evam etad upadeça-pade tvayéçe
   preñöho bhaväàs tanu-bhåtäà kila bandhur ätmä

tat-aìgé-kärät-because of Lord Kåñëa's acceptance of the gopés.


   In some circumstances there may be reference to the gopés' "husbands". These references are only
according to the understanding of ordinary people. In truth, the gopés had no real husband except
for Kåñëa. The description of the gopés' husbands found in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.29 and other
places should be understood in that way.


Text 42


mäm eva dayitaà preñöham
  ätmänaà manasä gataù

iti bhagavatä täsäm ätma-karaëa-prakäçanät.

   mäm-to Me; eva-certainly; dayitam-husband; preñöham- most dear; ätmänam-self; manasä-by the
mind; gataù-gone; iti-thus; bhagavatä-by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; täsäm-of the gopés;
ätma-karaëa-of the mind; prakäçanät-from the manifestation.


  The gopés always thought of Lord Kåñëa as their husband. this is described by Lord Kåñëa
Himself in the following statement to Uddhava (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.4):

  "The gopés always meditate upon Me as their dearmost husband."


Text 43


   gopyaù kim acarad ayam ity ädau damodarädhära-sudhäm api gopikänäm svam ity anena täbhiù
svayam ukteç ca.

   gopyaù kim acarad ayam ity ädau damodarädhära-sudhäm api gopikänäm svam ity anena-by the
description in Çrémad-Bhägavatam:

gopyaù kim äcarad ayam kuçalaà sma venur
   dämodarädhara-sudhäm api gopikänäm
bhuìkte svayaà yad avaçiñöa-rasaà hradinyo
   håñyat-tvaco 'çru mumucus taravo yathäryäù

täbhiù-by the gopés; svayam-personally; ukteù-from the statement; ca-also.


   The gopés themselves describe Lord Kåñëa as their only husband (Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.9):

   "My dear gopés, what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of
Kåñëa's lips independently and leave only a taste for the gopés for whom that nectar is actually
meant. The forefathers of the flute, the bamboo trees, shed tears of pleasure. His mother, the river,
on whose bank the bamboo was born, feels jubilation, and therefore her blooming lotus flowers are
standing like hair on her body."*


Text 44


tata etad uktaà bhavati,räsa-païcädhyayyam näsuyan khalu kåñëäya ity ukta-diçä.

   tataù-therefore; etat-this; uktam-said; bhavati-is; räsa-païca-adhyayyam-in the five chapters of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam which describe the rasa-dance; na-did not; asuyan- envy; khalu-indeed;
kåñëäya-Lord Kåñëa; iti-thus; ukta-diçä-by the indication of these words.


   From these descriptions of Çrémad-Bhägavatam we may understand that Lord Kåñëa was the real
husband of the gopés. The cowherd men who appeared to be the gopés' husbands according to
external vision were illusory presentations fashioned by the Lord's yogamäyä potency. Understood
in this way, the statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.37, quoted in Text 31):

   "The gopés' husbands harbored no ill feelings toward Lord Kåñëa."

does not at all contradict the statement that Lord Kåñëa was the only real husband of the gopés.


Text 45


   sa vo hi svämé iti täù prati täpané-sthita-durväsaso väkyavat.

   saù-He; vaù-your; svämé-husband; iti-thus; taù prati-to the gopés; täpané-sthita-in the Gopala-
tapani Upanisad; durväsasaù-of Durväsa Muni; vakyatvat-from the statement;

  That Lord Kåñëa is the husband of the gopés is also confirmed in Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad, where
Durväsä Muni says to the gopés "Lord Kåñëa is your husband."


Text 46


kåñëa-vadhvaù ity ukta-rétyä ca.

   kåñëa-of Lord Kåñëa; vadhvaù-the wives; iti-thus; ukta-rétyä-according to the statement; ca-also;


  That the gopés are Lord Kåñëa's wives is also confirmed in the following statement of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam:

   "The gopés are Lord Kåñëa's wives."


Text 47


   yaù khalu yogmäyäm upäçritaù iti çravaëät tat-tad-artha-bhagavan niyukta-yogamäyäkalpita-
kalpitatayä yogamäyaika-viditaù, svataù parataç ca pracchanna-dvividhäyamäna äsan, täs tu paçcad
yogamäyayaiva devyä prapitäbhyäà maryädotkalitäbhyäà sva-pälitasya rasa-poça-taroù
paryavasana-nirüpa-drava-mahä-sukha-präpti-rüpäya phaläya muny-äkäçädi-vany-ädikam dväri-
kåtya vä svayam eva prakaöé-bhüya eva vä çré-gokula-väsinaù prati tathaiva vyakti-kåtaù; svarüpeëa
mäm eva ramaëaà präptaù; näsuyan khalu kåñëäya ity ädy uktäsüya-parinärasya samyaktväya tat-
kalpitas tu sva-sva-patim ity eva çré-bhagavantam.

    yaù-who; khalu-certainly; yogamäyäm-the yogamäyä potency; upäçritaù-taken shelter; iti-thus;
çravaëät-from the Çrémad-Bhägavatam; tat-tat-various; artha-meanings; bhagavat-the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; niyukta-engaged; yogamäya-by the yogamäya potency; akalpita- not
fashioned; kalpitatayä-and fashioned; yogamaya-yogamaya; eka-one; vaditaù-understood; svataù-
own; parataù-others; pracchanna-conclealed; dvividhäyamänah äsan-were manifested in two ways;
täù-they; tu-but; paçcat-after; yogamäyaya-by Yogamäya; eva-certainly; devyä-by the goddess;
prapitäbhyäm-attained; maryäda-boundary of morality; utkalitäbhyam-pastimes; sva-by Him;
pälitasya-protected; rasa-poça-of transcendental mellows; taroù-of the desire tree; prayavasana-
conclusion; drava-of pastimes; mahä-great; sukha-happiness; präpti-of attainment; rüpäya-
consisting;phaläya-result; muni-of the sage; äkäça-from the sky; adi-beginning with; vani-
statements; ädikam- beginning with; dväri-kåtya-concealing; vä-or; svayam- directly; eva-certainly;
prkaté-bhüya-revealing; eva- certainly; vä-çré-gokula-of Gokula; väsinaù-the residents; prsti-to;
tatha-in the same way; eva-certainly; vyakté-kåtaù-manifested; svarüpeëa-in My original form; mäm-
Me; eva-certainly; ramaëam-as their husband; präptaù-they attained; na-did not; asuyan-envy;
khalu-certainly; kåñëäya-Lord Kåñëa; iti-thus; ädi-in the passage beginning with these words; ukta-
said; asüya-envy; parihärasya-rejecting samyaktväya-for propriety;.fn
 2 tat-kalpitaù-created by yogamaya; tu-also; sva-sva-patim-to gopa-husbands; iti-thus; eva-certainly;

çré-bhagavatantam- to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.


   Çrémad-Bhägavatam also explains:

   "The gopés had taken shelter of the Lord's internal potency known as yogamäyä."

    In order to facilitate the Lord's pastimes with His devoteees, the yogamäyä potency manifested
the gopés in two differnt ways. By the agency of yogamäyä, the gopés appeared in their original
spiritual forms and associated with Lord Kåñëa. In these original forms Lord Kåñëa was their only
husband. Then again, illusory representations of the gopés were also manifested in Gokula, and
these illusory forms became the wives of the various cowherd men. In this way, when the gopés went
to join Lord Kåñëa in the räsa-dance, they went in their original spiritual forms, whereas the
illusory forms manifested by yogamäyä remained with their various gopa-husbands. In this way, in
their original forms, the gopés obtained Lord Kåñëa as their only husband (svarüpeëa mäm eva
ramaëaà präptaù).


Text 48


  dåçyate ca, samjïä-chayädivat kalpanäya vyaktatvam eva pariëämaù sarvatra. tad ittham eva
mätä piträdénäm abhiñöaà sidhyati. çré-bhagavän.

   dåçyate-is observed; ca-also; samjïa-of names chaya- and shadows; adivat-beginning with;
kalpanäyaù-because of the conception; +vyaktatvam-manifestation; eva-certainly; pariëämaù-
fransformation; sarvatra-everywhere; tat- therefore; ittham-in this way; eva-certainly; mätä-
mothers; pitr-fathers; adénäm-and of others; abhiñöam-desire; sidhyati-is fulfilled; çré-bhagavan-the
Supreme Personality of Godhead.


    These illusory representations of the gopés were expansions of their names and shadow
reflections of their forms. Just as the reflection of a fruit cannot be tasted, however, these
reflections of the gopés were not actually the wives of the cowherd men. The entire relationship was
illusory. The gopés were actually the wives of Lord Kåñëa. The gopés' mothers, fathers, friends, and
relatives desired that that Lord Kåñëa would become the gopés' husband, and the Lord fulfilled their
desire.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.179
records.text:
Text 1


   pürvokta eväprakaöa-lélä-praveça-prakaöa-léläviñkära-rüpo 'rthas tad-anantara-praçnottaräbhyäm

apy abhipreto 'sti. praçnavat çré-uddhava uväca

   pürva-previously; uktaù-described; eva-certainly; aprakaöa-unmanifested; lélä-pastimes; praveça-
entrance; prakaöa-manifest; léla-pastimes; avioçkära-manifestation; rüpaù-consisting of; arthaù-
meaning; tat-that; anantara- after; praçna-question; uttaräbhyäm-and answer; api-also; abhipretaù-
intended; asti-is; praçnavat-as a question; çré-uddhavaù-Çré Uddhava; uväca-said Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (11.12.16).


   Lord Kåñëa's prakaöa (visible to the conditioned souls) and aprakaöa (invisible to the
conditioned souls) pastimes, which have already been discussed in these pages, were also described
in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.12.16), in the following question by Çré Uddhava and the answer given
by Lord Kåñëa:


Text 2


saàçayaù çåëvato väcaà
   tava yogeçvareçvara
na nivartata ätma-stho
   yena brähmyati me manaù

   çré-uddhavaù uväca-Çré Uddhava said; saàçayaù- doubt; çåëvataù-of one who is hearing; väcam-
word; tava- Your; yoga-éçvara-the lords of mystic power; éçvara-You who are the Lord of; na-not;
nivartate-goes away; ätma-in the heart; sthaù-situated; yena-by which; brähmyati-is bewildered; me-
my; manaù-mind.


   "Çré Uddhava said: O Lord of all masters of mystic power, I have heard Your words, but the doubt
in my heart does not go away; thus my mind is bewildered."***


Text 3


   tava väcaà çåëvataù avadhärayato 'pi mama ätma-sthaù saàçayaù mayoditeñv avahita ity
adikädhyäya-traya-gata-mahä-väkyärtha-paryälocanäsamarthyam na vivartate:. kutaù yena yata eva
rämeëa särdhaà mathuräà praëéte ity ädi lakñaëät tava väkyän mama mano bhrämyati. hanta
täsäm anana saìgamaù kutra kathaà vidyata iti cintayä na sva-sthaà vartata ity arthaù.

    tava-Your; väcam-statement; çåëvataù-hearing; avadhärayataù-hearing; api-although; mama-my;
ätma-in the heart; sthaù-situated; saàçayaù-doubt; maya-by me; uditeñu-expressed; avahitaù-
listening; iti-thus; adika- beginning; adhyäya-chapters; traya-three; gata-gone; mahä-väkya-of the
most important statements of the Vedas; artha- meaning paryälocana-understanding; asamarthyam-
inability; na- does not; vivartate-disappear; kutaù-beacuse of what reson?; yena-with wom; yataù-

because; eva-certainly; rämeëa-Lord Balarama; särdham-along with; mathuräm-to Mathurä; praëéte-
went; iti-thus; ädi-in the passage beginning with these words; lakñaëät-from the description; tava-
Your; väkyät-because of the words; mama-my; manaù-mind; bhrämyati-is bewildered; hanta-Oh;
täsäm-of the gopés; anena-by this; saìgamaù-association; kutra-where?; katham- how is it?; vidyate-
exists; cintayä-with the conception; na- not; sva-stham-in Your own place; vartate-remains; iti-thus;
arthaù-the meaning.


    In this verse the words "tava väcaà çåëvataù" mean "hearing these words". "Ätma-sthaù
saàçayaù" means "my inability to understand what You have said in the last three chapters has not
gone away". Why? "Because my mind is bewildered by Your statement (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
11.12.10):

rämeëa särdham mathuräà praëéte
   çväphalkinä mayy anurakta-cittäù
vigäòha-bhävena na me viyoga-
   tévrädhayo 'nyaà dadåçuù sukhäya

   When Akrüra took Balaräma and Me to Mathurä, the gopés, their hearts full of love for Me, were
tormented by separation from Me and could see no happiness apart from Me.

How is it that they always have Your association? It seems that they do not have Your association."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.180
records.text:
Text 1


  athottaram tatra tasya saàçayam apanetuà dväbhyäà tävat tac cittaà sva-sthäyan çré-bhagavän
uväca

sa eña jéva vivara-prasütiù
   präëena ghoçeëa guhäà praviñöaù
mano-mayaà sükñmam upetya rüpaà
   mäträ svaro varëa iti sthaviñöhaù

   atha-now; uttaram-the answer; tatra-there; tasya-of Uddhava; saàçayam-doubt; apanetum-to
remove; dväbhyäm-by two verses; tävat-until; tat-that; cittam-conception; sva-sthäyan-putting at
ease; çré-bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; uväca-said; sah esaù-that same person;
jivaù-the life of all living entities, and specifically the life of the residents of Vraja; vivara-prasutiù-
appearing in prakata and aprakata forms; pranena-more dear than life; ghosena-with the residents
of Vraja; guham-in an invisible form in Vraja; pravistaù-entered; manaù-mayam-of mental energy;
suksmam- subtle; upetya-attaining; rupam-a form; matra-with transcendental senses; svaraù-with a
transcendental form; varhah-iti-manifest.

  In order to resolve Uddhava's doubt, Lord Kåñëa spoke the following two verses (Çrémad-
Bhävagatam 11.12.17-18):

   "My dear Uddhava, I am the life of all living entities, and I am especially the life of the residents
of Vraja. Although I appear in both prakaöa and aprakaöa forms, I am now present in Våndävana in
My aprakaöa form, along with my friends, the cowherd men, boys, and gopés. Although present in
My aprakaöa transcendental form, endowed with transcendental senses, I am genarally invisible to
the conditioned souls, although they may percieve Me with their minds, by meditating upon Me
with devotion."


Text 2


    sa eñaù mal-lakñaëaù jévaù jagatäà jévana-hetuù; viçeñato vrajasya jévana-hetur väpi
parameçvaraù präëena mat-präëa-tulyena goçeëa vrajena saha vivara-prasütiù vivaräd aprakaöa-
lélätaù prasütiù prakaöa-léläyäm abhivyaktir yasya tathä-bhütaù san punaù guhäm aprakaöa-liläyäm
eva praviñöaù.

   saù eñaù-that very person; mat-lakñaëaù-I; jévaù-life; jagatäm-of all the universes; jévana-of life;
hetuù-the origin; viçeñataù-specifically; vrajasya-of Vraja; jévana- of life; hetuù-the origin; va-or; api-
also; parama-isvaraù- the Supreme Controller; präëena-with life; mat-präëa-to My own life; tulyena-
equal; ghoçeëa-with the residents of the cow-pasture; vrajena-known as Vraja saha-along with;
vivara-prasütiù-separation; vivarät-because of separation; aprakaöa-léläyäm-in the manifest
pastimes; abhivyaktiù- manifestation; yasya-of whom; tathä-bhütaù-in that way; san-being so;
punaù-again; guhäm-unmanifest presence; aprakaöa-léläyäm-in unmanifest pastimes; eva-certainly;
praviñöaù-entered.


    In this verse the words "sa eña jévaù" mean "I, who am the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the
life of all universes, and specifically the life of the residents of Vraja." The words "präëena ghoçeëa"
mean "with the residents of Vraja, who are more dear to Me than life." The words "vivara-prasütiù"
mean "I, who appear in manifest (prakaöa) and unmanifest (aprakaöa) pastimes", and the words
"guhäà praviñöaù mean "I am now appearing in Vraja in my unmanifest (aprakaöa) feature,
invisible to the eyes of the conditioned souls."


Text 3


   kédåçaù san, kià kåtvä? mäträ mama cakñur-ädéni, svaraù rüpam, iti ittham staviñöhaù sva-
parijanänäm prakaöa eva san. anyeñäm sükñmam adåçyaà bahiraìga-bhaktänäà ca manomayam
kathaïcin manasy eva gamyaà yad rüpam prakäças tad upetya.

   kédåçaù san-in what way am I maniest?; kim-what?; kåtvä-having done; mäträ-with My senses;
mama-My; cakñuù-ädéni-eyes and other senses; svaraù rüpam-with My transcendental form; iti-
ittham-thus; sthaviñöhaù-manifest; sva-parijanänäm-to my confidential associates; prakaöaù-
manifest; eva-certainly; san-being so; anyeñäm-to others; sükñmam-subtle; adåçyam-invisible;
bahiraìga-bhaktänäm-to the neophyte devotees; ca-also; manaù-mayam-in the mental platform;
kathäncit-to a certain extent; manasi-in the mind; eva-certainly; gamyam-approachable; yat-which;
rüpam-form; prakäçaù-manifestation; tat-therefore; upetya-having approached.


   How is He manifest? What does He do? The Lord says the word "mäträ", which means "with My
eyes and other senses." He says "svaraù", which means "in My transcendental form". The word "iti"
here means "in this way" and "sthaviñöhaù" means "manifest before My personal associates".
"Sükñmam" means "not seen by outsiders, the neophyte devotees." "Manomayam means "entered the
heart" and "rüpam upetya" means "manifesting".

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.181
records.text:
Text 1


prakaöa-léläviñkäraà ca sa-dåñöäntaà spañöayati

yathänalaù khe 'nila-bandhur uñmä
   balena däruëy adhimathyamänaù
aëuù prajäto haviñä samedhate
   tathaiva me vyaktir iyaà hi väëé

   prakaöa-léla-of the manifest pastimes; aviçkäram- appearance; ca-also; sa-with; dåñöäntam-an
example; spañöayati-explains; yathä-just as; analaù-fire; khe-in the space within wood; anila-air;
bandhuù-one who accompanies; uñmä-heat; balena-strongly; däruëi-within the wood;
adhimathyamänaù-being kindled by friction; aëuù-very tiny; prajätaù-is born; haviçä-with ghee;
clarified butter; samedhate-it increases; tathä-similarly; eva indeed; me-My; vyaktiù-manifestation;
iyam-this; hi-certainly; väëé-the explanation;


   Lord Kåñëa explains His prakaöa appearance and pastimes by giving the following example
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.12.18):

   "When firewood is rubbed together, heat is produced by contact with air, and by vigorously
rubbing the sticks, a spark of fire appears. Once the fire is kindled, ghee is added and the fire blazes.
Similarly, I become manifest in this world in My prakaöa pastimes."***


Text 2

   dåñöänto 'yaà garbhädi-krameëävirbhäva-mäträàçe. tåtéye 'pi tad uktaà çrémad-uddhavenaiva
ajo 'pi jäto bhagavän yathägniù iti; vyaktiù ävirbhävaù; yasmät iyam sva-rahasyaika-vijïasya mäm
eva väëé. näträsambhävanä vidheyety arthaù.

   dåñöäntaù-example; ayam-this; garbha-adi-beginning with infancy; krameëa-in sequence;
avirbhäva-mätra-of manifestation; aàçe-in a part; tåtéye-in the third Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(3.2.15); api-even; tat-that; uktam-said; çrémat-uddhavena-by Çré Uddhava; eva-certainly; ajaù-
unborn; api-although; jätaù-born; bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; yatha-just like;
agniù-fire; iti- thus; vyaktiù-ävirbhävaù-manifestation; yasmät-from which; iyam-this; sva-rahasya-
confidential knowledge; vijïasya-of one who is aware; mäm-Me; eva-certainly; väëé-words; na- not;
atra-here; asmbhävanä-impossibility; vidheya-may be considered; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.


   In this verse an example is given to explain the Lord's birth-pastimes within this material world.
This same example was also given by Çré Uddhava in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
3.2.15):

   "The Personality of Godhead, the all-compassionate controller of both the spiritual and material
creations, is unborn, but when there is friction between His peaceful devotees and persons who are
in the material modes of nature, He takes birth just like fire, accompanied by the mahat-tattva."*

   One who understands the confidential truth about Lord Kåñëa's descent to this material world
can properly understand the meaning of this example (iyaà väëé).


Text 3


   tataç cänantaraà vakñyamänaù evaà gadiù ity-adi-granthas tu säàsayäpanodane vyäkhyeyaù.
evam pürvokta-väkya-dvayasyaivärtha-bhedena gadiù laukikaà bhäçaëam api jïeyam. tasyäpy
utpattir jïeyety arthaù. sa ca sa-tät-paryako 'rtha-bhedaç tékäyäm eva dåçyata iti. çré-çukaù.

   tataù-then; ca-also; anantaram-afterwards; vakñyamänaù-which will be spoken; evam gadiù iti
adi granthaù-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.12.27:


gadiù karma gatir visargo
   ghräno raso dåk sparça-çrutiç ca
saìkalpa-vijïänam athäbhimänaù
   sütraà rajaù-sattva-tamo-vikäraù

tu-also; saàçaya-doubt; apanodane-in removal; vyäkhyeyaù- may be explained; evam-in this way;
pürva-previously; ukta- spoken; väkya-statement; dvayasya-of the two; eva-certainly; artha-of
meaning; bhedena-with the difference; gadiù-the word "gadiù"; lalukikam-of the material world;

bhäçaëam-speech; api-also; jïeyam-shoud be understood; tasya-of that; api- also; utpattiù-arisal;
jïeya-should be understood; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; saù-that; va-also; tätparyakaù-meaning;
artha-of meaning; bhedaù-difference; tékäyäm-in Çrédhara Svami's commentary; eva-certainly;
dåçyate-is seen; iti- thus; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvami.


   Some readers may doubt that the words "iyaà väëé" mean "this explanation may be given". They
may say that the words actually mean "The Supreme Personality of Godhead appears in the form of
the Vedas". This interpretation cannot be accepted, however, because a few verses after this
(11.12.27), in the verse beginning "evaà gadiù", Lord Kåñëa uses the word "gadiù" (synonymous with
"väëé") to mean "speech". The two words should be accepted to mean the same thing (speech). They
do not mean "the Vedas" in this context. This explanation is corroborated by the comments of Çréla
Çrédhara Svämé.

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.182
records.text:
Text 1


   tad evaà çrémad-bhägavate punar vrajägamanädi-rüpo 'yam artho bahudä labdho 'pi padmottara
khaëòavad yan na spañöayä varëitaù, tat khalu nijeñöa-devaasya bahir-mukhän
pratyacchanecchayantar-mukhäh pratyutkaëöhävardhanecchayeti gamyate. yata evoktam

parokña-vädä åçayaù
   parokñaà tu mama priyam iti.

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; çrémat-bhägavate-in the Çrémad-Bhägavatam; punaù-again; vraja-
to Vrajäbhumi; agamana-return; adi-beginning with; rüpaù-consisting of; ayam-this; arthaù-
meaning; bahudhä-in many ways; labdhaù- obtained; api-although; padma-uttara-khaëòa-vat-in the
Uttara-khanda of the Padma Puräëa; yat-wich; na-not; spañöatayä-with califty; varëitaù-described;
tat- therefore; khalu-certainly; nija-iñöa-devasya-of the worshipable Supreme Lord; bahih-mukhän-
to the ordinary living entities, who do not understand the confidential details of Lord Kåñëa's
pastimes; pratyacchanna-to cover; icchaya-with a desire; antah-mukhän-to the confidential
devotees of the Lord; pratyutkaëöha-with eagerness; vardhana-increasing; icchaya- with a desire; iti-
thus; gamyate-may be considered; yataù- because; eva-certainly; uktam-it is said; parokña-vädäù-
obscure explanations; åçayaù-sages; parokñam-difficult to be understood; tu-but; mama-to Me;
priyam-dear; iti-thus.


   At this point someone may object, saying that although Lord Kåñëa's return to Vrajabhümi is
clearly described in the Uttara-khaëòa of the Padma Puräëa, it is only hinted at in the Çrémad-
Bhägavatam. The reason this is not openly described in Çrémad-Bhägavatam is that Çukadeva
Gosvämé wanted to conceal this confidential pastime from the understanding of the ordinary

conditioned souls, and at the same time describe it to the intimate devotees of the Lord. In order to
fulfill both purposes Çukadeva Gosvämé described this pastime in an indirect way, so that the
intimate devotees could understand it and others would not understand it. This method of speaking
is described by Lord Kåñëa Himself in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.21.35):

  "The explanation of the Vedas and the great sages are very obscure and are not easily
understood. This is not accidental, but deliberate, for in this way I am not exposed to the
materialists. Only the pure-hearted devotees can understand the truth about Me by reading the
Vedas or hearing the descriptions of the sages."


Text 2


yad etat tu mayä kñudra-
   tareëa taraläyitam
kñamataà tat kñamä-çélaù
   çrémän gokula-vallbhaù

   yat etat-whatever; tu-but; mayä-by me; kñudratareëa- very insignificant; taraläyitam-wavered;
kñamatam-may forgive; tat-that; kñamä-çélaù-merciful; çrémän-full of all beauty and opulence;
gokula-vallabhaù-Lord Kåñëa who is very dear to the residents of Gokula.


   The insignificant author of this book (Jéva Gosvämé) prays that if I am wrong in my presentation
of this matter, may the merciful Lord Kåñëa, who is very dear to the residents of Gokula, please
forgive me.


Text 3


   tad etat çréla-våndävane lélä-dvayasya mélanaà sävasaram eva prastutam; dvärakäyäà tu
prasiddham eva. tatra mauçalädi-lélä mäyiky eveti pürvam eva darçitäm,vastutas tu dvärakäyäm eva
sa-parikarasya çré-bhagavato nigüòhatayä sthitiù. yädavänäà ca nitya-parikäratvät tat tyägena
svayaà-bhagavatä eväntardhäne tair atikñobheëomatta-ceñöair upamarditä prthivy eva nasyed iti
prathamaà taçäm antardhäpanam.

   tat etat-that; çréla-våndävana-in Våndävana; lélä-dvayasya-of the prakata and aprakata pastimes;
mélanam- meeting; sa avasaram-at the proper time; eva-certainly; prastutam-is described;
dvärakäyäm-at Dvarka; tu-also; prasiddham-celebrated; eva-certainly; tatra-there; mauçala-adi-lélä-
the pastimes of the Lord's dissappearance, beginning with the fratricidal war which destroyed the
Yadu dynasty; mäyiki-illusory; eva-certainly; iti-thus; pürvam- previously; eva-certainly; darçitäm-
established; vastutaù- in truth; tu-but; dvärakäyäm-in Dvaraka; eva-certainly; sa-parikarasya-with
His associates; çré-bhagavataù-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; nigüòhatayä-in a concealed
condition; sthitiù-situation; yädavänäm-of the member of the Yadu dynasty; ca-also; nitya-

parikäratvät-because of being eternal associates of the Lord; tat-that; tyägena-by abandoning;
svayam-personally; bhagavatäù-of the Supreme Lord; eva-certainly; antardhäne-on the
dissappearance; taiù-by them; ati-kñobheëa-with great agitation; unmata-ceñöaiù- with intoxicated
activities; upamarditä-crushed; prthivi-the earth; eva-certainly; nasyet-may be destroyed; iti-thus;
prathamam-first; teñäm-of them; antardhäpanam- dissappearance.


    At a certian point in Lord Kåñëa's pastimes, He became no longer present to the eyes of the
conditioned souls in Våndävana and Dvärakä. At that time He remained in those two holy places
in His aprakaöa (unmanifest) form, and there was no longer any distinction between prakaöa and
aprakaöa.
    Because the members of the Yadu dynasty are the Lord's eternal associates, they also remained in
Dvärakä with the Lord, although all of them were invisible to the eyes of ordinary living entities.
The fratricidal war that destroyed the Yadu dynasty and the other activities culminating in the
Lord's departure from the earth planet are the play of the Lord's illusory potency, and the reality of
all these activities is different from what first seems to be. Lord Kåñëa considered that after His
departure from the earth the members of the Yadu dynasty would be afflicted by separation from
Him and in a maddened condition would destroy the earth. In order to prevent this, Lord Kåñëa
arranged that the Yadu dynasty would leave the earth before His own departure.


Text 4


ata evoktam

bhü-bhära-räja-påtanä yadubhir nirasya
  guptaù sva-bähubhir acintayad aprameyaù
manye 'vaner nanu gato 'py agataà hi bhäraà
  yad yädavaà kulam aho aviñahyam äste

    atah eva-therefore; uktam-it is said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.1.3); bhü-bhära-existing as the
burden of the earth; räja-of the kings; påtanäù-the armies; yadubhiù-by the Yadus; nirasya-
eliminating; guptaiù-protected; sva-bähubhiù-by Hi own arms; acintayat-He considered;
aprameyaù-the unfathomable Lord; manye-I think; avaneù-of the earth; nanu- one may say; gataù-
it is gone; api-but; agatam-it is not gone; hi-indeed; bhäram-the burden; yat-because; yädavam-of
the Yadus; kulam-the dynasty; aho-ah; aviçah-yam-intolerable; äste-remains.


   The reason for the destruction of the Yadu dynasty is given in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.1.3):

  "The Supreme Personality of Godhead used the Yadu dynasty, which was protected by His own
arms, to eliminate the kings who with their armies had been the burden of this earth. Then the
unfathomable Lord thought to Himself, `Although some may say that the earth's burden is now
gone, in My opinion it is not yet gone, because there still remains the Yädava dynasty itself, whose

strength is unbearable for the earth.'"***


Text 5


   atra teñäm adharmikatayä tu påthivé-bhäratvaà na mantavyam:

brahmanyänäm vadäyänäà
   nityaà våddhopasevinäm
vipra-çäpaù katham abhüd
   våñëénäm kåñëa-cetasäm ity ädau;

   atra-in this connection; teñäm-of the members of the Yadu dynasty; adharmikatayä-by the
impiety; tu-but; påthivé-of the earth; bhäratvam-the burden; na-not; mantavyam-should be
considered; brahmaëyänäm-of them who were respectful to the brähmaëas; vadänyänäm-
charitable; nityam-always; våddha-upasevinäm-engaged in serving elders; vipra-çäpaù- the
brähmaëas' curse; katham-how; abhüt-did it come about; våñëénäm-of the Våñëis; kåñëa-cetasäm-
whose minds were totally absorbed in thought of Lord Kåñëa; iti ädau-in the passage beginning.


  It should not be thought that the earth was overburdened by the impiety of the Yadu dynasty.
That the Yadu dynasty was supremely pious, and that the earth was not burdened by the Yadu's
impiety is confirmed in the following verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.1.8. and 10.90.46):

   "King Parékñit inquired: How could the brähmaëas curse the Våñëis, who were always respectful
to the brähmaëas, charitable, and inclined to serve senior and exalted personalities and whose
minds were always fully absorbed in thought of Lord Kåñëa?"***


Text 6


çayäsanäöanäläpa-
   kréòä-snänädi-karmasu
na viduù santam ätmänaà
   våñëayaù kåñëa-cetasaù

ity adau ca parama-sadhutva-prasiddheh.

   çayän-sleeping; asana-sitting; aöana-walking; aläpa- taking; kréòä-recreation; snäna-bathing; adi-
beginning with; karmasu-in activities; na-did not; viduù-know; santam- being; ätmänam-
themselves; våñëayaù-the Yadavas; kåñëa-cetasaù-thinking of Kåñëa; iti adau-in the passage
beginning; ca-also; parama-supreme; sadhutva-of piety; prasiddheù-because of fame; iti-thus; adau-
in the passage beginning; ca-also; parama-supreme; sadhutva-piety; prasiddheù-because of fame.

   "The Yädavas loved Kåñëa so intensely that in their regular activities-in sleeping, sitting,
travelling, talking, sporting, cleansing, and bathing-they were simply absorbed in thoughts of Kåñëa.
and paid no attention to bodily necessities."***


Text 7


   påthvé-bhäraç ca vyakti-bähulya-mätreëa neçyate, parvata-samudrädénäm anantänäm
vidyamänatvät.

  påthivé-of the earth; bhäraù-burden; ca-also; vyakti-bähulya-mätreëa-merely by a great
manifestation; na-not; içyate-is overburdened; parvata-mountains; samudra-oceans; adénäm-and of
many other grand manifestations; anantänäm- unlimited; vidyamänatvät-because of the existence.


   The earth continually carries many great mountains, oceans, and limitless other things without
feeling overburdened. Therefore we cannot properly say that the earth became overburdened
merely by the increase of a kñatriya dynasty. Clearly Lord Kåñëa had certain reasons from removing
the Yadu dynasty form the earth, and the mere number of Yädavas was burdening the earth was
certainly not one of them.


Text 8


   tathä na vastavyam ity ädi bhagavad-väkyasya tätparyam idam. mäyayäpi yadünäà tadåçatva-
darçanaà mamänanda-vaibhava-dhämni madéya-jana-sukhada-mad-viläsaika-nidhau dvärakäyäà
nocitam, prabhäse tu tat-tad-yogäd ucitam iti.

    tathä-in the same way; na- ; vastavyam- ; iti- ; ädi-in the passage beginning (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
11.7.5):


na vastavyam ihäsmäbhir
   jijiviçubhir äryakäù
prabhäsaà su-mahat-puëyaà
   yäsyämo 'dyaiva mä ciram

bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; väkyasya-of the statement; tätparyam-meaning;
idam-this; mäyaya-by the illusory potency; api-even; yadünäm-of the Yadavas; tadåçatva-like this;
darçanam-sight; mama-My; ananda-vaibhava-of transcendental bliss; dhämi-in the abode; madéya-
My; jana-pure devotees; sukhada-delighting; mat-My; viläsa- of the pastimes; eka-sole; nidhau-the
ocean; dvärakäyäm-in Dvaraka; na-not; ucitam-is fit; prabhäse-at Prabhasa-ksetra; tu-but; tat-tat-
yogät-because of these things; ucitam- suitable; iti-thus.

    Lord Kåñëa thought: "It is not proper that the illusory activities of the destruction of the Yädavas
by fratricidal war occur in the holy place of Dvärakä, which delights My pure devotees, and which
is like a great ocean of My transcendental pastimes. I shall therefore lead the Yädavas to Prabhäsa-
kñetra, and these illusory activities may occur there." For this reason Lord Kåñëa spoke the
following words to the elder members of the Yadu dynasty (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.7.5.):

   "My dear respected elders, we must not remain any longer in this place if we wish to keep our
lives intact. Let us go this very day to the most pious place Prabhäsa. We have no time to delay."***


Text 9


  tathä jijéviñubhiù ity uktvä våjinäni bhaviñyämaù iti coktvä vastutas tu teñäà tadåçatvaà na
bhaviñyatéty evoktaà.

   tathä-in the same way; jijéviçubhiù-iti-the statement in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.6.3.; uktvä-saying;
våjiëäni bhaviçyämaù iti-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.6.34-38:


çré-bhagavän uväca
    ete vai su-mahotpätä
vyuttiñöhantéha sarvataù
    çäpas ca naù kulasyäséd

na vastavyam ihäsmäbhir
   jijéviçubhir äryakäù
prabhäsaà su-mahat-puëyaà
   yäsyämo 'dyaiva mä ciram

yatra snätvä dakña çäpäd
   gåhéto yakñmaëoòu-rät
vimuktaù kilbiñät sadyo
   bheje bhüyaù kalodayam

vayaà ca tasminn äplutya
   tarpayitvä piån surän
bhojayitvoñijo viprän
   nänä-guëavatändhasä

teçu dänäni pätreñu
   çraddhayoptvä mahänti vai
våjinäni tariñyämo
   dänair naubhir ivärëavam

ca-also; uktvä-having said; vastutaù-in truth; tu-also; teñäm-of them; tadåçtvam-condition like that;
na-not; bhaviçyati-will be; iti-thus; eva-certainly; uktam-said.


   Lord Kåñëa spoke the following words to convince the Yädavas to leave Dvärakä and go to
Prabhäsa-kñetra, where the fratricidal war and destruction of the Yadu dynasty could take place
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.6.34-38):

   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: Our dynasty has been cursed by the brähmaëas.
Such a curse is impossible to counteract, and thus great disturbances are appearing everywhere
around us.***
   "My dear respected elders, we must not remain any longer in this place if we wish to keep our
lives intact. Let us go this very day to the most pious place Prabhäsa. We have no time to delay.***
   "Once the moon was afflicted with consumption because of the curse of Dakña, but just by taking
bath at Prabhäsa-kñetra, the moon was immediately freed from his sinful reaction and again
resumed the waxing of his phases.***
   "By bathing at Prabhäsa-kñetra, by offering sacrifice there to placate the forefathers and
demigods, by feeding the worshipable brähmaëas with various delicious foodstuffs and bestowing
opulent gifts upon them as the most suitable candidates for charity, we will certainly cross over
these terrible dangers through acts of charity, just as one can cross over a great ocean in a suitable
boat."***


Text 10


   atra ca asmäbhiù iti vayam iti coktvä svenaikya-südanäya svätma-vad anyathä-bhävatvam eka-
gatitvaà ca vyaïjitam iti.

   atra-in this connection; ca-also; asmabi iti-in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.6.35; vayam iti-Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 11.6.38; ca-also; uktvä-having spoken; svena-with His own; aikya-the same nature;
sücanäya-with the indication; sva-atma-vat-as Himself; anyathä-bhävatvam-spiritual position
different from material manifestation; eka-gatitvam-with a single object; ca- also; vyaïjitam-
manifested; iti-thus.


  We may note that in the last part of this statement (verses 37-38), the Lord hinted to the
Yädavas that they would become liberated from the material world and enter the spiritual world.
They would attain spiritual bodies, like the Lord's own body.


Text 11


   tad evaà taiù säkaà çré-bhagavato dvärkäyäm eva nityaà sthitim äha

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; sthite-situated; taiù-säkam-with His associates; çré-bhagavataù-of
the Supreme Personality of Godhead; dvärakäyäm-in Dvaraka; eva- certainly; nityam-eternal;
sthitim-residents; äha-describes.


   In the following verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.31.23-24), Lord Kåñëa describes His eternal
residence in Dvärakä, accompanied by His liberated associates:


Text 12


dvärakäà hariëä tyaktäà
   samudro 'plävayat kñaëät
varjayitvä mahä-räjä
   çrémad-bhagavad-älayam

   dvärakäm-Dvärakä; hariëä-by Lord Hari; tyaktäm- abandoned; samudraù-the ocean; aplävayat-
inundated; kñaëät-in a moment; varjayitvä-having left; mahä-räjä-O king; çrémat-full of all beauty
and opulence; bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; älayam-the abode.


  "O King, after Lord Hari, the supremely opulent Personality of Godhead, left His abode of
Dvärakä, the ocean immediately rose and flooded it."


Text 13


nityaà sannihitas tatra
   bhagavän madhusüdanaù
småtyäçeñäçubha-haraà
   sarva-maìgala-maìgalam

   nityam-eternally; sannihitaù-remains; tatra-there; bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of
Godhead; madhusüdanaù- Lord Kåñëa; småtya-by rememberence; açeña-all; açubha- inauspicious
things; haram-removing; sarva-maìgala-maìgalam- the most auspicious.


   "Remembrance of the holy abode of Dvärakä brings all-auspiciousness and drives away
everything that is inauspicious. The Supreme Lord Kåñëa stays eternally in the city of Dvärakä."


Text 14

   loka-dåñöyaiva hariëä tyaktam atyaktam iti vä nityam sannihitaù iti vä vakñyamäëät. tataç
cobhayathäpy äplavanaà parito jalena parikhavad ävaraëam. taj-jala-majjanaà ca samudreëaiva çré-
bhagavad-äjïayä tyakta-bhümi-lakñaëasya hastinäpura-prasthäpita-bahirjana-gåhädy-adhiñöhäna-
bahir-ävaraëasyaiva.

   loka-of the conditioned souls; dåñöya-by the vision; eva-certainly; hariëä-by Lord Hari; tyaktam-
abandoned; atyaktam-not abandoned; iti-thus; vä-or; nityam-eternally; sannihitaù-remaining; iti-
thus; vä-or; vakñyamäëät-about to be described; tataù-therefore; ca-also; ubhayatha-in both ways;
api-also; äplavanam-inundation; paritaù-on all sides; jalena-by water; parikhavat-as a moat;
ävaraëam- covering; tat-that; jala-of water; majjanam-inundation; ca- also; samudreëa-by the
ocean; iva-just like; çré-bhägavat- of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; äjïayä-by the order;
tyakta-abandoned; bhümi-place; lakñaëasya-characterized as; hastinapura-in Hastinäpura;
prathäpita-established; bahih-jana-who had not descended with the Lord from the spiritual world;
gåha-adi-palaces and other paraphernalia; adhiñöhäna-esblishment; bahiù-externally; ävaraëasya-
covering; eva- certainly.


   To the eyes of the conditioned souls, it seemed that Lord Hari had abandoned Dvärakä, although
actually He had not, for it is said that He never leaves Dvärakä (nityaà sannihitas tatra). All the
Lord's associates that had not descended with Him from the spiritual world were then sent by the
Lord to Hastinäpura, and by Lord Kåñëa's order, the water of the ocean, which had surrounded
Dvärakä like a great moat, rose and flooded the city, covering all the palaces and other buildings of
Dvärakä.


Text 15


   tathä racanaà viçvakarmaëä tasyaiva prakaöa-léläyäù präpaïcika-miçratvät. ataù
sudharmädénäà svargäd ägamanaà ca yujyate. aprakaöa-léläyäà tato 'pi divyataraà
sabhäntarädikam api syät.

    tathä-in the same way; racanam-construction; viçvakarmaëä-by Viçvakarëä; tasya-of that; eva-
certainly; prakaöa-léläyäù-of the manifest pastimes; präpaïcika-with the material energy; miçratvät-
because of being mixed; ataù-therefore; sudharma-adénäm-of the Sudharma assembly-house and
other gifts; svargät-from the heavenly planets; ägamanam-return; ca-also; yujyate-occurs; aprakaöa-
léläyäm-in the unmanifest pastimes; tataù-than them; api- even; divyataram-more splendid; sabha-
antara-adikam-assembly houses and other paraphernalia; api-even; syät-is.


   Although identical with the Dvärakä in the spiritual world, the earthly Dvärakä manifest during
Lord Kåñëa's prakaöa pastimes became unmanifested after His departure. The parts of Dvärakä that
had been specially created by Viçvakarmä for the Lord's manifest pastimes, and were therefore
somewhat tinted with matter, and those parts of Dvärakä that were gifts from the demigods, such as
the Sudharmä assembly-house, were returned to their original places in the upper material planets,

where the demigods reside. The Dvärakä of Lord Kåñëa's aprakaöa pastimes in the spiritual world is
equipped with assembly houses and other paraphernalia far more opulent and dazzling than the
Suddharmä assembly house of the demigods.


Text 16


   çrémän yädavädi-gåha-vånda-lakñaëa-çobhopasobhavän yo bhagavad-älayas taà varjayitvä tad
evam adyäpi samudra-madhye kadäcid asau dürataù kiïcid dåçyata iti tätratyänäà mahaté
prasiddhiù.

   çrémän-the word "srimat"; yädava-of the Yadavas; adi- and the other residents of Dvaraka; gåha-
of palaces; vånda- multitude; lakñaëa-characterized by; çibha-upasobhavän-full of variegated beauty
and opulence; yaù-which; bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; älayaù-abode; tam-
that; varjayitva-having abandoned; tat-that; evam-in the same way; adya-today; api-even; samudra-
of the ocean; madhye-in the middle; kadäcit-sometimes; asau-this; dürataù-from a distance; kiïcit-
somewhat; dåçyate-is seen; iti-thus; tätratyänäm-of the local residents; mahaté-great; prasiddhiù-
fame.


   In these verses the word "çrémat" describes Dvärakä as full of all beauty and opulence because of
the grand palaces of the Yädavas and other residents of the city. After Lord Kåñëa had abandoned
Dvärakä, it was flooded by the ocean, and even today some ruins of what was once Dvärakä may be
seen in the middle of the ocean. These remains of Dvärakä are famous among the people who live
nearby.


Text 17


   atra mahäräja iti sambodhanam dåçtänta-garbham; yad vä mahanto räjäno yädava-lakñaëä yatra
tathä-bhütaà tad-älayaà çré-kåñëa-nitya-dhäma-svarüpaà dvärakä-puram.

   atra-in this verse; maha-räja-iti-the word "maharäja"; sambodhanam-in thevocative -case;
dåñöänta-garbham-an example; yat vä-or; mahantaù-great; räjänaù-kings; yädava-lakñaëäù-meaning
the Yadu dynasty; yatra-where; tathä-bhütam-in that way; tat-that; älayam-place; çré-kåñëa- of Lord
Kåñëa; nitya-eternal; dhäma-abode; svarüpam-the original form; dvärakä-of Dvärakä; puram-the
city.


   In this verse the (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.31.23, quoted in Text 12) the word "mahäräja" may be
understood to be in the vocative-case. In this way it is used to address King Parékñit "O great king."
The word "mahäräja" may also be taken as part of a compound word "mahäräja-çrémad-bhagavad-
älayam" which would then mean "Dvärakä, the eternal abode of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, which is full of all opulences and the residence of the great Yädava kings."

Text 18


   na kevalaà pura-mätrastivam, tatra ca çrémati bhagavad-élaye madhusüdanaù çré-kåñëah nityam
eva sannihitaù;arthät tu tätratyänäm. kià vä na tatra sannihitaù? bhagavän yädavädi-
lakñaëäkhilaiçvaryavän eva.

    na-not; kevalam-alone; pura-mätra-only the city; astitvam-remains; tatra-there; also; çrémati-
opulent; bhagavat-of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; älaye-in the abode; madhusüdanaù-the
killer of the Madhu demon; çré-kåñëaù-Sri Kåñëa; nityam-eternally; eva-certainly; sannihitaù-
remains; arthät-that is to say; tätrayänäm-of those remaining there; kim vä na-is it not so?; tatra-
there; sannihitaù-remains; bhagavän-the word "bhagavan"; yädava-of the Yädavas; adi-and the
other residents of Dvaraka; lakñaëa-characterized by; akhila-all; aiçvaryavän-with the opulences;
eva-certainly.


   It is not only that the city of Dvärakä still remains on this earth, but Lord Kåñëa also remains
there accompanied by the members of the Yadu dynasty. This is confirmed by the phrase (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 11.31.24, quoted in Text 13):

nityaà sannihitas tatra
   bhagavän madhusüdanaù

   "Lord Kåñëa stays eternally in Dvärakä."

   The word "bhagavän" here means "accompanied by all the opulences of the Yadu dynasty and the
other residents of Dvärakä."


Text 19


   tad älayam eva viçinañöi småtyä iti. säkñäd adhunä vyakta-tad-darçanäbhävät småtyä ity uktam.
yaù svayam evaà-bhütas tasyä tv anyathä sambhävitatvam api nästéti bhävaù. evam eva çré-viñëu-
puräëe

   tat-that; älayam-abode; eva-certainly; viçinañöi-is glorified; småtyä iti-by the phrase beginning
with the word "småtyä"; säkñät-directly; adhunä-at present; vyakta- manifested; tat-of that; darçana-
sight; abhävät-because of the non-manifestation; småtyä-iti uktam-the statement beginning with
the words "by the rememberance"; yaù-wich; svayam-personally; tasyä-of the Lord; tu-but; anyathä-
otherwise; sambhävitatvam-conception; api-also; na-not; asti-is; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning; evam-
in this way; eva- certainly; çré-viñëu-puräëe-in the Viñëu Puräëa.

   In these verses the abode of Dvärakä is glorified in the following words:

   "Remembrance of the holy abode of Dvärakä brings all auspiciousness, and drives away
everything that is inauspicious."

    The use of the word "småtyä" (by remembrance) in this verse indicates that the abode of Dvärakä
is not directly visible at the present time. This is true for Dvärakä in general, although the principal
palace of Lord Kåñëa is a notable exception to this. Lord Kåñëa's principal palace is directly
manifest even today. This is described in the following verses of Viñëu Puräëa (5.9-11):


Text 20


plävayäm äsa taà çünyäà
   dvärakäà ca mahodadhiù
yadudeva-gåhaà tv ekaà
   näplävayata sägaraù

   plävayäm äsa-inundated; tam-that; çünyäm-deserted; dvärakäm-Dvärakä; ca-also; maha-udadhiù-
the great ocean; yadudeva-of Lord Kåñëa, the monarch of the Yadu dynasty; gåham-the palace; tu-
but; ekam-alone; na-did not; aplävayata-inundate; sägaraù-the ocean.


   "When the Yädavas had abandoned Dvärakä, the ocean flooded the entire city, covering
everything with water, except for the principal palace of Lord Kåñëa, the worshipable Deity of the
Yädavas, which was not covered.


Text 21


nätyakramat tato brahmaàs
   tad adyäpi mahodadhiù
nityaà sannihitas tatra
   bhagavän keçavo yataù

   na-did not; atyakramat-overpower; tataù-therefore; brahman-O brahmana; tat-that; adya-today;
api-even; maha-udadhiù-the great ocean; nityam-eternally; sannihitaù- remains; tatra-there;
bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; keçavaù-Lord Keçava; yataù-because.


   "O brähmaëa, because Lord Kåñëa stays eternally in that principal palace of Dvärakä, that
specific palace was not covered by the ocean, and even today it remains untouched by water.

Text 22


tad atéva-mahä-puëyaà
   sarva-päpa-praëäçanam
viñëu-kréòänvitaà sthänaà
   dåçtvä päpät pramucyate. çré-çukaù.

   tat-that; atéva-mahä-puëyam-extremely pious; sarva- all; päpa-sins; praëäçanam-destroying;
viñëu-of Lord Viñëu; kréda-of the pastimes; anvitam-filled; sthänam- place; dåñövä-having seen;
päpät-from sins; pramucyate- one become delivered; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


   "That principal palace of Lord Kåñëa is very sacred, and it purifies one from all sinful reactions.
In that place, even today, Lord Viñëu enjoys transcendental pastimes. Anyone fortunate enough to
see this palace of the Lord becomes free from all sins."

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.183
records.text:
Text 1


   tad evam aprakaöa-prakaöa-lélayoù samänvayo darçitaù. ata eva padmottara-khaëòe bhoga-lélä-
sabdäbhyäm ucyete

bhogo nitya-sthitis tasya
  léläà saàharate kadä

ity ädinä kadäcit samharate sa lélety arthaù. atra prakaöa-lélägata-bhavasya viraha-samyogädi-lélä-
vaicitré-bhära-vahitvena balavattaratväd ubhaya-lélaiki-bhavanäntaram api tan-mayas teñäm
abhimäno 'nuvartata eva.

   tat-therefore; evam-in this way; aprakaöa-unmanifest; prakaöa-and manifest; lélayoù-of the
pastimes; samänvayaù- relationship; darçitaù-is revealed; atah eva-therefore; padma-uttara-khaëòe-
in the Uttara-khaëòa of the Padma Puräëa; bhoga-"bhoga"; lélä-"lélä"; a sabdäbhyäm-with the words;
ucyete-is described; bhogaù-the unmanifest pastimes; nitya-eternally; sthitiù-situated; tasya-of Lord
Kåñëa; léläm-manifest pastimes; samharate-concludes; kadä-when?; iti ädinä-in the passage
beginning; yam-which; kadäcit-at a certain time; samharate-concludes; sa-that; léla-manifest
pastimes; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; atra-here; prakaöa-lélä-gata-bhavasya-of the condition of the
manifest pastimes; viraha-separation; samyoga-and meeting; adi-beginning with; lélä-of pastimes;
vaicitré-bhära-vahitvena-with wonder; balavattaratvät-because of intensity; ubhaya-both; léla-
manifest and unmanifest pastimes; eki-bhava-become one; anäntaram-afterwards; api-although; tat-
mayaù-consisting of that; teñäm-of them; abhimänaù-concetion; anuvartate- follows; eva-certainly.

   The relationship between Lord Kåñëa's prakaöa and aprakaöa pastimes is described in the
following statement of Padma Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa:

   "When the Lord's prakaöa (manifest) pastimes are concluded, then the Lord enjoys aprakaöa
(invisible to the conditioned souls) pastimes, which are eternal, and never end."

   The Lord remains within the material world for a certain time, performs His astonishing prakaöa
pastimes, where sometimes the devotees have the opportunity to associate with Him, and sometimes
again they become separated from Him. When the prakaöa pastimes are completed, the Lord
remains in His aprakaöa pastimes.


Text 2


   tatraiçvarya-jïäna-samvalita-bhävänäà çré-yädavänäà sa bhävaà nünam evaà sambhavati aho
sarva-daivänanya-jévatünäm asmäkam éçitä çré-kåñëäkhyo bhagavän ayaà nänä-lélämåta-nirjharaiù
sandränanda-camatkäram äsvädayituà yädava-çikha-maëer nityam eva pitå-bhäva-samåddhasya
çrémad-anakadundubher gåhe svän svän alaà cakära.

   tatra-there; aiçvarya-of opulence; jïäna-with knowledge; samvalita-mixed; bhävänäm-natures;çré-
yädavänäm-of the members of the Yadu dynasty; saù-He; bhävan-being; nünam-certainly; evam-in
this way; sambhavati-appears; aho-Oh; sarva-all; daiva-dieties; ananya-jévatünäm-without any other
source of life; asmäkam-of us; éçitä-master; çré-kåñëa-akhyaù-named Çré Kåñëa; bhagavän-the
supremely opulent Personality of Godhead; ayam- He; nänä-various; léla-of pastimes; amåta-of
nectar; nirjharaiù-with the switftly moving streams; sandra-intense; ananda-bliss; camatkäram-
wonder; äsvädayitum-to relish; yädava-of the Yadu dynasty; çikha-maëeù-of the crest jewel; nityam-
eternally; eva-certainly; pitå-bhäva-samåddhasya- considering himself the father of the Lord; çrémat-
anaka dundubheù-of Maharaja Vasudeva; gåhe-in the home; svän svän-His own associates; alam
cakära-decorated.


   When Lord Kåñëa's prakaöa pastimes are concluded, and there is no longer any difference
between the prakaöa and aprakaöa pastimes, the members of the Yadu dynasty whose love for Kåñëa
is mixed with the knowledge of His transcendental opulences again meet Lord Kåñëa in the
spiritual world. At that time they think: "Lord Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is
our supreme master and the only goal of our lives. To relish the wonderful bliss of sporting in the
flowing nectarean rivers of His transcendental pastimes, He has now decorating the home of the
crest jewel of the Yadu dynasty, Mahäräja Vasudeva, who is convinced that Lord Kåñëa is His own
son."


Text 3

     tataç ca sadhitäsmad-änanda-satra-pradhäna-vividha-karyäù parama-bandhavo 'sau
parameçvaras tat-tad-rüpän evasmän punar brahmädyair api duradhigame çré-mathurä-nämni çré-
dvärakä-nämni va parama-dhämni nänä-mädhuré-dhüriëäbhir ätma-léläbhir anuçélita eva bibhräjita
iti.

   tataù-then; ca-also; sadhita-accomplished; asmat-our; änanda-satra-transcendental bliss;
pradhäna-primarily; vividha-various; karyäù-performing activities; parama- transcendental;
bandhavaù-friend and relative; asau-He; parama-içvaraù-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tat-
tat-rüpän-in various forms; eva-certainly; asmän-us; punaù-again; brahma-adyaiù-by Brahma and
the other demigods; api-even; duradhigame-difficult to approach; çré-mathurä-nämni-named
Mathurä; çré-dvärakä-nämni-named Dvärakä; va-or; parama- transcendental; dhämni-in the abode;
nänä-various; mädhuré-of sweetness; dhüriëäbhiù-with the best; ätma- His own; léläbhiù-with
transcendental pastimes; anuçélitaù- engaged; eva-certainly; bibhräjitaù-appears very splendid; iti-
thus.


    The Yädavas think: "Lord Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and He is our greatest
friend and relative. His transcendental activities plunge us in transcendental bliss. He now enjoys
sweet transcendental pastimes in His own spiritual abode, which is known as Mathurä and Dvärakä,
and which the demigod Brahmä and those like him find very difficult to enter."

Text 4


   so 'yam abhimänaù çré-våndävane tu nija-nija-sambandha-sandhäyaka-premaikänusäriëäà çré-
vraja-väsinäm nünam evaà samujjåmbhate

   sah ayam-that very; abhimänaù-conception; çré-våndävane-in Våndävana; tu-but; nija-nija-their
own; sambandha-sandhäyaka-relationships; prema-pure love; eka-anusäriëäm-exclusive; çré-vraja-
väsinäm-of the residents of Vraja; nünam-certainly; evam-in this way; samujjjåbhate- becomes
manifested.


    Although the Yädavas and other residents of Mathurä and Dvärakä think of Lord Kåñëa as the
dearmost friend and relative, their love for Him is mixed with the knowledge that He is the
Supreme, all-powerful, and all-opulent Personality of Godhead. The residents of Vraja, however,
are unaware that Lord Kåñëa is the Personality of Godhead. They consider Him their master,
friend, son, or lover, and they love Him with undivided pure devotion. When the Lord's prakaöa
pastimes are concluded, and there is no longer any distinction betweeen prakaöa and aprakaöa
pastimes, the residents of Vraja think:


Text 5


  aho yo 'sau gokula-kula-bhäga-dheya-puïja-maïjula-prakäço mädåçaà dåçäà jévana-saïcaya-

nirmaïchanéya-päda-laïchana-leço vaïchätéta-sukha-santati-santanako mahä-vana-vraja-mahä-
khani-jani-nélamaëir äviräsét.

   aho-Oh; yah asay-that very person; gokula-of Gokula; kula-of the community; bhäga-dheya-of
transcendental opulence; puïja-abundance; maïjula-charming; prakäçanù- manifestation; maòåçam-
like ours; dåçäm-of the eyes; jévana-of lives; saïcaya-by the multitude; nirmaïchanéya- worshipable;
päda-of the lotus feet; laïchana-leçaù-the markings; vaïcha-desire; atéta-beyond; sukha-of
transcendental bliss; santati-abundance; santanakaù-granting; mahä-vana-of the forest of
Mahavana; vraja-multitude; mahä- great; khani-in the mine; jani-born; nélamaëiù-sapphire; äviräsét-
has become manifested.


   "The same person who. His handsomeness the great wealth of the community of Gokula, the
markings on His lotus feet worshiped by our eyes birth after birth, Himself a delight that brings
limitless transcendental bliss greater than our desires or expectations, Himself a great sapphire born
from the great jewel-mine of Mahävana, . . .


Text 6


   yo 'sau duñöa-bhoja-räja-visåñöaiù pütanädi-graha-samühair uparakto 'pi muhur anukülena
vidhinä teñäà svayam eva viëaça pürvakaà cakorebhyaç candramä ivasmäbhyäm avatérëa eväsét.

   yah asau-the very person who; duñöa-wicked; bhoja-räja-by the king of the Bhoja dynasty
(Kamsa); visåñöaiù-sent; putana-Pütana; adi-beginning with; graha-of demons; samühaiù-by
multitudes; uparaktaù-attacked; anukülena vidhinä-with a benediction; teñäm-of them; svayam-
personally; eva-certainly; vinäça-destruction; pürvakam- previously; cakorebhyaù-to the cakora
birds; candramäù-the moon; iva-like; asmäbhyäm-to us; avatérëaù-descended; eva-certainly; asét-
has.


 . . .the same person who was attacked by Pütanä and a host of other demons sent by the wicked
Bhoja king, but was saved when kind fate personally killed them all, who is like a moon descended
for us cakora birds, . . .


Text 7


   yo 'sau tädåça-tadéya-mahä-guëa-gaëäd eva parituçyadbhir muni-devair iva dattena kenäpi
prabhävena muhur api vipad-ganäd ätma-kleçam aganayann eva nah pariträtavän.

   yah asau-that very person; tädåça-like that; tadéya- His; mahä-great; guëa-of transcendental
virtues; gaëät- because of the multitude; eva-certainly; parituçyadbhiù- pleased; muni-devaiù-by the
great sages and demigods; iva-as it were; dattena-given; kenäpi-something; prabhävena-potency;

muhuù-again and again; api-even; vipat-of calamities; ganät- form a multitude; ätma-to the self;
kleçam-giving distress; aganayan-not able to count; eva-certainly; naù-us; pariträtavän-protected.


 . . .the same person who, granted great powers by the demigods and sages pleased by the multitude
of His exalted virtues, at every moment protected us from the limitless sufferings of a host of
calamities, . . .


Text 8


  yo 'sau nija-çéla-rüpa-lävaëya-guëa-viläsa-keli-vinigüòha-sauhådya-prakaöana-cäturé-gumphita-
mädhurébhir asmän suñöhu puñöäàç cakära.

   yah asau-that same person; nija-with His own; çéla- exemplary character; rüpa-lävaëya-bodily
beauty; guëa- virtues; viläsa-keli-playful pastimes; vinigüòha-intimate; sauhådya-friendship;
prakaöana-manifestation; cäruré- expertise; gumhita-strung; mädhurébhiù-with sweetness; asmän-us;
suñöhu-intensely; puñöän cakära-enlivened.


. . .the same person who enlivened us with His exemplary good character, handsomeness, virtue,
playfulness, intimate friendship, expert intelligence, and charming sweetness, . . .


Text 9


   yo 'sau laghunäpi guëäbhäsenäsmäkam änanda-sandoham abhivindamäno yad yad api mädåçam
abhiläòitaà tad atétaà vä tat tad api pratilavam apy açcarya-bhütaà nija-mädhurya-väryaà
ulläsitavän.

   yah asau-that same person; laghuna-with a little; api- even; guëa-of His transcendental qualities;
abhäsena-with the dim reflection; asmäkam-of us; änanda-of bliss; sandoham- abundance;
abhivandamänaù-discovering; yat yat-whatever; api- even; mädåçam-of those like us; abhiläçitam-
desired; tat- that; atétam-beyond; vä-or; tat tat-that; api-even; prati-lavam-at every moment; api-
even; açcarya-bhütam-wonderful; nija-His own; mädhurya-of sweetness; väryam-superexcellence;
ulläsitavän-shone.


. . .the same person the faint reflection of whose virtues filled us with bliss beyond what we could
desire, the same person who shone with a wonderful sweetness at every moment, . . .


Text 10

   yo 'sau sakala-sädhu-janävanäya vikhyäpita-yädava-sambandhas tad dvärä svayam api
räjanyäsura-saìgha-samhäraëäya yadu-puréà prasthitavän.

   yad asau-that same person; sakala-all; sädhu-jana-of His devotees; avanäya-for protecting;
vikhyäpita-celebrated; yädava-of the Yadu dynasty; sambandhaù-relative; tat-dvärä- with the help
of His associates; svayam-personally; api-also; räjanya-kings; asura-demoniac; saìgha-multitude;
samhäraëäya-for killing; yadu-purém-Dvaraka, the capitol of the Yadus; prasthitavän-left for.


 . . .the same person who, famous a the Yädavas' relative, established the city of Yadupuré (Dvärakä)
to protect all the devotees and destroy the demon-kings, . . .


Text 11


  yo 'sau käryänurodhena tatraiva ciräya tiñöhata ätmano viprayogena santapta-buddhéh
uddhavädibhir asmän asakåd äçväsayäm äsa.

   yah asau-that same person; kärya-duty; anurodhena-in accordance with; tatra-there; eva-
certainly; ciräya-for a long time; tiñöhataù-remaining; ätmanaù-personally; viprayogena-by
separation;santapta-distressed; buddhéù- intelligence; uddhava-adibhiù-by sending Uddhava and
others; asmän-us; asakåt-repeatedly; äçväsayäm äsa-comforted.


 . . .the same person who, duty-bound to stay there for a long time, by sending Uddhava and others
again and again comforted us when our hearts burned in separation from Him, . . .


Text 12


   yo 'sau punar utkaëöha-koöi-samäkåñöa-mürtibhis tértha-vräjya-vyäjena kurukñetra-pragatair
asmäbhiù çväsa-mäträvaçiñöair ivämröa-varibhir upalabdho babhüva.

    yah asau-that same person; punaù-again; utkaëöha-koöi-samäkåñöa-mürtibhiù-filled with millions

gone; asmäbhiù-by us; çväsa-mätra-avaçiñöaiù-deas with separation; iva-as if; amåta-of nectar;
varidhiù-the ocean; upalabdhaù-seen; babhüva-was.


 . . .the same person who was like an ocean of nectar reached by us when only our breath remained,
our forms were filled with longings, and we had come to Kurukñetra on the pretext of a pilgrimage, .
..


Text 13

  yo 'sau tathä-vidhän asmän ätma-sannidhau mäsa-katipayaà samväsya parama-svajanatayä
müòhaiva kåtäbhimänebhyo yädavebhyo nigüòhaà kam api sneha-mudräm asmäsu samudghatayyä

some; sneha-of love; mudräm-sign; asmäsu-to us; samudghatayyä-indicating; bhavatäm-of you; eva-

. . .the same person who, hiding from the Yädavas foolishly proud of their kinship with Him, stayed
with us for some months, and who, by showing love for us, and by saying "I am yours," at every
moment kindled our love for Him, . . .


Text 14


   yo 'sau çré-våndävanam eväsmäkam ätmano 'pi paramam abhéñöam iti niñöaìkya çapathädinä nija-
jhatity-ägamane visrabhya sägraham asmän atraiva prasthäpitavän.

   yah asau-that same person; çré-våndävanam-Våndävana; eva-certainly; asmäkam-of us; ätmanaù-
than Yourself; api- even; paramam-more; abhéñöam-dear; iti-thus; niñöaìkya- having bound; çapatha-
adinä-with many promises; nija-Your own; jhatiti-swift; ägamane-in the return; visrabhya-

. . .the same person who, knowing that we desired to stay in Våndävana even more than we desired
Him, and promising to return soon, sent us, who have full faith in Him, here, . . .


Text 15


   so 'yam aho akåtäpara-kartavya-çeña eväsmän nijägamanaà vinä sämarabdha-präëa-koöi-mocana-

   sah ayam-that same person; aho-Oh; akåta-apara-kartavya- without completing; çeñaù-the
