äsaìkya- fearing; jhaöiti-immediately; svayam-personally; gokulam-to Gokula; sämpratam-at the
present moment; ägamya-having arrived; nija-His own; viraha-of separation; käla-black; vyäla-of
the snake; mukhän-from the mouth; niçkasya-having removed; ca-also; sva-His own; avalokana-of
the glance; amåta-of the nectar; püreëa-by the flood; siïcan- sprinkling; eva-certainly; aste-is.


. . .that same person, even though His mission is not yet complete, fearing that without His return
millions of us would give up our lives, has now suddenly come to Gokula, pulled us from the mouth
of the black snake of separation, and sprinkled us with a flood of nectar from His glance.


Text 16


   tatra ca pratikñaëam api nava-navé-kåtenänanya-sädhananeëa kenäpi sneha-sandohamayena
kevalena nija-svabhäva-viçeñeëa, taträpi nija-saundarya-väryämåta-püra-präpacaya-cayanena,
taträpi vividha-maëi-puçpädi-bhüçaëa-para-bhäga-paräbhogena, taträpi viläsa-mädhuré-dhura-
viçeñädhänena, taträpi vicitra-guëa-ganolläsa-camatkära-vidyä-vinodena, taträpi go-pälana-
gaväkaraëa-bälya-tülya-kréòana-mohana-manträyéta-muralé-väda-nadé-vibhramena, taträpi gokula-
nirgamana-praveçädi-lélä- cäturé-mädhuryädambareëa, taträpi suhådäà yathä-yathäm
anusantarpaëa-keli-kalä-viçeña-prakäçita-snehätiçayenäsmän upalälayann eväste, yena vayam aho
samaya-gamanägamanam api sambhälayituà na parayäma iti.

   tatra-there; ca-also; pratikñaëam-at every moment; api-even; nava-navé-kåtena-ever new and
fresh; ananya-sädharaneëa-unparalleled; kemäpi-with something; sneha-of love; sandoha-an
abundance; mayena-consisting of; kevalena- transcendental; nija-His own; svabhäva-nature;
viçeçeëa- specific; tatra-there; api-even; nija-with His own; saundarya-beauty; värya-excellent;
amåta-of nectar; püra-präpacaya-cayanena-with the great inundation; tatra-there; api-also; vividha-
with various; maëi-jewels; puçpa-flowers; adi-and other things; bhüçaëa-bhusana-ornaments; para-
excellent; bhäga-opulence; para-with transcendental; abhogena-happiness; tatra-there; api-also;
viläsa-of pastimes; mädhuré-of sweetness; dhura-viçeña-adhänena-with great opulence; tatra- there;
api-also; vicitra-wonderful; guëa-of transcendental qualities; gana-of the multitude; ulläsa-splendor;
camatkara- wonderful; vidyä-of transcendental knowledge; vinodena-with the pastimes; tatra-there;
api-also; go-of the surabhi cows; pälana-protection; gava-of he cows; akaraëa-calling; bälya-to those
of a child; tülya-equal; kréòana-pastimes; mohana-enchanting; manträyéta-singing; muralé-of the
flute; väda-the sound; nadé-of the rivers; vibhramena-with the pastime; tatra-there; api-also; gokula-
from Gokula; praveça- entrance; adi-beginning with; lélä-of pastimes; cäturé- expertise; mädhurya-
and sweetness; adambhareëa-by happiness; tatra-there; api-also; suhådäm-of His friends; yathä-
yathäm-properly; anusa
ntarpaëa-pleasing; keli-kalä- transcendental pastimes; viçeña-specific; prakäçita- manifest; snaha
sneha-love; atiçayena-with great; asmän-us; upalälayan-is affectionate; eva-certainly; aste-is; yena-
with whom; vayam-we; aho-Oh; samaya-gamana-agamana-although; api-although; sambhälayitum-
to speaking-not; na-not; parayämaù-we are able; iti-thus.

   With wonderful great love, with His very affectionate nature, with the nectar flood of His
handsomeness, with the splendor of His many jewel and flower ornaments, with the great sweetness
of His pastimes, with the splendor of His wonderful virtues and the bliss of His wonderful
knowledge, with His pastimes of playing the flute, speaking charming words, playing as a child,
calling the cows, and protecting the cows, with the sweetness of His pastimes of leaving and
entering Gokula, and with the playful love that delights His friends, He loves us dearly. We cannot
say how the time passes in His company.


Text 17


   etad-anusäreëa dvärakätaù samägate çré-kåñëe keñäïcid vrajaväsinäm eva tadänéà tanam ulläsa-
vacanam jayati jana-niväsaù ity ädikam çré-çuka-mukhäd ävirbhütam iti vrajaikanta-bhaktä
vyäcakñate. akleçenaivärtha-viçeña-parisphurteù sambhavati ca çré-bhägavatasya viciträrthatvam,
vidvat-kämadhenu-rüpatvät.

   etat-anusareëa-in accordance with this; dvärakätaù- from Dvärakä; samägate-arrived; çré-kåçne-
when Çré Kåñëa; keçäïcit-of certain; vraja-väsinäm-residents of Vraja; eva-certainly; tadäném-then;
tanam-that; ullasa-of joy; vacanam-expression in words; jayati-niväsaù-Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.90.48:


jayati jana-niväso devaké-janma-vädo
   yadu-vara-pariñat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam
sthira-cara-våjina-ghnaù susmita-çré-mukhena
   vraja-purä-vanitänäà vardhayan käma-devam;

iti ädikam-in the passage beginning; çré-çuka-of Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé; mukhät-from the mouth;
ävirbhüöam- manifest; iti-thus; vraja-of Vraja; eka-anta-bhaktäù-the pure devotees; vyäcakñate-said;
akleçena-without difficulty; eva-certainly; artha-meaning; viçeña-specific; parisphurteù- from the
manifestation; sambhavati-is produced; ca-also; çré-bhägavatasya-of Çrémad-Bhägavatam; vicitra-
variegated; artham-meanings; vidvat-kämadenu-rüpatvät-as from a kamadhenu cow.


    The Çrimad-Bhägavatam is like a wish-fulfilling kämadhenu cow in that it gives a great variety
of information in every verse. There are thus many different explanations of each verse. For
example, the following verse (10.90.48) may be understood to be spoken by the jubilant residents of
Våndävana, when Kåñëa returned there from Dvärakä:

   The following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.48) manifested from Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé's
mouth may be interpreted as words of joy spoken by the residents of Vraja when Kåñëa had just
arrived from Dvärakä:

  "Lord Çré Kåñëa is He who is known as jana-niväsa, the ultimate resort of all living entities, and

who is also known as Devaké-nandana or Yaçodä-nandana, the son of Devaké and Yaçodä. He is the
guide of the Yadu dynasty, and with His mighty arms He kills everything inauspicious as well as
every man who is impious. By His presence He destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities,
moving and inert. His blissful smiling face always increases the lusty desires of the gopés of
Våndävana. May He be all glorious and happy!"*

  Because it is a wise kamadhenu cow, Çrémad-Bhägavatam easily gives a wonderful variety of
meanings.


Text 18


   tathä hi jayati ity ädi. ko 'pi so 'yam asmäkaà jévana-koöi-priyatamo viñvak-pracäreëa çré-
våndävanasyaiva viçeñataù sthävaräëäà jaìgamäëaà ca tad-virahäd yad-duùkhaà tan-nihantä
jayati sarvotkärñeëa vartate; arthät çré-våndävanasya sthävaräëäm api bhävo varëita eva.

   tathä hi-furthermore; jayati iti ädi-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.48; kah api-a certain person; sah
ayam-He; asmäkam-of us; jévana-than life; koöi-millions of time; priyatamaù-more dear viçvak-
pracäreëa-with all pervasiveness; çré-våndävanasya-of Çré Våndävana; viçeñataù-specifically;
sthävaräëäm-of the inanimate trees and plants; jängamänäm-of the moving living beings; ca-also;
tat-virahäto-because of separation from Him; yat-which; duùkham-suffering; tat-of that; nihantä-
the destroyer; jayati-conquers; sarva-utkärçeëa-as superexcellent; vartate-is; arthät-that is to say; çré-
våndävane-in Våndävana; eva-certainly; çré-våndävanasya-of Våndävana; sthäväräëäm-of the
inanimate trees and plants; api-even; bhävaù-pure love; varëitaù-is described; eva-certainly.


   In this verse the word "jayati" means "is very glorious". The residents of Våndävana glorify Lord
Kåñëa, saying that His fame is spread all over the land of Våndävana, and He is millions of times
more dear to them than their own lives.
   The word "jayati" also means "conquers". In this sense the word means that Lord Kåñëa dispels
the sufferings the residents of Våndävana, including the gopas, gopés, cows, and even the inanimate
plants and trees, felt because of separation from Him. In this way the intense ecstatic love of Kåñëa
experienced by the residents of Våndävana, including even the plants and trees, is described in this
verse.


Text 19


   kena viçiñöah? su-smitena çré-mukhena atena sadätanam änandaika-rasatvam, svesu sadaiva su-
prasannatvaà ca tasya prakäçitam.

   kena-how?; viçiñöaù-is He glorious; su-simtena- gracefully smiling; çré-mukhena-with His
beautiful face; etena-with this; sada-continually; atanam-manifest; änanda- bliss; eka-sole; rasatvam-
nectar; svesu-among His own devotees; sada-eternally; suprasannatvam-auspiciousness; ca- also;

tasya-of Him; prakäçitam-is manifest.


   How is He glorious (jayati)? His gracefully smiling face brings eternal transcendental bliss and
auspiciousness to His devotees.


Text 20


   kim kürvan? vraja-rüpaà yat puram tat-sambandhinyo yä vanitä janitänurägäù kula-vadhväs
täsäm kämadevam sarva-premänandopari-viräjamänatvät täsäà kämas tu devaù parama-divya-
rüpas tam vardhayan.

   kim-what?; kürvan-is He doing; vraja-rüpam-Vraja; yat- which; puram-village; tat-
sambandhinyaù-residing there; yä- which; vanitä-women; janita-anurägäù-full of love of Kåñëa;
kula-vadhväù-pious girls; täsäm-of them; kämadevam-cupid; sarva-all; prema-pure love of Kåñëa;
upari-above; viräjamänatvät-because of shining; täsäm-of them; kämaù-cupid; tu-even; devaù-diety;
parama-supreme; divya-transcendental; rüpaù-form; tam-that; vardhayan- increasing.


   What does He do? He increases the lusty desires of the gopés (vraja-pura-vanitänäà vardhayan
käma-devam). In that phrase "vraja-pura" means "the village of Vraja," "vanitä" means "the
affectionate and pious women", "käma" means "lusty desire manifested from the splendor of the bliss
of all transcendental love", and "deva" means "He whose form is supremely splendid".


Text 21


   nanu devakyäù putro 'yam ity evaà vadanti, tat kathaà yuñmäkam aträsmadéyatvenäbhimänaù?
taträha jana niväsaù janäëaà sva-janäëam asmäkaà niväsatväd äçrayatväd eva tathäbhidhéyata ity
arthaù. sva-janeñv asmäsu kåta-väsatväd eva vä.

   nanu-is it not so?; devakyäù-of Devaké; putraù-He is the son; ayam-He; iti-thus; evam-in this
way; vadanti-they say; tat-therefore; katham-how is it?; yuçmäkam-of you; atra- here; asmadéyatvena-
as our property; abhimänaù-is considered; tatra-in this connection; aha-He says; jana-with His own
associates; niväsaù-resides; janänäm-of the people; sva-janänäm-of His own people; asmäkam-of us;
niväsatvät- because residing with; äçrayatvät-because of being the shelter; eva-certainly; tatha-in
that way; abhidhéyate-is named; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; sva-janeçu-among His own associates;
asmäsu-among us; kåta-väsatvät-because of residing with; eva-certainly; vä-or.


   The residents of Våndävana may be challenged in the following way: Lord Kåñëa is known as the
son of Devaké, and therefore He is the associate of Devaké and the Yädavas. How can you claim that
He is your intimate associate?

   To this objection the residents of Våndävana have replied with the word "jana-niväsa". "Jana"
here means "with His own people" and "niväsa" means "residence". (The residents of Vraja may say:)
Lord Kåñëa resides with us, and He is our supreme shelter. Because He stays with us, He is our
intimate friend.


Text 22


   tataç cädhikaraëe kartarir aunäto väsuù, sa ca divyati kréòatéti devaç ca sa iti vigrahaù präg ayaà
väsudevasya ity ädikä çré-gargoktir api näsmäkaà bhätéti bhävaù.

   tataù-therefore; ca-also; adhikaraëe-in this matter; kartariù-the performer of action; aunäikaù-
the affix vas+u; väsuù-the word "väsu"; saù-He; ca-also; divyati-kréòati- performs pastimes; iti-thus;
devaù-performer of pastimes; saù- He; ca-also; iti-thus; vigraha-the form; präk ayam väsudevasya iti
ädikä-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.14:


präg ayaà vasudevasya
   kvacij jätas tavätmajaù
väsudeva iti çrémän
   abhijïäù sampracakñate

çré-garga-of Gargamuni; uktiù-the statement; api-although; na-not; asmäkam-of us; bhäti-shines; iti-
thus; bhävaù- the meaning.


   Here someone may protest that Lord Kåñëa is known as "Väsudeva", the son of Mahäräja
Vasudeva, and therefore Lord Kåñëa's relationship with Mahäräja Vasudeva and the Yädavas is
prominent, and not His relationship with the cowherd residents of Våndävana. Even if Gargamuni
may describe Lord Kåñëa as Väsudeva (Çrémad-Bhagavatam 10.8.14), and may explain that He is the
son of Mahäräja Vasudeva, we understand the word Väsudeva as a name of Lord Kåñëa to mean "He
who enjoys transcendental pastimes". (vas+u+deva).


Text 23


   kim artham asau devaké-janma-vädo 'bhüd ity äkaìkñäyäm äha yadu-varaù pariçat sahäya-rüpa
yatra tädåçaà yathä syät tathä svair dorbhiù bhuja-präyair arjunädibhiù adharmam tat pracuraà
duñöa-kulam asyän nihantum lakñaëa-ketvoù kriyäyäù çatå-pratyaya-smaraëät. tasyätma-janmani
khyäpite te te sahäyä bhaviñyantéty evam anusandhayety arthaù.

   kim artham-why?; asau-He; devaké-janma-vädaù-appearing as the son of Devaké; abhüt-was; iti-
thus; äkaìkñäyäm- in the explanation of the meaning; äha-he says; yadu-varaù- the best of the
Yadus; pariçat-the assembly; sahäya-rüpe- assisting; yatra-where; tädåçam-in that way; yathä-just as;

syät-may be; tathä-in the same way; svaiù-with His own; dorbhiù-arms; bhuja-präyaiù-with His
arms; arjuna-Arjuna; adibhiù-and others; adharmam-impiety; tat-that; pracuram- large; duñöa-
kulam-community of demons; asyän nihantum-to destroy; lakñaëa-hetoù-because of indirect
meaning of the word; kriyäyäù çatå-pratyaya-smaraëät-because of the affix "satr"; tasya-His; atma-
janmani-appearance; khäpite- celebrated; te te-they; sahäyäù-assitants; bhaviçtanti-will appear; iti-
thus; evam-in this way; anusandheya-may be considered; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.


   The question may be raised: If Lord Kåñëa is actually the son of Yaçodä and Nanda Mahäräja,
why did He first appear as the son of Devaké?
   The answer to this question is: Lord Kåñëa appeared as the son of Devaké so He could associate
with His dear devotees, the members of the Yadu dynasty (yadu-varaù pariñat). The Lord's
associates all took birth with Him, and with the aid of Arjuna and other associates (svair dorbhiù),
the Lord destroyed the demons (asyann adharmam).


Text 24


   tathoktaà kaàsa-vadhäntaraà çré-kåñëena çré-vrajeçvaraà prati

jïätén vo drañöum eçyämo
   vidhäya suhådäà sukham iti.

   tatha-in the same way; uktam-said; kaàsa-of Kaàsa; vadha-the death; antaram-after; çré-kåñëena-
by Çré Kåñëa; çré-vraja-içvaram prati-to Nanda, the King of Vraja; jïätén-relatives; vaù-you; drañöum-
to see; eçyämaù-we will go; vidhäya-having given; suhådäm-to our friends; sukham-happiness; iti-
thus.


   That the residents of Våndävana are the actual intimate relatives of Çré Kåñës is confirmed by
the following statement of Lord Kåñëa to Nanda Mahäräja, spoken shortly after the killing of
Kaàsa (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.45.23):

   "My dear father and mother, although I was born of Vasudeva, and Devaké, you have been Our
real father and mother, because from Our very birth and chilhood, you raised Us with great love
and affection. Your affectionate love for Us was more than anyone can offer one's own children.
You are actually Our father and mother, because you raised Us as your own children at a time when
We were just like orphans. For certain reasons We were rejected by Our father and mother, and
you protected Us. My dear father and mother, I know you will be feeling separation by returning to
Våndävana and leaving Us here, but please rest assured that I shall be coming back to Våndävana
just after giving some satisfaction to My real father and mother, Vasudeva and Devaké, My
grandfather, and other relatives and family members."*


Text 25

   atra viçeñaëenaiva çré-kåñëa-rüpaà viçeñya-padam upasthäpyate

ayam udayati mudrä-bhaïjänaù padminénäm

itivat. çré-çukaù.

   atra-here; viçeñaëena-by the epithet; eva-certainly; çré-kåñëa-rüpam-Çré Kåñëa; viçeçya-padam-
the object of description; upasthäpyete-is established; ayam udayati mudrä-bhaïjähaù padminénäm-
Sahitya-darpana 9.6; itivat-just as; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


  We may also note that the many nominitive-case words in this sentence are all epithets of Çré
Kåñëa. This is described in the following verse of Sähitya-darpaëa (9.6):

ayam udayati mudrä-bhaïjänaù padminénäm.

records.text:
Text 1


   atha teñäà tena paramänandena samayänanusandhänäm apy uktam vrajati na hi yaträpi
samayaù iti. atas teñäà çré-kåñëägamana-paramänanda-mattänäm adyaiväyam agata itéva sadä hådi
vartate.

   atha-now; teñäm-of them; tena-by that; parama- transcendental; anandena-bliss; samaya-
ananusandhänäm-without time; api-also; uktam-is described; vrajati-goes; na hi-not; yatra-where;

   In the Bhagavat-sandarbha we have proven that the ultimate feature of the Absolute Truth is
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, full of all opulences and known as "bhagavän". In that
sandarbha we have also established that the Supreme Lord has two potencies: 1. the transcedental
potency known as "lakñmé", which is as worshipable as the Lord Himself, and 2. the material
potency, which is the material world, and is known as "mäyä", or illusion. These conclusions are
accepted by the pure devotees of the Lord. In this sandarbha (Çré-Kåñëa-sandarbha) we have
demonstrated that the original name of the Supreme Lord (bhagavän) is "Kåñëa". We shall now
proceed to consider what is the name of His transcendental potency (lakñmé).

clearly described in the Uttara-khaëòa of the Padma Puräëa, it is only hinted at in the Çrémad-

Gosvämé wanted to conceal this confidential pastime from the understanding of the ordinary
conditioned souls, and at the same time describe it to the intimate devotees of the Lord. In order to
fulfill both purposes Çukadeva Gosvämé described this pastime in an indirect way, so that the
intimate devotees could understand it and others would not understand it. This method of speaking
is described by Lord Kåñëa Himself in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.21.35):

understood. This is not accidental, but deliberate, for in this way I am not exposed to the
materialists. Only the pure-hearted devotees can understand the truth about Me by reading the
Vedas or hearing the descriptions of the sages."

conditioned souls in Våndävana and Dvärakä. At that time He remained in those two holy places
in His aprakaöa (unmanifest) form, and there was no longer any distinction between prakaöa and
aprakaöa.
    Because the members of the Yadu dynasty are the Lord's eternal associates, they also remained in
Dvärakä with the Lord, although all of them were invisible to the eyes of ordinary living entities.
The fratricidal war that destroyed the Yadu dynasty and the other activities culminating in the

all these activities is different from what first seems to be. Lord Kåñëa considered that after His
departure from the earth the members of the Yadu dynasty would be afflicted by separation from
Him and in a maddened condition would destroy the earth. In order to prevent this, Lord Kåñëa
arranged that the Yadu dynasty would leave the earth before His own departure.

    The Çrimad-Bhägavatam is like a wish-fulfilling kämadhenu cow in that it gives a great variety
of information in every verse. There are thus many different explanations of each verse. For
example, the following verse (10.90.48) may be understood to be spoken by the jubilant residents of
Våndävana, when Kåñëa returned there from Dvärakä:

   The following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.48) manifested from Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé's
mouth may be interpreted as words of joy spoken by the residents of Vraja when Kåñëa had just
arrived from Dvärakä:

   "Lord Çré Kåñëa is He who is known as jana-niväsa, the ultimate resort of all living entities, and
who is also known as Devaké-nandana or Yaçodä-nandana, the son of Devaké and Yaçodä. He is the
guide of the Yadu dynasty, and with His mighty arms He kills everything inauspicious as well as
every man who is impious. By His presence He destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities,
moving and inert. His blissful smiling face always increases the lusty desires of the gopés of

Våndävana. May He be all glorious and happy!"*

  Because it is a wise kamadhenu cow, Çrémad-Bhägavatam easily gives a wonderful variety of
meanings.

   Actually there is no difference between the Lord's manifest and unmanifest pastimes. The Lord's
ever-fresh pastimes are eternally performed, without any beginning in time. In order to display
those pastimes within the material world, the Lord descends to this world again and again. When
the Lord's pastimes are revealed to the material world, they are known as prakaöa (manifest), and
when the Lord does not choose to visit this world, but remains in His spiritual abode, the Lord
continues to enjoy pastimes, but they are known as aprakaöa (unmanifest).

   We have proven that Çré Kåñëa is the Original Supreme Personality of Godhead and the most
excellent manifestation of His transcendental form is displayed in Våndävana. His transcendental
glories may be divided into four broad categories: 1. opulence, 2. mercy, 3.sweetness, and 4.
transcendental pastimes. An example of the display of His transcedental opulence may be seen in
His revelation of millions of eternal, changeless, omnicient, and unlimitedly blissful Viñëu forms to
Lord Brahmä (In the pastime of Brahma-vimohana), and an example of His mercy may be seen in
His granting the position of His own mother to the demoness Pütanä.

   atra cedaà tattvam dvitéye sandarbhe khalu paramatvena çré-bhagavantaà nirüpya tasya çakti-
dvayé rirüpitä. tatra prathamä çré-vaiñëavänäà çré-bhagavad-vad upäsya tadéya-svarüpa-bhütä, yan-
mayy eva khalu tasyä sä bhagavattä. athä dvitéye ca teñäà jagad-vad upekñaëéya mäyä-lakñaëa, yan-
mayy eva khalu tasyä jagattä. tatra pürväsyäà çaktau çaktimati bhagavac-chabdaval lakñmé-çabdaù
prayujyata iti dvitéya eva darçitam. tato 'smin sandarbhe tu çré-bhagavän çré-krsnäkhya eveti
nirdhärite tadiya svarüpa-çaktis tu kim äkhyeti nirdhäryam.

    atra-in this connection; ca-also; idam-this; tattvam- truth; dvitéye-in the second (Çrémad-
Bhagavat); sandarbhe-Sandarbha; khalu-certainly; paramatvena-as the Supreme; çré-bhagavantam-
the Supreme Personality of Godhead; nirüpya-describing; tasya-of Him; çakti-potencies; dvayé-two;
nirüpitä-are described; tatra-in this connection; prathamä-the first potency; çré-vaiñëavänäm-by the
devotees; çré-bhagavat-vat-as the Suprem Lord; upäsya-worshipable; tadéya-of the Lord; svarüpa-
form the transcendental form; bhütä- manifested; yat-mayi-the Lord's potency; eva-certainly; khalu-
indeed; tasyä-of Lord Kåñëa; sä-she; bhagavattä-full of all opulences; athä-then; dvitéye-the second;
ca-also; teñäm-by the devotees; jagat-vat-as the material universe; upekñaëéya-considered; mäyä-
lakñaëa-known as "maya", or illusion; yat-mayi-the Lord'a potency; eva-certainly; khalu- indeed;
tasyä-of the Lord; jagattä-the material manifestation; tatra-in this connection; pürväsyäm-in the
first; çaktau-potency; çakti-mati-in the SupremeLord, the master of all potencies; bhagavat-çabda-
vat-as the word "bhagavan"; lakñmé-çabdaù-the word "laksmi"; prayujyate-is used; iti-thus; dvitéye-in
the Second Sandarbha; eva- certainly; darçitam-is demonstrated; tataù-therefore; asmin- in this;
sandarbhe-Sandarbha; tu-also; çré-bhagavän-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; çré-kåñëa-Çré
Kåñëa; akhyaù-named; eva-certainly; iti-thus; nirdhärite- demonstrated; tadiya-His; svarü-a-çaktiù-
internal potency; tu-but; kim-what; äkhya-na
me; iti-thus; nirdhäryam-should be established.

   In the Bhagavat-sandarbha we have proven that the ultimate feature of the Absolute Truth is
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, full of all opulences and known as "bhagavän". In that
sandarbha we have also established that the Supreme Lord has two potencies: 1. the transcedental
potency known as "lakñmé", which is as worshipable as the Lord Himself, and 2. the material
potency, which is the material world, and is known as "mäyä", or illusion. These conclusions are
accepted by the pure devotees of the Lord. In this sandarbha (Çré-Kåñëa-sandarbha) we have
demonstrated that the original name of the Supreme Lord (bhagavän) is "Kåñëa". We shall now
proceed to consider what is the name of His transcendental potency (lakñmé).


Text 17


    tatra dvayor api puryoù çré-mahiñy-äkhyä jïeyä. mathuräyäm aprakaöa-léläyäà çrutau rukmiëyäù
prasiddher anyäsäm upalakñaëät. çré-mahiçénäà tadéya-svarüpa-çaktitvaà skanda-prabhäsa-khaëòe
çré-çiva-gauré-saàväde gopy-äditya-mähätmye dåñöam

   tatra-in this connection; dvayoù-in the two; api-also; puryoù-cities (Dvaraka and Mathura); çré-
mahiçi-queens; äkhyä-named; jïeyä-should be known; mathuräyäm-in Mathura; aprakaöa-léläyäm-in
the Lord's unmanifest pastimes; çrutau-in the Gopala-tapani Upanisad; rukmiëyäù-of Çrémati
Rukmini-devi; prasiddheù-celebrated; anyäsäm-of the other queens; upalakñaëät-because of
implication; çré-mahiçinäm-of the queens; tädiya-of Lord Kåñëa; svarüpa- of the transcendental
form; çaktitvam-being the potency; skanda-prabhäsa-khaëòe-in the Prabhasa-khanda of the Skanda
Puräëa; çré-çiva-gauré-of Siva and Gauri; saàväde-in the conversation; gopi-äditya-mähätmye-in
the Gopy-aditya-mahatmya; dåñöam-is seen.


   The Lord's transcendental potency appears as the queens at Dvärakä and Mathurä. Although in
the Lord's manifest pastimes the queens only appear at Dvärakä, in the unmanifest (aprakaöa)
pastimes, they also appear in Mathurä. This is confirmed by the Gopäla-täpané Upanisad, which
describes the presence of Rukmiëé in Mathurä, and thus suggests that the other queens are also
present there. That the queens of Lord Kåñëa are His transcendental potencies is described in the
following conversation between Lord Çiva and Gauré (Skanda Puräëa, Prabhäsa-khaëòa, Gopy-
äditya-mähätmya, Chapter 118, verses 4,5,10-16):


Text 18


purä kåñëo mahä-tejo
   yadä prabhäsam ägataù
sahito yadavaiù sarvaiù
   çaö-païcäsat-prakoöibhiù

ñoòaçaiva sahasräëi

   gopyas tatra samägatäù
lakñäm ekaà tätha ñäñöhir
   ete kåñëa-sutäù priye

   purä-formerly; kåñëaù-Kåñëa; mahä-tejaù- unlimitedly powerful; yadä-when; prabhäsam-at
Prabhasa-ksetra; ägataù-arrived; sahitaù-accompanied by; yadavaiù- the members of the Yadu
dynasty; sarvaiù-all; çaö-païcäsat-prakoöibhiù-numbering 560 million; sodaça-sixteen; eva-
certainly; sahasräëi-thousand; gopyaù-gopis; tatra-there; samägatäù-assembled; lakñäm-100,000;
ekam-one; tathä-in the same way; çäñöhiù-six; ete-they; kåñëa-of Lord Kåñëa; sutäù-the sons; priya-
my dear Gauri.


   "My dear Gauré, when supremely powerful Lord Kåñëa went to Prabhäsa-kñetra, He was
accompanied by 560 million members of the Yädava dynasty. Also arriving at Prabhäsa were 16,000
queens and 600,000 sons of Lord Kåñëa.


Text 19


ity upakramya

tato gopyo mahä-devi
   vidyä yah ñoòaça småtäù
täsäà nämäni te vakñye
   täni hy eka-manaù çåëu

lambiné candrikä käntä
   krürä çäntä mahodayä
bhéçaëé nandiné çokä
   suparvavimalä ksayä

çubhadä çobhanä puëyä
   haàsaçétä kalä kramät
 haàsa eva mataù kåñëaù
   paramätmä janärdanaù

   iti-thus; upakramya-beginning; tataù-then; gopyaù-the queens; mahä-devi-O goddess; vidyäù-
with forms of transcendenrtal knowledge; yaù-who; småtäù-considered; täsäm-of them; nämäni-the
names; te-to you; vakñye-I shall speak; täni-these names; hi-certainly; eka-manaù-with single
pointed concentration; çåëu-please hear; lambiné- Lambini; candrikä-Candrika; käntä-Käntä; krürä-
Krürä; çäntä-Çäntä; mahodayä-Mahodayä; bhéçaëé- Bhéçaëé; nandiné-Nandiné; çokä-Çokä; suparva-
Suparva; vimalä-Vimalä; ksayä-Ksayä; çubhadä-Çubhadä; çobhana-Çobhana; puëyä-Puëyä;
haàsasétä-Haàsasétä; kalä-Kalä; kramät-in order; haàsaù-a swan; eva-certainly; mataù-considered;
kåñëaù-Kåñëa; parama-atmä-the Supersoul; janärdanaù-the rescuer from distress.

   "These queens have forms of transcendental knowledge. Their forms are not material. Among
those queens who arrived at Prabhäsa-kñetra, sixteen were considered very prominent. O goddess,
please listen with great attention, and I shall relate their names to you. These principal queens are
named: 1. Lambiné, 2. Candrikä, 3. Käntä, 4. Krürä, 5. Çäntä, 6. Mahodayä, 7. Bhéñaëé, 8. Nandiné, 9.
Çokä, 10. Suparva-vimalä, 11. Kñayä, 12. Çubhadä, 13. Çobhanä, 14. Puëyä, 15. Haàsaçétä, and 16.
Kalä. These are the names of the queens who are the associates of Lord Kåñëa, who appears like a
splendid transcendental swan, and who is the all-pervading Supersoul and the rescuer from distress.


Text 20


tasyaitäù çaktayo devi
   ñoòaçaiva prakértitäù
candra-rüpé mataù kåñëaù
   kalä-rüpäs tu täù småtäù

   tasya-of Lord Kåñëa; etäù-they; çaktayaù-potencies; devi-O goddess; ñoòaça-sixteen; eva-
certainly; prakértitäù-celebrated; candra-rüpé-appearing as the moon; mataù-considered; kåñëaù-
Lord Kåñëa; kalä-rüpäù- appearing as sixteen phases of the moon; tu-also; täù-they; småtäù-are
considered.


   "These sixteen queens of Lord Kåñëa are His transcendental potencies. Lord Kåñëa appears like
the splendid moon, and these queens appear like the sixteen phases of this Kåñëa-moon.


Text 21


sampürëa-maìgalä täsäm
   mäliné ñodaçé kalä
pratipat tithim ärabhya
   saïcaraty äçu candramäù

ñoòaçaiva kalä yäs tu
   gopé-rüpä varänane
ekaikaças täù sambhinnäù
   sahasreëa påthak påthak

   sampürëa-maìgalä-full of all auspiciousness; täsäm- among them; mäliné-decorated with garlands
and ornaments; ñoòaçé-the sixteenth; kalä-Kalä; pratipa-tithim-the new moon day; ärabhya-having
begun; saïcarati-changes; äçu- quickly; candramäù-the moon; ñoòaça-sixteen; eva- certainly; kaläù-
phases of the moon; yäù-wich; tu-certainly; gopé-rüpäù-queens; vara-anane-O beautiful faced Gauri;

eka-ekaçaù-one after another; täù-they; sambhinnäù-divide; sahasreëa-by the thousands; påthak
påthak-variously.


    "O beautiful Gauré, these queens appear like the sixteen phases of the moon, which begin with
the new moon day and proceed for sixteen days, culminating in the full moon. Among these sixteen
queens, Kalä-devé, who is supremely auspicious, and nicely decorated with garlands and ornaments,
is very prominent. These sixteen principal queens of Lord Kåñëa expand into many thousands of
queens. In this way the potencies of Lord Kåñëa are manifest.


Text 22


evaà te kathitaà devi
   rahasyaà jïäna-sambhavam
ya evaà veda puruñaù
   sa jïeyo vaiñëavo budhaiù iti.

   evam-in this way; te-to you; kathitam-is spoken; devi-O goddess; rahasyam-secret; jïäna-
sambhavam-knowledge; yaù-one who, evam-in this way; veda-understands; puruçaù-a person; saù-
he; jïeyaù-is known; vaiñëavaù-as a devotee of Lord Viñëu; budhaiù-by the wise.


  "O goddess, I have thus described to you the most confidential part of spiritual knowledge. One
who understand this knowledge is known by the learned to be a pure devotee of Lord Viñëu."


Text 23


   atra gopyaù räjïyä ity arthaù gopo bhü-po 'pi iti näma-liìgänuçäsanät. lambiné avatära-çaktiù;
supürvavimala" suvimala; haàsaçitä ity atra präptasya haàsa-çabdasya väcyam äha haàsa eva iti.

   atra-in these verses; gopyaù-the word "gopi"; räjïyäù-means "queen"; iti-thus; arthaù-the
meaning; gopaù-the word "gopa"; bhü-paù-means "king"; iti-thus; näma-liìga-anuçäsanät-from the
Amara-kosa dictionary; lambini-Lambiné; avatära-çaktiù-the Lord's potency which effects His
descent to the material world; supürva-vimala-Supurvavimala; suvimala- the potency of purity;
haàsaçitä-Haàsaçitä; iti-thus; atra-here; präptasya-attained; haàsa-çabdasya-the word "haàsa"
(swan); väcyam-object of description; äha-explains; haàsaù-the supreme swan; eva-certainly; iti-
thus.


   In these verses the word "gopé" means "queen". This is confirmed by the Amara-koça dictionary
in the words "gopo bhüpo 'pi". The names of some of the Lord's queens are explained in the
following words: 1.Lambiné means "the Lord's potency that effects His descent into the material

world", 2. Suparvavimalä means "the Lord's potency of transcendental purity", and 3. Haàsaçétä
means "the potency that pleases Lord Kåñëa, who is compared to a swan (haàsa eva).




Text 24


   sa ca candra-rüpé candra-dåñöäntenoddeçya ity arthaù. anuktam antimaà mahä-çaktim äha
sampürëa iti. seyaà tu kalä-samäñöi-rüpä jïeyä. dåñöäntopapädanäya candrasya tädåçatvam äha
pratipat iti. asu etat tulyasu kaläsu. vivakñitäà äha çoçaçaiva iti, ñoòaçänäm eva vidyä-rüpatväd eta-
upadeçasya jïäna-sambhava-rahasyatvät, taj-jïänasya vaiñëävänumäpaka-liìgatväc ca.

   saù-He; ca-also; candra-rüpä-appearing like the moon; candra-of the moon; dåñöäntana-by the
example; uddesya- with reference to; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning; anuktam-not said; antimam-
final; mahä-great; çaktim-potency; äha-said; sampürëa iti-the phrase beginning with the word
"sampurna"; sa iyam-that same potency; tu-certainly; kalä-of the parts; samäñöi-aggregate; rüpä-in
the form; jïeyä-should be understood; dåñöänta-the example; upapädanäya-for stating; candrasya-of
the moon; tädåçatvam-condition of being like that; äha-he said; pratipat iti-the phrase beginning
with the word "pratipat"; asu-among them; etat-tulyasu-equal; kaläsu-parts; vivakñitäm-intention;
äha-he says; ñoòaça eva-iti-the phrase beginning with the words "ñoòaçäiva"; ñoòaçänäm-of the
sixteen; eva-certainly; vidyä-rüpätvät-because of manifesting forms of transcendental knowledge;
etat-upadeçasya-of this construction; jïäna-sambhava-rahasyatvät-because of the explanation of
confidential knowledge; tat-jïänasya-of that knowledge; vaiñëaa-anumäpaka-liìgatvät-considered a
devotee of Lord Viñëu; ca-also.

   In these verses Lord Kåñëa is also compared to the moon (candra-rüpé). The last of the sixteen
potencies is at first not named, and only afterwards named, separately from the other potencies.
This great potency is called "sampürëä" because she possesses the powers of all the other potencies.
The phrase "pratipat-tithim ärabhya saïcaraty äçu candramäù" completes the metaphor comparing
Lord Kåñëa to the moon and His potencies to the moon's phases. They who understand this
confidential instruction about the Lord's potencies, whose forms are all composed of transcendental
knowledge, are known as Vaiñëavas, pure devotees of Lord Viñëu (sa jïeyo vaiñëavo budhaiù).


Text 25


    krüra-bhéçaëé-çokänäm api bhagavat-svarüpa-bhütänäm eva saténäm mallänäm açaëiù itivat çré-
kåñëasya kaöhiëatva-pratyayakatvät; måtyur bhoja-pateù itivad durjana-viträsakatvät; asatäm çäntä
itivat tadéya-çoka-hetuväd eva ca tat tan niruktir upapadyate.

   krüra-of Krüra (cruelty); bhéçaëé-Bhéçaëé (fear); çokänäm-and Çoka (grief); api-also; bhagavat-of
the Supreme Personality of Godhead; svarüpa-from the transcendental form; bhütänäm-
manifested; eva-certainly; saténäm-of the transcendental potencies; mallänäm-of the wrestlers;

äsaëiù-like a thunderbolt; itivat-just like; çré-kåñëasya-of Lord Kåñëa; kaöhiëatva-pratyayakatvät-
because of His harshness; måtyuù-the death; bhoja-pateù-of Kamsa, the king of the Bhoja dynasty;
itivat- just like; durjana-the demons; viträsakatvät-because of frightening; asatäm-of the demons;
çäntä-causing grief; itivat-just like; tadéya-His; çoka-grief; hetutvät-because of giving; eva-certainly;
ca-also; tat tat-various; niruktiù- explanations; upapadyate-are offered.


   The Lord's three potencies Krürä (Cruelty), Bhéñaëé (Fear), and Çokä (Grief) are described in
various places in Çrémad-Bhägavatam. For example, Krürä (Cruelty) is mentioned in the statement
"Lord Kåñëa appeared like a cruel thunderbolt to Kaàsa's wrestlers (10.43.17). The potency Bhéñaëé
(Fear) is mentioned in the statement "Lord Kåñëa appeared like death personified to King Kaàsa
(10.43.17). The potency Çokä (Grief) is mentioned in the statement "Lord Kåñëa caused great pain
to the demons" (10.43.17).


Text 26


   yathä prakäçaika-rüpäyä eva sürya-känter ülukeñu tama-ädi vyaïjakateti. ataù candra-rüpé mataù
kåñëaù kalä-rüpäs tu täù småtäù iti sphuöam eva svarüpa-bhütatvaà darçitam. tad evam abhipretya
lakñmétvam äha

    yathä-just as; prakäça-manifestation; eka-in one; rüpäyä-form; eva-certainly; sürya-of the sun;
känteù-of the effulgence; ülukeçu-among the owls; tamah-ädi-beginning with darkness; vyaïjakata-
illumination; iti-thus; ataù-candra-rüpé-appearing like the moon; mataù-considered; kåñëaù-Lord
Kåñëa; kalä-rüpäù-appearing like the moon's phases; tu-also; täù-the queens; småtäù-are considered;
iti-thus; sphuöam-clearly; svarüpa-from the Lord's personal form; sakti-potency; bhütatve-in the
condition of being manifested; lakñmétvam-the position of the goddess of fortune, Laksmi-devi;
sidhyati-is manifest; eva-certainly; tat-therefore; evam-in this way; abhépretya-intending;
lakñmétvam-the position of Laksmi-devi; äha-he describes.


    As the sun manifests it's potency in the form of innumerable rays of light that illumine the
darkness of night inhabited by owls and other creatures, in the same way the moon manifests it's
potency in the form of it's sixteen phases. By comparing the queens of the Lord to the moon's
phases and Lord Kåñëa to the moon itself, the relationship betweeen the Lord, who is the master of
all potencies, and the potencies themselves, which are manifested from His transcendental form, is
explained. That the queens at Dvärakä are expansions of the goddess of fortune, Çrématé Lakñmé-
devé the internal potency of Lord Kåñëa, manifested from His transcendental form, is explained in
the following statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.59.43):


Text 27


gåheñu täsäm anapäyy atarka-kån

   nirasta-sämyätiçayeñv avasthitaù
reme ramäbhir nija-käma-sampluto
   yathetaro gärhaka-medhikäàç caran

   gåheçu-in the palaces; täsäm-of them; anapäyi-wife; atarka-kåt-the performer of inconceivable
pastimes; nirasta- sämya-atiçayeçu-incomparable; avasthitaù-situated; reme- performed pastimes;
ramäbhiù-with the goddess of fortune; nija-käma-samplutaù-self-satisfied and blissful; yatha-just as;
itaraù-others; gärhaka-medhikän caran-absorbed in the duties of household life.


   "All the palaces of the more than 16,000 queens of Kåñëa were full of suitable gardens, furniture
and other paraphernalia, of which there is no parallel in this world. The queens of Kåñëa were all
expansions of the goddess of fortune, Lakñméjé. Kåñëa used to live with them in different palaces,
and He treated them exactly the same way as an ordinary man treats his wife."*


Text 28


   öékä ca ramäbhiù lakñmyä aàça-bhütäbhiù ity eçä. svarüpa-çaktitväd eva reme ity uktam. ata eva
mijaù svéyaù paramänanda-çakti-våtti-viçeñodaya-rüpa-prema-viçeña-svarüpo yaù kämaù tena
samplutaù iti. çré-çukaù.

   öékä-the commentary of Çréla Çridhara Svami; ca- also; ramäbhiù-with the goddess of fortune;
lakñmyäù-of Srimati Laksmi-devi; aàça-bhütäbhiù-with the expansions; iti-thus; eçä-the
commentary; svarüpa-of His own form; çaktitvät-because of being the potency; eva-certainly; reme-
He enjoyed; iti-thus; uktam-it is said; ataù eva-therefore; nijaù sviyaù-His own; parama-
transcendental; ananda-bliss; çakti-potency; våtti-action; viçeça-specific; udaya- manifestation; rüpa-
the form of; prema-pure love; viçeça- specific; svarüpaù-in the form; yaù-which; kämaù-desire; tena-
by Him; samplutaù syaptaù-manifested everywhere; iti- thus; çré-çukaù-spoken by Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvami.


   Çréla Çrédhara Svämé comments on this verse:

  "The word `ramäbhiù' means `with the goddesses of fortune, who are all expansions of Çrématé-
Lakñmé-devé'."

   The word "nija-käma" means "with His transcendental pleasure potency" and the word
"samplutaù" means "manifest everywhere".

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.185
records.text:
Text 1

   ittham añöänäà çré-paööa-mahiñénäà tu tat-tat-svarüpa-çaktitvaà kaimutyenaiva sidhyati. tatra
satyabhämäyä bhü-çakti-rüpatvaà padmottara-khaëòau prasiddham; çré-yamunäyä kåpä-çakti-
rüpatvaà skanda-yamunä-mähätmyädäv ity ädy anveçaëéyam. kintu çré-satyabhämäyä hari-
vaàçädau saubhägyätiçayasya vikhyätatvät prema-çakti-pracura-bhü-çaktitvaà jïeyam.

   ittham-in this way; añöänäm-of the eight; çré-paööa-mahiçéëäm-principal queens; tu-certainly; tat-
tat-svarüpa-çaktitvam-the status as internal potencies of Lord Kåñëa; kimutyena-what to speak of;
eva-certainly; sidhyati- is established; tatra-in that connection; satyabhämäyäù-of Satyabhämä;
bhü-çakti-rüpatvam-status as bhu-sakti; padma-uttara-khaëòau-in the Padma Purana, Uttara-
khanda; prassidham-is established; çré-yamunäyäù-of Kalindi-devi; kåpä-çakti-rüpatvam-status as
the krpa-sakti; skanda-yamunä-mähätmya/-adau-in the Skanda Purana, Yamuna-mahatmya; iti-
thus; ädi-beginning; anveçaëéyam-may be established; kintu-however; çré-satyabhämäyäù-of
Satyabhämä; hari-vaàça-adau-in the Hari-vamsa; saubhägya-good fortune; atiçayasya- of the great
extent; vikhyätatvät-from the explanation; prema-sakti-prema-çakti; pracura-great; bhü-çaktitvam-
status as bhu-sakti; jïeyam-should be understood.


   In this way we may understand that all the queens of Lord Kåñëa are the internal potencies of
the Lord. In the Padma Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa, Çrématé Satyabhämä-devé is described as the Lord's
bhü-çakti, and in the Hari-vaàça, she is described as both Bhü-çakti and Prema-çakti. In the Skanda
Puräëa, Yamunä-mähätmya, Çrématé Kälindé-devé is described as the Lord's Kåpä-çakti.


Text 2


svayaà lakñéçm tu çré-rukmiëé

dvärakäyäm abhüd räjan
   mahä-modaù puraukasäm
rukmiëyä ramayopetaà
   dåçtvä kåñëaà çriyaù patim

ity ädisu tasyäm eva bhüriçaù prasiddheù.

   svayam-personally; lakñméù-Çrimati Laksmi-devi; tu- but; çré-rukmiëé-Çrémati Rukmini-devi;
dvärakäyäm-in Dvärakä; abhüt-there was; räjan-O king; mahä-great; modaù-happiness; pura-
okasäm-of the citizens; rukmiëyä- with Rukmini; ramaya-Laksmi-devi; upetam-accompanied by;
dåñövä-seeing; kåñëam-Lord Kåñëa; çriyaù-of Laksmi-devi; patiù-the master; iti-thus; ädisu-in the
passage beginning; tasyäm-in relation to her; eva-certainly; bhüirçaù-greatly; prasiddheù-because of
fame.


   That Çrématé Rukmiëé-devé is personally the goddess of fortune, Lakñmé-devé, is confirmed in the

following statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.54.60):

   "All visitors as well as the inhabitants of Dvärakä City became joyful seeing Kåñëa and Rukmiëé
together. In other words, the Supreme Lord, the maintainer of everyone, and the goddess of fortune
were united, and all the people felt extremely jubilant."*


Text 3


  ataù svayaà lakñmétvenaiva paraspara-yogyatäm äha

asyaiva bharyä bhavituà
   rukmiëy arhati näparä
asäv apy anavadyätmä
   bhaiçmyäù samucitaù patiù

spañöam. vidarbha-pura-väsinaù parasparam.

   ataù-therefore; svayam-personally; lakñmétvea-with the status of Çrémati-Laksmidevi; eva-
certainly; paraspara- mutual; yogyatäm-compatibility; äha-he describes; asya-of Him; eva-certainly;
bharyä-wife; bhavitum-to be; rukmiëi- Rukmini; arhati-is suitable; na-not; aparä-anyone else; asäu-
He; api-also; anavadya-atmä-very handsome and free from any fault; bhaiçmyäù-of the daughter of
Maharaja Bhismaka; samucitaù-suitable; patiù-husband; spañöam-the meaning is clear; vidarbha-
pura-of the city of Vidarbha; väsinaù-the residents; parasparam-among themselves.


  That Çrématé Rukmiëé-devé is personally the goddess of fortune, Çrématé Lakñmé-devé, and she
and Çré Kåñëa are ideally suited for each other is confirmed in the following verse of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.53.37), where the residents of the city of Vidarbha say amomg themselves:

   "Only princess Rukmiëé, and no one else, is fit to become the wife of Lord Kåñëa, and only the
faultless Lord Kåñëa can be the suitable husband of Princess Rukmiëé."*

records.title: Krsna Sandarbha · KS.186
records.text:
Text 1


  tathä täà rüpiëéà çriyam ity ädau, ya lélayä dhåta-tanor anurüpa-rüpä iti. spañöam.

  tathä-in the same way; täm rüpiëém çriyam iti ädau ya lélayä dhåta-tanoh anurüpä iti-Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.60.9:

täà rüpiëéà çriyam ananya-gatià nirékñya

   yä lélayä dhåta-tanor anurüpa-rüpä
prétaù smayan alaka-kuntala-niñka-kaëöhä
   vaktrollasat-smita-sudhäà harir äbabhäse;

spañöam-the meaning is clear.


   That Çrématé Rukmiëé-devé is directly the goddess of fortune, Lakñmé-devé, is also confirmed in
the following verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.9):

   "When we take account of Rukmiëé's beautiful face, it appears that the curling hair on her head,
the beautiful earrings on her ears, her smiling mouth, and her necklace of gold, all combined to
shower rains of nectar; and it was definitely proved that Rukmiëé was none other than the original
goddess of fortune, who is always engaged in the service of the lotus feet of Näräyaëa."*


Text 2


  ataù svayaà-bhagavato 'nurüpatvena svayaà-lakñmétvaà siddham eva. ata eva

vaidarbhéà bhéçmaka-sutäà
   çriyo mätraà svayamvare

ity atra mäty antarbhavaty asyäm iti. mätra-padaà bähuyädhikaraëa evauëädikaà, jïeyam,
kärtsnye 'vadhäraëe mätram itivat. tataç ca vaikuëöhe prasiddhäyä lakñmyä antarbhaväspadatväd
eçaiva lakñméù sarvataù paripürëety arthaù.

   ataù-therefore; svayam-bhagavataù-the Supreme Personality of Godhead; anurüpatvena-as a
suitable companion; svayam-lakñmétvam-directly the goddess of fortune; siddham-proven; eva-
certainly; ataù eva-therefore; vaidarbhém-the princess of Vidarbha; bhéçmaka-sutäm-the daugter of
Maharaja Bhismaka; çriyaù-of the goddess of fortune; mätram-the complete manifestation;
svayamvare-in the svayamvara ceremony; iti-thus (the first part of the verse reads:


bhagavan api govinda
  upayeme kurudvaha;

atra-in this connection; mäti-measures; antarbhavati-is contained within; aysäm-Çrémati Rukmini-
devi; iti-thus; mätra-padam-the word "matra"; bähulya-adhikaraëe-in the sense of greatness; eva-
certainly; uëa-adikam-an affix of the uandi class; jïeyam-should be understood; kärtsnye-in the
sense of completeness; avadhäraëe-in this context; mätram- the word "matra"; itivat-just as; tataù-
therefore; ca-also; vaikuëöhe-in the spiritula world of Vaikuëöhaloka; prasiddhäyäù-of the
celebrated; lakñmyäù-Lakñmi-devi; antarbhava-aspadatvät-as the origin of the manifestation; eçä-
she; eva-certainly; lakñméù-the goddess of fortune; sarvataù-in all respects; paripürëa-perfect and
complete; iti-thus; arthaù-the meaning.

   That Çrématé Rukmiëé-devé is the original form of the goddess of fortune, Lakñmé-devé, just as
Lord Kåñëa is the original form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is confirmed in the
following statement of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.52.16):

   "O Mahäräja Parékñit, Kåñëa then married Rukmiëé, the daughter of King Bhéñmaka, ruler of the
province known as Vidarbha. Just as Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Väsudeva,
Rukmiëé is the supreme goddess of fortune, Mahä-Lakñmé."*

   We may note that the word "mätram" in this verse means "in completeness". This means that
Çrématé Rukmiëé-devé is the original complete form of the goddess of fortune. The goddess of
fortune manifested in the Vaikuëöha planets and known as Lakñmé-devé is an expansion of Çrématé
Rukmiëé-devé.


Text 3


yat tu

nanv evam etad aravinda-vilocanäha
  yad vai bhavän bhagavato 'sadåçi vibhümnaù
kva sve mahimny abhirato bhagavaàs try-adhéçaù
  kvähaà guëa-prakåtir ajïa-gåhéta-pädä

   yat-because; tu-but; nanu-is it not so?; evam-in this way; atat-this; aravinda-locana-O lotus-eyed
Lord; aha-says; yat-what; vai-certainly; bhavän-Your Lordship; bhagavataù- the Supreme
Personality of Godhead; asadåçi-not at all like; vibhümnaù-full of all powers and opulences; kva-
where?; sve- in Your own; mahimni-glory; abhirataù-completely; bhagavan-the Supreme Lord; tri-
adhéçaù-the master of the three planetary systems; kva-where; aham-am I; guëa-prakåtiù-a product
of the three modes of material nature; ajïa-gåhéta-pädä- ignorant.


   Someone may argue that Rukmiëé-devé is not the original goddess of fortune, and may quote the
following statement spoken by Rukmiëé-devé herself (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.34):

    "My dear lotus-eyed Lord, Your statement that we are not a fit combination is completely right.
It is not possible for me to come to an equal level with You because You are the reservoir of all
qualities, the unlimited Supreme Personality of Godhead. How can I be a fit match for You? There
is no possibility of comparison with You, who are the master of all greatness, controller of the three
qualities, and the object of worship for great demigods like Brahmä and Lord Çiva. As far as I am
concerned, I am a production of the three modes of material nature. The three modes of material
nature are impediments towards the progressive advancement of devotional service. When and
where can I be a fit match for You?"*

Text 4


   iti tasyä evoktis tatra nijäàçäbhäsam eva dainyena svaà matvoktam iti mantavyam. yad va guëa
gauëé prakåtiù svabhävo yasyäù sa apakåñöa-rüpety arthaù.

   iti-thus; tasyäù-of her; eva-certainly; uktiù- statement; tatra-there; nija-own; aàça-part and
parcel; abhäsam-dim reflection; eva-certainly; dainyena-with humility; svam-herself; matva-
considering; uktam-statement; iti-thus; mantavyam-should be considered; yat va-or; guëa- the word
"guëa"; gauëé-in the sense of "insignificant"; prakåtiù-the word "prakåtiù"; svabhävaù-in the sense of
"own nature"; yasyäù-of her; sa-she; aprakåçta-rüpa- inferior; iti-thus; arthaù-meaning.


   In this verse Çrématé Rukmiëé-devé expresses her humbleness by considering herself an
insignificant part and parcel of Lord Kåñëa. The word "guëa" here means "insignificant", and the
word "prakåtiù" means "by nature". Even though she is the supreme goddess of fortune, she
nevertheless thinks of herself in this humble way.


Text 5


   yathä tatraiva syän me taväghåir araëaà såtibhir bhramantyäù iti manuçyävatäratäbhiniveçät
tasyä eva dainyoktiù.

  yathä-just as; tatra-in that connection; eva-certainly; syät me tava aìghåir araëam såtibhih
bhramantyäù iti-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.43:


taà tv anurüpam abhajaà jagatäà adhéçam
   ätmänam atra ca paratra ca käma-püram
 syän me taväìghrir araëaà såtibhir bhramantyä
   yo vaibhajantam upayäty anåtäpavargaù

manuñya-human; avatära-incarnating as; abhiniveçät-because of adherance; tasyäù-of her; eva-
certainly; dainya-of humbleness; uktiù-statement.


   The humbleness of Çrématé Rukmiëé-devé may also be seen in the follwing statement, where she
carefully follows her role of appearing as an ordinary human being (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.43):

   "My dear Lord, You are the master of the three worlds. You can fulfill all the desires of Your
devotees in this world and the next because You are the Supreme Soul of everyone. I have therefore
selected You as my husband, considering You to be the only fit personality. You may throw me in
any species of life according to the reaction of my fruitive activities, and I haven't the least concern

for this. My only ambition is that I may always remain fast to Your lotus feet, because You can
deliver Your devotees from the illusory material existence and are always prepared to distribute
Yourself to Your devotees."*


Text 6


   atra daiva-prerito västavärrthas tv evam he aravinda-vilocana bhagavataù tava asädåçi aham ity
etat. yad bhavän aha, nanu niçcitam, nanv evam vakñyamäëa-prakaranam, na tv anya-prakaraëam.
tathaiväha- sve svarüpa-bhüte mahimni aiçvaryädäv abhitaù rato bhagavän kva kutränyatra. tathä
aham vä te guëäù aiçvaryädaya eva prakåtiù svarüpaà yasyäs tathä-bhüta kva kutränyatra. kintu na
kutracid anyatreti. dvayor ekatraiva svarüpe sthitir ity arthaù. ata eväjïair asya çré-viñëos tava-jïair
gåhétau sevitau pädau yasyäs tathä-bhütäham. tasmäc chakti-saktimator atyanta-bhedäbhäväd
evopamänopameyatväbhävena sädåçya-bhäva iti bhävaù.

   atra-in this connection; daiva-by destiny; preritaù- impelled; västava-actual; arthaù-meaning; tu-
but; evam-in this way; he-O; aravinda-vilocana-lotus eyes Lord; bhagavataù-of the Supreme Lord;
tava-of You; asädåçi-not similar; aham-I; iti-thus; etat-this; yat-what; bhavän-Your Lordship; aha-
has said; nanu-is it not true?; niçcitam-it certainly true; nanu-is it not true?; evam-in this way;
vakñyamäëa-prakaraëam-according to what is about to be explained; na-not; tu-but; anya-
prakaraëam-in any other way; tatha-in that way; eva-certainly; aha-You say; sve-in Your own;
svarüpa-from Your transcendental form; bhüte-manifest; mahimni-in the glory; aiçvarya-
transcendental opulences; adäu-beginning with; abhitaù-completely; rataù-engaged; bhagavän-the
Supreme Personality of Godhead; kva-where?; kutra-where?; anyatra-another place; tatha-in the
same way; aham-I; vä-or; te-Your; guëäù-qualities; aiçvarya- opulences; adayaù-beginning with; eva-
certainly; prakåtiù- nature; svarüpam-form; yasyäù-of whom; tathä-bhüt-in that way; kva-where?;
anyatra-in another place; kintu-however; na- not; kutracit-anywhere; anyatra-in any place; iti-thus;
dvayoù-of the two; ekatra-in one place; eva-certainly; svarüpe-in the transcendental form; sthitiù-
situation; iti-thus; arthaù- the meaning; ataù evä-therefore; ajïaiù-by ignorant persons; asya-of
Him; çré-viñëoù-Lord Viñëu; tava-of You; tattva-jïaiù-by the wise; gåhétau-accepted; sevitau-served;
pädau-lotus feet;.
fn 2 yasyäù-of whom; tathä-bhüta-in the same way; aham-I; tasmät-therefore; sakti-of the potency;
saktimatoù-and the master of the potencies; atyanta-great; bheda-distinction; abhävät-because of
the non-existence; eva-certainly; upamäna-upameya-tva-abhävena-because of not being like the
two objects compared in a simile; sädåçya-bhävaù- close similarity; iti-thus; bhävaù-the meaning.


   Çrématé Rukmiëé's statement in this verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.34), that she is not at all
similar in nature to Lord Kåñëa should be understood only according to the following
interpretation: Çrimaté Rukmiëé said: "O lotus-eyed Lord, You are the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, always situated in Your own transcendental opulence and glory (sve mahimny
abhirataù), and I am Your own transcendental potency, the personification of Your opulence and
glory (guëa-prakåtiù). You are the master of all potencies, and I am Your transcendental potency.
Because the potency and the master of potencies are simultaneously one and different, we cannot

be thought of as completely different or unrelated. When I say `What is the comparison betweeen
us?' This means that we do not have merely some similarities, as two objects compared in a simile,
but we are intimately related and very similar (kva). We are not sufficiently unrelated to invite
comparison. Therefore, O Lord Viñëu, when they who are actually intelligent worsip and serve
Your lotus feet, they also serve mine, for we are so similar in nature."


Text 7


   evam såtibhir bhramantyäù ity aträpi hi tvadéya-pädavébhir ity eva västavärthaù. tad uktam

devatve deva-deho 'yaà
   manuñatve ca mänuñi iti.

   evam-in the same way; såthibhiù-in the material world; bhramantyäù-travelling; iti-thus; atra-
here; api-also; hi- certainly; tvadéya-pädavibhiù-following Your path; iti-thus; eva-certainly; västava-
actual; arthaù-meaning; tat- therefore; uktam-it is said (in the Viñëu Purana; devatve-in the
position of a demigod; deva-of a demigod; dehaù-body; ayam-He; manuçatve-in the status of a
human being; ca-also; mänuçé-appearing as a human; iti-thus.


   When Queen Rukmiëé says that she is traveling in the material world (såtibhir bhramantyäù),
this means that she follows Lord Viñëu when He incarnates in the material world, and she appears
as His companion. This is confirmed in the following statement of Viñëu Puräëa:

   "When Lord Viñëu appears as a demigod, the goddess of fortuen assumes a form like that of a
demigoddess and accompanies Him, and when Lord Viñëu assumes a form like that of a human
being, the goddess of fortune also assumes a human-like form to become His companion."


Text 8


evam eva

astv ambujäkña mama te caraëänuräga
   ätman ratasya mayi cänatirikta-dåñöeù
yarhy asya våddhaya upatta-rajo-'ti-mätro
   mäm ékñase tad u ha naù paramänukampä. iti.

   evam-in the same way; eva-certainly; astu-let there be; ambuja-akña-O lotus eyed Lord; mama-
My; te-of Your; caraëa- feet; anurägaù-pure devotional love; ätman ratasya- experiencing
transcendental bliss in Yourself; mayi-in Me; ca- also; anatirikta-unequalled; drsteù-from the sight;
yarhi-if; asya-of that; våddayaù-increase; upatta-attained; rajaù- dust; ati-mätraù-a quantity; mäm-
me; ékñase-You see; tat- then; u ha-certainly; naù-to us; parama-anukampa-please be merciful; iti-

thus.


   The transcendental position of Çrématé Rukmiëé devé is also explained in the following verse
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.46), where she says:

    "My dear lotus-eyed husband, You are self-satisfied. You do not care whether or not I am
beautiful or qualified; You are not at all concerned about it. Therefore Your non-attachment for me
is not at all astonishing; it is quite natural. You cannot be attached to any woman, however exalted
her position and beauty. Whether You are attached to me or not, may my devotion and attention
be always engaged at Your lotus feet. The material mode of passion is also Your creation, so when
You passionately glance upon me, I accept it as the greatest boon of my life. I am ambitious only for
such auspicious moments."*


Text 9


  aträpi tasyäù prakåtitvaà dainyajenäbhedopacäreëaiva vyäkhyeyam. yad vä asya gärhasthasya
upatta aìgé-kåta rajo-'ti-mätraù sarva-bhütäi-raïjanätiçayo yena saù.

    atra-here; api-also; tasyäù-of Çrémati Rukmini-devi; prakåtitvam-material position; dainyajena-
because of humbleness; abheda-upacäreëa-with a different interpretation; eva-certainly;
vyäkhyeyam-should be explained; yat-because; vä-or; asya-of that; gärhasthasya-householder status
of life; upatta aìgé-kåta-accepted; rajah-ati-mätraù sarva-bhüta-ati-raïjaëa-atiçasaù-pleasing to all
conditioned souls; yena-by whom; saù-He.


   In this verse the word "asya" means "of the householder status of life", "upatta" means "accepted",
and "rajo-'pi-mätraù" means "the material mode of passion, which enlivens the conditioned souls".
In this verse Çrématé Rukmiëé-devé is playing the part of an ordinary wife, humbly describing her
attachment to Lord Kåñëa in the vocabulary of conditioned souls.


Text 10

devyäù svayaà-lakñmétvam. çré-çukaù.

vayam iti ädi-Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.20:
