Kåñëa was his son and not the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The truth of Uddhava's words,
that Lord Kåñëa is indeed the original form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is elaboratedly
explained in the Kåñëa-sandarbha. Even at Kuruksetra, when a great host of saintly devotees
affirmed that Lord Kåñëa is indeed the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nanda and Yaçodä
remained unconvinced. They continued to believe that Kåñëa was only their son. This is seen in
the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.35):


täv ätmäsanam äropya
   bähubhyäà parirabhya ca
yaçodä ca mahä-bhägä
   sutau vijahatuù çucaù


  "Raising their two sons onto their laps and holding Them in their arms, Nanda and saintly
mother Yaçodä forgot their sorrow."***

  It is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.66):


manaso våttayo naù syuù. . .

  "May our thoughts always take shelter of Kåñëa's lotus feet, may our words always chant His
names, and may our bodies always bow down to Him and serve Him."***

   Even though the truth that Çré Kåñëa is the all-powerful Supreme Personality of Godhead was
again and again proved to him, Nanda Mahäräja continued to believe Kåñëa was only his son and
nothing more. These words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.66) Nanda spoke to Uddhava mean: "We
pray that birth after birth we may love Kåñëa." This prayer of love spoken by Nanda is filled with
anuräga love. Loev is not absent from it. Then it is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.65):


taà nirgataà samäsädya
   nänopäyana-pänayaù
nandädayo 'nurägeëa
   prävocann açru-locanäù


  "As Uddhava was about to leave, Nanda and the others approached him bearing various items of
worship. With tears in their eyes they addressed him as follows."***

   In these verses it is seen that Nanda and Yaçodä are filled with anuräga ecstatic love for Lord
Kåñëa. Their devotion to the Lord is not in the mood of awe and veneration, the mood of
appreciating Lord Kåñëa's supreme power and opulence. Here Uddhava thinks: "Although I am far
from attaining this kind of good fortune, I still pray that someday I will attainj this kind of ecstatic
love. I pray this love will nto be denied to me." With a voice choked with emotion Uddhava prays
in this way. Praying that in some other lifetime he may some day attain this kind of anuräga
ecstatic love, Uddhava says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.67):


karmabhir bhramyamänänäm. . .


   "Wherever we are made to wander about this world by the Supreme Lord's will, in accordance to
the reactions to our fruitive work, may our good works and charity always grant us love for Lord
Kåñëa."***

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.66 may be interpreted in two ways. It may be interpreted to refer to
vätsalya-rasa alone, or it may also be interpreted to refer to the other rasas also. Here the phrase
beginning with the word "päda" (taking shelter of Kåñëa's feet) is considered appropriate in vätsalya-
rasa because Nanda Mahäräja feels great anguish because he cannto associate with Kåñëa who has
gone to a faraway country. A similar situation in karuëa-rasa is seen in the story of Mahäräja
Citraketu. Here the word "prahvana" means "bowing down". In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.67 the
word "éçvare" is used, as it was used before, as an affectionate term used to address a child. It is
sometimes used in that way in this world. These are included amongst the udbhäsvaras. Now the
sättvika-bhävas will be considered. Of these there are eight, as were described before. For Lord
Kåñëa's mother there is a ninth sättvika-bhäva, which is milk flowing from her breasts. Now the

saïcäri-bhävas will be considered. These are: 1. thoseborn from the pastimes Lord Kåñëa directly
performs, and 2. those born from the pastimes of power and opulence manifest with thr aid of Lord
Kåñëa's pastime potency. The first of these is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.34):


kasmän mådam ädantätman. . .


   "Dear Kåñëa, why are You so restless that You have eaten dirt in a solitary place? This complaint
has been lodged against You by all Your playmates, including Your elder brother, Balaräma. How is
this?"***

   This is an example of Lord Kåñëa's restlessness. The second of these saïcäri-bhävas (those
pastimes of power and opulence manifest with the aid of Lord Kåñëa's pastime potency) is seen in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.37):


sä tatra dadåçe viçvam. . .


    "When Kåñëa opened His mouth wide by the order of Mother Yaçodä, she saw within His mouth
all moving and nonmoving entities, outer space, and all directions, along with mountains, islands,
oceans, the surface of the earth, the blowing wind, fire, the moon, and stars. She saw the planetary
systems, water, light, air, sky, and creation by transformation of akaìkära. She also saw the senses,
the mind, sense perception, and the three qualities goodness, passion, and ignorance. She saw the
time allotted for the living entities, she saw natural instinct and the reactions of karma, and she
saw desires and different varieties of bodies, moving and nonmoving. Seeing all these aspects of the
cosmic manifestation, along with herself and Våndävana-dhäma, she became doubtful and fearful of
her son's nature."*

  In this passage is seen Mother Yaçodä's wonder and doubt. Here the sthäyi-bhäva is vätsalya-rasa.
This sthäyi-bhäva is seen in these owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.23):


tan-mätarau nija-sutau ghåëayä snuvantyau
   paìkäìga-räga-ruciräv upagåhya dorbhyäm
dattvä stanaà prapibatoù sma mukhaà nirékñya
   mugdha-smitälpa-daçanaà yayatuù pramodam


   "Dressed with muddy earth muxed with cow dung and cow urine, the babies looked very
beautiful, and when They went to Their mothers, both Yaçodä and Rohiëé picked Them up with
great affection, embraced Them, and allowed Them to suck the milk flowing from their breasts.
While sucking the breast, the babies smiled, and Their small teeth were visible. Their mothers,
upon seeing those beautiful teeth, enjoyed great transcendental bliss."*

   In this verse the word "tan-mätarau" means {.sy 168}the mothers of Kåñëa and Balaräma", and
"ghåëayä" means "with compassion". Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.23 was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.245
records.text:
Vätsalya-rasa is wonderful with many vibhävas and other bhävas. Even before the devotees have
seen Lord Kåñëa for the first time, these ecstasies are manifest. This is seen in the following words
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.5.9):


gopyaç cäkarëya muditä
   yaçodäyäù sütodbhavam
ätàanaà bhüñayäà cakrur
   vasträkalpäïjanädibhiù


   "The gopé wives of the cowherd men were very pleased to hear that mother Yaçodä had given
birth to a son, and they began to decorate themselves very nicely with proper dresses, ornaments,
black ointment for the eyes, and so on."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.246
records.text:
After the devotees attain Lord Kåñëa's direct association the ecstasies of vätsalya-rasa become
perfectly manifest. They are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.5.12):


ta äçiñaù. . .


   "Offering blessings to the newborn child, Kåñëa, the wives and the daughters of the cowherd
men said, `May You become the king of Vraja and logn maintain all its inhabitants.' They sprinkled
a mixture of turmeric powder, oil, and water upon the birthless Supreme Lord and offered their
prayers."*

   When the devotees become separated from Lord Kåñëa, the ecstasies of vätsalya-rasa are also
seen. An example is given in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.27-28):


iti saàsmåtya saàsmåtya
    nandaù kåñëänurakta-dhéù

aty-utkaëöho 'bhavat tüñëéà
   prema-prasara-vihvalaù


   "Thus intensely remembering Kåñëa again and again, Nanda Mahäräja, his mind completely
attached to the Lord, felt extreme anxiety and fell silent, overcome by the strength of his love.***


yaçodä varëyamänäni
   putrasya caritäni ca
çåëvaty açruni aväsräkñét
   sneha-snuta-payodharä


   "As mother Yaçodä heard the descriptions of her son's activities, she poured out her tears, and
milk flowed from her breasts out of love."***

  The meaning of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.27-28 is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 247 and 248


   After being separated from Him, when they again meet Kåñëa, the devotees in vätsalya-rasa are
very pleased. This is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.35):


täv ätmäsanam äropya


  "Raising their two sons onto their laps and holding Them in their arms, Nanda and saintly
mother Yaçodä forgot their sorrow."***

   These ecstasies are also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.84.66):


nandas tu sakhyuù priya-kåt
   premëä govinda-rämayoù
adya sva iti mäsäàs trén
   yadubhir mänito 'vasat


   "And on his part, Nanda was also full of affection for his friend Vasudeva. Thus during the
following days Nanda would repeatedly announce, `I will be leaving later today' and `I will be
leaving tomorrow'. But out of love for Kåñëa and Balaräma he remained there for three more
months, honored by all the Yadus."***

   In this verse it is said: "But out of love for Kåñëa and Balaräma he remained there for three more
months." For three months he would repeatedly announce, `I will be leaving later today' and `I will
be leaving tomorrow'." Overcome with bliss, Nanda felt those three months apss as if they were only
two days. Someone may ask: "What did he do as he resided there?" The answer is given here in the
words: "Nanda was also full of affection for his friend Vasudeva." This means that when Vasudeva
was present Nanda did not act as if Kåñëa were his son. Neither did he attempt to take Kåñëa back
with him to Vraja. Then it is said here: "Nanda was honored by all the Yadus." Afterward Nanda
was again separated from Lord Kåñëa. This is described in the following words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.84.67-69):


tataù kämaiù püryamänaù
   sa-vrajaù saha-bandhavaù
parärdhyäbharaëa-kñauma-
   nänänarghya-paricchadaiù

vasudevograsenabhyäà
   kåñëoddhava-balädibhiù
dattam ädäya paribarhaà
   yäpito yadubhir yayau


   "Then, after Vasudeva, Ugrasena, Kåñëa, Uddhava, Balaräma, and others had fulfilled his desires
and presented him with precious ornaments, fine linen, and varieties of priceless household
furnishing, Nanda Mahäräja accepted all these gifts and took his leave. Seen off by all the Yadus, he
departed with his family members and the residents of Vraja.***


nando gopas ca gopyaç ca
  govinda-caraëämbuje
manaù kñiptaà punar hartum
  anéçä mathuräà yayau


   "Unable to withdraw their minds from Lord Govinda's lotus feet, where they had surrendered
them, Nanda and the cowherd men and women returned to Mathurä."***

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.84.67 the word "kämaiù" means "with the desires that begin with the
desire that Kåñëa would return to Vraja", and the word "püryamänaù" means "satisfied by Lord
Kåñëa". It was Lord Balaräma who returned to Vraja. In describing that pastime Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvämé said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.65.6):


kåñëe kamala-paträkñe
   sanyastäkhila-rädhasaù

   "The cowherds had dedicated everything to lotus-eyed Kåñëa."***

   Çréla Çrédhara Svämé comments:

   "In this verse the word `kåñëe' means `for the purpose of attaining Lord Kåñëa's association', and `
sanyastäkhila-rädhasaù' means `they renounced everything'."

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.84.67-69 it is said: {.sy 168}With great love Vasudeva and the others
gave gifts of many ornaments." Here the word "äpitaù" means {.sy 168}escorted by a great army".
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.84.69 describes the great love the people of Vraja felt for Lord Kåñëa.
Whent hey had returned to Mathurä, the cowherd people again yearned for Lord Kåñëa's
association. Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.84.66-69 was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.249
records.text:
It was after these pastimes that the citizens of Dvärakä spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(1.11.9):


yarhy ambujäkñäpasasära bho bhavän
   kurün madhün vätha suhåd-didåkñayä


    "O lotus-eyed Lord, whenever You go away to Mathurä-Våndävana or Hastinäpura to meet Your
friends and relatives, every moment of Your absence seems like a million years. O infallible one, at
that time our eyes become useless, as if bereft of sun."*

   In Çré Kåñëa-sandarbha (Anuccheda 174) it was explained that Lord Kåñëa resides in Vraja
eternally in His aprakaöa (unmanifest) form, and therefore they people of vraja are never truly
separated from Him. Their desire to associate with Him is always satisfied. In this way vätsalya-rasa
has been described.
   Now sakhya-rasa will be described. In this rasa the älambana is Lord manifest as a friend. The
viñaya is Lord Kåñëa. The äsraya is the friends who aprticipate in Lord Kåñëa's glorous pastimes. In
this rasa the Lord sometimes manifests a form-armed form and other times manifests a humanlike
form. The four-armed form is described by Arjuna in these words of Bhagavad-gétä (11.46):


tenaiva rüpeëa catur-bhujena
   sahasra-bäho bhava viçva-mürte


   "O universal form, O thousand-armed Lord, I wish to see You in Your four-armed form."*

   Afterward, when Lord Kåñëa's humanlike form was manifest, Arjuna said in Bhagavad-gétä
(11.51):


dåñövedaà mänuñaà rüpaà
   tava saumyaà janärdana
idäném asmi samvåttaù
   sa-cetaù prakåtià gataù


   "When Arjuna saw Kåñëa in His origina form, he said: O Janärdana, seeing this humanlike form,
so very beautiful, I am now composed in mind, and I am restored to my original nature."*

   Amongst the devotees in sakhya-rasa are the mitras, suhåts, and sakhäs. Among the suhåts, Çré
Bhimasena and Çré Draupadé are prominent. Among the sakhäs, Çrémän Arjuna and Çrédämä Vipra
are prominent. In Gokula the gopa Çrédämä is prominent. These great devotees are glorified in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam and other scriptures. In the Agama-sastras, Vasudämä, Kiìkini, and other
devotees in sakhya-rasa are described. In the Bhaviñya Puräëa's description of pastimes of wrestling,
the names of some devotees in sakhya-rasa are given in these words:


subhadra-maëòalébhadra-
   bhadravardhana-gobhaöäù
yakñendrabhaöaù. . .


   "Subhadra, Maëòalébhadra, Bhadravardhana, Gobhaöa, and Yakñendrabhaöa participated in
these pastimes."

  The gopas in sakhya-rasa are also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.2):


tenaiva säkaà påthukäù sahasraçaù. . .


    "At that time, hundreds and thousands of cowherd boys came out of their respective homes in
Vrajabhümi and joined Kåñëa, keeping before them their hundreds and thousands of groups of
calves. The boys were very beautiful, and they were equipped with lunch bags, bugles, flutes, and
sticks for controlling the calves."*

  These gopas were all Lord Kåñëa's equals. It is said in the scriptures:


gopaiù samäna-guëa-çéla-vayo-viläsa-vañaiç ca

   "In their qualities, character, age, pastimes, and garments, the gopa boys were like Kåñëa."

   Of the gopas it is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.18.11):


gopa jäti-praticchannä. . .


   "O King, demigods disguised themselves as members of the cowherd community and, just as
dramatic dancers praise another dancer, worshiped Kåñëa and Balaräma, who were also appearing
as cowherd boys."***

    This verse has been explained in Çré Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anuccheda 117. The gopas' great learning
is seen in these words they spoke in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.23.8):


déksäyäù paçu-saàsthäyäù. . .


   "Except during the interval between the initiation of the performer of a sacrifice and the actual
sacrifice of the animal, O most pure brähmaëas, it is not contaminating for even the initiated to
partake of food, at least in sacrifices other than the Sauträmaëi."***

   The gopas' expert artistic skill is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.18.13):


kvacin nåtyatsu cänyeñu. . .


   "While the other boys were dancing, O King, Kåñëa and Balaräma would sometimes accompany
them with song and instrumental music, and sometimes the two Lords would praise the boys, saying,
``Very good! Very good!' "***

   In these words Lord Kåñëa Himself praised the gopas' glorious qualities. The gopas are of three
kinds: 1. sakhä (ordinary friends), 2. priya-sakhä (more confidential friends), and 3. priya-narma-
sakhä (intimate friends). The gopa Çrédämäa and the other gopas enjoy very sweeet pastimes with
Lord Kåñëa. They are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.11):


itthaà satäà. . .


   "In this way, all the cowherd boys used to play with Kåñëa, who is the source of the Brahman
effulgence for jïänés desiring to merge into that effulgence, who is the Supreme Personality of
Godhead for devotees who have accepted eternal servitorship, and who for ordinary persons is but
another ordinary child. The cowherd boys, having accumulated the results of pious activities for
many lives, were able to associate in this way with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. How can

one explain their great fortune?"*

   In this rasa lord Kåñëa is the älambana. Lord Kåñëa as the älambana is described in these words
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.5):


barhäpéòaà naöa-vara-vapuù. . .


   "Wearing a peacock-feather ornament upon His head, blue karnikära flowers on His ears, a
yellow garment as brilliant as gold, and the Vaijayanté garland, Lord Kåñëa exhibited His
transcendental form as the greatest of dancers as He entered the forest of Våndävana, beautifying it
with the marks of His footprints. He filled the holes of His flute with the nectar of His lips, and the
cowherd boys sang His glories."***

   Mow the uddépanas in this rasa will be considered. Amongst these uddépanas are included the
following transcendental qualities: loving friendship, straightforwardness, gratitude, intelligence,
learning, glory, expert skill, heroism, strength, tolerance, mercy, and giving delight to the people.
Also included amongst these uddépanas are youthful handsomeness, all-auspicious bodily features,
and other qualities. For the suhåt friends the qualities beginning with straightforwardness are
prominent. For the sakhä friends the qualities beginning with handsomeness and skill are
prominent. For the mitra friends the qualities beginning with straightforwardness, handsomeness,
and skill are prominent. The suhåt, sakhä, and mitra kinds of friendship are mentioned by
lamenting Arjuna in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.15.4):


sakhyaà maitréà sauhådaà ca. . .


  "Remembering Lord Kåñëa and His well wishes, benefactions, intimate familial relations and His
chariot driving, Arjuna, overwhelmed and breathing very heavily, began to speak."***

   Lord Kåñëa's friendly affection for the gopas is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.13.13 and 16):


tän dåsövä bhaya-santrastän
   üce kåñëo'sya bhé-bhayam
miträëy äçän mä viramate-
   häneñye vatsakän aham


   "When Kåñëa saw that His friends the cowherd boys were frightened, He, the fierce controller
even of fear itself, said, just to mitigate their fear, `My dear friends, do not stop eating. I shall bring
your calves back to this spot by personally going after them Myself.' "***

tato vatsän adåñövaitya
   puline 'pi ca vatsapän
ubhäv api vane kåñëo
   vicikäya samantataù


   "Thereafter, when Kåñëa was unable to find the calves, He returned to the bank of the river, but
there He was also unable to see the cowherd boys. Thus He began to search for both the calves and
the boys, as if He could not understand what had happened."*

   The meaning of these verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.13.13 and 16) is clear. These verses were
spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.250
records.text:
Sakhya-rasa is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.15.52):


anvamaàsata tad räjan
  govindänugrahekñitam. . .


   "O King, the cowherd boys then considered that although they had drunk poison and in fact had
died, simply by the merciful glance of Govinda they had regained their lives and stood up by their
own strength."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.251
records.text:
Sakhya-rasa is again seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.13.5):


aho 'tiramyaà pulinaà vayasyäh. . .


   "My dear friends, just see how this riverbank is extremely beautiful because of its pleasing
atmosphere. And just see how the blooming lotuses are attracting bees and birds by their aroma.
The humming and chirping of the bees and birds is echoing throughout the beautiful trees in the
forest. Also, here the sands are clean and soft. Therefore, this must be considered the best place for
our sporting and pastimes."*

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.252
records.text:
Sakhya-rasa is again seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.15.16):


kvacit pallava-talpeñu
   niyuddha-çrama-karçitaù
våkña-müläçrayah çete
   gopotsaìgopabarhanah


   "Sometimes Lord Kåñëa grew tired from fighting and lay down at the base of a tree, resting upon
a bed made of soft twigs and buds and using the lap of a cowherd friend as His pillow."*

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.253
records.text:
Sakhya-rasa is again seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.20):


kunda-däma. . .narma-daù praëayiëäà vijahära


    "O sinless Yaçodä, your darling child, the son of Mahäräja Nanda, has festively enhanced His
attire with a jasmine garland, and He is now playing along the Yamunä in the company of the cows
and cowherd boys, amusing His dear companions."***

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.254
records.text:
Sakhya-rasa is again seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.18):


maëi-dharaù. . .praëayino 'nucarasya kadäàse
  prakñipan bhujam agäyata yatra


   "Now Kåñëa is standing somewhere counting His cows on a string of gems. He wears a garland of
tulasé flowers that bear the fragrance of His beloved, and He has thrown His arm over the shoulder

of an affectionate cowherd boyfriend. "***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.255
records.text:
When Lord Kåñëa enjoys pastimes as a kñatriya (at Mathurä and Dvärakä), the suhåt friends are
more numerous. When Lord Kåñëa enjoys pastimes as a gopa, the sakhä friends are more numerous.
For these suhåt friends Lord Kåñëa's pastimes as a heroic warrior and other like pastimes are
prominent. For the gopa sakhä freinds Lord Kåñëa's pastimes of joking, singing, conversing, calling
the cows, playing the flute, showing artistic skill, and other like pastimes are prominent. Lord
Kåñëa's pastimes of joking are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.13.11):


bibhrad veëuà jaöhara-paöayoù. . .
. . .tiñöhan madhye sva-parisuhådo häsayan narmabhiù svaiù. . .


   "Kåñëa is yajïa-bhuk-that is, He eats only offerings of yajïa-but to exhibit His childhood
pastimes, He now sat with His flute tucked between His waist and His tight cloth on His right side
and with His horn bugle and cow-driving stick on His left. Holding in His hand a very nice
preparation of yogurt and rice, with pieces of suitable fruit between His fingers, He sat like the
whorl of a lotus flower, looking forward toward all His friends, personally joking with them and
creating jubilant laughter among them as He ate. At that time, the denizens of heaven were
watching, struck with wonder at how the Personality of Godhead, who eats only in yajïa, was now
eating with His friends in the forest."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.256
records.text:
Some of the other pastimes Lord Kåñëa enjoys with the gopa sakhäs are seen in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.15.9-10):


evaà våndävanaà çrémat
   krsëaù préta-manäù paçün
reme saïcärayann adreh
   sarid-rodhaùsu sänugah


  "Thus expressing His satisfaction with the beautiful forest of Våndävana and its inhabitants,

Lord Kåñëa enjoyed tending the cows and other animals with His friends on the banks of the river
Yamunä below Govardhana Hill.***


kvacid gäyati gäyatsu
  madändhäliñv anuvrataiù
upagéyamäna-caritaù
  pathi sankarñaëanvitah. . .


   "Sometimes the honeybees in Våndävana became so mad with ecstasy that they closed their eyes
and began to sing. Lord Kåñëa, moving along the forest Path with His cowherd boyfriends and
Baladeva, would then respond to the bees by imitating their singing while His friends sang about
His pastimes. Sometimes Lord Kåñëa would imitate the chattering of a parrot, sometimes, with a
sweet voice, the call of a cuckoo, and sometimes the cooing of swans. Sometimes He vigorously
imitated the dancing of a peacock, making His cowherd boyfriends laugh."***

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.257
records.text:
These pastimes are also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.13.12-13):


megha-gambhérayä väcä
  nämabhir düra-gän paçün
kvacid ähvayati prétyä
  go-gopäla-manojïayä


   "Sometimes, with a voice as deep as the rumbling of clouds, He would call out with great
affection the names of the animals who had wandered far from the herd, thus enchanting the cows
and the cowherd boys."***


cakora-krauïca. . .


    "Sometimes He would cry out in imitation of birds such as the cakoras, krauïcas, cakrähvas,
bhäraòiäjas and Peacocks, and sometimes He would run away with the smaller animals in mock fear
of lions and tigers."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.258
records.text:
These pastimes are also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.18.19):


tatropähüya gopälän
   kåñëaù präha vihära-vit
he gopä vihariñyämo
   dvandvé-bhüya yathä-yatham


   "Kåñëa, who knows all sports and games, then called together the cowherd boys and spoke as
follows: ``Hey cowherd boys! Let's play now! We'll divide ourselves into two even teams.''"***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.259
records.text:
These pastimes are also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.47):


barha-prasüna-vana-dhätu-vicitritäìgaù
   proddäma-veëu-dala-çåìga-ravotsaväòhyaù. . .


   "When Kåñëa returned home to Vrajabhümi, He was seen by all the inhabitants of Våndävana.
He was wearing a peacock feather in His helmet, which was also decorated with forest flowers.
Kåñëa was also garlanded with flowers and painted with different colored minerals collected from
the caves of Govardhana Hill. Govardhana Hill is always famous for supplying natural red dyes, and
Kåñëa and His friends painted their bodies with them. Each of them had a bugle made of buffalo
horn and a stick and a flute, and each called his respective calves by their particular names. They
were so proud of Kåñëa's wonderful activities that, while entering the village, they all sang His
glories. All the gopés in Våndävana saw beautiful Kåñëa entering the village."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.260
records.text:
Lord Kåñëa's apperance when He wears the garments of a gopa, wearing colorful and wonderful
garments, sash, pearls, and ornaments are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.19):


gä gopakair anu-vanaà nayatoù. . .
 . . .niryoga-päça-kåta-lakñaëayor vicitram

   "My dear friends, as Kåñëa and Balaräma pass through the forest with Their cowherd friends,
leading Their cows, They carry ropes to bind the cows' rear legs at the time of milking. When Lord
Kåñëa plays on His flute, the sweet music causes the moving living entities to become stunned and
the nonmoving trees to tremble with ecstasy. These things are certainly very wonderful."***

   Lord Kåñëa's appearance dressed as a wrestler is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.35.6):


barhiëa-stabaka-dhätu-paläçair
   baddha-malla-paribarha-viòambaù. . .


   "My dear gopé, sometimes Mukunda imitates the appearance of a wrestler by decorating Himself
with leaves, peacock feathers and colored minerals. Then, in the company of Balaräma and the
cowherd boys, He plays His flute to call the cows. At that time the rivers stop flowing, their water
stunned by the ecstasy they feel as they eagerly wait for the wind to bring them the dust of His lotus
feet. But like us, the rivers are not very pious, and thus they merely wait with their arms trembling
out of love."***

   Lord Kåñëa's appearance dressed as a dancer is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.22):


çyämaà hiraëya-paridhim. . .naöa-veñam


   "His complexion was dark blue and His garment golden. Wearing a peacock feather, colored
minerals, sprigs of flower buds, and a garland of forest flowers and leaves, He was dressed just like a
dramatic dancer."***

   The elder gopas' appearance dressed like kings is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.5.8):


mahärha-vasträbharaëa-
   kaïcukoñëéça-bhüñitäù
gopäù samayuyü räjan. . .


   "O King Parékñit, the cowherd men dressed very opulently with valuable ornaments and
garments such as coats and turbans."*

   In Dvaraka and other like places Lord Kåñëa wears a great variety of garments. In Gokula Lord

Kåñëa primarily wears the standard upper and lower garments of a pious householder. Lord Kåñëa's
Gokula garments are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.15.45):


névéà vasitvä ruciräà


   "By being bathed and massaged, the two young Lords were relieved of the weariness caused by
walking on the country roads. Then They were dressed in attractive robes and decorated with
transcendental garlands and fragrances."***

   Lord Kåñëa's paraphernalia include His garemnts, ornaments, conchshell, cakra, buffalo-horn
bugle, flute, stick, and dear associates. The appropriate times are the times appropriate for specific
pastimes. Some of these pastimes are seen in the following verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.20.25-
31):


evaà vanaà tad varñiñöhaà
   pakva-kharjura jambumat
go-gopälair våto rantuà
   sa-balaù präviçad dhariù


   "When the Våndävana forest had thus become resplendent, filled with ripe dates and jambu
fruits, Lord Kåñëa, surrounded by His cows and cowherd boyfriends and accompanied by Sré
Balaräma, entered that forest to enjoy."***


dhenavo manda-gäminyaù. . .


  "The cows had to move slowly because of their weighty milk bags, but they quickly ran to the
Supreme Personality of Godhead as soon as He called them, their affection for Him causing their
udders to become wet."***


vanaukasaù pramuditäù. . .


  "The Lord saw the joyful aborigine girls of the forest, the trees dripping sweet sap, and the
mountain waterfalls, whose resounding indicated that there were caves nearby."***


kvacid vanaspati-kroòe. . .


   "When it rained, the Lord would sometimes enter a cave or the hollow of a tree to play and to

eat roots and fruits."***


dadhy-odanaà samänétam. . .


   "Lord Kåñëa would take His meal of boiled rice and yogurt, sent from home, in the company of
Lord Saìkarñaëa and the cowherd boys who regularly ate with Him. They would all sit down to eat
on a large stone near the water."***


çädvalopari samviçya. . .
prävåö-çriyaà ca täà vékñya. . .


   "Lord Kåñëa watched the contented bulls, calves and cows sitting on the green grass and grazing
with closed eyes, and He saw that the cows were tired from the burden of their heavy milk bags.
Thus observing the beauty and opulence of Våndavana s rainy season, a perennial source of great
happiness, the Lord offered all respect to that season, which was expanded from His own internal
potency."***

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.261
records.text:
Now other features of sakhya-rasa will be considered. Amongst the anubhavas are the
udbhäsvaras. Amongst the suhrt friends the udbhäsvaras include attempts to bring limitless good
fortune to Kåñëa, discussion of what is proper and improper, smiling conversations, and other like
activities. Amongst the sakhä friends the udbhäsvaras include activities of unwavering affection,
activities like various playful games, singing, artistic skill, eating together, sitting down together,
taking naps, and other like pastimes. Telling jokes, hearing descriptions of confidential pastimes,
and other like activities are also included here. These friends are glorified in the following words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.11):


itthaà satäà. . .


   "In this way, all the cowherd boys used to play with Kåñëa, who is the source of the Brahman
effulgence for jïänés desiring to merge into that effulgence, who is the Supreme Personality of
Godhead for devotees who have accepted eternal servitorship, and who for ordinary persons is but
another ordinary child. The cowherd boys, having accumulated the results of pious activities for
many lives, were able to associate in this way with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. How can
one explain their great fortune?"*

  The sakhä friends are also described in these owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.18.9-14):


praväla-barha-stabaka-
   srag-dhätu-kåta-bhüñanäh
räma-kåñëädayo gopä
   nanåtur yuyudhur jaguh


   "Decorating themselves with newly grown leaves, along with peacock feathers, garlands, clusters
of flower buds, and colored minerals, Balaräma, Kåñëa and Their cowherd friends danced, wrestled
and sang."***


kåñëasya nåtyataù kecij
   jaguù kecid avädayan
veëu-päëitalaiù çåìgaih
   praçaçaàsur athäpare


  "As Kåñëa danced, some of the boys accompanied Him by singing, and others by playing flutes,
hand cymbals and buffalo horns, while still others praised His dancing."***


gopa jäti-praticchannä
   devä gopäla-rüpinau
éòire kåñëa-rämau ca
   naöa iva naöaà nåpa


   "O King, demigods disguised themselves as members of the cowherd community and, just as
dramatic dancers praise another dancer, worshiped Kåñëa and Balaräma, who were also appearing
as cowherd boys."***


bhramaëair laìghanaiù kñepair
   äsphoöana-vikarñaëaih
cikréòatur niyuddhena
   käka-pakña-dharau kvacit


   "Kåñëa and Balaräma played with Their cowherd boyfriends by whirling about, leaping, hurling,
slapping and fighting. Sometimes Kåñëa and Balaräma would pull the hair on the boys' heads."***


kvacin nåtyatsu cänyeñu

   gäyakau vädakau svayam
çaçaàsatur mahä-räja
   sädhu sädhv iti vòinau


   "While the other boys were dancing, O King, Kåñëa and Balaräma would sometimes accompany
them with song and instrumental music, and sometimes the two Lords would praise the boys, saying,
``Very good! Very good!''"***


kvacid bilvaiù kvacit kumbhaiù. . .


   "Sometimes the cowherd boys would play with bilva or kumbha fruits, and sometimes with
handfuls of ämalaka fruits. At other times they would play the games of trying to touch one another
or of trying to identify somebody while one is blindfolded, and sometimes they would imitate
animals and birds."***

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.262
records.text:
Lord Kåñëa's pastimes with His sakhä friends are also described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.13.8):


kåñëasya viñvak puru-räji-maëdalair
   abhyänanäù phulla-dåço vrajärbhakäù
sahopaviñöä vipine virejuç
   c hadä yathämbhoruha-karëikäyäh


   "Like the whorl of a lotus flower surrounded by its petals and leaves, Kåñëa sat in the center,
encircled by lines of His friends, who all looked very beautiful. Every one of them was trying to look
forward toward Kåñëa, thinking that Kåñëa might look toward him. In this way they all enjoyed
their lunch in the forest."*

   These pastimes are also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.13.9-10):


kecit puñpair dalaiù kecit. . .


    "Among the cowherd boys, some placed their lunch on flowers, some on leaves, fruits, or bunches
of leaves, some actually in their baskets, some on the bark of trees and some on rocks. This is what

the children imagined to be their plates as they ate their lunch."*


sarve mitho darçayantaù
   sva-sva-bhojya- rucià påthak
hasanto häsayantaç cä-
   bhyavajahruù saheçvaräù


   "All the cowherd boys enjoyed their lunch with Kåñëa, showing one another the different tastes
of the different varieties of preparations they had brought from home. Tasting one another's
preparations, they began to laugh and make one another laugh."*

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.263
records.text:
Now other aspects of sakhya-rasa will be considered. Now the sättvika-bhävas of the suhåt and
sakhä friends will be considered. Shedding tears is among the sättvika-bhävas of the suhåt friends.
This is described in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.71.27):


taà mätuleyaà parirabhya nirvåto
   bhémaù smayan prema-jaläkulendriyaù
yamau kiréöé ca suhåttamaà mudä
   pravåddha-bäñpaù parirebhire 'cyutam


    "Then Bhéma, his eyes bnrimming with tears, laughed with joy as he embraced his maternal
cousin Kåñëa. Arjuna and the twins-Nakula and Sahadeva-also joyfully embraced their dearmost
friend, the infallible Lord, and they cried profusely."***

   Of the Lord's associates described here some were elder than Kåñëa and some younger than
Kåñëa. Still, all of them considered Kåñëa their suhåt friend. There is no rasäbhäsa in this. This is a
proper arrangement of the rasas. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.264
records.text:
Devastation is a sättvika-bhäva manifest among the sakhä friends. It is described in these owrds
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.16.10):


taà näga-bhoga-parivétam adåñöa-ceñöam

   älokya tat-priya-sakhäù paçupä bhåçärtäù
kåñëe 'rpitätma-suhåd-artha-kalatra-kämä
   duùkhanusoka-bhaya-muòha-dhiyo nipetuù


    "When the members of the cowherd community, who had accepted Kåñëa as their dearmost
friend, saw Him enveloped in the snake's coils, motionless, they were greatly disturbed. They had
offered Kåñëa everything--their very selves, their families, their wealth, wives and all pleasures. At
the sight of the Lord in the clutches of the Käliya snake, their intelligence became deranged by
grief, lamentation and fear, and thus they fell to the ground."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.265
records.text:
Now the saïcäri-bhävas will be considered. An example of the saïcäri-bhäva harña (joy)
manifest among the suhåt friends is seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.71.27 (which was qouted in
Anuccheda 263). This same sancäri-bhäva (joy) as manifested among the sakhä friends is seen in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.17.13-14):


kåñëaà hradäd viniñkräntam. . .

. . .upalabhyotthitäù sarve
    labdha-präëä iväsavah
pramoda-nibhåtätmäno
    gopäù prétyäbhirebhire


   "Kåñëa rose up out of the lake wearing divine garlands, fragrances and garments, covered with
many hne jewels, and decorated with gold. When the cowherds saw Him they all stood up
immediately, just like an unconscious person's senses coming back to life. Filled with great joy, they
affectionately embraced Him."***

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.266
records.text:
In sakhya-rasa the sthayi-bhava is friendship. For Çrédämä Vipra and others like him the
sentiment of friendship is lessened by awareness of the Lord's power and opulence. For Arjuna and
others like him, however, their awareness of the Lord's friendship and opulence is itself lessened.
For the gopa boys there is no awareness of the Lord's power and opulence. Therefore their

friendship is pure and unalloyed. Their sentiment of friendship is never altered. Their friendship is
described in the following words in relation to Lord Balaräma's return to Vraja (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.65.5):


samupetyätha gopälän
   häsya-hasta-grahädibhiù. . .


   "Lord Balaräma then paid proper respects to the elder cowherd men, and the younger ones all
greeted Him respectfully. He met them all with smiles, handshakes, and so on."***

   In this way the activities of the Lord's friends are seen. The different kinds of suhåt friends may
be seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.71.27 (which was quoted here in Anuccheda 263). An example of
the activities of the sakhä friends is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.58.13-14):


ekadä ratham äruhya
   vijayo vänara-dhvajam
gäëòévaà dhanur ädäya
   tüëau cäkñaya-säyakau

säkaà kåñëena sannaddho
   vihartuà vipinaà mahat
bahu-vyäla-mågäkérëaà
   präviçat para-véra-hä


   "Once Arjuna, the layer of powerful enemies, donned his armor, mounted his chariot flying the
flag of Hanumän, took up his bow and his two inexhaustible quivers, and went to sport with Lord
Kåñëa in a large forest filled with fierce animals."***

  If this passage had been prose the word sequence would have been "kåñëena säkaà vihartum".
This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.267
records.text:
The gopa sakhäs are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.2):


tenaiva säkaà påthukäù sahasraçah
   snigdhäù suçig-vetra-viñäëa-veëavaù
svän svän sahasropari-saìkhyayänvitän
   vatsän puraskåtya viniryayur mudä

    "At that time, hundreds and thousands of cowherd boys came out of their respective homes in
Vrajabhümi and joined Kåñëa, keeping before them their hundreds and thousands of groups of
calves. The boys were very beautiful, and they were equipped with lunch bags, bugles, flutes, and
sticks for controlling the calves."*

  In this verse the word "eva" (indeed) emphasizes the gopas' great attachment to Lord Kåñëa.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.268
records.text:
The gopés' attachment to Kåñëa is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.6):


yadi düraà gataù kåñëo
   vana-çobhekñaëäya tam
ahaà pürvam ahaà pürvam
   iti saàspåçya remire


   "Sometimes Kåñëa would go to a somewhat distant place to see the beauty of the forest. Then all
the other boys would run to accompany Him, each one saying, ""I shall be the first to run and touch
Kåñëa! I shall touch Kåñëa first!'' In this way they enjoyed life by repeatedly touching Kåñëa."*

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.269
records.text:
The gopa sakhäs' friendship with Lord Kåñëa is also seen in these owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.14.45):


ücuç ca suhådaù kåñëaà
   sv-ägataà te 'ti-raàhasä
naiko 'py abhoji kavala
   ehiitaù sädhu bhujyatäm


   "They began to laugh, thinking that Kåñëa was not willing to leave their lunchtime company.
They were very jubilant and invited Him, "Dear friend Kåñëa, You have come back so quickly! All
right, we have not as yet begun our lunch, not even taken one morsel of food. So please come and
join us and let us eat together."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.270
records.text:
Lord Kåñëa is like the gopa boys' very life. This is seen in the following words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.11.49 and 53):


kåñëaà mahä-baka-grastaà
   dåñövä rämädayo 'rbhakäù
babhuvur indriyäëéva
   vinä präëaà vicetasaù


   "When Balaräma and the other boys saw that Kåñëa had been devoured by the gigantic duck,
they became almost unconscious, like senses without life."*


muktaà bakäsyäd upalabhya bälakä
   rämädayaù präëam ivendriyo gaëaù
sthänägataà taà parirabhya nirvåtaù
   praëéya vatsän vrajam etya taj jaguù


   "Just as the senses are pacified when consciousness and life return, so when Kåñëa was freed from
this danger, all the boys, including Balaräma, thought that their life had been restored. They
embraced Kåñëa in good consciousness, and then they collected their own calves and returned to
Vrajabhümi, where they declared the incident loudly."*

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.271
records.text:
The vibhävas and other features of sakhya-rasa have thus been described. The twho kinds of
friends, the suhrts and the sakhäs, ahve also been described. The situations before meeting Kåñëa
and while the friends haveKåñëa's association are like what has previously been described in the
decription of vätsalya-rasa. The situation when the friends are separated from Lord Kåñëa is seen in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.15.1-4):


evaà kåsëa-sakhaù kåsëo
   bhräträ räjïä vikalpitaù
nänä-çaìkäspadaà rüpaà

   kåsëa-viçlesa-karçita h


   "Arjuna, the celebrated friend of Lord Kåñëa, was griefstricken because of his strong feeling of
separation from Kåñëa, over and above all Mahäräja Yudhiñöhira's speculative inquiries.*


çokena çuñyad-vadana-
   håt-sarojo hata-prabhaù
vibhuà tam evänusmaran
   näçaknot pratibhäsitum


  "Due to grief, Arjuna's mouth amd lotuslike heart had dried up. Therefore his body lost all luster.
Now, remembering the Supreme Lord, he could hardly utter a word in reply.*


kåcchreëa saàstabhya çucaù
   päëinämåjya netrayoh
parokñeëa samunnaddha-
   praëayautkaëthya-kätarah


   "With great difficulty he checked the tears of grief that smeared his eyes. He was very distressed
because Lord Kåñëa was out of his sight, and he increasingly felt affection for Him.*


sakhyaà maitréà sauhådaà ca
   särathyadisu samsmaran
nåpam agrajam ity äha
   bäñpa-gadgadayä girä


  "Remembering Lord Kåñëa and His well wishes, benefactions, intimate familial relations and His
chariot driving, Arjuna, overwhelmed and breathing very heavily, began to speak."*

   In these verses the word "Kåñëaù" means {.sy 168}Arjuna". The word "räjïävikalpitaù" is divided
into "räjïä" and "ävikalpitaù".

The words "nänä-çaìkäspadaà rüpaà vikalpitaù" mean "He was filled with doubts". The words
"sucaù ämåjya" mean "He wiped the tears of grief from his eyes". "Parokñeëa" means "because Lord
Kåñëa was no longer present before his eyes". However, because Arjuna did not fear that some
calamity had befallen Lord Kåñëa, this is not an example of karuëa-rasa (compassion). Arjuna did
not fear that a calamity had befallen Lord Kåñëa becausze Arjuna was aware of Lord Kåñëa's
supreme power and opulence, His status as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is seen in the
next verse, where Arjuna laments (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.15.5):

vaïcito 'haà. . .


    "O King! The Supreme Personality of Godhead Hari, who treated me exactly like an intimate
friend, has left me alone. Thus my astounding power, which astonished even the demigods, is no
longer with me."*


Anucchedas 272 and 273


   Later in that chapter the devotee's attainment of blissful association with the Supreme Lord is
described in these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.15.46-48):


te sädhu-kåta-sarvärthä
    jïätvätyantikam ätmanaù
manasä dhärayäm äsur
    vaikuëtha-caranämbujam


   "They all had performed all the principles of religion and as a result rightly decided that the
lotus feet of the Lord Sré Krñëa are the supreme goal of all. Therefore they meditated upon His feet
without interruption.*


tad-dhyänodriktayä bhaktyä
   viçuddha-dhiñaëäù pare
tasmin näräyaëa-pade
   ekänta-matayo gatim

aväpur duraväpäà te
   asadbhir viñayätmabhiù
vidhüta-kalmañaà sthänaà
   virajenätmanaiva hi


   "Thus by pure consciousness due to constant devotional remembrance, they attained the
spiritual sky, which is ruled over by the Supreme Näräyaëa, Lord Kåñëa. This is attained only by
those who meditate upon the one Supreme Lord without deviation. This abode of the Lord Çré
Kåñëa, known as Goloka Våndävana, cannot be attained by persons who are absorbed in the
material conception of life. But the Päëdavas, being completely washed of all material
contamination, attained that abode in their very same bodies."*

    In these verses the word "te" means "the Päëòavas", sädhu" means "properly", "kåta-sarvärthäù"
means "having attained economic development, religiosity, sense gratification, and liberation",
"vaikuëtha-caranämbujam" means "the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead",
"ätyantikam" means "the supreme goal of life", "jïätvä" means "understanding". Understanding this
is the supreme goal of liife, they became rpat in meditation "manasä dhärayäm äsuù). Here
"näräyaëa" means "Çré Kåñëa", This means they again attained Lord Kåñëa's association. "Vidhüta-
kalmañaà sthänam" means "the supremely pure spiritual abode where Lord Kåñëa is manifest
eternally", and "ätmanaù" means "in their very same bodies". This was possible because their bodies
were not material (virajeëa). The word "hi" (certainly) is used here to dispell any doubt that is is
not possible.

   It is then said in the same passage of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.15.50):


draupadé ca tadäjïäya
   paténäm anapekñatäm
väsudeve bhagavati
   hy ekänta-matir äpa tam


   "Draupadé also saw that her husbands, without caring for her, were leaving home. She knew well
about Lord Väsudeva, Kåñëa, the Personality of Godhead. Both she and Subhadrä became absorbed
in thoughts of Kåñëa and attained the same results as their husbands."*

   Here the words "paténäm anapekñatäm" means {.sy 168}independent of their husbands", "tat"
means {.sy 168}the associationof Lord Kåñëa", "ajïäya" means {.sy 168}properly understanding",
"väsudeve" means {.sy 168}Lord Kåñëa, the son of Mahäräja Vasudeva", "hi" means "certainly", and
"ekänta-matiù" means {.sy 168}thoughts absorbed ion Lord Kåñëa". In this way they attained the
association of Lord Kåñëa.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.274
records.text:
The gopa boys of Vraja are separated from Kåñëa when Kåñëa goes to live in a faraway place.
Later they meet Him again and feel happiness. These experiences for them are like the previously
described experiences of the devotees in vätsalya-rasa. Thus concludes the description of sakhya-
rasa.
   Now çåìgära-rasa will be described. In this Kåñëa the älambana is Lord Kåñëa as the object of
amorous love. The viñaya is the beloved Kåñëa. The lovers (ädhära) are of two kinds: 1. sajätéya-
bhäva, and 2. tadéya-parama-vallabhä. Lord Kåñëa as the älambana and viñaya is described in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.52.37):


çrutvä guëän bhuvana-sundara çåìvatäà te

   nirviçya karëa-vivarair harato 'ìga-täpam
rüpaà dåçäà dåçimatäà akhilärtha-läbhaà
   tvayy acyutäviçati cittam apatrapaà me


   "O beauty of the worlds, having heard of Your qualities, which enter the ears of those who hear
and remove their bodily distress, and having also heard of Your beauty, which fulfills all the visual
desires of those who see, I have fixed my shameless mind upon You, O Kåñëa."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çré Rukmiëé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.275
records.text:
Lord Kåñëa as the älambana and viñaya is also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.32.2):


täsäm ävirabhüc chauriù
   smayamäna-mukhämbujaù
pétämbara-dharaù sragvé
   sakñän manmatha-manmathaù


   "Then Lord Kåñëa, a smile on His lotus face, appeared before the gopés. Wearing a garland and a
yellow garment, He directly appeared as one who can bewilder the mind of Cupid, who himself
bewilders the minds of ordinary people."***

  Here the word "manmatha-manmathaù" mweans {.sy 168}who bewilders even Cupid". This verse
was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.276
records.text:
The Supreme Lord's ordinary lovers (sämänya-vallabhä) include the girl Kubjä and the damsels
on Mount Kailäsa, damsels described in the Kürma Puräëa. Kubjä is described in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.48.8):


saivaà kaivalya-näthaà taà
   präpya duñpräpyam éçvaram
aìga-rägärpaëenäho
   durbhagedam äyacata

   "Having thus gotten the hard-to-get Supreme Lord by the simple act of offering Him body
ointment, unfortunate Trivakrä submitted to that Lord of freedom the following request."***

  This verse says: "Even though she was unfortuante, Kubjä attained the Supreme Personality of
Godhead simply by offering bodily ointment to Him. This is very surprising." Then Kubjä said to
Lord Kåñëa in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.48.9):


sahoñyatäm. . .


  "O beloved, please stay here with me for a few days more and enjoy. I cannot bear to give up
Your association, O lotus-eyed one."***

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.48.8 the word "ayäcata" means "she approached to beg a favor". What
were the characteristics of Lord Kåñëa? It is said here that He is {.sy 168}kaivalya-nätha", which
means "the beloved whose love is pure". Although originally she approached Lord Kåñëa so that she
herself would find pleasure, at the end Kubjä loved Kåñëa with pure and selfless love. In this way
she became like the goddesslike gopés of Vraja. Çré Rukmiëé and the other queens of Lord Kåñëa are
praised in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.90.27):


yaù samparyäcaran premëä
   pada-samvähanädibhiù
jagad-guruà bhartå-buddhyä
   täsäà kià varëyate tapaù


  "And how could one possibly describe the great austerities that had been performed by the
women who perfectly served Him, the spiritual master of the universe, in pure ecstatic love?
Thinking of Him as their husband, they rendered such intimate services as massaging His feet."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.277
records.text:
Lord Kåñëa's queens are also praised in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.61.5-6):


itthaà ramä-patim aväpaya patià striyas tä
   brahmädayo 'pi na viduù padavéà yadéyäm
bhejur mudäviratam edhitayänuräga-
   häsävaloka-nava-saìgama-lälasädyam

   "Thus these women obtained as their husband the master of the goddess of fortune, although
even great demigods like Brahmä do not know how to approach Him. With ever-increasing
pleasure, they felt loving attraction for Him, exchanged smiling glances with Him, eagerly
anticipated associating with Him in ever-fresh intimacy, and enjoyed in many other ways.***


pratyudgamäsana-varärhaëa-päda-çauca-
   tämbüla-viçramaëa-véjana-gandha-mälyaiù
keça-prasära-çayana-snapanopahäryaiù
   däçé-çatä api vibhor vidadhuù sma däsyam


   "Although the Supreme Lord's queens each had hundreds of maidservants, they chose to
personally serve the Lord by approaching Him humbly, offering Him a seat, worshiping Him wityh
excellent paraphernalia, bathing and massaging His feet, giving Him pän to chew, fanning Him,
anointing Him with fragrant sandalwood paste, adorning Him with flower garlands, dressing His
hair, arranging His bed, bathing Him, and presenting Him with various gifts."***

   Persons who think someone other than Lord Kåñëa is the supreme love of their life are criticized
in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.52):


ye mäà bhajanti däm-patye. . .


  "Although I have the pwoer to award spiritual liberation, lusty persons worship Me with penance
and vows in order to get My blessings for their mundane family life. Such persons are bewildered by
My illusory energy."***

   Later in that chapter Lord Kåñëa affirms (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.54):


diñöyä gåheçvari. . .


   "Fortunately, O mistress of this house, you have always rendered Me faithful devotional service,
which liberates one from material existence. This service is very difficult for the envious to
perform, especially for a woman whose intentions are wicked, who lives only to gratify her bodily
demands, and who indulges in duplicity."***

   In Ketumäla-varña Gosddess Lakñmé worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead manifest
there in His form as Kämadeva. She prays to Him (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 5.18.19):

striyo vratais tvä håñékeçvaraà svato
    hy ärädhya loke patim äçäsate 'nyam. . .

   "My dear Lord, You are certainly the fully independent master of all the senses. Therefore all
women who worship You by strictly observing vows because they wish to acquire a husband to
satisfy their senses are surely under illusion. They do not know that such a husband cannot actually
give protection to them or their children. Nor can he protect their wealth or duration of life, for he
himself is dependent on time, fruitive results and the modes of nature, which are all subordinate to
You."*

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.61.5-6 was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.278
records.text:
In addition to Lord Kåñëa's queens (svakéya), there are the goddesslike gopés of Vraja, who love
Lord Kåñëa as their paramour (parakéya). No lovers are equal or superior to the gopés, who are
glorified in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.60):


näyaà çriyo 'ìga u nitänta-rateù prasädaù
   svär-yoñitäà nalina-gandha-rucaà kuto 'nyäù
räsotasave 'sya bhuja-daëòa-gåhiöa-kaëöha-
   labdhäçiñaà ya udagäd vraja-vallabhénäm


   "When Lord Çré Kåñëa was dancing with the gopés in the räsa-lélä, the gopés were embraced by
the arms of the Lord. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or
other consorts in the spiritual world. Indeed, never was such a thing even imagined by the most
beautiful girls in the heavenly planets, whose bodily luster and aroma resemble the lotus flower.
Ansd what to speak of worldly women who are very beautiful according to material estimation?"*

   The gopés are again glorified in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.44.14):


gopyas tapaù kim acaran yad amuñya rüpaà. . .


   "What austerities must the gopés have performed! With their eyes they always drink the nectar
of Lord Kåñëa's form, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. That
lovliness is the only abode of beauty, fame, and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and extremely
rare."*

  This verse says: "The gopés gazed at Lord Kåñëa's form, which is not to be equaled or surpassed".
The gopés are again glorified in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.44.15):

yä dohane 'vahanane mathanopalepa. . .
   . . .dhanyä vraja-striya urukrama-citta-yänäù


   "The ladies of Vraja are the most fortunate of women because, with their minds fully attached to
Kåñëa and their throats always choked up with tears, they constantly sing about Him while milking
the cows, winnowing grain, churning butter, gathering cow dung for fuel, riding on swings, taking
care of their crying babies, sprinkling the ground with water, cleaning their houses, and so on. By
their exalted Kåñëa consciousness they automatically acquire all desirable things."***

   In this verse the word "urukrama-citta-yänäù" means "they whose chariot is the all-powerful
mind". This means that wherever their minds went, they, riding on the chariot of the mind, were
able to go." An alternate reading gives us {.sy 168}cinta-yänäù" instead of "citta-yänäù". The
meaning, however, remains the same. Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.44.15 was spoken by the women of
Mathurä City.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.279
records.text:
In this way the great glory of the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa is seen. Their love is gloriosu because
it is forbidden, because it is love for a paramour (parakéya). Even in ordinary affairs of the materuial
world, this kind of forbidden love is understood to be very intense. The author Bharata explains:


bahu väryate yataù khalu
   yatra pracchanna-kämukatvaà ca
yä ca mitho durlabhatä
   sä paramä manmathasya ratiù


   "The highest amorous pleasure is attained when love is forbidden, when the lovers must conceal
their love, when the lovers rarely meet."

   The author Rudra explains:


vämatä durlabhatvaà ca
   stréëäà ya ca niväraëä
tad eva païca-bäëasya
   manye paramam äyudham


  "Contrariness, difficulty of attainment, and rejection by women I consider Kämadeva's greatest
weapons."

   The author Viñëu-gupta explains:


yatra niñedha-viçeñaù
   su-durlabhatvaà ca yan mågäkñéëäm
tatraiva nägaräëäà
   nirbharam äsajjate hådayam


   "When love is forbidden and the doe-eyed beloved is difficult to attain, then the passionate
lover's heart becomes very attached to his beloved."

   Some gopé girls prayed to Goddess Katyayani that they might attain Lord Kåñëa as their
husband. Their desire to attain Him was very strong. Because Kåñëa was unattainable for them,
their love for Him was very great. The greatness oftheir love is described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.83.43):


vraja-striyo yad väïchanti. . .


   "We desire the same contact with the Supreme Lord's feet that thr young women of Vraja, the
cowherd boys, and even the aborigine Pulinda women desire-the touch of the dust He leaves on the
plants and grass as He tends His cows."***

   Their love is also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.58):


väïchanti yad bhava-bhiyaù. . .


   "Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have actually perfected their
embodied lives, for they have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Lord Govinda. Their
pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as
well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a
high-class brähmaëa, or even as Lord Barhmä himself?"***

   Still, the gs' intesne desire to attain Lord Kåñëa was not born merely because they were
forbidden to associate with Him. They certrainly did not wish to be forbidden or to have so many
obstacles placed befope them. Rather they loved Him in spite of being so strongly forbidden, This is
described in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.61):


yä dustyajam. . .

    "The gopés of Våndävana have given up the association of their husbands, sons, and other family
members, who are very difficult to give up, andf they have forsaken the path of chastity to take
shelter of tyhe lotus feet of Mukunda, Kåñëa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh,
let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers, or herbs in Våndävana, because the
gopés trample them and bless them with the dust of their feet."*

   As a wild elephant cannot be stopped, so the gopés' passionate love for Kåñëa could not be
stopped. Although the gopés were all forbidden in the smae way to associate with Lord Kåñëa, still
they each had a different intensity of love for Him. Of them all Rädhä had the greatest love. She
had the greatest power to bring Lord Kåñëa under Her control. The supremely exalted position of
Çré Rädhä's love is indirectly described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.28):


anayärädhito nünam. . .


   "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped the all-powerful Personality of Godhead,
Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a
secluded place."***

   In tyhis way the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa blossomed. It was as if they had been bitten by the
black snake of love for Kåñëa. They did not associate with Kåñëa as a wife associates with her
husband. Rather they passionately loved Kåñëa as a girl loves her paramour. This kind of love is
criticized in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.7-8):


niùsvaà tyajanti gaëikä. . .


   "Prostitutes abandon a penniless man."***


järä bhuktvä ratäà striyam


   "A lover abandons the woman he has enjoyed, even though she remains attached to him."***

   It is said that girls who love someone other than their husbands (parakéya) are fallen and worthy
of contempt. This is true for girls who take shelter of individual souls who live in the material
world. The situation of such girls is abominable. However these defects asnd criticisms do not apply
to the gopés. This truth is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.35):

gopénäà tat-paténäà ca. . .


   "He who lives as the overseeing witness within the gopés and their husbands, and indeed within

all embodied living beings, assumes forms in this world to enjoy transcendental pastimes."***

   From the material point of view it seemed that the gopés had husbands other than Kåñëa.
However, from the spiritual point of view these so-called husbands did not exist. In the Kåñëa-
sandarbha it has already been shown that the gopés' so-called husbands were in truth only a display
manifested from Lord Kåñëa's internal potency. Therefore it is Lord Kåñëa Himself who is
ultimately the gs only true husband. The gopés' exalted position, which has so equal or superior, is
described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.58):


etäù paraà tanu-bhåtaù. . .


   "Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have actually perfected their
embodied lives, for they have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Lord Govinda. Their
pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as
well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a
high-class brähmaëa, or even as Lord Barhmä himself?"***

   The gopés' glories are also described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi:


neñöä yad aìgini rase kavibhiù paroòhä
   tad gokulämbuja-dåçäà kulam antareëa
äçaàsayä rasa-vidher avatäritänäà
   kaàsäriëä rasika-maëòala-çekhareëa


   "Philosophers do not praise adultery. However, they do praise the pastimes Lord Kåñëa, the
crown of all rasikas, enjoys with Gokula's lotus-eyed girls, girls who descended to this world to enjoy
nectar pastimes with Him."

   The gopés did not have even a dim reflection of contact with their so-called husbands. This is
seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.37):


näsüyan khalu kåñëäya
   mohitäs tasya mäyayä
manyamänäù sva-pärçva-sthän
   svän svän därän vrajaukasaù


  "The cowherd men, bewildered by Kåñëa's illusory potency, thought their wives had remained
home at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against Him."***

   The gopés are eternally dear to Lord Kåñëa. They are His consorts eternally. This verse explains:

"The cowherd men, bewildered by Kåñëa's illusory potency, thought their wives had remained home
at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against Him."*** This verse was spoken
by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.280
records.text:
In this way it is seen that the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa is most exalted. The spiritual forms of
Lord Kåñëa and the gopés are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.43):


täbhiù sametäbhir udära-ceñöitaù. . .


   "Among the assembled gopés, the infallible Lord Kåñëa appeared just like the moon surrounded
by stars. He whose activifies are so magnanimous made their faces blossom with His affectionate
glances, and His broad smiles revealed the effulgence of His jasmine-bud-like teeth."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.281
records.text:
The spiritual forms of Lord Kåñëa and the gopés are again described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.33.6):


taträtiçuçubhe täbhir
   bhagavän devaké-sutaù
madhye maëénäà haimänäà
   mahä-marakato yathä


   "In the midst of the dancing gopés, Lord Kåñëa appeared most brilliant, like an exquisite sapphire
in the midst of golden ornaments."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.282
records.text:
The spiritural powers and glories and virtues of Lord Kåñëa and the gopés are described in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.32.10):

täbhir vidhüta-çokäbhir
   bhagavän acyuto våtah
vyarocatädhikaà täta
   puruñaù çaktibhir yatha


   "Encircled by the gopés, who were now relieved of all distress, Lord Acyuta, the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, shone forth splendidly. My dear King, Kåñëa thus appeared like the
Supersoul encircled by His spiritual potencies."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.283
records.text:
The transcendental artistic genius of Lord Kåñëa and the gopé is described in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.7-8):


päda-nyäsair bhuja-vidhutibhiù. . .


   "As the gopés sang in praise of Kåñëa, their feet danced, their hands gestured, and their eyebrows
moved with playful smiles. With their braids and belts tied tight, their waists bending, their faces
perspiring, the garments on their breasts moving this way and that, and their earrings swinging on
their cheeks, Lord Kåñëa's young consorts shone like streaks of lightning in a mass of clouds.***


uccair jagur nåtyamänä
   rakta-kaëöhyo rati-priyäù
kåñëäbhimarça-muditä
   yad-gétenedam ävrtam


  "Eager to enjoy conjugal love, their throats colored with various pigments, the gopés sang loudly
and danced. They were overjoyed by Kåñëa's touch, and they sang songs that filled the entire
universe."***

    In this verse the word "idam" (this) refers to the universe. This verse says that the gopés' songs
filled the entire universe. In the Saìgéta-sära itis said:


tävanta eva rägä syur
   yävatyo jéva-jätayaù
teñu ñoòaça-sähasré

   purä gopé-kåtä varä


   "The rägas number 16,000, as many as there are species of life. The gopés sang songs in all these
rägas."

  At the end of this book it is said that these rägas are seen in Svargaloka and the other higher
material planets.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.284
records.text:
The gopés' songs are also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.9):


käcit samaà mukundena
   svara jätér amiçritäù
unninye püjitä tena
   préyatä sädhu sädhv iti
tad eva dhruvam unninye
   tasyai mänaà ca bahv adät


   "One gopé, joining Lord Mukunda in His singing, sang pure melodious tones that rose
harmoniously above His. Kåñëa was pleased and showed great appreciation for her performance,
saying `Excellent! Excellent!' Then another gopé repeated the same melody, but in a special metrical
pattern, and Kåñëa praised her also."***

   In this verse the word "svaräù" means the scale of seven notes beginning with the sixth note",
and {.sy 168}jätayaù" means "the räga that comes from that scale". Here "amisritah" means that
because Kåñëa and the gopés were very expert, the melodies they sang did not become mixed. The
melodies remained pure, and "unninye" means "the melodies were gloriously sung". The gopés sang
together with Lord Kåñëa, Kåñëa whose melodies even Brahmä, Çiva, Indra and all the demigods
have no power to understand. The singing of Kåñëa and the gopés was equal. The singing of one did
not dominate the singing of the other. The words "püjitä tena" mean "with their treble voices the
gopés worshiped Lord Kåñëa". Here the word "dhruvam" means "a gopé sang a melody in the dhruva
rhythm, and "tasyai mänam adät" means "Lord Kåñëa praised her". This verse was spoken by Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 285 and 286


   Among the ordinary (sämänya) conjugal lovers of Lord Kåñëa, Kubjä is the most exalted. Among
the queens married (svakéya) to Lord Kåñëa, Çré Rukmiëé and Çré Satyabhämä are mosty exalted.

They are described in the following words of Hari-vaàça:


kuöumbasyeçvaré cäséd
   rukmiëé bhéñmakätmajä
satyabhämottamä stréëäà
   saubhägye cädhikäbhavat


  "Bhéñmaka's daughter, Rukmiëé, is the controller of Lord Kåñëa's household. Satyabhämä is the
most fortunate of Lord Kåñëa's wives."

  The most exalted of the goddesslike gopés of Vraja are described in these words of the Bhaviñya
Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa:


gopälé pälikä dhanyä
   viçäkhä dhyäna-niñöhikä
rädhänurädhä somäbhä
   tärakä daçamé tathä


  "The ten most prominent gopés are Gopälé, Pälikä, Dhanyä, Viçäkhä, Dhyäna-niñöhikä, Rädhä,
Anurädhä, Somäbhä, and Tärakä."

   Here the words "tärakä daçamé" mean "the tenth gopé is named Tärakä". In ther Skanda Purana,
Prahlada-samhita the four gopés Lalitä, Çaibyä, Padmä, and Bhadrä are included amongst the most
prominent gopés. In other places in the scriptures Candrävalé is also included amongst the
prominent gopés. The Somäbhä mentioned in the previous quote from the Bhaviñya Puräëa is the
same as Candrävalé. In the Agama-çästras it is said:


pramadä-çata-koöibhir äkulitaù


   "Lord Kåñëa is surrounded by hundreds and millions of beautiful gopés."

  Amongst all the gopés, Rädhä is the most important. It is because of her great love that Lord
Kåñëa disappeared from the räsa dance. This has already been described in the Çré Kåñëa-sandarbha
(Anuccheda 189). Rädhä is celebrated in all the scriptures. In the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad she is
known by the name Gändharvikä.

   Lord Kåñëa's beloveds are of three kinds: 1. mugdhä (meek), 2. madhyä (niteermediate), and 3.
pragalbhä (arrogant). They are also of three ages: 1. nava-yauavana (new youth), 2. spañöa (clearly
manifested youth), and 3. (samyag-yauvana (fully blossomed youth). According to these different
ages different kinds of activities are manifested. The age of samyag-yuavana is sixteen years. It is

not older than that. This is seeen in the following words of the Gautaméya Tantra:

kanyäbhir dvy-añöa-varñäbhiù


   "Lord Kåñëa is surrounded by sixteen-year-old gopés."

   The termperments of the Lord's beloveds are of three kinds: 1. dhérä (peaceful), 2. adhérä
(agitated), and 3. miçra-guëä (a mixture of peace and agitation). Their love for Lord Kåñëa they are
also of three kinds: 1. çreñöhä (best), 2. samä (intermediate), and 3. laghu (least).
   In their pastimes with Lord Kåñëa, His beloveds are in the following eight situations: 1.
abhisärikä (meeting Kåñëa ina rendezvous), 2. väsaka-sajjä (dressing in fine garments and
ornaments to prepare for a rendezvous with Kåñëa), 3. utkaëöhitä (yearning to meet Kåñëa at the
rendezvous), 4. khaëòitä (jilted by Kåñëa), 5. vipralabdhä (separated from Kåñëa), 6. kalahäntaritä
(feuding with Kåñëa), 7. proñita-preyasé (separated from Kåñëa because He has gone to a faraway
place), and 8. svädhéna-bhartåkä (dominating Kåñëa). In their realtions with each other, Lord
Kåñëa's beloveds have four kinds of natures: 1. sädåçya (alike), kiïcit-sädåçya (somewhat alike), 3.
aspañöa-sädåçya (not clearly alike), and 4. virodhi (opposed). These four natures are manifest as the
following four kinds of relationships: 1. sakhé (friend), 2. suhåt (well-wisher), 3. taöasthä (neutral
person), and prätipakñiké (rival). In this way the Lord's beloveds have different natures. A sakhé
spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.1):


apy eëa-patné. . .tanvan dåçäà sakhi su-nirvåtim


   "O friend, wife of the deer, has Lord Acyuta been here with His beloved, bringing great joy to
your eyes? Indeed, blowing this way is the fragrance of His garland of kunòa flowers, which was
smeared with the kuìkuma from the breasts of His girlfriend when He embraced Her."***

   Here the words "tanvan dåçäà sakhi su-nirvåtim" (O friend, has Lord Acyuta been here with His
beloved, bringing great joy to your eyes?) were spoken by the gopés because they yearned to see Lord
Kåñëa. Here the word "sakhi" (O friend) shows that the gopés imagined the deer to be like them,
delighted by the sight of Lord Kåñëa. In this way they imagined that the deer were their friends.
Here the word "käntä" means "the great good fortune of Lord Kåñëa's girlfriend", "kula-pateù" means
"of Lord Kåñëa", and "käntäìga-saìge" means "delighted by the fragrance of the two lovers'
embraces". The pleasures Rädhä and Kåñëa enjoy in Their pastimes are described in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.12):


bähuà priyäàsa. . .


     "O trees, we see that you are bowing down. When the younger brother of Räma walked by here,
followed by intoxicated bees swarming around the tulasé maïjarés decorating His garland, did He
acknowledge your obeisances with His affectionate glances? He must have been resting His arm on

the shoulder of His beloved and carrying a lotus flower in His free hand."***

   A suhåt (well-wisher) spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.28):


anayärädhito nünaà
   bhagavan harir isvaraù
yan no vihäya govindaù
   préto yäm amayad rahaù


   "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped the all-powerful Personality of Godhead,
Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a
secluded place."***

  Because she praises Çré Rädhä's good fortune, the gopé who speak this verse is a suhåt. After
hearing a sakhé speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.11, a The taöasthä (neutral person) spoke these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.13):


påcchatemä latä bähün
   apy äçliñöä vanaspateù
nünaà tat-karaja-spåñöä
   bibhraty utpulakäny aho


   "Let us ask these creepers about Kåñëa. Even though they are embracing the arms of their
husband, this tree, they certainly must have been touched by Kåñëa's fingernails, since out of joy
they are manifesting eruptions on their skin."***

  After hearing a suhåt speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.28, a taöasthä spoke these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.30.29):


dhanyä aho amé alyaù. . .


  "O girls! The dust of Govinda's lotus feet is so sacred that even Brahmä, Çiva and the goddess
Ramä take that dust upon their heads to dispel sinful reactions."***

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.287
records.text:
A prätipakñiké (rival) spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.30):

tasyä amüni naù kñobham-
   kurvanty uccaiù padäni yat
yaikäpahåtya gopénäà
   raho bhuìkte 'cyutädharam


   "These footprints of that special gopé greatly disturb us. Of all the gopés, She alone was taken
away to a secluded place, where She is enjoying the lips of Kåñëa."***
   The gopé who spoke this verse clearly displayed her envy of the gopé taken away by Lord Kåñëa.
In the pastime of capturing the pärijäta-tree, a pastime described in the Hari-vaàça and other
scriptures, Satyabhämä envied Çré Rukmiëé in the same way the gopé who spoke Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.30.30 envied the gopé taken away by Lord Kåñëa. The meaning of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.288
records.text:
Here someone may protest: "It is not possible that the devotees of the Lord can be rivals of each
other. That is a horrible idea. It is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.48):


täsäà tat-saubhaga-madam. . .


   " `Lord Keçava, seeing the gopés too proud of their good fortune, wanted to relieve them of this
pride and show them further mercy. Thus He immediately disappeared.'***

   "In this way it is seen that the Supreme Personality of Godhead wishes to cast far away all envy,
lust, and pride. Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé here uses the word `daurätmya' (wickedness) to describe
those vices."

   To this protest I reply: If sometimes the Lord's devotees are rivals of each other that is only to
nourish their love for the Lord and to nourish the Lord's pastimes. The Lord reveals His pastimes so
the souls may attain love for Him. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.36):


bhajate tädåçéù kréòä
  yäù çrutva tat-paro bhavet


   "When the Lord assumes a humanlike body to show mercy to His devotees, He engages in such
pastimes as will attract those who hear about them to become dedicated to Him."***

   Indeed, in çåìgära-rasa (the mellow of conjugal love), the rasa is noursihed by a wonderful
display of spiritual envy, lust, and pride. This truth is confirmed by the great philosophers. The
Supreme Lord personally accepts it in His pastimes. As the hero loved by His beloveds, the Supreme
Lord manifests four features: 1. dakñiëa (pleasing), 2. anuküla (a faithful lover), 3. çaöha (a cheat),
