the moment of Your birth there, Nanda's land of Vraja has been a place of pastimes for Goddess
Lakñmé. To attain the dust of your feet Goddess Tulasé always resides in Våndävana forest."
Someone may ask: "Why do Lakñmé and Tulasé yearn to attain the dust of Lord Kåñëa's feet?" The
answer is given here in the words "bhåtya-juñöam" (served by His servants). It is natural for a
maidservant to place her master's feet on her head. Someone may ask: {.sy 168}What are the glories
of Goddess Lakñmé?" The answer is given here in the words "yasyäù sva-vékñaëa utänya-sura-
prayäsaù", which mean: "the gloruy of Goddess Lakñmé is such that the other divine beings who are
her associates yearn to attain her glance." Their voices choked with emotion, the gopés then say the
words "vayaà ca", which menas "we are like them". Thrse words mean: "As Lakñmé and Tulasé are
enchanted by You, we are also enchanted by You. That is why we have now approached the dust of
Your feet. It is not otherwise." Then the gopés speak the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.38):

tan naù. . .


   "Therefore, O vanquisher of all distress, please show us mercy. To approach Your lotus feet we
abandoned our families and homes, and we have no desire other than to serve You. Our hearts are
burning with intense desires generated by Your beautiful smiling glances. O jewel among men,
please make us Your maidservants."***

   In this verse the word "vrjinardana" mreans {.sy 168}O Lord who removes all distress", and "nah
prasida" means "please be merciful to us and remove the obstacles that keep us from seeing You".
Here Lord Kåñëa may ask: {.sy 168}Did you gopés really come here only to touch My feet?" To this
question the gopés reply with the words: "We left our homes not only to touch Your feet, but
because we yearn to worship You. We did not come here to see Våndävana forest in the moonlight."
Then the gopés also say: "Our hearts are burning with intense desires generated by Your beautiful
smiling glances. Please make us Your maidservants." Because the idea of a gift here is not very
explicit, the word "ätmanäm" is in the genitive case, not the dative case. From this is may be
understood that this gift of devotional service is not always given, even in Gokula. The word
"puruña-bhüñaëa" (O ornament among men", which is in the vocative case, has a double meaning. It
may also mean: "O Lord who have become the ornament of You boyfriends in Gokula". This
interpretation implies: "Therefore You are never the ornament of Gokula's beautiful girls." Their
hearts burning, the gopés think all these thoughts. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.21 Lord Kåñëa
ignored the uddépanas that attracted the gs to Him. Then, in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.27, Lord
Kåñëa revealed the great power of His own attractive handsomeness. Thinking of these statements
of Lord Kåñëa, the gopés spoke the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.39):


vékñya. . .


   "Seeing Your face encircled by curling locks of hair, Your cheeks beautified by earrings, Your lips
full of nectar, and Your smiling glance, and also seeing Your two imposing arms, which take away
our fear, and Your chest, which is the only source of pleasure for the goddess of fortune, we must
become Your maidservants."***

   The word "ca" (and) spoken near the end of this verse by voices choked with emotion, refers to
the words that precede it. Here the gopés say: "Seeing You, we must become Your maidservants. It is
not otherwise." Here Lord Kåñëa may ask: "If You are so dedicated to Me, why do you not stay here
every night?" Thinking Lord Kåñëa may ask this question, the gopés speak the next verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.29.40):


kä stry aìga te. . .


   "Dear Kåñëa, what woman in all the three worlds wouldn't deviate from religious behavior when

bewildered by the sweet, drawn-out melody of Your flute? Your beauty makes all three worlds
auspicious. Indeed, even the cows, birds, trees and deer manifest the ecstatic symptom of bodily hair
standing on end when they see Your beautiful form."***

   This verse means: "O beloved (aìga) who sweetly plays on the flute (kala-padäyata-veëu-géta)
and who is enchanting (sammohita) with the arrows shot by Kämadeva, what woman in all the
three worlds wouldn't deviate from religious behavior for Your sake? For Your sake we throw far
away all vows of pious morality." If someone were to try to find fault in the qualities of the Lord
described in the two vocative words (kala-padäyata-veëu-géta and sammohita) mentioued above,
the gopés reply by speaking the word "trailokya-saubhagam" (who makes all three worlds auspicious).
The reason for the gopés deviating from religious behavior is given here in the words "ärya-caritän
nirékñya rüpaà kä na calet" (upon seeing Your handsome form, what woman would not deviate
from religious behavior?). The gopés then say: "Therefore (yat) even the cows, birds, trees and deer
manifest the ecstatic symptom of bodily hair standing on end when they see Your beautiful form."
Because they may thus easily deviate from the principles ofreligious behavior, beautiful girls and
handsome are forbidden to associate in this way in this world. Thinking of the words Lord Kåñëa
spoke in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.19, and thinking that in the context of those words Lord Kåñëa
might say: {.sy 168}I am a powerful hero. Stay with Me I I will protect You from all dangers", the
gopés offer a prayer in the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.41):


vyaktaà bhavän. . .


   "Clearly You have taken birth in this world to relieve the fear and distress of the people of Vraja,
just as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the primeval Lord, protects the domain of the
demigods. Therefore, O friend of the distressed, kindly place Your lotus hand on Your
maidservants' heads and burning breasts."***

    In this verse the word "arta-bandho" means {.sy 168}O You who have taken birth in this world to
protect the people of Vraja from the fearful condition of falling away from the principles of
religion". Here the words {.sy 168}kiìkaréëäà tapta-staneñu kara-paìkajaà ca çiraùsu no nidhehi"
have a hidden possible second interpretation, which gives this meaning of the words: "Please doi
not place Your lotus hand on Your maidservants' heads and breasts, breasts burning with desire
from the sight of You". These words thus imply: "Evenb in Your thoughts do not do such a thing to
saintly chaste girls like ourselves." This hidden meaning is hinted in this verse. Quoting the dharma-
çästras, Lord Kåñëa had previously proved that ther gopés should always faithfully serve their
husbands and relatives. Quoting the jïäna-çästras, the gopés now brilliantly refute Kåñëa's
arguments. The gopés here prove that Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead (paramätmä),
and therefore He is the meaning and the goal of all the scrptures' teachings. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.29.32 the gopés hint: "O Kåñëa, You are the meaning and goal of all the scriptures' teachings.
Devotional service to You is the final goal taught in the scriptures." Here Lord Kåñëa may protest:
{.sy 168}How is it possible that I am the goal of all the scriptures?" To this the gopés reply (in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.29.32) by speaking the word "ätmä", which means: "You are the Supreme Personality

of Godhead." The gopés hint here: {.sy 168}You are the goal of all the scriptures, the scriptures that
affirm (Båhad-äraëyaka Upaniñad 4.4.22):


tam etaà vedänuvacanena brähmaëä vividiñanti


   "By studying the Vedas the brähmaëas understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead."

   Then Kåñëa may again protest: "How is it possible that I am the Supreme Personality of
Godhead?" To this protest the gopés reply with the words "tanu-bhåtäà preñöhaù", which mean "for
the living entities You are the object of love without limit". Here the gopés also say: "bandhur
bhavän", which means "You bring limitless auspiciousness to the living entities". In these two ways
Lord Kåñëa possesses the symptoms of being the Supreme Personality of Godhead, symptoms
described in these words of the jïäna-çästras (Båhad-äraëyaka Upaniñad 2.4.5):


ätmanas tu kämäya sarvaà priyaà bhavati


   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead is loved by everyone. He fulfills everyone's desire."

   Here the gopés may say: "In this way we have proved that You are indeed the Supreme
Personality of Godhead. Because You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead we are very eager to
worship and serve You." It is said in Muëòaka Upaniñad (1.2.12):


brähmaëo nirvedam äyät, nästy akåtaù kåtena


  "Not merely by performing duties, but by renunciation a brähmaëa attains the company of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead."

   In this way the jnana-sastras affirmt hat it is not wrong for a transcendentalist to renounce his
prescribed duties. However, because knowledge of Lordf Kåñëa's sweetness (mädhurya) is superior
to knowledge of His power and opulence (aiçvarya), the gopés do not dwell on Lord Kåñëa's status as
the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.33 the gopés describe the
activities of true saintly persons. There the word "kuçaläù" means "saintly persons who know what is
important and what is not important, and "hi" means "certainly". Here "sva ätman" means "the
Supreme Personality of Godhead", as has previously been explained. Or the words "sva ätman nitya-
priye tvayi" may also mean "You are eternally dear to every soul". Then the gopés say: "tvayy eva
ratià kurvanti", which means "therefore saintly persons love You alone. They do not love the
principles of religion, their homes, or anything else." Then the gopés say: "paty-ädibhiù kim", which
means {.sy 168}What use do we have for our husbandsand relatives?" These truths the gopés futher
explain in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.36 and 37. In this way the samläpa-anubhäva (conversation),
which is one of the väcika-anubhävas (anubhavas of speech) has been described. These verses of

Çrémad-Bhägavatam were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 333 and 334


  Sandeça is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Anubhäva-prakaraëa, Text 82:

Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.40.52):


sandeças tu proñitasya
   sva-värtä-preñaëaà bhavet


  "A letter from a lopver living far away is called sandeça."

  Sandeça is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.52):


he nätha he ramä-nätha
   vraja-näthärti-näçana
magnam uddhara govinda
   gokulaà våjinärëavät


  "O master, O master of the goddess of fortune, O master of Vraja! O destroyer of all suffering,
Govinda, please lift Your Gokula out of the ocean of distress in which it is drowning!"***

  Apadeça is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Anubhäva-prakaraëa, Text 85:


anyärtha-kathanaà yat tu
  so 'padeça itéritaù


  "When a person misunderstands the statement of another, this is called apadeça."

  Apadeça is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.7-8):


niùsvaà tyajanti gaëikä. . .jarä bhuktvä ratäà striyam


   "Prostitutes abandon a penniless man, subjects and incompetent king, students their teacher
once they have finished their education, and priests a man who has remunerated them for a
sacrifice.***

   "Birds abandon a tree when its fruits are gone, guests a house after they have eaten, animals a
forest that has burnt down, and a lover the woman he has enjoyed, even though she remains
attached to him."***

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by the gopés to Uddhava.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.335
records.text:
Upadeça is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Anubhäva-prakaraëa, Text 87:


yat tu çikñärtha-vacanam
   upadeça sa ucyate


   "Words of instruction are called upadeça."

   Upadeça is seen in these words spoken at the time of Lord Balaräma's arrival in vraja and
recounted in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.65.14):


kià nas tat-kathayä gopyaù
   kathäù kathayatäparäù
yäty asmäbhir vinä kälo
   yadi tasya tathaiva naù


   "Why bother talking about Him, dear gopés? Please talk of something else. If He passes His time
without us, then we shall similarly pass ours without Him."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.336
records.text:
Vyapadeça is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Anubhäva-prakaraëa, Text 90:


vyäjenätmäbhiläñoktir
   vyapadeça itéryate


   "When the speaker uses a trick to reveal his actual desire, his statement is called vyapadeça."

  Vyapadeça is seen in these owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.12):


kåñëaà nirékñya. . .
. . .devyo vimäna-gatayaù smara-nunna-särä. . .


    "Kåñëa's beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods' wives
flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of Him and hear His resonant flute-song, their
hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair
and their belts loosen."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.337
records.text:
The five anubhävas named praläpa, anuläpa, apaläpa, atideça, and nirdeça are also included
among the väcica-anubhävas. Thus concludes the description of the anubhävas. Now the
vyabhicärés will be considered. Amongst them nirveda (despair) is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.47.15):


caraëa-raja upäste yasya bhütir vayaà kä


   "In heaven, on earth, or in the subterranean sphere, what woman is unavailable to Him? He
simply arches His eyebrows and smiles with deceptive charm, and they all become His. The supreme
goddess herself worships the dust of His feet, so what is our position in comparison? But at least
those who are wretched can chant His name, Uttamaùsloka."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.338
records.text:
Anutäpa is lamentation. Anutäpa is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.7):


akñaëvatäà phalam idam. . .


   "O friends, those eyes that see the beautiful faces of the sons of Mahäräja Nanda are certainly
fortunate. As these two sons enter the forest, surrounded by Their friends, driving the cows before
Them, They hold Their flutes to Their mouths and glance lovingly upon the residents of

Våndävana. For those who have eyes, we think there is no greater object of vision."***

   Dainya is helpless despair. Dainya is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.38):


tan naù praséda våjinärdana. . .


   "Therefore, O vanquisher of all distress, please show us mercy. To approach Your lotus feet we
abandoned our families and homes, and we have no desire other than to serve You. Our hearts are
burning with intense desires generated by Your beautiful smiling glances. O jewel among men,
please make us Your maidservants."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.339
records.text:
Gläni (exhaustion) is described in these words of Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu (2.4.26):


glänir niñpräëatä matä


   "Gläni is when one is breathless with exhaustion."

   Gläni is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.10):


käcid räsa-pariçräntä. . .


   "When one gopé grew tired from the räsa dance, She turned to Kåñëa, standing at Her side
holding a baton, and grasped His shoulder with Her arm. The dancing had loosened Her bracelets
and the flowers in Her hair."***

   Çrama (fatigue) is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.20):


täsäà rati-vihäreëa. . .


   "Seeing that the gopés were fatigued from conjugal enjoyment, my dear King, merciful Kåñëa
lovingly wiped their faces with His comforting hand."***

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.340
records.text:
Mada is becoming so wild with joy that one is bereft of discrimination. Mada is seen in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.17):


tad-aìga-saìga-pramudäkulendriyäù. . .


   "Their senses overwhelmed by the joy of having His physical association, the gopés could not
prevent their hair, their dresses and the cloths covering their breasts from becoming disheveled.
Their garlands and ornaments scattered, O hero of the Kuru dynasty."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.341
records.text:
Garva is contemptuous arrogance. Garva is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.60.44):


tasyäù syur acyuta nåpä bhavatopadiñöäù. . .


   "O infallible Kåñëa, let each of the kings You named become the husband of a woman whose ears
have never heard Your glories, which are sung in the assemblies of Çiva and Brahmä. After all, in
the households of such women these kings live like asses, oxen, dogs, cats, and slaves."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Queen Rukmiëé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.342
records.text:
Çaìkä is worry that a calamity will befall one. Träsa is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.53.24):


api mayy anavadyätmä
   dåñövä kiïcij jugupsitam


  "Perhaps the faultless Lord, even while preparing to come here, saw something contemptible in
me and therefore has not come to take my hand."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Queen Rukmiëé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.343
records.text:
Träsa is a heart shaken by fear. Träsa is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.34.27):


kroçantaà kåñëa rämeti
   vilokya sva-parigraham


   "Hearing Their devotees crying out `Kåñëa! Räma!, and seeing that they were just like cows being
stolen by a thief, Kåñëa and Balaräma began to run afterthe demon."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.344
records.text:
Avega is haste created by agitation of the heart. Avega is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.29.5):


duhantyo 'bhiyayuù käçcid. . .


  "Some of the gopés were milking cows when they heard Kåñëa's flute. They stopped milking and
went off to meet Him. Some left milk curdling on the stove, and others left cakes burning in the
oven."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.345
records.text:
Unmäda is bewilderment of the heart. Unmäda is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.30.4):


gäyantya uccair amum eva saàhatä. . .


   "Singing loudly of Kåñëa, they searched for Him throughout the Våndävana forest like a band of
madwomen. They even asked the trees about Him, who as the Supersoul is present inside and
outside of all created things, just like the sky."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 346 and 347


  Apasmära is being overwhelmed at heart. Apasmära is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.46.5):


mayi täù preyasäà preñöhe
  düra-sthe gokula-striyaù
smarantyo 'ìga vimuhyanti
  virahautkaëöhya-vihvaläù


   "My dear Uddhava, for those women of Gokula I am the most cherished object of love. Thus
when they remember Me, who am so far away, they are overwhelmed by the anxiety of
separation."***

   Vyädhi (disease) is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.6):


dhärayanty ati-kåcchreëa
  präyaù präëän kathaïcana


   "Simply because I have promised to return to them, My fully devoted cowherd girlfiends struggle
to maintain their lives somehow or other."***

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead to Uddhava.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.348
records.text:
Moha is being charmed at heart. Moha is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.16-
17):


nija-padäbja-dalaiù. . .kuja-gatià gamitäù. . .


   "As Kåñëa strolls through Vraja with His lotus-petal-like feet, marking the ground with the
distinctive embIems of flag, thunderbolt, lotus and elephant goad, He relieves the distress the
ground feels from the cows' hooves. As He plays His renowned flute, His body moves with the grace

of an elephant. Thus we gopés, who become agitated by Cupid when Kåñëa playfully glances at us,
stand as still as trees, unaware that our hair and garments are slackening."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.349
records.text:
Måti is leaving the body. In this situation a devotee not situated in a spiritual body attains, at the
moment of death, ecstatic love for Lord Kåñëa. Måti is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.29.9-11):


antar-gåha-gatäù käçcit. . .


   "Some of the gopés, however, could not manage to get out of their houses, and instead they
remained home with eyes closed, meditating upon Him in pure love.***
  For those gopés who could not go to see Kåñëa, intolerable separation from their beloved caused an
intense agony that burned away all impious karma. By meditating upon Him they realized His
embrace, and the ecstasy they then felt exhausted their material piety. Although Lord Kåñëa is the
Supreme Soul, these girls simply thought of Him as their male lover and associated with Him in
that intimate mood. Thus their karmic bondage was nullified and they abandoned their gross
material bodies."***

   Måti was also discussed previously in Kåñëa-sandarbha (Anuccheda 177). Languor is described in
these words:


anyatra kåñëa-kåtyebhyo
   balinaù kleça-çaìkayä
älasyam acikérñäyäà
   kåtrimaà teñu ujjvale


   "When faced with Lord Kåñëa's actions, the devotees in çåìgära-rasa sometimes manifest languor
born from agitation. Sometimes the languor is only a pretense."

   Languor caused by agitation that has its origin in Lord Kåñëa's actions is seen in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.17):


tad-aìga. . .keçän dukülaà kuca-paööikäà vä
   näïjaù prativyoòhum alaà vraja-striyaù

   "Their senses overwhelmed by the joy of having His physical association, the gopés could not
prevent their hair, their dresses and the cloths covering their breasts from becoming disheveled.
Their garlands and ornaments scattered, O hero of the Kuru dynasty."***

  In this verse the word "aïjaù" shows that the gopés became powerless because they were
overwhelmed with joy. In situations like this there may be agitation. This verse was spoken by Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.350
records.text:
In the course of enjoying srngara-rasa pastimes with Lord Kåñëa the devotee may sometimes only
pretend to be laguid. An example of this is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.30.37):


na päraye 'haà calitum. . .


   "As the two lovers passed through one part of the Våndävana forest, the special gopé began
feeling proud of Herself. She told Lord Keçava, ``I cannot walk any further. Please carry Me
wherever You want to go."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çré Rädhä.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.351
records.text:
Jäòya means "becoming stunned and not knowing what to do". It is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.53.31):


tam ägataà samäjïäya
   vaidarbhé håñöa-mänasä
na paçyanté brähmaëäya
   priyam anyän nanäma sä


   "Princess Vaidarbhé was overjoyed to learn of Kåñëa's arrival. Not finding at hand anything
suitable to offer the brähmaëa, she simply bowed down to him."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.352
records.text:
"Vréòä" means "snyness". Vréòä is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.54.4):


patyur balaà çaräsärais
   channaà vékñya su-madhyamä
sa-vréòam aikñat tad-vaktraà
   bhaya-vihvala-locanä


  "Slender-waisted Rumiëé, seeing her Lord's army covered by torrents of arrows, shyly looked at
His face with fear-stricken eyes."***

  The shyness here is mixed with love. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.353
records.text:
"Avahitthä" means "concealing one's true feelings". Avahitthä is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.32.15):


sabhäjayitvä tam anaìga-dépanam. . .


   "Çré Kåñëa had awakened romantic desires within the gopés, and they honored Him by glancing
at Him with playful smiles, gesturing amorously with their eyebrows, and massaging His hands and
feet as they held them in their laps. Even while worshiping Him, however, they felt somewhat
angry, and thus they addressed Him as follows."***

   By worshiping Him and serving Him the gopés concealed the anger they felt toward Him. This
verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.354
records.text:
"Småti" means "remembering past events". Småti is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.47.43):


täù kià niçäù smarati yäsu tadä priyäbhir
   våndävane kumuda-kunda-çaçäìka-ramye. . .


  "Does He recall those nights in the Våndävana forest, lovely with lotus, jasmine, and the bright

moon? As we glorified His charmign pastimes, He enjoyed with us, His beloved girlfriends, in the
circle of the räsa dance, which resounded with the music of ankle bells."***

   "Uha" means "mental speculation". Uha is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.31):


na lakñyante padäny atra. . .


   "These footprints of that special gopé greatly disturb us. Of all the gopés, She alone was taken
away to a secluded place, where She is enjoying the lips of Kåñëa. Look, we can't see Her footprints
over here! It's obvious that the grass and sprouts were hurting the tender soles of Her feet, and so
the lover lifted up His beloved."***

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.355
records.text:
"Dhyäna" means "meditation". Dhyäna is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.29):


kåtvä mukhäny ava çucaù. . .


   "Their heads hanging down and their heavy, sorrowful breathing drying up their reddened lips,
the gopés scratched the ground with their toes. Tears flowed from their eyes, carrying their kajjala
and washing away the vermilion smeared on their breasts. Thus they stood, silently bearing the
burden of their unhappiness."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.356
records.text:
"Mati" means "understanding the truth". Mati is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.60.39):


tvaà nyasta-daëòa-munibhir gaditänubhäva
   ätmätma-daç ca jagatäm iti me våto 'si


  "Knowing that great sages who have renounced the sannyäsé's daëòa proclaim Your glories, that
You are the Supreme Soul of all the worlds, and that You are so gracious that You give away even

Your own self, I chose You as my husband, rejecting Lord Brahmä. Lord Çiva, and the rulers of
heaven, whose aspirations are all frustrated by the force of time, which is born from Your eyebrows.
What interest, thene, could I have in any other suitors?"***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çré Rukmiëé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.357
records.text:
"Autsukya means "being impatient for the arrival of the appropriate time". Autsukya is seen in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.4):


niçamya gétaà tad anaìga-vardhanam. . .


   "When the young women of Våndävana heard Kåñëa's flute song, which arouses romantic
feelings, their minds were captivated by the Lord. They went to where their lover waited, each
unknown to the others, moving so quickly that their earrings swung back and forth."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.358
records.text:
"Augrya" means "anger". Augrya is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.39.21):


krüras tvam akrüra. . .


   "O Providence, though you come here with the name Akrüra, you are indeed cruel, for like a fool
you are taking away what you once gave us-those eyes with which we have seen, even in one feature
of Lord Madhudviña's form, the perfection of your entire creation."***

   Augrya is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.15):


dehi väsäàsi dharma-jïa
  no ced räjïe bruväma he


   "O Çyämasundara, we are Your maidservants and must do whatever You say. But give us back our
clothing. You know what the religious principles are, and if You don't give us our clothes we will
have to tell the king."***

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by the girls of Vraja.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.359
records.text:
"Amarña" means "impatience". Amarña is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.31.16):


pati-sutänvaya. . .kitava yoñitaù kas tyajen niçi


   "Dear Acyuta, You know very well why we have come here. Who but a cheater like You would
abandon young women who come to see Him in the middle of the night, enchanted by the loud
song of His flute? Just to see You, we have completely rejected our husbands, children, ancestors,
brothers and other relatives."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.360
records.text:
"Asüyä" means "envy, or hating someone because of that person's good fortune". Asüyä is seen in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.30):


tasyä amüni naù kñobham. . .


   "These footprints of that special gopé greatly disturb us. Of all the gopés, She alone was taken
away to a secluded place, where She is enjoying the lips of Kåñëa. Look, we can't see Her footprints
over here! It's obvious that the grass and sprouts were hurting the tender soles of Her feet, and so
the lover lifted up His beloved."***

   "Cäpala" means "restlessness of the mind". Cäpala is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.52.41):


çvo bhävini tvam ajitodvahane. . .mäà räkñasena vidhinodvaha vérya-çulkam


   "O unconquerable one, tomorrow when my marriage ceremony is about to begin, You should
arrive unseen in Vidarbha and surround Yourself with the leaders of Your army. Then crush the
forces of Caidya and Mägadhendra and marry me in the räkñasa style, winning me with Your
valor."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Princess Rukmiëé.


Anucchedas 261 and 362


   "Nidrä" means "closing the eyes and becoming rapt in thought". Nidrä is seen in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.53.26):


evaà cintayaté bäla
   govinda-håta-mänasä
nyamélayata käla-jïä
   netre cäçru-kuläkule


   "As she thought in this way, ther young maiden, whsoe mind had been stolen by Kåñëa, closed
her tear-filled eyes, remembering that there was still time."***

   "Nidrä" also means "sleep". Interpreted in this way, Rukmiëé's condition is like that of a person
who awakens at dawn. In this way nidrä is included among the 33 vyabhicärés. In the next verse
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.53.27) it is said:


evaà vadhväù pratékñantyä
   govindägamanaà nåpa
väma ürur bhujo netram
   asphuran priya-bhäñiëaù


  "O king, as the bride thus awaited the arrival of Govinda, she felt a twitch in her left thigh, arm,
and eye. This was a sign that something desirable would happen."***

   Trembling in this way, Rukmiëé acted as if awakening from sleep. These verses were spoken by
Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 363 and 364


   The sthäyi-bhäva in çåìgära-rasa is thinking of Lord Kåñëa as the beloved. This sthäyi-bhäva has
two causes: 1. Lord Kåñëa's nature, and 2. the nature of the girl who loves Him. The first of these
causes is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.42):


kanyäà çrayeta tava päda-saroja-gandham äghräya

   "The aroma of Your lotus feet, which is glorified by great saints, awards people liberation and is
the abode of Goddess Lakñmé. What woman would take shelter of any other man after savoring that
aroma? Since You are the abode of transcendental qualities, what mortal woman with the insight to
distinguish her own true interest would disregard that fragrance and depend instead on someone
who is always subject to terrible fear?"***

  The second of these causes is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.47 and 48):


naivalékam ahaà manye
   vacas te madhusüdana
ambäyä eva hi präyaù
   kanyäyäù syäd ratiù kvacit


   "Actually, I don't consider Your words false, Madhusüdana. Quite often an unmarried girl is
attracted to a man, as in the case of Ambä.***


vyüòhäyäç cäpi puàçcalyä
  mano 'bhyeti navaà navam


  "The mind of a promiscuous woman always hankers for new lovers, even if she is married."***

   Queen Rukmiëé spoke these words in reply to this joking suggestion spoken by Lord Kåñëa
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.17):


athätmano 'nurüpam. . .


  "Now you should definitely accept a more suitable husband, a first-class man of the royal order
who can help you achieve everything you want, both in this life and the next."***

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.47 means: "I don't consider Your words false. Quite often an
unmarried girl is attracted to a certain man, as in the case of Ambä, who was attracted to Çälva."
When an unmarried girl is attracted in this way, she cannot be restrained. The verse and the next
verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.48) affirm: "An unmarried girl is attracted to only one man. In this
way she is chaste. The example of Ambä is given here. However, a promiscuous woman always seeks
newer and newer lovers. Therefore a supremely chaste and saintly woman will be attracted only to
You." These verses were spoken by Çré Rukmiëé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.365
records.text:
Sthäyi-bhäva in çëågära-rasa is of two kinds: 1. säkñäd-upabhogätmaka (directly enjoying
amorous pastimes with Lord Kåñëa), and 2. tad-anumodanätmaka (being pleased that some other
girl is enjoying amorous pastimes with Lord Kåñëa). The first of these is enjoyed by the girls (säkñän-
näyikä) who directly enjoy amorous pastimes with Lord Kåñëa, and the second of these is enjoyed
by the girls who are the friends (sakhé) of these girls. Both kinds of girls will be described here. The
girls who directly enjoy amorous pastimes with Lord Kåñëa are described in a general way in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.12): .


kåñëaà nirékñya vanitotsava-rüpa-çélam. . .


    "Kåñëa's beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods' wives
flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of Him and hear His resonant flute-song, their
hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair
and their belts loosen."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.366
records.text:
The desire to enjoy amorous pastimes directly with Lord Kåñëa is manifested in the gurl Kubjä
and in other girls like here. This desire is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.48.9):


sahoñyatäm iha preñöha. . .


   "O beloved, please stay here with me for a few days more and enjoy. I cannot give up Your
association, O lotus-eyed one."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Kubjä.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.367
records.text:
The desire to enjoy amorous pastimes with Lord Kåñëa is also seen in the Lord's queens. This is
seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.61.4):


smäyävaloka-lava-darçita. . .

   "The arched eyeborws of these sixteen-thousand queens enchantingly expressed those ladies'
secret intentions through coyly smiling sidelong glances. Thus their eyebrows boldly sent forth
conjugal messages. Yet even with these arrows of Cupid, and with other means as well, they could
not agitate Lord Kåñëa's senses."***

   The desire to enjoy amorous pastimes directly with Lord Kåñëa is also seen amongst the gopés, as
described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.31.19):


yat te sujäta-caraëämburuham. . .


   "O dearly beloved! Your lotus feet are so soft that we place them gently on our breasts, fearing
that Your feet will be hurt. Our life rests only in You. Our minds, therefore, are filled with anxiety
that Your tender feet might be wounded by pebbles as You roam about on the forest path."*

   This kind of amorous desire is natural for the gopés. When Lord Kåñëa left them, the gopés
became very angry. This anger is not a fault on their part. They were unable to tolerate Lord
Kåñëa's absence. This anger of the gopés is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.17):

mågayur iva kapéndram. . .dustyajas tat-kathärthaù


   "Like a hunter He cruelly shot the king of the monkeys with arrows. Because He was conquered
by a woman, He disfigured another woman who came to Him with lusty desires. And even after
consuming the gifts of Bali Mahäräja, He bound him up with ropes as if he were a crow. So let us
give up all frindship with this dark-compexioned boy, even if we can't give up talking about
Him."***

   Among the gopés there are many different kinds of amorous love for Lord Kåñëa. For some gopés
their relationship with Lord Kåñëa is that of two lovers' mutual adoration. These gopés think, "O
Kåñëa, I am Yours." They possess a abundance of qualities like submissiveness, humbleness, speaking
sweet words, and politeness. Other gopés have a different mood. These gopés think, "Kåñëa is mine".
They possess an abundance of qualities like independence, knowing Kåñëa's heart, joking with
Kåñëa, and dealing with Kåñëa in a crooked way. These different qualities are manifested in
different ways. Sometimes these qualities in a large degree, in a lesser degree, or mixed with other
qualities. In this way there are many different ways these qualities may be manifested in the gopés.
Examples of how different gopés have different kinds of qualities in their amorous pastimes with
Lord Kåñëa are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.32.4-9):


käcit karämbujaà çaurer
   jagåhe 'ïjalinä mudä
käcid dadhära tad-bähum
   aàse candana-bhüñitam

  "One gopé joyfully took Kåñëa's hand between her folded palms, and another placed His arm,
anointed with sandalwood paste, on her shoulder.***


käcid aïjalinägåhnät
   tanvé tämbüla-carvitam
ekä tad-aìghri-kamalaà
   santaptä stanayor adhät


   "A slender gopi respectfully took in her joined hands the betel nut He had chewed, and another
gopé, burning with desire, put His lotus feet on her breasts.***


ekä bhru-kuöim äbadhya
   prema-samrambha-vihvalä
ghnantévaikñat kaöäkñepaiù
   sandañöa-daçana-cchadä


   "One gopé, beside herself with loving anger, bit her lips and stared at Him with frowning
eyebrows, as if to wound Him with her harsh glances.***


aparänimiñad-dågbhyam
   juñäëä tan-mukhämbujam
äpétam api nätåpyat
   santas tac-caraëaà yathä


    "Another gopé looked with unblinking eyes upon His lotus face, but even after deeply relishing
its sweetness She did not feel satiated, just as mystic saints are never satiated when meditating upon
the Lord's feet.***


taà käcin netra-randhreëa
   hrdi kåtvä nimélya ca
pulakäìgy upaguhyäste
   yogévänanda-samplutä


   "One gopé took the Lord through the aperture of her eyes and placed Him within her heart.
Then, with her eyes closed and her bodily hairs standing on end, she continuously embraced Him
within. Thus immersed in transcendental ecstasy, she resembled a yogé meditating upon the

Lord.***


sarväs täù keçaväloka-
   paramotsava-nirvåtaù
jahur viraha jaà täpaà
   präjïaà präpya yathä janäù


   "All the gopés enjoyed the greatest festivity when they saw their beloved Keçava again. They
gave up the distress of separation, just as people in general forget their misery when they gain the
association of a spiritually enlightened person."***

   In the first of these verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.4) is seen an example of a gopés whose
relationshuip with Lord Kåñëa is based on mutual adoration. That is the first relartionship
described here, therefore this gopé is considered very important. She meets Lord Kåñëa andHe
treats Him with great respect. Here it is saif that she took Lord Kåñëa's hand in her folded palms. In
this way she showed adoration for Him. She also showed submissiveness and other like qualities.
This gopé is situation in the midst of the other gopés. She is very important, and therefore she is
described first in this passage. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.6 is described another kind of gopé, a
gopé who thinks, "Kåñëa is mine." This gopé is also situated in the midts of the gopés. Her position is
very rare and exalted. She has a special kind of love for LLord Kåñëa. Thinking, {.sy 168}Kåñëa is my
property, she stares at Him with frowning glances and enjoys other like pastimes with Him. This
particular gopé is Çré Rädhä. Her exaltedposition is described in these words describing the month
of Kärttika in the Vraja-ratnäkara-dhåta part of the Bhaviñya Puräëa:


tasmin dine ca bhagavän
   rätrau rädhä-gåhaà yayau
sä ca kruddhä tam udare
   käïcé-dämnä babandha ha


   "That evening Lord Kåñëa went to Rädhä's home. Angry, she bound His waist with Her own
sash.


kåñëas tu sarvam ävedya
   nija-geha-mahotsavam
priyäà prasädayäm äsa
   tataù sä tam amocayat


   "Telling Her about a great festival at His home, Lord Kåñëa pacified His beloved Rädhä and She
set Him free."

   The exalted position of Çré Rädhä is also seen in these words of Padma Puräëa:


yathä rädhä priyä. . .


  "Just as Çrématé Rädhäräëé is dear to the Supreme Lord Kåñëa (Viñëu), so Her bathing place
(Rädhä-kuëòa) is equally dear to Kåñëa. Among all the gopés, She alone stands supreme as the
Lord's most beloved."*

   Çré Rädhä's great glory is also seen in these words (which refer to Her) in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.30.28):


anayärädhito nünam. . .


   "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped the all-powerful Personality of Godhead,
Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a
secluded place."*

  When She went to Dvärakä, Çré Rädhä was known by the name Satyabhämä. There She was the
most glorious of Lord Kåñëa's queens. This is seen in the following words spoken to Her by Lord
Kåñëa in the Çré Viñëu Puräëa (5.30.33):


yadi te tad-vacaù satyaà
   satyätyarthaà priyeti me
mad-geha-niñkuöärthäya
   tadäyaà néyatäà taruù


   "O Satyabhämä, if My words, `You are most dear to Me', are true, then I will certainly bring the
pärijäta tree to the pleasure garden in Your palace."

   In the Kärttika-mähätmya of the Padma Puräëa, Lord Kåñëa tells Çré Rädhä:


na me tvattaù priyatamä. . .


   "No one is more dear to Me than You."

   In Çré Hari-vaàça, Vaiçampäyana Muni says of Çré Rädhä:


saubhägye cädhikäbhavat

   "Çré Rädhä is the most fortunate of Lord Kåñëa's beloveds."

   Çré Rädhä also has a revial. Her celebrated rival is named Candravali. This is described in the
following words of Çré Bilvamaìgala Öhäkura:


rädhä-mohana-mandiräd upagataç candrävalém ücivän
   rädhe kñemam iheti tasya vacanaà çrutväha candrävalé
kaàsa-kñemam aye vimugdha-hådaye kaàsaù kva dåñöas tvayä
   rädha kveti vilajjito nata-mukhaù smero hariù pätu vaù


   "Bewildered by the ecstasy of thinking of Çré Rädhä, and walking alone, Lord Kåñëa suddenly
met Candrävalé. He said: `Rädhä, this is a bequtiful place.' Hearing these words, Candrävalé said:
`This is Kaàsa's place.' Then Kåñëa said: `O girl with the bewildered heart, where do you see
Kaàsa?' Then Candrävalé replied: `Where do You see Rädhä?' May Lord Kåñëa, who at that
moment smiled and bowed His face with embarrassment, protect you all."

   The gopés who are like Candrävalé are described in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.5. Candrävalé's
dearest friends are Padmä and Çaibyä. The gopés who are like Çré Rädhä are described in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.32.7-8. Çré Rädhä thinks: "Kåñëa is My property. He follows Me. He is in My grip."
Çré Rädhä's two dearest friends are said in the scriptures to be Viçäkhä and Anurädhä. In the
Bhaviñya Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa, it is said:


viçäkhä dhyäna-niñöhikä. . .rädhänurädhä


   "Prominent among the gopés are Viçäkhä, Dhyäna-niñöhikä, Rädhä and Anurädhä."

   Rädhä's friend Anurädhä is also known by the name Lalitä. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.4 are
described the activities of two gopés. The first gopé submissively and politely takes Lord Kåñëas' arm,
but the second gopé thinks, "Kåñëa is my property" as she takes Lord Kåñëa's arm. Çré Rädhä shows
Her love for Lord Kåñëa in that way, by insistently thinking, {.sy 168}Kåñëa is My property".
Another famous gopé is named Çyämalä. She is the eighth gopé. She is described in these words of
Viñëu Puräëa:


käcid äyäntam älokya
   govinda-mati-harñitä
kåñëa kåëeti kåñëeti
   präha nänyad udairayat

  "When she saw Lord Kåñëa approasch, her heart became joyful. She called out, `Kåñëa! Kåñëa!
Kåñëa!' She spoke no word but that."

  Another famous gopé is named Bhadrä. The gopés' blissful love for Lord Kåñëa is seen in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.32.9:


sarväù. . .


   "All the gopés enjoyed the greatest festivity when they saw their beloved Keçava again. They
gave up the distress of separation, just as people in general forget their misery when they gain the
association of a spiritually enlightened person."***

   The verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.4-9 were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.368
records.text:
Now will be described the situation were a devotee is pleased (anumodana) by another devotee's
attainment of love for Lord Kåñëa in çåìgära-rasa. An example of this is seen in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.53.37-39):


asyaiva bhäryä bhavituà
   rukmiëy arhati näparä
asäv apy anavadyätmä
   bhaiñmyäù samucitaù patiù


   "Rukmiëé, and no one else, deserves to become His wife, and He also, possessing such flawless
beauty, is the only suitable husband for Princess Rukmiëé.***


kiïcit su-caritaà yan nas
   tena tuñöas tri-loka-kåt
anugåhëätu gåhëätu
   vaidarbhyäù paëim acyutaù


  "May Acyuta, the creator of the three worlds, be satisfied with whatever pious work we may have
done and show His mercy by taking the hand of Vaidarbhé.***


evaà prema-kalä-baddhä
   vadanti sma puraukasaù

   "Bound by their swelling love, the city's residents spoke in this way."***

    In these verses it is seen that many different kinds of people, people with different thoyghts and
desires, people who have not even the slightest touch of the qualification to enjoy pastimes in
srngara-rasa with Lord Kåñëa as their beloved, still feel delight (anumodana) in their hearts when
Lord Kåñëa enjoys the pastime of wedding Princess Rukmiëé. Here the word {.sy 168}prema-kalä-
baddhäù" means "their hearts bound with a little love, they were delighteed". Even though it was
only a small particle of love, and even though the people were not refined or sophisticated, they
still felt delighted at heart. At the same time the most glroious kind of love took its birth within
them. The regal full moon of ecstatic love rose within them. In this way the greatest kind of delight
appeared in their hearts. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.369
records.text:
An example of the devotees who directly enjoy amorous pastimes with Lord Kåñëa is seen in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.11-12):


apy eëa-patny upagataù priyayeha gätrais
   tanvan dåçäà sakhi su-nirvåtim acyuto vaù
käntäìga-saìga-kuca-kuìkuma-raïjitäyäù
   kunda-srajaù kula-pater iha väti gandhaù


   "O friend, wife of the deer, has Lord Acyuta been here with His beloved, bringing great joy to
your eyes? Indeed, blowing this way is the fragrance of His garland of kunòa flowers, which was
smeared with the kuìkuma from the breasts of His girlfriend when He embraced Her.***


bähuà priyäàsa upadhäya gåhéta-padmo
  rämänujas tulasikali-kulair madandhaiù
anvéyamäna iha vas taravaù praëämaà
  kià väbhinandati caran praëayävalokaiù


     "O trees, we see that you are bowing down. When the younger brother of Räma walked by here,
followed by intoxicated bees swarming around the tulasé maïjarés decorating His garland, did He
acknowledge your obeisances with His affectionate glances? He must have been resting His arm on
the shoulder of His beloved and carrying a lotus flower in His free hand."***

   Here the word "ena-patni" means "O beautiful-eyed wife of the deer". Here the gopés imagine
that the doe is like a human being, like the gopés themselves, and thus is the wife of a deer. The

word "sakhi" means {.sy 168}you have attained my friendship because of your good fortune, which I
will soon describe". "Priyayä acyutaù" means {.sy 168}Çré Kåñëa accompanied by His beloved".
"Gätraiù" means "Their limbs entwined in an embrace". {.sy 168}Vaù" means "ofe persons like
tyourselves", {.sy 168}dåçäm" means "of the eyes", "sunirvåtim" means "the spiritual bliss born from
seeing Lord Kåñëa", "tanvan" means "granting the best of all", and "upagataù" means "did He come
near you?" Here the wives of the deer may ask: "How can you know if Lord Kåñëa was here?" Fearing
the does might speak those words, the gopés speak the second half (beginning with the word känta)
of this verse, where, speaking words that indirectly praise the divine couple's amorous pastimes,
they describe the symptoms of Lord Kåñëa's presence. ere the word "kula-pateù" means "the tilaka
mark decorating the family of Vraja's king", "kunda-srajaù gandhaù" means "the fragrance of the
jasmine garland", and "iha väti" means "is blown here by the breeze". What is the garland like? It is
described here in the words "käntäìga-saìga-kuca-kuìkuma-raïjitäyäù", which mean "reddened
with kuìkuma from the limbs of His passionate and all-virtuous beloved". The gopés say: "We think
that you, who perceive everything here, might have smelled this fragrance as you walked near
Them."
    Fearing this doe is concealing the joy she feels on seeing the divine couple and the grief she feels
by separation from Them, and thinking the doe must certainly have seen the divine couple, the
gopés joyfully describe a specific pastime the divine couple might have enjoyed at that time. Then,
seeing the bent-down trees, and thinking them servants now bowing down before them, the gopés
ask the trees if they had the good fortune of seeing the divine couple. In this way the gopés spoke
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.12. In that verse the word "anviyamanah" means "being followed", "caran
praëayävalokaiù" means {.sy 168}enjoying pastimes of mutual loving glances", "vaù praëämaà kià
väbhinandati" means "did He respectfully ackowledge your obeisances?" Here the gopés mean to say:
{.sy 168}Rapt in enjoying pastim,es with His beloved, did Lord Kåñëa greet you? We do not think He
did." These verses were spoken by Çré Rädhä's girlfriends.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.370
records.text:
Beginning with älambana and ending with sthäyi-bhäva, srngara-rasa has thus been described.
Srngara-rasa has two divisions: 1. vipralambha (separation), and 2. sambhoga (enjoyment).
Vipralambha means "attainment (lambha) of distance (vipra)". Vipralambha is described in these
words of
Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-prakaraëa, Texts 1-2:


yünor ayuktayor bhävo
  yuktayor vätha yo mithaù

abhéñöäliìganädénäm
   anävaptau prakåñyate
sa vipralambho vijïeyaù
   sambhogonnati-kärakaù

   "Vipralambha (love-in-separation) is of two kinds: 1. yünor ayuktayor bhäva (love-in-separation
of the youthful couple who have not yet directly met each other), and 2. yünor yuktayor bhava
(love-in-separation of the youthful couple who have already met each other).
   "The yearning to embrace and enjoy amorous pastimes on the part of the couple who have not
yet met becomes the source of their intense pleasure."

   The exalted nature of vipralambha is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-
prakaraëa, Text 3:


na vinä vipralambhena
   sambhogaù puñöim açnute
käñäyite hi vasträdau
   bhüyän rägo vivardhate


   "Just as one cannot redden cloth or some other object without the use of red dye, in the same
way the happiness of conjugal love cannot reach its fullness without there having been separation
of the lovers."

   This truth is confirmed by Lord Kåñëa Himself in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.32.20):


nähaà tu sakhyo bhajato 'pi jantün. . .


   "But the reason I do not immediately reciprocate the affection of living beings even when they
worship Me, O gopés, is that I want to intensify their loving devotion. They then become like a poor
man who has gained some wealth and then lost it, and who thus becomes so anxious about it that he
can think of nothing else."***

   Lord Kåñëa also confirms this truth in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.34-35):


yat tv ahaà bhavaténäà vai
   düre värte priyo dåçam
manasaù sannikarñärthaà
   mad-anudhyäna-kämyayä


   "But the actual reason why I, the beloved object of your sight, have stayed far away from you is
that I wanted to intensify your meditation upon Me and thus draw your minds closer to Me.***


yathä düra-care preñöhe

    mana äviçya vartate
stréëäà ca na tathä cetaù
    sannikåñöe 'kñi-gocare


   "When her lover is far away, a woman thinkñ of him more than when he is present before
her."***

    Vipralambha has four divisions: 1. pürva-räga (before the lovers have met), 2. mäna (jealous
anger), 3. prema-vaicittya (sorrow), and 4. praväsa (the beloved lives in a faraway place). Sambhoga
is defined as the love when the two lovers enjoy (sambhoga) together. Sambhoga is described in
these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Sambhoga-prakaraëa, Text 1:


daåsanäliìganädénäm
   änukülyän niñevayä
yünor ulläsam ärohan
   bhävaù sambhoga éryate


   "That state which, by glances, embraces, and other activities brings pleasure to the youthful
divine couple is called sambhoga."

   As was described before, vipralambha is divided into four parts, which begin with pürva-räga.
pürva-räga is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-prakaraëa, Text 5:


ratir yä saìgamät pürvaà
   darçana-çravaëädi-jä
tayor unmélati präjïaiù
   pürva-rägaù sa ucyate


  "That love born from seeing, hearing, or other kinds of contact before the couple have actually
met is called pürva-räga by the wise."

   Pürva-räga is seen in the following description of Queen Rukmiëé in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.52.23):


sopaçrutya mukundasya
   rüpa-vérya-guëa-çriyaù
gåhägatair géyamänäs
   taà mene sadåçaà patim

   "Hearing of the beauty, prowess, transcendental character, and opulencer of Mukunda from
visitors to the palace who sang His praises, Rukmiëé decided that He would be the perfect husband
for her."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.371
records.text:
Now the pürva-räga of the vraja-gopés will be considered. Although in some special
circumstances sambhoga is manifest even in Lord Kåñëa's early childhood (bälya), in general the
pastimes where Lord Kåñëa is the gopés' paramour arwe manifested in Lord Kåñëa's kaiçora (11-15
years) age. This is seen in the following words of Bhaviñya Puräëa's description of Kärttika-vrata:


bälye 'pi bhagavän kåñëaù
   kaiçoraà rüpam äçritaù


   "Even in His early childhood Lord Kåñëa manifested the same enchanting handsome form He
later manifested as a teenager (kaiçora)."

   This means that the form manifest in Lord Kåñëa's kaiçora's age is also manifest, although
hidden, in His other ages as well. Therefore the manifestation of sambhoga in these other ages is
not inappropriate. By the Lord's great power His kaiçora form may be manifested even in His
childhood, even when He was only six-years old. In trhis way even at that young age pürva-räga was
manifest. Pürva-räga is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.20.45):


äçliñya sama-çétosnaà
   prasüna-vana-märutam
janäs täpaà jahur gopyo
   na kåñëa-håta-cetasaù


   "Except for the gopés, whose hearts had been stolen by Kåñëa, the people could forget their
suffering by embracing the wind coming from the flower-filled forest. This wind was neither hot
nor cold."***

   Here the words "gopyo na jahuù" mean "the gopés did not leave". They did not leave because
their hearts were stolen by Kåñëa (kåñëa-håta-cetasaù). In this way it is seen that they were
tormented by separation from Kåñëa. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 372 and 373

   The gopés' pürva-räga love for Lord Kåñëa is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.21.1-19):


itthaà çarat-svaccha-jalaà
   padmäkara-su-gandhinä
nyaviçad väyunä vätaà
   sa-go-gopälako vanam


   "Thus the Våndävana forest was filled with transparent autumnal waters and cooled by breezes
perfumed with the fragrance of lotus flowers growing in the clear lakes. The infallible Lord,
accompanied by His cows and cowherd boyfriends, entered that Våndävana forest.***


kusumita-vanaraji-suñmi-bhånga-
   dvija-kula-ghuñöa-saraù-sarin-mahédhram
madhupatir avagähya cärayan gäù
   saha-paçu-päla-balaç cuküja venum


   "The lakes, rivers and hills of Våndävana resounded with the sounds of maddened bees and
flocks of birds moving about the flowering trees. In the company of the cowherd boys and Balaräma,
Madhupati [Sré Kåñëa] entered that forest, and while herding the cows He began to vibrate His
flute.***


tad vraja-striya äçrutya
   venu-gétaà smarodayam
käçcit parokñaà kåñëasya
   sva-sakhibhyo nvavarëayan


   "When the young ladies in the cowherd village of Vraja heard the song of Kåñëa's flute, which
arouses the influence of Cupid, some of them privately began describing Kåñëa's qualities to their
intimate friends.***


tad varëayitum ärabdhäh
   smarantyaù kåñëa-ceñöitam
nasakan smara-vegena
   vikñipta-manaso nåpa

  "The cowherd girls began to speak about Kåñëa, but when they remembered His activities, O
King, the power of Cupid disturbed their minds, and thus they could not speak.***


barhäpéòaà naöa-vara-vapuù karëayoù karëikäraà
   bibhrad väsaù kanaka-kapiçaà vaijayantéà ca mäläm
randhrän veëor adhara-sudhayäpürayan gopa-våndair
   våndaraëyam sva-pada-ramaëam pravisad gita-kirtiù


   "Wearing a peacock-feather ornament upon His head, blue karëikära flowers on His ears, a
yellow garment as brilliant as gold, and the Vaijayanté garland, Lord Kåñëa exhibited His
transcendental form as the greatest of dancers as He entered the forest of Våndävana, beautifying it
with the marks of His footprints. He filled the holes of His flute with the nectar of His lips, and the
cowherd boys sang His glories.***


iti veëu-ravaà räjan
    sarva-bhüta-manoharam
çrutvä vraja-striyaù sarvä
    varëayantyo 'bhirebhire


   "O King, when the young ladies in Vraja heard the sound of Kåñëa's flute, which steals the minds
of all living beings, they all embraced one another and began describing it.***


çré-gopya ücuù

akñaëvatäà phalam idaà na paraà vidämaù
   sakhyaù paçün anuviveçayator vayasyaiù
vaktraà vrajeça-sutayor anuveëu juñöam
   yair vä nipétam anurakta-kaöäkña-mokñam


   "The cowherd girls said: O friends, those eyes that see the beautiful faces of the sons of Mahäräja
Nanda are certainly fortunate. As these two sons enter the forest, surrounded by Their friends,
driving the cows before Them, They hold Their flutes to Their mouths and glance lovingly upon
the residents of Våndävana. For those who have eyes, we think there is no greater object of
vision.***


cüta-praväla-barha-stabakotpaläbja-
   mälänupåkta-paridhäna-vicitra-veçau
madhye virejatur alaà paçu-päla-goñöhyäà
   raìge yathä naöa-varau kvaca gayamanau

   "Dressed in a charming variety of garments, upon which Their garlands rest, and decorating
Themselves with peacock feathers, lotuses, lilies, newly grown mango sprouts and clusters of flower
buds, Kåñëa and Balaräma shine forth magnificently among the assembly of cowherd boys. They
look just like the best of dancers appearing on a dramatic stage, and sometimes They sing.***


gopyaù kim äcarad ayaà kuçalaà sma veëur
   dämodarädhara-sudhäm api gopikänäm
bhuìkte svayaà yad avaçiñöa-rasaà hradinyo
   håñyat-tvaco 'çru mumucus taravo yathäryäh


   "My dear gopés, what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of
Kåñëa's lips independently and leave only a taste for us gopés, for whom that nectar is actually
meant! The forefathers of the flute, the bamboo trees, shed tears of pleasure. His mother, the river
on whose bank the bamboo was born, feels jubilation, and therefore her blooming lotus flowers are
standing like hair on her body.***


vrndävanaà sakhi bhuvo vitanoti kértim. . .


    "O friend, Våndävana is spreading the glory of the earth, having obtained the treasure of the
lotus feet of Kåñëa, the son of Devaké. The peacocks dance madly when they hear Govinda's flute,
and when other creatures see them from the hilltops, they all become stunned.***


dhanyäù sma muòha-gatayo 'pi hariëya etäù. . .


   "Blessed are all these foolish deer because they have approached Mahäräja Nanda's son, who is
gorgeously dressed and is playing on His flute. Indeed, both the doe and the bucks worship the Lord
with looks of love and affection.***


kåñëaà nirékñya. . .


    "Kåñëa's beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods' wives
flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of Him and hear His resonant flute-song, their
hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair
and their belts loosen.***


gävaç ca kåñëa-mukha. . .

    "Using their upraised ears as vessels, the cows are drinking the nectar of the flute-song flowing
out of Kåñëa's mouth. The calves, their mouths full of milk from their mothers' moist nipples, stand
stdl as they take Govinda within themselves through their tearfilled eyes and embrace Him within
their hearts.***


präyo batämba vihagä munayaù. . .


   "O mother, in this forest all the birds have risen onto the beautiful branches of the trees to see
Kåñëa. With closed eyes they are simply listening in silence to the sweet vibrations of His flute, and
they are not attracted by any other sound. Surely these birds are on the same level as great
sages.***


nadyas tadä tad upadhärya. . .


   "When the rivers hear the flute-song of Kåñëa, their minds begin to desire Him, and thus the
flow of their currents is broken and their waters are agitated, moving around in whirlpools. Then
with the arms of their waves the rivers embrace Muräri's lotus feet and, holding on to them, present
offerings of lotus flowers.***


dåçövätape vraja-paçün. . .


   "In the company of Balaräma and the cowherd boys, Lord Kåñëa is continually vibrating His
flute as He herds all the animals of Vraja, even under the full heat of the summer sun. Seeing this,
the cloud in the sky has expanded himself out of love. He is rising"***


pürëäù pulindyaù. . .


   "The aborigine women of the Våndävana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass
marked with reddish kuìkuma
powder. Endowed with the color of Kåñëa's lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts
of His beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they give up all
their anxiety.***


hantäyam adrir abalä. . .

   "Of all the devotees, this Govardhana Hill is the best! O my friends, this hill supplies Kåñëa and
Balaräma, along with Their calves, cows and cowherd friends, with all kinds of necessities-water for
drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respects to
the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Kåñëa and Balaräma, Govardhana Hill appears very
jubilant.***


gä gopakaiù. . .


   "My dear friends, as Kåñëa and Balaräma pass through the forest with Their cowherd friends,
leading Their cows, They carry ropes to bind the cows' rear legs at the time of milking. When Lord
Kåñëa plays on His flute, the sweet music causes the moving living entities to become stunned and
the nonmoving trees to tremble with ecstasy. These things are certainly very wonderful."***

    In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.1-19 the word "ittham" (thus) means "as was described in the
previous chapter", and the words "kusumitam" (filled with flowers) and {.sy 168}vanam" (forest) also
mean "as was described in the previous chapter". The word "vanam" means "the forest in that place",
"çuñmi" means "wild", "tad-vraja. . .venu-gitam asrutya" means "hearing the music of Lord Kåñëa's
flute", "paeroksam anvavarnayan" means "in a secluded place they shyly described their love for
Lord Kåñëa. It was not appropriate to describe these feelings in the presence of their elders. The
gopés concealed all this from their elders' knowledge."We may note that here it is said they
described their love for Lord Kåñëa, but they did not say that He had yet become their lover. The
words "tad varnayitum nasakan" mean "they had no power to describe those confidential topics".
The reason they had no power to describe them is given in the words {.sy 168}smarantyaù"
(remembering) and "smara-vegena" (by the power of Cupid). Then in the next verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.21.5) the gopés describe the previously revealed activities of Lord Kåñëa. Here the
words "adhara-sudhaya" (with the nectar of His lips) refers to Lord Kåñëa's playing the flute. By
directly seeing Lord Kåñëa in this way the gopés became enchanted. Thus they had no power to
speak (nasakan). They wildly embraced each other (abhirebhire).
    Although they had no power to describe their love for Lord Kåñëa, the gopés still spoke (sri-
gopya ucuh). There weretwo reasons they could not remain silent. The first reason is, even they did
not understand that they were overcome by the great power of their ecstatic love for Lord Kåñëa.
The second reason is they did understand how they were overcome by their ecstatic love for Lord
Kåñëa. The first of these reasons is seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.7. This verse has a second
interpretation. Here the words It may also be interpreted to mean "The gopas drink the nectar of
the face of Lord Kåñëa, the younger (anu) of the two princes of Vraja (vrajesa-sutayoh), a face
where the flute is placed". The second reason is seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.8-9. Thus in the
first part (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.7) of the gopés' explanation they attaempted to keep their real
feelings hidden, and in the second part (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.8-9) of their statement they
found that they had no power to conceal their true felings. In the passage begionning with Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.21.13 the gopés desrcibed their feelings in a more circumspect, a hidden way.
Concluding this chapter of Çrémad-Bhägavatam, Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.21.20):

evaà-vidhä bhagavato
   yä våndävana-cäriëaù
varnayantyo mitho gopyaù
   kréòäs tan-mayatäà yayuù


  "Thus narrating to one another the playful pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as
He wandered about in the Våndävana forest, the gopés became fully absorbed in thoughts of
Him."***

   Here the word "tan-mayatäm" means "they became rapt in thinking of Lord Kåñëa". This means
they became like a rake who always thinks of women. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.374
records.text:
The pürva-räga of the unmarried gopé girls is also described in the Tenth Canto, 22nd chapter of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam, which begins with these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.1):


hemante prathame mäsi
   nanda-vraja-kumärikäù
cerur haviñyaà bhuïjänäù
   kätyäyany-arcana-vratam


  "During the first month of the winter season, the young unmarried girls of Gokula observed the
vow of worshiping goddess Kätyäyané. For the entire month they ate only unspiced khichré."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.375
records.text:
Sending a love-letter (käma-lekhä) is one of the activities of pürva-räga. An example of a love-
letter is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.52.37):


çrutvä guëän bhuvana-sundara çåëvatäà te. . .


  "Çré Rukmiëé said (in her letter read by the brahmana): O beauty of the worlds, having heard of

Your qualities, which enter the ears of those who hear and remove their bodily distress, and havong
alos heard of Your beauty, which fulfills all the visual desires of those who see, I have fixed my
shameless mind upon You, O Kåñëa."***

   After pürva-räga comes sambhoga. Sambhoga has four parts: 1. sandarçana (gazing), 2. saïjalpa
(conversation), 3. samsparça (touching), and 4. samprayoga (union). Sandarçana means "gazing". An
example of sambhoga characterized by gazing and touching is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.52.54-55):


saivaà çanaiç calayaté cala-padma-koçau
   präptià tadä bhagavataù prasamékñamänä
utsärya väma-karajair alakän apäìgaiù
   präptan hriyaikñata nåpän dadåçe 'cyutaà ca

täà räja-kanyäà ratham ärurukñatéà
   jahära kåñëo dviñatäà samékñatäm


   "On the pretext of the procession, Rukmiëé displayed her beauty for Kåñëa alone. Slowly she
advanced the two moving lotus-whorls of her feet, awaiting the arrival of the Supreme Lord. With
the fingernails of her left had she pushed some strands of hair away from her facw and shyly looked
from the corners of her eyes

at the kings standing before her. At that moment she saw Kåñëa. Then, while His enemies looked
on, the Lord seized the princess, who was eager to mount His chariot."***

  These verses mean: "She shyly waited for the arrival of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
She looked at the kings standing before her. Then, with an agitated heart, she saw the infallible
Supreme Lord." These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 376-378


    An example in sambhoga of gazing and conversation in relation to the unmarried girls of Vraja
is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.52.55):


täsäà väsäàsy upädäya
   népam äruhya satvaraù
hasadbhiù prahasan bälaiù
   parihäsam uväca ha


  "Taking the girls' garments, He (Kåñëa) quickly climbed to the top of the kadamba tree. Then, as
He laughed loudly and His companions also laughed, He addressed the girts jokingly."***

   Here it may be said that although the gopés already had very exalted love for Lord Kåñëa, Lord
Kåñëa still manifested this joking pastime to openly display that love and to enjoy a certain kind of
loving pastime with them. Scholars learned in rasa-çästra yearn to relish this display of the gopés'
love. In this pastime Lord Kåñëa does not touch the gopés or enjoy other kinds of sambhoga pastimes
with them. This kind of pürva-rasa is called "lajjä-ccheda" (breaking the shyness). It is one of the
different kinds of sambhoga. These different kinds of sambhoga are described in these words of

Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa, Text 66:


nayana-prétiù prathamaà
   cintä-saìgas tato 'tha saìkalpaù
nidrä-cchedas tanutä
   viñaya-nivåttis trapä-näçaù
unmädo mürchä måtir
   ity etäù smara-daçä daçaiva syuù


   "Some other authorities list the stage of sambhoga in this way: 1. nayana-préti (falling in love by
seeing the beloved), 2. cintä (thinking of the beloved), 3. saìkalpa (deciding to pursue the beloved),
4. nidrä-ccheda (loss of sleep), 5. tanutä (becoming emaciated), viñaya-nivåtti (becoming oblivious
to everything except the beloved), 7. trapä-näça (destroying shyness), 8. unmäda (becoming wild), 9.
mürchä (fainting), and 10. måti (death)."

   This condition of breaking shyness is the most exalted state in anuräga. Even when they accept
death, the last of these ten states, the gopés do not abandon their shyness. To relish this kind of
anuräga (breaking the gopés' shyness), Lord Kåñëa arranged these joking pastimes. In these pastimes
Lord Kåñëa said to the gopés (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.11):


na mayodita-pürvaà vä
   anrtam tad ime viduù


   "I have never before spoken a lie, and these boys know it. Therefore, O slender-waisted girls,
please come forward, either one by one or all together, and pick out your clothes."***

   That the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa is never broken and remained unchanged in every situation
(even when Lord Kåñëa laughed at them) is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (01.229):


hasadbhiù. . .


   "Lord Kåñëa laughed loudly and His companions also laughed,"

  Here the word "bäla" indicated Lord Kåñëa's friends. Only persons who are Lord Kåñëa's friends
may touch His body. Other's cannot. Lord Kåñëa friends are described in these words of Gautaméya
Tantra, Prathamävaraëa-püjä:


däma-sudäma-vasudäma-
  kiìkiëér gandha-puñpakaiù

antaùkaraëa-rüpäs te
   kåñëasya parikértitäù
ätmäbhedena te püjyä
   yathä kåñëas tathaiva te


   "With fragrant flowers Dämä, Sudämä, Vasudämä, and Kiìkiëé worshiped Lord Kåñëa. These
boys were all praised by Lord Kåñëa Himself. These boys all know Lord Kåñëa's heart. Their hearts
are not different from Lord Kåñëa's heart. As Lord Kåñëa is worthy of worship, so are they."

   Because these pastimes of Lord Kåñëa's relishing the gopés' anuräga love for Him are confidential,
Lord Kåñëa pretended these activities were all a joke. This joking pretense is not incompatible with
these pastimes. On the contrary, Lord Kåñëa joking enhances the bliss of the pastimes. The great
sage Sukadeva Gosvami describes Lord Kåñëa's purpose in performing these activities. The sage
explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.18):


bhagavän ähatä vékñya
   çuddha-bhäva-prasäditaù
skandhe nidhäya väsäàsi
   prétaù proväca sa-smitam


   "When the Supreme Lord saw how the gopés were struck with embarrassment, He was satisfied
by their pure loving affection. Putting their clothes on His shoulder, the Lord smiled and spoke to
them with affection."***

   In this verse the word "ähatäù" means {.sy 168}approached". Or, "ähaöaù" may also mean {.sy
168}Although they had renounced almost all shyness, because of their feminine nature a small
fragment of shyness remained. Because of this remaining shyness they gently bent their bodies."
The word "çuddha-bhäva-prasäditaù" means "pleased at heart by relishing the gopés' splendid love,
love that showed their longing to be with Him and their being enchanted by Him".
   The next verse explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.19):


yüyaà vivasträ yad apo dhåta-vratäù. . .


   "(Lord Kåñëa said:) You girls bathed naked while executing your vow, and that is certainly an
offense against the demigods. To counteract Your sin you should offer obeisances while placing
your joined palms above your heads. Then you should take back your lower garments."***

   In order to see the last remnants of the gopés' shyness come to their final end Lord Kåñëa spoke
these joking words. The next verse explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.20):

ity acyutena. . .


   "Thus the young girls of Våndävana, considering what Lord Acyuta had told them, accepted that
they had suffered a falldown from their vow by bathing naked in the river. But they still desired to
successfully complete their vow, and since Lord Kåñëa is Himself the ultimate result of all pious
activities, they offered their obeisances to Him to cleanse away all their sins."***

   In this way Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé, the king of sages, reveals first the gopés'being enchanted by
Lord Kåñëa and their longing to associatte with Him, and then their obedience to His command. In
the next verse Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.22):


dåòhaà pralabdhäs trapayä ca häpitäù
   prastobhitäù kréòana-vac ca käritah
vasträëi caiväpahåtäny athäpy amum-
   tä näbhyasüyan priya-saìga-nirvrtäh


   "Although the gopés had been thoroughly cheated, deprived of their modesty, ridiculed and made
to act just like toy dolls, ana although their clothing had been stolen, they did not feel at all
inimical toward Sré Kåñëa. Hather, they were simply joyful to have this opportunity to associate
with their beloved."***

   In the verse the word "dåòham" means {.sy 168}greatly", and "pralabdhäù" means "cheated". The
cheating of the gopés is described here in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.19. "Trapayä häpitäù" means
"deprived of their modesty". This is descibed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.10. "Prastobhitäù' here
means "mocked". Lord Kåñëa mocked the gopés in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.10. Lord Kåñëa's
making the gopés act like toy dolls is desscribed in His making them stand with folded palms on the
pretext of performing atonement. Even though Lord Kåñëa cheated them and teased them in many
ways, the gopés did not find fault with Lord Kåñëa. On the contrary. It is said here that even though
He had stolen their garments, the gopés did not feel eneimical toward Lord Kåñëa. On the contrary.
They were plunged into bliss because they had an opportunity to associate with their beloved.
These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 379-382


   Because they were brähmaëés, the yajïa-patnés were not qualified to associate with with Lord
Kåñëa as the gopés did. Still, the yajïa-patnés did have an ecstatic sentiment that was something like
pürva-räga. Gazing at Lord Kåñëa and conversing with Him, they experienced something in some
ways like sambhoga. They experienced sambhogäbhäsa (the reflection of sambhoga). After the
winter season had ended and summer had come, Lord Kåñëa's pastimes with the yajna-patnés
became visible. The beginning of these pastimes is desacribed in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam

(10.22.29):

atha gopaiù parivåto
   bhagavän devaké-sutaù
vrndävanäd gato düraà
   cärayan gäù sahägrajah


   "Some time later Lord Kåñëa, the son of Devaké, surrounded by His cowherd friends and
accompanied by His elder brother, Balaräma, went a good distance away from Våndävana, herding
the cows."***

   This verse means: "After Lord Kåñëa had given His mercy to the unmarried girls of Vraja, a
summer day came". That the day was a summer day distinguishes this pastime from the previous
pastime (which occurred in the winter). On this day Lord Kåñëa was accompanied by Lord
Balaräma. That is indicated here by the word "sägrajaù" (with His elder brother). Here the phrase "a
good distance away from Våndävana" indicates that Kåñëa and the boys were in the hilly part of
Kämyavana. That they were in the hills is seen by the fact that they decorated their bodies with
mineral pigments from the hills. That place is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.22.36):


tarüëäà namra-çäkhänäà
   madhyato yamunäà gatah


   "Thus moving among the trees, whose branches were bent low by their abundance of twigs,
fruits, flowers and leaves, Lord Kåñëa came to the Yamunä River."***

   With Vraja to their south and the Yamunä to the west, they entered a clearing to enjoy
pastimes. To the south was Mathurä City, and to the north was the place where some yäjïika-
brähmaëas lived. The home of these brahmana's was near King Kaàsa's palace. That is seen in
these words describing the thoughts of these brähmaëas (Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.23.52):


kaàsäd bhétä na cäcalan


   "Thus reflecting on the sin they had committed by neglecting Lord Kåñëa, they (the yäjïika-
brähmaëas) became very eager to see Him. But being afraid of King Kaàsa, they did not dare go to
Vraja."***

   In this way it is seen that those brähmaëas did not go to meet Lord Kåñëa. The summer qualities
of that day are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.30):

nidäghärkätape tigme
   chäyäbhiù sväbhir ätmanaù
atapatrayitan vikñya
   drumän äha vrajaukasaù


   "When the sun's heat became intense, Lord Kåñëa saw that the trees were acting as umbrellas by
shading Him, and thus He spoke as follows to His boyfriends."***

   In this verse the phrase "nidäghärkätape tigme" is a locative absolute. The yajna-patnis'
sambhogäbhäsa (reflection of sambhoga) is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.21-23):


yamunopavane 'çoka-
   nava-pallava-mandite
vicarantaà våtaà gopaih
   sägrajaà dadåçuù striyaù
