   "Along the river Yamunä, within a garden decorated with buds of açoka trees, they caught sight
of Him strolling along in the company of the cowherd boys and His elder brother, Balaräma.***


çyämaà hiraëya-paridhià vanamälya-barha-
   dhätu-praväla-naöa-veñam anuvratäàse
vinyasta-hastam itareëa dhunänam abjaà
   karëotpalälaka-kapola-mukhäbja-häsam


   "His complexion was dark blue and His garment golden. Wearing a peacock feather, colored
minerals, sprigs of Mower buds, and a garland of forest flowers and leaves, He was dressed just like a
dramatic dancer. He rested one hand upon the shoulder of a friend and with the other twirled a
lotus. Lilies graced His ears, His hair hung down over His cheeks, and His lotuslike face was
smiling."***


präyaù-çruta-priyatamodaya-karëa-pürair
   yasmin nimagna-manasas tam athäkñi-randhraiù
antaù praveçya su-ciraà parirabhya täpaà
   präjïaà yathäbhimatayo vijahur narendra


   "O ruler of men, for a long time those brahmana ladies had heard about Kåñëa, their beloved,
and His glories had become the constant ornaments of their ears. Indeed, their minds were always
absorbed in Him. Through the apertures of their eyes they now forced Him to enter within their

hearts, and then they embraced Him within for a long time. In this way they fionally gave up the
pain of separation from Him, just as sagesa give up the anxiety of false ego by embracing their
innermost consciousness."***

   In this verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.23.23) the word {.sy 168}abhimatayaù" means: "false ego",
and the phrase {.sy 168}prajnam tapam vijahuù" means "as the sages, situated in spiritual trace,
become free of all sufferings, so these women also became free of all sufferings".

   One of those brähmaëés, becoming free of their previous disqualifications, attained in her heart
pürva-räga love for Lord Kåñëa and then enjoyed sambhoga pastimes with Him, pastimes that begin
with touching Him. This attainment of hers is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.35):


tatraikä vidhåtä bharträ
   bhagavantaà yathä-çrutam
hådopaguhya vijahau
   dehaà karmänubandhanam


   "One of ther ladies had been forcibly kept back by her husband. When she heard the others
describe the Supreme Lord Kåñëa, she embraced him within her heart and gave up her material
body, the basis of bondage to material activity."***

  When she gave up the brahmana body she had attained by past karma, then he disqualification
was destroyed and she was able to embrace Lord Kåñëa in her heart. In that way she attained Lord
Kåñëa's association. This is described in these words of Bhagavad-gétä (8.6):


yaà yaà väpi smana bhävam. . .


   "Whatever state of being one remembers when he quits this body, O son of Kunté, that state he
will attain without fail."*

   The statement that she attained Lord Kåñëa's association means that she attained the form of a
gopé. She did not attain the form of a brähmaëé and in that form associate with Lord Kåñëa. That
Lord Kåñëa's close associates were all cowherd people is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.37):


evaà lélä-nara-vapuù. . .


  "Thus the Supreme Lord, appearing like a human being to perform His pastimes, imitated the
ways of human society. He enjoyed pleasing His cows, cowherd boyfriends and cowherd girlfriends

with His beauty, words, and actions."***

   In this verse it is said that Lord Kåñëa enjoyed pleasing the cows and cowherd people. He did not
enjoy pastimes with others, at least not in the land of Vraja. In Vraja that yajïa-patné could not
enjoy pastimes with Lord Kåñëa without becoming a gopé. She thus entered the Vraja that is not
manifested in the material world. In that unmanifested Vraja Lord Kåñëa enjoys many different
pastimes, pastimes without limit. This is explained in the Kåñëa-sandarbha. Therefore there is
nothing wrong in her death. She yearned to attain Lord Kåñëa. With a great effort she struggled to
attain Him. In that way she attained a very exalted relationship (rasa) with Him. Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.23.35 quoted above was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.383
records.text:
In the autumn after (Lord Çré Kåñëa's pastime of stealing the gopés' garments) all the vraja-gopés
enjoyed sambhoga pastime with Lord Kåñëa, pastimes born of the gopés' purva-raga love for Him,
pastimes that begin with gazing at Lord Kåñëa. These sambhoga pastimes are described (in the
scriptures). Although the unmarried girls of Vraja had already attained Lord Kåñëa's association,
theydid not feel fulfilled. Their purva-raga love for Him had still not attained its full nature. Still,
at least one gopés had enjoyed pastimes with Lord Kåñëa, as is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.21.17):


pürëäù pulindyaù. . .


   "The aborigine women of the Våndävana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass
marked with reddish kuìkuma
powder. Endowed with the color of Kåñëa's lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts
of His beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they give up all
their anxiety."***

   Still, many other gopés had not yet even touched Lord Kåñëa. This is seen in these words spoken
by the gopés in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.36):


yarhy ambujäkña. . .


    "O lotus-eyed one, the goddess of fortune considers it a festive occasion whenever she touches
the soles of Your lotus feet. You are very dear to the residents of the forest, and therefore we will
also touch those lotus feet. From that time on we will be unable even to stand in the presence of
any other man, for we will have been fully satisfied by You."***

   When the gopés first heard Lord Kåñëa's flute-music they at first tried to supress the ecstatic

emotions that came to overwhelm them. From this it may be seen that they had not yet directly
enjoyed sambhoga pastimes with Him. Also, because they had not yet enjoyed sambhoga pastimes
with Him, Lord Kåñëa at first rejected them, and they then appealed to Him. These pastimes are
seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam, Canto 10, Chapter 29, in the passage that begins with these words
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.4):


niçamya gétaà tad anaìga-vardhanaà
   vraja-striyaù kåñëa-gåhéta-mänasäù
äjagmur anyonyam alakñitodyamäù
   sa yatra känto java-lola-kundaläù


   "When the young women of Våndävana heard Kåñëa's flute song, which arouses romantic
feelings, their minds were captivated by the Lord. They went to where their lover waited, each
unknown to the others, moving so quickly that their earrings swung back and forth."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.384
records.text:
Jealous anger (mäna) may bring separation (vipralambha) of Lord Kåñëa and His beloved. This is
seen in the following words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text 93):


aher iva gatiù premëä
   sva-bhäva-kuöilä bhavet
ato hetor ahetoç ca
   yünor mäna udaïcati


   "The progress of loving affairs between young couples is by nature crooked, like the movement of
a snake. Becuase of this, two types of nager arise between young couples-anger with cause and anger
without cause."*

   Jealous anger without a cause is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-
prakaraëa (Text 70):


ahetur neti nety ukter
   hetor yan mäna ucyate
asya praëaya eva syän
   mänasya padam uttamam

  "When without any cause the beloved says `No. No.' and rejects the lover, this is called jealous
anger (mäna). This is the highest state of loving jealous anger."

   Jealous anger is thus with a cause and without a ccause. Jealous anger with a cause is described in
these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text 71):


hetur érñyä-vipakñäder
   viçiñöye preyasä kåte
bhävaù praëaya-mukhyo 'yam
   érñyä-mänatvam åcchati


   "When the lover gives special attention to a certain beloved, then all the rivals of the beloved
become jealous. In this way what was once love becomes jealous anger. This is anger with cause."

  Jealous anger is also described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa
(Text 72):


snehaà vinä bhayaà na syän
   nerñyä ca praëayaà vinä
tasmän mäna-prakäro 'yaà
   dvayoù prema-prakäçakaù


   "Without love there cannot be fear (for the loss of the beloved), and without love there cannot
be jealousy. For this reason fear and jealousy may be manifestations of love."

   Jealous anger is seen in the following words of Hari-vaàça, Viñëu-parva (66.4 and 65.50):


ruñitäm iva täà devéà
   snehät saìkalpayann iva
bhéta-bhéto 'ti-çanakair
   viveça yadu-nandanaù

rüpa-yauvana-sampannä
   sva-saubhägyena garvitä
abhimänavaté devé
   çrutvaiverñyä-vaçaà gatä


   "As He slowly entered the palace, Lord Kåñëa, who is feared by fear itself, and who is the
descendent of Maharaja Yadu, lovingly meditated on His angry queen Satyabhämä."

  "Meanwhile, hearing (how her rival Rukmiëé had attained a pärijäta flower from Indraloka),
Queen Satyabhämä, who was very proud of her opulent beauty and youthfulness, bexcame
overwhelmed with jealous anger."

   When the beloved suspects the lover no longer loves her, then jealous anger with cause is
manifest. Lord Kåñëa enjoys teasing His beloved in this way (to make her angry because she
suspects He no longer loves her). An example of such teasing is seen in these words Lord Kåñëa
spoke to Queen Rukmiëé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.29):


tvad-vacaù çrotu-kämena
   kñvelyäcaritam aìgane


   "I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say."***

Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.30):


mukhaà ca prema-samrambha-
  sphuritädharam ékñitum. . .


   "I wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your eyes
throwing sidelong glances and the line of your beautiful eyebrows knit in a frown."***

  Queen Rukmiëé refuted Lord Kåñëa's teasing arguments by speaking these words (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.60.40):


jäòyaà vacas tava gadägraja. . .


   "My Lord, as a lion drives away lesser animals to claim his proper tribute, You drove off the
assembled kings with the resounding twang of Your Çärìga bow and then claimed me, Your fair
share. Thus it is sheer foolishness, my dear Gadägraja, for You to say You took shelter in the ocean
out of fear of those kings."***

   Lord Kåñëa's teasing words in the pastime were proper, for they were meant only to increase His
beloved's love for Him. Such words are approved by ancient and modern poets and philosophers.
Now jealous anger in the mood of worship, which is called {.sy 168}ädaraëéya-mäna", will be
considered. When, during the räsa dance, at the time of their first intimate meeting, Lord Kåñëa
abandoned all the gopés and remained hidden from their sight, the gopés became slightly angry with
Him. This is seen in the passage beginning with these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.15):

sabhäjayitvä tam anaìga-dépanaà
   sahäsa-lélekñaëa-vibhrama-bhruvä
saàsparçanenäìka-kåtäìghri-hastayoù
   saàstutya iñat kupita babhasire


   "Sré Kåñëa had awakened romantic desires within the gopés, and they honored Him by glancing
at Him with playful smiles, gesturing amorously with their eyebrows, and massaging His hands and
feet as they held them in their laps. Even while worshiping Him, however, they felt somewhat
angry, and thus they addressed Him as follows."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadwva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.385
records.text:
By speaking words of praise the lover may pacify the beloved's anger. An example of this may be
seen in these words of praise spoken by Lord Kåñëa to the gopés (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.21-22):


evaà mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda-
   svänäà hi vo mayy anuvåttaye 'baläù
mayäparokñaà bhajatä tirohitaà
   masuyitum marhatha tat priyam priyah


   "My dear girls, understanding that simply for My sake you had rejected the authority of worldly
opinion, of the Veòas and of your relatives, I acted as I did only to increase your attachment to Me.
Even when I removed Myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you.
Therefore, My beloved gopés, please do not harbor any bad feelings toward Me, your beloved.***


na päraye 'haà niravadya-saàyujäm. . .


  "I am not able to repay My debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmä. Your
connection with Me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped Me, cutting off all domestic ties,
which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your
compensation."***

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.386
records.text:
Jealous anger or pride without a cause is called {.sy 168}praëaya-mäna" (anger or pride caused by
love). Such anger or pride has no external cause. Its only cause is the pastimes of love. The hero
(Lord Kåñëa) also manifests this kind of pride or anger. In the rasa of love for the Supreme
Personality of Godhead this kind of anger or pride is one of the uddépanas. An example of causeless
anger or pride, pride born of love, is seen in the passage that begins with these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.29.48):


täsäà tat-saubhaga-madaà
   vékñya mänaà ca keçavaù


   "Lord Keçava, seeing the gopés too proud of their good fortune, wanted to relieve them of this
pride and show them further mercy. Thus He immediately disappeared."***

  Here the gopés had pride born from love (pranaya-mana). There was a cause of their pride. They
were proud of their own good fortune. Therefore, to curb this pride and give them His mercy, Lord
Kåñëa suddenly disappeared from the gopés' sight. Then it is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.36):


yäà gopém anayat kåñëo
  vihäyänyäù striyo vane. . .


   "The particular gopé whom Kåñëa had led to a secluded forest when He had abandoned all the
other girls began to think Herself the best of women. `My beloved has rejected all the other gopés',
She thought, `even though they are driven by Cupid himself. He has chosen to reciprocate with Me
alone.' "***

   Tbis gopé also became proud with love (praëaya-mäna). Filled with pride, She spoke these words
to Lord Kåñëa (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.37):


na päraye 'ham calituà
   naya mäà yatra te manaù


  "I cannot walk any further. Please carry Me wherever You want to go."***

   As the other gopés were previously, this gopé also became proud with love. Then, with anger also
born of love, Lord Kåñëa spoke to Her the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.38):


skandha äruhyatäm. . .

   "Lord Kåñëa replied: `Just climb on My shoulder.' "***

   After speaking these words, Lord Kåñëa suddenly disappeared. The gopés have pride without
cause (ahetu) and Lord Kåñëa has pride with a faint reflection of a cause (hetv-äbhäsa). Flowing
through the great whirlpool of deceitful crookedness, the gopés' loving pride and anger become very
intense.When they are separated from Lord Kåñëa, their anger becomes sublimely pure. Lord
Kåñëa's other beloveds (other than the gopés) manifest grief, fear, and worry when they become
angry with a cause. As example of this is seen in the Çrémad-Bhägavatam chapter when Lord Kåñëa
teased Queen Rukmiëé with loving joking words. There Lord Kåñëa's intention was to make a
playful joke. Queen Rukmiëé was very deep and her love very sincere. There Lord Kåñëa thought:
"My wish is to enjoy pastimes of making My beloved angry. Her throat will be filled with emotional
words that reveal her great love for Me. However, she may not clearly understand My intention.
She will either become playfully angry, or she will say she does not undrstand My words. In this way
I will try to joke with her. Even when I made her brother very ugly-looking she still did not become
angry. It is not appropriate to continue in that direction. However, the happiness she feels by
associating with Me is the be-all-and-end-all of her life. It is everything for her. Perhaps by
mocking the pride she feels by being able to associate with Me I will make her angry. If she does not
become angry in that way, then perhaps by making her afraid that she will be separated from Me
she will speak many words revealing her love for Me." Thinking in this way, Lord Kåñëa spoke the
loving joking words that begin in this verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.10):


räja-putrépsitä bhüpaiù. . .


  "My dwear princess, you were sought after by many kings as powerful as the rulers of planets.
They were all abundantly endowed with polituical influence, wealth, beauty, generosity, and
physical strength."***

   That Lord Kåñëa was joking is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.9):


täà rüpiëém. . .prétaù smayan


  "As He contemplated her, the goddess of fortune herself, who desires only Him, Lord Kåñëa
smiled."***

   In this way it is seen that Lord Kåñëa was only joking. The sincerity of Queen Rukmiëé's love is
seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.25):


tad dåñövä bhagavän kåñëaù
   priyäyäù prema-bandhanam
häsya-prauòhim ajänantyäù

   karuëaù so 'nvakampata. . .


   "Seeing that His beloved was so bound to Him in love that she could not understand the full
meaning of His teasing, merciful Lord Kåñëa felt compassion for her.***
   "The Lord quickly got down from the bed. Manifesting four arms, He picked her up, gathered her
hair, and caressed her face with His lotus hand."***

   In these verses the word "häsya-prauòhim" means "the meaning of His joking words". Here Lord
Kåñëa proudly thought: "Even though she is very wise and profound, and even though her love is
very sincere, I will agitate her." The word "ajänantyäù" means "because there was no crookedness or
deceit in her sweet and sincere love, she did not understand the meaning of Lord Kåñëa's words".
This is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.28):


häsya-prauòhi-bhramac-cittäm


   "Rukmiëé's mind was bewildered by Lord Kåñëa's clever joking."

  As a joke Lord Kåñëa had wished to see her playful anger. Thus He said to her in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.60.29-31):


mä mä vaidarbhy asüyetha
   jäne tväà mat-paräyaëäm
tvad-vacaù çrotu-kämena
   kñvelyäcaritam aìgane


   "O Vaidarbhé, do not be displeased with Me. I know that you are fully devoted to Me. I only
spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say.***


mukhaà ca prema-samrambha-
   sphuritädharam ékñitum
kaöä-kñepäruëäpäìgaà
   sundara-bhrü-kuöé-taöam


   "I also wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your
eyes throwing sidelong glances, and the line of your beautiful eyebrows knit in a frown.***


ayaà hi paramo läbho
   gåheñu gåha-medhinäm

yan narmair iyate yämaù
   priyayä bhéru bhämini


   "The greatest pleasure worldly householders can enjoy at home is to spend time joking with their
beloved wives, My dear timid and tempermental one."***

   Although at first she was frightened, now Rukmiëé may be displeased. That is why Lord Kåñëa
now throws away the idea that Rukmiëé is meekly submissive to Him. Here the woprd {.sy
168}bhamini" is in the vocative case.

  Lord Kåñëa, who had yearned to see Rukmiëé reveal Her love for Him, says in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.60.49):


sädhvy etac-chrotu-kämais tvaà
   räja-putri pralambhitä


   "O saintly lady, O princess, We deceived you only because We wanted to hear you speak like
this. Indeed, everything you said in reply to My words is most certainly true."***

   Wishing to refute Lord Kåñëa's assertyion of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.49 and also wishing to
reveal the truth about Lord Kåñëa, Queen Rukmiëé spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.60.38):


tvaà vai samasta-puruñärtha-mayaù phalätmä. . .


   "You are the embodiment of all human goals and You are Yourself the final aim of life. Desiring
to attain You, O all-powerful Lord, intelligent persons abandon everything else. It is they who are
worthy of Your association, not men and women absorbed in the pleasure and grief resulting from
their mutual lust."***

  After understanding that Lord Kåñëa was only joking, Queen Rukmiëé manifested a little of the
anger that He had yearned to see. She said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.40):


jäòyaà vacas tava gadägraja. . .


   "My Lord, as a lion drives away lesser animals to claim his proper tribute, You drove off the
assembled kings with the resounding twang of Your Çärìga bow and then claimed me, Your fair
share. Thus it is sheer foolishness, my dear Gadägraja, for You to say You took shelter in the ocean
out of fear of those kings."***

   Here the word "jäòyam" means "great foolishness" just as "mädhuryam" means "great sweetness" in
these words of Çréla Bilvamaìgala Öhäkura's Çré Kåñëa-karëämåta (Text 68):


mädhuryam eva nu mano-nayanämåtaà nu


   "Lord Kåñëa is the great nectar sweetness that fills the eyes and the heart."

   In speaking these joking words, Lord Kåñëa's purpose was to agitate Queen Rukmiëé and destroy
the pride she felt in always having His association. This is seen in these words spoken by Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.21):


etävad uktvä bhagavän
   ätmänaà vallabhäm iva
manyamänäm aviçleñät
   tad-darpa-ghna upäramat


   "Rukmiëé had thought herself especially beloved by the Lord because He never left her company.
By saying these things to her He vanquished her pride, and then He stopped speaking."***

   Lord Kåñëa had another purpose also, a purpose seen in these words He personally spoke in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.56):


bhrätur virüpa-karaëaà yudhi nirjitasya
  prodväha-parvaëi ca tad-vadham akña-goñöhyäm
duùkham samuttham asaho 'smad-ayoga-bhétyä
  naiväbravéù kim api tena vayaà jitäs te


   "When your brother, who had been defeated in battle and then disfigured, was later killed during
a gambling match on Aniruddha's wedding day, you felt unbearable grief, yet out of fear of losing
Me you spoke not a word. By this silence you have conquered Me."***

   In this chapter of Çrémad-Bhägavatam are seen Queen Rukmiëé's great love for Lord Kåñëa and
her natural absence of anger. From this it is seen that it certainly truthfully said that Lord Kåñëa's
beloveds love Him very dearly. When the manifestation of pride and anger is concluded, then
sambhoga is manifest. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.1):


itthaà bhagavato gopyaù
   çrutvä väcaù su-peçaläù

jahur viraha jaà täpam-
   tad-aìgopacitäçiñaù


   "When the cowherd girls heard the Supreme Personality of Godhead speak these most charming
words, they forgot their distress caused by separation from Him. Touching His transcendental
limbs, they felt all their desires fulfilled."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 387 and 388


   Now prema-vaicittyam will be considered. Its qualities are described in these words of Ujjvala-
nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text 134):


priyasya sannikarñe 'pi
   premotkarña-svabhävataù
yä viçleña-dhiyärtis tat
   prema-vaicittyam ucyate


   "When, even in the beloved's presence, the lover, out of intense love, is aggrieved with fears of
separation in the future, such a state is called prema-vaicittyam."

   Prema-vaicittyam is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.90.13-24):


kåñëasyaivaà viharato
   gaty-äläpekñita-smitaiù
narma-kñveli-pariñvangaiù
   stréëäà kila håtä dhiyaù


   "In this way Lord Kåñëa would sport with His queens, totally captivating their hearts with His
gestures, talks, glances, and smiles, and also with His jokes, playful exchanges, and embraces.***


ücur mukundaika-dhiyo
   girä unmatta-vaj jaòam
cintayantyo 'ravindäkñam
   täni me gadataù çåìu


   "The queens would become stunned in ecstatic trance, their minds absorbed in Kåñëa alone.

Then, thinking of their lotus-eyed Lord, they would speak as if insane. Please hear these words from
me as I relate them.***


çré-mahiñya ücuù

kurari vilapasi tvaà véta-nidrä na çeñe
   svapiti jagati rätryäm éçvaro gupta-bodhaù
vayam iva sakhi kaccid gäòha-nirviddha-cetä
   nalina-nayana-häsodära-lélekñitena


   "The queens said: O kurari bird, you are lamenting. Now it is night, and somewhere in this world
the Supreme Lord is asleep in a hidden place. But you are wide awake, O friend, unable to fall
asleep. Is it that, like us, you have had your heart pierced to the core by the lotus-eyed Lord's
munificent, playful smiling glances?"***


netre nimélayasi. . .


   "Poor cakraväké, even after closing your eyes, you continue to cry pitifully through the night for
your unseen mate. Or is it that, like us, you have become the servant of Acyuta and hanker to wear
in your braided hair the garland He has blessed with the touch of His feet?***


bho bhoù sadä niñöänase udanvann. . .


   "Dear ocean, you are always roaring, not sleeping at night. Are you suffering insomnia? Or is it
that, as with us, Mukunda has taken your insignias and you are hopeless of retrieving them?***


tvaà yakñmänä. . .


   "My dear moon, having contracted a severe case of tuberculosis, you have become so emaciated
that you fail to dispel the darkness with your rays. Or is it that you appear dumbstruck because, like
us, you cannot remember the encouraging promises Mukunda once made to you?***


kià nv äcäritam. . .


  "O Malayan breeze, what have we done to displease you, so that you stir up lust in our hearts,
which have already been shattered by Govinda's sidelong glances?***

megha çrémän. . .


   "O revered cloud, you are indeed dear ot the chief of the Yadus, who bears the mark of Çrévatsa.
Like us, you are bound to Him by love and are meditating upon Him. Your heart is distraught with
great eagerness, as our hearts are, and as you remember Him again and again you shed a torrent of
tears. Association with Kåñëa brings such misery!***


priya-räva. . .


   "O sweet-throated cuckoo, in a voice that could revive the dead you are vibrating the same
sounds we once heard from our beloved, the most pleasing of speakers. Please tell me what I can do
today to please you.***


na calasi. . .


   "O magnanimous mountain, you neither move nor speak. You must be pondering some matter of
great importance. Or do you, like us, desire to hold on your breasts the feet of Vasudeva's darling
son?***


çuñyad-dhradaù. . .


  "O rivers, wives of the ocean, your pools have now dried up. Alas, you have shriveled to nothing,
and your wealth of lotuses has vanished. Are you, then, like us, who are withering away because of
not receiving the affectionate glance of our dear husband, the Lord of Madhu, who has cheated our
hearts?***


haàsa svägatam äsyatäà piba payo brühy aìga çaureù kathäà
   dütaà tvaà nu vidäma kaccid ajitaù svasty asta uktaà purä
kià na vaç cala-sauhådaù smarati taà kasmäd bhajämo vayaà
   kñaudräläpaya käma-daà çréyam åte saivaika-niñöha striyam


   "Welcome, swan. Please sit here and drink some milk. Give us some news of the descendent of
Çüra, dear one. We know that you are His messenger. Is that invincible Lord doing well, and does
that unreliable friend of ours still remember the words He spoke to us long ago? Why should we go
and worship Him? O servant of a petty master, go tell Him who fulfills our desires to come here
without the goddess of fortune. Is she the only woman exclusively devoted to Him?"***

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.13 means: "With His gestures and other activities Lord captivated the
hearts of His queens as He enjoyed pastimes with them." Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.14 means: "Rapt
in meditation on Lord Kåñëa and thus momentarily speechless (agiraù), and again and again
maddened by their anuräga love, and meditating on playful lotus-eyed Kåñëa as if He were not
present before them, the gopés spoke words devoid of common sense. Please hear these words as I
relate them."
   Maddened by the touchof separation from Lord Kåñëa, the queens speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.90.15-24. Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.15 means: "O Kurari bird, all alone, you lament at night
somewhere in this world. Therefore you do not sleep. In some hidden place our master sleeps.
Thinking, "Because of the similar sweetness of your lament and our lament, we think. . . ", the
queens spoke the second half of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.15. In the following verses the queens
think similar ideas in otber ways. Then, thinking that, sent by the Lord, a swan has come as a
messenger before them, the queens speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.24. In that verse they say: {.sy
168}Does Kåñëa remember what He spoke to us in private? or does He not remember it?" In that
verse the word "ksaudra" means "O messenger of our fickle friend", {.sy 168}kämadam" means "who
agitates young girls", and {.sy 168}äläpaya" means "please call". Then the queens say: "We leave
everything for Him. He should comw without the goddess of fortune (sriyam rt). Here the queens
sarcastically pretend to glorify the goddess of fortune. They say: "Of all women the goddess of
fortune alone has true devotion to Lord Kåñëa. Therefore how is it possible that Lord Kåñëa will nto
be devoted to her." Speaking these words with voices choked with emotion, the queens sarcastically
speak of the goddess of fortune and also reveal their own love and devotion for Lord Kåñëa. That is
seen in this verse.
   After this manifestation of love-in-separation, the queens enjoy eternal sambhoga pastimes with
Lord Kåñëa. It is said of these queens (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.25):


itédåçena bhävena
    kåñëe yogeçvareçvare
kriyamänena mädhavyo
    lebhire paramäà gatim


  "By thus speaking and acting with such ecstatic love for Lord Kåñëa, the master of all masters of
mystic yoga, His loving wives attained the ultimate goal of life."***

  In this verse the words "gatià lebhire" mean {.sy 168}they attained an eternal relationship with
Lord Viñëu-Kåñëa." The reason they attained this relationship is given here in the word
"mädhavyaù", which means "the eternal beloveds of Lord Kåñëa, who is called Mädhava because He
was born in the Madhu dynasty". This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 389 and 390


  Now praväsa (separation when the belovedhas gone to a faraway place) will be considered.

Praväsa is of many kinds. In the pravasa separation felt by the vraja-gopés, the gopés did meet Lord
Kåñëa again. The qualities of praväsa are described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-
bheda-prakaraëa (Text 139-140):


pürva-saìgatayor yünor
   bhaved deçäntarädibhiù
vyavadhänaà tu yat präjïaiù
   sa praväsa itéryate

taj-janya-vipralambho 'yaà
   praväsatvena kathyate


   "When ther young couple, after meeting and establishing Their relationship become again
separated by one of them moving to a foreign country or a distant place, such separation is called
praväsa by the wise."

   Praväsa is also described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text
153):


cintätra jägarodvegau
   tänavaà malinäìgatä
praläpo vyädhir unmädo
   moha-måtyur daçä daça


   "In Praväsa ten conditions are manifest: 1. cintä (meditation), 2. jägara (insomnia), 3. udvega
(agitation), 4. tänavam (becoming thin and emaciated), 5. malinäìgatä (withering of the body), 5.
praläpa (abundant talking), 7. vyädhi (disease), 8. unmäda (madness), 9. moha (bwilderment), and
10. måtyu (death."

   Praväsa is of two kinds: 1. kiïcid-düra-gamana-maya (where the beloved is separated by a short
distance) and 2. su-düra-gamana-maya (where the beloved isseparated by a great distance). The first
of these is also of two kinds: 1. eka-lélä-gata (in one pastime), and 2. paramparäntaräla-gata (within
a series of pastimes). The first of these (kiïcid-düra-gamana-maya praväsa) is seen in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.1):


antarhite bhagavati
   sahasaiva vrajäìganäù
atapyaàs tam acaksänäù
   kariëya iva yüthapam

   "When Lord Kåñëa disappeared so suddenly, the gopés felt great sorrow at losing sight of Him,
like a group of female elephants who have lost their mate."***

  This kind of praväsa is also seen in these owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.38):


tataç cäntardadhe kåñëaù
   sä vadhür anvatapyata


   "But as soon as He said this, Lord Kåñëa disappeared. His beloved consort then immediately felt
great remorse."***

  The meaning of this verse is cleear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.391
records.text:
The condition called praläpa is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.39):


hä nätha ramaëa preñöha. . .


   "O master! My lover! O dearmost, where are You? Where are You? Please, O mighty-armed one,
O friend, show Yourself to Me, Your poor servant!"***

  The meaning of this verse is cleear. This verse was spoken by Çré Rädhä.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.392
records.text:
Praläpa is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.31.1-19):


jayati te 'dhikaà janmanä vrajaù
   çrayata indirä çaçvad atra hi
dayita dåsyatam dikñu tavakas
   tvayi dhåtäsavas tväà vicinvate


"The gopés said: O beloved, Your birth in the land of Vraja has made it exceedingly glorious, and
thus Indirä, the goddess of fortune, always resides here. It is only for Your sake
searching everywhere for You, so please show Yourself to us."***

çarad-udäçaye sädhu jäta. . .


   "O Lord of love, in beauty Your glance excels the whorl of the finest, most perfec fly formed
lotus within the autumn pond. O bestower of benedictions, You are killing the maidservants who
have given themselves to You freely, without any price. Isn't this murder?"***


visa jaläpyayäd. . .


   "O greatest of personalities, You have repeatedly saved us from all kinds of danger--from
poisoned water, from the terrible maneater Agha, from the great rains, from the wind demon, from
the fiery thunderbolt of Indra, from the bull demon and from the son of Maya Dänava."***


na khalu gopikä-nandanaù. . .


   "You are not actually the son of the gopé Yaçodä, O friend, but rather the indwelling witness in
the hearts of all embodied souls. Because Lord Brahmä prayed for Yon to come and protect the
universe, You have now appeared in the Sätvata dynasty."***


viracitäbhayam. . .


   "O best of the Våñëis, Your lotuslike hand, which holds the hand of the goddess of fortune,
grants fearlessness to those who approach Your feet out of fear of material existence. O lover, please
place that wish-fulfilling lotus hand on our heads."***


vraja-janärti-han. . .


   "O You who destroy the suffering of Vraja's people, O hero of all women, Your smile shatters the
false pride of Your devotees. Please, dear friend, accept us as Your maidservants and show us Your
beautiful lotus face."***


praëata-dehinäm. . .


   "Your lotus feet destroy the past sins of all embodied souls who surrender to them. Those feet
follow after the cows in the pastures and are the eternal abode of the goddess of fortune. Since You
once put those feet on the hoods of the great serpent Kaliya, please place them upon our breasts
and tear away the lust in our hearts."***

madhurayä girä. . .


   "O lotus-eyed one, Your sweet voice and charming words, which attract the minds of the
intelligent, are bewildering us more and more. Our dear hero, please revive Your maidservants with
the nectar of Your lips."***


tava kathämåtam. . .


    "The nectar of Your words and the descriptions of Your activities are the life and soul of those
suffering in this material world. These narrations, transmitted by learned sages, eradicate one's
sinful reactions and bestow good fortune upon whoever hears them. These narrations are broadcast
all over the world and are filled with spiritual power. Certainly those who spread the message of
Godhead are most munificent."***


prahasitam. . .


   "Your smiles, Your sweet, loving glances, the intimate pastimes and confidential talks we enjoyed
with You--all these are auspicious to meditate upon, and they touch our hearts. But at the same
time, O deceiver, they very much agitate our minds."***


calasi yad vrajät. . .


   "Dear master, dear lover, when You leave the cowherd village to herd the cows, our minds are
disturbed with the thought that Your feet, more beautiful than a lotus, will be pricked by the spiked
husks of grain and the rough grass and plants."***


dina-parikñaye. . .


   "At the end of the day You repeatedly show us Your lotus face, covered with dark blue locks of
hair and thickly powdered with dust. Thus, O hero, You arouse lusty desires in our minds."***


praëata-käma-dam. . .


   "Your lotus feet, which are worshiped by Lord Brahmä, fulfill the desires of all who bow down to

them. They are the ornament of the earth, and in times of danger they are the appropriate object of
meditation. O destroyer of anxiety, please put those lotus feet upon our breasts.***


surata-vardhanam. . .


  "O hero, kindly distribute to us the nectar of Your lips, which enhances conjugal pleasure and
vanquishes grief. That nectar is thoroughly relished by Your vibrating flutc and makes people forget
any other attachment."***


aöati yad bhavän. . .


   "When You go off to the forest during the day, a tiny fraction of a second becomes like a
millennium for us because we cannot see You. And even when we can eagerly look upon Your
beautiful face, so lovely with its adornment of curly locks, our pleasure is hindered by our eyelids,
which were fashioned by the foolish creator."***


pati-sutänvaya. . .


   "Dear Acyuta, You know very well why we have come here. Who but a cheater like You would
abandon young women who come to see Him in the middle of the night, enchanted by the loud
song of His flute? Just to see You, we have completely rejected our husbands, children, ancestors,
brothers and other relatives."***


rahasi saàvidam. . .


   "Our minds are repeatedly bewildered as we think of the intimate conversations we had with
You in secret, feel the rise of lust in our hearts and remember Your smiling lace, Your loving
glances and Your broad chest, the resting place of the goddess of fortune. Thus we experience the
most severe hankering for You."***


vraja-vanaukasäm. . .


    "O beloved, Your all-auspicious appearance vanquishes the distress of those living in Vraja's
forests. our minds long for Your association. Please give to us just a bit of that medicine, which
counteracts the disease in Your devotees' hearts."***

yat te sujäta-caraëämburuhaà stanesu
   bhétäù çanaiù Priya dadhémahi karkaçesu
tenäöavém aöasi tad vyathate na kià svit
   kürpädibhir bhramati dhér bhavad-äyuñäà naù


   "O dearly beloved! Your lotus feet are so soft that we place them gently on our breasts, fearing
that Your feet will be hurt. Our life rests only in You. Our minds, therefore, are filled with anxiety
that Your tender feet might be wounded by pebbles as You roam about on the forest path."***

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.3 the gopés say: "As in the past You rescued everyone in Gokula,
please now rescue us." The meaning is: "As You rescued the people from the bull's son Vatsäsura,
and from Maya Dänava's son Vyomäsura, please rescue us." In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.4-5 the
gopés humbly pray: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As in the past with a single
glance You protected all the worlds, in the same way please protect us now." In Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.31.4 the words "sätvatäà kule" mean "You descended to this world in the family of Nanda
Mahäräja and other devotees". In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.5 the word "våñëi-dhürye" also refers to
Nanda and the people of Gokula, for they were all born in the Yadu dynasty". This is seen in the
following words of Skanda Puräëa, Mathurä-mähätmya:


govardhanaç ca bhagavän
   yatra govardhano dhåtaù
rakñitä yädaväù sarve
   indra-våñöi-niväraëät


   "In that place Lord Kåñëa lifted Govardhaana Hill and thus rescued all the Yädavas from the
torrential rains sent by Indra."

  That the people of Gokula were members of the Yadu dynasty is also seen in these words of
Skanda Puräëa, Çré Govinda-kuëòa-prastäva:


yaträbhiñikto bhagavän
   maghono yadu-variëaù


  "In that place Lord Kåñëa was bathed by the demigod Indra, who had attempted to harm the
Yadu dynasty.

   After speaking Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.3, the gopés, with a mixture of love and anger, say in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.4: "You are not a true son of the gopé who is Vraja's queen, a gopé who
always protected us when we were in distress. Rather, You are the Supersoul, the witness of the
pure souls' actions, a witness who remains always untouched by the souls' sufferings and joys. Is it
not so that on the demigod Brahmä's request You descended to this world to protect all living

beings? Therefore You should not ignore us." This the gopés humbly request in the second half of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.4. Then the gopés speak a similar prayer in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.5.
Then in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.7 the gopés say: "Your feet are the abode of the goddess of
fortune. They destroy the sins of the surrendered souls. Please very mercifully place Your feet on
our breasts and tear away the lust in our hearts." Then the gopés say in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.8:
"Is it not true that the sweetness of Your words, sweetness anointed with a very charming fragrance,
has enchanted out hearts? The nectar of Your lips is the medicine that will revive us. How can we
girls who have performed no pious deeds attain the nectar of Your lips? Even the nectar of Your
words is very far way for us. Our elders and superiors stop us and imprison us in our homes.
Therefore the nectar of Your pastimes is very difficult for us to attain." Thinking in this way, the
gopés speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.9, where they say: "Persons who chant Your glories give a
great gift to us." Then Lord Kåñëa might ask: "Why have you fallen in love (anuräga, with Me?" To
answer this question the gopés speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.10. Lord Kåñëa may then ask: "How
is it possible that My smiles and other actions and features could do such a thing to you?" To answer
this question the gopés say: "kuhaka", (You are a great cheater). This word mea
ns: "You know that within You lies a great power to cheat and deceive others." The gopés then speak
many other reasons also. Describing Lord Kåñëa's great, great attractiveness, the gopés then speak
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.31.19. These verses were spoken by the gopés.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.393
records.text:
After these verses an example of sambhoga is given in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.32.3):


taà vilokyägataà preñöham. . .


   "When the gopés saw that their dearmost Kåñëa had returned to them, they all stood up at once,
and out of their affection for Him their eyes bloomed wide. It was as if the air of life had reentered
their bodies."***

   In this way the gopés' distress at being separated from Lord Kåñëa is gradually relieved. The first
stage of this process is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.32.9):


sarväs täù keçaväloka-
   paramotsava-nirvåtaù
jahur viraha jaà täpaà
   präjïaà präpya yathä janäù


   "All the gopés enjoyed the greatest festivity when they saw their beloved Keçava again. They
gave up the distress of separation, just as people in general forget their misery when they gain the

association of a spiritually enlightened person."***

   The second stage of this process is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.32.13):


tad-darçanähläda-vidhüta-håd-rujaù. . .


   "Their heartache vanquished by the ecstasy of seeing Kåñëa, the gopés, like the personified Veòas
before them, felt their desires completely fulfilled. For their dear friend Kåñëa they arranged a seat
with their shawls, which were smeared with the kuìkuma powder from their breasts."***

   The gopés relief from distress is also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.1):


itthaà bhagavato gopyaù
   çrutvä väcaù su-peçaläù
jahur viraha jaà täpam-
   tad-aìgopacitäçisah


   "When the cowherd girls heard the Supreme Personality of Godhead speak these most charming
words, they forgot their distress caused by separation from Him. Touching His transcendental
limbs, they felt all their desires fulfilled."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 394-397


   The second kind of praväsa, where the beloved is a short distance away (kiïcid-düra-praväsa, is
also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.1):


gopyaù kåñëe vanaà yäte
   tam anudruta-cetasaù
kåñëa-léläù pragäyantyo
   ninyur duùkhena väsarän


   "Whenever Kåñëa went to the forest, the minds of the gopés would run after Him, and thus the
young girls sadly spent their days singing of His pastimes."***

   The gopés' conditioon of praläpa is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.2-21):

çré-gopya ücuù

väma-bähu-kåta-väma-kapolo
  valgita-bhrur adharärpita-veëum
komalangulibhir asrita-margam
  gopya érayati yatra mukundaù

vyoma-yäna-vanitäù saha siddhair
   vismitäs tad upadhärya sa-lajjäù
käma-märgaëa-samarpita-cittäù
   kaçmalaà yayur apasmåta-névyah


   "The gopés said: When Mukunda vibrates the flute He has placed to His lips, stopping its holes
with His tender fingers, He rests His left cheek on His left arm and makes His eyebrows dance. At
that time the demigoddesses traveling in the sky with their husbands, the Siddhas, become amazed.
As those ladies listen, they are embarrassed to find their minds yielding to the pursuit of lusty
desires, and in their distress they are unaware that the belts of their garments are loosening."***


hanta citram abaläù çåëutedam. . .
vrndaço vraja-våñä. . .


   "O girls! This son of Nanda, who gives joy to the distressed, bears steady lightning on His chest
and has a smile like a jeweled necklace. Now please hear something wonderful. When He vibrates
His flute, Vraja's buHs, deer and cows, standing in groups at a great distance, are all captivated by
the sound, and they stop chewing the food in their mouths and cock their ears. Stunned, they
appear as if asleep, or like figures in a painting."***


barhiëa-stabaka. . .
tarhi bhagna-gatayaù. . .


   "My dear gopé, sometimes Mukunda imitates the appearance of a wrestler by decorating Himself
with leaves, peacock feathers and colored minerals. Then, in the company of Balaräma and the
cowherd boys, He plays His flute to call the cows. At that time the rivers stop flowing, their water
stunned by the ecstasy they feel as they eagerly wait for the wind to bring them the dust of His lotus
feet. But like us, the rivers are not very pious, and thus they merely wait with their arms trembling
out of love."***


anucaraiù. . .
vana-latäù. . .
darçanéya-tilakaù. . .

sarasi särasa. . .


   "Kåñëa moves about the forest in the company of His friends, who vividly chant the glories of
His magnificent deeds. He thus appears just like the Supreme Personality of Godhead exhibiting
His inexhaustible opulences. When the cows wander onto the mountainsides and Kåñëa calls out to
them with the sound of His flute, the trees and creepers in the lorest respond by becoming so
luxuriant with fruits and flowers that they seem to be manifesting Lord Viñëu within their hearts.
As their branches bend low with the weight, the filaments on their trunks and vines stand erect out
of the ecstasy of love of God, and both the trees and the creepers pour down a rain of sweet sap."***
   "Maddened by the divine, honeylike aroma of the tulasé flowers on the garland Kåñëa wears,
swarms of bees sing loudly for Him, and that most beautiful of all persons thankfully acknowledges
and acclaims their song by taking His flute to His lips and playing it. The charming flute song then
steals away the minds of the cranes, swans and other lake-dwelling birds. Indeed, they approach
Kåñëa, close their eyes and, maintaining strict silence, worship Him by fixing their consciousness
upon Him in deep meditation."***


saha-balaù. . .
mahad-atikramaëa. . .


   "O goddesses of Vraja, when Kåñëa is enjoying Himself with Balaräma on the mountain slopes,
playfully wearing a flower garland on the top of His head, He engladdens all with the resonant
vibrations of His flute. Thus He delights the entire world. At that time the nearby cloud, afraid of
offending a great personality, thunders very gently in accompaniment. The cloud showers flowers
onto his dear friend Kåñëa and shades Him from the sun like an umbrella."***


vividha-gopa-caraëeñu. . .
savanaçaù. . .


   "O pious mother Yaçodä, your son, who is expert in all the arts of herding cows, has invented
many new styles of flute-playing. When He takes His flute to His bimba-red lips and sends forth the
tones of the harmonic scale in variegated melodies, Brahmä, Siva, Indra and other chief demigods
become •
confused upon hearing the sound. Although they are the most learned authorities, they cannot
ascertain the essence of that music, and thus they bow down their heads and hearts."***


nija-padäbja-dalaiù. . .
vrajati tena vayam. . .


   "As Kåñëa strolls through Vraja with His lotus-petal-like feet, marking the ground with the

distinctive embIems of flag, thunderbolt, lotus and elephant goad, He relieves the distress the
ground feels from the cows' hooves. As He plays His renowned flute, His body moves with the grace
of an elephant. Thus we gopés, who become agitated by Cupid when Kåñëa playfully glances at us,
stand as still as trees, unaware that our hair and garments are slackening."***


maëi-dharaù. . .
kvaëita-veëu-rava. . .


   "Now Kåñëa is standing somewhere counting His cows on a string of gems. He wears a garland of
tulasé flowers that bear the fragrance of His beloved, and He has thrown His arm over the shoulder
of an affectionate cowherd boyfriend. As Kåñëa plays His flute and sings, the music attracts the
black deer's wives, who approach that ocean of transcendental qualities and sit down beside Him.
Just like us cowherd girls, they have given up all hope for happiness in family life. ***


kunda-däma. . .
manda-väyuù. . .


    "O sinless Yaçodä, your darling child, the son of Mahäräja Nanda, has festively enhanced His
attire with a jasmine garland, and He is now playing along the Yamunä in the company of the cows
and cowherd boys, amusing His dear companions. The gentle breeze honors Him with its soothing
fragrance of sandalwood, while the various Upadevas, standing on all sides like panegyrists, offer
their music, singing and gifts of tribute."***

   These verses are written in pairs (yugala). In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.35.3 the word "saha-
siddhaiù" means "the goddesses and their husbands, the demigods, chanted the glories of Lord
Kåñëa's flute music. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.35.8, in the words "ädi-puruñaù iväcala-bhütiù", the
gopés, impelled by love, speculate: "Perhaps Kåñëa is the all-powerful and all-opulent Supreme
Personality of Godhead, the greatest of all." This statement is like that of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.29.32. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.35.9 "Perhaps Kåñëa is Lord Viñëu, who is manifest everywhere".
In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.35.16 the word "vraja-bhuvaù" indicates the grass and other living entities
manifest in the land of Vraja. Here the words "çayaman khura-toòam" mean "the touch of Lord
Kåñëa's feet is glorious because that touch relieves the distress of the ground. The newly sprouted
grasses on the ground suffer when they are trampled by the cows' sets of four hooves." Gazing at
Lord Kåñëa in sambhoga is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.22-23):


vatsalo vraja-gaväà yad aga-dhro
   vandyamäna-caraëaù pathi våddhaiù
kåtsna-go-dhanam upohya dinänte
   géta-veëur anugeòita-kértiù

utsavaà çrama-rucäpi drçénäm
   unnayan khura-rajas"-churita-srak
ditsayaiti suhåd-äçiña eña
   devaké-jaöhara-bhür uòu-räjaù


   "Out of great affection for the cows of Vraja, Kåñëa became the lifter of Govardhana Hill. At the
end of the day, having rounded up all His own cows, He plays a song on His flute, while exalted
demigods standing along the path worship His lotus feet and the cowherd boys accompanying Him
chant His glories. His garland is powdered by the dust raised by the cows hooves, and His beauty,
enhanced by His fatigue, creates an ecstatic festival for everyone's eyes. Eager to fulfill His friends'
desires, Kåñëa is the moon arisen from the womb of mother Yaçodä."***

  In this verse the word "devaké-jaöhara-bhüù" hints at Lord Kåñëa's name. The root of that hint of
Lord Kåñëa's name is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.14):


präg ayaà vasudevasya
   kvaciê jätas tavätmajaù


  "For many reasons, this beautiful son of yours sometimes appeared previously as the son of
Vasudeva. Therefore, those who are learned sometimes call this child Väsudeva."*

  In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.35.23 the word "devaké" should be understood to mean "yaçodä".
Yaçodä was also known by the name Devaké. That Lord Kåñëa's mother sometimes has more than
one name is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (2.7.10):


näbher asäö åñabha äsa sudevé-sünuù


  "The Lord appeared as the son of Sudevé, the wife of King Näbhi, and was known as
Åñabhadeva."*

  In this verse it is seen that Sudevé is another name for Queen Meru-devé. That Devaké is another
name of Yaçodä is seen in these words of Adi Puräëa:


dve nämné nanda-bhäryäyä
  yaäodä devakéti ca


   "Mahäräja Nanda's wife had two names: Yaçodä and Devaké."

   Gazing at Lord Kåñëa in sambhoga is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.24-

25):


mada-vighürëita-locana ésat. . .
yadu-patir dvirada-räja-vihäraù. . .


   "As Kåñëa respectfully greets His well-wishing friends, His eyes roll slightly as if from
intoxication. He wears a flower garland, and the beauty of His soft cheeks is accentuated by the
brilliance of His golden earrings and the whiteness of His face, which has the color of a baòara
berry. With His cheerful face resembling the moon, lord of the night, the Lord of the Yadus moves
with the grace of a regal elephant. Thus He returns in the evening, delivering the cows of Vraja
from the heat of the day."***

   In this verse the word "vraja-gaväm" refers to both the calves and the adult cows. It is then said
in the next verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.26):


evaà vraja-striyo räjan
   kåñëa-lélänugäyatéù
remire 'haùsu tac-cittäs
   tan-manaskä mahodayäh


    "O King, thus during the daytime the women of Våndävana took pleasure in continuously
singing about the pastimes of Kåñëa, and those ladies' minds and hearts, absorbed in Him, were
filled with great festivity."***

   Here the words "mahodayäù remire" mean "Joyful at Lord Kåñëa's return in the afternoon, they
always celebrated a great festival". This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadwva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 398-400


   Now düra-praväsa (separation when the beloved is far away, will be considered. This kind of
separation is of three kinds: 1. bhävé (in the future), 2. bhavan (in the present), and 3. bhüta (in the
past). This kind of separation in the future is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.39.13):


gopyas täs tad upaçrutya
   babhüvur vyathita bhåsam
räma-kåñëau puréà netum
   akrüraà vrajam ägatam

    "When the young gopés heard that Akrüra had come to Vraja to take Kåñëa and Balaräma to the
city, they became extremely distressed."***

   In this situation the gopés lamented in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.39.19-30):


aho vidhätas tava na kvacid dayä
   saàyojya maitryä praëayena dehinaù
täàs" cäkåtärthän viyunankñy aparthakam
   vikréòitaà te 'rbhaka-ceñöitaà yathä


    "O Providence, you have no mercy! You bring embodied creatures together in friendship and
love and then senselessly separate them before they fulfill their desires. This whimsical play of yours
is like a child's game."***


yas tvaà pradarçyäsita-kuntalävåtam. . .


  "Having shown us Mukunda's face, framed by dark locks and beautified by His fine cheeks, raised
nose and gentle smiles, which eradicate all misery, you are now making that face invisible. This
behavior of yours is not at all good."***


krüras tvam akrüra. . .


   "O Providence, though you come here with the name Akrura, you are indeed cruel, for like a fool
you are taking away what you once gave us--those eyes with which we have seen, even in one
feature of Lord Madhudviña's form, the perfection of your entire •
creation."***


na nanda-sünuù kñaëa-bhaìga-sauhådaù. . .


   "Alas, Nanda's son, who breaks loving friendships in a second, will not even look directly at us.
Forcibly brought under His control, we abandoned our homes, relatives, children and husbands just
to serve Him, but He is always looking for new lovers."***


sukhaà prabhätä rajanéyam. . .


  "The dawn following this night will certainly be auspicious for the women of Mathurä. All their
hopes will now be fulfilled, for as the Lord of Vraja enters their city, they will be able to drink from

His lace the nectar of the smile emanating from the corners of His eyes."***


täsäà mukundaù. . .


    "O gopés, although our Mukunda is intelligent and very obedient to His parents, once He has
fallen under the spell of the honeysweet words of the women of Mathurä and been enchanted by
their alluring, shy smiles, how will He ever return to us unsophisticated village girls?"***


adya dhruvaà tatra dåço bhaviñyate. . .


   "When the Däçärhas, Bhojas, Andhakas, Våñëis and Sätvatas see the son of Devaké in Mathurä,
they will certainly enjoy a great festival for their eyes, as w ill all those who see Him traveling along
the road to the city. After all, He is the darling of the goddess of fortune and the reservoir of all
transcendental qualities."***


maitad-vidhasyäkaruëasya. . .


   "He who is doing this merciless deed should not be called Akrüra. He is so extremely cruel that
without even trying to console the sorrowful residents of Vraja, he is taking away Kåñëa, who is
more dear to us than life itself."***


anärdra-dhér eñaù. . .


   "Hard-hearted Kåñëa has already mounted the chariot, and now the foolish cowherds are
hurrying after Him in their bullock carts. Even the elders are saying nothing to stop Him. Today
fate is working against us."***


nivärayämaù. . .


   "Let us directly approach Mädhava and stop Him from going. What can our family elders and
other relatives do to us? Now that fate is separating us from Mukunda, our hearts are already
wretched, for we cannot bear to give up His association even for a fraction of a second."***


yasyänuräga. . .

   "When He brought us to the assembly of the räsa dance, where we enjoyed His affectionate and
charming smiles, His delightful secret talks, His playful glances and His embraces, we passed many
nights as if they were a single moment. O gopés, how can we possibly cross over the insurmountable
darkness of His absence?"***


yo 'hnaù kñaye vrajam ananta-sakhaù. . .


   "How can we exist without Ananta's friend Kåñëa, who in the evening would return to Vraja in
the company of the cowherd boys, His hair and garland powdered with the dust raised by the cows'
hooves? As He played His flute, He would captivate our minds with His smiling sidelong
glances."***

  Then it is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.39.34 and 37):


gopyas" ca dayitam kåñnam
   anuvrajyänu raïjitäù
pratyädeçaà bhagavataù
   käìksantyas" cävatasthire


  "[With His glancesÝ Lord Kåñëa somewhat pacified the gopés, and they also followed behind for
some time. Then, hoping He would give them some instruction, they stood still."***


tä niräçä nivavåtur
   govinda-vinivartane
viçokä ahané ninyur
   gäyantyaù priya-ceñöitam


   "The gopés then turned back, without hope that Govinda would ever return to them. Full of
sorrow, they began to spend their days and nights chanting about the pastimes of their beloved."***

   In this verse the word "viçokäù" means "various kinds of sorrow". As they sang of Lord Kåñëa's
pastimes, it was as if those pastimes were directly manifest before them and they saw those pastimes
with their own eyes. Here the words "ahané ninyuù" means "in this way they passed the day and the
night". These two verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.401
records.text:
Düra-pravaça manifested in the past is seen in these words spoken by Lord Kåñëa in Çrémad-

Bhägavatam (10.46.4):


tä man-manaskä mat-präëä
   mad-arthe tyakta-daihikäù. . .


  "The minds of those gopés are always absorbed in Me, and their very lives are veer devoted to Me.
For My sake they have abandoned everything related to their bodies."***

   In this kind of praväsa there are written letters between the lover and beloved and there are also
messages orally repeated by a messnger. The messengers here may be Lord Balaräma, Uddhava, or
other friends of Lord Kåñëa. An example of such a messenger is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.47.3):


taà praçrayeëävanataù su-sat-kåtaà
   sa-vréòa-häsekñaëa-sunåtädibhiù


   "Bowing their herads in humility, the gopés duly honored Uddhava with their shy, smiling
glances and pleasing words. They took him to a quiet place, seated him, and comfortably began to
question him, for they recognized him to be a messenger from- Kåñëa, the master of the goddess of
fortune."***

   Although in the past they had kept everything secret, when Uddhava arrived, the distraught
gopés abandoned all shyness. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.40.9):


iti gopyo hi govinde
    gata-väk-käya-mänasäù
kåñëa-düte samäyäte
    uddhave tyakta-laukikäù


   "Thus speaking, the gopés, whose words, bodies, and minds were fully dedicated to Lord Govinda,
put aside all their regular work now that Kåñëa's messenger, Uddhava, had arrived among them."***

  This is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.3):


apåcchann


   "Bowing their herads in humility, the gopés duly honored Uddhava with their shy, smiling
glances and pleasing words. They took him to a quiet place, seated him, and comfortably began to
question him, for they recognized him to be a messenger from Kåñëa, the master of the goddess of

fortune."***

  In the sequence of verses in Çrémad-Bhägavatam this verse precedes Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.9
quoted above. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

records.title: Priti Sandarbha · PS.402
records.text:
Another example of the gopés greeting a messenger from Lord Kåñëa is seen in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.65.9):


gopyo hasantyaù papracchü
   räma-sandarçanädåtäù
kaccid äste sukhaà kåñëaù
   pura-stré-jana-vallabhaù


  "Honored to have the personal audience of Lord Balaräma, the young gopés smiled and asked
Him: `Is Kåñëa, the darling of city women, living happily."***

  In this verse the word "hasantyaù" means "with smiles mixed with love and anger, smiles that
mock Lord Kåñëa". This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 403-413


   In Uddhava's presence the gopés spoke wildly. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.47.11):


käcin madhukaraà dåñövä
   dhyäyanté kåñëa-saìgamam
priya-prasthäpitaà dütaà
   kalpayitvedam abravét


   "One of the gopés, while meditating on Her previous association with Kåñëa, saw a honeybee
before Her and imagined it to be a messenger sent by Her beloved. Thus She spoke as follows."***

   In this verse the word "käcit" (a certain gopé, refers to Çré Rädhä". This is explained in the
Väsanä-bhäñya commentary. This truth is also seen in the Daçama-öippané commentary of Çréla
Sanätana Gosvämé. In the following eigth verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.12-19), angry Çré Rädha'
speaks wildly. She says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.12):

madhupa kitava-bandho. . .


   "O honeybee, O friend of a cheater, don't touch My feet with your whiskers, which are smeared
with the kuìkuma that rubbed onto Kåñëa's garland when it was crushed hy the breasts of a rival
lover! Let Kåñëa satisfy the women of Mathurä. One who sends a messenger like you will certainly
be ridiculed in the Yadus' assembly."***

   Then She explains the reason for Her anger in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.13):


sakåd adhara-sudhäm. . .


   "After making us drink the enchanting nectar of His lips only once, Kåñëa suddenly abandoned
us, just as you might quickly abandon some flowers. How is, then, that Goddess Padmä willingly
serves His lotus feet? Alas! The answer must certainly be that her mind has been stolen away by His
deceitful words."***

  In this verse Çré Rädha' criticizes Her rival, Goddess Padmä. In the next verse She rejects the
words of praise brought by the messenger. She says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.14):


kim iha. . .


   "O bee, why do you sing here so much about the Lord of the Yadus, in front of us homeless
people? These topics are old news to us. Better you sing about that friend of Arjuna in front of His
new girlfriends, the burning desire in whose breasts He has now relieved. Those ladies will surely
give you the charity you are begging."***

   In this verse the word "vijaya" means "Lord Kåñëa, who brings all others under His control",
"sakhä" means "your friend", "sakhénäm" means "of the women of Mathurä", and "prasaìgaù" means
"songs that bring one under their control". The gopés here say: "These songs are faulty because they
make us attached to Kåñëa. Even if you take that fault away, these topics still make us wretched and
miserable. This proves that Kåñëa is completely merciless." The gopés say in the next verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.47.15):


divi bhuvi. . .


   "In heaven, on earth, or in the subterranean sphere, what woman is unavailable to Him? He
simply arches His eyebrows and smiles with deceptive charm, and they all become His. The supreme
goddess herself worships the dust of His feet, so what is our position in comparison? But at least

those who are wretched can chant His name, Uttamaùsloka."***

   In this verse the word "api ca" means "nevertheless", "kåpaëa-pakñe" means "wretched persons
like us", "and "uttama-çloka-çabdaù" means the sound of Lord Kåñëa's name may be present". Here
the gopés hint: "Because He will not allow us to see Him, He is not merciful, and because He is not
merciful, He should not be called by the name Uttamaçloka".
   Thinking the bee's gentle humming to be a host of flattering words from Lord Kåñëa, Çré Rädha'
says in the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.16):


visåja çirasi. . .


   "Keep your head off My feet! I know what you're doing. You expertly learned diplomacy from
Mukunda, and now you come as His messenger with flattering words. But he abandoned those who
fro His sake alone gave up their children, husbands, and all other relations. He's simply ungrateful.
Why should I make up with Him now?"***

  With love and anger criticizing Lord Kåñëa, Çré Rädha' admitShe cannot stop talking of Him.
Then She finds fault with Him. She says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.17):


mågayur iva. . .


   "Like a hunter He cruelly shot the king of the monkeys with arrows. Because He was conquered
by a woman, He disfigured another woman who came to Him with lusty desires. And even after
consuming the gifts of Bali Maharaja, He bound him up with ropes as if he were a crow. So let us
give up all frindship with this dark-compexioned boy, even if we can't give up talking about
Him."***

   Here the word "asita" means "Kåñëa, who is black because of all these misdeeds" and "sakhyaiù"
means with loving friendship". Again and again She affirms that Kåñëa should be rejected. She
again finds fault with Kåñëa when She speaks the next verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.18):


yad-anucarita. . .


    "To hear about the pastimes that Kåñëa regularly performs is nectar fro the ears. For those who
relish just a single drop of that nectar, even once, their dedication to material duality is ruined.
Many such persons have suddenly given up their wretched homes and families and, themselves
becoming wretched, traveled here to Våndävana to wander about like birds, begging for their
living."***

   In this verse the word "karna-piyusa" means "these topics may be nectar for the ears, but they are

not nectar for the heart". They are sweet only in the beginning. The words "vidhüta-dvandva-
dharmä vinañöäù" mean "at the end these topics make one almost unconscious". "Iha" means "in
Våndävana", "vihaìgäù" means "parrots and other birds", "bhikñu-caryäà caranti" means "they
follow the activities of the sannyasis, which means they ignore their material bodies and other
material things. It is seen that they act in this way". That is the meaning here.

   Then Çré Rädha' laments in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.19):


vayam åtam iva. . .


   "Faithfully taking His deceitful words as true, we became just like the black deer's foolish wives,
who trust the cruel hunter's song. Thus we repeatedly felt the sharp pain of lust cause by the touch
of His nails. O messenger, please talk about something besides Kåñëa."***

   Then, fearing that Her harsh and angry words spoken in these eight verses will chase the
messenger away, Çré Rädha' tries to end Her quarrel with Lord Kåñëa. She says in the next verse of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.20):


priya-sakha. . .


   "O friend of My dear one, has My beloved sent you here again? I should honor you, friend, so
please choose whatever boon you wish. But why have you came back to take us to Him, whose
conjugal love is so difficult to give up? After all, gentle bee, His consort is the goddess Çré, as she is
always with Him, staying upon His chest."***

   With words of crooked irony Çré Rädha' speaks the second half of this verse. Here the word
"dvandva" means "amorous pastimes"". The reason amorous pastimes with Kåñëa are difficult to give
up is given in the word "satatam" (Goddess Lakñmé always on Lord Kåñëa's chest). Here, speaking
words of love and anger, Çré Rädha' imagines that the Çrévatsa line on Lord Kåñëa's chest is actually
Goddess Lakñmé. At the end of this passage Çré Rädha' humbly speaks these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.47.21):


api bata. . .


   "O Uddhava! It is indeed regrettable that Kåñëa resides in Mathurä. Does He remember His
father's household affairs and His friends, the cowherd boys? O great soul! Does He ever talk about
us, His maidservants? When will He lay on our heads His aguru-scented hand? "***

   The messenger (Uddhava, sent by Lord Kåñëa consoled the gopés in two ways: 1. by praising
them, and 2. by speaking Lord Kåñëa's message to them. He praised them in these words of Çrémad-

Bhägavatam (10.47.23):


aho yüyaà sma pürëärthäù. . .


   "Certainly you gopés are all-successful and are universally worshiped because you have dedicated
your minds in this way to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Väsudeva."***

  Uddhava's repeating Lord Kåñëa's message is discussed in Kåñëa-sandarbha (Anuccheda 155)¾
That message is given in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.29):


bhavaténäà viyogo me. . .


   "The Supreme Lord said: You are never actually separated from Me, for I am the soul of all
creation. Just as the elements of nature-ether, air, fire, water, and earth-are present in every created
thing, so I am present within everyuone's mind, life-air, and senses, and also within the physical
elements and the modes of material nature."***

  These words describe Lord Kåñëa's eternal pastimes with the people of Vraja in the eternal
Våndävana in another manifestation (in the spiritual sky). These words also describe the
meditational process of jïäna-yoga, by which the people of this world may obtain relief from
material sufferings. However, the teaching of jïäna-yoga do not bring peace to the gopés. Lord
Kåñëa then explains in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.34):


yat tö ahaà bhavaténäà vai. . .


   "But the actual reason why I, the beloved object of your sight, have stayed far away from you is
that I wanted to intensify your meditation upon Me and thus draw your minds closer to Me."***

   Lord Kåñëa also explains in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.37):


yä mayä kréòatä rätryäm. . .


   "Although some gopés had to remain in the cowherd village and so could not join the räsa dance
to sport with Me at night in the forest, they were nonetheless fortunate. Indeed, they attained Me
by thinking of My glorious pastimes."***

  Further explaining the meaning of the words He spoke in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.34, Lord
Kåñëa says in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.41):

api smaratha naù sakhyaù
   svänäm artha-cikérñayä
gatän. . .


   "My dear girlfriends, do you still remember Me? It was for My relatives' sake that I stayed away so
long, intent on destroying my enemies."***

   By describing his purpose (in staying way, Lord Kåñëa's intention to increase the gopés' feelings
of happiness and love for Him. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.53):


tatas täù kåñëa-sandeçair
   vyapeta-viraha-jvaräù
uddhavaà püjayäà cakrur
   jïätvätmänam adhokñajam


  "Lord Kåñëa's messages having relieved their fever of separation, the gopés then worshipped
Uddhava, recognizing him as nondifferent from their Lord, Kåñëa."***

  In this verse the word "vyapeta-viraha-jvaräù" means "by hearing of Lord Kåñëa's return and by
hearing of other topics also, the gopés became pacified". In this context the gopés asked (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.47.40):


kaccid gadägrajaù saumya. . .


   "Gentle Uddhava, is the elder brother of Gada now bestowing on the city women the pleasure
that actually belongs to us? We suppose those ladies worship Him with generous glances full of
affectionate, shy smiles."***

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.53 the word "ätmänam" means "because he was a messenger sent by
Kåñëa, Uddhava was able to know what was in Lord Kåñëa's heart", and "adhokñajam" means "the
gopés thought Uddhava was Lord Kåñëa Himself". Because they thought he was Lord Kåñëa, the
gopés worshiped Uddhava (uddhavaà püjayäà cakruù). The idea that Uddhava was Lorrd Kåñëa
Himself is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.14):


tam ägatam samägamya
   kåñëasyänucaraà priyam
nandaù prétaù pariñvajya
   väsudeva-dhiyärcayat

  "As sson as Uddhava arrived in Nanda Mahäräja's home, Nanda came forward to meet him. The
cowherd king embraced him in great happiness and worshipped him as nondifferent from Lorrd
Väsudeva."***

  This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvnamni.


Anucchedas 414-421


  Lord Balaräma's carrying a message from Lord Kåñëa in Dvärakä is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.65.16):


saìkarñaëas täù kåñëasya
   sandeçair hådayaìgamaiù
säntvayäm äsa bhagavän
   nänänunaya-kovidaù


  "The Supreme Loord Balaräma, the attractoir of all, being expert at various kinds of conciliation,
consoled the gopés by relaying to them the confidential messages Lord Kåñëa had sent with Him.
These messages deeply touched the gopés' hearts."***

  After this message the gopés enjoyed sambhoga pastimes with Lord Kåñëa, directlyseeing Him at
Kurukñetra. Those pastimes are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.39):


gopyaç ca kåñëam upalabhya ciräd abhiñöaà
   yat-prekñaëe dåçiñu pakñma-kåtaà çapanti
dågbhir hådé-kåtam alaà parirabhya sarväs
   tad-bhävam äpur api nitya-yujaà duräpam


   "While gazing at their beloved Kåñëa, the young gopés used to condemn the creator of their
eyelids (which would momentarily block their vison of Him). Now, seeing Kåñëa again after such a
long separation, with their eyes they took Him into their hearts, and there they embraced Him to
their full satisfaction. In this way they became totally absorbed in ecstatic meditation on Him,
although those who constantly practice mystic yoga find such absorption difficult to achieve."***

   After in this way describing the condition of the gopés' hearts, Çrémad-Bhägavatam explains the
gopés' ecstatic love for Lord Kåñëa in these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.40):


bhagaväàs täs tathä-bhütä

   viviktä upasaìgataù
äçliñyanamayaà prñövä
   prahasann idam abravét


    "The Supreme Lord approached the gopés in a secluded place as they stood in their ecstatic
trance. After embracing each of them and inquiring about their well-being, He laughed and spoke
as follows."***

   Agitating the gopés' hearts, Lord Kåñëa made the gopés forgive his offenses. His smile was
glorious. Then He consoled the gopé with these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.41):


api smaratha naù sakhyaù
   svänäm artha-cikérñayä
gatäàç cérayatan chatru-
   pakña-kñäpaëa-cetasaù


   "My dear girlfriends, do you still remember Me? It was for My relatives' sake that I stayed away so
long, intent on destroying my enemies."***

   In this verse Lord Kåñëa says: "Please do not remember Me with anger. Then, to show that He is
indeed faultless, Lord Kåñëa says: "It was for My relatives' sake that I stayed away so long, intent on
destroying my enemies." Here the word "svanam" means "of My father, the king of Vraja, and also of
My kinsmen, the Yädavas". Thess words may also hint: "These two sides of the family (Kåñëa's
kinsmen in Vraja and Dvärakä, were both part of the Yädava dynasty". Then Lord Kåñëa explains
why He was so long in returning to Vraja. He says: "I was intent on destroying my enemies". These
words hint: "From now only you will enjoyMy company (sambhoga, without interruption".

   Fearing the gopés may remain dissatisfied at heart, Lord Kåñëa comforted them by explaining
that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the ultimate independent controller of everyone. He
said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.42):


apy avadhyayathäsman svid
   akåta-jïäviçaìkayä
nünaà bhütäni bhagavän
   yunakti vinuyakti ca


  "Do you perhaps think I'm ungrateful and thus hold Me in contempt? After all, it is the Supreme
Lord who brings living beings together and then separates them."***

   Fearing that the gopés might reply: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead", Lord Kåñëa
explains: "Your separation from Me gave birth to great love for Me in your hearts. This is not

against your actual desire." Lord Kåñëa told them in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.44):


mayi bhaktir hi bhütänäm
   amåtatväya kalpate
diñöyä yad äsén mat-sneho
   bhavaténäà mad-äpanaù


   "Rendering devotional service to Me qualifies any living being for eternal life. But by your good
fortune you have developed a special loving attitude toward Me, by which you have attained
Me."***

   Çrédhara Svämé comments on this verse:

  "This verse means: `Rendering devotional service to Me qualifies any living being for eternal life.
But by your good fortune you have developed a special loving attitude toward Me." The question
may be asked: `Why is this so?' The answer is given here in the words: `You have attained Me'."

   Then, in order to console the gopés and reassure them they they indeed have attained His
association, Lord Kåñëa explains to them that because He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead
manifest in a humanlike form. He explains to the gopés that He is present everywhere and He is the
shelter in which everything rests. He tells them in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.45-46):


ahaà hi sarva-bhütänäm. . .


   "Dear ladies, I am the beginning and end of all created beings and exist both within and without
them, just as the elements ether, water, earth, air, and fire are the beginning and end of all material
objects and exist both within and without them."*
   "In this way all created beings reside within the basic elements of creation, while the spirit souls
pervade the creation, remaining in their own true identity. You should see both of these-the
material creation and the self-as manifest within Me, the imperishable Supreme Truth."***

   In the description of the Lord's Dämodara pastimes it is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.13-
14):


na cäntar na bahir yasya. . .


   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead has no beginning and no end, no exterior and no interior,
